These findings emphasize the need to optimize TRID design configurations, including installation position, inertia ratio, and tuning frequency, to improve drivetrain durability and vibration control in OFWTs. The demonstrated robustness in complex offshore conditions indicates its potential to lower maintenance demands, enhance cost efficiency, and support future application in floating wind turbines.

title: Physics-constrained domain-decoupled transfer method: Application to cross-condition tooth-wise monitoring in multi-tooth tools
abstract: In the machining process, tool wear monitoring (TWM) technology is crucial for ensuring machining safety and optimizing production costs. However, due to tool manufacturing precision, workpiece material characteristics, and tool runout, multi-tooth tools often exhibit uneven wear among individual cutting edges. Existing monitoring methods primarily focus on overall tool wear, lacking precise evaluation of individual cutting-edge wear, which hinders a detailed understanding of tool wear behaviour. Moreover, current monitoring approaches fail to incorporate the physical mechanism of edge-wise cutting processes into transfer learning, limiting the adaptability of models in multi-condition scenarios. To this end, this paper proposes a physics-constrained transfer learning network for multi-condition tooth-wise monitoring (PCTLNet). By embedding a physics-informed model, the proposed network implicitly learns and captures tool wear characteristics, ensuring that the learning process of tooth-wise wear features adheres to physical laws in a self-consistent manner. Specifically, the network is based on the DenseNet architecture and integrates a multi-modal one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) with a multi-head self-attention mechanism (MHSA), effectively extracting static features from cutting parameters and dynamic features from time-series signals. This paper proposes an adversarial high-order moment alignment mechanism to reduce domain discrepancies and improve the model’s adaptability under disturbances across different machining conditions. Furthermore, a multi-axis machining force model considering tooth-wise wear is established to reinforce physical consistency in the transfer learning process and ensure conformity with cutting physics. Based on this model, a novel physics-constrained domain adaptation strategy is proposed to enhance the network’s ability to learn tooth-wise wear features in the target domain. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through multi-condition milling wear experiments, demonstrating its advantages over existing state-of-the-art models in tooth-wise monitoring under varying machining conditions.

title: Nonlinear vibration analysis and active vibration control of carbon fiber reinforced composite cantilever laminated plate
abstract: This study explores the geometric nonlinear modeling of a carbon fiber reinforced composite (CFRC) cantilever laminated plate bonded with macro-fiber composites (MFC) patches and the design of active controllers based on the nonlinear model. A nonlinear dynamic model for CFRC–MFC cantilever laminated plate is established using the assumed mode method combined with von Karman large deformation theory, and it was transformed into state space equation form to facilitate the design of active controllers. Based on the nonlinear state space equation, an extended Kalman filter state observer (EKF-SO) and an active controller are designed. A numerical solution algorithm for the nonlinear state equation is designed based on the implicit fourth-order Runge–Kutta method (IRK4), and the nonlinear state estimation process is embedded into the solution program. Finally, a vibration testing and active control experimental platform is established. The accuracy of the model, the efficiency and high precision of the solution algorithm, as well as the effectiveness and advantages of the designed active controller are verified through simulation and experiment. The nonlinear vibration control strategy combining LQR and EKF-SO proposed in this paper will provide theoretical guidance for the engineering practice of nonlinear vibration control.
keywords: Carbon fiber reinforced composite (CFRC) cantilever laminated plate

title: Adaptive reduced order modelling of acoustic LTI systems with input–output dead time
abstract: While many acoustic systems are well-modelled by linear time-invariant dynamical systems, high-fidelity models often become computationally expensive due the complexity of dynamics. Reduced order modelling techniques, such as the Eigensystem Realization Algorithm (ERA), can be used to create efficient surrogate models from measurement data, particularly impulse responses. However, practical challenges remain, including the presence of input–output dead times, i.e. propagation delays, in the data, which can increase model order and introduce artifacts like pre-ringing. This paper introduces an improved technique for the extraction of dead times, by formulating a linear program to separate input and output dead times from the data. Additionally, the paper presents an adaptive randomized ERA pipeline that leverages recent advances in numerical linear algebra to reduce computational complexity and enabling scalable model reduction. Benchmarking on large-scale datasets of measured room impulse responses demonstrates that the proposed dead time extraction scheme yields more accurate and efficient reduced order models compared to previous approaches. The implementation is made available as open-source Python code, facilitating reproducibility and further research.

title: Bearing housing as a sensor: Estimation of lumped bearing loads using accurate housing models
abstract: Accurate knowledge of bearing loads is crucial for assessing structural health state, estimating Remaining Useful Life (RUL), and optimizing performance in various mechanical systems. However, direct measurement of these loads is often intrusive and costly. This study presents a model-based virtual sensing framework for estimating lumped bearing loads using the bearing housing as a sensor. The approach relies on a finely tuned Finite Element (FE) model of the housing, combined with strategically placed strain and acceleration sensors. The linear FE model is integrated into an Augmented Kalman Filter (AKF) scheme to estimate both system states and input loads. A rigorous model updating procedure enhances the accuracy of the FE model, while a calibration-based Boundary Condition (BC) identification method enables strain gauge placement close to the boundaries, achieving a high Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of the strain measurements. To evaluate its effectiveness, the BC identification method is first assessed through a numerical example. Experimental validation on a setup with industrial complexity demonstrates that the proposed method enables load estimation across both quasi-static and higher frequency dynamic ranges. In comparison to existing virtual sensing methods, utilizing the high SNR locations and BC identification in this study has led to accurate estimation of individual bearing loads, without modeling the rotating components, and only using non-intrusive sensors placed on the housing. The results highlight the feasibility of transforming even stiff bearing housings into cost-effective and scalable virtual sensors for load estimation in various industrial applications.

title: Multidirectional negative stiffness electromagnetic mechanism for vibration isolation
abstract: The increasing industrial demand for low-frequency vibration isolation has positioned negative stiffness mechanisms (NSMs) as promising solutions. However, most existing NSMs can only generate negative stiffness along a single direction, whereas their implementation for practical multidirectional vibrations requires complex multiunit arrangements. This paper presents a multidirectional negative stiffness electromagnetic mechanism (MDNSEM). By designing coaxially nested magnetic poles, coupled air–gap magnetic fields along multiple directions are created, achieving simultaneous multidirectional negative stiffness within a single integrated structure. This approach simplifies system design, provides real-time stiffness adjustability through current control, and has contactless operation characteristics. An electromagnetic force model of the MDNSEM was established through the equivalent magnetic circuit method, and the air–gap fringing flux effects were incorporated. Experimental validation and parametric analysis were subsequently conducted. A high-static-low-dynamic stiffness (HSLDS) isolator was developed by paralleling the MDNSEM with positive stiffness mechanisms. The experimental results demonstrated significant broadening of the vibration isolation bandwidth along both the axial and radial directions. The MDNSEM provides an effective solution for multidirectional low-frequency microvibration isolation.

title: An adaptive Kriging-assisted reliability-based design optimization framework with reliability assurance and high efficiency
abstract: While reliability-based design optimization (RBDO) significantly improves engineering safety, computational expenses and accuracy concerns restrict its use in complex, high-dimensional, nonlinear, and black-box scenarios. To address this challenge, a Kriging-AMV-MCS reliability optimization method (KAMRO) is proposed in this paper. The algorithm integrates the Kriging surrogate model, an improved advanced mean value (AMV) method, and a Monte-Carlo simulation (MCS) validation mechanism, aiming to achieve efficient and robust design optimization. First, through an adaptive sampling strategy based on the expected feasibility function and space filling criteria, actively constrained regions are intelligently identified and sample distribution is optimized. Second, a two-stage optimization framework is adopted. In the first stage, the penalty function is used to quickly approximate the feasible domain, and in the second stage, explicit constraints are combined for precise optimization. Finally, an MCS-guided post-optimization process is proposed to further optimize and improve the design scheme when the reliability is insufficient. Through validation with engineering cases, including a two-dimensional analytical example, a seven-dimensional gear reducer structural optimization example, and a three-dimensional pressure control head structure design, this RBDO framework significantly reduces computational costs while ensuring design reliability, offering both optimization accuracy and engineering practicality.

title: A multi-scale wavelet and spectral kurtosis-guided framework for noise-resistant rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: The health status of rolling bearings is essential for ensuring the safe and stable operation of industrial equipment. However, vibration signals acquired under actual operating conditions are often contaminated by strong background noise. This contamination makes it difficult for traditional fault-diagnosis models to effectively extract subtle fault features, leading to low diagnostic accuracy and poor noise robustness. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel noise-resistant diagnostic network based on multi-scale wavelet convolution and kurtosis guidance (MWKG-Net). It is the first network to employ the lightweight Multi-Scale Wavelet Convolution Block (MWConv1D) to adaptively decompose one-dimensional vibration signals into multiple frequency subbands. This design not only enlarges the receptive field and achieves preliminary noise suppression, but also captures multi-scale fault information precisely, while reducing model parameters and computational overhead. Furthermore, we design a Kurtosis-Guided Feature Re-weighting (KGFR) module that quantifies the prominence of fault impulses by computing the spectral kurtosis of feature maps and dynamically re-weights feature channels. This enhances fault-related impulse components and further suppresses noise and unrelated harmonics. By combining wavelet-based multi-resolution analysis with kurtosis-based impulse sensitivity, the proposed MWKG-Net significantly improves the extraction of robust fault features under strong noise. Moreover, the model’s lightweight design makes it suitable for deployment on resource-constrained industrial platforms. Experimental results on the MFS-MG, BJTU-RAO and Urban Rail Train datasets demonstrate that, compared with state-of-the-art methods, our model maintains very high diagnostic accuracy even under extremely low signal-to-noise-ratio conditions, showcasing exceptional noise robustness, computational efficiency, and generalization capability.

title: Extended classification and generalized Vaiana–Rosati model accounting for rate-independent hysteresis loops with evolving shape
abstract: Mechanical systems and materials may exhibit rate-independent hysteretic responses that involve generalized force–displacement hysteresis loops with varying shape. With the aim of proposing a unified phenomenological modeling approach to accurately reproduce them, we first classify such hysteresis loops into four categories according to the analytical properties of their limiting curves. Subsequently, we generalize a modeling approach, recently developed by the authors, to simulate the vast majority of experimental hysteresis loops with evolving shape. The proposed approach offers both analytical and differential formulations, allows for an uncoupled modeling of the generic loading and unloading phases by employing two distinct sets of nine parameter functions having a clear mechanical meaning, and requires a straightforward computer implementation. A meticulous model validation is carried out by adopting experimental hysteresis loops retrieved from the literature. Additionally, a numerical application is performed to show the agreement between the results provided by two solution procedures that exploit the analytical and differential formulations of the model, respectively, to analyze four different mechanical systems subjected to three types of external generalized forces.

title: Physics-informed machine learning for the structural health monitoring and early warning of a long highway viaduct with displacement transducers
abstract: In Bridge Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), damage detection is often hindered by environmental and operational variability. Confounding influences such as traffic, wind, and especially temperature can significantly affect measured structural responses, making it difficult to distinguish true damage-related anomalies. This is particularly critical in the static monitoring of long steel-made viaducts, where thermal effects dominate the observed displacements, making small damage-induced perturbations almost impossible to notice in the raw data. To address this challenge, the present study introduces a predictive Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) model, aiming to establish a reliable baseline for the ‘normal conditions’ of the monitored infrastructure. This depurated baseline can then be used to properly isolate anomalies attributable to structural damage, while accounting for temperature-induced movements. The proposed grey-box approach combines data-driven modelling with physical knowledge of thermal behaviour, enhancing both accuracy and interpretability. A real-world application is demonstrated on a long-span highway viaduct, where longitudinal displacements are monitored using temperature and displacement sensors. By using only temperature and time as input variables, the model effectively captures the nonlinear effects of daily and seasonal thermal cycles without relying on additional instrumentation. Furthermore, to assess the model’s reliability, an Early Warning System (EWS) is developed, based on displacement anomaly thresholds and using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE). The PIML model is evaluated against both black-box (purely data-driven) and white-box (purely physics-based) alternatives. Damage scenarios are simulated by introducing anomalies into the experimental data to test each model's capability to detect abnormal behaviour while filtering out environmental influences. The results show that the grey-box PIML model consistently outperforms the black- and white-box approaches in terms of accuracy, robustness, and anomaly discrimination. These findings highlight the potential of PIML methods to enhance SHM practices and support the development of automated, reliable EWSs for bridge SHM.

title: A geometric-matrix method for cutting force modeling
abstract: A new digital model has been developed for predicting cutting forces of complex tool geometries. Based on the instantaneous stiffness force modeling method, this paper proposes a tool-workpiece cutting force prediction model based on a geometric matrix, taking into account the effects of vibration and curvature changes. First, by extracting the tool edge contour from pixelated images, a geometric representation method based on the tool-workpiece matrix is established, enabling the matrix description of arbitrarily complex tool geometries. Subsequently, a kinematic modeling method is introduced to account for vibration effects, covering both linear and curved motion conditions. Finally, the proposed method is validated through milling experiments, demonstrating its advantages in terms of cutting force prediction accuracy. By adopting discrete geometric modeling methods, the dynamic interaction process between complex tool geometries and the tool-workpiece system is effectively characterized.

title: Real-time estimation of states and unknown boundary conditions in pressurized pipeline systems
abstract: Accurate estimation of boundary conditions in pressurized pipelines is essential for effective monitoring, control, and fault detection. However, boundary variables such as unmeasured demands and unknown pressure heads are often unavailable, introducing uncertainty into hydraulic models. This study presents a real-time observer-based framework for joint estimation of system states and unknown boundary inputs. The approach employs the Elastic Water Column Model (EWCM) to derive a linear time-invariant (LTI) representation compatible with observer design. Because the system does not satisfy the observer matching condition, auxiliary outputs are generated to transform it into a matched form. These outputs are first estimated using a High-Gain Observer (HGO) and then incorporated into a Sliding Mode Observer (SMO) for reconstructing both states and boundary conditions. The framework is validated through two numerical case studies and laboratory experiments involving transient pipeline flows. Results demonstrate accurate real-time estimation of unknown boundary conditions using only internal pressure data. Compared with batch-based methods such as Expectation–Maximization and Weighted Least Squares, the proposed observer-based strategy provides a computationally efficient and real-time alternative for hydraulic system monitoring.

title: Zero-shot transfer learning for structural damage detection using target-to-source structure domain data mapping
abstract: In the field of structural health monitoring (SHM), transferring damage detection knowledge, e.g., parametric models trained with structural damage across different structures or damage types (namely, domains), is pivotal in addressing the reliance on gathering labeled data from test (target) structures. Recently, powerful Deep Learning models in conjunction with Transfer Learning (TL) have been explored to accommodate the process; however they still show limited generalizability across different types of structures. This paper introduces a novel approach for zero-shot TL in SHM, leveraging autoencoders to facilitate structural damage detection in the presence of limited training data. The proposed approach employs an autoencoder that maps undamaged data from the target domain to the undamaged data of the source domain. This mapping enables a damage detection model, trained exclusively on the source domain, to effectively identify anomalies in the transformed target domain data without requiring additional training or labeled target data. This unique framework allows the autoencoder to effectively capture the underlying structural characteristics by learning to map the target domain to the source domain, thereby facilitating knowledge transfer. Training an autoencoder to map from undamaged data in the target structure to undamaged data in the source structure also transfers knowledge related to damaged data. Once the autoencoder has experienced this mapping, it is leveraged to the source structure to detect any damage in the target structure. To diagnose damage, a trained one-class support vector machine is used on the source structure to identify any anomalies in the target structure. The resulting outcome of two benchmark problems underscores the efficacy of the proposed method in accurately reconstructing source domain data from target domain inputs, thereby demonstrating its potential to enhance structural damage detection using limited training data. Moreover, for the studied cases, the adaptability of the proposed approach to different structural benchmark types demonstrates a strong ability to surpass typical structural similarity requirements in TL-SHM applications. Thus, with further experiments and development, it can support the creation of SHM tools suitable for large-scale adoption.

title: Efficient identification of flutter derivatives of bridge girders at multiple reduced wind speeds based on the Bayesian spectral density approach
abstract: An efficient identification method for flutter derivatives of bridge girders at multiple reduced wind speeds from buffeting displacement responses was proposed based on the Bayesian spectral density approach. Firstly, a likelihood function based on the theoretical and measured power spectral densities (PSDs) of buffeting displacements was formulated, and the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to sample the posterior distributions of the parameters was employed. Then, the parameter estimates were determined from the maximum of the posterior probability densities, and 95% quantile bounds were provided to quantify the uncertainties of the identified flutter derivatives. Finally, by traversing the entire frequency domain of the buffeting displacement PSDs with a moving frequency window, the flutter derivatives at multiple reduced wind speeds were subsequently identified. The results show that the feasibility of the proposed method is validated through case studies on a flat plate, a single box girder section, and a double box girder section. More importantly, different from existing methods, the proposed method requires only a single wind tunnel test in turbulent flow to identify the flutter derivatives at multiple reduced wind speeds, thereby demonstrating both efficiency and practicality. The research conclusion can provide a new idea for the efficient and accurate identification of flutter derivatives of bridge girders.

title: Nonlinear dispersion properties and tunable vibration suppression in metamaterial beam with inertial amplification
abstract: Compressional-torsional coupling local resonators demonstrate prominent advantages in low-frequency vibration control through inertial amplification effects, yet their inherent narrow-band characteristics critically constrain engineering application potential. To address this limitation, this study proposes a novel compressional-torsional coupling local resonator incorporating nonlinear stiffness. Theoretical investigations reveal that the introduced nonlinear stiffness effectively extends the bandgap range of conventional linear resonators. The dynamic characteristics of the nonlinear resonator are systematically investigated using the harmonic balance method, while the excitation-amplitude-dependent bandgap properties are further elucidated through multi-scale method. A nonlinear compressional-torsional coupling local resonator prototype was designed and fabricated by implementing magnetically induced nonlinear stiffness. Experimental results verify the tunable bandgap characteristics in the nonlinear compressional-torsional coupling metamaterial beam. Furthermore, the in-situ tunability of the developed resonator was experimentally investigated. By adjusting the magnetic pole spacing, a resonance frequency shift of up to 122.9% was achieved. This work provides a highly promising solution for low-frequency broadband vibration control.

title: Decision fusion for damage localization in CFRP laminate using Lamb wave and acoustic emission
abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) structures are particularly vulnerable to barely visible impact damage during service, requiring advanced methods for assessment. This study presents a novel damage localization approach that synergistically combines Lamb wave (LW) and acoustic emission (AE) techniques through decision-level fusion. Experiment using low-velocity impacts generated complementary active LW and passive AE datasets, which were processed using Hilbert transform and envelope extraction for feature extraction. A deep learning regression model was developed to predict damage coordinates, augmented by an optimized weighted-average fusion strategy. However, due to signal distortion and sparse sensor coverage, single-modality methods suffer from degraded performance in certain regions, particularly near structural edges. Feature-level fusion struggles to reconcile the nonlinear differences between LW and AE signals, often leading to information redundancy or loss. To overcome these limitations, this work proposes a novel decision-level weighted fusion framework that leverages the complementary strengths of LW and AE while preserving their individual signal characteristics. Comparative analysis shows that the localization errors in the x and y coordinates are reduced by 41.49 % and 38.36 %, respectively, compared to single-modality methods. In the edge regions, the errors in the x and y coordinates are reduced by 18.04 % and 14.44 %, respectively. The methodology demonstrates significant potential in practical implementation in CFRP structural health monitoring systems, offering enhanced reliability for impact damage assessment.

title: Multi-view feature consistency learning for cross-domain open-set mechanical fault diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning-enabled cross-domain fault diagnosis plays a crucial role in improving the operational reliability and safety of mechanical systems. Conventional approaches usually assume that the testing data share an identical label space with the training data, implying consistent fault types across different engineering scenarios. However, in practical applications, fault types encountered during deployment are often unpredictable, and novel faults may arise, thereby undermining the effectiveness of existing domain adaptation methods. To address these challenges, a novel open-set domain adaptation framework termed multi-view feature consistency learning (MFCL) is proposed. Specifically, source-domain prototype constraints and domain-adversarial learning are jointly employed to align feature distributions between source and target domains, while multi-view contrastive learning enhances the representational quality of multi-view unlabeled target samples. Furthermore, an entropy-based adversarial separation mechanism is introduced to enable accurate identification of unknown classes during adaptation, thereby facilitating the separation between known and unknown classes. In addition, an unknown-aware consistency learning strategy is developed by integrating prototype-guided pseudo-labeling with multi-view features, which further boosts cross-domain classification performance. Extensive experiments on the SDUST and BJTU-RAO bearing datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in open-set domain adaptation and holds strong potential for enhancing the reliability of mechanical systems in practice.

title: Fast Eserogram: A novel adaptive spectrum segmentation method for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Early fault diagnosis of rolling bearings remains a critical challenge in industrial applications due to weak fault features and strong background noise interference. While the Fast Kurtogram (FK), as a classic fault diagnosis method, has been widely employed for fault detection in rotating machinery, its fixed frequency-band segmentation strategy may discard fault-related components, and conventional statistical indices often lack robustness under strong noise interferences. To overcome these challenges, a novel Fast Eserogram method for early fault detection is proposed in this paper. First, the Fourier model-fitting method is employed to extract spectral trends. Second, the local minima points of the spectral trend are integrated with a 1/3-binary tree filter bank to construct an adaptive filter group, maximizing the preservation of fault-related frequency bands. Subsequently, a robust statistical index—the Envelope Spectrum Energy Ratio (ESER) is established to evaluate the fault information richness in narrowband signals, enabling the selection of the optimal demodulation frequency band (ODFB). Finally, fault diagnosis is achieved through envelope spectrum analysis of the selected ODFB. The Fast Eserogram method exhibits superior performance to FK, Autogram, Accurgram, RCCgram and Log-cycligram in detecting early rolling bearing faults, as evidenced by experimental results.

title: Lightweight fault diagnosis for ferrography analysis of wear debris in lubricating oil
abstract: Nondestructive ferrography analysis of wear debris in lubricating oil is widely used for the fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. With the great success of deep neural networks (DNN) in computer vision, intelligent diagnosis models have been developed and proven to be effective for ferrograph images. However, strong computing power is needed, and diagnosis can hardly be done in portable computing devices due to the sophisticated structure and the large number of DNN parameters. To tackle the dilemma between model capacity and computing afford, this paper proposes a lightweight fault diagnosis model via cosine-similarity-based group pruning. First, training data are augmented by synthetic ferrograph images produced by generative adversarial networks; second, residual convolutional networks are introduced to construct the fault diagnosis model, with the input ferrograph images and the output of wear debris classification results; third, the cosine-similarity-based group pruning method is proposed for the diagnosis model based on the geometric properties between parameters. The newly proposed lightweight fault diagnosis model was validated by our labeled ferrograph images in real lubricating oil systems; compared to the unpruned model, the lightweight diagnosis model achieved a compression rate of 66.89% (from 1102KB to 682KB) with a slight accuracy decrease of 0.25% (from 99.875% to 99.625%).

title: Augmented data-driven dynamic predictive maintenance strategy for multi-state system with RUL-maintenance level trade-off
abstract: In real industrial scenarios, critical components of multi-state systems experience performance degradation as operating time accumulate. Traditional data-driven Predictive Maintenance (PdM) methods fail in improving system performance and prolonging Remaining Useful Life (RUL) due to the insufficient data and set maintenance level manually. Therefore, in this work, a novel PdM strategy is proposed for multi-state system to address these issues. A minimum discrepancy criterion-based data augmentation method is first proposed to generate high-quality realistic samples by calculating the minimum discrepancy value from pairwise comparisons in the data sequence. A Stage Transition Points (STPs) localization method is then developed to detect degradation STPs by calculating mutation values in the two-dimensional feature space. Meanwhile, an Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm-Support Vector Machine (ISSA-SVM) is constructed to adaptively identify Multi-Stage Degradation (MSD). A hierarchical RUL prediction model is subsequently customized to predict the RUL of each degradation stage. Finally, an RUL-dependent PdM model is developed to minimize the total maintenance cost and maximize the RUL-maintenance level trade-off, obtaining optimized maintenance decision-making and avoiding over- or under-maintenance. The proposed method is compared to other methods using the C-MAPSS dataset and Silicon Rod Slicing Machine (SRCM) run-to-failure industrial dataset. Comparative results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other methods in both RUL prediction and maintenance strategy.

title: Nonlinear dynamic responses of variable-thickness graphene-reinforced porous aluminum-based sandwich plate with MFC and elastic foundation
abstract: The fuselage, wings and tails of the aircraft and spacecraft are usually composed of the variable thickness thin plates as skins. Adjusting the thickness of the thin plates according to the force condition can improve the bearing capacity and reduce the weight. In the work of the aircraft, these components may be damaged by internal resonance and chaotic vibration. Therefore, in this paper, a nonlinear dynamic model of mechanical- electric-elastic coupling is established for the variable-thickness graphene-reinforced porous metal aluminum-based (VT-GRPMA) sandwich plates with the macro fiber composite (MFC) to study the nonlinear dynamic responses with delay time. The VT-GRPMA sandwich plate with the MFC is located on Winkler-Pasternak elastic foundation, with the uniform springs distributed along four edges to obtain the arbitrary elastic boundary conditions. On the inner and outer surfaces of the VT-GRPMA sandwich plate, the smart materials MFC-d31 and MFC-d33 are pasted for the sensors and actuators for the active vibration control, respectively, with the attachment positions optimized using the genetic algorithm (GA). Based on the First-order shear deformation theory (FSDT), the von Kármán strain–displacement relations and linear elastic constitutive relations, the nonlinear governing equations of motion are derived via Lagrange’s equations for the first two mode-coupled vibrations of VT-GRPMA sandwich plates. The average equations of the primary resonance and 1:2 internal resonance with the MFC delay effects are investigated by using the multiple scale method. We discuss the amplitude-frequency response curves (A-FRC), force-amplitude response curves (F-ARC), bifurcation diagrams, waveforms, phase portraits and Poincaré map of the VT-GRPMA sandwich plate under the transverse harmonic excitation. This study reveals that the introducing the velocity feedback control gain is equivalent to increasing the structural damping, while the introducing the displacement feedback gain leads new resonances, breaking the original 1:2 internal resonance condition. Further experimental investigations the plate on the elastic foundation reveal that primary resonance, secondary resonance and chaotic vibrations are observable through sweep-frequency tests. These findings provide valuable guidance for advancing vibration control strategies in plate-shell structures and optimizing practical applications of elastic-based plates.

title: Multiple wheelsets-rail dynamic interaction and its influence on rail corrugation: A perspective of elastic wave propagation
abstract: This study addresses the dynamic interaction between multiple wheelsets and the rail from the perspective of elastic wave propagation and connects it to rail corrugation. A numerical analysis model based on vehicle-track coupled dynamics theory is established and applied to three progressively advancing scenarios from simple to complex. Upon this, the systematic analyses are conducted, beginning with the characteristics of the elastic wave propagation and the corresponding dynamic interaction in the single wheelset-rail system, extending to those in the multiple wheelsets-rail system, and ultimately delving into the mutual influence of the wheelset-rail dynamic interaction when both wheelsets of the bogie are concurrently subjected to external excitation. To support these modeling and analyses, the influence of fastener constraints on the dispersion relation of elastic waves in the rail is clarified, and the wavenumber-frequency curve is obtained accordingly. Furthermore, the long-term evolution simulation maps the dynamic interaction characteristics of the multiple wheelsets-rail system onto the rail corrugation. Through the analytical framework and findings of this study, the understanding of multiple wheelsets-rail dynamic interaction and its influence on the formation of rail corrugation is enhanced, providing important theoretical support for addressing related rail corrugation issues.

title: Residual-informed deep meta regressor for predicting modal frequencies of historical masonry buildings under environmental and operational data scarcity
abstract: Dynamic monitoring of historical masonry buildings is essential for preserving architectural heritage and ensuring structural safety under varying operational and environmental conditions. Field measurements for dynamic monitoring, while invaluable, often face significant limitations including high costs, logistical challenges of masonry buildings, limited sensor coverage, and sensor malfunctions. Although machine learning-based predictive models offer promising alternatives to complement or replace in-situ monitoring, their performance is often degraded by unmeasured environmental and operational factors, resulting in reduced accuracy and uncertainty in dynamic response prediction. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel predictive method called Residual-informed Deep Meta Regressor (RiDMR) designed to forecast dynamic responses (modal frequencies) of heritage masonry buildings under partially observed environmental and/or operational conditions. The proposed RiDMR model is developed from a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network trained on a meta dataset. This meta dataset is constructed by combining measured data with residuals (prediction errors) extracted from some baseline regression models, thereby capturing hidden information of unmeasured but influential environmental/operational variables. The major innovation of this research lies in the development of a residual-informed meta learning framework that integrates statistical and deep learning models by leveraging residual learning to capture unmeasured influences, meta learning to enhance generalization under uncertainty, and hybrid learning to combine the strengths of multiple predictive approaches. Validation on a real-world historical masonry building demonstrates that the proposed RiDMR method significantly enhances prediction accuracy and generalization under unobservable and evolving environmental or operational conditions.

title: Stereo-vision-based mooring tension monitoring method for offshore floating photovoltaic platforms
abstract: Conventional mooring tension monitoring methods rely on contact sensors, which are expensive and prone to corrosion-induced failure, compromising their stability and durability for long-term monitoring. To address these limitations, this study proposes a stereo-vision-based mooring tension monitoring method for offshore floating photovoltaic (OFPV) platforms. Stereo cameras are used to capture video and identify markers mounted on the platform, from which 3D coordinates are reconstructed. The platform’s motion is then calculated to determine the spatial positions of the fairleads. Based on these positions and the known coordinates of the anchors, mooring tensions can be calculated using a quasi-static approach. A scaled physical model for the actual OFPV platform was produced, and hydrodynamic experiments on the scaled model were conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The two-chain mooring experiment confirmed the feasibility of this method, and the monitoring accuracies for fairlead position and mooring tension were approximately 97% and 95%, respectively. Moreover, the effects of camera viewing angles and perspective distortion on measurement accuracy were also examined. Based on the four-chain mooring experiment, the stability of this method was validated by successfully enabling simultaneous tension monitoring for multiple mooring lines. Experiment results indicate that the measurement accuracy exceeds 95% and 88% under moderate and extreme conditions, respectively. Compared to conventional methods, this method significantly reduces the measurement cost and implementation difficulty, and shows broad application prospects in both model testing and prototype monitoring.

title: Visual vibration measurement based on adaptive decomposition cascaded martingale difference wavelet denoising for post-processing enhancement
abstract: Video-based vibration measurement has been extensively utilized in structural health monitoring and industrial inspection due to its non-contact and full-field acquisition capabilities. However, environmental disturbances such as poor illumination and complex backgrounds often introduce substantial noise, leading to the impairment of extracted modal information and reduced accuracy in modal identification. Existing approaches largely concentrate on front-end noise suppression, which lacks robustness when faced with diverse and unpredictable noise sources. This paper presents an adaptive decomposition cascaded martingale difference wavelet denoising (ADMW) method tailored for post-processing enhancement in video vibration measurement. This method is specifically designed to address the nonlinear and non-stationary characteristics of vibration signals contaminated by noise. It applies variational mode decomposition (VMD) to decompose vibration signals, and a dynamic enhanced red-billed blue magpie optimizer (DRBMO) is developed to adaptively optimize the parameters of VMD. This method effectively enhances the ability of the optimization process to escape local optimum. Components obtained from decomposition are classified into useful, mixed, and noise components based on correlation analysis. After eliminating noise components, a cumulative martingale difference risk threshold wavelet denoising (CRW) algorithm is designed to denoise the mixed components. The final vibration signal is reconstructed by combining the denoised mixed component with the useful component. The simulation and experimental results show that the ADMW algorithm not only enhances the versatility of visual measurements but also enables the extraction of vibration signals under intensive noise interference. It improves the noise rejection ratio by 23.8%, ensuring reliable visual vibration analysis.

title: Slow and safe motion trajectory generation for final positioning support of a load considering load-sway and obstacle avoidance in large rotary crane operation
abstract: Rotary crane systems are essential for transporting heavy loads and hazardous materials. Manual operation can be challenging for new or unskilled operators. This study addresses the challenge of precise final load positioning in construction sites by proposing a trajectory generation system that integrates obstacle avoidance and load-sway suppression. A load monitor camera (LMC) captures the load environment, and the result is displayed on a user-friendly interface designed with error prevention, simplicity, and ergonomic considerations. A usability evaluation has confirmed that the interface reduces task completion time and is well accepted by novice users. The operator selects the final load position from the LMC image, after which a slow-motion trajectory is automatically generated using a cycloidal velocity profile to suppress load-sway. The A* algorithm is used for obstacle avoidance, and its efficiency has been validated through comparison with the Dijkstra algorithm. A benchmark comparison with an S-curve trajectory using trapezoidal trajectory profile has demonstrated the proposed method’s superiority in minimizing sway. Additionally, a disturbance sensitivity analysis under wind conditions has evaluated system robustness and highlights potential improvements. Simulations and lab-scale experiments have confirmed that the proposed method enables safe, smooth, and precise final positioning while avoiding obstacles.

title: MAFN: A multi-view adaptive fusion network with image and time-series signal aggregation for additive manufacturing fault diagnosis
abstract: Fault diagnosis of additive manufacturing (AM) processes is crucial for improving product quality and performance. However, existing single-view fault diagnosis methods based solely on acoustic emission (AE) signals are limited in capturing the comprehensive features of the signals. In this research, a multi-view adaptive fusion network (MAFN) is proposed, which fully combines the image and time-series features of AE signals to achieve accurate fault diagnosis. Firstly, the one-dimensional time-series signals acquired by the sensors are converted into two-dimensional image signals using gramian angular difference fields (GADF) encoding. Subsequently, adaptive convolution neural network and Mamba (ACNN-Mamba) architecture is designed to capture the global contextual information and local features of the image signals, which effectively solves the insufficient extraction of high-frequency detail features of the images. Particularly, bi-directional gated recurrent unit and global focusing mechanism (BiGRU-GF) architecture is utilized to capture bidirectional dependencies of the sequence data. In addition, a cross-view signal interaction module (CSIM) is designed, which uses an adaptive interaction strategy to dynamically adjust the weights between images and time-series features. The proposed MAFN outperforms existing single-view and multi-view methods in terms of diagnostic performance and noise robustness after experimentally validated on selective laser melting and laser directed energy deposition datasets. This study not only provides an efficient and accurate new method for fault diagnosis in AM, but also provides new ideas for the application of multi-view fusion technology in industrial equipment monitoring and maintenance.

title: An efficient method for nonlinear response analysis and identification based on pre-fitting energy functions: Application to systems with nonlinear joints
abstract: In this paper, an efficient dynamic response analysis method based on pre-fitting energy functions (PFEF) is developed for systems with nonlinear joints. This method significantly accelerates the solution process of the multi-harmonic balance method (MHBM) by calculating the residual vector and the Jacobian matrix analytically. To achieve this, the harmonic coefficients of the nonlinear force are expressed by the elastic and dissipation energy functions of the contact model of the joint interface, where the energy functions are fitted using piecewise polynomials. Then, an efficient identification method based on the PFEF is presented, where the analytical sensitivities of the harmonic coefficients of the nonlinear force are expressed by the fitted energy sensitivities of the contact model. In this way, the computational burden of the identification process is significantly reduced by calculating the sensitivity matrix analytically. In addition, two model reduction strategies are adopted, which include the exact dynamic condensation and the incremental modal expansion. A nonlinear force interpolation method (NFIM) is proposed to further reduce the dimension of the reduced order model (ROM) and the computational effort of the nonlinear force. Finally, the PFEF-based method is extended to the general nonlinear models, which has a broad prospect. A lumped parameter system, a simple FE model of the double-beam structure, and two high-fidelity FE models of the bolted assembly structures are used to demonstrate the proposed methods. Results show that, for detailed FE models, the PFEF-based solution method can significantly reduce the computation time of the nonlinear responses without loss of accuracy, and the reduction techniques can provide acceptable accuracy with less computational cost. The convergence and the efficiency of the PFEF-based identification method are discussed in detail with the experimental case study, showing the prospect of applying the proposed method to practical assembly structures.

title: European satellite benchmark for control education & industrial training — Lesson learned in the control design of a fine pointing mission
abstract: This paper presents the development of a benchmark problem for the integrated structure, control & optical design of a fine pointing mission. A baseline controller is proposed based on a preliminary robust design which takes into account several uncertainties in a model of industrial complexity. Current synthesis and analysis tools are proposed to both highlight their potential interest for academy/industry technological transfer and their limits to push future research in this promising direction. A high fidelity non-linear simulator is developed as well to show the impact of several non-linear phenomena on the line-of-sight control. In particular, the present work has the ambition to make a connection between the frequency domain and time domain analysis by revealing how validation and verification (V&V) time can be shorten with an intelligent use of the cutting edge algorithms. Moreover, the free availability of the benchmark, will help future users to propose their solution to a common shared problem or use it for other interesting research topics making use of its data.

title: Dynamic modeling and vibration analysis of ball recirculation system considering return device assembly error
abstract: This study proposes a dynamic model of the ball recirculation system (BRS) that explicitly incorporates return device assembly error (RDAE). The model captures the dynamics of the return device (RD), the nut, the balls, and the segment of the screw raceway engaged with the nut. Model predictions are validated by vibration tests on a BRS test bench; the predicted ball-pass frequency (BPF) agrees closely with the experimental measurements. We analyze the load distribution under combined loads and the transient variations of elastic forces as balls pass through the RD. Based on the modeling of RDAE, we quantify the relationship between RDAE and the BRS dynamic response, evaluate the sensitivity of the response to variations in screw rotational speed at several representative RDAE magnitudes, and analyze the impact of asymmetry in the assembly errors of the RD’s inlet and outlet on the dynamic characteristics of the BRS. The results provide guidance for optimizing high-precision, low-vibration ball screw transmission in precision grinding machines and inform the design and assembly of the RD.

title: Cross-domain prediction method for structural response of jacket platforms integrating dual-path modeling and multi-domain adaptation
abstract: As critical infrastructure for offshore oil development, jacket platforms require accurate prediction of structural mechanical responses to ensure safe operations. However, existing prediction methods face insufficient cross-domain generalization capability due to distribution discrepancies between simulation data and field measurement data. This paper proposes a mechanical response prediction method based on dual-path domain adaptation, which constructs a dual-path domain classifier architecture to achieve shallow-deep dual-branch domain feature learning and designs a multi-domain adaptation module framework that integrates innovative domain adaptation strategies, effectively addressing the knowledge transfer challenge from simulation domains to field measurement domains. The method employs adversarial feature alignment techniques to eliminate inter-domain distribution differences, utilizes adaptive weight controllers and conditional activation gating mechanisms to achieve intelligent domain adaptation strategy selection, and successfully transfers rich simulation domain knowledge to label-scarce field measurement domains, significantly improving cross-domain prediction accuracy and generalization capability. Through comprehensive validation using jacket model experiments and field measurement data from jacket platforms, the method maintains excellent predictive performance under extreme sea conditions including Typhoon “Saola,” demonstrating significant performance improvements compared to mainstream domain adaptation methods. The approach achieves full structural response prediction based on local monitoring, providing reliable technical support for structural health monitoring in marine engineering.

title: On demand design of two-dimensional phononic crystal bandgap based on machine learning and multi-objective topology optimization
abstract: To address the issue of human resource wastage and the lack of direction in phononic crystal design, this study adopts the network structures of variational autoencoder, multi-layer perceptron, and twin neural network, to achieve high-precision forward and inverse predictions for two-dimensional phononic crystals. Five-fold cross-validation was conducted on the dataset, and the resulting accuracy demonstrated the strong generalization capability and robustness of the model structures of the multi-layer perceptron and twin neural network. Specifically, 90% of the accuracy values in forward predictions are equal to or greater than 0.98, while 98% of the accuracy values in inverse predictions are no less than 0.95. From a practical design standpoint, by incorporating a loss function into the twin neural network while considering both lightweight and bandgap performance, we can achieve high-precision, on-demand design with multiple objectives. The approach and methodology presented in this study offer significant insights for the rapid and accurate development of composite or structured materials.

title: A dual-objective optimized reweighted overlapping group sparse framework integrating frequency slice function for robust bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Robust detection of incipient bearing faults remains a significant challenge in industrial environments characterized by strong background noise. This paper introduces a dual-objective optimized reweighted overlapping group sparse shrinkage (ROGSS) framework combined with frequency slice function (FSF) to enhance weak fault feature extraction. The proposed approach begins by constructing frequency slice wavelet transform (FSWT) to achieve decoupled frequency-domain representations of signal components. Subsequently, a reweighted overlapping group sparse shrinkage model is designed to suppress noise through frequency-band energy redistribution. To overcome multi-parameter optimization challenges, a dual-criteria evaluation framework integrating harmonic spectral kurtosis (HSK) and correlation Theil index (CTI) is developed, with a multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) algorithm employed for Pareto-optimal parameter selection. Validation through simulation and experimental case studies demonstrates that the proposed method significantly enhances fault-related impulse features while effectively suppressing noise, achieving 15–20% improvement in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and 30% reduction in root mean square error (RMSE) compared to state-of-the-art techniques. The approach establishes a novel spectral analysis framework for weak fault detection, providing superior performance in feature enhancement and diagnostic reliability under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions.

title: Simulation of near-fault strong ground motion with generative adversarial network
abstract: This paper proposes a generative adversarial network (GAN) for feature extraction and simulation generation of seismic data. Specifically, a Wasserstein-distance-based GAN model has been adopted using the well-acknowledged NGA-West2 ground motion American database of the Pacific Earthquake Engineering Research Center (PEER). Notably, this study adopts multi-dimensional convolution/deconvolution to extract and reconstruct multi-dimensional features from one-dimensional data, ensuring the generated data exhibit required features simultaneously. The validity and diversity of the generated data are verified by four aspects, such as time–frequency power spectrum, data similarity, and seismic intensity parameter distribution map. The results show that the generated data by the proposed method have good and diverse features and waveforms.

title: NDE 4.0: The confluence of cutting-edge nondestructive inspection practices, data fusion techniques, artificial intelligence, and cyber-physical systems for effective evaluation of materials and structures
abstract: The fourth industrial revolution (Industry 4.0) has transformed manufacturing by integrating machines, materials, and human inputs through advanced operational and information technologies. This transformation has likewise reshaped nondestructive evaluation (NDE), giving rise to NDE 4.0. This new paradigm is enabled by key technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital twins (DTs), automation, smart/cognitive sensors, and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). These technologies enhance quality assurance, streamline workflows, enable real-time data-driven decision-making, and facilitate intelligent asset management. While NDE 4.0 is continuously transforming traditional practices, critical sectors such as aerospace, energy, and biomedical imaging still rely on conventional NDE methods, which struggle with scalability, data silos, and insufficient real-time analytics. To address these gaps, this paper offers a comprehensive strategic review and a forward-looking roadmap for advancing NDE 4.0 toward NDE 5.0. It synthesizes state-of-the-art developments while proposing a data-centric framework that integrates evolving DT technologies (from static to dynamic multi-tiered systems), autonomous inspection platforms, and hybrid data-fusion methods. Practical deployment challenges such as workforce skill gaps, cybersecurity, sustainability, and regulatory standardization, are examined alongside transformative emerging technologies such as terahertz sensing, quantum techniques, robotics and drones, augmented and virtual reality-assisted frameworks, blockchain, and big-data analytics. Recognizing the importance of ethical AI and open-science principles, this study advocates for a cohesive, globally standardized approach to accelerate NDE 4.0 adoption. Looking ahead, this work envisions NDE 5.0 as a synergistic human-machine ecosystem featuring self-learning, autonomous inspection systems that deliver enhanced reliability, safety, and efficiency across industries.

title: A review of industrial full-matrix imaging methods through ultrasonic bulk waves
abstract: The ultrasonic phased array assembles multiple transducer elements into one system, greatly increasing the detection coverage and allowing for high-resolution imaging of reflectors. In recent years, full matrix imaging has gained its prominence in the development of ultrasound detection technology because of its comprehensive information, flexible imaging and efficient detection. In this review, the scope is focused on ultrasonic imaging methods targeting industrial products and manufacturing processes. The effectiveness of full-matrix imaging strongly depends on the imaging method, which is grounded in the wave propagation behavior of the measurement structure. The theoretical frame of the imaging methods is composed of wavefield reconstruction and imaging condition. The former reconstructs the wavefield in the measurement region through full wave equations, Green function, or one-way equation, and this step determines the imaging accuracy and efficiency, while the latter processes the wavefields to yield the imaging results. The existing wavefield reconstruction methods are compared through two simulation models, wherein the effects of spatial and temporal factors are investigated. Moreover, the existing full-matrix imaging methods are grouped into four categories according to the imaging theory, namely total focusing method, phase shift migration, time-reversal method and reverse time migration, wherein the characteristics and development directions are summarized. In addition, the relationship between full-matrix imaging methods and those for other ultrasonic acquisition modalities is also analyzed. Furthermore, the industrial application and technical gaps of full-matrix imaging methods are discussed and analysed. This review is expected to provide strong technical support in full-matrix imaging methods.

title: Temperature-compensated baseline signal reconstruction of ultrasonic guided wave via local matching and non-negative elastic net regression
abstract: Pipeline structures are widely used in petrochemical and other industries. Over time, pipelines are prone to damage, leading to economic losses and safety risks. Ultrasonic guided wave (UGW) structural health monitoring is an effective method for detecting such damage. However, environmental factors such as temperature variations affect UGW propagation, reducing monitoring performance. This paper proposes a baseline signal reconstruction method based on local matching and non-negative elastic network regression (LM-NNEN) to compensate for temperature effects. First, a sliding time window is applied to capture local UGW signals. A matching matrix combining dot product and cross-correlation delay is proposed to optimally match the local baseline signal matrix with the test signal. Then, a two-step processing method is designed based on signal strength to determine the regularization parameters for NNEN regression, and the coefficient vector was used to reconstruct the baseline signal. The damage index indicates the presence of damage, and the damage location is determined by calculating the scattered signal envelope. Monitoring data from a 9.2 m pipeline segment under natural temperature fluctuations verify the LM-NNEN method’s effectiveness in temperature compensation and damage identification. Two damage defects were created and each subjected to growth processing separately. The results show that the LM-NNEN method offers improved temperature compensation during the monitoring period and accurately identifies damage. The maximum average localization error for both defects is 0.043 m, with a standard deviation of 0.006.

title: Complex-valued mixture generalized modified Blake–Zisserman algorithm for widely linear active noise control system
abstract: Currently, the conventional active noise control (ANC) system has been extensively studied, and a rich number of robust algorithms for ANC system have been successively introduced. However, in the realm of complex-valued signals, there is still a lack of an appropriate ANC system to cope with it. To counteract this constraint, a widely linear active noise control (WL-ANC) system is designed in our work. Then, we propose the widely linear filtered-x complex-valued mixture generalized modified Blake–Zisserman (WL-FxCMGMBZ) algorithm for WL-ANC system. WL-FxCMGMBZ employs the complex-valued mixture generalized modified Blake–Zisserman (CGMBZ) loss function as its cost function and exhibits remarkable noise control capability. We also develop the variable step-size widely linear filtered-x complex-valued normalized mixture generalized modified Blake–Zisserman (VSS-WL-FxCNMGMBZ) algorithm to enhance the performance of WL-FxCMGMBZ. The mean convergence, mean-square steady-state performance, and computational complexity analysis are presented for theoretical analysis. Finally, extensive simulations are conducted to demonstrate the superior noise control capability of WL-FxCMGMBZ and VSS-WL-FxCNMGMBZ in various signal scenarios.

title: A Neural Network-Assisted Boussinesq pressure bulb model for load assessment of cylindrical rolling element bearings
abstract: • A NN-assisted pressure bulb model was proposed for load assessment of roller bearings. • The accuracy of the Boussinesq pressure bulb model was investigated. • Two NNs were integrated into the model to enhance accuracy. • High accuracy was validated through simulations and experiments. The accurate assessment of contact forces and radial load is critical for the performance and reliability of the cylindrical rolling element bearings. The current theoretical models based on Hertzian theory are challenging since the deformation is relatively small to measure, and installing sensors on the contact area is difficult. This paper introduced the Boussinesq pressure bulb model for bearing load assessment and found that the original model had a maximum of 33% error because it did not consider the boundary effects and material properties. To improve accuracy, a Neural Network-assisted Boussinesq model is proposed by integrating two Neural Networks (NNs) with the original Boussinesq model. The first NN accurately transfers strain measurements from Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) optical sensors into stresses at the point of interest, while measuring strain is easier in practical applications. The second NN provides an accurate tuning factor to address errors in the original model. The NN-assisted Boussinesq model greatly outperforms the original model and shows an error below 3.73%. The performance of the proposed model is validated through simulations and experiments. In simulations, errors were below 1% when the outer race and housing were made of the same material, 6.7% for a GCr15 steel outer race with a spheroidal graphite iron housing, and 11.6% for a GCr15 steel outer race with a grey cast iron housing; the latter remains acceptable for non-precision applications. In experiments, radial load estimation errors were below 3% in static tests and 4.6% in dynamic tests. All these simulations and experiments demonstrated the superiority of the proposed method. Moreover, it is practical and easy to implement in real-time bearing stress and load measurements.

title: An efficient inverse design framework of manufacturable phononic metaplates via combining generative deep learning and Bayesian latent space exploration
abstract: While deep learning (DL) techniques emerge as powerful tools for inverse designs of phononic metamaterials, prevailing DL-driven approaches heavily rely on predicting structure–property relationship that is very time-consuming in data collection and model training. Moreover, most reported methodologies have only been conceptually validated in numerical models of 2D planar phononic crystals (PnCs), with limited implementation in practical, manufacturable metastructures. In this study, we present a prediction-free framework to efficiently design manufacturable phononic metaplates via a combination of generative DL model and Bayesian space exploration strategy. The generative DL model is used to construct the design space and encode unit cell patterns into low-dimensional latent vectors. Thereafter, Bayesian optimization is employed to efficiently search for desirable structures in the encoded latent space, where unit cells satisfying user-customized dispersion properties can be discovered after a small set of iterations. Band gap properties of inversely designed metaplates are demonstrated by the experimentally measured wave transmission. Our developed framework greatly enhances the design efficiency of manufacturable metaplates and is generalizable to 2D metamaterials.

title: Constitutive modeling and reliability evaluation of interfacial slip damage in three-dimensional stacked micro/nano-scale through-silicon vias
abstract: Micro/nano-interconnect structures are critical components in three-dimensional high-density packaging, yet their reliability is critically constrained by the copper pumping effect induced by the thermal mismatch between copper and silicon. This study investigates interfacial failure at the copper/silicon interface in through-silicon via (TSV) composite structures. Based on continuum damage mechanics, a constitutive relation for interfacial slip is established using energy dissipation as a damage indicator. The reliability under thermoelectrical coupling is evaluated, and the model is further applied to analyze thermal residual stress and strain in common liner materials. A Bayesian support vector regression (BSVR) model is integrated into a cross-entropy-based framework for failure probability assessment. Within this framework, importance sampling is employed to optimize BSVR hyperparameter selection, while BSVR serves as a surrogate to reduce computational cost in constitutive simulations. To address the analytical intractability of the marginal likelihood integral in BSVR, a simulation-based sampling method is proposed as an alternative to Laplace approximation. The proposed computational framework effectively combines the advantages of cross-entropy methods and BSVR surrogate modeling in handling high-dimensional problems with small failure probabilities, thereby mitigating efficiency degradation caused by data sparsity and complex failure domains.

title: Thermal error mechanism modeling of motorized spindle systems: Coupled modeling of internal and external heat source components and thermal deformation transfer mechanism
abstract: To address the thermal error issue, this study proposes a method of thermal error mechanism modeling for motorized spindle systems. First, informed by structural configuration and heat conduction analysis, the internal assembly of the spindle is divided into internal and external heat source components. Thermal conduction equations are respectively formulated for each component type, enabling transient temperature field prediction for both the internal and external heat source components. Next, based on thermoelastic theory, the thermal deformation of each component under temperature rise is determined in the non-assembled state. Then, considering the interference stress induced by thermal deformation at the contact surfaces in the assembled state, further thermal deformation is analyzed under the influence of this stress, enabling the prediction of spindle system thermal error. The predictive capability of the developed mechanism model for spindle temperature distribution and thermally induced errors is verified through both numerical simulations and experimental validation. In contrast to conventional techniques, the proposed framework facilitates an analytical description of thermal behavior within the spindle systems, enabling a systematic investigation into the deformation mechanism and thermal characteristics, thereby markedly improving the precision and robustness of prediction outcomes.

title: Research on the cage rotational stability of high-speed precision special ball bearing based on the visual trajectory capture method
abstract: Cage rotational stability serves as a critical indicator of lubrication performance and operation status in high-speed precision ball bearings, directly impacting the operational reliability and service life of both the bearing and the overall mechanical system. Addressing the limitations of existing methods, hindered by the bearing’s complex structure and the lack of effective evaluation metrics, this study proposes an image-based method for analyzing cage centroid trajectories. First, a transfer learning network integrating unsupervised domain adaptation, synergistic attention mechanism, adaptive pseudo-label generation mechanism and weak-strong augmentation mechanism, is proposed to achieve trajectory recognition. Subsequently, the Fast Fourier Transform extracts the cage whirling error. Based on error sources, the non-repeatable run-out, which reflects rotational stability, is isolated and quantified. Finally, a novel metric, the box dimension number, was proposed. It can simultaneously capture the irregularity of the trajectory, which reflects the smoothness of motion, and the degree of space filling, which indicates the amplitude of the whirl motion. It was applied in experiments investigating the effects of multiple influencing factors, including rotational speed, load, lubrication condition, and wear degree. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieved cross-operational-condition micrometer-level trajectory recognition, and the proposed metric significantly enhances the depth and precision of the evaluation, providing a robust theoretical foundation for studying the bearing performance degradation patterns, optimizing the structural parameters and material properties of the cage, and advancing lifespan prediction research.

title: Ultrasonic signal decomposition through gradient descent assisted successive parameter estimation
abstract: Accurate decomposition of ultrasonic signals into simple pulses is valuable both for data compression purposes, as well as various medical and engineering applications. This work proposes a matching pursuit (MP) based algorithm that deploys a traditional successive parameter estimation approach, to express ultrasonic signals as sums of Gaussian pulses or chirplets. However, here the MP algorithm is aided by mathematical optimisation (gradient descent), which allows for significantly more precise parameter estimation. Our method is validated on simple input signals, and following its validation, its performance is assessed against cases of increasing complexity. The results not only suggest the accuracy and robustness of our approach, but also show how the proposed method performs well with signals containing strongly overlapping pulses, a challenge for existing methods. Results are also obtained from realistic signals generated through finite element modelling or experimental measurements. Finally, beyond the reconstruction results, we discuss and demonstrate how even complicated signals are well described through only a few parameters, eliminating the need for storing full time traces, allowing for effective ultrasonic data compression. • Accurate decomposition of signals into sums of Gaussian pulses or chirplets. • Achieved via gradient descent assisted matching pursuit algorithm. • Process initialised via established grid search approach, avoiding local minima. • Achieved good results for challenging cases, without manual input. • Adaptable to decomposition into pulses other than Gaussian or chirplets.

title: Research on a disk-type piezoelectric balancing actuator for rotor dynamic balancing
abstract: This paper presents a novel disk-type, dual-sided piezoelectric actuator integrated with a Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) strategy for real-time rotor dynamic balancing in magnetically sensitive or space-constrained environments. The actuator exploits ninth-order out-of-plane vibration modes excited via segmented piezoceramic rings to generate high-resolution traveling waves that drive dual compensation masses. This compact system offers magnetic immunity, strong self-locking capability, and fast dynamic response. A dynamic model of the actuator–rotor system is developed, and a feedforward adaptive control law is implemented to suppress residual imbalance. Simulation results confirm stable excitation of the target mode and effective vibration attenuation across a range of gain parameters. Quantitative evaluations using the Integral of Time-weighted Absolute Error (ITAE) and Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) show that lower control gains yield faster convergence and improved steady-state performance. Experimental validation on a custom rotor test platform demonstrates that the actuator delivers up to 0.21 N·m torque under 300 Vp-p excitation and reduces vibration amplitudes by over 74 % within 6 s under both variable- and fixed-speed conditions. The proposed approach provides a compact, efficient, and robust solution for online rotor balancing, offering strong potential for deployment in aerospace, precision manufacturing, and embedded electromechanical systems.

title: Physics inspired sparse deconvolution network for dispersion compensation of terahertz wave
abstract: Terahertz (THz) technique, as a rising nondestructive testing (NDT) approach, has emerged great potentials in the nondestructive assessment of various non-metallic materials due to its high time resolution and penetrability. However, the dispersion effect of THz wave during propagation process can cause the broadening, overlap and distortion of THz response signal, which brings a significant challenge for accurate extraction of time-of-flight (ToF) information of structure. The present methods mainly rely on traditional signal processing techniques to improve the estimation accuracy of ToF from the signal, rather than focus on the effects of dispersion on detection resolution. Also, such methods are usually limited by the sophisticated manual interventions and the requirements of prior knowledge of structure, which may fail for complex signals from multilayer structure. Therefore, in this work, a physics inspired sparse deconvolution network is specially proposed for the dispersion compensation of the signal. The core aims to utilize the sparse deconvolution network to address the sparse inverse problem in THz testing, and establish the mapping relationship between dispersive signal and sparse impulse vector corresponding to ToF. Initially, an improved physical transmission model is established based on the dispersion characteristics of the wave. Subsequently, the sparse deconvolution network is specially constructed to obtain ToF information based on THz detection mechanism. Then, the dispersion compensation process can be performed by convoluting the estimated ToF with the THz reference signal. During this process, to improve the dispersion compensation performance, the progressive curriculum weighted loss (PCW-Loss) and the amplitude-position joint error (APJE) metric is designed for the optimal performance. Finally, a series of numerical simulations and experiments, including the single-layer and multi-layer structures, are implemented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Overall, the proposed method is the first attempt to solve the dispersion issue of the signal by sparse deconvolution network, and can provide a novel insight and solution for the accurate and automatic ToF estimation in various THz NDT scenarios.

title: Interpretable compound fault diagnosis of hydraulic gear pumps via fusion of physical priors and probabilistic joint reasoning
abstract: The external gear pump is susceptible to coupled degradation involving multiple faults under complex operating conditions, which poses considerable challenges to fault diagnosis. However, existing methods generally lack interpretability and the capability to quantify uncertainty in compound fault modeling, which limits their reliability in practical applications. To address this issue, this paper proposes a three-stage compound fault diagnosis framework.
