The framework sequentially employs a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to invert key structural parameters under unlabeled conditions, a Bayesian Neural Network (BNN) to model parameter distributions and perform uncertainty reasoning, and a lightweight Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) based on the statistical features output by the BNN to accomplish fault classification. Using seven typical fault datasets obtained from an Electro-Hydrostatic Actuator (EHA) experimental platform, the results demonstrate that the proposed method substantially outperforms baseline models such as Transformer and 1D-CNN in terms of overall accuracy and compound fault recognition. It also maintains high robustness under small-sample and high-noise conditions, and exhibits promising generalization capability in partially labeled and unknown fault recognition tasks, providing a feasible path toward transparent and interpretable fault diagnosis under complex working conditions.

title: MLFNet: A novel multi-level fusion mechanical fault diagnosis network under limited and imbalanced datasets using multi-source information
abstract: With the continuous improvement of the Internet of Things and sensing technology, it is becoming easier to obtain multi-source information from different types of sensors. In multi-source information fusion (MSIF), three types of fusion, including data-level, feature-level, and decision-level are crucial for bridging the multi-source information and final fault diagnosis. However, most existing intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD)-based methods use only a single type and ignore the other two types, which makes high-quality features contained in the multi-source information extracted by the deep learning methods incomplete. Meanwhile, IFD under limited and imbalanced (L&I) datasets is a challenging and important issue for practical industrial applications owing to the complex and harsh operating conditions. Most importantly, the current MSIF-based methods still have defects in three types of fusion. To tackle these issues simultaneously, a multi-level fusion network based on multi-source information (MLFNet) is presented to enable three types of fusion in a unified deep network and achieving fault diagnosis under L&I conditions. In the data-level, a signal preprocessing technique is first employed to obtain RGB images from multi-source signals. In the feature-level, dynamic multiscale feature extraction (DMFE) is built to select the appropriate feature scale and hierarchical feature fusion network (HFFN) is proposed to mine the shallow and deep features, which not only solves the unreliability problem of fixed feature scale but also acquires more representative and complementary features. In the decision-level, dual classifiers are used to produce more accurate diagnostic results under L&I datasets. Extensive experiments conducted on four datasets show the validity and dominance of our proposed method for fault diagnosis under L&I conditions, which outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in this article.

title: Fourier-Laplace based semi-analytical solution and optimization for vehicle and infinite-length road interaction
abstract: The coupled dynamics between vehicles and deformable roads represents a fundamental moving load problem (MLP) that is theoretically significant for improving vehicle performance and guiding road design. However, accurately modeling infinite-length roads and obtaining the responses of the vehicle-infinite-length-road interaction (VIRI) system remain the major challenges that limit effective suspension optimization for vehicles. To address this issue, this study introduces a moving coordinate framework for the VIRI system and proposes a semi-analytical approach using Fourier and Laplace transforms. Cauchy’s residue theorem is applied to derive the system responses from the transformed equations. Under sinusoidal and random road profiles, comparisons show that the peak error using the proposed method is 3.03 %, and the root mean square error remains below 1.88 % compared to those in existing literature and calculated by the modal superposition method. The effects of key parameters including vehicle speed, mass ratio, suspension stiffness, damping, and road roughness, are then systematically investigated, laying the foundation for suspension optimization. Parametric analysis shows that an optimal suspension stiffness enhances both ride comfort and road friendliness, whereas excessive damping amplifies vehicle acceleration and interaction forces. A genetic algorithm is applied to optimize suspension stiffness and damping for enhanced ride comfort, handling, and tire–road contact. The objective fitness function converges well, yielding significant reductions in vertical acceleration (53.8 %), interaction force (66.38 %), and pavement deformation (73.24 %), with a moderate improvement in vertical displacement (11.56 %). This paper presents an innovative framework for accurately calculating the responses of a VIRI system that considers road roughness with suspension optimization, offering an analytical method for the MLP and providing valuable insights into the theoretical analysis of vehicle–road interaction.

title: A novel clustering based curvature method with wavelet transform for detecting progressive damage of simply supported ultra-high performance fiber-reinforced concrete beams using laser scanner vibrometer
abstract: Monitoring the structural performance of Ultra-High-Performance Fiber-Reinforced Concrete (UHPFRC) beams is essential for understanding damage progression and improving long-term durability in advanced structural elements. This study presents a novel reference-free clustering-based algorithm that leverages high spatial resolution and higher vibrational modes obtained using a laser scanning vibrometer (LSV) during a progressive damage test on UHPFRC. In the experimental phase, the vibrational behavior of a 2-meter one-span simply-supported UHPFRC beam was measured by laser scanning vibrometry under progressively increasing damage levels. Two different reference-free damage detection methods are developed and compared. In the first method, the curvature is calculated using the central difference approximation, and a clustering-based algorithm combining LoOP outlier detection with locally weighted nonparametric regression fitting using a second-order polynomial (LOESS) is applied to construct an intact baseline directly from the damaged data. In the second method, a wavelet-based curvature formulation is introduced to overcome the noise sensitivity and boundary effects inherent in central difference schemes. Both approaches are evaluated for their ability to identify damage zone characteristics, such as position and severity, and are validated through finite element simulations where strain energy variation is used as a numerical severity index.

title: PGVAE-VBAKF: A robust strategy for complex system response prediction and noise variance estimation considering modeling errors and nonstationary noises
abstract: Accurate system response prediction is essential in understanding the latent physics and assessing the performance, safety, and durability of structures. Although numerous model- and data- based methods have been developed for structural response prediction, the combined effects of modeling errors and time-varying measurement noises can significantly reduce the response prediction accuracy. To address this issue, the present study proposes a Physics-Guided Variational Auto-Encoder with Variational Bayesian Adaptive Kalman Filter (PGVAE-VBAKF) strategy for complex system response prediction and noise variance estimation. First, to mitigate the impact of modeling errors on complex system learning, this study proposes a PGVAE-based approach that integrates state-space modeling with neural networks. This method enhances the accuracy of response modeling for complex systems. Compared to data-driven methods, the proposed PGVAE-based approach can significantly reduce the relative root mean square error (RRMSE) of response prediction. Second, this study employs a well-trained PGVAE to replace the transition and observation models in the Kalman filter, which can effectively mitigate the influence of inaccurate system matrices and yield precise response estimation. Third, to handle nonstationary noises, this study integrates PGVAE with VBAKF to enable effective response estimation for complex systems subject to modeling errors and nonstationary noises, which can quantify time-varying noise variances. Furthermore, a model reduction strategy that integrates PGVAE with Z-score normalization, modal superposition, and residual neural network is proposed to improve the training efficiency and high-dimensional system learning accuracy. Numerical and experimental studies are implemented to validate the performance of the proposed method. Research results show that the proposed method can accurately predict the complex system response and quantify the uncertainty of noise variances. The proposed method can effectively mitigate the combined adverse effects of modeling errors and nonstationary noises for complex system learning and has the potential to be applied for structural health monitoring (SHM) of complex nonlinear structures.

title: An UDA bearing fault diagnosis method based on synergistic optimization of unbalanced data
abstract: Aiming at the problems of unbalanced cross-domain generalizability features difficult to be learned, unbalanced category distribution, and biased classification probability in the unsupervised domain adaptive (UDA) bearing fault diagnosis methods under unbalanced data, an UDA bearing fault diagnosis method based on synergistic optimization of unbalanced data is proposed. Firstly, this method designs a multi-mechanism synergistic feature extractor, including multi-domain feature adaptation extractor (MDFAE)and multi-domain feature interaction enhancer (MDFIE). MDFAE realizes feature weight balance between majority class samples and minority class samples through fixed correction layer and dynamic correction layer, and further extracts unbalanced cross-domain generalizability features. MDFIE designs an encoder-decoder structure to realize deep mining of complex association patterns and adaptive calibration of key features in the initial feature space output by MDFAE with a two-dimensional dynamic capturing mechanism across channels and time series. Secondly, this paper proposes a Multi-Level Joint Distribution Alignment (MLJDA) mechanism. Through a dual-stage collaborative framework combining global structural alignment and local semantic alignment, it systematically addresses domain distribution bias in unbalanced data and cross operational scenarios. Global structural alignment corrects overall cross domain distribution differences to mitigate data unbalance effects, while local semantic alignment matches fine-grained feature clusters to weaken semantic misalignment caused by operational variations. Finally, the SI-Softmax function is designed for classification output to transform the correlation between feature vectors and weight vectors into an angle-based cosine similarity relationship, and transforms hard labels as soft labels through label smoothing to prevent the model from overly favoring the majority class, and introduces hyperparameters k and m to dynamically adjust the decision boundary, it significantly enhances the discrimination capability for fault categories and reduces probability bias. Using the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) bearing dataset, roller gear dataset and wind power bearing dataset for experimental verification, the results show that the proposed method has better ability to balance the weights of normal samples and fault samples under crossing operating conditions.

title: Variational and approximated Bayesian updating with data-driven autoencoder and homotopy eigenpair expansions
abstract: The variational inference is frequently employed in Bayesian updating framework to enable efficient estimation of the posterior distribution. To enhance its efficiency and adaptability in uncertain and high-dimensional applications, this study proposes a variational Bayesian model updating method that integrates Homotopy Stochastic Finite Element Method (HSFEM) into the architecture of Variational Autoencoder (VAE). A deep neural network is set as the encoder to be optimized, and HSFEM is used as the decoder to estimate the likelihood function through Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC), thus obtaining explicit expression of Evidence Lower BOund (ELBO). The posterior distribution can be efficiently approximated by maximizing the ELBO. In this architecture, the Bhattacharyya distance is introduced as the distance metric in ABC to ensure a precise quantification of the likelihood function; Gaussian kernel based binning technology is used to construct a derivable Probability Mass Function (PMF) of the distribution, reducing the calculation cost of estimation of probability density with certain accuracy. The proposed approach also addresses the potential complexity of the ‘two-step procedures’ when employing both the Euclidian distance and Bhattacharyya distance as metrics in two separate steps. Two numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method, as well as its advantages in facing high-dimensional problems. Finally, the proposed method was applied to update a lab-scale aircraft model, yielding satisfactory results and demonstrating its practical value for engineering applications.

title: Identification of fluid-borne and structure borne vibration sources from displacement measurements in immersed beams
abstract: We investigate an inverse source problem in a coupled fluid–structure interaction (FSI) framework, in which a compressible fluid occupies a rectangular domain bounded below by an elastic Euler–Bernoulli beam. The system is excited by two unknown spatial sources with known time dependence: one acting in the fluid, the other on the beam. We aim to determine both spatial components from partial measurements of the beam displacement over a finite time interval. The mathematical model consists of a coupled system of wave and beam equations with appropriate interface and boundary conditions. We establish a uniqueness result for the recovery of the source pair from restricted observations. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical findings, highlighting the role of a minimal observation time and the sensitivity of the reconstruction to noise in the data. These results contribute to the mathematical understanding of inverse problems in vibroacoustics and provide a foundation for practical applications such as structural health monitoring and source localization.

title: Application and analysis of MUSIC algorithm for anomaly detection in microwave imaging without a switching device
abstract: Although the MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm has demonstrated suitability as a microwave imaging technique for detecting anomalies, there is a fundamental limit that it requires a switching device to be used which permits an antenna to transmit and receive signals simultaneously. In this paper, we design a MUSIC-type imaging function using scattering parameter data to find small anomaly and explore its mathematical structure. Considering the investigated structure, we confirm that the imaging performance is highly dependent on the antenna configurations and suggest an arrangement of antennas to enhance imaging performance. Simulation results with synthetic data are displayed to support theoretical result.

title: Identification of the Silverbox benchmark using extended polynomial kernel-based nonlinear observer canonical models
abstract: This work presents new results on the Silverbox nonlinear system identification benchmark problem which has already been considered by many methods. For the Silverbox benchmark, we propose the extended polynomial kernel-based nonlinear observer canonical form (K-NOCF) model and estimate its parameters using a genetic algorithm-based concurrent estimation (GA-CE) method. The GA-CE method searches the initial parameter set that minimizes the output estimation error, such that convergence to the optimal or near-optimal solution without trial and error for initial parameter values is achieved. The results obtained on the Silverbox problem are discussed and compared with all previously published results. Compared to earlier published results, the presented modeling and estimation approach achieves the best compromise between model accuracy for both estimation and validation data and complexity.

title: State Space Kriging model for emulating nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems with parameter uncertainty
abstract: We extend our recently proposed state space Kriging (S2K) model [12], which approximates the system dynamics in state space with a sparse Kriging surrogate, to deal with system parameter uncertainty. We propose and investigate two methods. 1) A two-step method that employs the standard S2K model to approximate the conditional state space representation given a series of realizations of the uncertain system parameters. The surrogate model for arbitrary system parameter values is then approximated by interpolation. 2) A one-step method that represents the random system parameters by pseudo stochastic processes. This allows the direct application of the S2K framework to approximate the state space representation with uncertain system parameters. We numerically compare the performance of the two S2K methods with the state-of-the-art PC-NARX model for emulating the response of complex nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems. The results indicate that S2K results in more accurate predictions while reducing the required number of input training time histories by two orders of magnitude relative to PC-NARX.

title: Identification of weak cyclostationary fault features in rotating machinery under aliasing interference and non-Gaussian noise
abstract: Recently, cyclostationary analysis has gained significant attention in mechanical fault diagnosis, as it has been proven that vibration signals from faulty rotating machinery often exhibit second-order cyclostationarity. However, in practical applications, the complex transmission paths and harsh operating conditions make the vibration signals susceptible to aliasing interference and non-Gaussian impulsive noise. As a result, the second-order cyclostationarity associated with fault is weak and difficult to detect. To address this issue, a blind adaptive frequency-shift filtering algorithm based on the generalized maximum Versoria criterion (GMVC-based BA-FRESH) is proposed to accurately extract fault feature signals. This algorithm can extract the desired cyclostationary signal from spectrally overlapping interference without prior statistical knowledge of the reference signal. The generalized maximum Versoria criterion ensures the robustness of the algorithm against noise, particularly non-Gaussian impulsive noise caused by outliers. Additionally, to further improve performance, a variable step-size strategy and an adaptive moment estimation (Adam) optimizer are incorporated into the algorithm. By integrating the proposed algorithm with a blind cyclic frequency detection technique, a robust method is developed for detecting weak cyclostationary fault features in rotating machinery under aliasing interference and non-Gaussian noise. The mean-sense and mean-square-sense convergence of the algorithm are subsequently derived for the baseline update, with the Adam variant presented as an optional heuristic. Its performance is comprehensively evaluated using the representative cyclostationary signal model from four perspectives: effectiveness, noise robustness, method comparison, and key parameter influence. Finally, its applicability for fault diagnosis in rotating machinery is validated through two engineering case studies involving industrial centrifugal pumps and rolling-element bearings.

title: Non-smooth cantilever-type piezoelectric vibration energy harvester: Experimental study and global dynamic response
abstract: This paper proposes and designs a new non-smooth cantilever-type piezoelectric vibration energy harvester with oblique springs as well as bilateral elastic and rigid stoppers (NSCPVEH). The design innovations that significantly improve the energy harvesting performance are: (i) The simultaneous introduction of two different types of impact effects as well as non-smooth and nonlinear characteristics via impacts between the cantilever beam and bilateral stoppers; (ii) The introduction of geometric nonlinearity via a pair of oblique springs. The multi-mechanism collaboration formed by these introductions can promote the better balance between bandwidth and power. Based on the vibration experiments of the NSCPVEH prototypes with nine different setups of stoppers, the electricity generation performance and the operational bandwidth are tested, studied and compared. Experimental results demonstrate that the NSCPVEH, equipped with the top and bottom elastic stoppers as well as the top and bottom rigid stoppers of 35 mm height, achieves a bandwidth of 7.4 Hz and a power of 0.95 mW at a base acceleration of 0.6 g. This performance represents a 362.5% increase in the bandwidth compared to the NSCPVEH without any stoppers under the same conditions. Moreover, power tests and a demonstration in which 17 LEDs are successfully illuminated fully attest to the corresponding performance and practical application potential. The performance comparison of the NSCPVEH with 10 other recently reported energy harvesters is also provided to justify its innovations. In addition, for the parametric study and the dynamic response analysis, the electromechanical coupling model corresponding to the NSCPVEH is established, experimentally validated, theoretically and numerically investigated. Specifically, the global bifurcation and chaotic dynamics are analyzed using the piecewise approximation method and the new non-smooth Melnikov method. The theoretical innovation is that we extend the classical Melnikov method of smooth systems to make it applicable for analyzing this new NSCPVEH that combines nonlinearity, non-smoothness and impacts. The response under different impact effects is analyzed using the global approximation method, the averaging method and the stochastic averaging method of energy envelope, respectively. Overall, the rich experimental, theoretical and numerical results provide strong support for the design and analysis of future broadband vibration energy harvesters.

title: Minimum probability transition improved GMM modeling and reliable damage imaging method under changing time-varying conditions
abstract: Reliable damage monitoring of aircraft structures under time-varying environment is an important step toward the real engineering applications of structural health monitoring (SHM). Combining Gaussian mixture model (GMM) with guided wave (GW) array based imaging has proved to be an effective and promising strategy in suppressing the time-varying environment caused uncertain influence on GW signals and realizing accurate damage localization. However, a major concern is that this strategy needs to build baseline GMM and monitoring GMM under the same time-varying environmental range, which limits its application. Aiming at this issue, this paper proposes a novel minimum probability transition based updating method of the GW feature sample set when building the monitoring GMM. The proposed method is capable of overcoming the probability modal shift in probability distribution of healthy samples by taking a nearest-sample updating mechanism, and preserving damaged samples during the updating process by adopting a minimum probability update threshold. With the proposed method, the damage information can be effectively preserved while the environmental range caused influence can be suppressed, when updating GW feature sample set and building monitoring GMM, resulting in accurate and reliable damage monitoring. To validate this method, experimental research is conducted on a typical aircraft structure under temperature variation from −50 °C to 80 °C. Different temperature ranges are adopted when building baseline GMM and monitoring GMM, cracks and loosen bolts are all located accurately, the maximal localization error is less than 1.0 cm. Compared with the conventional GMM and GW based damage imaging method, the monitoring results have been significantly improved.

title: Dynamic modelling and power boosting strategies for triboelectric energy harvesting: A tutorial
abstract: Triboelectric energy harvesters (TEHs) have gained significant attention within the realm of energy harvesting research, owing to their notable advantages, including lightweight construction, cost-effectiveness, and high efficiency at low frequencies. The rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) has expanded the potential applications of TEHs, particularly in small-scale energy harvesting systems and self-powered sensor technologies. This tutorial is presented to help readers understand the fundamental theory of TEHs and learn to model structural and electrical dynamics of TEHs. A brief introduction to the basic concepts and working mechanisms of TEHs is provided, which includes triboelectric series and four basic working modes of TEHs. The electrical dynamic modelling is then described for readers to understand the basic characteristics. Subsequently, mathematical modelling of five TEHs from the perspectives of structural dynamics is elaborated as examples, in which nonsmooth nonlinear dynamics is the main focus. As the power generation of TEHs depends on the contact-separation or relative sliding between the surfaces of two distinct triboelectric materials, vibro-impact and stick–slip vibration are shown to directly affect the charge transfer process. In order to broaden the frequency bandwidth and enhance the energy harvesting efficiency under low-frequency excitations, nonlinear mechanisms such as bistability are usually utilized in TEHs, resulting in complex nonlinear dynamic behaviours. Finally, this tutorial provides a brief review of diverse power augmentation strategies, thereby facilitating an expedited entry for readers into the intricacies of their specific areas of interest.

title: Vibration data-driven supervised learning for low-speed bearing fault diagnosis using classical and nonlinear features
abstract: Fault diagnosis of low-speed bearings via vibration analysis is challenging due to the low energy of fault signatures and the high susceptibility to noise, particularly in early degradation stages. Recent deep-learning approaches have shown promising results in mitigating those limitations, yet many require large datasets, high sampling rates, or complex preprocessing for ensuring generalization. This study proposes a supervised learning framework optimized for limited data scenarios, advancing the state-of-the-art through four contributions. First, Rosenstein’s Largest Lyapunov Exponent (LLE) algorithm is modified by replacing Euclidean with Pearson correlation distance for nearest-neighbor identification in reconstructed phase space, enhancing class separability. Second, a hybrid feature set integrates classical time-domain indicators with nonlinear measures (LLE and Higuchi Fractal Dimension), tailored for incipient-fault conditions. Third, the influence of vibration signal window size, expressed in shaft revolutions, is systematically evaluated with the use of Welch’s t-test, providing guidelines for balancing sensitivity and computational cost. Finally, the framework is validated on two datasets, namely, (1) an experimental set simulating abrasive wear on bearing outer races at three severities under varied loads, representing a non-periodic defect type rarely studied, and (2) naturally degraded industrial pulley bearings. The results show high classification accuracy without complex preprocessing, confirming suitability for predictive maintenance in data- and resource-constrained environments. The approach offers a compact, interpretable, and data-efficient solution for early fault detection in low-speed bearings, with potential for deployment in industrial contexts where robustness and scalability are critical.

title: Design and sound absorption mechanism of bio-inspired honeycomb-spiderweb coupled acoustic metamaterials
abstract: This study presents the design, theoretical modeling, and experimental validation of a bio-inspired Honeycomb-core Network Acoustic Metamaterial (HNAM) for broadband low-frequency noise control, addressing critical challenges in engineering applications such as aerospace and high-speed railways. By integrating hierarchical spider web-inspired topology with hexagonal honeycomb structures, the proposed HNAM achieves synergistic coupling effects and hierarchical scaling, enabling continuous broadband sound absorption below 1 kHz while maintaining structural stiffness and lightweight design. Theoretical and numerical analyses reveal that the hierarchical architecture generates multiple coupled resonance peaks, effectively mitigating absorption dips and expanding the operational bandwidth. Experimental results demonstrate that the first-order HNAM attains a 50 % half-absorption bandwidth and 32 % high-efficiency bandwidth (α ≥ 0.8) within the 200–800 Hz range, outperforming conventional honeycomb and Helmholtz resonator designs. Parametric studies identify key geometric factors (scaling factor λ, perforation diameters, and cavity thickness) governing acoustic performance and provide a systematic optimization framework. The HNAM integrates multifunctional acoustic and mechanical properties of advanced materials, providing a referential solution for next-generation engineering systems that require simultaneous vibration isolation, noise reduction, and load-bearing capacity.

title: Band gap properties of the planar beam-like truss metamaterial structures using the plane wave expansion method
abstract: In this paper, an integrated numerical and experimental study on a type of planar beam-like truss metamaterial structures is presented. These novel structures are formed by adding local resonators periodically to the planar beam-like periodic truss structures. To investigate the band gap characteristics of the proposed structures, this paper first derives the equivalent vibration equations of the structures based on the energy equivalence principle and Hamilton’s principle, and then obtains the band structures using the plane wave expansion method. The plane wave expansion method is validated through a vibration transmission analysis, which is implemented through simulation and experiment. The computational results of the wave spectral element method are also presented for reference. Both the results of band structures and vibration transmission analysis show that the plane wave expansion method provides higher computational accuracy for the in-plane flexural vibration band gap than for the out-of-plane flexural vibration band gap. However, the accuracy for both types of band gaps meets engineering precision requirements. This study pioneers the application of the plane wave expansion method to the investigation of band gap characteristics in truss structures, overcoming the current limitations where only finite element methods and spectral element methods can be employed to calculate band gap ranges of the truss structures. It provides novel methodological guidance for researching band gap properties in truss structures. The proposed method can also be extended to investigate band gaps in other periodic 2D or 3D truss structures with more complex configurations.
keywords: In-plane and out-of-plane flexural vibration band gaps

title: Stability assessment and oscillation prediction in free-piston linear generator using an approximate analytical method
abstract: The application and deployment of high-efficiency, multi-fuel compatible Free-piston linear generators are hindered by the difficulty in rapidly analyzing the stability and performance of their inherently nonlinear dynamics. This study proposes an innovative approximate analytical method, which transforms the system dynamics from the time domain into the frequency domain using the describing function. Unlike conventional methods, the proposed method uniquely integrates describing function theory with a trust-region-reflective algorithm, which effectively solves the transcendental equations that typically limit analytical analysis. This fusion retains the physical insight of an analytical approach while ensuring a fast and robust solution. The developed model accurately predicts the stability boundaries, such as stall and collision, and reveals that design and operating parameters like moving component mass, fuel energy, and ignition position exhibit unique, coupled, and decoupled control authorities over the output response. The predictive capability of the method is rigorously validated against two structurally and parametrically distinct prototypes, including methanol and gasoline-fueled, with prediction errors consistently below 4% for both operating frequency and stroke. The proposed methodology provides a computationally efficient and reliable tool that bridges the gap between complex theory and practical engineering, facilitating the accelerated design, optimization, and control of FPLG systems.

title: Periodic and aperiodic hierarchical chiral metamaterials for broadband vibration suppression
abstract: While chiral metamaterials excel in wave manipulation, their potential for low-frequency broadband vibration suppression remains underexplored. This study proposes a new design paradigm that integrates the principles of “tacticity” and “hierarchy” into chiral lattices. Eight hierarchical chiral elementary cells with self-similar geometry are assembled to construct periodic and aperiodic metamaterials, enabling reduced starting frequencies of band gaps at an identical stiffness-mass ratio. To facilitate the customization design, a theoretical framework is established for predicting the transmittance spectra and band structure of these hierarchical chiral metamaterials, which is validated through simulational results and experimental tests. It is demonstrated that the periodic syndiotactic metamaterial generates two wide band gaps, the normalized starting frequency of which is lower than that observed in non-hierarchical, mono-hierarchical, and de-chiralized reference configurations. The intrinsic band gap formation mechanisms are elucidated, and a systematic parametric analysis is conducted to guide band gap tailoring. Furthermore, through the combinatorial optimization of topological configurations and structural parameters, the resulting aperiodic hierarchical chiral metamaterial achieves superior broadband vibration suppression performance. Compared to the periodic configuration, the aperiodic design not only broadens the initial band gap by 122.2% but also reduces the starting frequency by 34.4%. Overall, the tacticity-hierarchy framework and theoretical model developed in this work provide a general pathway to engineer customizable, low-frequency, broadband band gaps for vibration suppression.

title: Physics-guided design of graded acoustic-black-hole lattices for vibration suppression: Reduced-order modeling and antiresonance mechanism
abstract: Graded metamaterials offer a promising route for broadband vibration suppression via varying local resonances. However, studies remain relatively limited on how to efficiently model and integrate multiple resonant mechanisms within lattice-based graded structures. This paper presents a graded metamaterial structure integrating simple cubic (SC), body-centered cubic (BCC), and acoustic black hole (ABH) configurations for effective vibration suppression. A reduced-order model of the SC-BCC-ABH unit is developed to improve computational efficiency while maintaining high accuracy. Modal analysis of both the SC-BCC-ABH structure and equivalent graded-resonator chain reveals the bandgap formation and antiresonance mechanisms. The results indicate that the anti-resonance frequencies are governed by the natural frequencies of the second to fourth resonators and remain independent of the first resonator that is directly connected to the excited main mass. Additionally, the sequence of the second to fourth resonators has negligible influence on the system’s transmissibility. These findings are validated through experimental measurements. A physics-guided multi-objective optimization combining reduced-order model and antiresonance effect is conducted to design a lightweight SC-BCC-ABH structure. Overall, this work provides a comprehensive modeling, analysis, and optimization strategy for the design of graded metamaterials with enhanced vibration suppression capability.

title: An USPCD multi-feature fusion method for bridge underwater structure identification
abstract: Recent achievements in 3D sonar enable centimeter-level resolution of underwater bridge structure measurement. However, this theoretical accuracy cannot be directly obtained from the raw underwater sonar point cloud data (USPCD) due to the significant scattering characteristics, non-uniform density distribution, and a large amount of noise that seriously pollute and mask the structural features of interest. Therefore, we propose an advanced USPCD multi-feature extraction method for bridge pile morphological inspection, providing valuable substructure in-service condition. This method is based on two-dimensional space, fusing point cloud density and edge features to identify the edge points of piles, and using spectral clustering methods to classify and locate pile foundations. Subsequently, coarse segmentation based on minimum cuts and fine extraction based on statistical methods are implemented in sequence to achieve complete segmentation of pile foundations and effective filtering of various environmental noises, thereby realizing high-performance extraction of piles with different distribution patterns and different degrees of incompleteness. The efficacy of the method is validated through an application to deep-water group pile foundations from two bridges across the Yangtze River. The results demonstrate the strong generalizability of the proposed method, with instance segmentation accuracy metrics exceeding 0.88 across all validation cases. Specifically, for relatively complete pile groups, the P¯,R¯,F¯1, and mIoU metrics all surpass 0.89. Even for pile groups with an incompleteness rate of 90%, the minimum P¯ still reachPes 0.863, thereby satisfying the requirements for detailed inspection of underwater bridge substructures.

title: Editorial Board
An efficient optimal transport-based polynomial chaos representation for non-Gaussian random fields
abstract: In the last decade, the class of polynomial chaos (PC) methods for non-Gaussian random field modeling has received considerable attention. Although an optimal transport framework has been introduced very recently for overcoming the curse of dimensionality in existing Rosenblatt-based PC representations of non-Gaussian fields (Zhang and Dai, 2025), the computationally intensive BFGS procedure in the construction of optimal transport map greatly limits the application of this framework in complex engineering problems. In this paper, we further extend the present optimal transport-based method to a general and efficient framework for the PC representation of non-Gaussian fields. Our method firstly reformulates the original optimal transport problem as an assignment problem with similar objects by identifying the discrete structure of the optimal transport map with allocation constraints. Then, the auction algorithm is further embedded in the assignment formulation to determine the optimal transport map. With the resulting map, the PC representation of the non-Gaussian field is accordingly constructed. Since the auction algorithm enforces the allocation constraints and guarantees a bounded number of iterations, the optimal transport map can be constructed with substantially higher efficiency, overcoming the intensive computational cost in BFGS procedure. Consequently, the PC representation of non-Gaussian fields can be achieved in a far more efficient manner. Three illustrative examples, including the stochastic dynamic analysis of a bridge–vehicle system, are presented to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed PC representation of non-Gaussian fields, with speedups exceeding an order of magnitude over BFGS, as well as its applicability in subsequent stochastic response analysis.

title: Integrated signal processing and nonlinear control for valve positioners systems in precision chemical manufacturing
abstract: In precision chemical manufacturing, valve positioner systems serve as critical hubs between distributed control systems and control valves, processing multi-source signals and driving control valves to precisely regulate flow, pressure, and temperature. However, noise-contaminated valve displacement signals, process-fluctuation interference, time-varying nonlinearities, parameter uncertainties, and dead zones degraded its performance. This paper proposes an integrated signal processing and nonlinear control scheme. First, a Fal-function filter suppresses high-frequency noise in valve displacement signals, while a composite observer, combining a state observer and a disturbance observer, accurately estimates unmeasurable states and rapidly compensates disturbances. Then, a nonlinear controller employs radial basis function neural networks to approximate unmodeled dynamics arising from time-varying nonlinearities and parameter uncertainties, thereby improving model accuracy. In parallel, dynamic surface control prevents the “explosion of complexity” caused by higher-order derivatives, yielding a smooth and bounded control law. Utilize a BLF-based constraint mechanism to handle valve position, valve-stem velocity, and input saturation within a unified framework. This reduces dead-zone induced start-up delay, prevents end-stroke impacts, and suppresses overshoot and oscillations caused by excessive stem speed and overly large control amplitudes. In addition, an auxiliary system based on an approximate coordinate transformation compensates the saturation nonlinearity, enhancing robustness under large control amplitudes. Finally, experiments confirm that the controller achieves efficient signal processing and precise control, ensuring semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded closed-loop signals and strict compliance with state constraints. It attains a 0.94 % steady-state error, 3.7 s settling time, and 0.14 mm overshoot, significantly improving the accuracy and operational stability of precision chemical manufacturing.

title: Non-iterative optimal blind deconvolution and its application to machine condition monitoring
abstract: Blind deconvolution method (BDM) has remarkable performance in mechanical fault feature extraction and is widely used in mechanical fault identification. However, classical blind deconvolution (BD) methods have many theoretical flaws, which limit their deconvolution performance. (i) The optimization objective function of classical BD is often highly nonlinear and non-convex, making it difficult to obtain the optimal solution. (ii) Classical BDMs are often solved through iterative optimization algorithms, which require a given initialization parameter. Different initialization strategies will yield different results. These theoretical flaws can lead to insufficient deconvolution performance and unstable deconvolution results. Aiming at these theoretical limitations, this paper proposes a non-iterative optimal BDM that explores the differentiated spectral structures of healthy and faulty samples to obtain the optimal inverse filter. The proposed method uses a health indicator (HI) called the differential spectral energy ratio to characterize fault features, and uses the generalized Rayleigh quotient to obtain a non-iterative optimization solution. The proposed method can obtain the global optimal solution without giving any initialization parameters, and does not require iterative optimization algorithms. These advantages directly improve the deconvolution performance and deconvolution stability of BDM. In addition, compared with the classical BDM that only utilizes faulty samples, the proposed method combines healthy samples and faulty samples for deconvolution, providing a new approach for BD design. Three case studies have shown that the proposed method outperforms five classical BDMs (three non-parametric BDMs and two parametric BDMs) in terms of fault feature extraction.

title: Hybrid state-space coupling of experimental models and parametric reduced order models for enhanced real-time simulations
abstract: Virtual prototyping has emerged as a key enabler in modern engineering design, allowing extensive virtual testing during the early development phases and reducing reliance on costly and time-consuming physical prototypes. In the NVH field, virtual prototyping techniques are essential for accurately predicting vibro-acoustic behavior, which is critical to achieving optimal vehicle performance and passenger comfort. This paper presents an innovative hybrid state-space coupling framework that integrates parametric reduced order models with systems characterized experimentally. The proposed approach enables the real-time computation of target responses derived from blocked force time histories. By leveraging the advantages of state-space representation and parametric model order reduction technology, the framework offers several key benefits. It supports fast design optimization by eliminating the computational overhead of recomputing transfer functions, a task traditionally required during iterative simulation processes. Additionally, the flexible architecture of the framework enhances its adaptability to various interactive applications. A critical aspect of the workflow proposed is the system identification process, which should respect certain physical properties of the systems to be coupled. This adherence to physical constraints is essential to guarantee the stability of the coupled structure and achieving accurate simulation result. The virtual coupling is evaluated both in terms of frequency response functions and time-domain responses, demonstrating results that align with state-of-the-art approaches. Computation analyses show the advantage of the approach proposed over frequency-based techniques. The findings underscore the framework’s potential as a powerful tool for NVH analysts and design engineers, enabling faster and more reliable decision-making during early development stages.

title: Self-reference UAV motion elimination and structural modal parameter restoration method
abstract: To ensure the accuracy of vision-based vibration testing, close-range measurement using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) demonstrates significant advantages. However, the required fixed reference point in each measurement view to eliminate the UAV ego motion is hardly satisfied. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a self-reference UAV motion elimination and structural modal parameter restoration method. First, different from the traditional fixed reference point required in each segment vibration test, a vibration measurement point within the field of view is selected as self-reference point to eliminate the UAV motion. Second, the modal parameters are identified using self-reference relative pixel displacement responses. The modal frequencies and damping ratios can be obtained directly, while the mode shape segments are distorted except the segment that include pier reference point. Therefore, the mode shape segments are restored sequentially through the relationship between the false mode shape and the true mode shape. Third, a numerically simulated example was generated and used to verify the effectiveness of the derived restoration method. Finally, a set of laboratory vibration tests on a clamped-supported beam, monitored with UAV vision, fixed camera, and accelerometers were conducted to verify the method. The results showed that the proposed method can identify modal parameters with high measurement point density and high accuracy.

title: Structural optimization and experimental research of a high-temperature piezoelectric force sensor based on AFSA-NSGA-II fusion algorithm
abstract: To address the issues of reduced sensitivity and output signal drift in piezoelectric force sensors under high-temperature conditions, this paper proposes a structural optimization design method for high-temperature piezoelectric force sensors that integrates the response surface methodology (RSM) with the AFSA-NSGA-II algorithm. Significant factors influencing sensor parameters were identified through Plackett-Burman trials. A mathematical model linking input parameters to output performance was constructed using RSM. Leveraging the global search and multi-objective optimization capabilities of the AFSA-NSGA-II algorithm, a synergistic optimization of sensor sensitivity, thermal stress, and structural stiffness was achieved. The optimal structural design, which balances high sensitivity and temperature drift resistance, was selected. A high-temperature dynamic calibration experimental system was established, and calibration experiments were conducted on a prototype high-temperature piezoelectric force sensor. The experimental results demonstrate that the optimized sensor exhibits an 18.87% increase in sensitivity and a 45.05% reduction in thermal stress of the crystal group, significantly enhancing the high-temperature stability and mechanical performance of the sensor. Furthermore, the study reveals the sensitivity patterns of key parameters on sensor performance, providing theoretical support and practical guidance for the design of high-temperature piezoelectric force sensors.

title: Rub-induced nonlinear vibration and discontinuity-induced bifurcation analysis of a noisy rotor-stator system with different compliant contact force models
abstract: The rotor-stator rubs that may occur due to optimized clearance combined with high shaft vibration are significant issues for machine stability, reliability, and lateral shaft motion. The present work numerically and experimentally investigates the rub-induced nonlinear vibration characteristics and discontinuity-induced bifurcation in a non-smooth Jeffcott rotor-stator system with different forms of compliant rub-impact models subjected to combined unbalance force and noise. First, a two degree-of-freedom (DOF) Jeffcott model with symmetric and asymmetric support stiffness with cross-coupling is considered. Various models for compliant contact have been considered, including Hertz, Kelvin-Voigt, elastic, piecewise linear, and nonlinear dissipative contact force models. Next, a four DOF rotor-stator model is developed, where the rotor impacts the visco-elastically suspended elastic stator model through a nonlinear compliant contact model that includes local stiffness of the stator coating with an elastic wear layer. The effects of unbalance force, friction coefficient, damping coefficient, bearing clearance, shaft nonlinearities, system anisotropy, such as due to gravitational forces, cross-coupling stiffness, asymmetric stiffness, and parametric as well as additive noise on the dynamic response and stability are investigated. The uncertainty is modelled by generating appropriate Gaussian as well as non-Gaussian coloured noise processes, by filtering Gaussian white noise through a first-order linear and nonlinear filter, respectively. The dynamic behaviour is presented using time waveform, whirling motion, Poincare’ section, bifurcation diagram, wavelet transform, recurrence plots and the largest Lyapunov exponent. An experimental study is carried out using a Jeffcott rotor and a movable elastic rod to simulate the rubbing phenomenon. Numerical results are also compared with actual rubbing, as observed during troubleshooting and condition monitoring for various rotating machinery.

title: Composite fault diagnosis of mechatronic transmission system based on current harmonic mutual verification and enhanced order spectral analysis under variable speed conditions
abstract: The ease of installation and high signal purity of current sensors have driven the adoption of motor current signature analysis (MCSA) in fault diagnosis of mechatronic transmission systems. However, MCSA-based fault diagnosis is challenged by complex modulation effects from composite faults, which obscures fault features, and by its heavy reliance on tachometers under variable speed conditions. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel diagnostic scheme that integrates harmonic mutual verification (HMV) with enhanced order spectral analysis for detecting composite faults in mechatronic transmission systems. First, inductive mechanism of rotor slot harmonics is analyzed, leading to the development of an HMV-based tacholess speed estimation method that leverages the relationship among rotor slot harmonics, thereby eliminating the dependence on rotor slot number. Second, an enhanced order spectral analysis strategy is proposed, which solves the challenge of composite fault representation under variable speed conditions through fault decoupling and feature enhancement. The effectiveness of proposed method is validated using experimental data collected from two composite fault scenarios in a mechatronic transmission system, complemented by an ablation study to demonstrate its advantages. Experimental results confirm that HMV-based method offers high accuracy, non-invasiveness, and does not require pre-training. Notably, it enables induction motor speed estimation solely from current signals, even when rotor slot number is unknown. Furthermore, enhanced order spectrum effectively identifies composite fault types under variable speed conditions and significantly reduces the likelihood of missed diagnoses, enhancing overall diagnostic reliability.

title: Fleet-based transfer learning for anomaly detection in industrial systems
abstract: This work considers the problem of developing a data-driven anomaly detection method in the common situation in which a large dataset is available only for few systems of a fleet and the data therein are unlabeled, i.e., the equipment health state (normal/anomalous) is unknown. An innovative two-stage unsupervised Transfer Learning (TL) framework is developed. In the first stage, a Long Short-Term Memory Encoder–Decoder (LSTM-ED) is pre-trained to reconstruct the values expected in normal condition of a specific (“source”) system of the fleet using a dataset of signal measurements collected during a long period of time. Since industrial systems are typically in normal condition during most of their operational time, this pre-trained model is expected to reproduce their behavior in normal condition. In the second stage, the network architecture and parameters of the pre-trained model are used to initialize the dedicated LSTM-ED-based signal reconstruction model for another (“target”) system of the same fleet, for which only a limited amount of data collected during a short period of time is available. Data of the Aramis Data Challenge and of traction systems of a fleet of trains have been used to validate the proposed anomaly detection method in two different case studies. The obtained results show the superior performance of the proposed method in comparison to other state-of-the-art methods.

title: Self-powered tunable mechanical oscillators: An analytical, numerical, and experimental study
abstract: This research investigates and validates the self-powered resonance frequency tuning of a vibrating oscillator through energy harvesting. The oscillator is a doubly-clamped composite beam, partially covered by piezoelectric layers, with two magnets at its center. Two linear actuators equipped with magnets tune the resonance frequency, and the system undergoes harmonic base excitation. By connecting a full-bridge rectifier to the piezoelectric layers, the energy is stored on a capacitor. A geometrically nonlinear model is derived using Hamilton’s principle, Euler-Bernoulli beam theory, dipole magnetic model, and Gauss’s law. The harmonic balance method (HBM), validated by time integration, reveals hardening nonlinearity and cyclic-fold bifurcations. The capacitor charging process is approximated analytically and demonstrates that the harvested energy is sufficient to drive the actuators for resonance frequency tuning. Next, sine-sweep and frequency dwell tests validate the concept by measuring the nonlinear beam responses and the voltages in the capacitor charging process. Furthermore, under the same acceleration, increasing the frequency yields a larger change in the resonance frequency over a shorter charging time. Increasing the acceleration and frequency, while retaining the same charging time and capacitance, gives a notable increase in the resonance frequency. For the cases investigated, with a 10-minute dwell time, the resonance frequency is increased by up to 28.9 percent. Finally, using experiments, model parameters are extracted and a more accurate magnetic model than the dipole model is developed, showing a good agreement between the updated model and experiments. This research demonstrates the viability of self-powered resonance frequency tuning using oscillator inherent energy.

title: Revisiting Lempel-Ziv complexity in machine condition monitoring: a fresh perspective
abstract: Lempel-Ziv Complexity (LZC) and its variants have become popular measures of signal complexity across a wide range of disciplines. In machine condition monitoring, most existing work treats LZC as a fault-sensitive feature and explores—largely through experiments—how LZC changes with fault signal sparsity. These empirical studies, however, offer only partial insight into the precise relationship between LZC and sparsity. More fundamentally, several well-established complexity measures—sample entropy, approximate entropy, and fuzzy entropy—have been shown to exhibit the “bilateral reduction” effect: their values fall when a signal becomes either too sparse or too dense. Whether and how the LZC family, in particular its normalized form (NLZC), shares this property has not been systematically examined. A rigorous understanding of this bilateral reduction effect is indispensable for interpreting NLZC fluctuations as a fault signal grows sparser or denser in real applications. Motivated by this gap, the present study pursues two objectives: (1) to establish the theoretical existence of the bilateral reduction effect in NLZC; (2) to exploit this effect in explaining how NLZC evolves with varying fault-signal sparsity. Combining analytical derivations with systematic experiments, we prove that NLZC indeed follows the bilateral reduction effect. Building on this theoretical finding, we introduce a Cumulative Energy Partition (CEP) symbolization scheme that amplifies NLZC’ s sensitivity to impulsive fault components. Extensive tests on bearings, motors, and gears demonstrate that the CEP-enhanced NLZC detects both incipient and severe faults, while the observed NLZC variations can be transparently interpreted through the proven bilateral reduction principle. This work contributes new theoretical understanding of the interplay between NLZC and signal sparsity, elevates the interpretability and practical utility of NLZC in machine condition monitoring, and enriches the broader landscape of sparsity-aware complexity metrics.

title: A nonlinear electromagnetic energy harvester with a repulsive magnetic spring for multi-directional excitations
abstract: The common ultra-low frequency vibration in the natural environment represents a significant energy source. However, the energy harvesting performance is always limited by the ultra-low frequency and uncertain directional excitations. In this paper, a nonlinear electromagnetic energy harvester (NEMEH) with a repulsive magnetic spring is proposed to lower the working frequency and enhance the electromechanical coupling efficiency. The energy harvesting performance under ultra-low frequency vibration excitation is thus enhanced. The nonlinear stiffness and transduction factor are characterized through fitting for theoretical analysis. The corresponding NEMEH dynamic model is built to calculate the motion response results of the moving magnets. The output results from both numerical calculations and experiments verify the theoretical model, and also demonstrate the better output performance of the proposed NEMEH under little acceleration excitation than that of the linear EMEH with conventional steel springs. Moreover, the direction adaptability of the NEMEH is explored to show the energy harvesting efficiency variation principles with different excitation directions. The results show that zero deviation angle corresponds to the maximum output, and the cutoff deviation angle of the presented NEMEH is influenced by both the frequency and amplitude of the excitation.

title: A novel interval prediction model for buffeting response of a long-span bridge based on machine learning
abstract: With bridges being longer and lighter, buffeting response can be of importance for bridge management and corresponding prediction model is needed. Data-driven models have advantages on prediction accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional buffeting analysis. However, existing data-driven models mainly focus on deterministic prediction, few models can perform probabilistic prediction. To this end, a novel interval prediction model for buffeting response of a long-span bridge is proposed. The proposed model selects gated recurrent unit neural network as the basic module, and it incorporates quantile regression and lower upper bound estimation for interval prediction. Specifically, the proposed model employs quantile regression for initial estimation of interval bounds in the form of quantiles, and then it uses lower upper bound estimation method to optimize initial bounds to enhance prediction accuracy. Besides, to enhance training efficiency of lower upper bound estimation method, an adaptive-weight training strategy that can tune the weight parameter during the training process is proposed. The proposed model is validated by the monitoring data of a long-span bridge, where effectiveness and superiority of the proposed interval prediction model are demonstrated.

title: A new nonlinear friction model based on actual pressure distribution of bolted joint interface and its characterization analysis
abstract: A novel cubic bolt pressure distribution curve was proposed, and the slip modeling of bolted joint interfaces was improved in this study. A representative model was constructed via finite element analysis to clarify interface pressure distribution, accurately represented through the cubic curve’s innovative application. An advanced Iwan model was derived using a new density function processing method to characterize the joint’s nonlinear dynamics. Quasi-static experiments evaluated the model’s ability to capture complex nonlinear behavior. This study pinpoints key factors influencing hysteresis curves and energy dissipation in bolted systems, and defines how these factors act, laying theoretical support for optimizing bolted joint designs. Furthermore, the reasons for the emergence of the stiffness softening phenomenon were analyzed at the theoretical level.

title: Experimental study of flexoelectric dynamic actuations of SpPVDF laminated beams
abstract: Understanding the flexoelectric actuation characteristics is essential for developing high-precision flexoelectric actuators. In this study, flexoelectric actuators based on a new lab-made SpPVDF material are employed to achieve actuation and vibration control of a macroscopic cantilever beam. The flexoelectric actuator is fabricated by configuring a line electrode on the upper surface and an electrode layer on the lower surface of synthesized SpPVDF film. An experimental method is developed for flexoelectric coefficient measurement based on the converse flexoelectric effect. This method employs the resonance phenomena to amplify the macroscopic structural dynamic displacement response induced by the weak flexoelectric effect, thereby enabling measurable displacements without requiring excessively high driving voltages. The effects of input voltage frequency and amplitude on dynamic actuation behavior are experimentally investigated. Experimental results reveal a near-linear relationship between the actuation displacement and applied excitation voltage amplitude. The actuation displacement demonstrates a notable frequency dependence, attaining peak values at the resonant frequency while exhibiting rapid attenuation when the excitation frequency deviates from resonance. Theoretical predictions are in good agreement with experimental measurements. The influences of actuator design parameters, i.e., line electrode position, line electrode radius, flexoelectric patch thickness and beam thickness, on the resulting actuation control performance are investigated. These findings provide a fundamental understanding of dynamic flexoelectric actuation behavior of the SpPVDF material.

title: A unified Cross-Modal adaptive contrastive learning framework for acoustic fault diagnosis of rolling bearing under limited & imbalanced data
abstract: The intelligent fault diagnosis method based on acoustics provides a effective approach for achieving reliable data-driven maintenance in industrial scenarios. However, in actual scenarios, mechanical equipment is mainly in a normal operating state, which leads to limited monitoring data and an imbalance in fault categories (L&I). Moreover, multi-source heterogeneous data are often fragmented and difficult to integrate, while most artificial intelligence models merely provide fault warnings without dynamic optimization or decision-making capabilities. To address these issues, this paper proposes a unified cross-modal adaptive contrastive learning framework jointly models the ideas of data-level augmentation and algorithm-level adaptation within a single end-to-end architecture. From a data-level perspective, inspired by the multi-view representation theory, the proposed method constructs a same-source dual-modality input by transforming raw acoustic signals into temporal waveforms and gramian angular difference field (GADF) images, thereby enriching feature diversity without introducing sensor inconsistency. A multi-scale residual image encoder (MSR-IE) and a hybrid temporal encoder with multi-receptive convolutions (HTE-MRC) are designed to extract modality-specific features. Subsequently, integration is carried out through a cross-modal contrastive fusion module. During this process, heterogeneous feature Spaces are aligned into a unified, domain-invariant embedding. At the algorithmic level, a dual-task guided fault discriminator (DGFD) is developed to jointly perform coarse-grained health assessment and fine-grained fault identification, with dynamic task reweighting to balance learning under class-imbalanced conditions. Results on two rolling bearing acoustic datasets across six imbalance regimes show that the proposed method achieves 97.9 % accuracy and 98.9 % G-mean, with notably improved minority-class detection and balanced performance under severe imbalance.

title: Speed-guided diffusion probabilistic model integrated with variational autoencoder for fault diagnosis under limited data
abstract: Deep learning-based fault diagnosis has shown great potential in intelligent condition monitoring. However, its performance heavily depends on large amounts of labeled data, which are often scarce in real-world industrial scenarios, especially under varying speed conditions. The data limitations hinder the generalization ability of fault diagnosis models. To address this issue, we propose a novel speed-guided denoising diffusion probabilistic model integrated with variational autoencoder (SDPM-VAE) for generating high quality data. The speed signal is incorporated as a conditional prior through a cross-attention mechanism to preserve speed-dependent characteristics in the generated data. Additionally, a hybrid VAE and DDPM framework is proposed to enhance data quality while reducing computational cost. The coarse reconstructions and latent representations derived from the VAE are integrated into the reverse diffusion process. Experimental results on two gearbox datasets demonstrate that the SDPM-VAE outperforms four state-of-the-art methods in both the quality of the generated data and fault diagnosis accuracy, thereby validating its effectiveness for data augmentation under limited data conditions.

title: ARDiff: An adaptive reverse-step diffusion framework for unsupervised vibration signal denoising with frequency attention
abstract: This paper proposes ARDiff, an adaptive reverse-step diffusion framework for unsupervised denoising of vibration signals under high-noise industrial conditions. Unlike conventional diffusion models that rely on fixed denoising trajectories or external condition inputs, ARDiff enables adaptive noise-aware reconstruction without any class labels or guidance, through the integration of three key components. First, the frequency attention module (FAM) introduces a complex-valued attention mechanism in the frequency domain, enabling the model to effectively capture fault-relevant spectral features critical for signal reconstruction. Second, the noise step prediction model (NSPM) estimates the optimal reverse diffusion timestep based on the input noise level, improving reconstruction accuracy. Third, the variance-based scaling method (VSM) aligns the scale of the input signal with the expected distribution of the diffusion model at the predicted timestep, ensuring stable and consistent restoration. Experimental validation using the open-source CWRU dataset, the experimental HAI-PUMP dataset, and the SNU Planetary Gearbox dataset demonstrated that ARDiff consistently outperformed existing denoising models, particularly under extremely low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Ablation studies confirmed the individual contributions of FAM, NSPM, and VSM, verifying that ARDiff is a robust and generalizable denoising framework capable of operating effectively without any external conditions or label supervision. Moreover, ARDiff consistently maintained stable denoising performance under both Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise conditions, highlighting its practical robustness in realistic industrial environments.

title: Enhanced far-field acoustic signal detection via a deep subwavelength Fabry-Pérot resonator coupled with space-coiling metamaterial
abstract: Far-field acoustic signal detection is a significant but challenging task in many areas. One possible solution is the use of acoustic metamaterials, however, their implementation in practice is typically hindered by poor enhancement performance and large physical size. This paper proposes an acoustic metamaterial formed by a Fabry-Pérot (FP) resonator coupled with space-coiling metamaterial (FP-SCM) to improve the enhancement performance and shrink the size of the metamaterial simultaneously. Inspired by non-radiative energy transfer among identical resonators in magnetic fields, the twin FP-SCMs are employed for acoustic energy transfer and enhanced far-field acoustic signal detection. The acoustic enhancement properties of the FP-SCM are investigated through theoretical analysis, numerical simulation, and experimental verification. Taking weak Gaussian pulse signals as an example, the enhanced detection results demonstrate that the proposed FP-SCM can amplify weak signals by more than 230 times, even under strong background noise interference. Furthermore, the FP-SCM also achieves a deep subwavelength scale at the center frequency of the enhanced acoustic signal whose total size does not exceed λ/16. This work holds great potential for applications in non-destructive testing, underwater sonar systems, acoustic communication, etc.

title: Fault diagnosis of ball screws in servo mechanisms using deeply integrated MEMS sensors and convolutional neural networks
abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis in critical mechanical systems like ball screws is hampered by the difficulty of acquiring high-fidelity signals from core operational areas. This paper presents a novel methodology for ball screw fault diagnosis that overcomes this limitation by leveraging a deeply integrated wireless monitoring system (WMS). The WMS utilizes both embedded and surface-attached MEMS accelerometers and temperature sensors with sensitivities of 18.8 mV/g and 3 mV/°C respectively to capture vibration and thermal signals directly from the ball-raceway contact zones, enabling more detailed observation of internal dynamics compared with conventional external sensing methods. The multi-modal signals are processed and analyzed using time–frequency analysis and a custom-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for automated condition recognition. Experimental results on a dedicated platform show that single-modal sensing achieves 76.7 % to 85.0 % accuracy for temperature signals and 93.3 % to 96.7 % accuracy for vibration signals, while multi-modal fusion of the WMS data enables the CNN model to reach 100 % classification accuracy, effectively distinguishing between normal and faulty conditions under various speeds. This work demonstrates a fully functional research prototype combining hardware and intelligent analysis for machinery fault diagnosis, from innovative signal acquisition to intelligent data analysis, offering significant potential for advancing predictive maintenance.

title: A rapid method for identifying blasting seismic components based on source characteristics and polarization analysis
abstract: Accurate identification of blasting seismic components is essential for vibration control and structural safety assessment. However, the transient, complex, and non-stationary nature of blasting vibration signals makes conventional identification methods from seismology difficult to apply directly. To address this issue, this study proposes a rapid and physically interpretable method for identifying blasting seismic components. Building on conventional polarization-based methods, the proposed approach explicitly incorporates source characteristics specific to blasting seismic waves. By cross-validating phase-difference analysis with particle motion trajectory computation, the method can accurately identify the different blasting seismic components. Numerical simulations and on-site blasting experiments both show that the proposed method can accurately identify the dominant seismic components under different charge and boundary conditions. Compared with other approaches, the proposed method identifies P-, S-, and R-waves simultaneously. For each component, it also determines the time at which it becomes dominant in the vibration record, rather than only its arrival time. This capability will facilitate more detailed analysis of the propagation characteristics and relative contributions of different seismic components and provide a new avenue for evaluating and controlling blasting seismic effects.

title: Vehicle semi-active air inerter-spring-damper suspension with frequency-varying negative stiffness: design, control, and experimental validation
abstract: This paper addresses the performance limitations of conventional spring-damper suspensions by proposing a design methodology for a semi-active air inerter-spring-damper (ISD) system. The design incorporates a solenoid valve-controlled fluid inerter as its central element, which exploits frequency-varying negative stiffness behavior to enhance suspension dynamics. First, the fundamental frequency-varying negative stiffness mechanism is thoroughly analyzed. A high-fidelity suspension model that integrates a nonlinear air spring, a continuous damping control (CDC) damper, and the fluid inerter is established and validated. Subsequently, an inerter-damping coordinated control strategy is developed to leverage the frequency-varying negative stiffness characteristics. Furthermore, a Kalman filter-based state observer is designed to accurately estimate system states, enabling effective real-time control. The performance of the proposed suspension system is validated through experimental quarter-vehicle bench tests. Test results demonstrate that the proposed system reduces the root mean square (RMS) of body acceleration by 30.45% and the suspension working space by 10.39% compared to a passive air suspension under identical conditions. These findings confirm that the proposed method significantly enhances ride comfort without compromising safety and stability.

title: Enhanced multiple fault diagnosis in industrial robots through node-level capsule graph neural networks optimized with elk herd optimizer
abstract: The problem diagnosis and status monitoring are essential for industrial equipment to continue operating continuously. While the dynamics of the physical process must be modelled using traditional diagnostic techniques, it might be difficult to create an accurate dynamic model of intricately linked industrial systems. In this paper, Enhanced Multiple Fault Diagnosis in Industrial Robots through Node-Level Capsule Graph Neural Networks Optimized with Elk Herd Optimizer (EMFD-IR-NLCGNN-EHO) is proposed. Here, the input data is gathered from PHME 2021 dataset. The gathered input data are given to the preprocessing stage. In preprocessing, Box-cox-sparse-measures-based blind filtering (BCSMBF) is used to data merging, columns concatenating, missing values imputation and dataset normalization. Then, pre-processed data are given into NCGNN for classifying fault diagnosis in industrial robots as fault and no fault. Finally, the Elk Herd Optimizer (EHO) enhances NCGNN for classifying fault diagnosis in industrial robots. The performance of the EMFD-IR-NLCGNN-EHO is compared with other existing models. The EMFD-IR-NLCGNN-EHO method attains 6.58%, 8.25% and 5.29% higher accuracy; 8.96%, 5.21% and 6.89% higher recall; 6.12%, 5.23% and 8.87% higher f1-score when compared with existing techniques: Multi faults diagnosis for industrial robot fuse quality test bench utilizing DL (MFD-IRFTB-DL), Online fault detection of industrial robot utilizing IoRT with hybrid DL models, Experimental technique (OFD-IR-HDLT) and Model-dependent fault diagnosis algorithms for robotic systems (FDA-RS) respectively.

title: Nonlinear wave propagation and dynamic control in multi-unit Kresling origami metamaterials with conical architectures
abstract: Kresling origami structures have emerged as versatile mechanical metamaterials, offering unique capabilities such as deployability, tunable stiffness, energy absorption, and vibration mitigation.
