While prior research has predominantly focused on their kinematic and quasi-static behavior, especially in cylindrical configurations, this study presents a comprehensive investigation into the nonlinear wave dynamics and control of multi-unit Kresling origami systems featuring conical architectures. By introducing conicity at the unit cell level, we exploit geometric nonlinearity and axial–twist coupling to program dynamic responses across a broadened design space. Through an integrated analytical, numerical, and experimental approach, we demonstrate how conical Kresling modules enable programmable wave propagation, multi-stable energy landscapes, and enhanced stability. Our findings reveal new avenues for the design of adaptive origami metamaterials with engineered nonlinearities, offering significant potential for advanced vibration control, impact mitigation, and controlling wave propagation.

title: Line segment tracking for camera-based vibration measurement of large structures in outdoor conditions
abstract: This paper introduces and validates a computer vision method called the Line Segment Tracking (LST). It is designed for vibration measurement of large structures under outdoor conditions. Compared to conventional window-based methods such as Digital Image Correlation (DIC) and Lucas-Kanade Optical Flow (LKOF), the LST method minimizes disturbances within the region of interest by estimating the displacement of an intersection point determined by tracked line segments. First, error quantification and a parametric study of the LST method were conducted using synthetic images. The results were further validated with real images captured under laboratory conditions, utilizing a real-time camera orientation estimation program for precise alignment. Finally, the displacement of a tower crane in operation within an outdoor environment was measured. The validation of the LST method was performed by comparing its results with acceleration measurements. Comparative analysis demonstrated that the LST method not only produced results consistent with those obtained using DIC and LKOF but also effectively reduced the impact of light variations in images. In conclusion, the proposed LST method is a robust alternative to traditional window-based tracking techniques, suitable for vibration measurement in challenging outdoor environments. • Description of the Line Segment Tracking (LST) method for vibration measurement. • Validation of LST on synthetic and real images in lab and outdoor conditions. • Error and parametric analysis of LST with a real-time camera pose estimation program. • Measurement of the 3 dimensional displacement of a tower crane using LST. • Reduction of local light disturbance within ROI compared to window-based methods.

title: Periodic problems of unforced/periodically-forced nonlinear oscillators: Theoretical formulation and boundary shape function method
abstract: For the second-order conservative nonlinear oscillator and the Liénard equation we derive integral-type theoretical formulas to compute the periods through a generalized conservation law equipped with a weight function. Minimizing the error to satisfy periodicity conditions the optimal value of parameter is determined; hence, very accurate value of the period can be obtained for examples in testing. Three methods to solve periods and periodic solutions are developed for the Liénard equations without/with periodically-forcing terms. The periodicity conditions and nonlinear differential equation for the oscillatory motion constitute a special kind boundary value problem (BVP), rather than the initial value problem (IVP). This study is concerned with two possible cases: (a) given initial values, and (b) unknown initial values. For case (a) the boundary values at two end points of a time interval are known but with an unknown period, while for case (b) the resulting BVP is more difficult with both unknown period and boundary values on an unknown time interval. By means of boundary shape function method (BSFM) we can transform the BVP to an IVP for an easy computation of periodic problem, where the initial values for the new variable are given and derived explicitly; however, the period and terminal values of the new variable are unknown to be determined iteratively. BSFM’s periodic solutions automatically satisfy the periodicity conditions. Numerical examples disclose the merit of BSFM, which is convergent fast to offer very accurate period and periodic solution.

title: Structural phase optical flow: A visual vibration measurement method based on edge-guided and locally smooth priors
abstract: This paper presents a Structural Phase Optical Flow (SPOF) method for vision-based vibration measurement. Based on the phase vibration estimation (PVE) framework, SPOF addresses the inherent phase instability in phase motion representation by incorporating edge-focused and local smoothness constraints on the optical flow structure, effectively improving the accuracy and stability of phase optical flow estimation. By introducing a Gaussian mixture model combined with a weighted expectation–maximization algorithm, SPOF detects and corrects abnormal flow vectors, enhancing the continuity and physical consistency of full-field vibration signals. Experiments conducted on laboratory modal exciters, cantilever beams, and real-world cable structures demonstrate that SPOF outperforms existing mainstream PVE methods under various test conditions, accurately recovering vibration displacements highly consistent with accelerometer measurements. In the exciter tests, SPOF achieved a mean absolute error as low as 3 micrometers, while outdoor cable measurements maintained errors around 0.3 millimeters, demonstrating strong robustness and adaptability. This study provides a practical and effective technical solution for video-based non-contact structural health monitoring, with broad potential for engineering applications.

title: Domain-adaptive deep information disentanglement for cutting force dynamics prediction in machining processes
abstract: Cutting force dynamics are closely associated with key machining conditions such as tool wear and chatter. However, existing prediction methods adopt a global alignment strategy to rigidly align the data distributions of the source and target domains, overlooking domain-specific representations and thereby compromising model generalizability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel deep information disentanglement framework (TFR-DA), incorporating time–frequency joint reconstruction and a dual-discriminator adversarial strategy, to achieve robust prediction of cutting force dynamics. Specifically, TFR-DA first utilizes the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to improve the separability between domain-invariant and domain-specific representations. Next, a time–frequency joint reconstruction module is introduced to optimize the signal’s overall shape and to capture phase- and frequency-sensitive regions. Finally, a dual-discriminator adversarial training scheme is employed to promote domain indistinguishability and mitigate the interference of domain-specific components within the shared representation space. For two representative machining scenarios, including thin-walled workpiece and conventional block workpiece, the proposed method reduces prediction errors of cutting force dynamics by 66.89% and 46.31%, respectively, compared to a baseline model without domain adaptation, and further improves the performance of practical tool condition monitoring. This method offers advantages such as non-intrusiveness and low cost, making it particularly suitable for large-scale manufacturing settings with limited sensor deployment, and serving as an effective enhancement to intelligent monitoring systems in industrial applications.

title: Computer vision-based cross-scale structural displacement estimation using amplitude-phase fusion
abstract: Accurate and robust structural displacement monitoring is essential for the safety assessment and maintenance of civil infrastructure. While phase-based vision methods offer sub-pixel precision, their applicability is severely limited by phase wrapping under large inter-frame motions. This issue hinders reliable monitoring in real-world scenarios where large pseudo-static displacements and small vibrations coexist. To address this limitation, this study proposes a cross-scale displacement estimation technique that fuses amplitude and phase information from vision measurements. The technique employs a two-stage estimation framework: amplitude-based pixel-level coarse alignment, followed by phase-based sub-pixel refinement. To ensure robustness and accuracy across varying structural responses, three key strategies are introduced: (1) a correlation-based active pixel selection algorithm to extract structurally meaningful regions, (2) a pyramid level optimization algorithm based on inter-scale phase linearity, and (3) a self-calibration algorithm using synthetic image sequences to determine the phase-to-pixel scale. The effectiveness of the proposed technique was validated through experimental testing on a single-story building model and a footbridge under multiple excitation scenarios. The results indicate that the proposed technique is capable of achieving high-precision displacement estimation, with root mean square errors maintained below 0.2 mm even for displacement amplitudes reaching up to 50 mm.

title: Dynamic modeling and vibration analysis for cycloid gear bearing fault diagnosis of rotate vector reducers
abstract: Among the rolling bearings in rotate vector (RV) reducers, cycloid gear bearings (CGBs) need to undertake torque load, and are more prone to fault. However, the CGB kinematics and dynamics are highly complex, and this poses a tremendous challenge to vibration based fault diagnosis. To address this issue, it is necessary to reveal the CGB fault dynamic mechanism and vibration symptoms. To this end, a lumped parameter dynamic model in the translational-torsional degree of freedoms is established to investigate in-depth the CGB vibration characteristics, considering the gear meshing of planetary and cycloidal stages, the Hertz contacts between rolling elements and raceways of rolling bearings, as well as the time-varying vibration transfer path and vibration measurement angle relative to fixed sensor. Specifically, the time variability in mesh stiffness for the sun-planet and cycloid-pinwheel pairs are evaluated using the potential energy method and moment equilibrium theory, respectively. The loss of contact force between rolling elements and raceways, and the resultant time variability in bearing stiffness due to CGB localized faults, are calculated based on Hertz contact theory. These time-varying parametric excitations are imposed on the dynamic model, to simulate the RV reducer vibrations under CGB faults. Furthermore, the vibrations are analyzed through Fourier and envelope spectra, thereby the CGB fault symptoms are discovered. The dynamic model and fault vibration characteristics are validated experimentally, and localized faults on the CGB raceways and rolling elements are effectively diagnosed.

title: Editorial Board
An Improved Instantaneous Wavelet Bispectrum Feature for gear fault diagnostics using a Wireless MEMS sensor
abstract: Gears are prone to defects such as spalling, which can compromise the entire mechanical system. Effective condition monitoring is therefore essential to prevent unexpected failures. Local gear tooth defects produce transient impacts, exhibiting nonlinearity in vibration signals. Wavelet-based high order spectra (WHOS) analysis has shown promise in extracting fault-related features from such signals. However, existing methods rely on manual selection of informative bifrequency bands, limiting physical interpretability and practical applicability. To address this, an Improved Instantaneous Wavelet Bispectrum Feature (IIWBSF) for gear fault diagnostics is proposed. It incorporates a novel strategy to optimize bifrequency band selection by quantifying the fault relevance of each sub-band. The methodology is validated on both simulated signals and experimental dataset collected from a gearbox test rig at KU Leuven. The dataset comprises tests on both healthy and faulty gears (artificially induced spalling) under various speeds and loads. Vibration signals are simultaneously captured by a Wireless MEMS sensors (WMS) and a traditional piezoelectric accelerometer. Compared with the conventional approach, IIWBSF achieves superior performance in detecting faulty gear teeth and accurately identifying their quantity, angular position, and relative severity. Moreover, its consistent results on both WMS and piezoelectric accelerometer demonstrate the practical potential for industrial applications where wired accelerometer installation is constrained.

title: A novel optimal control strategy for active suspension systems with control weighting coefficient dynamically adjusted based on operating conditions
abstract: Optimal control has been extensively used in vehicle’s active suspension control. However, the fixed control weighting coefficient is difficult to meet the dynamic changes in suspension performance requirements of vehicles at different speeds and road levels. This paper proposes an innovative optimal control strategy for active suspension systems with control weighting coefficient dynamically adjusted based on operating conditions, with the aim of ensuring a good ride comfort for vehicles under various operating conditions. Firstly, by using the theory of random vibration and the real integral residue theorem, the analytical calculation formulas of the performance evaluation index for optimal control active suspension systems are derived, and an effective control weighting coefficient characterization method is explored from a theoretical analysis perspective. Subsequently, an identification method of road roughness based on RIME-NARX neural network and vehicle ride comfort inverse model, and a real-time adjustment method of optimal control weighting coefficient based on performance evaluation index analytical calculation are established. Then an optimal control strategy for active suspension systems with control weighting coefficient dynamically adjusted based on operating conditions is proposed. The correctness of the established method is verified through bench test. Experimental results show that the proposed optimal control strategy can significantly improve the vehicle’s ride comfort while ensuring its safety. This study provides a new idea for optimal control active suspension systems’ design.

title: Dynamic modelling and vibration behaviors of shaft-blisk-coated-casing system with blade rubbing
abstract: To enhance the thrust-to-weight ratio of aircraft engines, the clearance between the blades and the coated casing has been progressively reduced, thereby increasing the likelihood of blade-casing rubbing. Therefore, to investigate the nonlinear behaviors induced by rubbing, a shaft-bladed disk-casing dynamic model incorporating component flexibility is developed in this study. First, dynamic models of the shaft, bladed disk, and coated casing are established using the finite element method. A beam-shell coupling technique is applied at the shaft-disk interface and a shell-shell coupling technique is utilized the blade-disk interface to facilitate the system’s dynamic modeling. Next, considering the effect of casing deformation and coating wear, a new blade-coated casing rubbing force model is proposed for the solid-element casing. Finally, the developed dynamic model is validated using measured modal characteristics and vibration responses, and the wear effect is indirectly verified by the measured rubbing force. The results indicate that due to the nonlinear bearing contact forces and nonlinear rubbing forces, the system spectrum shows harmonics of the rotational frequency, the bearing’s varying compliance vibration frequency, as observed in both the simulation and experiment. When a partial rubbing fault occurs at the blade tip, the tip experiences alternating stress as the rubbing intermittently occurs. Additionally, the additional stiffness effect induced by rubbing also causes noticeable frequency fluctuations in the time–frequency diagram of the casing.

title: Full-matrix microscopic ultrasound for 3D reconstruction of leakage microholes in thin-walled stainless steel
abstract: The spent fuel pool is constructed by welding stainless steel and is susceptible to corrosion, damage, degradation, and micro-leakage due to prolonged exposure to boric acid and high-radiation environments. Accurate three-dimensional reconstruction of defects is challenging with traditional methods because of the coarse grains in stainless steel, severe scattering attenuation, high background noise, and the complex morphology and small scale of micron-sized pores. In this study, we propose a novel method for detecting and 3D reconstructing internal micropores in stainless steel using an ultrasound microscope. The proposed method involves three key steps: (1) signal denoising and filtering using the adaptive sparrow search algorithm combined with variational mode decomposition (ASFSSA-VMD), (2) slice-by-slice threshold segmentation for image mask extraction, and (3) 3D reconstruction of the segmented masks using the Visualization Toolkit (VTK). The results show that this workflow effectively addresses the challenges of noise interference and segmentation accuracy, enabling high-quality 3D visualization of minor defect. The 3D microleak hole in the thin stainless plate can be shown visually. The results indicate that the maximum reconstruction error in the stainless steel base material is 0.2 mm, while the maximum reconstruction error in the stainless steel cladding layer is 0.5 mm. It provides robust technical support for the safety maintenance and defect characterization of spent fuel pools.

title: Composite disturbance rejection via continuous SMC and ESO for uncertain nonlinear systems with input constraints
abstract: This paper presents a continuous sliding mode control method (SMC) scheme integrated with an extended state observer (ESO) for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems subject to input constraints, external unknown disturbances, and model uncertainties. First, the non-ideal actuator characteristics (such as input saturation and dead-zone), unknown external disturbances, and system uncertainties are uniformly modeled as a composite disturbance term. The ESO is employed to perform real-time estimation and feedforward compensation of this disturbance. Building upon this framework, a second-order sliding surface and a novel control law synthesis mechanism are developed to suppress chattering while maintaining continuity of both the control signal and its derivatives. Furthermore, an adaptive update law incorporating the ESO estimation error is introduced, enabling accurate disturbance compensation and enhanced tracking precision. A rigorous Lyapunov-based analysis demonstrates the asymptotic convergence of the tracking error. Finally, experiments on two distinct platforms demonstrate the practical effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method under realistic operating conditions.

title: Automated high-resolution characterization of concrete crack pattern using wavefield-centric diagnostic framework
abstract: High-resolution characterization of concrete crack patterns using a minimal number of sensors remains a critical challenge in intelligent infrastructure diagnostics. This study proposes a wavefield-centric diagnostic framework that integrates acoustic-optical fusion sensing with wavefield image-driven model for crack parameterization. The ultrasonic wavefield for concrete crack sensing is generated using only a single excitation source. Non-contact optical sensing permits complete ultrasonic wavefield reconstruction across structural surfaces. The proposed model realizes automated crack characterization by extracting ultrasonic-crack interaction features from time-series wavefield images. The model is trained with 32,000 frames of wavefield images of the crack-interface. The results show that the mean localization error, as measured by the Chamfer Distance (DCD), was 0.586 ± 0.086 mm (95 % confidence intervals) through forty numerical cases. The crack length measurement achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.956. Experimental results from three concrete slabs confirm the framework’s effectiveness, with a crack localization error under 6 mm (DCD) and a length measurement error of less than 15 %. The proposed framework has considerable potential for application in the automated inspection and health monitoring of infrastructure.

title: Data-driven system identification using improved recurrent network for structure-borne noise in vehicle cabin
abstract: This study proposes a data-driven system identification framework for predicting structure-borne noise in vehicle cabins using real-world driving data. An Inception network, applied in the time–frequency domain, is combined with a linearized pseudo-time stepping method to enhance accuracy and generalization. Structural acceleration is used as input, and cabin noise as output, with both signals transformed via short-time Fourier transform. The model effectively captures hysteretic and nonlinear behaviors under various driving conditions. As a result, the proposed framework achieves improved prediction performance across multiple frequency bands and scenarios, demonstrating its potential for practical vehicle noise modelling.

title: Systematic error modeling and hybrid CMK compensation for high-precision non-contact angle measurement of ultrasonic micromotors
abstract: Ultrasonic micromotors are widely used in precision microsystems due to their small size and high electromagnetic compatibility. For millimeter-scale micromotors, accurate angle measurement provides the essential state information required for closed-loop control. However, the measurement process is easily disturbed by multiple-source errors, and the lack of systematic error modeling and effective compensation strategies makes high-precision angle measurement challenging. To address these issues, this study employs a TMR-based measurement platform to analyze major error sources, establish an error model, and develop a collaborative compensation method that combines deep learning with adaptive filtering. A systematic error model is constructed to account for gain deviation, zero offset, temperature drift, nonlinear errors, and random noise. Frequency-domain decomposition using the fast Fourier transform quantifies the energy distribution of deterministic and stochastic errors, revealing that approximately 70.9% of the error originates from learnable deterministic nonlinear components. Based on these findings, a hybrid compensation framework (CMK) that integrates temperature feedforward correction, adaptive sliding-window drift suppression, convolutional neural network (CNN)–multilayer perceptron (MLP) nonlinear modeling, and adaptive Kalman filtering is proposed. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the mean absolute error from 0.3166°to 0.0099°and lowers the root-mean-square error from 0.3784°to 0.0147°, achieving a compensation rate of 96.87%. The method also demonstrates excellent stability and robustness under long-term operation, with temperature variations ranging from 25 to 100 °C, electromagnetic interference, and changes in rotational speed. These results confirm that systematic error modeling combined with collaborative compensation provides a reliable, generalizable, and deployable high-precision non-contact angle measurement solution for ultrasonic micromotors.

title: Spatio-temporal variational reconstruction deep support vector data description for anomaly detection in bridge SHM data
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) systems are essential for ensuring infrastructure safety, particularly in the long-term evaluation of structures like bridges. However, factors like sensor malfunctions, traffic accidents, and data anomalies resulting from structural deformations can cause monitoring data to deviate from the actual structural response, significantly compromising the accuracy of assessment results. Existing anomaly detection methods often encounter challenges such as class imbalance, strong temporal dependencies, and spatial correlations in multi-sensor data. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel anomaly detection framework, Spatiotemporal Variational Reconstruction with Deep Support Vector Data Description (STVR-DeSVDD). First, the STVR-DeSVDD model integrates a graph attention network (GAT) with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network, enabling the model to effectively capture sensor interactions and their time-varying patterns. This approach addresses both temporal and spatial dependencies in multi-sensor data during long-term monitoring. Second, the model combines a variational autoencoder (VAE) with deep support vector data description (DeSVDD). By minimizing latent space reconstruction error and controlling hypersphere volume, the model improves the compactness of normal data and reduces the risk of hypersphere collapse, thereby refining the boundary between normal and anomalous data. Finally, a pseudo-data-driven adaptive thresholding method is proposed. This method incorporates physical information noise to dynamically adjust the detection boundary, allowing the model to adapt to changing detection criteria in multi-sensor and time-series data environments. Experimental validation using both a truss bridge model dataset and the Z24 bridge benchmark dataset demonstrates that STVR-DeSVDD outperforms traditional methods in anomaly detection, showcasing its substantial potential for practical applications.

title: A novel tool wear and remaining useful life prediction network based on multi-scale time–frequency information of milling force
abstract: Tool wear and remaining useful life (RUL) monitoring technology plays a crucial role in enhancing machining quality and reducing production costs. Nevertheless, prevailing methodologies predominantly focus on utilizing models to automatically extract features directly from temporal signal data, often overlooking the rich time–frequency information inherent within these signals, thus compromising the prediction accuracy of the models. Research indicates that time–frequency information associated with tool wear in cutting force signals is primarily concentrated within the vicinity of the tool’s rotational fundamental frequency and its harmonics. Therefore, this study proposes a network architecture (SRT-MFF-TWPN) for tool wear and RUL prediction based on multi-scale time–frequency information. Initially, the one-dimensional (1D) cutting force signals are transformed into two-dimensional (2D) time–frequency representations (TFR) through the Synchro-Reassigning Transform (SRT) to enhance the feature representation capability of the data. Concurrently, the Multi-Frequency Focusing (MFF) module is employed to automatically extract time–frequency features localized at the tool’s rotational fundamental frequency and its harmonics. The extracted time–frequency features are input as multi-channel features into the 1D convolutional neural network based on the DenseNet architecture, with the SE block adjusting channel weights to improve the model’s predictive capability. Finally, validation tests conducted on both the PHM2010 benchmark dataset and a self-constructed dataset demonstrate that, for identical backbone networks, data processed with the SRT-MFF method yields a marked improvement in the model’s predictive capability for tool wear and RUL.

title: An innovative diagnostic method for lubricant faults with multiple contaminants in journal bearings using acoustic emissions
abstract: In journal bearings, early and reliable detection of lubricant contamination is critical for fault diagnosis and condition-based maintenance. Acoustic emission (AE) technology, as a nondestructive testing method, can capture the minute energy releases associated with bearing faults and thus offers clear advantages for early fault monitoring in rotating machinery. Focusing on particulate and water contamination in journal-bearing lubricants, this paper proposes an AE signal processing and diagnosis framework that combines the Enhanced Feature Mode Decomposition (EFMD), Robust Median Difference (RMD), Adaptive Huber Synchrosqueezing Transform (AHST), and a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN). The EFMD builds on conventional FMD by introducing adaptive spectral-peak-based subband segmentation and a correlated-kurtosis-gain early-stopping mechanism, and, when combined with the RMD, enables the selection of frequency bands that carry the most fault-relevant information. The AHST leverages higher-order phase correction, Huber-loss-based adaptive weighting, and energy-driven smoothing windows to improve the accuracy of instantaneous-frequency estimation and the time–frequency energy concentration under noisy conditions. Comparative experiments conducted at rotational speeds of 900, 1200, and 1500 r/min under various particle and water contamination levels show that the EFMD-RMD-AHST scheme achieves higher and more stable classification performance on the tested platform, with average recognition accuracies exceeding 99 % for particle contamination and ranging from 98.30 % to 99.19 % for water contamination, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency under the considered operating conditions.

title: Bio-inspired caudal-fin-like downstream spoiler for enhancing power generation performance of an upstream piezoelectric wind-induced vibration energy harvester
abstract: Wind-induced vibration energy harvesting via piezoelectric transduction has received significant attention to implement the autonomous self-sustaining wireless sensor networks over the past few years. To offer a viable option for the performance improvement of an upstream Piezoelectric Wind-induced Vibration Energy Harvester (PWVEH), a bio-inspired Caudal-fin-like Downstream Spoiler is introduced to construct an enhanced PWVEH (CDS-PWVEH) in this paper. This conception is inspired by the swimming stroke of the whale taking use of the caudal fin to adjust the propulsion and direction. The proposed CDS-PWVEH was characterized by the easy-to-implement performance improvement, downwind excitation mode and strong robustness. The performance tuning of PWVEHs could be readily fulfilled by merely changing the angle of the caudal-fin-like spoiler without modifying the self-structure of the bluff body and piezoelectric vibrator. The theoretical analysis, computational fluid dynamics simulation and experiments were carried out to verify the feasibility of the proposed design and examine its performance. The results indicated that both distance-to-diameter ratio and CDS angle exerted a great influence on the output characteristics of the harvester. Also, there existed an optimal CDS angle to maximize the vibration amplitude of the cylindrical blunt body under a given distance-to-diameter ratio. Moreover, the CDS angle brough a more significant impact on the critical wind speed than the distance-to-diameter ratio. Additionally, the CDS-PWVEH could achieve the maximum output powers of 3.15 mW, 2.52 mW and 1.8 mW at 300 kΩ and 10 m/s with the CDS angle of 45°, 60°, and 75°, respectively. In practical application demonstration, the CDS-PWVEH could successfully power about 250 blue LEDs, electronic thermometer, and small-size LED screen.

title: Remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings considering sensor degradation
abstract: Rolling bearings are critical components in rotating machinery, and the prediction of their remaining useful life (RUL) is essential for ensuring operational safety and reliability. The accuracy of prediction is largely dependent on the quality of sensor data. However, during long-term operation, sensors exposed to harsh environments may degrade, leading to distorted data and reduced RUL prediction accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a framework for bearing RUL prediction that incorporates sensor degradation modeling. A joint degradation model is first constructed to characterize the coupled degradation of the bearing and sensor under real operating conditions. Then, a prior-enhanced multi-source joint estimation strategy is proposed, integrating historical data, calibration data, and real-time monitoring data to support hierarchical parameter estimation and dynamic updates. Kalman filtering is employed to estimate the bearing’s degradation state in real time. Finally, a composite dataset is constructed by combining actual bearing degradation data with simulated sensor degradation data for validating the proposed method. Experimental results indicate that the proposed approach enhances the accuracy and robustness of RUL prediction compared to conventional methods that ignore sensor degradation.

title: SOH-DLF: A double-loop framework for time-dependent system reliability analysis
abstract: Time-dependent reliability analysis quantifies the evolution of system failure probabilities under time-varying uncertainties, such as dynamic loading and material degradation. However, surrogate model-based methods still face challenges in sampling efficiency and modeling accuracy, particularly in high-dimensional problems and scenarios involving multiple failure modes. To address these challenges, this study introduces a double-loop time-dependent system reliability analysis (TSRA) framework based on the Safe Optimal Hypersphere (SOH) method, referred to as SOH-DLF. The main contributions of this study are as follows: First, a SOH-based Kriging-guided stratified learning strategy is developed, which automatically partitions the Monte Carlo sample space, reduces the candidate sample pool, and simultaneously parallelizes new samples to update the surrogate model, thereby improving sampling efficiency and modeling accuracy. Second, an enhanced SOH search strategy is implemented, integrating performance function information to provide better directional guidance and accelerate the convergence of the β-iteration search. Finally, by tightly integrating SOH-based sampling, Kriging surrogate modeling, and failure probability estimation, a closed-loop process is established. The effectiveness of the SOH-DLF framework is demonstrated through three numerical examples and one black-box engineering application, confirming its accuracy, computational efficiency, and broad applicability to complex time-dependent structural systems.

title: Autonomous aerial docking for compound VTOL UAVs with thrust vectoring rotors
abstract: This paper focuses on autonomous aerial docking of compound Vertical Take-Off and Landing (VTOL) Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) with thrust vectoring rotors for urban air mobility applications, in order to overcome the payload and endurance limitations inherent in each individual UAV. First, a novel compound VTOL UAV with thrust vectoring capability is introduced for the decoupling of position and attitude control. Next, a specially designed wingtip-embedded docking mechanism and the relative positioning module based on monocular vision are developed for in-flight assembly. Afterwards, the PID-based control strategy is developed for autonomous aerial docking of two UAVs, with one performing the docking maneuver and the other maintaining a stable hover state. In the end, the prototype of the compound VTOL UAV is constructed and preliminary outdoor flight experiments are conducted to validate the proposed autonomous aerial docking system.

title: An improved mass variation method for rapid prediction of position-dependent modal characteristics of large-scale machine tools using single-position modal data
abstract: Large-scale machine tools are extensively employed in the manufacturing of oversized structural components. However, their dynamic characteristics show significant position-dependent variation across the workspace, posing challenges for accurate measurement and dynamic analysis. The mass variation method has attracted attention for efficiently predicting position-dependent natural frequencies based on a single set of experimental modal data. However, by neglecting stiffness effects, it is mainly suited for small-scale machine tools and becomes significantly limited for large-scale machine tools with heavy, long-travel moving components. To address these challenges, this study proposes an improved mass variation method that integrates the mass–stiffness coupling effects arising from the motion of structural components. A coupled parameter transformation framework is developed, and a closed-form analytical expression is derived to estimate the variation of multi-order natural frequencies as a function of moving component positions. Unlike traditional approaches, the proposed method explicitly accounts for the change of both mass and stiffness caused by moving substructures, enabling accurate, high-fidelity predictions even under conditions of significant structural change. Numerical simulations confirm the method’s predictive accuracy across a broad range of modal orders and mass ratios. Furthermore, experimental modal analysis conducted on a large-scale gantry-type machine tool validates the robustness and practical feasibility of the proposed approach. These results demonstrate the method’s potential as a generalizable and efficient solution for position-dependent multiple-mode prediction in large machine tool systems.

title: Realistic 3D complex crack and engineering structure reconstruction based on adaptive stereo photogrammetry
abstract: The inspection of cracks in complex engineering structures is increasingly important, as crack characteristics serve as a key indicator for Structural Health Monitoring (SHM). However, accurately segmenting and realistically reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) complex cracks remains challenging in the field of civil engineering. To this end, this paper proposes a computer vision method, by introducing a fine-tuning Segment Anything Model (SAM), and further proposing an Adaptive View 3D Gaussian Splatting (AVGS). Firstly, in the two-dimensional (2D) domain, fine-tuning SAM is used to robustly segment cracks from multiple camera views. Then, in the 3D domain, AVGS is applied to realistically reconstruct 3D cracks and engineering structures, by developing adaptive sampling, spatially-aware densification, and multi-view geometric consistency. The proposed method has been applied in three complex practical engineering structures. Results show that the method can realistically reconstruct and segment both 3D engineering structures and detailed cracks. This capability will offer valuable technical support for advancing intelligent inspection and SHM applications, throughout the entire urban pre- and post-disaster process.

title: Uncertainty variations and quantification of motor bearing time-varying resistance–capacitance characteristics
abstract: During the operation of generators and drive motors, current breakdown conduction through bearings can cause electrical erosion, thereby reducing motor reliability and performance. This phenomenon results from mode-switching between the resistance–capacitance (RC) characteristics of the bearing. However, the transient variations of these time-varying RC characteristics remain insufficiently understood. To elucidate the uncertainty variation laws of bearing time-varying RC characteristics under realistic motor operating conditions, this study analyzes more than ten million bearing current breakdown conduction events across over five thousand transient and steady-state motor operating conditions. The influences and mechanisms of four key motor operating parameters—rotation speed, torque, rotation speed change rate, and torque change rate—on the time-varying RC characteristics (including equivalent resistance, equivalent capacitance, and RC mode-switching frequency) are systematically investigated. Based on these analyses, the boundary conditions of RC mode-switching are redefined, and a mixture density network is employed to model the mixed probabilistic distributions of RC characteristic parameters. Accordingly, a constitutive modeling framework based on interpretable descriptor surrogate models is developed to quantitatively characterize and probabilistically predict the uncertainty variations of bearing time-varying RC characteristics under both transient and steady-state operating conditions. This framework achieves high predictive accuracy while maintaining interpretability, simplicity, reliability, and generalizability. The proposed approach provides a theoretical foundation and modeling framework for the design and optimization of motor and bearing systems, offering potential strategies to suppress bearing currents and mitigate electrical erosion in generators and drive motors.

title: Domino-inspired energy harvesting system (DiEHS) with modular interlocking mechanism for reliable self-powered applications
abstract: With the rapid expansion of 5G technology, the growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and wireless sensors is advancing at an unprecedented pace, and their low power demands have stimulated advances in energy harvesting technologies. Inspired by the dynamics of dominoes, we propose a modular, interlocking mechanical energy harvester (MIMEH) that integrates a buckling beam with an electromagnetic power-generation unit. Parametric analysis of a single MIMEH module showed that increased beam thickness and indentation distance can boost voltage output by enhancing stored potential energy. When multiple modules are assembled into a modular array, a domino-inspired energy harvesting system (DiEHS) is obtained, with its voltage output scaling with the number of modules. Notably, the DiEHS array displayed contrasting behaviors: voltage amplification along the propagation path under low-energy input, and voltage attenuation under high-energy input. Nevertheless, the harvested energy by the DiEHS remains relatively stable across conditions, safeguarded by the bistable mechanism. The system’s practicality was validated by powering an IoT node, highlighting its promise for distributed sensing applications.

title: Data-driven diagnosis of wind turbines based on structural response data using environmental and operational conditions normalization and soft assignment methods
abstract: Data-driven structural health monitoring (SHM) frameworks are becoming an important part of the SHM practice due to ease of data collection and processing. Normalization of structural response data with respect to environmental and operational conditions (EOCs) is critically important for these data-driven frameworks as they do not use any baseline physical model and make predictions solely based on observations used in training. A key issue in real world experimental datasets collected for SHM is the lower quality of EOCs data available compared to structural response data. In this work, a strategy is proposed to extract features that correlate with EOCs from the high-quality structural response data. To do so, a mechanical model of the structure without and with structural damage is built and the response of the structure is simulated under different EOCs. Structural response features are regressed against EOCs and those that correlate with EOCs and are insensitive to structural damage are used for EOCs data normalization. Furthermore, a new approach based on soft assignment is introduced for EOCs data normalization and its performance is evaluated relative to the existing state of the art clustering in EOCs space approach. The efficiency of proposed methodologies is evaluated using the experimental and simulation datasets from a small scale research wind turbine located at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL).

title: The improved focusing of flexural waves by reconstructing a curved lens instead of the plane lens
abstract: Controlling the focusing of flexural waves in plates and shells is crucial for many regions, e.g., energy harvesting, structural health monitoring, and vibration control. Conventional plane lenses based on gradient index or meta-surface usually exhibit normal focusing behavior, resulting in a relatively low energy and larger focal spot size. To enhance the focusing performance, increase the focal energy, and further reduce the focal spot size, this work proposes a curved lens by modifying the traditional plane lens into a curved profile. Firstly, the design scheme is illustrated with the mechanism interpreted in detail. After that, the relationship of the phase of flexural waves versus the plate thickness is established based on the Timoshenko beam theory, utilizing which the curves lens is designed. Then, the frequency-domain analysis is carried out in the structural mechanics module of the COMSOL Multiphysics software, with the main performance indexes systematically compared with the traditional plane lens, including the focal position, energy concentration, and the focal spot size. Finally, experiments are conducted to verify the feasibility of the curved lens. Both numerical and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed curved lens can effectively improve the focusing effect, i.e., the energy concentrated has been increased, with the focal spot size reduced simultaneously. Especially, the lens exhibits the subwavelength focusing phenomenon, which can be controlled by the structure parameter. In addition, the lens can work normally in a frequency region centered the target frequency. Overall, the design scheme in this paper is applicative, which can also further extend into the lens design in acoustics and optics.

title: Cascaded self-attention hybrid model for synergistic prediction of tool wear and classification of surface roughness in the turning process
abstract: The condition of the tool serves as a critical factor influencing surface quality, with surface roughness being a crucial parameter that indicates the quality of the surface. Existing research has predominantly treated tool wear and surface quality monitoring as independent tasks, failing to effectively leverage the tightly coupled relationship rooted in their physical mechanisms. To address this, this paper proposes a Cascaded Self-Attention Hybrid Model (CSAHM) for turning processes. This model is built upon a multi-task learning framework, featuring a powerful shared feature extraction backbone composed of dual-branch 1D-CNN layers, bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM) layers, and multi-head self-attention mechanism layers. The innovation lies in the model’s adoption of a logically coherent cascaded prediction structure: the output from the upstream tool wear regression task is used as strong prior knowledge and fed into the downstream surface roughness classification branch, thereby providing a critical physical basis for classification decisions. This physically-informed architecture significantly enhances performance, improving surface roughness classification accuracy by over 8 % compared to Quasi-Shared Bottom Multi-Task Model (QSB-MTM). Validation on experimental data demonstrates the proposed model’s performance, achieving a maximum prediction error below 25 μm,and a surface roughness classification accuracy exceeding 93 %. Further comparative and ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of the proposed cascaded structure, self-attention mechanism, and synergistic learning framework. This research offers an effective new paradigm for the intelligent and synergistic monitoring of multiple parameters in manufacturing processes.

title: Stochastic dynamic response analysis based on the probability density function expression of MDOF nonlinear system response
abstract: Stochastic nonlinear analysis continues to pose significant challenges in contemporary research, particularly for complex nonlinear systems. In the present paper, an enhanced approach for response analysis of complex nonlinear dynamic systems is developed. First, the state space is partitioned into a series of subspaces of interest, and a virtual excitation is introduced into the governing equation. By integrating the principle of equation integration with nonlinear regression analysis, the high-dimensional nonlinear equation is effectively decoupled. Subsequently, a stochastic response analysis method is enhanced through reconstruction of the reduced governing equation, thereby establishing a quantitative relationship between the undetermined coefficients in the probability density function (PDF) and the governing equation. As a result, the PDF expression can be efficiently solved using the proposed improved method. Several numerical examples – including complex nonlinear dynamic systems such as nonlinear systems under filtered white noise excitation, and multi-degree-of-freedom hysteretic systems, etc – are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and broad applicability of the proposed methodology. The numerical results show that the probabilistic solutions are in good agreement with those obtained from simulations. Compared to existing methods, the enhanced approach significantly expands the scope of application and improves the convergence of the response analysis.

title: Hyper-Gain omnidirectional ultrasonic SH waves by overlapping dual Fabry-Perot Meta-Superstrates
abstract: Omnidirectional ultrasonic wave manipulation is critical for non-destructive evaluation and structural health monitoring due to its advantage in simultaneous monitoring of broad inspection areas. However, omnidirectionality inherently suffers from energy dissipation with distance, seriously harming inspection quality in the far field. Here, we propose novel elastic meta-superstrates (EMSs) to achieve extraordinary gain in omnidirectional ultrasonic SH wave emission. Each EMS creates dual Fabry-Perot cavities (an internal cavity and an edge cavity) that confine source energy and release it in a highly amplified manner under precise resonance conditions. Multiple EMSs can be overlapped for cumulative amplification, with the total gain proportional to the product of individual impedance ratios. We establish a rigorous theoretical foundation for this emission enhancement using an effective medium model and validate the gain principle with single and multiple EMS configurations. Numerical simulations and experimental results confirm the hyper-gain phenomenon, demonstrating excellent agreement with theoretical predictions. The proposed EMS concept provides a practical approach for enhancing the omnidirectional performance of ultrasonic transducers.

title: A co-designed on-rotor sensing and tacholess order tracking framework for robust fault diagnosis in marine electric propulsion systems
abstract: Fault diagnosis of marine electric propulsion systems (MEPS) is significantly challenged by non-stationary operating conditions, where varying speeds and loads cause severe spectral smearing that obscures fault signatures. Conventional methods, reliant on housing-mounted sensors and often impractical encoders, are further limited by signal attenuation. To address these issues, this study introduces an integrated hardware-algorithm framework that combines a novel wireless On-Rotor Sensing (ORS) system with a computationally efficient algorithm. The ORS system captures high-fidelity vibration signals directly from the rotating shaft, bypassing structural transmission paths to achieve an average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement of 90.3% over conventional sensors. It also enables real-time, tacholess speed estimation via centrifugal acceleration. Leveraging this data, we propose the Zero-Crossing Tacholess Order Tracking (ZC-TOT) algorithm. Unlike methods based on complex time–frequency transformations, ZC-TOT employs an event-driven zero-crossing strategy to extract instantaneous frequency with high efficiency. Benchmarked on a standard laptop, ZC-TOT processes 500,000-point datasets across varying speeds 25.9 times faster than the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), effectively eliminating spectral blurring. Experimental validation on a dedicated MEPS test bench, involving realistic speed and load transients with over ten repeated fault trials per component, demonstrates the framework’s transformative performance. The results show average SNR improvements of 92.6% for bearing outer race faults, 242% for inner race faults, 186.9% for gear faults, and 121.8% for propeller faults. This integrated solution establishes a single-sensor paradigm capable of simultaneous high-fidelity acquisition, tacholess order tracking, and real-time diagnosis for multiple MEPS components, demonstrating robust performance under hydrodynamic disturbances and representing a significant advance in marine propulsion diagnostics.

title: Toward performance-matched active line spectrum vibration control: A theory-guided sensor placement framework
abstract: Despite widespread adoption of active line spectrum vibration control (ALSVC), performance degradation across validation domains remains a critical barrier for large flexible structures. This paper derives a necessary and sufficient condition ensuring matched performance between local and global domains for ALSVC. Building upon this theoretical foundation, we propose a data-driven sensor placement method for commonly used output-feedback controllers. The method requires only limited model information and experimental data, making it practical for engineering applications. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulation and experimental case studies on an industrial-grade validation isolator.

title: Modelling and design of a bio-inspired dual-axis hybrid piezoelectric–electromagnetic energy harvester for perpendicular low-frequencies vibration collection
abstract: Vibration energy harvesting provides a sustainable solution for powering low-energy electronic devices. However, most existing harvesters suffer from narrow operational bandwidths, single-direction excitation sensitivity, and limited power output. This study presents a bio-inspired dual-axis hybrid piezoelectric–electromagnetic energy harvester that is capable of collecting vibrations in perpendicular directions through coordinated motions of a main wing–like beam and an aileron-like auxiliary beam. The proposed hybrid energy harvester consists of a main wing–like beam for piezoelectric strain energy conversion and a perpendicular aileron-like beam integrated with magnet–coil assemblies for electromagnetic induction, forming a dual-axis structure capable of capturing vibrations from multiple directions. Experiments demonstrate that the device can generate a maximum voltage of 9.555 V and a peak power of 13.862 mW at low frequencies (∼12–15 Hz). The hybrid transduction mechanism enables complementary high-frequency strain-based harvesting and low-frequency displacement-based harvesting, significantly enhancing overall energy conversion efficiency compared with single-mode designs. These results indicate that the proposed structure offers a compact and effective solution for broadband and multi-directional vibration energy harvesting suitable for various self-powered sensing applications.

title: Fast and accurate visual measurement of structural displacement using feature-enhanced polyphase decomposition
abstract: Vision-based displacement measurement techniques have garnered significant attention in structural health monitoring due to their advantages, including non-contact operation and full-field-of-view capabilities. Among these techniques, correlation matching is particularly notable as it allows for sub-pixel displacement measurements from video data. However, extracting structural displacement from large volumes of video data (thousands of time-delayed frames per measurement) poses several challenges. These include high computational demands and potential errors, especially in the presence of sparse structural features (e.g., textures or contours) within the video. To overcome these challenges, this study introduces a feature-enhanced polyphase decomposition method for more accurate and efficient displacement measurement. By applying morphological dilation to video data contained structural displacement, a complex amplitude model is constructed, yielding multi-feature amplitudes with enhanced discriminability. Within a video -to-reality mapping framework, the decomposed impulses between these amplitudes are analyzed through the combination of phase spectrum correlation matching and polyphase decomposition. This yields a geometric motion model for decomposed impulses, resolves sampling parity ambiguity, and enables precise displacement recovery. Compared to existing spatial- and frequency-domain correlation matching techniques, the proposed method significantly reduces computational time while maintaining high accuracy. It also maintains robust performance under varied conditions, including video s with sparse features, limited visibility, or complex backgrounds. The method’s superiority has been demonstrated through extensive simulations and experiments. In challenging low-contrast complex scenarios, it achieved a correlation coefficient value of 95.54% and a root mean square error value of 3.69, significantly outperforming existing methods. Moreover, it processes data up to 8 times faster than traditional methods.

title: Rotor eccentricity in electric machines: An analytical framework with experimental validation for fault diagnosis
abstract: Rotor eccentricity is a major fault in electric machines, as it distorts the air–gap magnetic field and generates unbalanced electromagnetic forces that can excite vibration and reduce reliability. While numerous studies have explored aspects of eccentricity, most remain fragmented, lacking a unified framework that connects electromagnetic modeling with diagnostic applications. This paper presents an analytical framework for fault diagnosis of rotor eccentricity, integrating mathematical modeling, predictive analysis, and multi-fidelity validation. A rigorous analytical model is first established to quantify electromagnetic force components arising from both static and dynamic eccentricity, clarifying their spectral characteristics. Based on this formulation, a predictive approach is developed to anticipate eccentricity-related fault features in a physically interpretable manner. The framework is validated through finite element analysis and experimental tests on a custom-designed motor with adjustable eccentricity, confirming its accuracy and practical feasibility. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach not only deepens understanding of eccentricity-induced electromechanical interactions but also provides a reliable basis for early fault detection in electric machines.

title: A novel robotic milling chatter monitoring framework based on types identification and frequencies estimation
abstract: Abstract Regenerative and low frequency chatter are prone to occur in robotic milling processes, significantly restricting both workpiece quality and machining efficiency. The chatter types identification and online chatter frequencies estimation are crucial for effective chatter suppression. Nevertheless, few studies concerning these aspects have been published in robotic milling. This research proposes a novel robotic milling chatter monitoring framework, which includes chatter types identification and online chatter frequencies estimation modules. To identify chatter types at an early stage, dual-tree complex wavelet packet energy entropy (DTCWEn) and weighted cumulative spectral distribution entropy (WCSDEn) are introduced from the time–frequency domain and frequency domain, respectively. Unlike entropy or statistical indicator used in previous works, WCSDEn takes into account both the frequency probability and the frequency values in the spectrum domain, making it more sensitive to spectral changes within the chatter band. According to the distribution characteristics of regenerative chatter and low frequency chatter frequencies, a chatter frequency search (CFS) algorithm is proposed. This algorithm integrates the estimation of signal parameters via rotational invariance technique (ESPRIT) for online chatter frequencies estimation. The proposed algorithm not only enables the online identification of multi-order regenerative chatter and low frequency chatter frequencies, but also achieves exceptionally high frequency estimation accuracy even with a limited number of data samples. The presented framework is utilized in robotic milling processes, and experimental results demonstrate that it effectively identifies chatter types and estimates chatter frequencies early.

title: Fully coupled nonlinear vibration characteristics of aerostatic spindle for precision-grinding
abstract: For the high-speed precision grinding process, multi-excitation loads act together to determine the complex motion behavior of the spindle. In order to accurately predict the transient dynamics, a thorough dissection of global synergistic effects is urgently needed to establish a dynamic model of the coupling between loads and vibration. In this paper, the interaction between multiple excitation effects is analyzed from the load-vibration variation characteristics, and the nonlinear dynamics characteristics is investigated under the consideration of multiple dynamic loads. The differential mesh iteration is utilized to obtain the dynamic air film excitations through Reynolds equation for the instantaneous air film variation due to spindle vibration. Based on the change of the magnetic gap path during machining, the unbalanced magnetic pulling force considering the effect of vibration response is calculated. The dynamic unbalanced eccentric load model is established by the derivation of relative position coordinates. The precision grinding force loads are obtained by determining the cutting mode based on the judgement of instantaneous chip thickness. In addition, an innovative iterative solution process for obtaining the vibration response under global load excitations is proposed to enhance the exactness of simulation modelling. The validity and applicability of the coupled model are verified through experiments. In this paper, the global coupled interaction idea is used to analyze the nonlinear dynamical behavior. The transient changes between multiple physical fields determine the complex and variable dynamic characteristics and amplitude curve trajectories. Due to the influence of different parameters, the distribution state of the air film inside the bearing varies significantly, which directly affects the machining accuracy.

title: Active and passive noise control based on Helmholtz resonator acoustic metamaterials and EDGF-HAFxLMS algorithm
abstract: To effectively enhance low-frequency noise control performance, this study combines Helmholtz resonator-based acoustic metamaterials with Active Noise Control (ANC) technology, proposing an innovative hybrid active–passive noise control method. First, an in-depth mechanism analysis is conducted on the thermal viscous effects in narrow ducts. Based on the theory of Helmholtz resonator-based acoustic metamaterials, a novel metamaterial structure with superior sound absorption performance is designed, and its effectiveness is validated through both simulation and experimental tests. Secondly, a feedback channel is introduced into the traditional FxLMS algorithm, resulting in the development of the Hybrid Adaptive FxLMS (HAFxLMS) algorithm, which enhances the algorithm’s adaptability to dynamic noise environments. To further optimize computational efficiency, a coprocessor is employed to replace the filtering module of the algorithm, leading to the creation of the Enhanced Dual-Generation Filter HAFxLMS algorithm (EDGF-HAFxLMS), which achieves higher noise reduction accuracy and real-time performance. Compared to the HAFxLMS algorithm, the runtime for processing 1 s of noise data is reduced by 77.42 %. Simulation results show that the average noise control performance for industrial and mixed noise is −15.39 dB and −14.34 dB, respectively, both outperforming other algorithms. The experimental results align with these findings, with average control performances of −13.94 dB and −13.16 dB, respectively. The hybrid active–passive noise control method demonstrates significantly improved effectiveness in suppressing low-frequency noise, further validating the advantages of this approach and providing a new technological path for low-frequency noise control.

title: A digital Twin–Driven performance correlation analysis method for wind turbine gearbox journal bearings
abstract: The higher-power demand of wind turbines limits the application of rolling bearings in gearboxes, making journal bearings a viable alternative. However, under low-speed and heavy-load conditions, planet gear journal bearings (PGJBs) are prone to performance degradation, such as the occurrence of wear and the transition of lubrication regimes. Performance of PGJBs is related to bearing design, manufacturing, and operating condition parameters, but how these parameters correlate to bearing performance remain unknown. To address this issue, a digital twin (DT)-driven performance correlation analysis method is proposed. First, a DT model of a PGJB is constructed by integrating a laser cladding (LC) module, a mixed elastohydrodynamic lubrication module, and a wear module. The DT model is experimentally calibrated with a dataset of a full-scale PGJB test rig. Subsequently, a refined XGBoost-SHAP approach is proposed to capture the nonlinear relationships between design, manufacturing, operating condition parameters and PGJB performance indicators and quantifies global and individual importance. Results show that PGJB design parameters play a dominant role in determining bearing lubrication and wear performance, followed by operating condition parameters and then manufacturing parameters. The most influential parameters are aspect ratio, LC layer thickness, and rotational speed. Besides, how these most influential parameters affect the oil film thickness, oil film pressure, maximum elastic deformation, and wear depth are revealed via detailed parametric analysis. This study provides theoretical guidance for the design and manufacturing of high-performance PGJBs in wind turbine gearboxes.

title: A piezoelectric energy harvester integrating frequency up-conversion and passive directional adaptive mechanism for multidirectional vibration environments
abstract: To address multidirectional vibration challenges, this study proposes FUC-PDAPEH, a piezoelectric energy harvester that integrates frequency up-conversion (FUC) with passive directional adaptation (PDA). Directional self-adaptation is achieved via a unidirectional bearing and an eccentric mass, while a rope–spring structure couples cantilever beams with discrete resonant frequencies for FUC implementation. Experimental and simulation results demonstrate strong agreement. Parametric studies reveal critical dependencies: the magnitude and distribution of the eccentric mass, along with excitation intensity, govern self-adaptive behavior, whereas spring stiffness, air gap, and rope length dictate output performance. When the excitation direction is perpendicular to the beam vibration, RMS open-circuit voltages increase by 21.1, 118.6, 172.1, and 44.2 times compared with fixed-direction harvesters. The harvester achieves a 5–14 Hz directional bandwidth, surpassing state-of-the-art designs. Under a 0.4 g excitation amplitude, maximum power reaches 59.66 mW. Practical demonstration confirms its capability to drive 138 LEDs while simultaneously powering various low-power electronic devices. The integrated broadband operation, full directional self-adaptation, and high power output of FUC-PDAPEH establish it as an ideal candidate for deployment in multidirectional vibration scenarios, particularly in remote seismic monitoring and structural health diagnostics.

title: A mechano-electromagnetic active decoupling design for a high-dynamic, large-stroke XY nanopositioning stage
abstract: This paper introduces a mechano-electromagnetic active decoupling paradigm for high- performance XY nanopositioning stages. The main contribution lies in redefining electromagnetic actuators as dual-function components that provide both motion generation and active dynamic constraints. This approach enables a radical simplification of the compliant structure, reducing the number of system modes and widening the frequency gap between parasitic and operational modes, thereby facilitating high-bandwidth control. A prototype stage integrating C-shaped leaf-springs with a parallel-kinematic actuator arrangement validates the concept. Experimental results confirm the benefits of the approach: an ultra-compact design (12.85% flexure area ratio) and a high modal separation ratio of 15.2. The stage achieves a large stroke exceeding 3.7 mm, a servo bandwidth of 140 Hz (a 576% extension relative to the open-loop natural frequency), and over 90 dB rejection of cross-axis and rotational coupling.

title: Dynamic modeling and analysis of defective bearings with thorough consideration of fluid-thermal-solid coupling
abstract: The internal operating environment of an actual bearing is a scenario of fluid-thermal-solid (FTS) coupling. However, due to the limited parameters considered in existing studies, the dynamic model and characteristics of defective bearings under FTS coupling have not been well established or understood. Therefore, this paper thoroughly considers the FTS coupling relationships among various important parameters, the interactions among the inner ring, outer ring, and sensor, the influence of nonlinear Hertz contact force, load, centrifugal force, friction force, and gravity, the changes of the actual contact angles, and the local defects that consider the shift distance and skew angle. A defective bearing dynamics (DBD) model that thoroughly considers FTS coupling is proposed. Then, the validity and accuracy of the actual contact angle theory, oil film theory, bearing thermal effect theory, and the proposed DBD model are verified through previous research and this paper’s bearing experiments. Finally, the dynamic characteristics of defective bearings under the FTS coupling effect are studied. The results indicate that the shift distance and radial clearance can decrease the impact of defects on the dynamic characteristics of bearings, the skew angle may either decrease or increase this impact, and the rotational speed helps to increase this impact.

title: A frequency domain time-delay identification method for drag-free control systems
abstract: In this paper, a method for the identification of system delays is proposed for drag-free control applications. Within a multi-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) system, the concept of a pseudo-impedance function is introduced. The relationship between the pseudo-impedance function of the time-delay system and that of the uncontrolled system is derived. The “frequency”of the difference between the pseudo-impedance function of the time-delay system and that of the corresponding uncontrolled system is identified as the system’s time delay. This delay can be determined using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) applied to the difference between the two pseudo-impedance functions. In both simulation and experimental tests, the frequency response curve of the time-delay system is obtained. However, the frequency response curve of the uncontrolled system is unavailable, which prevents direct calculation of its pseudo-impedance function. To address this limitation, the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) algorithm is employed to remove the trend line of the time-delay system. This trend line effectively represents the pseudo-impedance function curve of the uncontrolled system. Additionally, the impact of the system’s noise on the identification results is examined. To enhance the algorithm’s capability to extract signal features from noisy data, the parameters of the VMD algorithm are optimized using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Finally, the algorithm is simulated and tested in the multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. In experimental tests, white noise is introduced into the control loop to further refine the time delay identification process. Both simulation and experimental results indicate that the proposed identification algorithm achieves high recognition accuracy.

title: Multi-output classification using a cross-talk architecture for compound fault diagnosis of motors in partially labeled condition
abstract: The increasing complexity of rotating machinery and the diversity of operating conditions, such as rotating speed and varying torques, have amplified the challenges in fault diagnosis in scenarios requiring domain adaptation, particularly involving compound faults. This study addresses these challenges by introducing a novel multi-output classification (MOC) framework tailored for domain adaptation in partially labeled target datasets. Unlike conventional multi-class classification (MCC) approaches, the MOC framework classifies the severity levels of compound faults simultaneously. Furthermore, we explore various single-task and multi-task architectures applicable to the MOC formulation-including shared trunk and cross-talk-based designs-for compound fault diagnosis under partially labeled conditions. Based on this investigation, we propose a novel cross-talk architecture, residual neural dimension reductor (RNDR), that enables selective information sharing across diagnostic tasks, effectively enhancing classification performance in compound fault scenarios. In addition, frequency-layer normalization was incorporated to improve domain adaptation performance on motor vibration data. Compound fault conditions were implemented using a motor-based test setup and evaluated across six domain adaptation scenarios. The experimental results demonstrate its superior macro F1 performance compared to baseline models. We further showed that the structural advantage of RNDR is more pronounced in compound fault settings through a single-fault comparison. We also found that frequency-layer normalization fits the fault diagnosis task better than conventional methods. Lastly, we analyzed the RNDR with various conditions, other models with increased number of parameters, and compared with the ablated RNDR structure.

title: Broadband performance of a rotating piezoelectric energy harvester with bending-torsion composite and magnetic nonlinearity
abstract: A bidirectional bistable bending-torsional piezoelectric energy harvester is designed to capture magnetic excitation in two directions under low-speed time-varying and high-speed steady input conditions. A nonlinear electromechanical coupled mathematical model is established for the harvester. Numerical methods are employed to analyze the effects of nonlinear forces, excitation conditions, and structural parameters on the vibrational response and power generation performance. The study reveals the bidirectional magnetic excitation provides dual frequency bands for low-and high-speed regions, while the nonlinear energy sink broadens the low-speed band. Additionally, the number of excitation magnets can effectively enhance energy harvesting performance in the medium-to-high speed range, ensuring continuous energy conversion between low-and-high speed regions. Experimental results demonstrate that the harvester can successfully illuminate LEDs and power a wireless Bluetooth sensor at 115 rpm, 200 rpm, and 600 rpm, whereas the device fails to activate without the nonlinear energy sink. Moreover, the wireless Bluetooth sensor operates normally at wind speeds from 4 m/s to 12 m/s, overcoming the bandwidth limitations inherent in resonant piezoelectric oscillators.

title: Multi-fidelity robust design optimization for ride comfort of wide-body mining dump trucks under uncertain environments
abstract: Wide-body mining dump trucks play a crucial role in the mining process. However, the pronounced undulations commonly present in unpaved excavation areas pose significant challenges to extending vehicle service life and improving ride comfort. In practice, uncertainties arising from operational environments and manufacturing tolerances, coupled with the difficulty of constructing high-fidelity models from limited data, further complicate performance optimization. To address these issues, a multi-fidelity robust optimization framework is proposed. Within this framework, the wide-body mining dump truck is first modeled theoretically, and both low-fidelity and high-fidelity datasets are generated through ADAMS/CAR and EASY5 co-simulations. Subsequently, the multi-fidelity curriculum learning (MFCL) method is employed, wherein a clustering-based strategy determines the training scheme, enabling the integration of multi-fidelity data for rapid and accurate vehicle performance prediction. Furthermore, a non-dominated sorting hippopotamus optimization (NSHO) algorithm is developed, yielding superior Pareto frontiers in multi-objective optimization tasks. Finally, considering realistic mine road conditions, a physical-scene simulation is constructed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Under the combined influence of environmental fluctuations and design tolerances, the multi-fidelity robust optimization of vehicle ride comfort reduces the mean RMS value of the vertical sprung mass acceleration by 7.2% and its variance by 88.2%.

title: Active and collaborative Bayesian calibration of model parameters and bias
abstract: Calibration of computational models to minimize the discrepancy between model prediction and observations is a fundamental yet challenging task in modern computational science. The root sources of uncertainties resulting in this discrepancy can be complex, but can generally be captured by quantifying the uncertainties of model parameters and model bias. Thus, the numerical problem for joint calibration of model parameters and model bias has attracted widespread attention, but is extremely challenging, especially when the simulators are expensive to evaluate. To fill this gap, a new modular Bayesian inference methodology framework, named active and collaborative Bayesian calibration, is developed based on Bayesian numerical methods, where model bias is described using the Gaussian Process models. By reformulating the calibration problem as an equivalent optimize-then-integrate nested problem, a Bayesian algorithm is then developed for inferring the hyper-parameters of model bias and generating training samples for model parameters in a sequential manner, which allows for collaborative calibration of both model parameters and bias with high efficiency. The upper confidence bound function is generalized to identify the hyper-parameters of model bias, and the posterior error contribution function, is developed for actively enriching the training data set and further updating the trained GPR models.
