The ghost feature factor s is introduced to control the number of ghost feature mappings generated by linear transformations within the Ghost layer, increasing the quantity of feature mappings in the network to enhance representational capabilities with minimal computational and parameter overhead. Moreover, the Gradient Harmonizing Mechanism (GHM) Loss function addresses the class-imbalance issue by dynamically adjusting the gradient weights of each sample to achieve a balanced gradient distribution. The comprehensive performance of GBAMNet with respect to classification accuracy and inference velocity are validated by a series of experiments on the class-imbalanced dataset. Overall, our proposed system will promote the actual applications of Terahertz non-destructive testing (THz NDT) scenarios for automatic and real-time defect characterization.

title: Prototype-routed multi-source unsupervised domain adaptation framework for RUL prediction via online fine-tuning
abstract: The domain shift issue is often encountered in prognostics and health management (PHM) domain due to variable operating conditions, load fluctuations, environmental changes, etc. A common limitation lying in the existing transfer learning methods for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is their reliance on a rigid offline training paradigm, which leads to distinct challenges for two commonly used transfer learning methods: the domain generalization (DG) methods suffer from unreliable performance, while unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) methods are constrained by high- and costly-data requirements. To overcome these limitations, we propose a prototype-routed multi-source unsupervised domain adaptation framework via online fine-tuning (PR-OFT) for RUL prediction in this paper. Specifically, a prototype-routed degradation stage identification (PDSI) model is designed firstly, which integrates an efficient Mamba-based feature extractor with a novel prototype-guided supervised contrastive learning strategy to precisely identify the health state stage of target sample in real time. Based on the online identified stage, a candidate knowledge base is then dynamically constructed and enriched via a pseudo-domain augmentation strategy. Furthermore, the framework precisely routes and matches the optimal knowledge for the target sample, executing a one-time and distribution-aligned online fine-tuning to instantly generate a personalized predictor. The proposed PR-OFT framework follows a novel paradigm of generalizing at training and adapting at testing, i.e., it requires no exposure to target domain data during training and dynamically constructs personalized predictors for individual unlabeled target samples arriving in a data stream during inference. The proposed PR-OFT method is experimentally validated on two publicly available bearing datasets as well as a hard disk drive dataset, where the proposed method consistently outperformed several state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its outstanding predictive performance and strong generalization capability.

title: A synchronized estimation method for time-varying vehicle states via hybrid of cubature Kalman filter and long short-term memory network
abstract: The autonomous driving system relies on time-varying states such as longitudinal velocity, lateral velocity, yaw rate, and centroid sideslip angle to achieve safe and stable control. However, the high cost of high-precision sensors hinders their widespread adoption in mass-produced vehicles, making state estimation techniques critical. To improve estimation accuracy and robustness, this paper proposes a hybrid LSTM-based cubature Kalman filter (HLCKF), which integrates a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network into the Cubature Kalman Filter (CKF) framework. Firstly, a nonlinear system model is constructed to provide physical support for the estimation. Then, a Multi-output Head and Peeking-Coupled LSTM (MHPC-LSTM) is designed and embedded into the CKF to reduce the impact of model uncertainty and sensor noise on CKF prediction. Lastly, the predictive performance of MHPC-LSTM and the state estimation of HLCKF are validated by constructing a simulation platform. Experimental results show that the proposed MHPC-LSTM outperforms traditional model-based methods and standard LSTM networks in terms of both prediction accuracy and robustness, making it suitable for the CKF prediction phase. Further analysis indicates that the HLCKF surpasses both standalone CKF and LSTM methods in estimation accuracy and output stability, while maintaining an inference time that satisfies the real-time requirements of autonomous driving systems.

title: A single-domain generalization framework integrating Zernike-Based detail blur feature extraction and Mamba global attention mechanism
abstract: In recent years, single-source generalization (SDG), which involves training with only one source domain and generalizing to multiple target domains, has garnered widespread attention. However, the current research focus is primarily concentrated on the generation of pseudo-domains. Methods used for generating pseudo-domains inevitably introduce unnecessary noise or produce unreliable features. Therefore, this paper proposes a single-domain generalization framework integrating Zernike-based detail-blurred domain-invariant feature extraction and the Mamba global attention mechanism, focusing on extracting domain-invariant features from a single source domain. Firstly, Zernike moments are utilized to conduct further feature extraction on the features transformed by Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). In combination with the selective mixup method, the high-order Zernike moments that depict noise and other details are discarded, while the integrative expression of the middle and low-order moment features is enhanced. Consequently, preliminary detail-blurred domain-invariant features with summarizing properties are obtained. To enhance the expression of single-domain features while maintaining their domain invariance, a novel Global-Local Feature Fusion Model (GLFM) is constructed. The Mamba Attention-Guided Global Feature Extraction module (MGFE) aims to extract global features, while the Convolutional Local Feature Extraction module assisted by spatial attention (CLFE) aims to extract local features. These two types of features are fused and selected through the Fusion Selection Module (FSM) to enhance useful features and suppress less useful ones. Experiments were conducted on 12 single-domain generalization tasks across the CWRU and BJTU datasets. The proposed method demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance, with average accuracies of 98.48% and 95.38%, respectively.

title: Frequency estimation and parallel control for multi-disturbance rejection: Application to image-stabilized piezoelectric tip-tilt stages
abstract: In astronomical observation, line-of-sight (LOS) accuracy is constrained by unknown disturbances and sensor-induced delays. This paper proposes an adaptive modular framework that incorporates frequency decomposition and estimation into parallel control channels, enabling structurally independent suppression of multiple narrow-band disturbances under sensor delays. Firstly, a cascaded and order-reduced parallel filtering framework is proposed to decouple multi-frequency disturbances into single-frequency components, thereby simplifying estimation and reducing computation. To address inherent image sensor delays, a frequency-based fractional time-delay compensation strategy is incorporated to ensure phase alignment with the delayed feedback, particularly in the high-frequency range. Finally, a small-gain stability analysis is performed to guarantee robust closed-loop performance under the proposed adaptive scheme. Experimental validation on an image-based piezoelectric tip-tilt stage demonstrates that the proposed method enhances multi-disturbance rejection up to the Nyquist frequency.

title: Enhanced H∞ loop-shaping control with virtual sensor fusion for active seismic vibration isolation
abstract: Ultra-low-frequency seismic vibration remains a major performance bottleneck for precision engineering platforms, such as metrology instruments, semiconductor equipment, and large-scale scientific facilities. To address this challenge, this work presents an enhanced H∞ loop-shaping framework integrated with a virtual sensor fusion architecture to meet these requirements in active seismic vibration isolation systems. The proposed formulation employs carefully constructed weighting functions to shape the loop for stringent low-frequency disturbance rejection while maintaining adequate robustness margins. To further mitigate the influence of unmodelled high-frequency dynamics—factors known to degrade H∞ controllers—a frequency-partitioned sensing scheme is introduced. Complementary filters allocate low-frequency feedback to physical sensors, ensuring accurate regulation, and high-frequency feedback to virtual sensor channels, effectively conditioning the control loop against adverse high-frequency dynamics. Experimental validation on a three-degree-of-freedom isolation platform demonstrates that the resulting controller achieves up to 65 dB reduction in transmitted motion within the target 0.1–10 Hz band. These results confirm that the proposed synthesis approach not only enhances practical seismic isolation performance but also extends the theoretical applicability of H∞ loop-shaping methods in systems where sensing constraints and broadband uncertainties are coupled.

title: Mode-resolved, reconfigurable particle damping for printed circuit boards vibration control
abstract: Printed circuit boards (PCBs) operating in harsh vibrational environments are prone to cracking and mission-critical failures. This study proposes a reconfigurable, partition-enabled particle damper (PD) whose cavity can be rapidly switched between single- and multi-unit configurations without redesign. Mode‑resolved sine-sweep tests on a PCB, combined with discrete element method (DEM) simulations, quantify vibration attenuation at the first two bending modes and clarify the underlying damping mechanisms. Energy‑budget analysis shows that inelastic normal collisions and tangential friction dominate dissipation, whereas rotational effects are negligible; their relative contributions vary strongly with filling ratio. DEM further reveals distinct mode-dependent particle‑motion regimes: a collect-and-collide state at the first resonance, and a gas-like state at the second, consistent with the measured frequency-dependent performance. Parametric studies demonstrate that damping efficiency is highly sensitive to particle material, size, and filling ratio, while cavity geometry in the present design space plays a secondary role. An empty‑cavity control confirms that the observed vibration reduction arises primarily from granular dissipation rather than added mass. Compared with existing PCB vibration studies that use fixed particle dampers or address single-mode response, this work (i) introduces a reconfigurable, partition-enabled PD that can be rapidly switched between single- and multi-unit layouts without redesign and (ii) systematically links DEM-resolved energy dissipation mechanisms to mode-resolved PCB experiments. The resulting framework provides physics-based, practically oriented design guidelines for implementing granular damping in high-reliability electronic systems.

title: Quantification of model uncertainties in regional-scale seismic analysis of building portfolios
abstract: Seismic events are characterized by abrupt onset, wide spatial impact, and substantial destructive potential, often leading to cascading socioeconomic consequences. At the regional scale, seismic assessment faces two persistent challenges: (i) building inventories typically lack complete, high-resolution structural information, and (ii) refined nonlinear models are computationally prohibitive for large portfolios. Against this background, this paper develops simplified multi-spring models for building portfolios in regional-scale seismic analysis. Specifically, the modeling framework consists of a lumped-shear multi-degree of freedom (MDOF) model for multi-story building, and a lumped flexural-shear-coupling MDOF model for high-rise buildings. Moreover, two types of parameters (i.e., coarse-scale and fine-scale) are compared in model generation, which are based on the building-level attributes and the component-level capacity characteristics, respectively. Both the parameter variability and seismic uncertainties (i.e., individual and combined parameter) are incorporated during the simulation to assess the demand variations. The results show that the simplified representation preserves essential seismic response characteristics while enabling high computational efficiency suitable for regional applications. To further enhance reliability, a lognormal-based probabilistic revision strategy is introduced to calibrate coarse-scale seismic demand statistics (median and dispersion) using fine-scale reference data. The resulting framework provides a practical and efficient solution for seismic assessments at a regional scale, particularly for diverse building portfolios.

title: Simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressure process based on machine learning-enhanced Hermite polynomial model
abstract: Accurately simulating non-Gaussian wind pressure fields on low-rise building roofs is critical for wind-resistant reliability design. This paper proposes a machine learning-enhanced Hermite polynomial model (ML-EHPM)-based method for the rapid and precise simulation of stationary non-Gaussian wind pressures. Building upon traditional moment-based HPM simulation methods, this study develops two machine learning models to enhance simulation accuracy and efficiency. First, in determining the ML-EHPM-based translation function, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), combined with the Bald Eagle Search optimization algorithm, is used to establish a nonlinear mapping from the first ten-order raw moments to the statistical moments of the translation function. This processing eliminates the need for integral solutions and monotonic interval constraints. Subsequently, a backpropagation neural network (BPNN) is employed to map non-Gaussian power spectra to Gaussian power spectra. To validate the simulation performance, three univariate simulation cases (strongly non-Gaussian, non-monotonic regions, and bimodal distributions) and one multivariate simulation case are given. Results indicate that the ML-EHPM approach offers substantially improved simulation accuracy than the conventional HPM method. Additionally, it can also simulate wind pressures in non-monotonic regions where the traditional HPM method is unavailable. Therefore, the proposed method provides a practical and efficient tool for high-precision simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressures.

title: Deep learning-based mechanism- and signal-driven framework for early prediction of milling surface roughness
abstract: As a key part of intelligent machining systems, surface roughness prediction plays a vital role in improving machining efficiency and ensuring product quality. However, the prediction accuracy of traditional mechanism-based physical models is restricted by idealized assumptions, whereas data-driven approaches rely excessively on monitoring signals, limiting their ability to capture future machining information and lacking model interpretability. To address these issues, this study proposes a deep learning-based mechanism- and signal-driven framework for the early prediction of milling surface roughness. First, a physical model of surface morphology is established by comprehensively accounting for the tool rigid motion trajectory, runout, and deflection. The global mechanism knowledge generated by the physical model is embedded into the data-driven modeling process. Second, multi-source signals are synchronously monitored online during machining, and preliminary multi-domain features are extracted from the time-series data to support subsequent modeling. Third, an integrated mechanism- and signal-driven Transformer (IMSformer) is constructed, consisting of the deep mechanism knowledge mining module, deep signal feature extraction module, mechanism-signal fusion module, and regression prediction module. Mechanism knowledge and signal features are jointly used as inputs to IMSformer, enabling the prediction task through deep extraction and fusion of high-level representations. Experimental validation is conducted under both the same and different conditions using milling data collected from a machining center, demonstrating the superior performance of the proposed framework.

title: A power-law signature framework for cross-structure decoding and inverting thermal effects in ultrasonic structural health monitoring
abstract: Ultrasonic non-destructive testing (NDT) plays a critical role in structural health monitoring (SHM), yet its reliability is frequently undermined by temperature-induced nonlinear modulation of acoustic signals, which obscures genuine structural responses. To address this fundamental challenge, this paper introduces a groundbreaking Power-Law Signature Framework (PLSF) that enables high-fidelity decoding and inversion of thermal effects in ultrasonic wave propagation. By projecting ultrasonic signals into a high-dimensional vector space, the PLSF characterizes temperature-driven variations through a set of orthogonally decoupled power-law characteristic vectors, which inherently capture the nonlinear thermoacoustic interactions while maintaining stable functional mappings within consistent temperature regimes. Extensive experimental validation on reinforced concrete beams demonstrates the framework’s exceptional accuracy, achieving temperature inversion errors below 0.3°C and feature value errors within 5% across diverse structural configurations. The PLSF not only provides a novel pathway for quantifying thermoacoustic phenomena but also offers a computationally efficient and physics-interpretable tool for real-time temperature compensation and damage diagnostics in complex engineering environments.

title: Dynamic target-aware multi-objective reinforcement clustering for intelligent fault diagnosis
abstract: In recent years, intelligent fault diagnosis has faced great challenges due to the lack of labeled data and the complexity of dynamic industrial conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dynamic Target-Aware Multi-Objective Reinforcement Clustering (MORC) framework for unsupervised intelligent fault diagnosis. MORC models the deep clustering task as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), in which an intelligent agent dynamically assigns cluster labels and optimizes feature learning, cluster allocation, and exploration strategies through multi-objective rewards. The proposed triple reward mechanism integrates reconstruction accuracy, cluster compactness, and entropy maximization, effectively balancing exploration and exploitation to prevent mode collapse. Furthermore, an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) encoder provides stable representation targets, while a dynamic cluster update mechanism adapts to evolving feature spaces. Experimental results on benchmark fault datasets demonstrate that MORC achieves superior clustering accuracy, stability, and adaptability compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: Influence of roughness-dependent interface contact behavior on vibration characteristics of blade with under platform dampers
abstract: This study investigated the nonlinear vibration of blades with under-platform dampers (UPDs), explicitly incorporating the effect of contact interface roughness. A novel dynamic analysis method was developed, where the rough interface is represented by a statistical ensemble of asperities following a Gaussian distribution. Based on this representation, the nonlinear normal contact force was derived from probabilistic contact mechanics, and the tangential force was modeled using Coulomb friction. These forces were integrated into a few-degree-of-freedom blade model formulated via the Assumed Mode Method (AMM), with the blade simplified as a lumped-mass beam. The model was validated through frequency-sweep tests on a dedicated rig, which also serve to identify the structural damping ratio. A parametric study quantitatively evaluated the influence of preload, excitation force, contact angle, and surface roughness on UPD performance. Key findings indicate that optimal damping requires higher preload at increased excitation levels, and that smaller contact angles promote vibration suppression by maintaining a friction-dominated regime. Crucially, neglecting surface roughness is shown to lead to a significant overestimation of damping performance. Therefore, the design of both blades and UPDs must comprehensively account for surface treatment (roughness), the preload-excitation interplay, and contact angle.

title: Phoneme-inspired acoustic frame embedded lightweight transformer for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Acoustic-based fault diagnosis has gained increasing attention due to its flexibility and applicability under diverse operating conditions. Recent studies have demonstrated that Transformer-based architectures exhibit remarkable capability in modeling long-range temporal dependencies, so they are particularly effective for complex time series representation and analysis. However, applying Transformers to acoustic fault diagnosis faces the following critical challenges. The primary hurdle lies in discriminating short-duration nonstationary acoustic features amidst complex environmental interference, Simultaneously, how to ensure model diagnostic performance under limited computing resources is a challenge. Inspired by the phoneme processing paradigm where continuous speech is discretized into meaningful units, this paper proposes a lightweight acoustic segment-frame embedded Transformer, termed ASFE-Transformer, to address these issues effectively. First, an Analytic Amplitude-Phase Representation Module is introduced to derive physically meaningful representations, ensuring that the instantaneous evolution characteristics of multidimensional acoustic signals are faithfully retained. Second, an Acoustic Frame Embedding Module is developed to aggregate continuous analytic samples into a single token during the embedding stage. This strategy generates a more efficient token sequence and explicitly enhances the discriminability of transient fault cues while substantially reducing the computational burden. Third, the feed-forward network of the Transformer is redesigned by proposing a novel Swish-Depthwise Gated Linear Unit. By embedding a lightweight depth-wise convolution within the Swish-activated gating mechanism, this module introduces local contextual awareness into the encoder. Comprehensive experiments on two bearing acoustic datasets verify that the proposed framework delivers robust diagnostic performance with a lightweight design and highlight its strong potential for real-world industrial deployment.

title: Integrated design of Low-Frequency circumferential acoustic stealth composite structure under Deep-Water wave incidence
abstract: With the shift toward lower frequencies in active sonar systems, conventional acoustic coatings struggle to achieve efficient attenuation of meter-scale low-frequency sound waves within confined centimeter-scale thicknesses. To address this challenging issue in the domain of underwater acoustics, a novel embedded large-scale active–passive composite acoustic plate has been developed. Designed with Fx-LMS active control theory, this composite structure integrated giant magnetostrictive materials (GMMs) embedded in a viscoelastic rubber substrate. Through the structural design, electromagnetic system analysis, radiate plate shape optimization, and boundary constraints simulation, the vibro-acoustic performance of the active control unit was enhanced. Meanwhile, the peak source level of single active control unit exceeded 150 dB and the lower limit of the operational frequency range was expanded to 236.37 Hz. Based on different array topology configurations, combined with the theory of low-frequency phased arrays, an optimal layout was derived for large-scale plates. The circumferential active acoustic stealth performance of optimal configuration under oblique incidence conditions was further explored, demonstrating effective noise reduction exceeding 10 dB for narrowband oblique incidence within ± 30°. The secondary noise increase in the non-controlled regions was effectively suppressed by over 5 dB. This active–passive composite thin-plate provides a novel approach for acoustic field regulation and noise suppression of underwater vehicles, demonstrating certain scientific and practical value.

title: Machining chatter detection using optimized VMD with multi-metric adaptive mode selection and hierarchical weighted permutation entropy
abstract: Chatter is a key factor limiting the high-quality and high-efficiency machining of components. Therefore, research on machining chatter detection technology is of great significance. The combination of variational mode decomposition (VMD) and multiscale entropy is commonly used for signal processing and feature extraction in chatter detection. However, this method faces challenges such as difficulty in setting key parameters, a single criterion for selecting high-quality intrinsic mode functions (IMF), low sensitivity to local signal variations, and the need for manual comparison for IMF selection. To address these issues, this paper proposes a new method for machining chatter state detection. Firstly, the Newton-Raphson-based optimizer (NRBO) is employed to optimize the parameters of VMD and develop the NRBO-VMD algorithm. During the optimization process, the permutation entropy and envelope entropy ratio (PEER) are used as the composite fitness function, with the minimum PEER value as the optimization target for NRBO. This approach determines the optimal parameter settings for VMD to decompose the original machining signal. Subsequently, a multi-criteria fusion adaptive IMF selection algorithm based on the reciprocal of spectral entropy, energy ratio, and Spearman rank correlation coefficient was proposed. The algorithm evaluates the quality of each IMF decomposition signal from multiple dimensions to identify IMF sensitive to machining chatter characteristics for signal reconstruction. Finally, hierarchical weighted permutation entropy (HWPE) and support vector machine (SVM) are used for feature extraction and state classification of machining chatter. Through simulation experiments, the proposed NRBO-VMD algorithm and multi-criteria fusion adaptive IMF decomposition signal selection algorithm are verified to have superior performance in processing chatter signals. To further verify the effectiveness of the proposed chatter state detection method, a series of comparative experiments were conducted on a machining chatter dataset. Experimental results show that under two different cutting parameter settings, the proposed method achieves average accuracies of 98.21% and 98.89% in machining chatter state identification tests. Under variable cutting parameter conditions, the method proposed in this paper achieves a testing accuracy of 98.53%. In addition, the detection window time required by the proposed chatter detection method is only 0.03 s. The superiority of the machining chatter detection method proposed in this paper is verified through comparisons with other machining chatter detection methods.

title: Integration of ATMD-structure coupling system identification with semi-active vibration control of high-rise buildings under unknown wind loads
abstract: Recent advances have been made in integrating structural identification with vibration control to develop cost-effective smart structures. However, there is a lack of research on the integration of identification with vibration control of high-rise buildings under unknown wind loads. Moreover, the control device-structure coupling effect needs to be considered in the identification due to large-scale damper control devices used in buildings. To address these gaps, this paper proposes a novel method that integrates system identification with semi-active control of the active tuned mass damper (ATMD)-structure coupling system of high-rise buildings under unknown wind loads. First, the full-order ATMD-building coupling system is reduced by a reduced-order control strategy, and the state of the reduced-order model is transformed to modal coordinates, while the ATMD state remains in physical coordinates. Then, the modal Kalman filter with unknown input (MKF-UI) method is employed to identify the state of the reduced-order model under unknown modal forces. The identified state is used to estimate the semi-active force using the linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) algorithm and the Hrovat control strategy. Finally, the semi-active control force is applied to mitigate structural dynamic responses in real time. To validate the proposed method, a wind-excited benchmark building equipped with the ATMD is investigated under wind tunnel excitation. Additionally, ± 15% uncertainties in building stiffness are considered to demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method.
keywords: Modal Kalman filtering with unknown input

title: Instantaneous frequency identification of time-varying and nonlinear structures using extremum squeezing transform
abstract: Time-frequency energy divergence affects the identification accuracy of instantaneous frequencies for time-varying and nonlinear civil structures, especially with small and slow frequency variation ranges. To improve the frequency band identification capacity of the local maximum synchrosqueezing transform, an extremum squeezing transform method has been proposed, in which the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is first applied to response signals for time–frequency spectrum and coefficients. Then, a recursive segmentation operator is established to calculate the local minimum frequencies corresponding to the minimum STFT coefficients between two adjacent continuous curves in the binary graph of the STFT result. After that, the time-varying cut-off frequency curves are attained by arranging the local minimum frequencies at each time point in an ascending and connecting the arranged local minimum frequencies in chronological order, by which means the time–frequency spectrum segmentation is achieved. Subsequently, the estimated instantaneous frequencies are calculated by taking the partial derivatives of STFT coefficients with respect to time. Finally, an extremum squeezing operator is constructed to retain the estimated instantaneous frequencies that are equal to the frequency corresponding to the peak of the STFT coefficient within each time–frequency spectrum segmentation, enhancing the energy aggregation of the frequency bands. The feasibility of the proposed method has been verified against a simulated two-component signal with closely-spaced modes, a simulated two-component signal with nonlinear frequencies, a numerical shear frame with time-varying stiffnesses, a simulated three-component signal with nonlinear frequencies and an experimental reinforced concrete shear wall structure with time-varying and nonlinear behaviors. The analysis results demonstrated that the proposed extremum squeezing transform algorithm well extracted the instantaneous frequencies of these numerical and experimental structures by providing better energy aggregation and precision than the current local maximum synchrosqueezing transform algorithm.

title: Mechanism of the bias error for fiber optic gyroscopes induced by the damping-system nonlinearity
abstract: When fiber optic gyroscopes (FOGs) are installed in the inertial navigation system (INS), significant FOG bias errors may appear under vibration environments, even if the FOG is free from angular motion and violent linear vibrations are greatly attenuated by the damping system in the INS. The reason lies in the unclarified nonlinear behavior of the damping system, which has impeded the deployment of FOGs in high-precision applications. In this work, the mechanism of the FOG bias error induced by the damping-system nonlinearity is comprehensively analyzed, including the generation of higher-order harmonic stresses induced by the damping-system nonlinearity, the transmission of mechanical stresses inside the FOG, and the propagation of errors in the FOG optical and electrical signals. Particularly, we found that, as multiple-frequency harmonic stresses induced by the damping-system nonlinearity simultaneously act on the FOG, significant bias errors are generated through the beating among multiple frequencies in the demodulation process. Experimentally, the bias error of the FOG is evaluated under different damping-system nonlinearities. Under the 30 Hz/6g sinusoidal vibration, as the nonlinearity ratio declines from 1.71 × 104 m−2 to 1.00 × 102 m−2, the amplitude of the third-harmonic stress acting on the FOG decreases from 1.6 g to 0.1 g, consequently reducing the FOG bias error from 0.0445 °/h to 0.0118 °/h, which coincides with numerical simulation results. This work lays theoretical foundations for optimizing the damping system as well as the FOGs in the INS under vibration and is also applicable to the mechanical and material design of absorbers in the damping system.

title: Disbond imaging of adhesive joints using low-rank representation of Lamb waves
abstract: Adhesive joints play a vital role in the aerospace and automotive industries, where non-destructive defect detection is critical for ensuring structural reliability. Lamb wave testing using a scanning laser Doppler vibrometer (SLDV) provides a full wavefield inspection approach that enables visualization of wave propagation and its interaction with damage. However, developing an automated wavefield imaging method for adhesive joints that transforms the measured wavefield into interpretable damage maps, without requiring manual tuning of imaging parameters based on material or dispersion properties during the wavefield process, remains a challenging task. In this paper, an unsupervised disbond imaging approach based on low-rank representation (LRR) is proposed. This method considers the propagation nature of Lamb waves within the LRR framework: In a pristine structure, the waves propagate stably, governed by a finite number of wave modes; while defects introduce localized perturbations, causing localized wave scattering or amplitude attenuation. Accordingly, the wavefield can be decomposed into a low-rank background, representing the pristine wavefield, and sparse deviations, capturing defect-induced perturbations. Based on this LRR, the time and frequency domain wavefields are segmented frame by frame to extract disbonds induced perturbations. An imaging technique is then constructed based on the extracted perturbations. Finally, experimental validations were conducted on two adhesive joints with various disbond sizes, including an aluminum lap joint and an aluminum-CFRP (Carbon Fiber Reinforced Plastic) adhesive joint. Quantitative comparison and evaluations are made with weighted root mean square and multi-time instantaneous wavenumber analysis, using the high-frequency ultrasonic C-scan as a reference. The improved performance highlights its effectiveness for reliable non-destructive testing and evaluation (NDT&E) of adhesive joints.

title: Digital twin of a pipe conveying fluid: Flow rate anomaly detection and quantification via multi-fidelity Kalman filters and event based cameras signals
abstract: This work is motivated by the need for scalable Digital Twins (DT) for hydro turbines. We propose a DT framework using Bayesian algorithms embedded with machine learning techniques to study a simplified pipe conveying fluid (PCF) system. The Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) is employed for parameter identification by estimating the unknown flow rate that excites the pipe by leveraging the known nonlinear dynamical equations. Experimental validation using event-based camera data and a 3D reconstruction algorithm demonstrates the effectiveness of the UKF, estimating the flow rate with an average estimation error of 6%. To enhance scalability and enable real-time anomaly detection, a Linear Kalman Filter (LKF) is coupled with Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD). DMD is trained on the states estimated by the UKF, providing physical insight to the data-driven model order reduction method. This embedded LKF-DMD approach reduces the complexity of the model and accelerates the computation by three orders of magnitude, from 12 s to 1 0 − 3 s per iteration. When the flow velocity changes, anomaly detection is performed by applying a steepest-ascent hill climbing method which quantifies the change in entropy of the distribution of the Euclidean distance between the trained DMD modal phase diagram and the LKF estimates. The integration of the UKF for system identification, and the accelerated LKF-DMD for state estimation and anomaly detection within a unified DT framework, which have been validated using the lab-scale PCF setup, highlights the potential of these techniques to develop scalable and predictive maintenance tools for engineering systems. • A Digital twin framework of a pipe conveying fluid is proposed. • An efficient approach reconstructs the 3D pipe motion with event-based cameras. • The integration of Bayesian methods enhanced with a data-driven technique is provided. • Anomaly detection and quantification through parameter identification is performed. • Validation is realized with a true experimental setup in real-time.

title: Adaptive control of pneumatic servo system based on fuzzy inversion
abstract: The novel, adaptive, nonlinear control algorithm is specifically designed for pneumatic servo systems. The derivation is based on innovative modeling approaches. A key contribution is a new fuzzy model for valve operation, which effectively handles typical nonlinearities of proportional valves, provides short execution time, and ease of inversion. Thanks to these features, this solution is suitable for real-time implementation on DSP boards. In addition, a modified LuGre friction model is introduced, featuring position- and velocity-dependent bristle stiffness and simplified deflection dynamics. This model uses only two tunable parameters, which makes it adaptable and experimentally accessible. It also incorporates a fuzzy model for steady-state friction, enhancing its applicability across various pneumatic drive systems. The final control algorithm integrates three fuzzy models – for friction and both valves – and relies on fuzzy inversion of the valve model. The stability of the closed-loop system is rigorously proven using Lyapunov methods, ensuring uniform ultimate boundedness. Despite the complexity of its theoretical foundation, the controller is easy to tune and practically implementable on standard DSP hardware. Experimental results and simulations confirm that the controller performs reliably even with a significant uncertainty of the model, unmodeled dynamics, and external disturbances. Moreover, although physical constraints such as pressure, voltage, and speed are not explicitly addressed in the design, the controller was easily adjusted to respect these limits during operation. In general, the proposed method demonstrates strong performance, practical feasibility, and potential for broader use in pneumatic control systems.

title: Damping oil visco-elastic characterisation and modelling framework in high-frequency tuned mass dampers for boring bar applications
abstract: Tuned mass dampers (TMDs)- regarded as a passive damping element, integrated into the boring bar, enhance dynamic stability. However, maintaining optimal damping remains a challenge due to the complexity of studying (i) viscous- and (ii) elastic- characteristics of the damping oil at high frequency excitations (≥450 rad/s). The coupled dynamic interactions in the TMD-boring bar-tool holder system hinder the independent viscous and elastic characterisation. In addition, simplified models cannot capture their distinct frequency-dependent characteristics. To address this challenge, the present work proposes and demonstrates a comprehensive visco-elastic characterisation and modelling framework for damping oils under high-frequency TMD oscillations. This includes the development of a novel test rig to isolate the TMD dynamics, enabling controlled oscillatory testing of low-, medium-, and high-viscosity damping oils. The newly proposed characterisation framework exploits the stiffness-controlled frequency response of the test rig to quantify the oil response- loss and storage stiffness due to viscous and elastic characteristics. The visco-elastic constitutive model is then calibrated against the measured response to capture the frequency-dependent oil behaviour. Results from the experimental and modelling efforts reveal that (i) the high-viscosity oil exhibits pronounced elastic effects at high frequencies, negatively impacting the TMD by detuning, (ii) medium-viscosity oils demonstrate superior damping characteristics, offering broadband energy dissipation, (iii) the calibrated constitutive model predicts the visco-elastic responses within 15% error, and (iv) oil response is linear visco-elastic in nature. This indicates that the proposed framework enables frequency-specific damping oil selection, ensuring optimal TMD performance across operational conditions.

title: Acousto-optic tomography-holography: quantitative imaging of the 3D nonlinear air-coupled emission field of damaged composites
abstract: Defects in structures alter the propagation characteristics of ultrasonic guided waves. Contact-type defects, such as cracks and delaminations, can induce non-classical nonlinear phenomena under sufficiently high excitation. In addition to generating nonlinear elastic wave components within the material, nonlinear acoustic wave components are radiated into the surrounding air environment. Analysis of this nonlinear air-coupled emission (NACE) enables a novel approach for remote damage detection and localization. This study introduces an acousto-optic tomography-holography imaging method to quantitively visualize the NACE field from Scanning Laser Doppler Vibrometer (SLDV) measurements. Instead of measuring the sample’s surface, the SLDV probes the air column above the sample according to the acousto-optic principle. A fixed reflector with a predefined line grid is scanned to acquire one-dimensional (1D) fan-beam projections of the NACE field. The test sample is then rotated, capturing projections across the full angular range. This set of 1D fan-beam projections is subsequently processed via tomographic principles to reconstruct a two-dimensional (2D) planar cross-section of the NACE field. Finally, acoustic holography is employed to extend the 2D planar reconstruction into a three-dimensional (3D) volumetric representation of the NACE field. The proposed acousto-optic tomography-holography imaging method is first demonstrated on a numerical dataset collected from a 3D finite element model of a cross-ply carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) containing a kissing bond defect. Experimental validation is conducted on a CFRP plate containing a delamination defect. Both numerical and experimental results confirm the high performance of the developed tomography-holography approach to quantitatively reconstruct the defect-induced NACE fields, demonstrating its potential for damage detection applications.

title: Stochastic stability of a two-degree-of-freedom vibro-impact system driven by non-Gaussian colored noise
abstract: Vibro-impact systems are prone to stochastic instabilities when operating under random parametric excitations, yet a comprehensive stability analysis for multi-degree-of-freedom configurations remains a challenge. This paper presents the first analytical framework for quantifying the stochastic stability of a two-degree-of-freedom vibro-impact system driven by non-Gaussian colored noise, extending moment-Lyapunov-exponent methods to coupled non-smooth dynamics. The original non-smooth dynamics are transformed into an analytically tractable system via the Zhuravlev coordinate transformation, while the excitation is equivalently modeled as a one-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. The pth moment and largest Lyapunov exponents are derived asymptotically using the singular perturbation method, with excellent agreement observed with Monte Carlo simulations, thereby validating the analytical approach. A comprehensive parametric study reveals that stability is compromised by increasing noise intensity D and deviation coefficient r0, but is mildly enhanced by longer correlation time τ0. For system parameters, stability is significantly improved by a higher damping ratio c, albeit with diminishing returns for c > 4, and a lower restitution coefficient r. Crucially, the mass ratio a governs stability sensitivity when a < 5, while a stiffness ratio b exceeding unity is profoundly destabilizing and can induce D-bifurcation. These findings yield concrete design guidelines: maintaining b < 1, maximizing c, and optimizing mass distribution for a < 5. This study provides both a validated methodological framework and quantitative principles for the design and optimization of robust vibro-impact systems in stochastic environments.

title: Hybrid generative-probabilistic machine learning approach for predicting residual tensile strength and elastic modulus of FRP coupons under environmental exposure
abstract: The continuous deterioration of concrete and masonry structures has increased the demand for rehabilitation and strengthening of aging civil assets. Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites have been utilized to enhance the structural capacity of deteriorated structures. While these composites can be used in various environments, their performance is often compromised after exposure to harsh conditions, leading to a reduction in the structural capacity of the strengthened elements. Therefore, understanding the post-exposure residual performance of FRP composites, specifically residual tensile strength and elastic modulus is crucial for developing effective rehabilitation strategies. However, predicting the post-exposure performance of FRP coupons is inherently complex due to the involvement of multiple environmental and material parameters, as well as limited experimental data. This challenge necessitates the implementation of innovative modelling approaches to enhance both prediction accuracy and reliability and potentially mitigate the limitations of available small datasets. To address these challenges, this study employed credible synthetic data generated by advanced generative models, specifically a conditional tabular generative adversarial network (CTGAN) and a tabular variational autoencoder (TVAE), for machine learning model development. Moreover, probabilistic neural networks (PNNs) and natural gradient boosting (NGB) models were developed to predict the residual tensile strength and elastic modulus of FRP coupons and quantify the prediction uncertainty. The results indicated that the TVAE synthesizer demonstrated greater capability for generating credible synthetic data for predictive model development than the CTGAN synthesizer. Furthermore, the NGB model exhibited marginally better performance than the PNN model in predicting the residual tensile strength and elastic modulus of the FRP coupons, achieving testing coefficient of determination values of 0.9635 and 0.9914, respectively. In addition, the Shapley additive exPlanations feature importance analysis was employed to evaluate the influence of input parameters on the predictions, providing valuable insights into the performance evaluation of FRP composites under exposure conditions.

title: Prestress evaluation of steel strands based on interwire energy dissipation of longitudinal guided waves
abstract: Accurate evaluation of the prestress of steel strands is crucial for ensuring the safety of structures such as cable-stayed bridges and prestressed concrete bridges. Ultrasonic guided waves, with low attenuation and long propagation distance capabilities, have been introduced for the prestress evaluation of steel strands. However, the complex helical structure of the peripheral wires causes mode aliasing and multipath interference of the guided waves, affecting the reliability of the evaluation results. Therefore, this paper adopts a central straight wire single-path excitation-reception strategy to ensure the mode purity and path clarity of guided wave propagation. And based on this strategy, a dimensionless Prestress Evaluation Index (PEIE) is further proposed. First, the energy dissipation mechanism of longitudinal guided waves caused by friction contact between steel wires was analyzed theoretically. Subsequently, tension tests were conducted on steel strands to validate the feasibility of the PEIE-based method for prestress evaluation. Additionally, numerical simulation methods were employed to improve the amplitude and energy attenuation models of longitudinal guided waves propagating along the central straight wire under prestress. The results indicate that the amplitude and energy of guided wave signals decrease linearly with prestress, while the PEIE shows a linear increase with prestress. The optimal agreement between simulation and experiment is achieved with an interwire friction coefficient of 0.1, as evidenced by the minimal relative deviations in the linear fit (8.76% for slope, 6.06% for intercept) of the PEIE-prestress relationship. Both the amplitude and energy attenuation coefficients increase linearly with increasing prestress. The improved attenuation models accurately characterize the attenuation behavior under the coupling effect of propagation distance and prestress, with determination coefficients of 0.9932 (amplitude) and 0.9935 (energy). The established prestress-propagation distance two-variable PEIE model lays the foundation for the quantitative evaluation of prestress in steel strands.

title: Trade-off analysis for active suspension systems: A novel performance-based preset-trajectory method
abstract: This paper investigates the trade-off relationships between arbitrary pairs of control objectives in active suspension systems. A novel integrated approach that combines performance-based preset trajectories with error-based active disturbance rejection control (EADRC) is proposed. First, preset trajectories are constructed within a performance envelope using predefined transient performance indices. Based on the tracking errors between the actual and preset trajectories, a generalized suspension model is then established to comprehensively analyze trade-offs between pairwise combinations of three critical objectives: ride comfort, road holding, and suspension deflection. Subsequently, an EADRC law is designed, with closed-loop stability rigorously proven via Lyapunov theory, and analytical upper bounds for each decoupled control objective are derived. Furthermore, a systematic parameter selection guidance is provided to meet the performance requirements. Last but not least, numerical simulations and experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively achieves desired transient performance and avoids singularity issues. Additionally, this method provides a systematic framework for handling multi-objective trade-offs in vehicle suspension control.

title: Lamb wave-based cross-domain damage identification for CFRP composite structures using a modular deep learning framework
abstract: Machine learning in Lamb wave-based damage identification has significantly advanced diagnostic technologies due to its exceptional feature extraction capability in processing massive monitoring data. However, existing methods still exhibit significant limitations in identifying damage at locations not covered by the training data, which severely hinders their practical engineering applications. To address this, this study proposes a cross-domain damage identification method for CFRP composite structures based on a modular deep learning framework. The framework architecture integrates three core modules: a multi-channel signal fusion module, a feature extraction module, and a domain adaptation regression module. The multi-channel signal fusion module enhances the characterization of damage features by integrating Lamb wave damage-scattered signals from multiple sensing paths. The feature extraction module employs continuous wavelet convolutional layers to realize adaptive extraction and interpretability enhancement of sensitive features of Lamb wave signals. The domain adaptation regression module introduces a novel joint distribution adaptation approach, significantly improving the model’s generalization performance for unseen damage locations. Lamb wave signals are collected using the lead zirconate titanate (PZT) sensors array on a composite stiffened panel and an aluminum plate, covering four cross-domain damage localization tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significantly lower localization errors in identifying unseen damage locations compared to the existing state-of-the-art damage localization methods. Meanwhile, the framework maintains its excellent cross-domain generalization ability under scenarios involving variations in damage size, material, and structure.

title: Implementation of distributed multichannel active noise control with intermittent communication and coprocessor assisted data combination
abstract: Multichannel active noise control (MCANC) with distributed control offers a more computationally efficient alternative to traditional centralized schemes by leveraging multiple low-cost controllers. In this distributed MCANC (DMCANC) architecture, each node, comprising an error microphone, a loudspeaker, and a local controller, collaborates through mutual data exchange to refine global control filters and improve overall noise attenuation. However, communication network issues may affect the system’s stability. Therefore, an intermittent communication DMCANC (IC-DMCANC) system is developed to improve the system’s robustness, where each ANC node exchanges data at flexible intermittent and possibly heterogeneous communication instants, determined by hardware capability and network conditions. Moreover, with the aim of preventing instability caused by non-communication phases and transmission delays, the weight-constrained filtered reference least mean square (WCFxLMS) algorithm is used for iterative updating of each node. To further alleviate the computational and communication burden of each node, a coprocessor is introduced to be responsible for the data fusion and then send the combined result to each node for updating the parameters in the WCFxLMS. Thus, the proposed IC-DMCANC with coprocessor assisted (IC-DMCANC-CPA) system is more efficient and easier to implement. The numerical simulation results validate the satisfactory noise reduction performance of the proposed method compared to the centralized method. Furthermore, the real-time experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the IC-DMCANC-CPA system in a real scenario.
keywords: Weight-constrained filtered reference least mean square

title: Utilization of acoustic emission signals for monitoring CFRP drilling quality with AI-based methods: evaluation, prediction, and morphological reconstruction
abstract: Drilling Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers (CFRP) is a critical process in composite manufacturing, but ensuring high precision and quality poses significant challenges. The presence of defects such as delamination, fraying, and rough hole walls directly impacts the material’s performance and durability. Conventional quality control methods often involve post-process inspection, which is time-consuming and cannot prevent defects during manufacturing. There is a need for real-time, non-destructive monitoring methods to maintain high-quality standards while improving efficiency. This study aims to develop an advanced approach for real-time monitoring and prediction of CFRP drilling quality using Acoustic Emission (AE) signals and state-of-the-art machine learning models. A robotic drilling system was employed to conduct the experiments. During drilling, AE signals were collected, and hole edge images were captured using an industrial camera. White-light confocal profilometry was used to acquire hole wall morphology data. Relationships between drilling parameters and hole quality were analyzed, alongside AE signal features. Advanced AI models were proposed, including a probabilistic drilling stage identification model, K-means-based defect evaluation, a Transformer-based real-time defect monitoring model, and a VAE-Transformer hybrid model for reconstructing hole wall morphologies from AE signals. The proposed models successfully characterized drilling defects and enabled precise identification of drilling stages. Real-time defect monitoring based on AE signal slices showcased high accuracy, while the reconstruction model effectively predicted hole wall morphologies. This study introduces a transformative approach for real-time, non-destructive CFRP quality monitoring during drilling, significantly enhancing production efficiency and ensuring defect-free manufacturing in aerospace and automotive applications.

title: Design and motion control of an auto-adjusting center-of-mass mechanism
abstract: An unmanned deformable vehicle represents a novel reconfigurable robot that transitions between a vehicle state and a humanoid state. To enhance the stability during this reconfiguration, an auto-adjusting center-of-mass mechanism was developed for the vehicle. By studying the motion control of the slider in the mechanism, the vehicle’s center of mass can be adjusted to keep the system’s zero moment point (ZMP) centered within the support domain. An electromechanical dynamic model for the auto-adjusting center-of-mass mechanism was created. Furthermore, a kinematic model for the vehicle’s reconfiguration process was developed using homogeneous coordinate theory, with a reconfiguration stability criterion established based on Newton–Euler theory. To improve stability during reconfiguration, the slider’s displacement was controlled using a fuzzy-PID controller. In addition, a velocity look-ahead anti-shock rapid motion planning method based on quintic polynomials was devised to minimize motion shock while enhancing slider velocity. An integral sliding mode controller, optimized through the whale optimization algorithm (WOA), was used to track the slider’s velocity, ensuring smooth motion. Simulations and testing showed that by controlling the slider’s displacement and velocity in the auto-adjusting center-of-mass mechanism, the slider could quickly reach its optimal position without shock, thereby significantly improving the stability of the vehicle’s reconfiguration.

title: Thermo-mechanical coupling-induced strain anomalies in ballastless track slabs: mechanistic insights from embedded GFRP-OFBG sensors
abstract: Temperature gradients inducing warping deformation of ballastless track slabs is a prevalent phenomenon. Most studies have focused on the long-term effects of temperature-induced warping, but systematic research on dynamic strain responses remains limited. This gap complicates our understanding of thermo-mechanical coupled (TMC) behaviors. This study explored the nonlinear TMC mechanism in the strain response. It attempts to better understand and monitor track structures in real time to detect structural anomalies, improve railway safety, and optimise maintenance. We used GFRP-OFBG sensors combined with CEEMDAN time–frequency decomposition to process strain signals. Then, we established a finite element model of the CRTSIII ballastless track to determine the critical gradient threshold. The main findings include: 1. Strain Reversal Effect: When ΔT/Δx ≤ −10 °C/m, the upper track slab exhibits tensile strain, while the lower SCC layer demonstrated compressive strain. When ΔT/Δx ≥ 30 °C/m, the situation alters significantly. 2. Strain Superposition Effect: When ΔT/Δx ≤ −10 °C/m, warping deformation modifies load transmission pathways. The strain response patterns at different positions and layers within the composite slab exhibit variability, with five peaks in the track slab’s center and four troughs in the non-central area of the SCC. The strain anomalies enrich our understanding of track structure behaviour and provide a new perspective for fault diagnosis in structural health monitoring systems (SHM). By analysing anomalous strain patterns, the warping of the track structure can be determined. Furthermore, identifying the gradient thresholds that alter strain behaviour and load transfer mechanisms enables the development of practical strategies to mitigate the impacts of extreme climatic conditions. Establishing the relationship between strain signals and algorithms can further enhance the intelligence and diagnostic capabilities of SHM systems.

title: Multi-sensor collaborative imputation for probability distributions of missing data in structural health monitoring: a multiple distribution-to-distribution regression approach
abstract: Data loss remains a pervasive challenge that significantly undermines the effectiveness of structural health monitoring (SHM) systems. While the SHM community has developed diverse missing data imputation methods that involve replacing missing values with plausible estimates, conventional approaches exhibit significant limitations in compensating the distribution information of missing data. For instance, it is essential to ensure that the imputed data approximately follow the distribution of true missing data; failure to do so can result in substantially biased statistical estimates. However, conventional imputation methods in SHM lack this guarantee. The copula-based imputation method addresses this limitation but requires reliable distribution imputation. Furthermore, consecutive large-scale data loss can result in significant loss of distributional information, thereby diminishing the detection capability of damage identification methods that rely on hypothesis testing to identify changes in the distributions of damage-sensitive features. Therefore, distribution imputation techniques are necessary to compensate for this information loss. The emerging distribution-to-distribution (DTD) regression method can effectively impute distributions of missing data; however, current implementations are limited to univariate regression models that cannot account for the synergistic effects of multiple variables on outcome distributions, often resulting in significant bias in missing data imputation. This study proposes a new DTD regression approach to address this limitation. The main contributions include (1) developing a multiple DTD regression model to handle complex dependent scenarios, where multiple predictors jointly influence the distributions of the target sensor; (2) constructing a multivariate Nadaraya-Watson-type estimator for the regression operator with a computationally efficient bandwidth selector; and (3) proposing a novel distributional correlation coefficient for collaborative sensor selection. Simulation and real-data results confirm the superiority of the proposed method. Its engineering utility is demonstrated by application to strain monitoring data of a long-span bridge.

title: Vibration analysis of the propulsion shaft system caused by motor manufacturing imperfections based on electromechanical dynamic model
abstract: Manufacturing tolerances are inevitably introduced into the permanent magnet synchronous motor due to stamping die precision and process-related die wear. Revealing the mechanism of the typical stator and rotor core manufacturing imperfections on electromechanical vibration characteristics can provide references for the selection of manufacturing tolerances, thereby enabling the design of a propulsion shaft system permanent magnet synchronous motor with lower vibration and processing costs. Therefore, a developed electromechanical coupling dynamic model of the propulsion shaft system considering permanent magnet synchronous motor manufacturing tolerances is proposed. The current vector control, the permanent magnet synchronous motor magnetic equivalent circuit model, and the flexible rotor-bearing subsystems of the coupling model are comprehensively included, and interaction relationships among these subparts are fully demonstrated. The shape function method utilized in the traditional magnetic equivalent circuit model is developed to precisely quantify the air gap permanence under rotor displacements, and the correctness of the coupling model is verified by the finite element method and the experiment. Based on the proposed coupling model, the effectiveness of five kinds of stator and rotor manufacturing imperfections on the time–frequency characteristics of the electromagnetic excitations and propulsion shaft system vibration is studied. The manufacturing tolerance selection interval of the permanent magnet synchronous motor in this study is given, and the spectral characteristics of each imperfection are obtained, which can provide theoretical guidance for the diagnosis of permanent magnet synchronous motor manufacturing imperfections.

title: On the BIBO stability of passive control structures
abstract: This paper investigates the stability mechanism of a class of engineering structures incorporating a single passive controller. The passive controller under consideration is composed of springs, dampers, and inerters, and can be characterized by positive-real functions. Rather than providing only sufficient conditions or investigating a specific structure, this work establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for the bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability of a general multi-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) system with an arbitrary linear passive controller. It is demonstrated that the BIBO instability arises either from the resonant coupling among substructures and the passive controller, or from the absence of strict passivity in both the main structure and the controller. Moreover, this work reveals the instability of structures with multiple natural frequencies, and provides a theoretical justification for controller placement at either the bottom or the top in engineering practice. The developed results can be conveniently used to determine the stability of various engineering structures, including vehicle suspension systems, isolation systems, and building systems incorporating tuned-mass-damper-type (TMD-type) controllers. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed results.

title: Reduced-order modeling of bolt loosening: application to a pair of oscillators under transverse shock excitation
abstract: The safety and integrity of engineered structures are critically dependent on maintaining sufficient preload in their bolted joints. This preload can be dynamically lost due to sustained vibrations or sudden shock that are large enough to induce slip in the threads. While high-fidelity finite element simulations and analytical methods can accurately model the loss of preload for a single bolt, their prohibitive computational expense and complexity render them unfeasible for analyzing large-scale structures with many bolts. This creates a critical need for reduced-order models that capture the essential physics of loosening while remaining computationally efficient. This paper introduces a reduced-order modeling methodology for predicting the loosening of bolted lap joints subjected to transverse shock excitation. The core idea is to treat the bolt tension as a dynamic degree-of-freedom that governs the effective properties of the joint through tension-dependent stiffness and damping that couple the components together. The methodology is applied to a pair of oscillators coupled by a lap joint with a strain-sensing bolt. Three different sets of experimental measurements are used to interrogate the dynamics of the system. Mathematical models are identified for the joint stiffness and damping and the instantaneous tension, which are combined with the equations of motion for the oscillators to simulate and reproduce the experimental measurements. Ultimately, the results validate the treatment of bolt tension as a dynamic degree-of-freedom, such that the methodology provides an effective framework for predicting loosening behavior in bolted joints.

title: Multi physics driven pipeline damage localization method based on Helical guided wave under noise environments
abstract: The structural health monitoring technology based on helical guided waves is an effective method for detecting damage in pipeline structures. However, environmental factors during service often introduce unpredictable noise, causing defect scattered signals to become weak or obscured by noise, thereby hindering accurate defect identification. To achieve damage localization under unknown noise conditions, this paper proposes a Multi-Channel and Multi-Branch Convolutional Denoise Autoencoder-Transformer model (MC2DAE-Transformer) driven by multiple physical priors. Firstly, a feature encoder is constructed that can extract multiple temporal and spatial features. Local and global information are fused and subsequently decoded to achieve denoising reconstruction of the noise signal. The propagation path similarity of HGW is introduced as prior knowledge to enhance the spatial correlation of the denoising model. And a loss term containing multiple physical information is introduced to improve the denoising performance of the model. Subsequently, Transformer module can extract the damage information contained in the denoised signal and map it to the damage coordinates to complete the damage localization. The experimental results show that MC2DAE can increase the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) from −10 dB − 6 dB to an average SNR of 7.42 dB for noise signals. The average localization error of MC2DAE-Transformer is 7.43 mm, the standard deviation is 4.76 mm, and the relative error is 1.48%. Compared with other deep learning methods, the proposed method can achieve accurate damage localization under unknown noise, and has good stability and generalization. Our code will be available upon paper acceptance (https://github.com/red895866-rgb/MC2DAE-Transformer.git).

title: Chatter control in end-milling process using time-delay variation driven by workpiece excitation
abstract: This study investigated the impact of excitation and cutting conditions on regenerative chatter control using a novel workpiece excitation method to induce time-delay variation. Numerical simulations and milling tests were conducted using a designed active workpiece holder. While spindle speed variation is an effective approach to prevent regenerative chatter by introducing time-varying delays that disrupting the regenerative effect, excessive amplitude and frequency of variations can adversely affect the spindle life and reliability. Herein, an alternative approach was investigated by exciting the workpiece in two orthogonal directions to alter the relative velocity between the cutting edge and workpiece at the cutting point, thereby suppressing regenerative chatter. This allowed for the time delay to vary at higher frequencies and amplitudes than in the spindle speed variation method. A stability analysis conducted using high-precision time delay variations obtained via numerical calculation demonstrated that higher excitation frequencies and amplitudes considerably increased the critical axial depth of cut at the onset of chatter, even at high spindle speeds. The cutting tests conducted using the proposed active workpiece holder confirmed that introducing time-delay variations reduced the workpiece vibration amplitude during chatter generation, particularly when the excitation frequency was an integer multiple of the tooth-passing frequency, which corresponds with the numerical simulation results. The workpiece excitation not only reduced the chatter vibration amplitude but also improved the surface roughness of the machined workpiece.

title: A novel quasi-zero stiffness isolation platform for enhancing the effective operating range via a quasi-linear stiffness compensation mechanism
abstract: Quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) isolators have been widely applied in various engineering fields for low-frequency vibration suppression due to their characteristic combination of high-static and low-dynamic stiffness (HSLDS). However, most QZS isolators exhibit these properties only in the vicinity of the equilibrium position, which significantly limits their effective operating range. This study proposes a QZS isolation platform based on a quasi-linear stiffness compensation mechanism to extend its effective operating range. The negative stiffness produced by the two types of rhombic structures exhibits different variation trends. With suitable parameter combinations, effective quasi-linear negative stiffness can be realized and combined with linear positive stiffness to construct an isolator featuring a wide QZS range. The modified incremental harmonic balance method is employed to conduct a detailed and accurate analysis of the dynamic characteristics under varying base excitation amplitudes and damping parameters. The transmissibility characteristics under different mass loads indicate that effective vibration isolation can still be maintained even when the load is not located at the zero-stiffness position. Comparison with a linear isolator and a typical X-shaped isolator demonstrates that the proposed isolation structure exhibits a wider QZS range and superior vibration isolation performance. Static and dynamic tests are conducted based on the fabricated prototype, and the accuracy and effectiveness of the theoretical model are validated through experimental testing. The quasi-linear stiffness compensation mechanism provides an effective approach to broaden the working range of isolators. The proposed isolator exhibits QZS characteristics over most of its total stroke, enabling practical realization of low-frequency vibration isolation requirements in engineering applications.

title: Two-stage autoencoder reconstruction based unsupervised delamination imaging using laser sensed wavefields
abstract: Delamination quantification using guided wavefields has gained attention due to the high sensitivity of ultrasonic guided waves and advances in wavefield scanning. Although supervised deep learning enhances wavefield analysis, its application is limited by the high cost of large-scale labeling. Semi-supervised approaches alleviate this issue but still depend on curated, defect-free reference data. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes an unsupervised framework that integrates Convolutional Autoencoders (CAE) with guided wavefields, requiring neither labels nor historical data. The framework enables delamination quantification from a single wavefield snapshot captured when direct waves fully cover the inspection region. It leverages neural networks’ tendency to overfit dominant healthy patterns, causing poor reconstruction in delaminated areas. The snapshot is divided into uniform patches and symmetrically flipped to enhance data diversity. Each patch is independently reconstructed by the CAE, and a pixel-wise reconstruction error map highlights delamination regions as high-error zone. A two-stage training strategy further reinforces healthy-region reconstruction. Experiments on scanning laser Doppler vibrometer data validate the effectiveness of the augmentation scheme, the two-stage strategy, and the framework’s robustness to varying defect shapes and locations. Overall, the proposed method provides a practical and robust solution for wavefield-based delamination detection without pre-collected or labeled data.

title: High-accuracy tip timing measurement of compressor blade cold-to-hot deformation
abstract: The cold-to-hot deformation of blades is critical for evaluating aerodynamic performance and structural durability, yet remains challenging to measure accurately. This study proposes a tip airfoil fitting method with extended spot model (TAF-ES) for high-precision couple deformation measurement based on blade tip timing (BTT). A simplified parameterization of tip coupling deformation is introduced, along with a blade-sensor triggering model that accounts for the finite size of the emitted light spot. The effects of spot size deviations on deformation measurement accuracy is investigated in numerical simulation. In the laboratory experiments, ground truth deformation parameters of blades with preset deformation were obtained using a 3D scanner and a laser displacement sensor, verifying that the proposed method maintains axial shift errors within ±0.2 mm and rotational angle errors within ±0.1°. The method is further validated on a six-stage industrial compressor operating up to 12,000 rpm, where the measured deformation trends align well with simulation, confirming its feasibility and reliability in practical applications.

title: Optimized S-transform embedded time–frequency interpretable neural network for aero-engine fault diagnosis
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) has attracted significant attention for its powerful capability in fault feature extraction, and has has found widespread applications in intelligent fault diagnosis of mechanical systems. Nevertheless, its limited interpretability and vulnerability to noise remain key challenges in both academic and industrial contexts. Motivated by the strong theoretical foundations and physical interpretability of traditional signal processing methods, this study aims to enhance the performance of CNN by integrating signal analysis theory. Given the non-stationary characteristics and high noise levels commonly observed in aero-engine vibration signals, conventional time–frequency analysis methods often fail to provide optimal representations. To address this limitation, a first-order frequency function with two adjustable parameters are introduced into the Gaussian window function of the original S-transform, deriving an optimized S-transform (OST) that exhibits improved window adaptability and enhanced time–frequency representation capability. Then, an OST embedded time–frequency interpretable neural network (OSTNN) is proposed for fault diagnosis in aero-engines without any predefined parameters. This design enables the transformation of standard first layer convolutional kernel in the CNN method into OST convolutional kernel, whose parameters are continuously adjusted during the training procedure. The proposed OSTNN framework not only effectively suppresses noise interference effectively but also enhances model interpretability through visualization of learned time–frequency feature distributions and analysis of overall amplitude-frequency response.
