Extensive experiments on three aero-engine datasets, covering typical bearing and rotor faults, demonstrated that the OSTNN method consistently outperforms surpasses eight state-of-the-art diagnostic approaches in terms of effectiveness, noise robustness, interpretability, imbalance, generalization, and few-shot learning capability.

title: Two-layer Kronecker product decomposition-based robust recursive adaptive filtering for multichannel active noise control
abstract: Active noise control (ANC) serves as an effective technique for suppressing unwanted environmental noise, thereby enhancing acoustic comfort and improving the overall quality of human living and working environments. However, traditional adaptive filtering methods encounter significant challenges in multichannel ANC systems, as the increasing number of channels often results in sharply elevated computational demands and slower convergence rates. To address these issues, this paper proposes a two-layer Kronecker product decomposition (TLKPD) strategy, which decomposes the original long adaptive filter into multiple shorter subfilters. Based on this framework, a TLKPD-based multichannel filtered-x recursive least squares (TLKPD-MFxRLS) algorithm is developed. Furthermore, to enhance robustness against impulsive noise, a robust variant of the TLKPD-MFxRLS algorithm is introduced by constraining the magnitude of filter updates. The computational complexity of the proposed algorithms is then analyzed, and simulation results are presented to validate their effectiveness and advantages under various acoustic paths and noise environments.

title: A formulation for rotor-foundation interaction via dynamic substructuring and virtual point transformation
abstract: This work presents a substructuring-based methodology for coupling and decoupling rotor-foundation assemblies. The approach eliminates the need for prior knowledge of bearing coefficients by directly using measured responses or through an extended Virtual Point (VP) transformation specifically formulated for rotating machinery and their support structures. Two rotor systems with contrasting dynamic behaviors – one with flexible and one with rigid behavior – are used to demonstrate the procedure. Coupling results show that direct methods are satisfactory in many cases, while VP coupling improves accuracy near resonance and antiresonance regions. Decoupling techniques also enable the construction of detached rotor models, which can be reused with different support structure configurations. Furthermore, the VP-based decoupling approach provides improved identification of forward and backward modes. The results confirm that both direct and VP-based substructuring methods are effective tools for analyzing rotor-support interactions in operational conditions.

title: Research on the impact dynamics of blade-casing rubbing in aero-engines during maneuvering flight based on blade tip clearance signals
abstract: Increasing efficiency demands have led to progressively reduced blade-casing tip clearances in aero-engines. Meanwhile, advances in vectoring engines have markedly enhanced aircraft maneuverability. However, excessively small tip clearances make the engine rotor highly susceptible to hazardous rubbing faults during maneuvering flight, posing severe risks to operational safety. This paper proposes a dynamic modeling approach for a dual-rotor aero-engine system that incorporates flexible blade-casing rubbing faults occurring during maneuvering. Flexible deformation induced by blade-casing contact is represented using frequency response functions, and a coating correction factor is introduced based on Coulomb’s friction law. A rubbing force formulation is derived that accounts for elastic deformation of both blade and casing. Due to the presence of nonlinear terms such as maneuvering loads and rubbing forces, a transient dynamic computation method combining the Hilber-Hughes-Taylor-α (HHT-α) scheme with a nonlinear separation-reconstruction technique is proposed. Subsequently, a vibration monitoring and signal-processing method for detecting rubbing faults based on blade tip clearance signals during maneuvering is developed. Finally, a maneuvering-flight test rig is constructed, and the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method are validated using BTC measurements. The results indicate that rubbing faults can significantly alter the rotor’s vibration characteristics during maneuvering. A complex nonlinear relationship exists between casing curvature radius and rubbing force. Both experiments and simulations reveal that differences between flexible and rigid rubbing mechanisms lead to distinct time-domain, frequency-domain, and impact-force characteristics of the rotor. This study establishes a new theoretical and technical framework for rubbing-fault prevention and condition monitoring during maneuvering.

title: Narrow and third-octave spectra of total flexural vibration and sound power radiation from optical camera measurements
abstract: This research presents an optical camera-based method for measuring narrow band and third-octave band spectra of the total flexural vibration and total sound radiation of 2D and 3D structures. The proposed method overcomes key issues inherent in classical vibro-acoustic measurements, such as the requirement of long-duration and full-field measurements and, to some extent, the need of physically masking flanking sources and background noise. Digital image correlation combined with frequency-domain triangulation is employed, which is particularly suited for the derivation of spectral measurements, although classical time-domain triangulation could be employed too. The narrow-band vibration and sound radiation spectra are derived from integral formulations. In particular, the total sound power radiation is derived using the radiation resistance matrix, which can be calculated from numerical quadrature of the boundary integral for the sound radiation. The third-octave band spectra are computed by integration of the narrow band spectra over appropriate frequency-bands. The proposed method is validated for a baffled cylinder model-structure by contrasting the narrow band and third-octave band spectra of the total flexural vibration and total sound power radiation estimated from camera recordings with those obtained from direct measurements taken with a scanning laser vibrometer and a microphones array. The proposed approach offers a valid alternative to traditional vibroacoustic measurements, which does not require expensive laboratory facilities and long lasting and costly measurement campaigns. Furthermore, it can be effectively integrated into laboratory equipment for the offline synthesis and measurement of specific vibroacoustic fields, thus reducing the costs and time of conventional tests on real systems, such as the measurement of a) car tire noise, b) airplane cabin noise caused by the aerodynamic turbulence and the engines, c) room airborne and structure-borne noise produced by household appliances, and d) interior noise transmission through windows and partitions of building.

title: Ultrasonic measurement of lubricating film thickness with oblique incident waves facing on tapered roller bearings
abstract: Tapered roller bearings serve as the core components of wind turbines. To improve their reliability, the in-situ measurement of lubricating film thicknesses, serving as the most direct indicator of lubrication failure, is necessary. Ultrasonic-based methods are suitable for this purpose due to its strong penetration. However, current methods rely on the principle of vertical reflection of ultrasound. For oblique incident waves, the reflection mechanism remains unclear. This paper focuses on the propagation of oblique incident ultrasound that enables a wide-range measurement of lubricating film thickness under oblique conditions. Firstly, the propagation model of oblique incident waves is established by investigating the properties of the oblique incidence. Next, the analytical formula of the reflection coefficient is deduced from the wave superposition principle. Based on this, the complex model and resonance model are constructed for oblique incidence, by which wide-range film thicknesses can be computed. Furthermore, a finite element simulation is carried out to validate the accuracy of the proposed two methods. For the complex model, compared with the classical vertical-incidence method, the results show a low error below 1% within 0°-50° incident angles whereas for the vertical-incidence method the errors increase positively with incident angles and reach 5% when the incident angle exceeds 15°. Moreover, for the proposed resonance model, the method maintains errors less than 2.5%. Finally, linearity calibration experiments are carried out and reveal that the resonance model represents a higher robustness to noise and the complex model exhibits a decreasing uncertainty with thinner films.

title: Theoretical and experimental approaches for the motion characteristics of the cage considering ball-cage random collision behavior
abstract: Dynamic imbalance of the cage frequently occurs due to collisions, friction, and intermittent impacts, resulting in reduced dynamic stability and wear. A new dynamic model of the cage that accounts for variations in its spatial orientation, real-time collision effects of the ball-cage pocket is presented in this paper, and the interactions of the cage-guiding ring during axial deflection is considered. The accuracy and reliability of the model are validated through the experiment. A comprehensive investigation is conducted into the effects of single axial load and combined loads on the dynamic performance of the cage. This includes analysis of spatial trajectory characteristics, distribution of ball-cage pocket collision points, stress distribution patterns, and the cage acceleration. Furthermore, the influence of the guiding clearance and the pocket clearance on cage trajectory, contact forces, and wear rate is examined. Results show that under single axial load and combined loads, the cage trajectory pattern and the location of maximum stress distribution differ significantly. The cage whirling performance is improved by the increasing the guiding clearance, whereas instability can be inspired by an excessively large pocket clearance. An appropriate clearance range can effectively optimize the cage whirling radius, reduce the axial random disturbances, thereby enhancing its spatial motion stability and reducing wear. This research offers new perspectives for failure analysis and structural optimization of bearing cages.

title: Nonlinear dynamic of aircraft-like shell coupled with internal nonlinear components
abstract: This paper is dedicated to carrying out the comprehensive analysis of the dynamical behaviors for an aircraft-like composite laminated combined shell with built-in components connected by multiple nonlinear isolators. The whole shell system is decoupled as a series of shells, including spherical shells, multi-taper shells, cylindrical shells, circular plates, based on geometrical characteristics, where neighboring shells are coupled together by imposing mechanical conditions through penalty parameters. Nonlinear vibration isolators are represented by several spring-damper systems to characterize the connection relationship of the built-in rigid components to the plate, where the stiffness of each spring along the normal direction of the plate is described as a polynomial function associated with the spring deformation. The first-order shear deformation theory (FSDT) for shell incorporated with the energy functionals for rigid components is adopted to derive the nonlinear mathematical formula for the whole system, and the available dynamic solutions are formulated by using incremental harmonic balance method (IHBM). The modal frequencies and vibration responses calculated from the developed model matches well with those from the archived literature, finite element model (FEM), and dynamic experiments, indicating the applicability of the current model to shell dynamics problems. Also, the influence of load parameters, the nonlinear spring parameters on the dynamic behaviors of the aircraft-like shell system carrying the internal components are investigated, which may serve as the design and evaluation of the dynamic environment of shell-type structures.

title: FCTransformer: An intelligent fault diagnosis method for multi-sensor information fusion based on Fourier convolution and transformer
abstract: Aiming at the problems of missing information and insufficient modelling in the frequency domain and time domain for the existing multi-sensor data fusion methods, an intelligent fault diagnosis method based on Fourier convolution and Transformer (FCTransformer) is proposed. Firstly, the method uses principal component analysis (PCA) to downscale high-dimensional and multi-modal sensor data, and converts them into RGB images by continuous wavelet transform (CWT). Then, a Fourier convolution (FC) is designed, which can not only effectively extract local periodic frequency domain features, but also enhances the nonlinear feature extraction capability of the model. Finally, a variational auto-encoding transformer (VAETransformer) is designed to achieve global dependency modelling, which enhances the identification for multi-sensor coupled features. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, experimental validation is carried out on the bearing and gearbox datasets. The results show that the average fault diagnosis accuracy of FCTransformer is 99.58% under normal sample conditions, and its average fault diagnosis accuracy is 96.10% under small sample conditions. This indicates that FCTransformer has superior fault diagnosis performance and can meet the requirements of rotating machinery fault diagnosis tasks.

title: A coupled dynamic model and verification of vehicle-traction motor-bearing for high-speed train with bearing faults
abstract: Traction motor bearings of high-speed trains are prone to failure in harsh working environments such as long-term service and high-speed heavy loads. It is extremely important to perform real-time and accurate fault state identification to ensure the safe operation of trains. Precision fault identification algorithms often require a significant number of traction motor bearing fault data samples under various track conditions. However, acquiring such data through field tests is impractical due to cost, safety hazards, and constrained track availability. Moreover, bench tests do not accurately reflect the bearing fault characteristics under actual track operating conditions. In this paper, a mathematical model is established to calculate the Hertz contact force and impact force between the rolling-elements and the raceway of traction motor bearings caused by bearing fault. For the first time, a 45-degree-of-freedom coupled dynamic model of vehicle-traction motor-bearing for high-speed train with bearing faults is developed. The model considers vertical, pitch, and roll degrees of freedom of the vehicle–traction motor system, as well as vertical and longitudinal degrees of freedom together with pitch and yaw degrees of freedom of the bearing–rotor system. The correctness of the model is validated through analysis of bearing fault characteristics and comparison with bench test data. The research findings indicate that: (1) The dynamic model of faulty bearing that comprehensively considers the Hertz contact force and dynamic impact force between the rolling-elements and the raceway can accurately replicate the dynamic behavior of faulty bearings. (2) The established coupled dynamic model of the vehicle-traction motor-bearing can generate traction motor bearing fault data samples that conform to actual track operating conditions, thereby laying a solid foundation for precise fault diagnosis algorithms of traction motor bearings in track operating environments.
keywords: Coupled dynamics model of vehicle-traction motor-bearing with bearing faults

title: A novel pre-stress parallel kinematic robot for multi-DoF forming process: mechanism principle, pre-stress design, and actively dynamic pre-stress control
abstract: Industrial multi-DoF forming requires robots capable of sustaining thousand-ton loads, far beyond the limits of existing systems. This paper introduces a pre-stressed forming robot (Nonapod) that achieves a 10 MN payload by employing a dynamic pre-stress enhancement strategy inspired by architectural tension structures. The flexible-redundant 6-PSS/3-SPS parallel kinematic mechanism (PKM) is first developed to realize pre-stress loading. The principle of novel actively dynamic pre-stress method is then clarified. Further, the integrated pre-stress design criterion for maximizing payload of Nonapod is proposed. To track the above designed pre-stress, a novel force/position control scheme for pre-stress loading is proposed. Finally, a novel pre-stressed forming Nonapod for the multi-DoF forming process is developed and tested, showing a 1.25 times improvement in payload with pre-stress. Besides, a complex aircraft gear is formed demonstrating the high performance of the new Nonapod in application. This work introduces a novel idea to significantly enhance the payload of robotics.

title: MS-DAWCAE: multi-scale deep adversarial wavelet convolutional autoencoder toward unseen fault diagnosis with limited data
abstract: Deep learning has achieved rapid development in mechanical fault diagnosis. However, it still faces challenges in practical applications due to limited fault samples and the emergence of unseen fault types. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale Deep Adversarial Wavelet Convolutional Autoencoder (MS-DAWCAE) for unseen fault detection and known fault diagnosis in small-sample scenarios. The model first integrates wavelet scattering transformation with multi-scale convolutional encoding to extract hierarchical features that capture both local anomalies and global structural patterns, thereby improving reconstruction of known categories and enlarging reconstruction errors for unknown faults. Accordingly, a collaborative adversarial learning module with dual discriminators is then designed to regulate latent representations and supervise reconstruction quality, effectively compressing intra-class variations and enhancing separability between known and unknown categories. Furthermore, a fully connected classifier is incorporated into a multi-task framework to enable accurate identification of known faults while maintaining sensitivity to novel ones. Extensive experiments on industrial datasets demonstrate that, compared with advanced machine learning and transfer learning–based methods, MS-DAWCAE achieved an F1 score of at least 0.90 on the FST dataset under various operating conditions. Moreover, on a publicly available centrifugal pump dataset, MS-DAWCAE outperforms the optimal method by 15%–25% under small-sample settings, validating its effectiveness, robustness, and scalability for practical industrial fault diagnosis.

title: Stress evaluation using quasi-static component generated by longitudinal critically refracted (LCR) wave
abstract: Nonlinear ultrasonic techniques offer a viable approach for stress assessment. Nevertheless, the practical adoption of the second harmonic generation method is constrained by two principal factors: pronounced signal attenuation and spurious harmonics generated by the measuring apparatus. To overcome the limitations, the study interrogates the generation mechanism of the quasi-static component (QSC), which arises from the interaction of longitudinal critically refracted (LCR) waves with stress, for its application in nondestructive stress evaluation. We systematically assess the feasibility of using the QSC to quantify tensile stress in aluminum specimens through integrated numerical simulations and experiments. The results demonstrate that a normalized acoustic nonlinearity parameter (ANP) derived from the QSC increases monotonically with applied tensile stress from 0.0 to 120.0 MPa. The QSC-based ANP exhibits a strong linear correlation with stress, and validation on pre-stressed specimens yields prediction errors below 5.6%. The findings of this study establish the QSC-based ANP method as an effective and reliable factor for measuring elastic tensile stress. Compared to other nonlinear ultrasonic techniques, the proposed approach offers a highly sensitive method for stress evaluation in load-critical aluminum structures.

title: Multi-stage quasi-zero stiffness vibration isolation with linear-to-torsion magnetic negative stiffness mechanism for variable load
abstract: Load variations would significantly degrade the low-frequency vibration isolation performance of conventional quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) vibration isolators. To address this challenge, this work proposes a multi-stage QZS vibration isolator (MS-QZS-VI) with a novel linear-to-torsional magnetic negative stiffness (LTMNS) mechanism, including regular and irregular configurations, to improve the low-frequency vibration isolation under varying loads. The geometric and dynamic models of the MS-QZS-VI are established. One, two, or three QZS regions can be obtained by adjusting parameters of tile magnets for the two LTMNS configurations, such as the number, angular width, etc. The periodic negative stiffness induced by the regular LTMNS configuration enables single-stage or multi-stage QZS behavior, while the irregular LTMNS configuration further broadens the working range of the multi-stage QZS regions, thus improving low-frequency vibration isolation under variable loads. A longer rod length, a smaller initial torsional angle, and a lower radius ratio are beneficial for enhancing the low-frequency vibration isolation performance. The MS-QZS-VI with the irregular LTMNS configuration can effectively realize considerable vibration isolation performance when the load is increased from 1 kg, 1.6 kg, 3.0 kg, to 3.7 kg, demonstrating strong load adaptivity characteristics. The proposed MS-QZS-VI provides a feasible and effective solution for high-performance low-frequency vibration isolation in engineering applications involving variable loads.

title: Non-parametric failure identification of in-service multi-damper systems based on sparse constraint
abstract: Dampers in service inevitably undergo progressive performance degradation, directly impairing their designed control efficacy. Current damper failure detection methods mainly rely on parametric approaches that need prior knowledge of the failure models. While non-parametric methods have emerged as alternatives, they persist with two critical limitations: (i). Multi-damper applications introduce an ill-posed problem due to excessive unknown quantities. (ii). Complex structure implementations require burdensome global analyses. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes two novel methodologies for the non-parametric identification of damper failure. The first innovation conceptualizes damper failure forces as unknown inputs acting on the structure, subsequently introducing failure sparsity constraints to resolve the inherent ill-posed problem. Building upon the classical Kalman filter under unknown input (KF-UI) framework, the sparse Kalman filter under unknown input (SKF-UI) is proposed, which enables the identification of multiple damper failure forces. The second method further decomposes large-size structures through substructure analysis, treating interface forces as unknown inputs acting on substructure. This process leads to the development of a hybrid methodology termed the sparse Kalman filter under unknown input with substructure analysis (SKF-UI-S), specifically designed for damper failure detection in complex structural systems. Numerical validations demonstrate the effectiveness through non-parametric identification of multiple dampers under different failure scenarios in both a 10-story shear frame and a 76-story benchmark model. The comprehensive testing confirms that the proposed approaches successfully overcome traditional limitations in identification accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Macro–micro feature driven digital twin for assembly planning of aero-engine rotor under weak correlation
abstract: Assembly planning guided by macro–micro features of aero-engine rotor is crucial for ensuring assembly quality. The semi-automated dual-arm measurement robot (DAM-Robot) relied upon in the rotor measurement process still requires manual guidance. Under the influence of global multi-source data, it is difficult to achieve effective human–machine collaboration. Furthermore, the spatiotemporal discontinuity between measurement and assembly optimization reduces the reliability of the mapping between data and individual rotors. Emerging digital twin (DT) technology provides an effective solution for system integration. We design the assembly planning digital twin (AP-DT) that covers the entire assembly planning process, using the DAM-Robot as the basis. Leveraging the macro–micro features of aero-engine rotor, we realize intelligent measurement guidance for DAM-Robot and effective assembly planning. During assembly optimization, we substitute the strong correlation between the first-stage rotor’s datum plane and the assembly coordinate system with a weak one. The optimization constraint of coaxiality error is resolved by allowing the first-stage rotor to adjust its own spatial pose. In the assembly experiments of a three-stage aero-engine rotor, AP-DT completes measurement tasks based on rotor macro–micro features acquired online. Assembly optimization module derives assembly planning recommendations from the evaluation results of geometric errors of each rotor within the assembly group. AP-DT can provide system-level support for the aero-engine rotor assembly.

title: Principal component stochastic subspace identification for output-only modal analysis
abstract: Stochastic Subspace Identification (SSI) is widely used in modal analysis of engineering structures, known for its numerical stability and high accuracy in modal parameter identification. SSI methods are generally classified into two types: Data-Driven (SSI-Data) and Covariance-Driven (SSI-Cov), which have been considered to originate from different theoretical foundations and computational principles. In contrast, this study demonstrates that SSI-Cov and SSI-Data converge to the same solution under the condition of infinite observations, by establishing a unified framework incorporating instrumental variable analysis. Further, a novel modal identification approach, Principal Component Stochastic Subspace Identification (PCSSI), is proposed based on this framework. This method employs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to extract key components of the signal subspace and project the observed data onto this space, enhancing modal identification stability while significantly reducing computational complexity. Through 5000 Monte Carlo numerical simulations, the statistical analysis shows that PCSSI consistently outperforms traditional SSI methods in terms of numerical stability and noise reduction, demonstrating clear advantages over both SSI-Cov and SSI-Data. Its effectiveness is further validated using experimental data from a scaled bridge model. Compared to conventional SSI approaches, PCSSI demonstrates superior robustness under complex engineering conditions, especially when dealing with limited data or high noise levels, underscoring its strong potential for practical applications.

title: Non-invasive radio frequency (RF)-driven in-process monitoring and control for enhancing micro-electrical discharge machining stability and efficiency
abstract: The extremely narrow inter-electrode gap and complex gap conditions in micro-electrical discharge machining (micro-EDM) cause highly stochastic and dynamic nature of discharge behaviour. Process monitoring is essential for enhancing machining stability and efficiency by detecting discharge patterns and anomalies, particularly when combined with control strategies. Traditional EDM monitoring approaches predominantly rely on electrical sensors to discriminate pulses and infer machining states, which are subsequently used as control variables through statistical metrics. However, they suffer from high instrumentation cost, process interference, and inherent inability to capture transient dynamics. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a radio frequency (RF)-driven in-process monitoring and control scheme for micro-EDM at pulse-train level due to the non-invasive nature of RF radiation. Three machining states are defined from the integral value of voltage signals within a time window, simplifying the complex state labelling task. Given the high-frequency yet information-sparse nature of these RF signals, a low-dimensional feature dataset is constructed for machining state identification. A hybrid hierarchical deep learning model is introduced and evaluated, achieving over 90% classification accuracy under various working conditions, with average and weighted accuracies beyond 94% and 96%, respectively, highlighting its reliability and robustness. Based on the identified machining states, an adaptive servo control strategy is developed and applied to deep-hole drilling scenario, significantly improving the stability and efficiency. This study integrates deep learning and in-process control to establish a cost-effective and high-performance monitoring system for micro-EDM, offering a promising pathway toward intelligent micromachining. Future work will focus on the systematic engineering integration, exploring deep synergy with CNC platforms and edge computing to accelerate the smart manufacturing.

title: Fractional-order subband p-norm adaptive filter via transformation nearest Kronecker product decomposition for active noise control
abstract: The conventional normalized subband p-norm (NSPN) algorithm achieves robustness in $α$-stable noise ($1<α\leq 2$) by utilizing low-order error moments. However, its performance degrades significantly under three scenarios: (1) non-Gaussian inputs, (2) $α$-stable noise with $0<α\leq 1$, and (3) sparse system identification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a fractional-order NSPN algorithm based on the nearest Kronecker product (NKP) decomposition and fractional-order stochastic gradient descent, termed NKP-FoNSPN. Theoretical bounds for the fractional-order parameter $β$ are also derived. Notably, when $β=1$, the NKP-FoNSPN reduces to a new NKP-NSPN algorithm, while its non-NKP decomposition variant becomes the fractional-order NSPN (FoNSPN) algorithm. Furthermore, a novel transformation-based NKP (TNKP) decomposition technique is designed, which exhibits lower computational complexity than conventional NKP for specific filter structures. The resulting TNKP-based FoNSPN (TNKP-FoNSPN) achieves lower steady-state misadjustment and multiplication cost compared with the NKP-FoNSPN algorithm. Additionally, complete computational complexity analyses are provided. For active noise control (ANC) scenarios, we develop filtered-x variants: NKP-FxFoNSPN and TNKP-FxFoNSPN. From the former, two additional variants are derived: NKP-FxNSPN and FxFoNSPN. Simulations using diverse noise sources (pink, helicopter, gunshot, pile driver, and traction substation noise) demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithms. Finally, we validate their noise reduction performance in a real constructed single-channel duct ANC and a simulated multi-channel ANC systems.

title: Maximum prediction discrepancy domain adaptation network for rolling bearing RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios
abstract: Achieving cross-domain remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, improves efficiency of RUL prediction in ensuring the reliability of mechanical equipment. However, current research mainly focuses on single cross-domain scenario such as cross-working conditions, while few studies concerning applicability for multiple cross-domain scenarios. In practical applications, the challenge of extracting domain-invariant features caused by diverse data distribution discrepancies accompanying multiple cross-domain scenarios, coupled with the inherent limitations of existing methodological frameworks, limits the generalization performance and application efficiency of current cross-domain RUL prediction methods. Therefore, this paper proposes a maximum prediction discrepancy domain adaptation network (MP2DAN), to achieve rolling bearing RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios. In MP2DAN, to address the performance limitation under multiple cross-domain scenarios, a maximum prediction discrepancy (MPD) domain adaptation (DA) approach is proposed. Leveraging the correlation between decision boundaries of different RULs and target domain samples, MPD flexibly learns domain-invariant feature representations from diverse data distribution discrepancies, through a three-stage adversarial training designed between the feature extractor and two RUL predictors. Then, drawing on the characteristics of MPD framework, a synergistic adversarial self-supervised learning (SASL) approach is designed, which aims to empower the target domain to promote MPD in achieving DA, and constrain the feature generation of target domain to ensure the effectiveness of prediction results through knowledge transfer and self-supervised learning. Finally, the ablation and comparative experiments are performed on three bearing datasets. Through the performance quantification and visualization analysis, it is verified that MP2DAN can effectively and generically realize RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios.

title: Tool wear monitoring and multi-step forecasting in deep hole boring based on physics-informed neural network and ARIMA model
abstract: Tool wear monitoring (TWM) is critical for deep hole boring, significantly impacting production efficiency, machining quality, and cost reduction. Traditional TWM approaches, primarily relying on physics-based models or data-driven models, face limitations: physics-based models often fail under complex, non-idealized machining conditions, while data-driven models require substantial high-quality data. To overcome these challenges, this study first proposes a novel physics-informed neural network (PINN) with a dual-branch architecture: (1)A data-driven branch takes multi-channel features and flank wear width (VB) as inputs and outputs to model their relationship. The multi-channel features were extracted and selected based on relevance from cutting force, vibration, and audio signals, combined with time information. The VB values are derived through a detailed study of the wear mechanisms of boring tools, supported by measurement of the tool’s worn morphology. (2)A physics-informed branch takes as input the multi-channel features and VB, the first- and second-order derivatives of wear with respect to time and health indicators, as well as the mixed second-order derivative, and outputs the tool wear rate. This network implicitly learns the underlying partial differential equation governing wear dynamics. The total loss function combines data-driven loss, physics-informed loss, and a tool wear monotonicity constraint to align with physical wear mechanisms. Next, a hybrid approach employing second-order smoothing and an autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model enables robust multi-step wear forecasting even with limited historical data. Finally, validated across 10 distinct deep hole boring conditions, the PINN model demonstrates superior performance: it reduces average prediction errors by over 42.9% compared to other models, while exhibiting enhanced robustness. Crucially, the multi-step forecasting achieves exceptional accuracy, maintaining a maximum prediction error below 0.04 mm across all boring conditions, significantly outperforming the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model. This work provides both theoretical insights and practical guidance for implementing advanced tool condition recognition in deep hole machining applications.

title: Fractional modeling of nonlinear ship rolling dynamics under evolutionary and irregular sea-wave loads
abstract: This paper presents an efficient semi-analytical methodology for determining the non-stationary response of ships undergoing nonlinear rolling under stochastic sea-wave excitations. The dynamic response is captured through a comprehensive and physically consistent nonlinear formulation that incorporates both softening and hardening restoring moment characteristics, non-conventional fractional-order hydrodynamic damping mechanisms that naturally embed memory effects, and non-stationary stochastic wave loads representative of complex maritime environments. By leveraging a refined blend of stochastic averaging and statistical linearization the proposed stochastic fractional-order framework delivers computationally efficient, time-dependent second-order response statistics together with fully non-stationary roll angle amplitude probability-density surfaces. Tailored weighting factors and fractional derivative orders allow flexible tuning of restoring and damping characteristics to represent a wide range of relevant ship roll dynamics. Numerical analyses across a range of case studies, validated against benchmark Monte Carlo simulations, demonstrate the robustness and efficiency of the proposed methodology, underscoring its potential for assessing ship rolling response and seakeeping performance under dynamic and uncertain maritime conditions.

title: Real-time classification and fault diagnosis of machine signals via a novel decision-tree-inspired analog circuit classifier
abstract: Conventional machine learning algorithms implemented on digital signal processors (DSPs) require the conversions between analog and digital signals, which leads to unavoidable delay and considerable energy consumption. This paper investigates a novel decision-tree-inspired analog circuit classifier for real-time machine signal classification and fault diagnosis. Compared with traditional DSP-based fault diagnosis methods, the designed analog circuit-based method offers low-delay response time and low computing cost; hence, it is particularly suitable for embedded and low-power scenarios. The main idea of decision tree algorithm is integrated into the design of analog circuit composed of a filter matrix and amplitude quantification modules. The acquired signal flows into different branches through conditional judgment. This design innovatively transforms the hierarchical judgment mechanism of the traditional decision tree into the analog circuit implementation, where the filter matrix corresponds to the child nodes of the decision tree, and the amplitude quantization module realizes branch selection. The final outputs are the classification results of the corresponding leaf nodes, and the outputs are coded according to the number of signals to be classified. This all-analog processing method avoids the analog-to-digital conversion delay, maintains the interpretability of decision tree, and has the advantages of low delay, ease of implementation, and scalability, and thereby shows great application potentials in real-time intelligent machine signal processing, condition monitoring, and fault diagnosis.

title: GC-TimeGAN: Time–frequency domain model for high-fidelity reconstruction of Maglev track irregularity
abstract: Track irregularity is one of the primary sources of vibration disturbances in maglev trains, and its precise modeling is critical to improving simulation model fidelity and optimizing controller design. This paper proposes a model for modeling high-speed maglev track irregularity that integrates both time domain and frequency domain, namely the globally conditioned time series generative adversarial network (GC-TimeGAN). The model captures the complexity of track irregularity comprehensively by conditioning on frequency spectrum information, which is relevant to engineering applications. It generates high-speed maglev track irregularity data that align with the spectral characteristics of the track. Experimental results demonstrate that GC-TimeGAN outperforms traditional methods and other generative models in terms of modeling accuracy and feature consistency. This research provides a more accurate and practical modeling approach for track irregularity data generation, with direct relevance to engineering applications.

title: Classification of concrete damage modes via probabilistic acoustic emission clustering: A moving average-Gaussian mixture approach
abstract: Concrete remains indispensable in modern infrastructure yet susceptible to progressive damage threatening structural integrity. While acoustic emission (AE) technology enables real-time monitoring of damage evolution, prevailing methods for classifying failure modes exhibit critical limitations: The RA-AF method relies on subjective threshold demarcation. To resolve these constraints, this study introduces the moving average-Gaussian mixture (MaGM) framework-an integrated methodology combining a moving average algorithm for denoising AE-derived RA-AF parameters and a Gaussian mixture model for probabilistic clustering of damage modes without predefined thresholds. The approach was rigorously validated through uniaxial compression tests on concrete cubes spanning strength grades (C30, C40, C50) and loading rates (0.50, 0.65, 0.80 MPa/s), with AE signals systematically analyzed across three characteristic failure stages: Stage I (microcrack closure/compaction), Stage II (stable crack propagation), and Stage III (unstable macrocrack coalescence). Results demonstrate that MaGM eliminates operator-dependent biases while providing unprecedented quantification of damage mode proportions through cluster volume analysis. Key insights reveal: Evolution from tensile-dominated AE activity in Stage I to transitional mixed-mode damage in Stage II, culminating in strength-dependent Stage III failure-manifested as shear dominance in C40/C50 concretes (73.24–92.71% shear proportion at 0.80 MPa/s) versus tensile resurgence in lower-strength C30 (64.96–66.81% tensile proportion at 0.50–0.65 MPa/s). Furthermore, loading rate critically influences damage mechanisms, with increased rates promoting shear damage across all grades (e.g., C50 shear proportion rising by 19.47% from 0.50 to 0.80 MPa/s in Stage III). By resolving signal ambiguity in high-density AE regions and low-activity regimes, MaGM establishes a robust, threshold-free paradigm for concrete damage diagnosis, advancing objective structural health monitoring in civil engineering applications.

title: Dynamic modeling and analysis of a shaft system with the floating spline and angular misalignment
abstract: Floating splines are widely used in aerospace and marine power transmission systems. The angular misalignment is one primary form of misalignment in the floating splined shaft systems. Most previous works ignored the spline tooth meshing stiffness (TMS) variations caused by the meshing point differences along the tooth width direction, which did not comprehensively consider the combined influences of additional radial forces, axial force, and torque induced by the angular misalignment. These issues may reduce the accuracy of the calculated dynamics for floating splined shaft systems. Therefore, a spline force model including six-directional excitations induced by the angular misalignment is presented. Moreover, a meshing force calculation model considering the meshing point changes along the tooth width direction is proposed. The accuracy of the proposed spline force model and the floating splined shaft dynamic model is validated by the experiments. Then, the influence of angular misalignment on the dynamics of the floating splined shaft system is analyzed. The underlying mechanisms are also investigated.

title: Online detection of milling chatter based on multi-order graph convolutional neural network
abstract: Chatter is a type of self-excited vibration that occurs during machining, particularly when processing weak-rigidity aerospace parts, adversely affecting machining quality and efficiency. In order to prevent the detrimental effects of chatter in milling processes, a physically interpretable multi-order graph convolutional neural network (GCN)-based method is proposed for online chatter detection. In this method, the vertex and edge of the network are first constructed through the measured multi-channel vibration signal time series segments with short duration, establishing the groundwork for online chatter detection. Then, a multi-order GCN is developed by gathering feature information from multiple orders of neighbors of the target vertex to enhance its accuracy. Next, based on the multi-order GCN, a deep neural network is constructed and trained using the vibration data obtained by numerous milling experiments. During the training process, the edge weights are optimized by the gradient descent method. After that, an online chatter detection system is constructed, which demonstrates robust noise resistance through tests with different levels of noise interference added. Finally, experiments under various milling conditions validate that the proposed method can accurately detect milling chatter at its early weak stage, thereby successfully preventing its adverse effects.

title: Vibration Koopman Neural Operator: A Koopman-based approach for reliable remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Trustworthy maintenance decisions for industrial equipment depend on accurate prediction and uncertainty assessment of its Remaining Useful Life (RUL). However, the inherent nonlinear dynamics of the equipment degradation process pose a fundamental challenge to reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ). In nonlinear systems, the propagation of uncertainty is complex and analytically intractable, rendering existing UQ methods unreliable and poorly interpretable. To this end, this paper proposes an innovative framework for RUL prediction and UQ, rooted in the principle of Koopman-based lifting to a space of observables, where the dynamics evolve linearly. Its core contribution is the Vibration Koopman Neural Operator (VKNO), a deep network that, for the first time, learns a time-varying Koopman operator and transforms the complex evolution of non-autonomous (time-varying) systems into a stable and analytically tractable linear evolution in the learned observable space. Through a dual-branch architecture, the framework synergizes VKNO’s global dynamic insights with a data-driven branch’s ability to capture local patterns, and achieves dynamic UQ via a probabilistic output deeply coupled with the dynamics. Experiments on public and self-constructed datasets show that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models in both prediction accuracy (a 23.1% reduction in Mean Absolute Error) and uncertainty quantification (achieving a 99.87% Prediction Interval Coverage Probability), providing a new paradigm for high-reliability prognostics.

title: A novel dynamic model for magnetorheological dampers with multiscale insights into field-responsive yield transitions
abstract: Magnetorheological (MR) dampers provide tunable stiffness and damping properties for adaptive rotor systems, yet the underlying rheological transitions governing their performance remain insufficiently characterized. This work introduces a novel dynamic model of an MR damper based on a smooth-transition constitutive equation, accurately capturing progressive yielding and re-yielding behavior of MR fluids under coupled axial-circumferential shear. The model is consistently validated through theoretical analysis and targeted MR-damper rotor experiments, demonstrating reliable predictive capability at both local and system levels. High-resolution simulations reveal that increasing magnetic field strength can induce a topological transformation of the oil-film pressure-field distribution, where broad shear plateaus evolve into localized high-pressure peaks driven by yield-surface contraction and migration. This reconfiguration alters the phase relationship between load and motion, giving rise to a previously unreported non-monotonic damping response as rotor eccentricity grows. At large eccentricities, shear-rate dominance diminishes the relative contribution of field-dependent yield stress, triggering a saturation regime that limits further controllability. These findings provide multiscale insights that connect film-scale yield evolution and flow-field reorganization to the macroscopic dynamic characteristics of MR dampers, offering critical design guidance for smart MR-fluid-based damping systems.

title: Distribution-aware consistency via aligned teacher-student domain generalization for machine fault diagnosis
abstract: Domain generalization has received extensive attention for it can achieve cross-domain diagnosis without touching the target mechanical data. However, the traditional method lacks sensitivity to the distribution differences between categories and is difficult to maintain reliable decision boundaries in cases where categories are easily confused. Besides, common data augmentation strategies mostly focus on local perturbations and cannot take into account the global distribution characteristics and semantic consistency of samples, resulting in limited generalization ability of the model. To address these problems, this paper proposes Distribution-aware Consistency via Aligned Teacher-student Domain Generalization for Machine Fault Diagnosis (DCATDG). In particular, we propose a teacher-student interaction model mechanism that can improve the generalization ability of model. Subsequently, a distribution boundary awareness method is proposed that can adjust the decision boundary through inter-class overlap and thereby suppress the idea of class confusion. Finally, a generalized distribution measurement method is proposed, which can measure discrepancy between teacher and student features from the perspectives of the mean, variance, and freedom of probabilities. Three different datasets from different test rigs are used to verify the effectiveness of DCATDG. The experimental results show that DCATDG has better generalization ability than other methods, and get average diagnosis accuracy of 90.27%, 91.50%, and 94.50% in different generalization tasks.

title: Editorial Board
Data-model-co-driven approach for real-time reconstruction of unmeasured responses via multi-fidelity surrogate modeling
abstract: The data-model-co-driven approach offers a promising solution for real-time reconstruction of structural responses without prior measurements, exemplified by unmeasured responses. However, the accuracy of existing co-driven approaches is highly dependent on the fidelity of the Finite Element (FE) model, which limits their practical applicability in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM). To tackle this issue, this study proposes a co-driven framework based on multi-fidelity surrogate modeling. In the proposed framework, a Low-Fidelity (LF) model substitutes the FE model to estimate the full-field structural responses, while a High-Fidelity (HF) model learns the error mechanism between FE-simulated and measured data and subsequently improves the accuracy of all LF outputs. The proposed approach is validated through the full-field reconstruction of cable forces in a cable net structure. For three cable force locations assumed to be unmeasured, an investigation into the influence of the correlation between LF outputs and measurements on reconstruction accuracy reveals that the proposed approach is not strictly dependent on the fidelity of the FE-simulated data. Meanwhile, the proposed approach achieves a maximum Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 17.93 kN at these measurement points, compared with RMSE values exceeding 38 kN obtained using an existing co-driven approach. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the proposed approach enables real-time reconstruction of unmeasured structural responses with acceptable accuracy, while reducing its dependence on the fidelity of the FE model.

title: Zero-shot bearing life state identification method based on multi-scale envelope entropy and contrastive generative Kolmogorov-Arnold network
abstract: Rolling bearings exhibit diverse failure modes, and obtaining fully annotated data for all failure modes in industrial scenarios is challenging, which limits the applicability of traditional diagnostic models. To address this issue, a zero-shot life-cycle state identification method is proposed. First, a Multi-Scale Envelope Entropy (MSEE) health indicator is constructed by integrating frequency-domain and time-domain features, enabling sensitive monitoring and division of degradation states. Second, a Contrastive Generative Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CGKAN) model is proposed. This network utilizes B-spline functions to accurately fit local transient features, combined with radial basis functions to capture global patterns, allowing it to learn feature distributions from data of known failure modes. Additionally, Wasserstein distance and a gradient penalty mechanism are incorporated with contrastive learning to optimize the feature space, generating high-quality sample features for unknown failure modes and training a classifier to identify these unseen failure modes. The proposed method is validated on two full-life-cycle bearing datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the method effectively divides life-cycle states and, by leveraging data from known failure modes, achieves accurate identification of unknown failure modes not encountered during the training phase.

title: Online detection and model-free adaptive control of titanium alloy laser welding penetration depth based on spectral diagnosis
abstract: The stable weld penetration depth is of great significance for ensuring the joint strength. However, due to the complex welding heat dissipation conditions, online detection and control of laser welding penetration depth remains a great challenge. This study analyzed the variation mechanism of laser-induced plasma spectrum and its relationship with penetration depth in pulsed laser welding. To acquire valuable interaction information between the laser and the base metal from the redundant spectral data, several feature extraction were investigated. A multi-layer backpropagation neural network was introduced to predict penetration depth. The results showed that the model based on spectral features acquired by uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) had the highest accuracy in predicting the penetration depth, with R2 of 0.982. Since the prediction period of data processed by UMAP was longer than that of spectral intensity ratio of Ti I 503.995 nm / Ti I 586.919 nm based on the spectral emission theory, the spectral intensity ratio was selected as the controlled object to ensure the real-time performance of penetration depth control. The nonlinear characteristics of the pulsed laser welding process were identified through step response experiments. Furthermore, an optimized Hammerstein nonlinear system model was constructed to verify that the spectral intensity ratio accurately characterized the penetration depth. In this paper, a model-free adaptive control algorithm was adopted to develop a control system of penetration depth. The simulation results showed that the intelligent controller had a short regulation time and a small overshoot. The welding test on dumbbell-shaped workpieces showed that the designed control system well achieved the stable control of weld penetration depth under variable heat dissipation conditions.

title: Role of sprag angle in friction-induced vibration in catenary–pantograph systems
abstract: Suppressing friction-induced vibration (FIV) in catenary–pantograph systems is critical because it impacts both stable transportation and maintenance costs. Numerous studies have investigated FIV using analytical, experimental, and numerical methods. However, none of these studies considered the sprag angle—the upper-frame angle of the pantograph—although its role in brake squeal has been extensively investigated. This study integrates full-scale experiments, a flexible multibody dynamics (MBD) model, and theory to elucidate the role of the sprag angle in FIV in catenary–pantograph systems. Experiments with an actual pantograph demonstrate that FIV is self-excited, and transitions to impact vibration, and that larger sprag angles and higher friction destabilize the system and shift the dominant FIV frequency. On the numerical side, we propose a fast equilibrium solver for the pantograph that enables efficient flexible MBD simulations. Moreover, complex eigenvalue analysis reproduces the measured stability boundaries, growth rates, and dominant frequencies. Mechanistically, a circulatory matrix induced by Coulomb friction drives mode coupling; the eigenvalues depend strongly on the sprag angle, explaining the observed frequency shifts. The model further shows that effective countermeasures require both adjusting the sprag angle and mitigating mode coupling. We also clarify, theoretically, the relationship between the eigenvalue perturbation and mode displacement methods. The results demonstrate that combining these approaches enables a deeper understanding of FIV and that FIV can be captured, both qualitatively and quantitatively, by a three-degree-of-freedom system. This combined approach advances FIV research and contributes to other fields that address mode coupling.

title: Event-triggered sliding mode predictive control for piezoelectric-actuated hybrid vibration isolators subject to hysteresis and time delays
abstract: The piezoelectric-actuated hybrid vibration isolator (PAHVI) is widely used for vibration isolation owing to its reliability, controllability, and high resolution. However, the hysteresis and time delays in PAHVI may limit its vibration suppression performance. In addition, the computation of redundant control signals may waste system resources and even shorten the service life of the equipment. In this study, an event-triggered sliding mode predictive control (SMPC) algorithm is designed for the PAHVI system subject to hysteresis and time delays. Firstly, a neural network approximator combined with the finite covering lemma is employed to compensate for the time delays. Subsequently, a fast search implicit inverse algorithm is adopted to deal with the hysteresis behavior. Moreover, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism is introduced into the SMPC method to reduce the computation of redundant control signals. The stability of the closed-loop system is proved via Lyapunov theory. Finally, comparative experiments are conducted on the PAHVI system to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Pareto-optimal target definition for multi-axis random vibration testing
abstract: In random vibration testing with multiple control channels, existing control laws require specification of a complete spectral density matrix at each control frequency. Spectral density matrices include autospectral densities on the diagonal and cross-spectral densities on the off-diagonal. In practice, the off-diagonal terms are often unknown, and recent vibration testing research has focused on fixing the diagonal and specifying the off-diagonal to minimize the required control energy, subject to a constraint that the target matrix is positive semidefinite. This paper shows that, even with a fixed diagonal, off-diagonal terms strongly affect control residuals. This overlooked effect occurs in both square and rectangular systems. By jointly considering input energy and control residuals, open-loop inputs are derived directly from the diagonal without specifying the off-diagonal terms. Vibration targets that can be used in closed-loop control are then derived using the optimal inputs, with positive semidefinite constraints applied during the derivation. The result is a set of Pareto-optimal control solutions. For each solution in the set, any other possible solution produces greater control error, greater input energy, or both. A balanced solution is selected automatically, though others can be chosen based on test needs. Simulations and experiments show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art energy-minimizing approaches, achieving significant reductions in both control error and input energy.

title: A low-cost dual-IMU–aided camera-motion compensation method for vision-based vibration measurement of wind-turbine tower
abstract: In wind farms, camera-based measurement of wind-turbine vibration and displacement is prone to image jitter caused by wind-induced camera motion, which degrades accuracy. Conventional vision-based approaches often rely on static background target methods for motion correction; however, such stationary references are frequently unavailable in field deployments. To address this limitation, we propose a dual–inertial measurement unit (dual-IMU) fused six-degrees-of-freedom (6-DOF) camera-motion estimation method. By combining a Kalman filter with rigid-body physical-consistency constraints, the proposed approach estimates yaw, pitch, roll, surge, sway, and heave and performs image compensation based on the recovered motion. Laboratory validations across five stand-off distances (4–15 m), four focal lengths (70 mm, 100 mm, 135 mm, 210 mm), and multiple excitation types (impulse, quasi-harmonic, and wind-like) demonstrate effectiveness, accuracy, and robustness, achieving a correction ratio of 0.80. Field tests on a utility-scale turbine further evaluate applicability and stability under idle and operating conditions (with/without yaw) and different focal lengths, and enable accurate identification of the natural frequency with an error less than 0.01 Hz.

title: An Error Innovation-based Adaptive Kalman Filter for multi-channel Active Noise Control
abstract: This paper presents an Error Innovation-based Adaptive Estimation Kalman Filter (eIAEKF) tailored for multi-channel Active Noise Control (ANC) systems using MIMO filtered-x structures. Conventional Kalman-based ANC methods are computationally demanding and typically rely on fixed or manually tuned noise covariance matrices, limiting their robustness under changing acoustic conditions. The proposed eIAEKF introduces an error-driven mechanism that adaptively updates the measurement-noise covariance R ( n ) using the measured error signal, directly aligning the estimation process with the ANC objective. Building on the principles of innovation-based adaptive estimation, the algorithm reduces computational complexity by avoiding the need for an explicit transition matrix and by simplifying the computation of the Kalman gain, while also improving robustness to poor initialization. Simulation results under both stationary and dynamic scenarios, including changes in the primary noise spectrum, source position, and microphone location, show that eIAEKF achieves faster convergence and higher attenuation than an adaptive Kalman-like baseline, while maintaining numerical stability. Real-time experiments on a hardware platform further demonstrate the practical viability of the proposed approach. • The effectiveness of the Kalman filter depends on the elusive initial knowledge. • The noise covariance matrices control the responsiveness of the filter. • Traditional Kalman Filter keeps the parameters time-invariant. • Adaptive parameters can make the filter suitable for real-world applications.

title: Tactile feedback in mid-air ultrasound haptics with adjustable spatial resolution
abstract: This research presents a novel beamforming method for mid-air ultrasound haptic devices, targeting a key limitation in existing technologies–the inability to dynamically adjust the size of the acoustic focal area. This constraint directly impacts spatial resolution and limits the design flexibility of haptic feedback. As interest in human–machine interaction grows, mid-air ultrasound haptics has emerged as a promising solution; however, conventional approaches such as delay-and-sum (DAS) beamforming offer minimal adaptability without hardware changes. To address this challenge, we propose a beamforming algorithm based on the energy difference method (EDM), which enables software-controlled modulation of the focal area by optimizing the phase and amplitude of individual transducer channels. The proposed method was validated through both acoustic simulations using an analytical model and experimental measurements using a custom-built 8-by-8, 40-kHz ultrasonic array with transducer-level phase compensation. Results demonstrated that the focal area could be adjusted by approximately 25–30% across various focal positions, showing strong agreement between simulations and experiments. Furthermore, the modulated acoustic radiation force was visualized using a thin (20 μm) polymer film, confirming the spatial resolution adjustability. This capability enables either precise tactile localization or stronger radiation force, significantly enhancing the versatility and application potential of mid-air haptic systems in next-generation human–machine interfaces.

title: Singularity-free prescribed performance control method with three-region constraints and its implementation in distributed electro-hydraulic servo systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel three-region-constrained prescribed performance control (PPC) method, which divides the domain of control error into Safe region, Transition region, and Danger region, then designs an adjustment factor to dynamically regulate the constraint, ensuring that the control error is subjected to different constraint characteristics depending on the region it lies. This method can completely avoid singularity problems that may arise from any adverse influence, while guaranteeing strict satisfaction of performance constraints under normal operating conditions. In addition, a new bi-bandwidth extended state observer (BESO) with reasonably smooth bandwidth switching mechanism and simple structure is presented, which can achieve high estimation accuracy while effectively suppressing the influence of measurement noise on the obtained signals. Furthermore, the proposed method is implemented in the synchronization control of distributed electro-hydraulic servo systems (DEHSS), an area where relevant research is scarce. Corresponding adaptive fault-tolerant distributed controllers are developed for all follower nodes, which can compensate for the effects of actuator partial loss of effectiveness (LOE) faults and actuator bias faults, while also coping with challenges including measurement noise, input saturation, external disturbances, and unknown nonlinearities. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by both simulations and experiments.

title: Dynamic analysis of rotor-bearing systems considering cage-guiding surface contact with a modified conformal model
abstract: The accurate simulation of vibration for rotor-bearing systems is vital for the prediction of bearing useful life. However, for large-diameter bearings with small cage guiding clearance, dynamic models considering the conformal contact between the cage and guiding surface are still lacking. This paper proposes a roller bearing model with a 6 DOFs cage by introducing a modified conformal contact model to describe the stress distribution of cage-guiding surface contact. On this basis, a prediction method for rotor-bearing vibration is established to consider the cage-guiding surface contact due to the angular deflection of the rotor shaft. Then, a scaled rotor system with a large-diameter bearing of a turbofan engine is studied numerically and experimentally. The motion of the tested bearing is captured with the high-speed camera to study the cage-guiding surface contact. Experimental results show good agreement with the numerical solutions. Results show that when the bearing cage contacts severely with the guiding surface, the bearing fundamental train frequency and its modulation frequencies with rotor spinning frequency would occur in the rotor vibration spectrum, which could be an effective indicator to identify bearing cage wear.

title: Contact Property input strategies for nonlinear dynamics and wear prediction of frictionally damped blades
abstract: Dry friction dampers are utilized in turbomachinery for vibration suppression through friction dissipation. Recent advancements in modeling highlighted the accurate characterization of contact mechanical properties as a significant factor for nonlinear vibration prediction. However, it also introduces high analysis costs. In this paper, we quantitatively evaluate the influence of different contact mechanical properties on the prediction accuracy for both nonlinear forced response and wear analysis, and propose the corresponding simplified input schemes. The aim is to provide designers with a practical guidance for selectively inputting contact properties, thereby balancing the trade-off between the method complexity and required prediction accuracy. To this end, an experimental-computational integrated framework is developed. It can incorporate the detailed contact characterizations to explore the prediction accuracy boundaries. In wear analysis, the state-of-art wear-vibration solver is extended and enriched by incorporating the joint evolution of interface topography and friction coefficient. The corresponding novel accelerated update technique is developed to reduce the computational cost. In experiments, the static contact analysis, friction tests and long-term wear tests are conducted for parameter calibration. A blade-damper vibration test rig is established for validation. The results show that detailed contact characterization brings high predictive accuracy, with maximum errors below 3% in frequency and 6% in amplitude. The proposed simplified input schemes, such as averaging contact parameters or applying uniform pressure only in actual contact regions, can maintain acceptable accuracy under certain conditions. For wear analysis, the evolution of friction coefficient and surface topography should be considered simultaneously to accurately capture the response decay.

title: Fatigue life prediction method for cantilever bolted connections based on equivalent structural stress signals
abstract: In this study, the fatigue behavior of cantilever bolted connections was investigated through numerous bending fatigue tests, and load amplitude–life (Fa–N) curves were established. Cantilever bolted connections are highly sensitive to geometric parameters, resulting in a low correlation of the overall Fa–N curve, which cannot directly predict the fatigue life of complex cantilever bolted connections. Therefore, an equivalent structural stress signal acquisition model that comprehensively considers the influence of geometric and loading parameters and accurately characterize the stress state of these connections was derived. This equivalent structural stress signal overcomes the shortcomings of excessive simplification of nominal stress and the inadequacy of hot-spot stress in characterising stress gradients by converting the three-dimensional local concentrated stress of the complex structure into an equivalent one-dimensional structural stress signal. To obtain the load inputs for the model, a beam–shell equivalent finite element model of the cantilever bolted connection was established. The load parameters of the bolted connection were obtained via simulation and coupled into concentrated forces and moments through the beam element nodes. The equivalent structural stress signal (σs) of the connection was obtained by inputting the nodal loads into the equivalent structural stress signal acquisition model. Subsequently, the fatigue characteristic curves (Ss–N and P–Ss–N curves) normalized to Fa–N curves with different geometric and loading parameters were established. Finally, using the proposed fatigue life prediction method, the fatigue life of a cantilever bolted connection for an antenna bracket was predicted. The prediction results were highly consistent with the test data, which fully verified the effectiveness and accuracy of the equivalent structural stress signal method.

title: A hybrid active control approach for the attenuation of low-frequency vibrations and multi-narrowband disturbances
abstract: In aerospace applications, unwanted vibrations pose a significant challenge, particularly in complex vibration environments that contain both low-frequency vibrations and narrowband disturbances. However, the frequencies of the narrowband disturbances are unknown, and the low-frequency vibrations are close to the measurement limits of inertial sensors. Therefore, a hybrid control algorithm is proposed, which combines filtered-x least mean square (FxLMS) and enhanced active disturbance rejection control (EADRC). Specifically, the normalized frequency estimator is first employed to obtain a preliminary estimate of the disturbance frequency and the Kalman filter (KF) is then utilized to smooth fluctuations, thereby addressing the frequency mismatch issue in the FxLMS. Furthermore, by introducing the concept of zero-pole compensation into the extended state observer, correction in the feedback loop enables active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) to achieve more precise control. Experimental results confirm that the proposed algorithm significantly suppresses low-frequency vibrations and four narrowband disturbances.

title: Vibration measurement with neuromorphic vision sensors
abstract: In this paper, a novel methodology for vibration measurements of flexible structures with neuromorphic vision sensors (i.e. event cameras) is proposed and validated. Unlike conventional frame-based sensors, event cameras asynchronously record changes in scene brightness, enabling high temporal resolution with reduced data redundancy. In this study, a framework is developed for marker tracking and 3D triangulation from event recordings. The experimental setup involves four synchronized event cameras observing a cantilever beam coated with a grid of markers. The beam is excited harmonically at the first two flexural resonance frequencies, and the resulting 3D trajectories of the markers are reconstructed with subpixel accuracy. The resulting flexural deflection shapes are reconstructed through bundle adjustment of the camera recordings. The results have been benchmarked against laser vibrometer measurements, which confirmed the accuracy and applicability of the proposed measurement approach. Overall, the study demonstrates the potential of event cameras for dynamic testing in scenarios where high-speed, low-latency, low-bandwidth acquisitions are required without recording redundant data.

title: A piezoelectric stack-actuated gas microflow valve with high precision and fast response
abstract: As a core component for process gas flow control in lithography machines and semiconductor equipment, microflow valves face challenges in simultaneously achieving both high precision and fast response of gas flow under low flow conditions with existing technologies. To address this, this study proposes and validates a theoretical method for simultaneously achieving high-precision and fast-response of gas flow at low flow rates by adjusting the gap between the diaphragm and the annular surface boundary via a piezoelectric actuator assembly (PAA). Based on this method, a novel working principle for the microflow valve is introduced, where flow control is achieved by regulating the gap height between the diaphragm and the annular surface boundary via the PAA. The dynamic flow model of the microflow valve integrating electromechanical coupling and fluid–solid interaction is also established accordingly. Considering the rate-dependent hysteresis nonlinearity of the PAA, a rate-dependent modified Prandtl–Ishlinskii hysteresis model is proposed, and a hybrid control strategy combining feedforward compensation using the inverse hysteresis model with PID feedback is subsequently developed. Numerical simulations and experimental verification demonstrate that the microflow valve designed according to the proposed theoretical method simultaneously enables high precision and rapid control of low gas flow rates. Specifically, the hybrid control method achieves a control accuracy of ± 0.435% F.S. with a response time of only 14.71 ms. This study provides an effective solution for precision fluid control in lithography machines and semiconductor equipment.

title: A digital twin guided physical-virtual denoising method for early fault detection of rolling element bearings
abstract: Rolling bearings are key components in rotating machinery, widely used in aerospace, high speed railways and wind turbines, etc. Frequent operation in extreme working conditions such as high loads and high rotational speeds is prone to unpredictable failures, which can induce equipment shutdowns and even catastrophic accidents. Therefore, early fault detection is crucial to ensure the safe operation of the equipment. However, the vibration signals picked up by the sensors often contain strong noise and normal vibration responses excited by other healthy components, which seriously restrict the early fault feature extraction. For this reason, this paper proposes a digital twin-guided denoising method for early fault detection of rolling bearings by considering the knowledge of the intrinsic fault mechanism of the bearings. First, a dynamic model of the bearing is established to generate rich simulated fault signals, and the dynamic model is corrected and updated by the cosine similarity between the measured and simulated signals, so as to generate high-precise simulated signals close to those of the real bearing. Secondly, a physical-virtual signal denoising method based on wasserstein generative adversarial denoising network with gradient penalty (DeWGAN-GP) is proposed. Finally, the proposed method is validated using bearing failure as well as fatigue degradation experiments. The experimental results show that, compared with other non-knowledge-driven methods, the proposed method can take full advantage of the knowledge of the bearing failure mechanism to accurately extract the early failure characteristics of bearings under strong background noise.

title: Experiments on the influence of oil temperature and pressure on subsynchronous bifurcation and shaft orbit behaviour in automotive turbochargers
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive experimental study of the nonlinear dynamic behavior of a high-speed automotive turbocharger rotor system supported by semi-floating bearings. The investigation focuses on how oil supply temperature and pressure influence subsynchronous bifurcation, dynamic instability, and shaft orbit evolution under realistic lubrication environments. Experiments were performed on a dedicated test bench that enabled precise control and monitoring of oil parameters while decoupling rotor dynamics from engine-related disturbances. Shaft-end displacements were measured using dual radial probes, with simultaneous high-frequency vibration and speed tracking.
