Then, the normal contact force model in radial clearance joint is established using nonlinear contact force model. The gear meshing force model is established using dynamic meshing force model considering time-varying meshing stiffness and nonlinear damping coefficient. Finally, a gear-linkage mechanism with multiply clearances is used as application example to implement the investigation. The dynamic responses obtained with numerical simulation are compared with that of experimental gear-linkage mechanism setup. Dynamic tests with different clearance sizes and driving speeds are performed respectively. The comparison between simulation and experimental results shows that the simulation results agree quite well with experimental results, which proves the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method for dynamic analysis of gear-linkage mechanism system with multiply clearances. The investigation indicates that the radial clearances in revolute joints and tooth backlash in gear pair are interaction with each other, and the existence of clearances plays an obvious effect on the dynamic characteristics of gear-linkage mechanism, which significantly reduce the performance of the gear-linkage mechanism, especially the backlash of the gear pair.

title: Towards bandgap widening through beam-based coupling in mass–spring chains
abstract: This study investigates wave attenuation in a bi-coupled periodic chain composed of two unequal masses interconnected through beam elements and longitudinal springs. The baseline configuration is first examined to characterize its inherent dispersion behavior. To enhance its attenuation performance, diagonal springs are introduced between non-adjacent nodes, and their influence is evaluated through a spectral element formulation. Dispersion analysis based on the invariance-plane approach and complex wavenumber evolution shows that a single diagonal spring produces a distinct Bragg-type attenuation band, whereas incorporating two diagonal springs fundamentally alters the dispersion topology by inducing branch merging and the formation of a fully complex band. This geometric coupling mechanism results in a substantial widening of the attenuation region. Frequency–response functions computed for finite chains, and validated through numerical simulation and experimental measurements, confirm the transition from dual propagating modes to mixed propagation–attenuation behavior and ultimately to complete evanescence. Parametric studies reveal that increasing the diagonal stiffness from 6 × 1 0 3 to 1 × 1 0 4 N/m widens the bandgap by approximately 60% in the single-spring configuration and nearly 80% in the dual-spring system; variations in mass ratio produce comparable trends, while beam-width changes primarily shift the bandgap location. Collectively, the analytical, numerical, and experimental results establish diagonal geometric coupling as a robust and previously unreported strategy for tunable broadband vibration suppression in periodic mechanical systems.

title: Nonlinear modeling and analysis of an AMB-rotor system with time delay
abstract: Time delay is inherent in active magnetic bearing (AMB)-rotor systems and can induce complex nonlinear dynamics, potentially leading to system instability. Existing time delay models for AMB-rotor systems typically overlook delays induced by voltage saturation, iron losses, and signal processing. Furthermore, conventional solution methods frequently obscure the direct analytical relationship between the time delay parameter and the nonlinear dynamic response. To address these limitations, we propose an AMB-rotor model incorporating time delays arising from the controller, voltage saturation, iron losses, and signal transmission and processing. Furthermore, the method of multiple scales is employed to analyze the nonlinear dynamics of the AMB-rotor system with time delay. Simulations reveal that increasing time delay amplifies vibration amplitude by inducing a stiffness softening effect. Conversely, increasing the proportional and derivative gains can suppress the amplitude of the AMB-rotor with time delay and significantly modify the equivalent stiffness of spring characteristics. Finally, these nonlinear behaviors are experimentally validated, providing valuable guidance for the optimization of control parameters.

title: Posterior probability perspective for obtaining physically interpretable optimized weights for machine condition monitoring
abstract: Interpretable machine learning methods have garnered significant attention in the field of machine condition monitoring, as they not only reveal the internal structure of machine learning-based approaches but also provide physically meaningful explanations of their outputs. This interpretability is crucial for gaining trust and practical insights for monitoring engineering applications. Among the recent interpretable approaches, one important development involves the construction of a generalized health indicator defined in the frequency or envelope spectrum domain. This indicator uses interpretable, optimized weights to distinguish between fundamental and fault-related frequencies, even when underlying fault mechanisms are unknown. As a result, it facilitates simultaneous health monitoring and fault diagnosis in a physically interpretable manner. Previous studies have employed various objective functions—such as those inspired by optimal linear hyperplane, logistic regression, and linear discriminant analysis—to guide the optimization of these interpretable weights. However, practitioners and researchers are often confused regarding which objective function to choose, how they relate to one another, and what their statistical implications are in the context of interpretable machine learning for condition monitoring. This paper aims to address this gap by providing a deeper interpretation of these objective functions from the perspectives of statistical learning and posterior probability. First, we revisit the generalized health indicator and demonstrate how its optimized weights can effectively differentiate between fundamental and fault frequencies in a data-driven manner. Then, we review several loss functions commonly used in prior works. Next, we introduce the statistical decision theory to clarify that the essence of classification lies in estimating a posterior probability conditioned on an input. This theoretical foundation allows us to interpret the relationships among different loss functions through their implied posterior probabilities, thereby revealing their statistical connections. Finally, we conduct comprehensive experiments to compare the performance of these posterior probabilities and their loss functions in distinguishing and locating fundamental and fault-related frequencies, offering practical guidance for interpretable machine condition monitoring.

title: A novel multiscale inverse FEM for stiffened panels under sparse sensing
abstract: The inverse Finite Element Method (iFEM) is a robust model-based computational technique for reconstructing full-field displacement and strain states from experimental measurements, relying solely on strain data, geometry, and boundary conditions. It has proven highly effective for shell-like structures commonly found in aerospace, marine, and mechanical engineering. However, its application to stiffened panels—one of the most prevalent structural configurations in these domains—remains challenging due to geometric discontinuities, stiffness variations, and limited sensor coverage that hinder accurate full-field reconstruction. This study addresses these challenges by introducing a novel multiscale iFEM–dehomogenization framework designed to extend iFEM applicability to complex stiffened structures under sparse sensing conditions. The proposed methodology operates in two stages. First, iFEM reconstructs the displacement field on a macroscale plate-only model representing the sensorized surface of the structure. Then, a dehomogenization procedure, based on Representative Volume Elements (RVEs), transfers the reconstructed global response to the detailed stiffened geometry, enabling the recovery of local displacements, strain and stresses in non-instrumented regions. The main objectives of this work are to (i) reduce the dependency on dense sensor networks, (ii) maintain high reconstruction accuracy despite geometric and sensing limitations, and (iii) enable efficient multiscale recovery of local fields for Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) applications. The framework has been validated against both experimental and numerical studies on a stiffened aluminum panel. Results show that the proposed approach achieves displacement reconstruction errors below 6% compared with high-fidelity finite element and experimental benchmarks. These findings demonstrate that coupling iFEM with multiscale dehomogenization provides a physically consistent, computationally efficient, and scalable strategy for real-time shape sensing and SHM of complex engineering stiffened structures.

title: Nonlinear dynamics study of 4–6 order non-circular planetary gear systems
abstract: Non-circular planetary gear systems exhibit significant time-varying transmission characteristics, which can easily trigger complex nonlinear dynamic responses during operation, adversely affecting vibration stability. This paper develops a 36-degree-of-freedom bending-torsional coupling nonlinear dynamic model for 4–6 order non-circular planetary gear systems, incorporating multiple excitation factors, including time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS), meshing damping, backlash, friction, and comprehensive transmission error. A TVMS calculation method applicable to both internal and external meshing pairs is proposed based on curvature radius theory. The system’s nonlinear dynamic equations are solved numerically using the Runge-Kutta method. Nonlinear dynamic analyses, including bifurcation diagrams, time histories, phase diagrams, and Poincaré sections, were employed to systematically investigate the influence of key parameters-rotational speed, eccentricity, damping, and backlash on the system response. Multi-scale methods were further used to examine their effects on main resonance characteristics. Quantitative results show that the system transitions from periodic motion to 2-periodic and chaotic states as rotational speed increases, with peak vibration amplitudes rising from 1.12 m/s2 to over 5.6 m/s2 across tested speeds. Eccentricity critically affects dynamic behavior: under identical speed conditions, the external meshing pair enters a quasi-periodic state at an eccentricity of 0.22, earlier than the internal pair at 0.32. Increasing tooth flank clearance can trigger chaotic responses, whereas enhancing system damping reduces peak amplitudes by up to 32%-45%, significantly improving operational stability at medium to high speeds. Finally, a prototype test platform was established to validate the model. Experimental results and theoretical predictions show good agreement, peak to peak comparison has good consistency, confirming that the model effectively captures the system’s main dynamic behavior. These findings elucidate the unique nonlinear dynamics of non-circular planetary gear systems, providing a quantifiable theoretical basis for structural optimization and engineering applications.

title: Bayesian approach for bridge system reliability assessment accounting for spatial dependence of structural health monitoring data
abstract: Reliability assessment based on structural health monitoring (SHM) data is regarded as a promising strategy for assessing the condition of in-service bridges. However, bridge system reliability assessment that accounts for the dependence among monitoring responses of multiple bridge members remains challenging. This study proposes a bridge system reliability assessment method that considers both the multimodal and uncertain characteristics of SHM data and the spatial dependence among multiple members. First, the response SHM data of bridge members are probabilistically modeled using a Bayesian Gaussian mixture model (BGMM). Second, the reliability of each member is assessed based on the first-order reliability method (FORM). Subsequently, the bridge system reliability is assessed by integrating series–parallel models with copula functions. Finally, Bayesian updating is performed by integrating prior information with newly acquired SHM data, enabling the dynamic assessment of bridge reliability. The proposed method is validated using six months of SHM data from a long-span cable-stayed bridge. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively captures multimodality, uncertainty, and member dependence in bridge system reliability assessment. Traditional methods based on the assumption of member independence tend to overestimate the bridge system reliability index (by an average of 0.897), which may lead to safety risks. As newly acquired SHM data are incorporated into Bayesian updating, the bridge system reliability index stabilizes and the 95% confidence interval gradually narrows.

title: Effect of tracking resolution and loudspeaker arrangements on a headtracked active headrest noise control system
abstract: Head-tracking techniques offer the potential of improving the performance of local active noise control headrest systems during head movements. However, the effectiveness of head-tracked local active noise control can be limited by various aspects of the headrest design. This paper presents a thorough investigation into how head-tracking accuracy influences the control performance for both translational and yaw rotational head movements and, in addition, how this is affected by the geometry of the headrest control loudspeakers. The presented results highlight a notable difference in the attenuation performance achieved at the two ears when modelling errors exist between the physical plant response and the plant model utilised by the controller, which arise due to the accuracy of the head-tracking. It is demonstrated that the mismatch in performance between the two ears is influenced by the initial head position, the direction of head movements, and the layout of the headrest control loudspeakers. In the presence of plant modelling errors, the presented results reveal a trade-off between the balance in attenuation performance at the two ears and the spatial extent over which effective control is achieved. The presented insights can be utilised to help design local active noise control headrest systems with head-tracking that are well-suited to their intended application.

title: Data-Driven and Physics-Informed hybrid identification of a spacecraft simulator using optimized NARX neural networks
abstract: Spacecraft attitude dynamics simulators based on hemispherical air bearings are considered among the most innovative tools in the study of space system stability and control, as they provide unconstrained rotational motion and facilitate realistic ground-based testing of spacecraft. Nonetheless, the presence of nonlinear dynamics, external disturbances, frictional effects, complex aerodynamic phenomena within the air bearing, and inherent uncertainties has posed significant challenges to the development of high-fidelity analytical models for such systems. To tackle these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid identification approach that integrates physics-based modeling with data-driven learning. Accordingly, a NARX neural network is employed to account for the unknown residual dynamics not captured by nominal analytical models. To enhance model accuracy and generalization capabilities, two techniques—Genetic Algorithm and Taguchi method—are utilized to fine-tune the hyperparameters of the NARX network. The modeling process is quantitatively assessed using the Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Relative Root Mean Squared Error (RRMS) metrics under various input torques, including doublet and sinusoidal signals, as well as closed-loop control scenarios applied to the spacecraft simulator via reaction wheels. The results are compared with those from LSTM-based models, where the proposed model outperformed LSTM in terms of prediction accuracy, further demonstrating its suitability for aerospace applications. The high-fidelity model representation makes it valuable for the design and validation of control algorithms in aerospace applications.

title: A novel approximate-analytical method for prediction of milling stability
abstract: Accurate prediction of stability lobe diagrams (SLDs) is essential for chatter suppression and productivity enhancement in milling. Existing approaches are typically analytical or discretization-based: the widely used zero-order approximation (ZOA) is computationally efficient but may suffer from non-negligible prediction errors, whereas discretization-based methods improve accuracy at the expense of high computational cost. To address this trade-off, this paper proposes a novel approximate-analytical method (AAM) for efficient and accurate milling stability prediction. Based on nonlinear dynamic theory, an implicit analytical condition for the milling stability boundary is derived by incorporating higher-order harmonics of the directional coefficients, in which the stability limit is defined as the solution of a closed-form algebraic equation and traced directly without exhaustive parameter-space scanning. A numerical continuation scheme is then employed to efficiently construct SLDs, and a dedicated strategy is developed to robustly handle initial-point selection and lobe transitions. The proposed formulation provides a unified treatment of stability limits associated with both Neimark–Sacker and period-doubling bifurcations within a unified framework. Benchmark comparisons with ZOA, SDM, E-FDM, and FDM demonstrate that AAM achieves comparable prediction accuracy while significantly improving computational efficiency.

title: Experimental wavelet-based identification of nonlinear contact dynamics via instantaneous frequency and amplitude
abstract: This paper proposes a system identification framework tailored for mechanical systems exhibiting nonlinear dynamics. By leveraging wavelet analysis to extract instantaneous frequencies and amplitudes from vibration responses, the approach offers a powerful means of model updating. This study demonstrates the efficacy of using instantaneous frequencies and amplitudes as intrinsic dynamic features for updating nonlinear structural models. The methodology begins with the selection of an optimal mother wavelet, determined through the minimisation of several entropy measures. Conditional entropy minimisation is introduced to effectively handle abrupt, severe variations in instantaneous characteristics typically observed in nonlinear systems. Mathematical justifications for the entropy formulations are provided to underpin the methodology, alongside a comparative numerical case study that illustrates their effectiveness in accurately capturing instantaneous features. To validate the proposed framework, an experimental system exhibiting localised nonlinearity, arising from a frictional contact interface, is investigated. This nonlinearity stems from both slippage and micro-vibro-impact phenomena triggered under high excitation levels. The aim is to characterise these effects as nonlinear restoring forces, thereby enabling the development of a reliable simulator and predictive model in which the instantaneous characteristics extracted from structural responses serve as the principal indicators. A modified Valanis model is introduced and combined with a bilinear Hunt–Crossley model to replicate the nonlinear contact behaviour. The results demonstrate that the proposed model successfully predicts the key nonlinear features of the contact interface and accurately reproduces experimental observations across varying vibration amplitudes.

title: A two-phase multi-fidelity framework for virtual sensing of a rotating shaft system with physics-informed machine learning
abstract: This paper proposes a physics-informed machine learning framework for virtual sensing in the unmeasurable regions of a rotating shaft system. This framework addresses the challenge of predicting dynamic responses in regions where direct sensor installation is difficult or infeasible, thereby enabling real-time full-field virtual sensing under diverse operating conditions. The proposed framework comprises two sequential phases with distinct objectives. First, a physics-guided multi-agent diverse generative adversarial network (PhyMAD-GAN) synthesizes high-fidelity full-field synthetic responses under specific operating conditions by integrating full-field low-fidelity data from multiphysics finite element analysis (FEA) with point-wise measurements. The PhyMAD-GAN employs multiple generators to enhance synthetic data diversity, a shared discriminator to ensure consistency with measurements, and a physics-guided loss to preserve physical constraints. Second, a physics-informed adversarial domain-adaptive deep operator network (PADO-NET) constructs a generalized surrogate model that performs virtual sensing across both trained and untrained operating conditions. PADO-NET integrates operator learning to represent nonlinear mappings, domain-adversarial alignment to extract domain-invariant features, and physics-informed regularization to supervise governing physics laws. Extensive validation using dynamic responses, measured from an induction motor testbed under diverse operating conditions, confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The systematic analysis demonstrated significant improvements in predictive accuracy, robustness, and generalization compared with conventional data-driven neural networks. The proposed framework contributes to the artificial intelligence transformation of mechatronic systems by enabling reliable full-field virtual sensing. This capability provides physically consistent and reliable full-field reconstructions of shaft dynamics, which are essential for intelligent condition monitoring and fault diagnosis.

title: Dual-stream spatiotemporal graph attention network guided by lamb wave physics for damage localization
abstract: Lamb wave technology has become a powerful tool in composite structural health monitoring, enabling the detection and characterization of internal damage. However, the pronounced anisotropy of composite structures gives rise to intricate spatiotemporal correlations among multi-channel Lamb wave signals. Existing methods typically treat these signals as independent Euclidean sequences, which restricts their capacity to capture the coupling characteristics across multiple channels. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a novel damage localization approach based on a dual-stream spatiotemporal graph attention network (DS-STGAT), which is explicitly grounded in the physical principles of Lamb wave propagation. First, a Lamb wave graph is constructed using transfer entropy (TE) and time-of-flight (ToF), providing a graphical representation of multi-channel Lamb wave signals. Second, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) and a graph attention network (GAT) are employed to extract temporal and spatial features, respectively. Third, a bidirectional cross-attention (BCA) module is introduced to fuse spatiotemporal information, while damage localization regression is subsequently conducted using a multi-layer perceptron mixer (MLP-Mixer). Finally, experimental evaluations on simulated damage in composite plate structures demonstrate that DS-STGAT achieves superior damage localization performance, significantly outperforming existing benchmark methods.

title: A global DIC algorithm for tracking rotating objects using image unwrapping and FFT analysis
abstract: Digital Image Correlation applied to rotating objects is a challenging task due to the extremely large displacements to be detected and to the rotation of the subsets during revolutions. For these reasons, conventional DIC algorithms are limited to about 7◦ rotations before losing tracking capabilities. Nevertheless, a full 360◦ rotation is to be tracked in practical scenarios, so that a new paradigm in optical tracking of rotating objects remains urgent. In this paper, a global DIC algorithm is proposed to overcome the limitations of conventional methods. A simple analytical representation of the roto-translation is proposed, and an optimization algorithm is developed to find the rotation angle and center to minimize the discrepancies between the reference and rotated image. The critical issue of the procedure is represented by the selection of a reliable first guess, which, due to the presence of several local minima and a really sharp global minimum, needs to be extremely accurate for the optimization to converge. To this extent, a robust procedure is proposed based on image unwrapping and spatial-FFT analysis of the unwrapped image to infer a reliable first guess to be fed to the subsequent final optimization process. The approach was validated through experimental analysis of a rotating PC fan.

title: Enhancing interpretability via fine-grained objectives: A manifold-learning structured model for fault diagnosis of rolling bearings under noisy conditions
abstract: Dictionary learning (DL) has emerged as an effective data-driven approach for fault diagnosis due to its powerful sparse representation capability. However, its application to rolling bearing fault diagnosis still faces several challenges, including low accuracy, vulnerability of sparse reconstruction to strong noise interference, and insufficient discriminative power of the encoding. To address the above challenges, we propose a bearing fault diagnosis method based on a dual-analysis dictionary learning (DADL) with non-local sparsity (NLS) and block-diagonal (BD). The proposed method introduces a NLS term to characterize the underlying geometric manifold structure of the samples, aiming to extract key class-discriminative features under strong noise conditions. In addition, a BD term is incorporated to constrain the encoding into structured and discriminative sparse subspaces, with the goal of constructing features that are more easily recognized by the classifier. The proposed method maps the two learned constraints into a first analysis dictionary and a second analysis dictionary, respectively. For test samples, diagnostic results can be obtained through a simple projection operation, making the process more computationally efficient. In addition, the dual-analysis dictionary not only mines the essential features of the data, but also encourages the sub-analysis dictionary to learn more refined and interpretable feature subspaces. Finally, a linear classifier is jointly trained to perform the fault identification task. Extensive experiments on three challenging bearing fault datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high average diagnostic accuracies. In addition, comparative results with several advanced DL methods further demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

title: Reliability updating of structural dynamical systems under stochastic excitation using a two-phase subset simulation approach
abstract: This contribution addresses the task of updating the first-passage probability of structural dynamical systems under stochastic excitation. In this regard, a two-phase subset simulation approach is implemented within the framework of Bayesian model updating with structural reliability methods (BUS). Phase I focuses on the identification process, yielding an estimate of the evidence and a set of posterior samples. These samples are then used to construct the initial population for Phase II, which performs reliability updating. The procedure ultimately provides an estimate of the updated first-passage probability, along with a set of failure samples that follow the updated distribution. In essence, the same fundamental sampling strategy is employed, with only minor modifications, to carry out both identification and reliability updating in a sequential manner. The resulting method offers several features that are advantageous from a practical standpoint. Two numerical examples are presented to illustrate the capabilities of the proposed strategy. Overall, the approach constitutes an effective and theoretically sound alternative for data-informed performance assessment of stochastic structural systems.

title: Experimental investigation of the rocking and sliding behaviour of laterally flexible oscillators
abstract: This paper presents an experimental programme investigating the dynamic response of flexible rocking structures. Specimens which mimic a previously developed analytical flexible rocking oscillator model (the Sliding Flexible Rocking Model, i.e., SFRM) were created for this purpose. In these models, flexibility is introduced through the use of mechanical lateral springs connecting two effectively rigid subsystems (e.g. a bottom structure and a top mass). Furthermore, stiff support media with different coefficients of friction were placed under the specimen to enable the investigation of sliding and free flight behaviour. Preparatory tests were first conducted to verify the stiffness and coefficient of friction of system components. Free rocking tests and pulse excitation tests were then performed to investigate the dynamic response with stereo Digital Image Correlation (DIC) and accelerometer measurements. A Least Squares approach was used to extract motion of the rigid subsystems from DIC data. Furthermore, a data fusion method that extracts rigid subsystem velocities was also developed to explore system response at impact. The results illustrate that the chosen specimen geometry ensures repeatable 2D rocking motion as intended. Several key findings were concluded from the experiments. First, the conservation of horizontal momentum of the top mass during impacts is demonstrated by the experimental observations. Second, lateral flexibility was observed to influence rocking behaviour, primarily through its influence on energy dissipation at impact. Previous numerical observations that lateral flexibility can have either beneficial or detrimental influence on overturning instability are confirmed with experimental results. Third, the coefficients of friction of the support media affect rocking response significantly. For example, sliding is shown to accelerate the expiration of rocking motion by dissipating energy. However, low-friction support media can lead to excessive sliding, which may need to be avoided in practical applications. Finally, SFRM is demonstrated to be capable of capturing the general rocking and sliding motions observed in the experiments.

title: Deep reconstruction of sparse elastic wavefield and graph-based damage detection for accelerated health monitoring of PZT ceramics
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) of piezoelectric ceramics, particularly Lead Zirconate Titanate (PZT) substrates, requires accurate acquisition of elastic wave propagation to detect and localize damage. However, full-field wave acquisition is experimentally intensive and time-consuming. This study presents a sparse nonlinear reconstruction framework based on Coulomb coupling measurements that reduces acquisition complexity while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. Spatiotemporal wavefields are first acquired at a coarser temporal resolution from both healthy and damaged PZT specimens. For the healthy condition, the reduced data are used to compute a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) basis, and QR pivoting identifies optimal sensing locations. The corresponding sparse measurements are then used to train a shallow decoder network (Q-SDN) for wavefield reconstruction. Rather than training a separate decoder for the damaged condition, transfer learning adapts the Q-SDN model to the damaged dataset. This refines the learned representation to accommodate damage-induced variations while leveraging knowledge from the healthy data. Transfer learning allows the model to retain prior knowledge and adapt to new conditions without full retraining. However, the QR-selected sensor locations optimal for the healthy state may not be ideal for capturing wave propagation in the damaged case. Despite this, maintaining the same sensor layout avoids experimental reconfiguration. These locations effectively act as random placements in the damaged state, leading to the QR-Random-SDN (Q-R-SDN) framework. The proposed method avoids reconfiguration and separate model training for each state. Reconstruction performance is compared with a linear QR/POD baseline. The Q-R-SDN shows improved accuracy in both healthy and damaged scenarios. The reconstructed wavefields are further analyzed using an unsupervised Graph Deviation Network (GDN) trained only on healthy data. Damage localization is performed using forecast-based deviation scores, followed by contrast enhancement and morphological filtering.

title: Continuous flow matching framework for scalable density estimation in stochastic dynamical systems
abstract: The probability density function (PDF) plays a fundamental role in characterizing the evolutionary behavior of stochastic dynamical systems. However, the inherent high dimensionality, strong nonlinearity, and multiscale nature of most stochastic dynamical systems pose formidable challenges for both theoretical analysis and computational modeling. To address these issues, we propose a flow matching density estimation framework (FMDEF) for continuous modeling of complex distributions in stochastic systems. FMDEF leverages continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) with time-dependent vector fields to capture the temporal evolution of probability densities. The framework introduces a scalable, simulation-free training mechanism that directly optimizes vector fields to match target probability paths, eliminating the need for explicit stochastic process modeling while enabling direct extraction of probabilistic structures from system measurements. Extensive numerical experiments on stochastic systems demonstrate the method’s effectiveness and robustness. Both theoretical analysis and experimental results confirm FMDEF’s potential for extension to high-dimensional problems, establishing it as a rigorous and practical solution for real-world applications in stochastic dynamical systems.

title: Race shape error effects on automatic ball balancer performance
abstract: This study developed and evaluated a comprehensive multi-degree-of-freedom dynamic model of an Automatic Ball Balancer (ABB) system, formulated using the Euler–Lagrange method. The model rigorously integrates the key physical mechanisms, including nonlinear viscous–Coulomb friction, elastic ball-to-ball collisions based on Hertzian contact theory, and geometric imperfections in the race structure represented as sinusoidal waviness with variable order, magnitude. The friction model parameters were identified experimentally using a dedicated static test, and the combined nonlinear viscous and a Coulomb friction model was selected for its superior agreement with measurements. Using the derived equations of motion, time-domain numerical simulations were performed for 2275 cases covering wide variations in race shape order, shape amplitude, imbalance phase, angular acceleration, and imbalance levels. The simulation results quantitatively showed that race shape errors, particularly those with higher waviness order and magnitude, severely degrade the ABB self-balancing performance by increasing the residual vibrations and phase deviations. Angular acceleration predominantly affects the transient peak vibrations during startup, whereas imbalance magnitude strongly influences the steady-state vibration and balancing accuracy. The proposed modeling and simulation provides a predictive tool for assessing the coupled effects of structural imperfections and operating conditions on the ABB dynamics. These findings offer valuable design guidelines for optimizing the ABB geometry and specifying manufacturing tolerances to enhance the stability and reliability of rotating systems.

title: Analysis and control of nonlinear vibrations for piezoelectric FG-GRCRCL variable cross-section wing in unmanned aircraft using extended Melnikov method and NPPF controller, theory and experiment
abstract: The development of the low-altitude aircrafts is rapidly advancing. The unmanned aircrafts exhibit the large-amplitude nonlinear vibrations during the flight. The resonance issues and irregular chaotic motions are the primary contributors to the fatigue failure of the unmanned aircrafts. In this paper, the unmanned aircraft wings are simplified as the piezoelectric functionally graded graphene-reinforced composite rectangular cantilever laminated (FG-GRCRCL) variable cross-section plate. The nonlinear vibration characteristics occur for the aircraft wing trapezoidal plate by the experiment. Therefore, the researches of the nonlinear vibration control are extremely significant. The resonance responses control and chaotic motions control of high-dimensional non-autonomous nonlinear system for the piezoelectric FG-GRCRCL variable cross-section plate with the nonlinear positive position feedback (NPPF) controllers are investigated by the theory. The extended Melnikov method is employed to examine the control of the double-parameter multi-pulse chaotic motions for the nonlinear four-degree-of-freedom system. Regarding the primary resonances, 1/2 sub-harmonic parametric excitation resonances, as well as 1:1:1:1 internal resonances, the multiple scale perturbation (MSP) method is used for deriving the averaged equations for the piezoelectric FG-GRCRCL variable cross-section plate with the NPPF controllers. The resonant responses of the piezoelectric FG-GRCRCL variable cross-section plate with the NPPF controllers are analyzed through the amplitude-frequency and force-amplitude response curves. Based on the combination of theoretical analysis and vibration testing experiment, the piezoelectric FG-GRCRCL variable cross-section plate displays the hard-spring properties. It is found that the NPPF controller effectively controls the response amplitude of the amplitude-frequency response curves for low-order modes and the double-parameter multi-pulse chaotic motions under smaller parameter excitation. The bubble response shape of amplitude-frequency response curves and the wave transform reveal the transfer of energy between two-order modes of the system, confirming the control effectiveness of the NPPF controller.

title: A novel machinery RUL prediction method based on dynamic sparsely-connected spatial–temporal graphs and multi-scale lightweight design
abstract: Accurately predicting remaining useful life is crucial for mechanical equipment health management under multi-sensor monitoring. However, existing methods often model either the temporal correlations or the spatial correlations between sensors individually, thereby neglecting the crucial cross-temporal sensor correlations (CTSC) that arise from interactions between different sensors at varying times. In addition, noise interference and high computational complexity also restrict accurate, real-time prediction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a lightweight prediction model based on dynamic sparsely-connected spatio-temporal graphs (DSCSTG-LPM), aiming to effectively extract spatio-temporal features and improve prediction accuracy and efficiency. The model first utilizes an adaptive multi-scale identifier (AMSI) to extract noiseresistant multi-scale representations of time series. Then, through the ProbSparse self-attention mechanism, dynamic sparse spatiotemporal maps at each scale are constructed, and based on this, multi-hop feature propagation is achieved through Mixhop graph convolution to capture the global CTSC feature representation. Furthermore, two lightweight strategies, namely fully connected pruning and hierarchical propagation pruning, significantly reduce computational burden while maintaining performance. Experiments on the XJTU-SY bearing and C-MAPSS datasets show that the proposed model achieves an average reduction of 28% in MAE, 25% in RMSE, 5% in RMSE and 13% in SF compared to existing methods in evaluation indicators, verifying its effectiveness and superiority.

title: Dynamic analysis of the elastic ring squeeze film damper rotor system with bearing angular misalignment
abstract: The elastic ring squeeze film damper (ERSFD), with its excellent vibration suppression performance, has been applied in rotating machinery systems such as aero-engines. As essential components in rotating machinery, rolling bearings directly shape the dynamics of rotor systems. Due to installation errors and other factors, bearings are prone to angular misalignment faults. However, investigation into ERSFD-rotor systems with bearing angular misalignment is still insufficient. In this paper, a model capturing ERSFD-rotor system dynamic behavior accounting for bearing misalignment was established using the finite element method and lumped-mass method. Subsequently, bearing angular misalignment effects on ERSFD system vibrations and bearing contact characteristics were investigated. Partial simulation results were experimentally validated using a rotor test rig. Results indicate that the ERSFD effectively suppresses vibrations caused by bearing misalignment, reduces ball contact deformation, and reduces both ball contact forces and bearing force fluctuations.

title: Dynamic characteristics and evaluation of gear crack in electric drive system considering axial vibration
abstract: In electric drive systems dominated by transverse excitations, the axial response induced by the large helix angle of helical gears can more prominently reflect fault characteristics. However, this aspect has not received sufficient attention. In this paper, a complete degree-of-freedom dynamic model is established, which integrates unbalanced magnetic pull, bearing restoring forces, and multi-stage helical gear meshing excitations. On this basis, the effects of crack spatial propagation and center distance error on stiffness degradation and meshing phase, as well as their dynamic characteristics, are investigated in detail. In addition, a novel crack fault analysis and evaluation method is proposed for the quantitative identification of crack fault severity under complex operating conditions. The results demonstrate that the axial response is more sensitive to crack-induced stiffness degradation, exhibits richer fault features, and shows stronger robustness against assembly errors. The proposed analysis and evaluation methods effectively suppress interference from multi-stage gear transmissions and mitigate inaccuracies in crack severity assessment arising from crack-induced and meshing-phase-related band asymmetry. These findings provide applicable theoretical foundations and analysis tools for health monitoring and fault diagnosis of electric drive systems.

title: A knowledge fusion-driven domain generalization diagnosis framework for unseen operating conditions
abstract: In engineering applications, deep learning-based fault diagnosis must balance generalization and model complexity amid dynamic conditions. High generalization often demands complex models, yet excessive complexity reduces computational efficiency and hinders deployment. To address this, we propose Multi-knowledge Domain Generalization with Dynamic Temperature Distillation (MDG-DTD), a knowledge fusion-driven framework. First, we introduce a distillation method that fuses multiple specialized teacher models via confidence weighting and feature alignment to derive a generalized teacher model. Second, a dynamic temperature distillation strategy integrates attention transfer and adversarial temperature regulation to adaptively adjust the distillation process, optimizing student model learning and efficiency. Experimental results on the motor current and industrial robot vibration datasets validate MDG-DTD’s superiority over existing domain generalization methods in diagnosing faults under unseen conditions. Notably, the student model, using only 0.15% of the teacher model’s parameters and 0.36% of its floating point operations, retains at least 96.33% and 97.78% of its performance, respectively.

title: Bandgap tunability in strongly and weakly nonlinear periodic tensegrity structures
abstract: This study explores bandgap formation in periodic nonlinear tensegrity structures within a non-dimensional framework. Nonlinear equations of motion were derived for a general tensegrity structure and rendered non-dimensional. Band structures were predicted using both perturbation and harmonic balance methods, with perturbation limited to the weakly nonlinear regime. Although the formulation accommodates general two- and three-dimensional lattices, the analysis focuses on a one-dimensional D-bar tensegrity chain as an example. Nonlinearity is introduced via a cubic constitutive law in the strings, capturing hardening or softening behavior. All combinations of nonlinearity type and location are investigated under varying wave amplitudes to assess their impact on bandgap characteristics. In the weakly nonlinear case, excellent agreement is observed between perturbation and harmonic balance method results. Amplitude-dependent bandgaps exhibit shifting, shrinking and widening, while in the strongly nonlinear regime, more pronounced effects such as the roton effect and complete closure and significant shifts in bandgap location and width emerge.

title: Methods for discovering first- and second-order hidden periodicities and their application to vibration signal analysis
abstract: Hidden periodicities are modeled as periodically non-stationary random processes (PNRPs), which describe both the deterministic and stochastic recurrences of signals. Detecting the time-periodic behavior of moment functions and estimating their corresponding frequencies is the first step in analyzing experimental data. Estimators of the fundamental frequencies for the PNRP mean and covariance functions – obtained by maximizing a reduced least-squares functional – are analyzed in this paper. The estimating functionals take the form of magnitudes representing the time-averaged powers of the superpositions of harmonics of the test frequency and its multiples. For a Gaussian PNRP, it is shown that the maxima of these functionals are asymptotically unbiased and consistent estimators of the basic frequencies, provided that the covariance function decays with increasing lag. The basic frequency estimators are analyzed as solutions to nonlinear equations representing the necessary conditions for maximum excitation. These solutions are obtained using the small-parameter method, and formulas for the biases and variances are derived from the first-order approximations. The formulas are then specified for simple particular cases of a PNRP, and numerical results are presented. The proposed techniques are verified using simulated sequences and a real-world time series of vibration signals.

title: Multi-super-synchrosqueezing short-time fractional fourier transform algorithm and its applications
abstract: Time-frequency analysis (TFA) techniques have important application values in fields such as mechanical equipment fault diagnosis. They can expand one-dimensional signals to the two-dimensional time–frequency (TF) plane, revealing the dynamic evolution of the frequency components of non-stationary signals. The traditional Short-time Fourier transform (STFT) has limited TF resolution due to its fixed window function. Although the Short-time Fractional Fourier transform (STFrFT) has better performance, it still has deficiencies in optimal rotation order matching, window function selection, and energy concentration. These limitations severely restrict the application of existing methods in complex engineering scenarios where signals are often multi-component, low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), and nonlinear frequency-modulated. To address these issues, this paper proposes the Multi-Super-Synchrosqueezing Short-time Fractional Fourier transform (MSSTFrFT) algorithm. This algorithm integrates the multi-scale synchrosqueezing concept and STFrFT, and improves the TF energy concentration of complex multi-component signals through an iterative re-distribution strategy in the fractional domain, essentially different from the LPFT-based multi-synchrosqueezing method that relies on polynomial fitting and single-domain energy redistribution. Its process includes signal pre-processing, selection of the optimal window length, and iterative synchrosqueezing to obtain a TF distribution with high-energy concentration. Compared with existing TFA methods, this work achieves four key novelties: (1) the integration of multi-super-synchrosqueezing with STFrFT for cross-domain synergy; (2) a kurtosis-based adaptive rotation order selection mechanism with mathematical derivation of energy clustering and convergence proof for universal applicability; (3) a fractional domain iterative energy re-distribution strategy enhancing both concentration and anti-noise performance; (4) a unified framework adaptable to diverse simulated and engineering signals. The performance of the algorithm is verified using two simulated signals in a noisy environment. After comparing multiple algorithms, it is found that MSSTFrFT has the best performance in terms of TF concentration and anti-noise ability. Notably, the algorithm adaptively determines the optimal rotation order and achieves iterative energy redistribution, realizing a balance between TF concentration and anti-noise performance that outperforms state-of-the-art methods by addressing their inherent limitations in domain adaptability, rotation order matching, and synergy between concentration and anti-noise capability. When applied to the processing of actual signals such as bearing fault signals, rotor rub-impact fault signals, and cantilever beam hammer-impact modal vibration signals, it demonstrates excellent TF feature extraction capabilities.

title: A real-time and offline weld defect detection framework using planar EMT with selective measurement and deep learning
abstract: Electromagnetic tomography (EMT) offers a non-contact approach for weld defect imaging, yet traditional full-pair configurations suffer from low speed and limited adaptability to uneven weld surfaces. This study proposes an integrated real-time and offline weld-defect detection framework that couples selective coil-pair planar EMT with a prototype-guided similarity-fusion UNet (ProSiF-UNet). A 16-channel planar EMT sensor was developed, and a simplified sensitivity matrix using next-nearest coil pairs (d = 2) significantly reduced computation while preserving image fidelity. For real-time monitoring, a lightweight linear back projection (LBP)-based reconstruction enables 200+ frames per second (FPS) imaging, whereas an offline Landweber (LW) iteration ensures high-fidelity analysis. The prototype-guided similarity-fusion segmentation network (ProSiF-UNet) integrates cosine-similarity prototypes and exponential moving average (EMA)-based fusion to enhance defect segmentation on limited data, reducing missed detections by 40% compared with standard U-Net. The unified framework achieves a practical balance between speed, accuracy, and robustness, demonstrating strong potential for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled industrial weld inspection.

title: Frequency-selective transmission of one-way ultrasounds based on wave barriers
abstract: Artificial manipulation of ultrasounds is of great interest in sensor development. However, simultaneous manipulation of frequency and directivity of ultrasounds is rarely reported. This study proposes a standing wave barrier to transmit one-way ultrasound with a selective frequency. First, a resonator is developed to confine standing waves inside itself. The confined wave frequency is artificially controlled by resonator size. The transmission is reduced while the reflection remains unchanged when waves pass through the resonator. Second, the proposed resonators constitute a barrier in backing materials and transducer housing to absorb unwanted waves and transmit ultrasounds in one direction. The developed transducer effectively suppresses the interference from multidirectional waves, achieving a 1255.9% improvement in signal fidelity. Finally, the transducer is applied to detect both the geometric contour and internal defects of a steel plate. The proposed method promotes the sound control and sensor development.

title: Intelligent time–frequency feature embedding and reshaping for bearing fault diagnosis in motion control applications
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of bearing faults under nonstationary operating conditions presents significant challenges, particularly in independent cart systems where variable speeds, coupled translational–rotational motion, and transient dynamics substantially influence vibration signals. In such contexts, traditional time–frequency representations and unsupervised learning methods often yield inadequate class separation and unreliable anomaly detection results. This study presents a fully unsupervised diagnostic framework that overcomes existing limitations through two complementary innovations. First, an intelligent strategy automatically selects the lengths of the spectrogram windows using Theil index-based inequality measures. Second, a technique for reshaping distributions transforms the extracted features into compact, uniformly distributed representations without the need for class labels. Experimental validation using the MOIRA–UNIMORE bearing dataset demonstrated significant enhancements in terms of feature compactness and class separability. Further robustness and cross-dataset validation on the Case Western Reserve University and Politecnico di Torino bearing datasets corroborated the stability and generalizability of the proposed framework. These findings suggest that integrating adaptive time–frequency analysis with principled distribution reshaping provides an effective, computationally efficient solution for unsupervised bearing-fault diagnosis in nonstationary industrial environments. • Automatic STFT window length selection via Theil index. • DRBT enables stable, bounded bimodality-aware feature compaction. • Fully unsupervised TAIW → t-SNE/UMAP → DRBT pipeline proposed. • Validated on CWRU, Politecnico, and MOIRA–UNIMORE datasets.

title: Dual-stage adaptive long-gauge fiber optic strain sensor for service-to-failure monitoring
abstract: Despite significant advancements in the field of structural health monitoring (SHM), there have been significant challenges in the development of a full-lifecycle SHM. To enable a reliable, comprehensive and accurate full-lifecycle SHM, even under extreme conditions, this study proposes a novel Dual-Stage Adaptive Long-Gauge Fiber Optic Strain Sensor (DS-LGFS). This sensor seamlessly transitions between high-precision monitoring in small strains and reliable sensing during large deformations. A hybrid deployment scheme, integrating conventional LGFSs with the new DS-LGFSs, is designed to facilitate a full-lifecycle SHM. We establish a comprehensive theoretical framework to clarify the relationship between key design parameters and the sensor’s dual-stage behavior. Furthermore, a dual-stage temperature compensation strategy and an error analysis are developed to ensure measurement reliability. Experimental results demonstrate an ultimate strain measurement capability of 2%, a 178% improvement over standard bare FBG sensors, alongside exceptional repeatability and stability. These findings underscore the DS-LGFS’s significant potential for accurate, reliable, and practical full-lifecycle SHM.

title: Complex modes identification of fluid-conveying pipeline in the concurrent existence of harmonic and broadband-random excitations
abstract: Identifying the modal parameters of operational fluid-conveying pipelines under operational states is crucial for assessing their safety and stability. However, current operational modal analysis methods can only identify real modal parameters of engineering structures under broadband random excitation, failing to accurately extract complex modal parameters of fluid-conveying pipelines subjected to combined excitation of harmonic and broadband random loads. Hence, this paper theoretically derives the difference in the vibration response correlation functions of a fluid-conveying pipeline caused by the broadband random and harmonic excitations and establishes the mathematical relationship between the vibration response correlation functions excited by broadband random loads and the complex modal parameters. On this basis, this paper proposes a first-ever method for identifying complex modal parameters of fluid-conveying pipelines under combined excitation of harmonic and broadband random loads. This method integrates variational modes and time–frequency analysis techniques and is capable of identifying the natural frequencies, damping ratios, as well as amplitude and phase of complex mode shapes of the fluid-conveying pipeline under operational states. The proposed method has the advantages of high accuracy and strong anti-interference capability. The accuracy and superiority of the proposed method are demonstrated through a numerical U-shaped fluid-conveying pipeline and comparison with the classical method. The application of the method to the identification of the first four complex modal parameters of a real fluid-conveying pipeline with a centrifugal pump under an operational state gives experimental evidence of its effectiveness.

title: Robust model-based single-source localization in reverberant environments using a statistically enhanced TR-MUSIC framework
abstract: Sound source localization (SSL) in reverberant environments remains a challenging topic, as reflections typically create overlapping signals that mask the direct path and make it difficult to locate the source. To this end, although Time Reversal Multiple Signal Classification (TR-MUSIC) has proven effective for localizing scatterers in complex media, its use is hindered for source localization in acoustics. Within TR-MUSIC experimentally measured signals are typically compared to also experimentally derived so-called steering vectors. However, experimentally constructing such steering vectors is not only tedious, but sometimes even not feasible, especially in small cavities and complex geometries. Although replacing experimentally measured steering vectors with model-based ones is possible, due to model uncertainties the robustness of the method is significantly affected, often leading to false detections. To mitigate this, signals from multiple microphones are often employed, again impacting its applicability in smaller cavities and complex geometries. In that context, aiming at simultaneously increasing the robustness of the model-based application of the TR-MUSIC, while minimizing the number of required microphones, this paper proposes a statistically enhanced TR-MUSIC algorithm. Specifically, within a pre-processing step based on a statistical correlation rule, the number of candidate source points is reduced, which in combination with a frequency selection algorithm significantly enhances the localization performance of the standard TR-MUSIC. The effectiveness of the proposed method is initially evaluated in a well-characterized reverberant cavity of industrially relevant dimensions, demonstrating improved performance compared to the baseline method and, in the benchmarking comparisons, to the Steered Response Power with Phase Transform (SRP-PHAT) approach. The sensitivity of the proposed framework is systematically investigated with respect to different signal-to-noise ratios, selected frequency ranges, and geometric uncertainties. Furthermore, the method is validated in a complex Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) chamber characterized by a higher geometric uncertainty, confirming its robustness under realistic engineering conditions.

title: Optimal reduced-order model for Vehicle-Bridge Interaction and bridge damage detection using model based SHM-ML techniques
abstract: • Optimal reduced-order vehicle-bridge interaction model. • Reliable Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) and damage detection. • VBI computational framework with significantly reduced computational cost. • Enriched model with realistic rail irregularities. • Experimental validation over multiple operating speeds, loads, and damage scenarios. Bridge structures subjected to moving vehicle loads exhibit complex dynamic behavior influenced by structural flexibility and rail surface irregularities. The correct approach and optimal modeling of vehicle-bridge interaction effects are crucial for the accurate computational determination of dynamic bridge vibrations, for reliable Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) and damage detection. The purpose of this work is twofold. First, a novel computational framework is introduced to generate an optimal reduced-order Vehicle-Bridge Interaction (VBI) model that captures the essential dynamics of the system with significantly reduced computational cost. This process begins with the development of a high-fidelity finite element (FE) model of the bridge which is updated using experimental modal data. This model is then reduced using Component Mode Synthesis (CMS) to enable efficient simulation while preserving the essential dynamic behavior and is combined with a simplified vehicle model enriched with realistic rail irregularities, producing an accurate and computationally efficient VBI system. Second, the study introduces a classification framework based on a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on numerically generated data from the validated VBI model. The CNN operates on frequency-domain features derived from bridge acceleration responses, which reflect damage-induced changes in stiffness and energy distribution of the structure. Using these features and an ensemble of independently trained CNNs, the framework classifies the structural health condition of the bridge.

title: Digital Twin-Enabled thermal error prediction and compensation system for CNC Machine tool feed systems
abstract: Thermal deformation in computer numerical control (CNC) machine tool feed systems severely degrades machining accuracy. Conventional mechanism-driven thermal models require complex parameter calibration and intensive computation, while data-driven approaches demand extensive high-quality data and struggle to reconstruct unmeasurable temperature fields. Moreover, existing digital twin (DT) solutions for machine tool thermal behavior lack effective mechanisms to dynamically update model parameters and maintain consistency between the virtual twin and the physical system. To address these limitations, this article proposes a digital twin-enabled thermal error prediction and compensation system for CNC machine tool feed systems (DT-TEPCS-FS), integrating the thermal characteristic mechanism model construction (TCMMC) module, thermal characteristic mechanism model update (TCMMU) module, thermal error prediction model construction (TEPMC) module, and thermal error compensation (TEC) module. Initially, the TCMMC module constructs the thermal mechanism model with boundary conditions that incorporate multi-source heat generation, contact thermal resistance, and convection effects. Subsequently, the thermal characteristic mechanism model is updated with industrial data in the TCMMU module. The updated model then provides unmeasurable temperature information to the TEPMC module, which implements a dual-stage prediction strategy for thermal error prediction. Ultimately, the TEC module deploys the predicted thermal errors to the CNC systems for online compensation. Industrial validations demonstrate that the DT-TEPCS-FS achieves a mean absolute prediction error of 1.59 μm and reduces machining dimensional errors by 76.71% after compensation, highlighting its potential for high-precision and thermal error control in practical manufacturing environments.

title: Energy attenuation based on vibration power flow in high-speed CRTS III slab ballastless track systems
abstract: This study investigates vibration energy transmission and attenuation in the CRTS III ballastless track structure of high-speed railways. High‑frequency vibration tests on a standard multilayer ballastless track structure and low‑frequency vibration tests on a CRTS III ballastless track structure were conducted. A finite element model of the train–track system was established, incorporating random track irregularities as excitation. The power flow method was applied to quantify vibration energy transmission and attenuation characteristics in the time, spatial, and frequency domains (0–1500 Hz) for the CRTS III ballastless track structure, and to identify the critical frequencies and energy concentration locations. Results show that the vibration energy of the track structure during train operation is mainly concentrated in the 0–200 Hz range, and the critical frequencies increase with train speed. Reducing fastener stiffness, increasing fastener damping, and increasing isolation layer stiffness can reduce the maximum power flow amplitude transmitted to the sub-rail structure, while increasing isolation layer stiffness can also reduce the amplitude transmitted to the foundation.

title: Nonlinear identification and waveform prediction of blast-induced ground vibrations using regularized Volterra series
abstract: Predicting the complete waveform of blasting vibration responses remains a significant challenge in blasting engineering. Existing empirical models only capture peak parameters, necessitating extensive field tests while failing to characterize the nonlinear dynamic properties of vibration propagation. Based on Volterra series theory, this paper presents a technological application framework for nonlinear system identification specifically adapted to transient strong excitation systems, such as blasting vibrations. The core contribution lies in adapting standard Volterra identification techniques to the extreme time-scale mismatch between short-duration blast excitations and long-duration seismic responses. By proposing a domain-specific sparse regression matrix construction method coupled with Tikhonov regularization, the study effectively resolves the severe ill-conditioning and underdetermined problems inherent to this specific engineering context. To validate the method, an empirical study was conducted using blasting as a representative transient excitation source. Requiring only a single reference test for parameter identification, the proposed method successfully predicts complete system responses under varying excitation intensities (charge weights) and complex timing sequences (multi-hole delays). In a time–frequency dual-domain evaluation using field data, the Volterra model accurately predicted responses across all complex scenarios. Its weighted comprehensive performance index reached 66.65, a 33.3% improvement over the benchmark linear Anderson method (50.00), demonstrating superior nonlinear capture capability and robustness. This study establishes a new paradigm for blasting vibration prediction and provides a solution for broader transient mechanical systems subjected to impact or seismic loads.

title: Multi-channel chatter detection in robotic milling based on successive multivariate variational mode decomposition and hybrid deep convolutional neural network
abstract: Chatter is a critical factor that limits machining quality and production efficiency in robotic milling. Therefore, timely and accurate online chatter detection is essential for achieving high-precision and high-efficiency machining. However, the dynamic properties of milling robots are highly pose-dependent, which significantly increases the randomness and complexity of chatter. Furthermore, due to the strong nonlinearity and flexibility of milling robots, chatter induces coupled three-dimensional vibrations. As a result, relying on vibration signals from a single direction is insufficient for achieving reliable chatter detection. In this paper, a multi-channel online chatter detection method in robotic milling is proposed, based on successive multivariate variational mode decomposition (SMVMD) and hybrid deep convolutional neural network. First, the SMVMD method combined with a dimensionless chatter index is employed to adaptively extract the chatter components in the three-channel acceleration signals. Then, the energy ratio sequence between the reconstructed chatter signal and the milling signal is calculated. Finally, a hybrid deep convolutional neural network (ICR-DCN), composed of Inception, convolutional block attention module (CBAM), residual network (ResNet) and classification module, is constructed to automatically extract chatter features from the energy ratio sequence and achieve online chatter detection. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve high-precision online chatter detection across variations in different robotic poses, cutting parameters, workpiece materials and tools. Comparative studies further validate the accuracy and stability of the proposed method across various scenarios.

title: Topological mechanical neural networks as classifiers through in situ backpropagation learning
abstract: Recently, a new frontier in computing has emerged with physical neural networks (PNNs) harnessing intrinsic physical processes for learning. Here, we explore topological mechanical neural networks (TMNNs) inspired by the quantum spin Hall effect (QSHE) in topological metamaterials, for machine learning classification tasks. TMNNs utilize pseudospin states and the robustness of the QSHE, making them damage-tolerant for binary classification. We first demonstrate data clustering using untrained TMNNs. Then, for specific tasks, we derive an in situ backpropagation algorithm, a two-step, local-rule method that updates TMNNs using only local information, enabling in situ physical learning. TMNNs achieve high accuracy in classifications of Iris flowers, Penguins, and Seeds while maintaining robustness against bond pruning. Furthermore, we demonstrate parallel classification via frequency-division multiplexing, assigning different tasks to distinct frequencies for enhanced efficiency. Our work introduces in situ backpropagation for wave-based mechanical neural networks and positions TMNNs as promising neuromorphic computing hardware for classification tasks. • Mechanical analogue of in situ backpropagation allows for local physical learning. • Topological mechanical neural networks use pseudospin states for classification tasks. • We demonstrate high accuracy in various classification tasks. • We realize the implementation of classification tasks in parallel.

title: Wind farm-level scour detection around offshore monopile foundations using unsupervised domain adaptation
abstract: This study proposes a novel Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) approach for scour detection around offshore wind turbines (OWT) at the wind farm level. In this approach, acceleration data collected from a single reference OWT (so-called source turbine) are used to detect scour presence around other turbines (so-called target turbines), located within the same wind farm. Acceleration data are collected along the tower height under varying environmental conditions and are processed to extract the tower bending modal frequencies, which serve as structural health features. To address the distributional shift in the data across OWTs within a wind farm - arising from changes in structural configurations, environmental loading conditions, and soil properties - four UDA techniques, Geodesic Flow Kernel (GFK), Unsupervised Domain-Invariant Component Analysis (UDICA), Subspace Alignment (SA), and Correlation Alignment (CORAL), are employed. By using these UDA methods, the healthy feature distributions from the source OWT are aligned with those of the target turbines and subsequently used to train an Autoencoder (AE) deep learning algorithm for scour detection. The study evaluates the limitations of traditional anomaly detection methods for scour in terms of their ability to be generalised across turbines, and demonstrates how UDA techniques enable model generalisation at the wind farm level. The results highlight the effectiveness of the GFK in mitigating feature distribution discrepancies and enabling an accurate detection of scour at multiple OWTs within the same wind farm, followed by SA and UDICA. However, CORAL demonstrated a lower capacity for reducing the distribution shift across different OWTs, making it less feasible for a scour detection application.

title: Separated-variable physics informed neural operators for solving dynamic PDEs
abstract: Solving dynamic partial differential equations (PDEs) remains a fundamental challenge in computational science and engineering. Although physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) provides a mesh-free approach to solutions, it continues to face several persistent issues, such as spectral bias in high-frequency problems, optimization difficulties in high-order PDEs, and multi-objective optimization problem arising from complex boundary conditions. To address these challenges, we propose the separated-variable physics informed neural operators (SV-PINO). The method decomposes dynamic PDEs into a family of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) within the eigenfunction space, effectively transforming the original difficulties into a unified problem of learning ODE coefficients that are readily handled by neural operators. Beyond establishing a robust framework for a broad class of challenging PDEs, SV-PINO also demonstrates its versatility through successful extension to model the dynamic response of discrete systems that often lack definite PDE formulations. Extensive numerical experiments show that SV-PINO achieves high accuracy and strong generalization under demanding conditions, thereby offering a systematic solution to key bottlenecks in PIDL for engineering simulation and dynamics modeling.

title: Parametric excitation response analysis and experimental study of deepwater managed pressure drilling riser system
abstract: Managed Pressure Drilling (MPD) technology was crucial to solve the issue of narrow mud density windows in deepwater drilling operations. Under complex environments, the top tension fluctuation of MPD riser system due to platform heave motion would cause possible parametric excitation response (PER) of the riser system, which further posed significant risks to the safety of the risers. However, theoretical researches on the PER of MPD riser system could be found sporadically in related literatures. In this study, a theoretical model was developed to analyze the PER of MPD riser system, considering platform heave motion, internal managed pressure and drilling fluid velocity. The differential element method and d’Alembert’s principle were utilized to establish the governing equations of the PER of MPD riser systems, then the equations were solved using Newmark-β integration method, and scaled experiments were conducted to verify the theoretical model. A case study showed an increase in the top tension ratio from 1.4 to 1.8 would result in a decrease in the PER amplitude of the riser system by 46.43% approximately, and when the backpressure was increased from 8 MPa to 16 MPa, the amplitude of the riser system would decrease by 18.19% approximately. Additionally, when the drilling fluid velocity was increased from 2 m/s to 6 m/s, the amplitude of the riser system would slightly increase by about 2.15%. The related approaches and conclusions could provide theoretical references for the design and safe operation of the deepwater MPD riser system.

title: A closed-form approximation of the Wiener path integral most probable path for efficient stochastic response determination of nonlinear dynamical systems
abstract: An approximate analytical approach within the Wiener path integral (WPI) technique is developed for efficiently determining the response transition probability density function (PDF) of nonlinear dynamical systems. Specifically, in the WPI formulation, the transition PDF is expressed as a functional integral over the space of response trajectories satisfying prescribed initial and final conditions. Typically, this functional integral is approximately evaluated by considering only the contribution of the most probable path, i.e., the trajectory with the highest probability of occurrence. Since the most probable path is an extremum of the functional integral, it is determined by solving a functional minimization problem that takes the form of a boundary value problem (BVP). For general nonlinear systems, this BVP must be solved numerically. Furthermore, the conventional WPI implementation requires solving a large number of such BVPs — one for each point of the discretized response PDF domain — leading to substantial computational cost. To address this challenge, the BVP is cast herein into a convenient approximate form for which an exact analytical solution exists. This enables the computation of the response transition PDF at practically zero computational cost while maintaining satisfactory accuracy. Two representative oscillators exhibiting Duffing-type nonlinearities and Preisach hysteresis are considered to demonstrate the reliability of the developed approach. Comparisons with PDF estimates based on Monte Carlo simulation data are included as well.

title: Accelerometer-only displacement reconstruction for influence line identification under a passing vehicle
abstract: Traditional approaches to identifying bridge influence lines (ILs) often face significant environmental and deployment constraints, making reliable displacement measurement difficult for bridges lacking stable reference points or favorable sensing geometry. This work introduces an accelerometer-only approach that reconstructs displacement from measured acceleration through double integration, followed by piecewise-linear constraint enforcement to suppress low-frequency drift while preserving the physically meaningful response components required for IL extraction. The proposed procedure is lightweight and sensor-efficient, requiring only accelerometers and known inspection-vehicle information, and it can be implemented without interrupting normal traffic or installing external reference frames. Its performance is verified through numerical simulations, laboratory experiments, and field measurements on in-service bridges. The method maintains stable accuracy across variations in inspection vehicle mass and speed, span configuration, road roughness, and surrounding traffic disturbances, etc. Across all examined cases, the relative error of the peak value of bridge IL has not exceeded 4.31%, demonstrating the proposed approach as a practical, non-intrusive, and cost-effective solution for bridge condition assessment under real-world conditions.

title: A generalized pareto distribution-enabled health indicator via joint parameters for bearing degradation monitoring
