We then develop a generalized numerical framework that enables the inversion of dispersion relations for metamaterials with arbitrary band structures, including active and damped components, variable mass distributions, and inertial interactions. By formulating the inverse problem as an optimization task, we incorporate constraints ensuring physical realizability while employing L1 regularization to promote sparsity in interaction matrices. Our approach successfully reconstructs desired dispersion relations for various test cases, demonstrating the ability to design lattices with customized multiband wave characteristics. The results highlight the robustness and versatility of our methodology, providing a powerful toolkit for advanced wave manipulation and nonreciprocal wave control.

title: Generative adversarial fault-tolerance for robust multimodal sensor fusion in industrial systems
abstract: Modern industrial systems rely heavily on multimodal sensor data to handle random emerging faults. To address this, we propose a novel generative adversarial framework embedded within a multimodal autoencoder architecture for active latent restoration of compromised sensor streams. Our method leverages a two-stage training process: first, a multimodal autoencoder is pre-trained on clean data to learn robust latent representations; then, a generative adversarial network is optimized to map corrupted latent vectors to their correct distributions while preserving cross-modal consistency through a task-specific penalty. Additionally, we adopt the discriminator optimization process to identify anomalies in the underlying data. Therefore, the discriminator is designed to conditionally initiate the generator’s fault-correction mechanism. Experiments on multimodal industrial robotic datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms conventional methods in reconstructing accurate signals from corrupted inputs, even under several failure scenarios. The proposed system not only enhances fault resilience but also opens new directions for generative models in industrial automation, bridging the gap between robust data fusion and real-time error recovery.

title: Event-triggered control and dynamical compensator for active suspension systems with high-order fully actuated system approach
abstract: Achieving efficient vibration isolation control for active suspension systems while reducing communication burden contributes to improved ride comfort and enhances the practical applicability. This paper investigates the event-triggered control (ETC) for active suspension systems based on the high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system approach. First, we model the active suspension system as a fourth-order system, which facilitates the direct synthesis of control laws for desired tracking error dynamics. To conserve communication resources in networked control systems, a fixed-threshold event-triggering mechanism is employed, and a hyperbolic tangent function is introduced to guarantee exponential stability of the controlled system. Moreover, uncertainties and disturbances in practical systems can severely degrade the vibration isolation performance of suspension systems. Therefore, a universal dynamical compensator is designed to better suppress unknown disturbances. Finally, stability analysis is conducted for the uncertain nonlinear suspension system, and experiments demonstrate the efficacy and feasibility of the developed method.

title: Multiscale synergistic adaptive multi-mapping entropy: A novel approach for enhanced fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: To effectively capture the dynamic characteristics inherent in the vibration signals associated with rotating machinery, multiscale analysis methods can extract features at various time scales, which is essential for improving the accuracy of fault diagnosis. While current entropy-based methods have been effectively applied within a multiscale framework, they typically depend on a single analytical criterion to quantify signal complexity. This limitation often leads to insufficient feature extraction and limited diagnostic performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel multiscale synergistic adaptive multi-mapping entropy (MSAME) method. MSAME constructs a multi-mapping analytical framework by integrating four nonlinear mapping functions with different characteristics, and employs an adaptive weighting mechanism based on Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD) to dynamically evaluate and fuse the unique information provided by each mapping. This approach enables a more comprehensive feature representation of the signals. Analysis of numerical simulation signals demonstrates the superiority of synergistic adaptive multi-mapping entropy (SAME) as a complexity index under single-scale conditions, proving its advantage over traditional entropy methods in quantifying and distinguishing different signal complexities. Experimental results show that compared with several multiscale entropy methods and various single-mapping entropy methods, the MSAME achieves the highest fault diagnosis accuracy, 96.42% and 97.95% on bearing and gear datasets respectively, and also exhibits stronger feature stability and noise robustness. These findings confirm the excellent fault feature extraction capability of MSAME as well as the effectiveness of its multi-mapping adaptive fusion strategy.

title: FMCW radar dynamic demodulation: Enabling accurate vibration measurement
abstract: High-accuracy vibration displacement reconstruction and parameter estimation using frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar are essential for non-contact condition monitoring of engineering structures. However, conventional displacement estimation methods (e.g. CZT) suffer from phase jump phenomenon and high computational cost. Moreover, phase-based displacement extraction yields heteroscedastic measurement uncertainty due to additive observation phase noise (AOPN), which reduces the reliability of vibration parameter estimation when using unweighted spectral or least-squares methods. To address these issues, this paper proposes a two-stage framework consisting of a dynamic demodulation algorithm (DDA) and an AOPN-weighted iterative optimization (AWIO) method. The DDA updates the demodulation beat frequency on a sweep-by-sweep basis to suppress phase jump and stabilize slow-time displacement tracking for vibrating targets. The AWIO formulates vibration frequency and amplitude estimation as a weighted optimization problem, where sample-wise weights are derived from the uncertainty induced by observation phase noise, improving robustness to noise and multi-component interference. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods maintain superior performance under low signal-to-noise ratios and multi-component interference. The displacement estimation error is significantly lower than that of conventional methods, and the amplitude estimation accuracy can reach the micrometer scale. This paper provides a high-accuracy, computationally efficient, and practical non-contact solution for engineering vibration monitoring.

title: Enhanced AR-based simulation method for non-Gaussian wind pressure process using machine learning model and piecewise Johnson transformation model
abstract: Accurate simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressures on low-rise buildings is essential for structural wind-resistant design. Recently, autoregressive (AR) models combined with the maximum entropy method (MEM) have been employed to develop an AR–MEM-based non-Gaussian wind pressure simulation approach, which has demonstrated satisfactory accuracy and convenience. However, this method suffers from low computational efficiency, limited applicability, and difficulty in extension to multivariate wind pressure simulations. This study comprehensively uses AR, piecewise Johnson transformation model (PJTM), machine learning model (ML), and proposes a novel ML-enhanced AR-PJTM (ML-AR-PJTM) method for simulating non-Gaussian wind pressure, which significantly improves simulation efficiency and widens the application range. In this method, the Extra Trees (ET) model is firstly adopted to map the target power spectral density to the parameters of a set of formulas to determine the first ten-order standardized central moments of the input process in AR model, in which a formulation for expanding the number of training samples based on limited experimental data has been developed. Subsequently, the Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) model, combined with Bayesian optimization (BO), is employed to establish a nonlinear mapping from the first ten-order standardized central moments to the corresponding statistical moments used to determine PJTM, in which another similar formulation for expanding the number of training samples based on limited experimental data has also been developed. Numerical cases show that the proposed method achieves significant improvements in computational efficiency while maintaining the same accuracy as the traditional AR-MEM-based method.

title: Command shaping control of a multi-mode flexible system with time-varying parameters
abstract: A novel command shaping procedure is proposed to control a multi-mode flexible system with time-varying parameters. Unlike the traditional input shaping commands that are designed assuming constant system parameters, the present approach accommodates the changes in the system parameters during the command duration. Furthermore, the independence of the command duration from the system modeling helps in compromising between the system move time, the required reduction in the transient vibrations, and the command’s robustness to the system uncertainties. For illustration purposes, a general polynomial profile was used as a system input where its unknown coefficients were determined from prescribed system and input constraints. In addition, the continuous form of the polynomial profile renders the possibility of enhancing the command’s smoothness in order to eliminate any generated jerks, i.e., inrush currents, and reduce timing inaccuracies and delays of the actuator. The proposed approach is tested numerically and validated experimentally by effectively eliminating the residual oscillations of a multiple pendulum system with simultaneous traveling and hoisting/lowering maneuvers. Results show the effectiveness of the proposed control in eliminating the residual vibrations regardless of the rate and the interval of the hoisting/lowering operation.

title: DHFGAT: A dynamic heterogeneous fusion graph attention network for early gearbox fault detection
abstract: Accurate detection of early faults in industrial gearboxes is a critical but challenging task, particularly under dynamic operating conditions. Converting multi-sensor signals into graph-structured data via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a framework based on signal correlation modeling. However, the efficacy of this approach hinges on the quality of the graph structure, which is generally compromised by suboptimal construction methods and the inclusion of redundant features. To address these challenges, this study proposes a heterogeneous data fusion framework named Dynamic Heterogeneous Fusion Graph Attention Network (DHFGAT). Specifically, the current signal is first preprocessed to align its data morphology with the vibration signal. Then, to construct an information-rich graph structure, the Regularized Dual Averaging (RDA) algorithm adaptively selects the key feature subsets of the signal, thereby suppressing interference from redundant features. Subsequently, a training architecture that integrates the Spiking Neural Encoder (SNE) with the Simplified Graph Attention Network (SGAT) is adopted to achieve accurate and robust feature fusion and fault classification. Finally, extensive experiments were conducted on a test rig with eight fault types. The results demonstrate that DHFGAT achieves maximum average detection accuracies of 99.59% and 98.36% under constant and variable speed conditions, respectively. The proposed method provides a robust, reliable solution for early gearbox fault detection and offers insights into the optimal sensor combination for complex industrial scenarios.

title: Knowledge-guided RUL prediction for multi-sensor devices under a data-model interactive framework
abstract: For complex industrial devices monitored by multi-sensors, accurate and reliable remaining useful life (RUL) prediction directly determines the effectiveness and economy of preventive maintenance strategies. Current mainstream methods either rely excessively on data-driven models, resulting in the lack of physical interpretability, or are limited by fixed knowledge constraints, making it difficult to adapt to the dynamic characteristics of multi-sensor data. To address this, this paper proposes a knowledge-guided RUL prediction method under a data-model interactive framework. Specifically, based on the composite health indicator (CHI) constructed by weighted fusion of multi-sensor monitoring data and the RUL predicted by stochastic degradation modeling under the concepts of first hitting time (FHT), an optimization objective function integrating RUL prediction accuracy, monotonicity, and slope consistency is designed. This forms a feedback loop for knowledge-guided CHI construction and stochastic degradation modeling, enabling optimal adjustment of fusion coefficients for multi-sensor data and failure thresholds corresponding to CHI. Thus, dual optimization of the accuracy and physical rationality of prediction results is achieved. Meanwhile, a Bayesian update method for degradation model parameters is proposed to realize online RUL prediction and quantification of prediction uncertainty. Finally, the advantages of the proposed method in improving RUL prediction accuracy, interpretability, and generalization are verified based on the C-MAPSS dataset and milling cutters dataset.

title: Attention-enhanced transformer with prototype alignment for few-shot fault diagnosis under noisy cross-condition
abstract: This paper introduces a robust and adaptive few-shot learning framework for intelligent fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions and diverse noise interferences. The architecture integrates multi-scale signal encoding, adaptive condition modulation, prototype-driven alignment, and transformer-based decision modeling. To ensure noise robustness, raw sensor signals are first processed via parallel dilated depthwise separable convolutions and refined by a channel-spatial attention unit to enhance fault-relevant patterns. A context-aware modulation stage then recalibrates feature maps according to operating-condition indicators, promoting cross-condition generalization. For classification with limited labeled examples, prototype estimation is performed using a median-based reliable estimator, and query embeddings are aligned to these prototypes through a cross-domain attention-based alignment mechanism. A transformer encoder captures global interactions among aligned features and produces the final predictions. Training is guided by a composite loss combining classification, outlier, and dependency-aware terms, with a warm-up strategy to balance fitting and regularization. Evaluation on two industrial benchmarks, the Tennessee Eastman process and gold hydrometallurgy process, demonstrates that the framework consistently outperforms existing methods in noise resilience and domain adaptation.

title: Real-time monitoring of mechanical damage in lithium-ion batteries using ultrasonic guided waves and cumulative energy feature analysis
abstract: Indentation damage in lithium-ion pouch cells poses safety risks and induces hidden internal degradation. Conventional electrical monitoring (voltage, temperature, and current) typically detects anomalies only after severe structural damage occurs, providing limited warning time. In this study, an in-situ monitoring experiment is conducted to track progressive mechanical damage from an intact state to failure in lithium-ion cells subjected to quasi-static indentation. Ultrasonic guided-wave (UGW) signals, surface temperature, and terminal voltage were continuously recorded until voltage drops and temperature spikes were observed. To process the acoustic responses during loading, a monitoring method is proposed, coupling waveform decomposition, baseline subtraction, and a cumulative energy-feature (CEF) scheme with threshold-controlled integration. The cumulative shift of signal centroid (CoC) is proposed as the primary indicator to convert wavefield fluctuations into a monotonic trend, addressing the non-monotonicity of standard energy metrics and the early saturation of shape coefficients. The experimental results indicate that the CoC exhibits a monotonic relationship with damage progression and provides an early warning as early as 15 min prior to the onset of electrical/thermal abnormalities in the tested cells, outperforming voltage and temperature monitoring. Moreover, combining complementary features further improves the prediction performance, providing a quantitative approach for the early detection of mechanically induced battery faults.

title: Physics-guided multimodal neural operator for predicting point response under arbitrary impulse excitation in the medium with internal boundary
abstract: Predicting the stress wave propagation response in the medium with internal boundary has important applications in nondestructive testing. However, the existing methods focus on full-domain prediction, lack excitation generalization ability and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a stress wave propagation response calculation method based on physical a priori information, for predicting point responses in infinite medium containing internal boundaries such as holes or cracks under arbitrary excitation. Firstly, the waveform time–frequency invariant property was proved based on the fluctuation theory. This property constructed an excitation-independent operator which transforms the point response prediction into operator prediction. Then, a novel multimodal neural operator model was developed. This model integrated the internal boundary, material parameters, and excitation-reception point pairs to form a multimodal input, and cascaded the CNN, Bi-LSTM, and Self-Attention modules to achieve accurate prediction for the operators. The ablation experiments verified that the model architecture is rational. The comparison experiments demonstrated that the model’s prediction accuracy outperforms other deep learning algorithms. The case study revealed that the proposed prediction method can accurately compute the point response waveforms under arbitrary excitation and generate wavefield snapshots by multipoint parallel prediction. Combined with optimization algorithms, it can be used to achieve defect imaging. This study contributes a computational framework and algorithmic implementation for the complex medium fluctuation problem, which has excellent potential for structural health monitoring and nondestructive testing.

title: FedMAPS: A federated meta-learning framework with adaptive cross-domain contrastive learning for few-shot fault diagnosis
abstract: Intelligent industrial fault diagnosis faces significant challenges in cross-domain generalization due to domain shifts, privacy preservation constraints, and few-shot learning scenarios. Existing Federated Learning (FL) methods often fail to explicitly model cross-domain invariance and are prone to blurred feature boundaries when clients observe only partial subsets of the global class set — a scenario we term Partially Class-Disjoint Distribution (PCDD). To address these issues, a federated contrastive meta-learning method called FedMAPS is proposed, which employs adaptive contrastive learning and prototype alignment for zero-shot domain generalization in rolling bearing fault diagnosis. In the proposed method, an adaptive cross-domain contrastive learning mechanism and a prototype guidance mechanism are constructed into a computationally efficient federated meta-learning framework built upon First-Order Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (FOMAML). Specifically, the adaptive cross-domain contrastive learning mechanism, which relies on measuring distances between domains for each class, is designed to distinguish between intra-domain and cross-domain positive pairs. This mechanism enables precise feature alignment cross-domain through dynamic weight adjustment, which avoids the negative impact of domain shifts and ensures that the learned features remain consistent and effective across different scenarios. Additionally, the prototype guidance mechanism, leveraging global alignment and selective penalization of shadow classes, is proposed to stabilize decision boundaries in PCDD scenarios, which effectively improves aggregation within classes through synchronization at the prototype level. The proposed FedMAPS is evaluated using three datasets, including two public datasets and our laboratory dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that FedMAPS achieves superior diagnostic performance on unseen domains, showing clear advantages over several representative federated learning methods and maintaining strong robustness even under extreme PCDD conditions. This work offers an effective technical pathway for cross-domain few-shot fault diagnosis of rolling bearings in privacy-sensitive industrial applications.

title: Physics-guided filtering for super-elliptical anisotropic wave propagation in structural material characterization
abstract: In this work, we introduce an unsupervised, physics-guided learning framework for modeling anisotropic waves. Prior approaches have been limited to isotropic wave propagation modeled using a Helmholtz filter. We extend this framework for super-elliptical anisotropy by incorporating elements of fractional calculus to enable direction-dependent wavenumbers and mode shape deformation of the wavefield. This is formulated as a physics-guided least squares optimization in the frequency–wavenumber domain, where super-elliptical anisotropy is captured by a parametric mode filter. Variants of the super-elliptical model are discussed in-depth to retain band-pass filter behavior. We evaluate our approaches on five wavefields acquired from a laser Doppler vibrometer experimental setup: an isotropic aluminum plate, a uniaxial carbon fiber epoxy matrix, a bidirectional carbon fiber epoxy matrix composite with layups, a bidirectional woven carbon fiber epoxy matrix composite, and a bidirectional woven plastic fiber cement matrix composite. These materials are characterized by their estimated filter parameters, dispersion curves, and wavefield reconstructions. The proposed framework supports structural material characterization by estimating frequency-dependent anisotropic parameters that encode propagation directionality and geometry from individual measured wavefields through a frequency–wavenumber optimization with a physics-guided regularizer, in which the governing wave operator softly constrains the admissible anisotropy.

title: Multi-region matrix interpolation for dynamic analysis of geometrically perturbed metamaterials
abstract: This work introduces a surrogate-based model for efficiently estimating the frequency response of dynamic mechanical metamaterials, particularly when dealing with geometrically perturbed substructures undergoing mode crossing. The research builds upon a previous matrix interpolation method applied on top of a Craig–Bampton modal reduction, allowing the variations of geometrical features without the need to remesh and recompute Finite Element matrices. This existing procedure has significant limitations since it requires a common modal projection, which inherently restricts the allowable perturbation size of the model parameters, thereby limiting the model parameter space where matrices can be effectively interpolated. The present work offers three contributions: (1) It provides structural dynamic insight into the restrictions imposed by the common modal projection, demonstrating that ill-conditioning can be controlled, (2) it proposes a sampling-based procedure to identify the usable model parameter subspace for matrix interpolation, and (3) it enhances the surrogate model to accommodate mode crossing due to model parameter perturbations by proposing a multi-region interpolation strategy. The efficacy of this proposed framework is verified through two illustrative examples. The first example, involving a unit cell with a square plate and circular core, validates the approach for a single numerically stable projection region. The second example, using a beam-like structure with vibration attenuation bands, demonstrates the true advantage of the multi-region approach, where predictions from traditional Lagrange interpolation deviated significantly with increasing perturbations, while the proposed method maintained high accuracy across different perturbation levels.

title: Bridge health monitoring via drive-by sensing: A novel CNN-based framework with full-scale field validation
abstract: This study introduces a pioneering approach to bridge Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) that integrates drive-by sensing with 1D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). In one of the first known field tests that combined drive-by sensing and controlled damage of an in-service bridge, a full-scale reinforced concrete (RC) bridge in Nebraska was subjected to a series of progressive damage scenarios, with each subsequent damage state building upon the previous structural damage: healthy state (D0), saw-cutting of a parapet (D1), scour (D2), and deck damage (D3). A U-Haul truck, equipped with five strategically placed accelerometers, collected vibration data while traversing the bridge at speeds ranging from 0 to 30 mph (48 km/h), simulating real-world traffic conditions. The acquired time series from accelerometers were processed and input into a custom-designed 1D CNN model for damage detection and classification. The model demonstrated 99.9% training accuracy, 94.44% validation accuracy, and 93% testing accuracy. Detailed analysis of the confusion matrices revealed high classification precision across all damage states, with healthy (D0) and severely damaged (D3) conditions classified with over 95% accuracy, scour damage (D2) with over 92% accuracy, and parapet damage (D1) classified with slightly lower but robust performance exceeding 85%. This research represents the first successful application of 1D CNNs for damage detection of a full-scale, in-situ, bridge using drive-by sensing. These findings serve as an important step towards offering a non-intrusive, cost-effective, and scalable alternative to traditional SHM techniques. The proposed method demonstrated promising accuracy and efficiency in classifying bridge damage states, representing a significant first step toward advancing bridge health assessment practices. This approach has strong potential to enable safer and more resilient transportation infrastructure while optimizing maintenance resources.

title: Geometric algebra singular spectrum analysis: A novel multivariate signal decomposition method
abstract: In this work, we have re-modeling singular spectrum analysis within the framework of geometric algebra, resulting in a novel multivariate signal decomposition method, which we term Geometric Algebra Singular Spectrum Analysis (GA-SSA). GA-SSA innovatively embeds multivariate signals into the geometric algebra framework, representing them through multi-vectors. Based on this, the proposed method decomposes the multivariate signals into a series of fundamental components, leveraging the faithful representation of geometric algebra to uncover potential relationships between different channels. Furthermore, GA-SSA presents a transformation of these fundamental modal components into intrinsic modal components, guided by periodic pulse frequency correlation, effectively overcoming the issue of over-decomposition. It is worth noting that we provide a fast algorithm that accelerates the decomposition process by utilizing the convolution theorem. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of GA-SSA through experiments on both synthetic data and real-world multivariate datasets. In particular, we demonstrate the practicality of the method in two real-world applications: gear fault diagnosis and physiological signal separation. Experimental results confirm the superior ability of GA-SSA to separate complex multichannel signals, effectively revealing components that are otherwise challenging to isolate and identify.

title: Adaptive deterministic spectral representation method for simulating univariate and multivariate non-stationary stochastic ground motions
abstract: Efficient and accurate simulation of stochastic ground motions is fundamental for assessing the seismic performance of engineering structures. To address the challenges posed by high-dimensionality, full nonstationarity, and sampling-induced variability, this study develops an adaptive deterministic Spectral Representation Method (SRM) for simulating both univariate and multivariate non-stationary stochastic ground motions. Within this method, a key innovation is the development of a deterministic high-dimensional sampling scheme based on a Spectral Decomposition Transform (SDT), which modulates the New Generating Vector-based Number-Theoretic Method (NGV-NTM) point set in the standard normal space. The resulting SDT-NGV-NTM point set satisfies the orthogonality requirements of SRM using fewer points, making it well-suited for representing high-dimensional random inputs involved in SRM. To further improve efficiency, the analytical covariance matrix of the SDT-NGV-NTM point set is derived, enabling the proposed Maximum Correlation Constraint (MCC) strategy to adaptively determine the minimum number of representative samples required to accurately preserve both the probabilistic and spectral characteristics of stochastic ground motions, while maintaining computational efficiency. By integrating SDT-NGV-NTM and MCC strategy into the SRM framework, the proposed method achieves dimensional scalability, avoids sampling-induced variability, and adaptively balances accuracy and efficiency. Numerical examples involving simulating univariate and multivariate non-stationary stochastic ground motions demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach.

title: Research on centrifugal stiffening effect of wind turbine rotating blades based on visual monitoring data
abstract: During the operation of a wind turbine, the blades generate a centrifugal stiffening effect due to rotation, and the degree of this centrifugal stiffening is crucial for the assessment of the structural safety performance. This paper proposes a centrifugal stiffening model for wind turbine blades under different rotational speeds, and quantifies the centrifugal stiffening effect of rotating blades based on visual monitoring data. Firstly, a centrifugal stiffening model for the blades is derived by considering the loads acting on them at different rotational speeds, and a centrifugal stiffening coefficient is proposed to quantify the centrifugal stiffening effect of the blades. Secondly, the existing target-free monitoring algorithm for rotating blades is optimized by adopting the external rectangle method and the key point displacement prediction method to achieve full-field displacement monitoring of the blades. Subsequently, rotating blade tests demonstrated that the blade frequency increased quadratically and nonlinearly with the rotational speed. Moreover, the centrifugal stiffening effect was more pronounced for blades with fewer laminates or greater lengths. Finally, the reliability of the centrifugal stiffening model proposed in this paper is verified through the monitoring of the rotational condition of an actual wind turbine, and the monitored centrifugal stiffening coefficient can be used as a basis for evaluating the condition of the wind turbine.

title: A nonlinear vibration model for coupled faults in aero-engine rolling bearings and its experimental validation
abstract: To address the problems of unclear fault transmission paths and poorly understood early-stage fault-frequency formation mechanisms in aero-engine main bearings, which make monitoring difficult, this paper establishes a nonlinear dynamic model of the entire rotor-support-casing system coupled with main bearing spalling faults. The model integrates fault evolution mechanisms with nonlinear Hertzian contact forces and employs a combined implicit Newmark-β and explicit Zhai method to solve for the nonlinear dynamic responses. Validation tests conducted on a main bearing test rig and an actual aero-engine with outer ring defects show that the simulation results are in high agreement with the measured data, confirming the validity of the model. This study provides important theoretical support and technical assistance for the diagnosis of main bearing faults in aero-engines.

title: Synergistic design and control of a hybrid electromagnetic suspension to enhance output force and energy efficiency
abstract: To address the limited output force and high energy consumption of conventional electromagnetic suspensions, this paper proposes a magnetorheological hybrid electromagnetic suspension (MR-HES) that integrates a magnetorheological damper (MRD) with a permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM). A synergistic design methodology and coordinated control strategy are developed to fully exploit the advantages of the two components. The viscous damping force of the MRD is designed to provide an optimal system damping level. Based on the force–velocity quadrant principle, the magnetorheological force generated by the MRD is prioritized to reduce energy consumption. Under extreme operating conditions, it cooperates with the electromagnetic force generated by the PMLSM to overcome the force output limitation of conventional electromagnetic suspensions. To further overcome the dynamic performance limitations of existing hybrid suspension controllers, a novel layered robust control strategy is developed, which evolves from disturbance compensation to smooth multi-component force allocation. Furthermore, a multi-parameter nested optimization method is proposed to enhance controller adaptability and maximize the synergistic efficiency of the system. Experimental results obtained from a class C road test demonstrate that the proposed MR-HES system reduces the sprung mass acceleration by 27.99% compared with a passive suspension and increases the output force by 24.27% relative to a conventional electromagnetic suspension. Meanwhile, the input power and energy consumption are reduced by 46.88% and 70.13%, respectively, achieving simultaneous improvements in dynamic performance and energy efficiency.

title: Effectively recovering fault features from deconvolution filters
abstract: Accurate early fault detection in rotating machinery is critical for preventing failures and improving system reliability. To accurately detect early faults in rotating machinery, an Adaptive Frequency Band Deconvolution (AFBD) method is proposed. This method uses frequency band filtering to dynamically identify key frequency bands in the signal, avoiding the reliance on predefined pulse sequences used in traditional methods, thus ensuring more flexible and accurate analysis. Notably, AFBD does not require prior fault-frequency and pulse-train information; instead, it exploits adaptively identified key frequency-band information. The filtered signal is used to compute weight vectors, which contain the periodic information of the key signal components. AFBD utilizes this information for deconvolution, thereby customizing the process to enhance the sensitivity and specificity of fault detection. During the deconvolution process, AFBD employs a spectral sorting mechanism that organizes signal components and reconstructs those with envelope frequency domain peaks above a specified threshold, effectively eliminating low-amplitude frequency components that may mask fault features. This process helps highlight early fault characteristics. Additionally, a new quantitative fault feature extraction analysis metrics, FFE, is proposed to facilitate the quantitative analysis of fault feature extraction. Experimental analysis was conducted using simulation signals, IMS data, XJTU-SY data, and servo tool tower power head system data of CNC machine tools. The results demonstrate that AFBD can accurately detect hidden transient impact components in the signal, making it more effective for early fault detection in rolling bearings and gears.

title: Machining condition variation decoupling adversarial domain adaptation network: A multi-target domain tool wear state recognition method
abstract: Accurate tool wear monitoring (TWM) is crucial for enhancing parts quality and production efficiency. Practical metal cutting often necessitates frequent adjustments to working conditions, which introduces data distribution shifts highly correlated with the operating environment when classifying tool wear states across datasets. These lead to domain inconsistency and distribution mismatches, severely impeding multi-target domain adaptation. To overcome the above limitations, this paper proposes a novel machining condition decoupling adversarial domain adaptation network (MCDADAN) for multi-target domain tool wear condition recognition under varying working conditions. First, prototype discrepancy alignment is implemented through a weight-sharing wavelet convolutional feature extractor, which enhances the class prototypes discriminability and ensures clear representation boundaries in the feature space. Second, the adaptive domain discriminator weight is leveraged alongside extracted multi-domain discrepancies to decouple the effects of varying operation conditions. This mechanism effectively suppresses environment-correlated interference features while fully preserving intrinsic tool wear-related features. Moreover, the blended multi-domain alignment framework minimizes source domain and multiple target domains distributional differences and address mismatches encountered during the transfer process. The effectiveness of MCDADAN was validated on two milling datasets (a self-constructed GH4169 dataset and PHM2010 dataset). Experimental results demonstrate that MCDADAN generalizes effectively from a single source domain to multiple target domains, significantly outperforming conventional methods in TWM. The findings indicate its potential for supporting efficient tool replacement decisions during practical machining of difficult-to-machine materials.

title: Stability analysis of the helicopter supercritical tail drive shaft system with rub-impact and ballistic impact
abstract: Ballistic impact damage can cause dynamic instability of the supercritical tail drive shaft system, posing a threat to the helicopter’s safe flight. However, the effect mechanisms of ballistic impact parameters on the stability of the supercritical tail drive shaft system are unknown. Therefore, the stability characteristic equation of the supercritical tail drive shaft system with rub-impact and ballistic impact is established in this paper, which is verified by the dynamic equation through experimental verification, and then the effect laws of the rub-impact and the ballistic impact parameters on the system stability are evaluated. The research work in this paper conducts stability analysis for the first time by comprehensively considering mass loss, center of mass displacement, stiffness decrease, stiffness asymmetry, and rub-impact. Rub-impacts ensure the stable flight capability of the supercritical tail drive shaft system with hole or scratch damage, but the system becomes unstable after crack damage. The reasonable selection of rub-impact parameters is beneficial for improving the system stability, which provides a potential technical approach for the system stability control. This paper can provide new insights into the stability analysis of rotor systems at the theoretical level and assist helicopters in achieving high-reliability operation at the technical application level.

title: Quality-aware gated cross-modal transformer for noise-robust underwater propeller fault diagnosis
abstract: Underwater propeller fault diagnosis is crucial for marine engineering applications and autonomous underwater vehicles; however, traditional methods can degrade severely in complex underwater environments where sensor reliability is unpredictable. This paper proposes a quality-aware gated cross-modal transformer (GCM-T) for robust fault diagnosis by fusing acoustic and visual information. The core innovations include (i) a quality-aware gating mechanism that dynamically adjusts modality weights based on domain-specific quality metrics and (ii) a gated cross-attention module that mitigates contamination from low-quality inputs via quality-guided feature enhancement. Evaluation on a novel underwater propeller dataset (7 fault categories, 17 scenarios ranging from clean conditions to extreme degradation) shows that GCM-T achieves 99.4% overall accuracy, maintains 100% accuracy under clean conditions, and remains robust under severe degradations. Sea-trial validation on a real AUV platform further demonstrates the framework’s practical applicability. Compared with existing methods, GCM-T delivers consistent gains under extreme conditions, demonstrating improved adaptability. Interpretability analyses validate the quality-aware design by revealing strong correlations between the learned gate weights and the measured modality-quality gaps.

title: Editorial Board
FedSSLMfg: Federated self-supervised learning for heterogeneity-resilient and label-efficient condition monitoring in smart manufacturing
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, reliable condition monitoring increasingly relies on cross-factory collaboration. However, operational data from industrial equipment are highly sensitive, leading to data silos that hinder collaboration and limit the development of generalizable diagnostic models. While federated learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving paradigm that enables distributed factories to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data, its performance is often constrained by data heterogeneity and label scarcity. To address these two challenges, a federated self-supervised learning framework for heterogeneity-resilient and label-efficient condition monitoring in smart manufacturing, referred to as FedSSLMfg, is proposed. It involves three steps: signal preprocessing, federated self-supervised pre-training, and federated supervised fine-tuning. First, all vibration signals are unified to the same sampling frequency through anti-aliasing filtering and downsampling, and then transformed into time–frequency representations using the continuous wavelet transform. Then, feature representations are learned using a masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning scheme within a federated setting. Lastly, the learned representations are transferred to downstream tasks by fine-tuning the federated models with labeled samples. The effectiveness of FedSSLMfg is validated on a federated setting consisting of three real-world rolling bearing datasets. Experiments show that it achieves high diagnostic accuracy and strong robustness under heterogeneous data distributions and label scarcity, outperforming both federated and non-federated baselines. Ablation studies further reveal that FedSSLMfg has low dependency on data augmentation, benefits from moderate masking ratios, and maintains high accuracy even when only a small fraction of samples are labeled.

title: Development of a novel multi-mode ultrasonic vibration cutting system with free–shaped trajectory generation
abstract: Functional microstructures on material surfaces can impart superior properties, but their efficient and flexible fabrication still faces significant challenges, particularly the severely limited machining efficiency in processing complex-shaped microstructures. In this research, a novel multi-mode ultrasonic vibration cutting (MUVC) system is developed to address this challenge. The coupling of multiple vibration modes is utilized for the first time to precisely generate arbitrary two-dimensional tool trajectories in the ultrasonic frequency range. Based on theoretical analysis of vibration modes and a finite element optimization method incorporating genetic algorithms, two longitudinal vibration modes and two bending vibration modes are successfully coupled. Furthermore, the trajectory decoupling method and driving signal adaptive control strategy are proposed to achieve precise control of complex ultrasonic vibration trajectories. Ultimately, a surface topography prediction model has been established and validated through machining experiments. Utilizing resonant triangular and trapezoidal trajectories, different types of microstructures were successfully fabricated on brass material at an ultra–high rate of 42,400 units per second. The results confirm that the MUVC system offers a promising new approach for the highly efficient and highly flexible manufacturing of complex microstructures.

title: Corrigendum to “Tactile feedback in mid-air ultrasound haptics with adjustable spatial resolution” [Mech. Syst. Sig. Process. 249 (2026) 114056]
Research on an online monitoring system for tool wear status based on digital twin
abstract: Tool wear monitoring (TWM) can reduce unnecessary tool replacement and improve production efficiency. The actual TWM has the characteristics of complex cutting conditions, difficult data set construction, and poor generalization ability of the monitoring model. Therefore, this paper proposes an online monitoring system for tool wear state based on digital twin (DT). Firstly, the real-time perception of cutting state, the setting of tool and workpiece parameters, and user interaction are realized through the DT front-end, and the cutting force is calculated in real time at the DT back-end. Secondly, based on hybrid physics-data-driven models, a dual-channel input CNN-Transformer model is proposed to realize the classification of tool wear state without data samples under different cutting conditions. Thirdly, a data management method for DT is proposed, and the data processing method and the real-time performance of the digital twin monitoring system (DTMS) are explained. Based on the cloud database, the model update iteration of the DTMS is realized. Finally, the TWM accuracy of DTMS is tested. The prediction accuracy under the same cutting conditions with data samples is 90.47%, and the prediction accuracy under different cutting conditions without data samples is 85.87%, which proves that the DTMS has high accuracy and generalization ability. The application effect of “self-sensing of working conditions, self-analysis of tool wear state, and self-decision of tool change instruction” is realized, which provides a guiding ideology for the application of DT in intelligent manufacturing.

title: Enhanced mechanical motion rectifier for inertial vibration energy harvesting by the energy-accumulation-and-rapid-release strategy
abstract: Based on the Energy-Accumulation-and-Rapid-Release (EARR) strategy, an enhanced mechanical motion rectifier (E-MMR) harvester is proposed by incorporating a bistable negative-stiffness mechanism. Unlike the traditional Mechanical Motion Rectifier (MMR) harvester, in which the generator rotor speed freely decays after mechanical disengagement, the proposed E-MMR design enables sustained acceleration of the rotor following disengagement. The kinematic mechanism of the E-MMR harvester is explained by addressing the release condition of the secondary spring in the EARR design. Building on this kinematic mechanism, a dynamic model and simulation framework for the E-MMR harvester are established, elucidating its complex dynamic characteristics. Through simulation, the effects of secondary spring stiffness, installation parameters, and excitation intensity on the performance improvement over the traditional MMR are analyzed. Simulation results from time‑domain responses, Poincaré sections, and frequency‑domain analysis demonstrate that the frequency reallocation of absorbed energy within the system serves as the key mechanism through which the EARR strategy enhances harvesting efficiency. The balance between the energy storage capacity of the secondary spring and the excitation intensity is identified as the key to improving the output performance of the harvester. Experimental analysis is performed to evaluate the influence of impedance and excitation intensity on output performance. Experimental results demonstrate that under an excitation of 2 Hz and 0.01 m amplitude, the E-MMR harvester achieves up to a 50% enhancement in output performance compared to the traditional MMR harvester, while exhibiting significantly reduced sensitivity to variations in load impedance.

title: KSOPKS-SJDM: Signal mechanism-based temporal feature spectrum and sparse joint denoising for debris induced voltage detection
abstract: Inductive sensors represent an important branch of debris detection and exhibits superior performance in harsh environments characterized by low oil cleanliness, intense acoustic interference, and other disturbances. However, its output induced voltages are often submerged in strong background interference, which impairs the accurate identification of mechanical wear conditions. The enhancement of weak debris signals without distorting their local features remains a critical challenge in practical engineering applications. In this article, a signal mechanism-based temporal feature spectrum and sparse joint denoising method is proposed. First, a simplified signal model of the three-coil inductive debris sensor is constructed to provide an intuitive theoretical foundation. Subsequently, a kernel scale-oriented point kurtosis spectrum (KSOPKS) integrated with an optimal wavelet kernel function is presented to enhance the perception of weak debris signatures under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Meanwhile, an adaptively parameterized sparse joint denoising model (SJDM) is established to effectively suppress interference components in the KSOPKS, which is solved using a simple yet reliable optimization algorithm. Finally, an innovative adaptive low-destructive denoising scheme is developed for debris induced voltage signals. In simulation studies, the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed KSOPKS and SJDM are rigorously validated. At the same time, Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that the proposed denoising method yields recall rates of 100% and 89.03% for debris signals under −10 dB and −25 dB, respectively, and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in false recall, feature preservation, and SNR improvement. On 12 groups of experimental signals ranging from 78μm to 250μm, the proposed method achieves an average recall rate of 100% and a false recall rate of 3.33% without additional identification algorithm, illustrating significant advantages in denoising performance, reliability and practicality.

title: Sparse stability diagrams of LSCF method via strategic pole destabilization using orthogonal matching pursuit
abstract: In various engineering fields including mechanical, aerospace, and civil engineering, the identification of modal parameters—natural frequencies, damping ratios, and mode shapes—is crucial for determining the vibration characteristics of engineered structures. A common method for identifying the modal parameters of structures involves experimental modal analysis using frequency response functions (FRFs) obtained from forced vibration tests. The least squares complex frequency (LSCF) domain method is a widely-used frequency-domain curve-fitting method for the FRFs using the polynomials of high order, which can extract modal parameters with high accuracy. However, increasing the polynomial order tends to result in the generation of non-physical spurious poles that need to be eliminated from the stability diagrams. To overcome this issue, we propose a method that strategically destabilizes the stable yet spurious poles of the characteristic polynomials by making their coefficients as sparse as possible, via orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP). This results in sparse stability diagrams because unstable poles can be eliminated from the diagrams. In this paper, the proposed method is first applied to numerically-obtained FRFs of a rectangular plate using finite element model, and its validity is discussed. Then, the method is applied to experimentally-obtained FRFs of rectangular plates with low-damping and with high-damping. Furthermore, to confirm its applicability to industrial applications with realistic complexity, it has also been applied to the FRFs of the electric machine’s stator core used for electric vehicles. Based on the results, we have confirmed that the spurious roots can be eliminated from the stability diagrams without compromising accuracy for the cases considered. • A novel curve-fitting method that achieves sparse stability diagrams is proposed. • The orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) is used to destabilize the poles. • The method is tested on a numerical and three experimental examples. • Sparse stability diagrams are obtained without degrading the solution accuracy.

title: Fixed-time swing suppression for ship-to-ship cranes: an adaptive tracking strategy with online disturbance estimation
abstract: Ship-to-ship payload transportation using marine cranes is a highly challenging operation, characterized by pronounced payload swing and uncertain relative motions induced by ocean waves. To achieve rapid swing suppression and precise positioning under these unmodeled disturbances, this paper proposes an adaptive fixed-time tracking control strategy. Firstly, a coordinated fused non-inertial coordinate system is established to accurately capture the relative dynamics between the vessels. Subsequently, a backstepping-based controller is developed to ensure the system states converge within a fixed time, independent of initial conditions. Crucially, an adaptive updating law is designed for the online estimation and compensation of the upper bound of unknown disturbances. Theoretical analysis rigorously guarantees that the tracking errors and swing angles converge to a sufficiently small neighborhood. Finally, comparative experiments conducted on a hardware platform demonstrate the superiority of the proposed strategy, achieving up to 76.78% reduction in steady-state tracking error compared with traditional methods, which validates its effectiveness and robustness in suppressing payload swing under complex marine environments.

title: Online Adaptive Reinforcement Learning and Approximate Bayesian Computation (OARL-ABC) for real-time long-term calibration of rotordynamic models
abstract: Efficient, timely and accurate calibration of digital twins is critical for their application in real-time decision-making and condition monitoring. Digital twins, as dynamic virtual representations of connected physical systems, require continuous recalibration to adapt to evolving system states, environmental changes, and degradation over time. Without timely and effective recalibration, discrepancies between the digital and physical counterparts accumulate, potentially leading to compromised safety and operational inefficiencies. This study addresses these challenges by introducing the Online Adaptive Reinforcement Learning and Approximate Bayesian Computation (OARL-ABC) framework, a novel and model-agnostic calibration algorithm. Building upon the foundational RL-ABC framework, OARL-ABC offers enhanced adaptability, scalability, and robustness, facilitating real-time adjustment of model parameters across diverse systems. By integrating reinforcement learning strategies with approximate Bayesian computation, the proposed framework effectively accounts for uncertainties in model parameters and environmental variables, ensuring reliable predictions in complex and dynamic scenarios. To validate its efficacy, the OARL-ABC framework is applied to the calibration of a rotordynamic system for rotating machine fault diagnosis, demonstrating its capability to maintain alignment between the digital and physical domains in real-time. However, while the results demonstrate improved real-time calibration performance in this context compared to conventional calibration methods, OARL-ABC remains limited by its use of sampling techniques for repeated full-scale model runs. Further improvement should prioritize applying the method to a broader range of use cases, exploring simplified model forms, or enhancing the sampling scheme to run more efficiently.

title: Universal domain adaptation with adaptive dual-confidence bounds for rotating machinery fault diagnosis
abstract: In rotating machinery fault diagnosis, universal domain adaptation (UniDA) enables knowledge transfer across multiple operating conditions, even when the target domain contains unknown fault types. However, unknown fault detection and domain-invariant feature extraction remain difficult due to missing class references and large distribution shifts across conditions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a UniDA method based on decoupled mixture-of-experts and adaptive dual-confidence bounds (DMoE-ADCB), which integrates feature decoupling, adaptive confidence modeling, and confidence-aware domain alignment for fault diagnosis. First, the decoupled mixture-of-experts module splits the feature space into two parallel experts, guided by a covariance loss to promote feature decorrelation. Their outputs will support accurate known-class prediction and dual-confidence modeling. Then, an adaptive dual-confidence bounds module derives the confidence regions using a dual-confidence constraint loss, improving domain-invariant feature learning and the separation of unknown classes. Furthermore, a confidence-aware maximum mean discrepancy loss aligns source and target distributions only within high-confidence shared class regions. Extensive experiments on two rotating machinery datasets validate the effectiveness and robustness of DMoE-ADCB in achieving universal fault recognition and superior cross-domain adaptation.

title: A physical knowledge-informed bearing fault feature extraction network based on Mamba
abstract: In contrast to signal processing methods that depend extensively on significant domain expertise, deep learning offers end-to-end feature self-learning capabilities, thereby providing a promising option for rolling bearing fault diagnosis. However, supervised learning paradigms that rely on categorical labels predominantly capture class-discriminative features, potentially resulting in the omission of essential fault-specific information within the feature space and diminishing the interpretability of the model. Therefore, this paper proposes an interpretable weak fault feature extraction framework, named Mamba-FeNet, which integrates Mamba’s exceptional sequence modeling strengths with physical prior knowledge of bearing fault. Firstly, a modal information estimation algorithm based on the marginal spectrum is introduced to extract potential resonance parameters from the frequency domain. This algorithm guides the resonance frequency settings in the simulation model and generates fault template signals based on prior physical knowledge. Secondly, the Mamba-FeNet is designed to model the vibration signals using selective state space, achieving end-to-end extraction of fault features under the encode-mask-decode paradigm. Thirdly, fault impact template signals are combined with normal signals scaled randomly in amplitude to form mixed signals for training the Mamba-FeNet, and a multi-model information weighted fusion strategy is designed based on the Envelope Spectrum Kurtosis (ESK). Finally, an interpretable analysis visualizes Mamba-FeNet’s internal structure and variables to intuitively demonstrate the fault feature extraction process. The proposed method is validated through simulations and experimental signals, showing superior performance compared to several advanced signal processing methods and deep learning methods.

title: Three-state switching magnetostrictive energy harvester featuring a non-conductive state
abstract: Infrastructure systems are frequently subjected to vibrations from a variety of sources. Harnessing these vibrations for energy generation has been the focus of extensive research in vibration energy harvesting (VEH), which converts vibration into electrical energy. Magnetostrictive materials have garnered significant interest in VEH applications owing to their superior resistance to shock and heat. For efficient electrical energy generation, semi-active energy harvesting techniques utilizing magnetostrictive materials have been proposed. These methods employ electronic switches to dynamically alter circuit configurations in response to varying vibration conditions. However, conventional semi-active energy harvesting approaches often suffer from continuous current flow within the circuit, which can suppress vibrations and consequently reduce the amount of harvested energy. To overcome this limitation, this study introduces a novel semi-active harvesting method using magnetostrictive materials. The proposed approach incorporates a circuit capable of temporarily interrupting current flow through the use of electronic switches. Furthermore, a novel switch control strategy is developed that operates independently of the current. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulations and experiments. Simulations are conducted to analyze circuit behavior and evaluate the impact of parameter variations. Experimental results validated that the proposed method achieved higher energy output compared with conventional techniques under both single-mode and multi-mode structural vibrations.

title: Coaxial face-gear power-split and power-combining transmission: rigid-flexible coupled dynamics and SVD-Kalman inverse meshing force identification
abstract: Focusing on dynamic meshing force identification at the power-combining stage and system-level coupling assessment of a coaxial face-gear power-split and power-combining transmission, this study conducts a comprehensive investigation including tooth-surface contact analysis, rigid-flexible coupled system dynamics with a discretized shaft-line, synchronous torque–speed experiments, and model-driven inverse identification of the combining-stage meshing force. First, based on established meshing theory, discretized contact representation of face-gear tooth surfaces is employed, and load-dependent meshing stiffness is derived using Hertzian contact theory. Second, a system-level dynamic framework integrating meshing interactions and a discretized output shaft is formulated to analyze vibration transmission and nodal coupling mechanisms in the multi-component drivetrain. Third, acceleration, torque, and speed responses are measured under various operating conditions, and a model-driven SVD-Kalman filtering scheme is implemented to reconstruct the dynamic meshing force at the power-combining stage from acceleration signals. Results show that the predicted acceleration spectra reproduce the dominant gear meshing frequency (GMF) and its harmonics observed experimentally, while the inversely identified meshing force remains physically consistent with measured dynamic responses. Furthermore, improved load sharing and enhanced synchronization are observed at higher rotational speeds. These findings provide theoretical and experimental insight into dynamic load distribution and coupling mechanisms in complex multi-branch transmissions.
keywords: Coaxial face-gear power-split and power-combining transmission

title: Analysis, optimization, and feature reduction in neural network models for quasi-static prediction in systems exhibiting Bouc-Wen hysteresis
abstract: This article addresses quasi-static torque prediction in systems with Bouc–Wen hysteresis, illustrated using a Vacuum Packed Particles Torsional Damper (VPPTD). A modified Bouc–Wen model (augmented with additional dry-friction and nonlinear stiffness components) was employed, with its parameters generalized as functions of chamber vacuum. The study was conducted on a dataset containing n=399,200 samples generated for multiple vacuum and material configurations. Five neural network architectures were compared, including a single-output model and multi-output variants predicting intermediate Bouc–Wen variables before estimating the torque M. Two input-reduction strategies were investigated: (S1) only physical parameters of the model, and (S2) a minimal control set (p,ABS) extended with selected intermediate signals. Feature selection was based on repeated-measures correlation (rmcorr), block-permutation clustering, and SHAP analysis; hyperparameter tuning was performed with Hyperopt. The highest accuracy was obtained for S2: the multi-output architecture with skip-connections achieved MAE(M)=0.043Nm (≈0.18%σM) for the full set of intermediates (INVI), while with only four inputs {φ,sign(φ̇),p,ABS} (INIVb) it maintained MAE(M)=0.051Nm (≈0.21%σM). Excluding dynamic signals (S1) increased the error to 0.38–0.61Nm (≈1.6–2.5%σM). Robustness tests (Gaussian noise, sign reversal of sign(φ̇), feature occlusion, repeated data splits) confirmed the greater stability of configuration INVI and the key role of φ and the correct sign of φ̇. A comparison with classical regressors (kNN, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) indicated that although sometimes competitive under noise, they failed to provide consistent estimation of intermediate variables. The recommended solution is a multi-output architecture with skip-connections; in applications with limited sensor availability, a four-input configuration can be employed, with a conscious trade-off in robustness.

title: Accumulated subband Wiener filter algorithm for active road noise control
abstract: Active noise control (ANC) systems for vehicle road noise often require multiple reference sensors to achieve effective noise reduction, leading to high computational complexity. Conventional adaptive algorithms, such as filtered-x normalized least mean squares (FxNLMS) and delayless subband adaptive filtering, frequently suffer from slow convergence and performance degradation due to eigenvalue spreading and reference signal coupling. To address these challenges, we introduce a combination of the delayless subband structure with the Wiener solution to tackle the road noise reduction problem. A finite impulse response (FIR)-based fullband filter reconstruction method is developed, forming the basis of the accumulated subband Wiener filter (ASWF) algorithm, which incorporates enhancements to mitigate numerical instability in both the stopband and transition band. The ASWF algorithm leverages Wiener filter properties to improve convergence and uses a delayless subband structure to reduce computational complexity, facilitating real-time ANC implementation. Simulations using real-world high-speed road noise data demonstrate that ASWF outperforms conventional delayless subband adaptive algorithms in terms of convergence speed and computational efficiency. These results demonstrate the potential of ASWF for practical implementation in advanced ANC systems, offering an effective and potentially scalable solution for road noise control.

title: Low-frequency human motion energy harvesting with a tumbler-inspired triboelectric nanogenerator
abstract: Harvesting human body motion energy to power wearable devices instead of chemical batteries offers an alternative approach, however, high-efficient low-frequency (< 5 Hz) energy harvesting still remains a challenge. Here we propose a tumbler-inspired triboelectric nanogenerator (T-TENG) consisting of a tumbler, an electromechanical conversion structure, and an adjustment mechanism, where the electromechanical conversion structure is positioned above the tumbler to enable effective conversion of irregular human motion energy into electricity. A theoretical model of T-TENG is established and the low-frequency energy harvesting characteristics are evaluated numerically and experimentally. T-TENG possesses considerable energy harvesting performance around 4 Hz, and can successfully light up 102 LEDs under 0.3 g excitation and charge a 0.47 μF capacitor to 0.37 V in 65 s. Furthermore, the peak voltage of the T-TENG can reach 19.6 V at a speed of 12 km/h and the maximum power density is 37.86 W/m³ during human motion test. The work provides a guideline for the design of compact, lightweight, high-efficiency and low-frequency wearable and portable triboelectric nanogenerators.

title: Physically Knowledge Anchored Kolmogorov-Arnold Classifier Network for Continual Fault Diagnosis under Class-Imbalanced Scenarios
abstract: Current mainstream continual diagnosis models predominantly rely on linear classifiers, which exhibit notable deficiencies in sustaining a stable classification space during the incremental learning of novel tasks. Additionally, traditional replay strategies tend to cause data distribution imbalance, interfering with the learning of new tasks and limiting the mitigation of catastrophic forgetting. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Physics-Knowledge-Anchored Kolmogorov-Arnold Classifier Network (PKAKACNet), whose core consists of three components: 1) A Physics-Knowledge-Anchored Kolmogorov-Arnold Classifier (PKAKAC) is proposed — a novel classifier embedded with physical knowledge and specifically tailored for continual diagnosis scenarios — to solve the unstable classification space problem of linear classifiers; 2) A physics-knowledge-guided two-stage selection strategy for replay samples (PKTSSRS) is designed to complement PKAKAC. By combining prediction confidence and similarity preservation, dynamic sample replay is realized, avoiding the interference of traditional replay samples on new task learning; 3) To tackle the data distribution imbalance of new tasks caused by replay, a feature- retention loss function is proposed to construct an old knowledge retention mechanism at the feature level, further enhancing the anti-forgetting ability of PKAKAC. The performance of our proposed method is rigorously validated by conducting continual diagnosis experiments, ablation studies, and parameter sensitivity tests in sequence.

title: Hybrid stepwise topology optimization for versatile bandgap design in single-phase elastic metamaterials
abstract: Elastic metamaterials offer extraordinary wave manipulation capabilities, yet efficiently navigating the vast design space for bandgap optimization remains challenging. Here, we propose a hybrid stepwise topology optimization framework synergizing global exploration via a real-coded genetic algorithm with local refinement via floating projection topology optimization, enabling efficient bandgap engineering of single-phase elastic metamaterials while preserving solution diversity and ensuring manufacturable topologies. Optimized unit-cell designs with targeted-order bandgaps are obtained, with formation mechanisms elucidated through eigenmode analysis and complex dispersion calculations, revealing the interplay between Bragg scattering and local resonance effects. The optimized designs support directional wave propagation, defect-induced localization, and topologically protected edge and corner states, demonstrating broad multi-modal wave control capability. Numerical simulations and experimental measurements confirm selective wave transmission and attenuation at targeted frequencies in excellent agreement with predicted band structures, establishing a generalizable route for inverse design of elastic metamaterials with applications in vibration isolation, energy harvesting, and acoustic sensing.

title: Koopman operator-based end-to-end learning for posture-dependent FRFs prediction in robotic systems
abstract: The accurate prediction of posture-dependent frequency response functions (FRFs) is critical for chatter suppression in robotic machining. However, current mode-parameter-based prediction methods suffer from two fundamental limitations rooted in their formulation: (1) the fixed-dimensional parameter output cannot adapt to posture-dependent variations in dominant mode counts, and (2) the reliance on local interpolation in configuration space leads to poor extrapolation performance. To overcome these challenges, we propose the Multi-dimensional Koopman Neural Operator (MKNO) — an end-to-end framework that directly learns the functional mapping between FRFs without requiring explicit mode count specification. The key theoretical innovation lies in extending the operator theory from univariate to multivariate cases by introducing exponential coordinate embeddings that linearize the FRF manifold and exchangeable operator hypotheses that ensure path-independent predictions. Experiments on a disconnected virtual benchmark and a real-world 6-DOF industrial robot show that MKNO achieves stronger interpolation performance and more favorable extrapolation behavior than both traditional baselines and representative operator-learning methods under the evaluated settings. For the measured dataset, the conclusions are explicitly limited to local-region validation within the tested operating range.

title: Improved and automatic frequency domain decomposition for output-only modal identification with closely spaced modes by joint approximate diagonalization and resonant frequency band selection
abstract: Frequency domain decomposition (FDD) has been widely used in operational modal analysis due to the simplicity and intuitiveness in identifying modes at the spectrum peaks and the efficiency in dealing with large number of sensor data. However, it is difficult to separate closely spaced modes and requires manual peak selection to avoid spurious noise-induced peaks, which prevent the FDD to be well applied in real-time modal identification for long-term structural monitoring. To address these difficulties, an improved and automatic FDD is proposed to accurately identify closely spaced modes and enable automated modal identification. The key ingredients of the method are mainly two-fold. On the one hand, the joint approximate diagonalization (JAD) of power spectral density (PSD) matrices in the resonant frequency band is innovatively introduced to improve the identification accuracy of closely spaced mode shapes and then, the natural frequencies and damping ratios are obtained by simple least-squares regression; this also avoids subjective errors in selecting frequency peaks. On the other hand, to render fully automatic identification, the number of closely spaced modes is determined by the singular values of the PSD matrix at a resonant peak and then, the resonant frequency band is automatically selected through a generalized modal assurance criterion. Numerical, laboratory and field tests are conducted to demonstrate the improved accuracy of the JAD-FDD method in separating closely spaced modes as well as the remarkable effectiveness and efficiency in realizing automatic frequency-domain modal identification.

title: GraphDARTS: Contrastive graph metric learning for unsupervised differentiable architecture search in Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) requires unsupervised pattern recognition for damage detection when labeled data is unavailable. While Differentiable Architecture Search (DARTS) excels in supervised settings, its application to unsupervised SHM remains unexplored. Existing methods focus on similarity-based clustering while neglecting dissimilarity constraints, leading to suboptimal separation in acoustic emission (AE) feature spaces. This work addresses: (1) the architectural bias problem in fixed topology networks; (2) the scalability bottleneck in graph-based similarity computation that fails to encode both similarity and dissimilarity relationships. We introduce GraphDARTS, a novel framework that extends DARTS to unsupervised acoustic emission signal analysis in SHM applications through dual graph construction and contrastive metric learning. Our approach makes three methodological contributions: Single-level unsupervised optimization in which we reformulate the traditional bilevel DARTS procedure into a unified contrastive graph metric learning objective that simultaneously optimizes MLP architectures and embedding representations; Dual graph metric learning where we construct complementary similarity and dissimilarity graphs in which similarity matrices derive from low-rank spectral decomposition of Gram matrices while dissimilarity matrices employ uniform baseline encoding; Dual-criterion cluster validation where the Silhouette coefficient drives unsupervised cluster selection, while recall serves as a post-hoc evaluation metric within the ORION-AE benchmark protocol, resolving ambiguities that arise with traditional single-metric approaches. The core algorithmic contribution uses LogDet relaxation for rank optimization through contrastive graph Laplacians encoding clustering and separation constraints. The search space includes MLPs (8-2048 neurons, varied activations/dropout), with embeddings processed via Time Series K-Means to capture temporal AE dependencies, enabling unsupervised architecture discovery for damage recognition. GraphDARTS achieves perfect recall (precision: 0.188-0.833, ARI: 0.823-0.969) across five ORION-AE campaigns, outperforming baseline methods and correctly identifying all damage classes. The code is available at https://github.com/OualidLai/GraphDARTS.

title: Deep generative models in condition and structural health monitoring: Opportunities, limitations and future outlook
abstract: Condition and structural health monitoring (CM/SHM) is a pivotal component of predictive maintenance (PdM) strategies across diverse industrial sectors, including mechanical rotating machinery, aircraft structures, wind turbines, and civil infrastructures. Conventional deep learning models, while effective for fault diagnosis and anomaly detection through automatic feature learning from sensor data, often struggle with operational variability, imbalanced or scarce fault datasets, and multimodal sensory data from complex systems. Deep generative models (DGMs) including deep autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, diffusion-based models, and emerging large language models, offer transformative capabilities by synthesizing high-fidelity data samples, reconstructing latent system states, and modeling complex multimodal data streams.
