This review systematically examines state-of-the-art DGM applications in CM/SHM across the four main industrial systems mentioned above, emphasizing their roles in addressing key challenges: data generation, domain adaptation and generalization, multimodal data fusion, and downstream fault diagnosis and anomaly detection tasks, with rigorous comparison among signal processing, conventional machine learning or deep learning models, and DGMs. Lastly, we discuss current limitations of DGMs, including challenges of explainable and trustworthy models, computational inefficiencies for edge deployment, and the need for parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies. Future research directions can focus on zero-shot and few-shot learning, robust multimodal data generation, hybrid architectures integrating DGMs with physics knowledge, and reinforcement learning with DGMs to enhance robustness and accuracy in industrial scenarios.

title: A rapid ultra-micro internal leakage detection method based on digital twins for hydraulic cylinders of hydro turbine speed control system
abstract: Rapid and precise detection of ultra-micro internal leakage in hydraulic cylinders within hydro turbine speed control systems (HTSCS) is critical for ensuring the stable operation of power generation unit. The pressure decay test (PDT) method provides an efficient inspection approach for acceptance test and periodic offline maintenance of hydraulic cylinders. However, the poor stability of the pressure decay threshold limits the practicality and effectiveness of the PDT method. To address these issues, this paper proposes a research framework for rapid ultra-micro internal leakage detection of hydraulic cylinders of HTSCS based on digital twin (DT). First, a surrogate model between unknown parameters in the hydraulic test system and simulation-experiment errors was constructed. Combining the multi-objective artificial hummingbird algorithm (MOAHA) with the technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) enabled the estimation of optimal parameter combinations. Second, a novel two-dimensional signal warping (2DSW) optimization algorithm is introduced to reconstruct simulation data and generate highly reliable DT data. Finally, a multi-stage data processing scheme based on simulation, experimental, and DT data is designed, systematically validating the proposed method’s effectiveness. Experimental results demonstrate that DT data significantly enhance the linear relationship between the pressure decay rate and the ultra-micro internal leakage rate. Under high-pressure conditions, the standard deviation and coefficient of variation of the pressure decay threshold indicator in the PDT method decreased by 67.46% and 77.29%, respectively, with significantly improved stability. This research framework establishes a systematic solution integrating a mechanism, data, and decision-making for the stable operation of HTSCS.

title: Linearised modelling and nonlinear dynamic properties of bolted assemblies with machined surfaces
abstract: Real-life structures contain numerous bolted joints, and their contact surfaces are often patterned due to machining. A procedure to build linearised model of bolted assemblies with milled surfaces under various orientations is proposed, and the degree of nonlinear behaviour of bolted joints with various surfaces are sought experimentally. In the linearised model, the contact area and contact stiffness are determined with digital image processing methods and mesoscopic finite element analysis, respectively. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed procedure limits the natural frequency error to within 2.5%, whereas the fixed-connection assumption and the traditional pressure cone-based contact area estimation would lead to errors up to 7%. Experimental results further show that assemblies with ground contact surfaces give higher natural frequencies, higher damping ratio and higher nonlinear effects compared with the milled counterpart.

title: On the use of Gaussian Process Regression of transmissibility functions for loosening detection in bolted structures under excitation level variations
abstract: Bolted joints are widely used in industrial structures, but they require regular inspections to prevent failures such as bolt loosening. Conventional inspections are costly and time-consuming, as they involve manual checks and downtime. Therefore, indirect detection of loosening is a major challenge, further complicated by variability and nonlinear effects. This paper proposes a damage detection approach that avoids feature extraction by using the raw frequency response signal. A Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model is directly trained on transmissibility functions to build a baseline model in the frequency domain. A GPR-based damage index is then formulated to detect outliers relative to this baseline. To improve sensitivity, a Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA) with Sobol’s indices is applied as a feature selection method, identifying frequency ranges most affected by loosening. The paper also extends the GPR-based model to a three-dimensional formulation that captures the evolution of nonlinear behavior as input levels increase. In this way, the GPR-based damage index can distinguish different motion regimes and separate changes caused by nonlinear regime transitions from those caused by loosening. In summary, with proper feature selection, the proposed probabilistic frameworks reliably detect bolt loosening while minimizing false diagnoses in a clear way. • Efficient monitoring methods for bolted joints are required to reduce reliance on costly manual inspections. • Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) is trained directly on transmissibility functions, thereby eliminating the need for feature extraction. • A GPR-based damage index identifies loosening by detecting outliers relative to a healthy baseline. • Sobol-based GSA identifies frequency ranges most sensitive to loosening. • 3D GPR captures nonlinear effects, improving sensitivity and reducing false alarms.

title: Research on the mechanism of the impact of measurement positions on distributed dynamic load identification
abstract: In distributed dynamic load identification, loads are inferred from the response-load relationship based on measurements taken at multiple positions. Therefore, the selection of measurement positions is crucial. This work investigates the impact of measurement positions on identification results, assuming a fixed number of measurement positions, and proposes an optimization method aimed at improving identification stability. Two key challenges are addressed in this context. The first is that measurement positions act as a hyperparameter in the response-load relationship, making it difficult to directly assess their influence on the identification results. The second challenge is the need to consider the effect of measurement positions across different identification methods. This work provides solutions to both issues. To tackle the first challenge, it is demonstrated for the first time that, in methods based on generalized orthogonal base functions, the effects of measurement positions and the choice of base functions on identification results are independent. Regarding the second challenge, it is shown that any valid identification method is an approximation of the correct response-load relationship, meaning that it suffices to study the impact of measurement positions in a single method. Based on these findings, an optimization method for measurement positions is proposed to enhance identification stability. Fast optimization methods for one-dimensional structures and more general optimization methods for complex structures are proposed. Experimental results demonstrate that optimizing measurement positions reduces identification errors by 20.5%, significantly improving stability.

title: Tuning mechanical parameters by four-quadrant converter for orbit jump in nonlinear vibration energy harvesters
abstract: Nonlinear vibration energy harvesters (NVEH) introduce nonlinear restoring forces to achieve a wider power-frequency bandwidth. However, NVEHs may have multiple stable operation orbits. If they happen to work in a low-energy orbit, the output power will be greatly reduced. To force the operation orbit jump to the highest-energy one, mechanical parameters of the NVEH need to be tuned. However, the reliance on external actuators in traditional methods results in high power consumption and low reliability. Some other approaches that employ electromagnetic force to tune mechanical parameters suffer from weak robustness. This paper proposes a universal mechanical-parameter tuning mechanism via a dual-function four-quadrant converter, eliminating the need for additional dedicated circuitry. To improve the robustness in orbit jump, a jump strategy with multiple smooth tuning steps is further proposed. Finally, a self-contained mono-stable NVEH module with both energy harvesting and orbit jumping capabilities is built. The experiment result shows orbit jump is successfully achieved across the entire hysteresis frequency band. The output power increases to 82 times that of the original low-energy orbit, while the overall energy harvesting efficiency reaches 81.1%, under vibration acceleration of 53.3 Hz and 3 m/s2. The acceptable range of parameter variations for orbit jumping reaches 23%, which demonstrates that the proposed orbit jumping mechanism exhibits strong robustness.

title: Sparse identification of blocked forces using a global-residual interface representation
abstract: Choosing an appropriate interface representation is a crucial step when identifying forces by inverse methods. A preferred interface representation should be interpretable, but also well conditioned and able to recover forces with low error. Currently, the most widely adopted representation is that of the Virtual Point (VP), a local projection of measured degrees of freedom (DoFs) onto a set of co-located rigid-interface modes. Though easily interpretable, poor conditioning/large errors are often obtained at low frequencies when the source dynamics are dominated by global rigid body motions; a result of over-parametrising the interface model. In this paper we explore a reformulation of the VP representation by separating the global and residual components of the interface dynamics; global dynamics are filtered out of the local interface motions and projected onto their own global VP, the remaining residual interface motions are projected onto a set of local VPs. The result is an interpretable interface representation that provides a clear separation of the local and global source dynamics. Its application is demonstrated on a heavy weight stamping press under rigid and resilient boundary conditions. Results suggest that the proposed Global Residual Virtual Point (GR-VP) performs on par with the standard VP, with notable improvements in the low and high frequency range. We further investigate the application of the GR-VP in conjunction with best subset DoF selection. It is shown that compared to the standard VP, the GR-VP can provide a more robust interface representation when comparing blocked forces obtained from rigid and resilient installations.

title: Probabilistic vibration-based weight-in-motion solution for ballasted tracks of railway networks
abstract: Exceeding permissible axle loads and uneven load distribution between axles are critical safety and maintenance concerns for railway networks. Most existing weigh-in-motion (WIM) systems rely on rail deformation measurements. This paper proposes a vibration-based WIM method for ballasted tracks, in which the acceleration time history measured at the midspan between two sleepers is used to estimate train speed and axle loads. A probabilistic, mechanics-based framework is developed to interpret rail vibration measurements. An approximate closed-form expression is derived to predict rail acceleration at the forcing frequency. Its predictive accuracy is improved by adding a probabilistic correction term, calibrated through a Bayesian approach using results from Monte Carlo simulations. These simulations model the dynamic response of the train–track–ballast system, with input parameters randomly sampled within realistic ranges. The vehicle is represented as a two-degree-of-freedom vertical–pitching system, and the track is modelled with discrete sleeper supports. The framework is validated against experimental measurements on a ballasted track section. The proposed method provides a fast and practical procedure for estimating both the mean value and uncertainty of axle loads, given axle spacing, sleeper spacing, rail properties, and the measured peak acceleration at the forcing frequency.

title: Enhancing hybrid dynamic substructuring: A comprehensive review of numerical and experimental techniques
abstract: Analyzing complex dynamic systems with intricate joints and interfaces presents significant challenges due to modeling uncertainties and computational complexity. Current methods often lack a unified framework for integrating numerical and experimental approaches, leading to inaccuracies in system characterization. Hybrid dynamic substructuring techniques, which combine numerical simulations with experimental data, offer a promising solution by leveraging the strengths of both domains. Motivated by the need to bridge existing gaps in the literature for the application of hybrid modeling, this paper provides a comprehensive review of linear projection-based model order reduction techniques. It introduces a novel unified classification that covers key areas, including condensation formulations for model order reduction, modeling of complex interfaces, selection of suitable modes for reduction matrices, and exploration of different assembly options for subsystems, all within a single framework. Special emphasis is placed on component mode synthesis and frequency-based substructuring due to their relevance in industrial applications and suitability for hybrid models. Consequently, theoretical foundations are linked with practical implementation to facilitate method selection. Additionally, this work provides structured guidelines that clarify methodological similarities and differences, enabling efficient hybrid modeling of complex structural systems. The paper also identifies current limitations and highlights areas for future research. This unified perspective advances understanding and practical use of hybrid dynamic substructuring, supporting improved prediction quality and computational efficiency in structural dynamics, with applications in mechanical engineering. This article is particularly well-suited for newcomers to the field, offering a comprehensive overview of various dynamic substructuring concepts.

title: Performance enhancement of swing-type electromagnetic energy harvesters through synchronization ratio of coupling factors
abstract: In this paper, we introduce and rigorously analyze the synchronization ratio (SR) of the electromechanical coupling factor—a novel figure-of-merit designed to optimize the energy harvesting performance of swing-type electromagnetic energy harvesters (S-EMEHs). While prior research has focused extensively on maximizing magnetic flux density through complex magnet arrangements, the geometric coherence between multi-coil arrays and magnetic poles has remained an under-explored domain. The SR is defined as the quotient of the actual series-connected coupling factors among multiple coils to the theoretical optimum achievable in S-EMEHs. Illustrated with theoretical analysis, numerical simulations and experimental demonstrations, we show that the harvested power is not necessarily maximal at a suboptimal synchronization ratio even if the vibrational energy is large. Our theoretical framework reveals that the SR is governed by the geometric relationship between the coil separation angle and the magnet separation angle. Based on the theoretical analysis, we prove the optimal angle-separation ratio is approximately 1, 1 and 2 for the alternating-pole, uniformly distributed pole and Halbach magnetic arrangements, respectively. Experimental results from a fabricated S-EMEH prototype corroborate the theoretical model, demonstrating that optimizing the SR amplifies the maximal output voltage by a factor of 2.85 compared to non-optimized configurations. Theoretical tools and findings in this paper can serve as a guideline for the design and optimization of S-EMEHs and EMEHs of any types.

title: Active low-frequency chatter control in robotic milling
abstract: Industrial robots have the potential to replace machine tools and improve the efficiency of machining large parts. However, low-frequency chatter often occurs during robotic milling, significantly reducing machining efficiency and undermining process advantages. In this paper, a novel piezoelectric drive device is designed, and a robust active control method based on the fully actuated system theory (FRAC) is proposed to control low-frequency chatter during robotic milling. First, a novel piezoelectric drive device integrating piezoelectric actuators, encoders, and other parts is designed. Next, a time-varying model is developed that accounts for both the dynamic characteristics and the milling process of the industrial robot equipped with a piezoelectric drive device. Then, the FRAC method is proposed, which does not need to transform the time-varying model into a linear time-invariant model and avoids control failures caused by approximation errors. In addition, the robustness of the proposed FRAC method is proved theoretically. Finally, the effectiveness of the designed piezoelectric drive device and the proposed FRAC method is verified by numerical simulations and experiments. The results demonstrate that low-frequency chatter can be actively controlled during robotic milling.

title: A novel quasi-zero stiffness vibration isolator with load-adaptive adjustment
abstract: Low-frequency line spectra are crucial characteristic signals for detecting, tracking, and identifying targets in modern underwater acoustic warfare. A novel quasi-zero stiffness vibration isolator with load-adaptive adjustment (QZS VI-LA) is proposed to address the inherent payload sensitivity of conventional QZS isolators. First, a quasi-zero stiffness matching analysis of the QZS VI-LA system is conducted, and a non-ideal load adjustment mechanism (NLAM) is designed, by which the system’s static equilibrium position is physically recentered following payload changes through a worm-gear and trapezoidal screw assembly. Second, the dynamic equations of the QZS VI-LA system with flexible foundation are formulated. The dynamic characteristics are analyzed using the harmonic balance method combined with pseudo-arclength continuation. Finally, experimental validation is performed on a 100 kg prototype, demonstrating a natural frequency reduction to 1.7 Hz under small-amplitude excitation and broadband vibration attenuation of 20.16 dB over 2–1000 Hz. Crucially, the system is successfully recentered within 15 s under payload offsets of ± 10 kg by the NLAM, and effective ultra-low-frequency isolation performance is restored. It is demonstrated that the QZS-VI-LA system exhibits excellent low-frequency vibration isolation performance and load adaptation capability.

title: Hardening/softening transition near snap-through in MEMS arches via high-order perturbation
abstract: Electrostatically tunable MEMS shallow arches provide compact platforms for achieving large frequency tuning and high sensitivity. Experimental evidence indicates there is a possible softening–hardening–softening stiffness transition near snap-through. A high-order analytical framework is developed to explore nonlinear stiffness transitions in such systems operating near but not reaching the snap-through threshold. A full dynamic map is established, revealing a softening–hardening–softening sequence governed by the competing voltage-dependent contributions of geometric, electrostatic, and stretching-induced nonlinearities. Within this transition, quasi-linear dynamics responses emerge where third- and fifth-order effects offset across the relevant amplitude range. The analytical outcome reveals the underlying mechanism of the experimental phenomenon. These findings establish a predictive route toward voltage-programmable stiffness modulation, offering practical implications for the design of responsive, instability-free MEMS resonators and filters.

title: Fringe projection enabled dual-weight enhanced prototype network for non-contact bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Intelligent mechanical fault diagnosis has achieved remarkable advancement in recent years, yet it remains dominated by contact sensors whose installation constraints, load effect, invasive measurement, and single-point acquisition severely restrict applicability in complex environments. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposed a framework that synergizes a fringe projection vision system with a Dual-Weight Enhanced Prototype Network (DWEPN) for non-contact bearing fault diagnosis. The main contributions of this work were summarized as follows: 1) A fringe projection system is employed to acquire radial shaft vibration in a non-contact manner, eliminating sensor installation and load effects while enabling multi-point, material-independent, and long-distance measurement. 2) Shaft center orbit images reconstructed from radial vibration are used as diagnostic inputs, providing intuitive geometric representations of defect-induced deviations while preserving richer fault information by shortening vibration transmission paths. 3) To address the limitations of conventional prototype networks, a Dual-Weight Enhanced Prototype Network is proposed, incorporating adaptive weighting during both prototype construction and metric evaluation. Specifically, an Adaptive Prototype Weighting Network assigns sample-specific weights to mitigate prototype shift caused by heterogeneous support sample quality, instead of generic prototype refinement. Meanwhile, a Query Channel Weight Generator selectively enhances fault-sensitive channels in query features prior to distance computation, explicitly improving query feature discrimination rather than applying a unified attention mechanism across all learning stages. Finally, experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method achieved superior diagnostic performance across different operational conditions compared to existing meta-learning methods, providing a non-contact solution for industrial equipment intelligent maintenance that combines high precision with strong generalization capability.

title: A full-field displacement monitoring method for target-free traditional brick walls using low resolution videos based on unsupervised learning
abstract: Non-contact monocular displacement automatic monitoring can address the issues of sparse measurement points and expensive equipment in traditional contact-based displacement monitoring methods. However, existing non-contact monocular displacement monitoring methods exhibit low accuracy in large-displacement measurement under low-resolution and target-free conditions, and weak resistance to temporary occlusion. To solve these problems, this study aims to establish the SAM2-SR-DIS model based on few-shot unsupervised learning and improved optical flow method. The SAM2-SR-DIS algorithm requires only manual prompt points in the first frame to enable full-process automatic monitoring. The reliability of the results is verified by comparing the algorithm’s outputs with experimental displacements captured from video data of sulfate-eroded brick walls under compression. The research results show that all recognition accuracies reach millimeter-level, with over 60% achieving submillimeter-level precision. The per-frame computation time can reach sub-second level, representing a 57.20% reduction compared to the benchmark. Furthermore, SAM2-SR-DIS demonstrates better robustness against brightness variations, noise, and temporary occlusions, compared to the existing methods. This research can support establishing non-contact automatic structural health monitoring systems in masonry structures.

title: Calibrating Vaiana–Rosati phenomenological model for generic symmetric/asymmetric hysteretic behaviors by enhanced response sensitivity analysis
abstract: The Vaiana–Rosati phenomenological model (VRM) provides a closed-form expression to describe generic generalized force–displacement hysteretic behaviors. It utilizes two sets of physically interpretable parameters to explicitly formulate symmetric/asymmetric hysteretic loops without solving differential equations. To calibrate the VRM, this paper proposes an enhanced response sensitivity analysis method to identify parameters that minimize a least-squares objective function defined by the residual between the measured and theoretical hysteresis forces. The objective function is linearized by the response sensitivity and minimized using the Tikhonov regularization. Furthermore, the trust-region constraint is combined with the Tikhonov regularization process to enhance parameter convergence. Numerical simulations about symmetric/asymmetric hysteresis and experimental investigations on a wire rope isolator and a magnetorheological damper verify the proposed method’s accuracy and effectiveness, offering a unified framework for calibrating the VRM to simulate symmetric/asymmetric and rate-independent/rate-dependent hysteretic curves.

title: Dynamic distance polarization regularized optimal transport for cross domain fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: In recent years, optimal transport (OT) theory has garnered substantial attention in the cross-domain intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. OT theory is defined by the minimal cost required for transporting one distribution to another, even in the face of notable domain disparities. However, current OT-based fault diagnosis methods have limitations: distance-regularized method such as Wasserstein distance lack explicit modeling of the OT plan, and the learned OT plan cannot establish the relationship between fault clustering structures; coupling-regularized method such as entropy-regularized OT will cause the OT plan to be too dense, and the uncertainty of cross-domain transport plans will increase accordingly. To tackle these challenges, a cross-domain fault diagnosis framework based on dynamic distance polarization regularization for optimal transport is developed, which framework can explicitly model the structure of the OT transport plan and mitigate the complexity of cross-domain transport processes. Firstly, a distance polarization mechanism based on large-margin learning has been constructed and integrated into the optimal transport plan. By enforcing intra-class and inter-class thresholds, the optimal transport scheme is guided toward bipolar-oriented optimization, and a clear boundary between similar and dissimilar transport pairs is established, thereby reducing the uncertainty in the transport process. Secondly, a dynamic threshold mask strategy has been proposed, through which diagnostic category information is incorporated into the polarization process, thereby capturing intra-class/inter-class correspondences and ensuring the correct transport of diagnostic knowledge. Finally, to ensure target-domain Classifier diagnostic accuracy, source-domain samples are mapped to the target domain via Barycenter mapping, enabling the model to learn discriminative class boundaries in the target representation space and enhance diagnostic accuracy for unlabeled target data. The cross-domain diagnosis model is validated on two bearing datasets under different loads and speeds. The results demonstrate that its diagnostic performance is significantly improved compared with existing transfer learning models. The related work has been open-sourced at: https://github.com/Pear-so/OT_Fault-Diagnosis.

title: Editorial Board
High-precision identification of asynchronous blade vibration frequency using under-sampled single sensor tip-timing signals
abstract: Asynchronous vibration (non-synchronous vibration, NSV) is an important phenomenon that persistently exists during the operation of rotating blades and can easily lead to high-cycle fatigue and structural failure. Under constraints such as limited sensor installation and signal aliasing, accurately identifying blade asynchronous vibration frequencies under multiple operating conditions remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, a high-precision identification method for blade asynchronous vibration frequency based on under-sampled single-sensor blade tip timing (BTT) signals is proposed. The method locates the blade resonance interval by calculating the aliasing frequency. Approaches for separating asynchronous vibration components under different operating conditions are developed, and an asynchronous regression traversal model based on BTT (ART-BTT) between the asynchronous components and non-integer engine order (EO) is established, enabling identification of blade asynchronous frequencies using a single sensor. The method is validated through numerical simulations and a large-scale compressor blade test bench. The results show that the asynchronous frequency identification errors of the proposed method in numerical simulations are below 1% under constant speed, speed-up, speed-down, and resonance conditions. In the experimental validation, the maximum error between the identified frequency and the strain-gauge measurement is 0.945%, and the method is successfully applied to the frequency identification of a whole-stage blades. The proposed method features wide applicability, single sensor, and achieves high accuracy, enabling vibration frequency monitoring of blades under multiple operating conditions.

title: Laser Doppler vibrometers on moving platforms: advancements, challenges, and future opportunities
abstract: Laser Doppler Vibrometer (LDV) is a non-contact sensing technology widely used for vibration, acoustic, and wave measurements. In recent years, the deployment of LDV on moving platforms (LDVom), such as ground vehicles, robots, and drones, has enabled new solutions for remote sensing and condition monitoring of (infra)structures. LDVom leverages the mobility of manned and unmanned platforms, which offer distinct advantages in flexibility, coverage, and efficiency, but also face challenges arising from laser speckle, platform motion and vibration, and optical turbulence. This review synthesizes the technological enablers, diverse applications, unresolved challenges, and future opportunities of LDVom. The key technological enablers include tailored de-noising, signal diversity, laser head vibration compensation, and multi-point sensing. Current implementations of LDVom are predominantly vehicle-based, achieving real-world monitoring of road and railway infrastructure at near-traffic speeds, while emerging airborne implementations extend LDVom to drones and aircraft. Despite these advances, unresolved issues related to platform dynamics, target surface properties, environmental disturbances, and operational complexity continue to limit measurement quality, resolution, and reliability. Future advances in miniaturization, advanced signal diversity, multi-dimensional, multi-quantity LDV, and digital twins hold the potential to expand the capability and performance of LDVom. This review positions LDVom as an evolving and versatile technology with strong application potential across diverse domains.

title: Cross-condition fatigue life prediction in pre-corroded Q690E steel using failure mode-guided ultrasonic diffuse field
abstract: Service environments alter corrosion morphology and crack-driving mechanisms in high-strength steels, resulting in pronounced life scatter across conditions. Consequently, life predictors calibrated under a single environment often fail to transfer, especially when only sparse early-stage monitoring data are available. To reduce the sensitivity to environment-specific experiments, this study proposes a failure mode-guided fatigue life prediction framework based on diffuse guided wave responses. The approach focuses on characterizing damage evolution using a mean cumulative Euclidean distance that couples cumulative time shift and amplitude of ultrasonic signals. In addition, progressive multi-crack initiation and growth failure mode simulations are used to generate full-life ultrasonic response data, providing physics-informed priors and a prototype damage–life evolution curve in the feature space. To further improve cross-condition generalization, the model is strengthened via domain calibration and regularized fine-tuning. The framework is validated on Q690E high-strength steel under two representative corrosion conditions, namely acetic acid salt spray (AASS) and electrically accelerated corrosion (EAC). The results demonstrate that reliable cross-condition fatigue life prediction and remaining-life trajectory tracking can be achieved using only early-stage damage data from each condition, supporting prognostics-oriented structural health monitoring in corrosive environments. Specifically, the cross-condition prediction capability originates from the unified failure-evolution prior provided by the progressive multi-crack model, and this prior remains effective under different stress amplitudes, confirming cross-condition prediction across both corrosion environments and loading levels.

title: Interfacial debonding imaging in steel-concrete composite structures via a semi-supervised spatiotemporal wavefield autoencoder
abstract: Precise imaging of interfacial debonding in steel–concrete composite structures (SCCS) remains a significant challenge in the non-destructive testing of civil infrastructure. This study proposes a semi-supervised Spatiotemporal Wavefield Autoencoder (ST-WAE) based on ultrasonic wavefield imaging. Distinct from supervised approaches, the proposed model circumvents the need for prior labeled training data. Instead, it learns exclusively from localized healthy regions of the structure under test to reconstruct the latent spatiotemporal distribution of healthy wavefields. Consequently, interfacial debonding is visualized by extracting wave-damage interaction features via the reconstruction error between the input and the output. The proposed method was cross-validated using 3D meso-scale finite element simulations and experiments. Results demonstrate its capability to simultaneously image multiple debonding sites. It achieves a Maximum F1-score (MaxF1) of 0.66, significantly outperforming traditional wavefield imaging algorithms. This study provides a novel approach for precisely imaging invisible damage in SCCS. Furthermore, it holds substantial potential for the automated structural health monitoring of civil infrastructure.

title: A Riemannian-Hyperbolic Space-Based Algorithm for multisensor data fusion in spline degradation monitoring
abstract: Spline wear threatens the reliability of mechanical transmission systems, but conventional monitoring fails to reconcile heterogeneous data, capture dynamic degradation, or delineate hierarchical states. Here we present a geometric deep learning framework for multisensor fusion: vibration (macroscopic dynamics) and acoustic emission (AE, microscopic damage) signals are encoded as symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices to form a Riemannian manifold. Log-Euclidean metrics and Riemannian means mitigate cross-modal misalignment, while an attention-based graph neural network (GATConv) fuses features to learn spatiotemporal dependencies. Fused representations are embedded into Poincaré ball space—leveraging hyperbolic geometry’s exponential volume growth to enhance hierarchical wear separability—with unsupervised clustering and temporal mapping enabling time-resolved monitoring. On industrial datasets (slewing bearing, spline wear), the framework consistently outperforms mainstream methods by achieving effective cross-modal alignment, superior clustering quality, and accurate full-cycle wear tracking. This work establishes a geometric deep learning paradigm for mechanical health monitoring, advancing predictive maintenance in critical engineering systems.

title: Self-determining multiderivative-enhanced phase motion estimation for accurate visual vibration measurement
abstract: Visual vibration measurement is an emerging non-contact technique capable of high spatial resolution and full field. Phase-based motion estimation (PME) has gained widespread attention in visual vibration measurement due to its robustness and insensitivity to measurement environment. However, most existing PME methods, including both filter-based and derivative-based approaches, rely on empirically tuned parameters for either filter design or analytic signal construction, which limits their accuracy and generalizability. To address this, this paper proposes a self-determining multiderivative-enhanced phase motion estimation (MDPME) framework. By leveraging structured multi-order spatial derivatives of image intensity, MDPME constructs a parameter-free complex analytic signal and intrinsically determines the phase-to-displacement scale factor, eliminating the need for manual tuning or empirical calibration. This formulation transforms PME from a parameter-dependent approach into a self-determining framework while preserving the computational efficiency of derivative-based methods. Experimental results demonstrate that MDPME achieves a correlation coefficient exceeding 99.13% with reference sensor data, underscoring its superior performance over established PME techniques.

title: Effective energy harvesting in weak- and limited-airflow environments via butterfly-inspired rotary aerodynamic mechanism
abstract: Supplying energy to building safety equipment autonomously and reliably from weak and spatially confined airflow—such as that encountered in heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems—is challenging due to the lack of excitation mechanisms capable of sustaining stable energy conversion at low wind speeds. Conventional wind energy harvesters, based on linear resonance or classical galloping, typically exhibit narrow operating bandwidths and insufficient robustness under such conditions. Hence, this study introduces a nonlinear energy-harvesting pathway based on rotational galloping inspired by the dynamics of slowly flapping butterfly wings. The proposed mechanism enables stable energy extraction through moment-driven self-excited rotation rather than transverse force instability. Based on this principle, a rotational galloping electromagnetic energy harvester is designed and experimentally investigated in a wind tunnel, with its rotational response and electrical output characterized under varying geometric configurations. To elucidate the underlying dynamics, a coupled electromechanical model is developed based on the extended Hamilton principle, which represents unsteady aerodynamic torque with a multiple-time-delay formulation. High-fidelity numerical simulations combined with finite-time Lyapunov exponent analysis reveal the role of 3D coherent vortices in sustaining rotational oscillations. A Morlet wavelet analysis further captures the system’s nonlinear dynamic characteristics. Finally, the proposed harvester is integrated with an ultra-low-voltage energy management scheme to enable power conditioning and low-power device operation under weak-airflow conditions.

title: Semantic information hybrid distribution calibration-enabled multi-modal fusion network for unsupervised health state diagnosis of manipulator
abstract: Multimodal data fusion-driven intelligent health diagnosis is integral to predictive maintenance of mechanical equipment, yet it confronts two critical practical hurdles: unverified credibility of disentangled modal-invariant features and the sacrifice of fine-grained critical information for macro-consistency. These challenges significantly hinder its performance improvement and broader adoption. Inspired by this, a novel unsupervised fusion framework — the Semantic Information Hybrid Distribution Calibration-enabled Fusion Network (SIHDC-FN) — is developed, with its core comprising two modules: the Semantic-guided Vibration-Acoustics Joint Disentanglement (SVAJD) Module and the Category-aware Fine-grained Distribution Calibration (CFDC) Module. Within each module, maintenance log information — textual data that, despite being frequently overlooked, records the real health state of manipulators — is treated as a bridge endowed with authentic semantic attributes and an ideal calibration anchor, a dual role that enables it to facilitate, on one hand, the credible disentanglement of modal-invariant information at the macroscale. On the other hand, through the incorporation of a multivariate variational distribution joint constraint strategy, it further ensures the aligned enhancement of detailed features at the class-aware fine-grained scale, a process that ultimately preserves the subtle critical information inherent in modal-invariant features. The comprehensive performance of the proposed fusion method — encompassing feasibility, superiority, robustness, and anti-interference capacity — is thoroughly verified via multi-scenario tests on a typical 3-PRR planar parallel manipulator.

title: Large amplitude motion estimation via multi-scale phase-based video processing
abstract: Image phase-based motion estimation algorithms can process the natural texture of structural surfaces with strong environmental robustness. However, the phase wrapping effect limits their ability to measure large amplitude motion, restricting them to the range of ± π radians (equivalent to half a wavelength of physical displacement). For scenarios involving large amplitude motion, such as blade rotation, this study proposes a multi-scale phase-based motion estimation (M−PME) algorithm. This algorithm decomposes large amplitude motion into small amplitude sub-motions across multiple scales by constructing a Gaussian pyramid. This implements a multi-scale motion search strategy, progressing from coarse to fine, and avoids phase unwrapping by decomposing the motion into multiple scales. A phase motion constraint model is then fitted to identify sub-motions at each scale. Ultimately, high-precision tracking of large amplitude motion is achieved through motion field fusion. Validation of the M−PME algorithm was achieved through experiments involving both non-rotational and rotational large amplitude motion. The results show that the M−PME algorithm can effectively solve the problem of the traditional PME algorithm being unable to recognise large amplitude motion. Compared with real motion, the M−PME algorithm’s average absolute error (MAE) and standard deviation (STD) are between 0.4 and 0.04 pixels. Compared with the modal frequency of the rotating structure obtained using the classical DIC algorithm, the M−PME algorithm performs well in identifying rotational motion in actual measurement environments.

title: Dual-layer optimization of tower crane operations: Integrating safe offline trajectory generation with real-time swing damping
abstract: Tower crane operations in complex environments require the simultaneous achievement of obstacle avoidance, time-optimal transportation, and payload swing suppression. However, existing methods face a fundamental dilemma: trajectory-planning-based approaches can ensure collision-free paths but lack real-time adaptability to disturbances, whereas feedback-control-based methods can suppress swing effectively but cannot guarantee global obstacle avoidance because of their myopic nature. To address this issue, this paper proposes a unified dual-layer optimization framework that, for 4-DOF tower crane systems, for the first time, integrates an offline time-optimal obstacle-avoidance trajectory planner with an online real-time swing-damping controller. The novelty of the proposed framework lies in the coordinated co-design of offline planning and online control, the reformulation of trajectory optimization through auxiliary payload states, and the use of differentiable exponential cost functions to preserve both safety-margin flexibility and optimization tractability. In the offline phase, novel auxiliary state variables are introduced to transform the system dynamics, and an exponential cost function is designed to enforce safe obstacle clearance while maintaining differentiability for gradient-based optimization. The resulting optimal trajectory, obtained via the Newton trust-region method, inherently preserves a safety margin that accommodates subsequent online adjustments. In the online phase, a Lyapunov-based damping controller dynamically modifies the reference accelerations using real-time swing-angle feedback, thereby achieving asymptotic stability without compromising collision safety. Extensive hardware experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing methods in both swing suppression and energy efficiency while strictly satisfying obstacle-avoidance constraints.

title: Iterative chirp-basis transform for accurate and efficient separation of closely spaced and crossing multi-family synchronous signals
abstract: Many dynamic signals comprise multi-family synchronous components, complicating the analysis and extraction of nonstationary features. Although time–frequency analysis (TFA) methods can reveal some of these features, efficiently and accurately separating closely spaced non-proportional components and cross-components remains challenging. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a new TFA method, termed the iterative chirp-basis transform (ICBT). In ICBT, an iterative peak-search strategy is developed based on the residual frequency-chirp-basis (FCB) representation. The frequency and chirp-basis parameters of the highest-energy component are first identified from the residual, after which the component is reconstructed and subtracted to update the residual for the next iteration, and this process repeats until all components are recovered. Subsequently, a novel sliding-window strategy with variable initial positions is proposed to mitigate endpoint effects at the initial window, enabling more reliable classification of synchronous components across different families. Building upon this strategy, adaptive FCB search ranges are then constructed for forward and backward windows to further reduce computational cost while maintaining close alignment of the same-family components. Finally, the inter-family interference inherent to CBT is eliminated based on the obtained time–frequency parameters to correct the amplitude of each component. Both simulated and experimental studies indicate that ICBT can effectively separate closely spaced non-proportional and crossover components, providing enhanced accuracy in instantaneous frequency and amplitude estimation, robustness to noise, computational efficiency, and high fidelity in signal reconstruction. These attributes make it more suitable for vibration analysis and fault diagnosis in complex rotating machinery.

title: Adaptive entropy-integrated VMD for robust quantitative characterization of surface notches using laser ultrasonic Rayleigh waves
abstract: Surface-breaking notches modulate laser-ultrasonic Rayleigh waves and enable non-contact notch sizing, yet practical signals are frequently degraded by noise, modal interference, and waveform distortion, leading to unstable quantification. This paper presents a physics-guided framework that integrates thermoelastic finite-element (FE) modelling, adaptive entropy-integrated variational mode decomposition (AIE-VMD), and fused-feature monotonic inversion for robust notch characterization. The FE model disentangles depth–width effects on the transmitted Rayleigh wave: notch depth primarily reduces transmission energy via frequency-dependent loss, whereas notch width mainly introduces phase/time-delay perturbations and dispersion-related asymmetry. To stabilize feature extraction under noise-dominated conditions, AIE-VMD performs automatic parameter optimization and entropy-based mode screening, producing distortion-minimized reconstructions while suppressing redundant components and stochastic fluctuations. From the reconstructed signals, peak-to-peak amplitude, RMS, envelope energy, and absolute negative peak are fused into normalized indices and mapped to notch depth and width using low-parametric monotonic exponential models with closed-form inversion. Experiments on aluminum plates with surface notches whose depth and width each span 0–1.2 mm show close agreement with simulation, achieving R2≥0.99 and mean absolute errors of 0.02–0.03 mm in calibration and blind validation.

title: Dynamic modelling and analysis of the floating spline with locating surfaces, O-rings, and misalignment
abstract: Dynamic performances of floating splines are directly related to the safe operation of helicopter transmission systems. The dynamic behaviour analysis of floating splines should comprehensively consider the coupling effects of O-rings, locating surfaces, and misalignment. Currently, this type of spline dynamic model is not yet available. Considering the locating surface rub-impact, misalignment, vibration displacement, this study modeled the meshing state of spline teeth and reserved clearance of locating surfaces, simplified O-rings into mechanical Voigt models, and then proposed a general floating spline dynamic model. By coupling the floating spline to the spline-rotor system, the equation of motion for the spline-rotor system is obtained, whose accuracy was verified through dynamic experiments on the spline-rotor system dynamic experimental rig. Detailed effect mechanisms of locating surfaces, O-rings, misalignment, and vibration displacement on the spline-rotor system were revealed. The floating spline dynamic model proposed in this paper can accurately determine whether locating surfaces are rub-impact or not, which can provide theoretical basis for the dynamic design of floating splines and related rotor systems.

title: A self-adaptive piezoelectric-electromagnetic hybrid wind energy harvester with broadband operation and low startup wind speed
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable power sources for microelectronics and wireless sensor networks has intensified research into ambient energy harvesting. This study introduces an Adaptive Wind-Speed Piezoelectric–Electromagnetic Hybrid Harvester (AWS-PEMH) that combines a novel tilt-adjustable slide-rail adaptive unit with one piezoelectric module (PEH) and two electromagnetic modules (EMH-1, EMH-2) to achieve a low startup wind speed, a widened effective operating range, and promising operational stability. Unlike conventional spring-based adaptive harvesters, the AWS-PEMH employs a novel tilt-adjustable slide-rail mechanism utilizing gravity as a fatigue-free restoring force. This springless design minimizes initial rotational resistance, enabling an exceptional startup wind speed of 1.6 m/s. As wind speed increases, centrifugal force engages both modules synergistically. Empirical investigations reveal a beneficial friction-induced hysteresis during mode switching, acting as a mechanical low-pass filter to prevent high-frequency chattering under fluctuating natural winds. By staggering discrete resonant peaks via a multi-mass piezoelectric array, the continuous operational bandwidth is effectively broadened to 4.1 m/s (sustaining > 10 mW integrated output). Discrepancies between ideal models and empirical data are systematically resolved through parameter sensitivity analysis and the incorporation of Duffing-type nonlinear magnetic hardening dynamics. Electrically, an independent dual-path power management topology effectively decouples the modules, achieving a high conversion efficiency even under low-input-power conditions (< 5 mW) typical of weak winds. The fully enclosed prototype yields a peak power of 38 mW (volumetric power density of 22 μW/cm3) and demonstrates stable short-term performance with negligible degradation after a 72-hour continuous test (7.128 × 105 cycles). Validated by rooftop field tests, the AWS-PEMH provides a highly resilient power solution for distributed outdoor sensing.

title: EPicMT: edge-aware physics-informed concurrent multiplexed transformer for high-fidelity signal compression, reconstruction, and diagnosis/prognosis
abstract: Prognostics & Health Management (PHM) systems collect high‑rate, multi‑sensor signals that must traverse bandwidth‑limited networks and run on resource‑constrained edge devices. Uniform, ratio-driven signal compression often erases weak yet diagnostic structures and degrades decision quality under operating drift. Many learned codecs store dense floating-point latent codes that are ill-suited to edge budgets, require per-sensor or per-fault specialization, and rarely embed physics. Under drift, these methods smear the sidebands and harmonics that carry critical evidence of degradation in vibration and acoustic signals. We introduce the Edge-aware Physics-informed Concurrent Multiplexed Transformer (EPicMT), a signal-processing framework, which couples selective transmission with physics-guided signal reconstruction within a single architecture spanning compression, reconstruction, and decision tasks. EPicMT implements content-aware token selection (sampling) to control the number of transmitted coefficients, and structure-aware, non-uniform quantization that assigns finer steps to harmonic/envelope bands and coarser steps to broadband background, achieving bit-budgeted signal compression rather than mere dimensionality reduction. On the decoder, a physics-guided Transformer with time–frequency priors, multi-scale envelope consistency and a physically-constrained diffuser, regularizes reconstruction so that spectral energy, phase relations, and envelope trends are preserved. Concurrent reflects the joint optimization of diagnostic and prognostic objectives within the same network, while multiplexed denotes parameter sharing across tasks through a common backbone and token interface, enabling unified training and signal-adaptive bit allocation under varying operating conditions. Case studies on an in-house gearbox testbed, the CWRU bearing dataset, and NASA CMAPSS demonstrate high-fidelity signal reconstructions at compression ratios up to 64:1 while maintaining or improving fault-classification accuracy and remaining useful life prediction relative to representative autoencoder and Transformer baselines. The learned gating reduces transmitted bits and on-device compute without hand-tuned heuristics, and an embedded deployment confirms feasibility on resource-constrained hardware.

title: Interaction strategy between ultrasonic phased arrays for particle acoustic manipulation
abstract: Although significant progress has been made in non-contact manipulation based on acoustic levitation, the range of object manipulation is limited to the ultrasonic phased arrays. In this study, an ultrasonic interaction system consisting of an ultrasonic mechanical system and an opposing ultrasonic phased array is proposed. This system successfully achieves non-contact transportation and assembly of millimeter-sized irregular micro-objects between two ultrasonic phased arrays. When the ultrasonic interaction system operates between two ultrasonic phased arrays, the acoustic fields generated by the ultrasonic phased array will undergo fusion. Focusing on this acoustic field fusion phenomenon, we simulated the changes in the acoustic field during interaction and analyzed the relationship between the acoustic trap distance and sound pressure distribution. In addition, to achieve stable interaction with objects, this paper proposes a strategy for adjusting the position of suspended objects based on the preset posture of the robotic arm. This strategy enables objects to remain in a stable suspended state during interaction and significantly reduces system complexity and real-time feedback errors. The experimental results show that the ultrasonic interaction system proposed in this paper can achieve stable transportation and assembly of objects, effectively overcoming the limitations of traditional acoustic levitation, which only operates within a single ultrasonic phased array. This technological breakthrough in the field of acoustic levitation is expected to provide a new non-contact operation solution for chemical engineering, biological assembly, and micro-assembly.

title: A rotating stall warning method for a contra-rotating compressor based on deep learning with automatic hyperparameter optimization
abstract: The dynamic pressure signals during the rotating stall process of a compressor exhibit pronounced nonlinearity and non-stationarity. In addition, the small amplitude of pre-stall disturbances makes early stall identification and warning a challenging signal-processing problem. Moreover, the hyperparameters of conventional neural network models rely on manual, experience-based tuning, which limits their prediction accuracy and robustness under complex operating conditions. To address these issues, this study proposes a rotating stall early warning method based on a convolutional neural network combined with a long short-term memory network (CNN-LSTM) with automatic hyperparameter optimization. A low-speed axial flow contra-rotating compressor is selected as the test object. Stall experiments are conducted under different inlet and rotational speed configurations. Dynamic pressure time series data are acquired using sensor arrays mounted at the blade tip of the front and rear rotors. After preprocessing, including filtering, normalization, and resampling, a dataset is constructed for neural network training and validation. The Northern Goshawk Optimization (NGO) algorithm is introduced to globally optimize key hyperparameters of the CNN-LSTM network. And the optimal NGO-CNN-LSTM model is then applied to predict dynamic pressure stall time series data. The results show that the NGO-CNN-LSTM model achieves higher prediction accuracy than the conventional CNN-LSTM model. Furthermore, a kernel density estimation (KDE) method is employed to adaptively determine stall warning thresholds for different operating conditions. Under uniform inlet conditions, the NGO-CNN-LSTM model achieves a stall warning lead time exceeding 10 s for most speed configurations and improves the poor warning performance of the CNN-LSTM model under some speed conditions. Under inlet distortion conditions, the proposed model still provides a stable stall warning time of no less than 7 s. Comparison between the predicted data and the original measurements indicates that the NGO-CNN-LSTM model can identify smaller amplitude pre-stall disturbances with clear physical significance at an earlier stage. Its predictions show higher consistency with the original data, leading to more reliable stall warning results.

title: Local instantaneous velocity estimation for effective thickness mapping (LIVE-ETM) in composite panels
abstract: Guided wavefield data in composite structures contain rich information about structural anomalies such as damage and geometric discontinuities. However, the effectiveness of damage detection is often hindered by wave attenuation and signal reflections from structural features such as stiffeners. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel damage index termed the local instantaneous velocity, which is used for detecting damage in composite structures. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on energy compensation, the proposed method enhances interpretability by exploiting wave velocity, a physically meaningful parameter. The local instantaneous velocity highlights propagation anomalies in the wavefield that are associated with damage and stiffeners, enabling more reliable localization. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated through both numerical simulations and experimental testing on a glass fiber-reinforced polymer aircraft panel containing stiffeners and delaminations. In the experiments, the guided wavefield is generated using a piezoelectric transducer and measured using a scanning laser Doppler vibrometer. The results demonstrate strong agreement with the actual locations, sizes, and shapes of delamination and debonding regions, confirming the robustness and noise insensitivity of the proposed method for detecting barely visible damage in composite structures.

title: Bearing fault diagnosis via dual-level Bayesian regularization and frequency-domain kurtosis-driven dictionary learning
abstract: Sparse representation methods obtain sparse representations of bearing transient impulse signals through sparse coding and dictionary learning, which are then utilized for feature extraction, and have received widespread attention in fault diagnosis. However, during the incipient stage of faults, the impulse features of the signals are weak, with energy levels substantially lower than those of the background noise. This makes it difficult to effectively separate true impulse components from noise during sparse coding, resulting in dictionary atoms that are more susceptible to noise contamination rather than capturing authentic fault characteristics. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel dual-level Bayesian regularization and frequency-domain kurtosis-driven dictionary learning (DBR-FKDL) method for extracting weak fault features of bearings under strong noise interference. During sparse coding, a differentiated penalty is applied to the sparse coefficient level based on a Mean Kurtosis (MK) weighting method, which quantifies the impulsiveness of signal segments. The variational Bayesian (VB) framework is then employed to adaptively update the regularization parameter, thereby achieving global sparsity control. Furthermore, within the dictionary learning stage, a guidance mechanism utilizing the frequency-domain kurtosis-weighted residual is proposed to guide the learning of dictionary atoms toward more prominent impulse features. Finally, fault diagnosis is conducted via envelope spectrum analysis of the reconstructed sparse signal. Validation using both simulated and experimental data demonstrates the superiority of the proposed method in extracting weak bearing fault features.

title: A novel mechanism-data dual-driven prediction method for tracking error in ultra-precision machining
abstract: The formation mechanism of tracking error in ultra-precision machining is highly complex, as it is influenced by multiple coupled factors.Traditional single-driven modeling methods—either mechanism-driven or data-driven—face inherent limitations: the former struggles to accurately capture the nonlinear dynamics of servo systems, while the latter suffers from poor interpretability.To fill this gap, this paper proposes a novel mechanism-data dual-driven tracking error prediction method. Firstly, a mechanism-driven prediction module for the deterministic physical components of tracking error is established based on servo control theory and parameter identification experiments. Then, based on the hybrid deep learning algorithm (TCN-BiLSTM-MHA), a data-driven module is developed to fit the unmodeled tracking error residuals. TCN and BiLSTM capture the long-term dependencies inherent in servo dynamics, while the MHA mechanism identifies key features and adaptively allocates their weights. Finally, a dual-driven prediction method is proposed by integrating the theoretical model with the residual prediction model. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with conventional single-driven methods, the proposed method achieves superior prediction accuracy, with a mean absolute error (MAE) as low as 0.000012 and a relative improvement of up to 65.71%. This work provides a reliable technical support for tracking error compensation and further improves the machining accuracy of optical components.

title: Cross-range displacement measurement using a single MIMO FMCW radar
abstract: Displacement measurement using microwave radar has attracted extensive research interest. However, existing techniques are limited to detecting motion along the radial direction. This paper proposes a method for measuring cross-range displacement based on a single multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar, achieving for the first time the measurement of non-radial displacement using a single radar system. The proposed approach compensates for the phase variations induced by range and angle migration caused by cross-range motion, and decouples the phase components in the intermediate-frequency (IF) signal that are jointly dependent on target range and angle, thereby extracting the cross-range displacement. Rigorous theoretical analysis demonstrates the feasibility of the method, while simulation results confirm its effectiveness. Experimental results further verify that the proposed method can reliably measure both small-amplitude high-frequency displacements and large-amplitude low-frequency displacements.

title: Dynamic stiffness analysis of angular contact ball bearings based on fully coupled bearing-rotor dynamic model
abstract: A fully coupled dynamic model of a ball bearing-rotor system is developed and experimentally validated to investigate the interaction between bearing internal dynamics and rotor vibration. The model resolves bearing contact forces and moments directly from internal dynamics, enabling the dynamic stiffness to evolve naturally with rotor motion. Results show that the dynamic stiffness of angular contact ball bearings exhibits pronounced non-stationary behavior, in which low-frequency variations induced by rotor load modulation coexist with high-frequency fluctuations transmitted through the rolling elements. These stiffness fluctuations demonstrate that bearing stiffness is continuously modulated by rotor dynamics rather than being an intrinsic local property. At high rotational speeds and low axial loads, additional inertial loads induced by rotor vibration significantly degrade effective bearing stiffness and destabilize ball-raceway contacts. Based on this mechanism, a stiffness-based criterion is proposed to characterize the limiting speed governed by internal bearing dynamics. Furthermore, stiffness variations have a limited influence on low-order rotor modes but strongly affect higher-order modes, leading to shifts in hazardous operating speed ranges and modulation of rotor vibration responses.

title: Grey-box Gaussian processes for mode shape normalisation: Damage localisation under environmental and operational variability
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) offers a promising path towards automated, long-term monitoring of critical infrastructure such as offshore structures and bridges. A crucial component of such monitoring schemes is the localisation of damage, with model-based SHM providing a possible framework for this task. Here, damage localisation can be achieved by minimising the discrepancy between the modal properties of a damaged state and those of a healthy reference, but it is severely hindered by changes in the modal properties induced by environmental and operational variations (EOVs). This difficulty is compounded by the fact that measurement data are often limited, with data commonly unavailable across the full operational span, missing due to sensor failure and dropout, or sparsely sampled because of hardware constraints. In particular, mode shapes are often used without adequately accounting for the limited coverage of EOVs in continuous model-based damage localisation frameworks, resulting in inaccurate localisation. In this paper, we propose a regression-based data normalisation scheme that learns vector-valued mode shapes explicitly as functions of EOVs, allowing them to vary across a structure’s operating envelope and thereby enabling model-based damage localisation under varying environmental and operational conditions. To further alleviate the problem of limited training data, we consider two grey-box modelling strategies based on Gaussian processes that incorporate accessible engineering knowledge: (i) a Hilbert-space Gaussian process enforcing boundary conditions, and (ii) a Gaussian process with a physics-based prior mean given by finite-element mode shapes. We target long-term monitoring scenarios, where training data are limited and standard machine learning regression techniques underperform. Using the Leibniz University Test Structure for Monitoring, a representative real-world structure, we show that incorporating accessible engineering domain knowledge into a Gaussian process alleviates data scarcity and improves damage localisation under partially observed EOVs. This significantly extends the range of scenarios where model-based damage localisation is feasible, thereby improving the continuous, long-term monitoring capabilities of operational structures.

title: An unsupervised domain adaptive fault diagnosis for rotating machinery based on physical wavelet convolution and joint distribution alignment
abstract: Under the conditions of strong noise and small samples, the subtle fault features of rotating machinery are often obscured, and traditional deep learning methods face the challenges of poor interpretability and a heavy reliance on large labeled datasets. To address these issues, an unsupervised fault diagnosis method based on an asymmetric modulated Gaussian difference wavelet kernel convolutional neural network (AMGDWKCNN) is proposed. Firstly, an asymmetric modulation physical convolution layer (AMPConv) is designed. By employing an asymmetrically modulated Gaussian difference wavelet kernel, it matches the asymmetric impact characteristics of vibration signals, thereby enhancing the model’s physical interpretability. Secondly, a dynamic nonlinear noise reduction mechanism is constructed, which employs a dual-attention-guided flexible soft threshold function to adaptively suppress noise interference, while leveraging the KAN activation function to enhance the nonlinear expression capability of fault features. Finally, a joint distribution alignment module is proposed. By combining category-conditional second-order statistical matching loss with predictive entropy uncertainty metrics, it dynamically weights and aligns category semantics with global distributions, thereby enhancing the model’s generalization performance across operating conditions. Experimental validation conducted on two publicly available bearing datasets and a self-built gearbox dataset demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively extract subtle fault features under the scenarios with strong noise and small samples, achieving high accuracy and strong generalization.

title: Thermo-mechanical bidirectionally coupled analysis of rolling bearings based on stepwise associative iteration strategy
abstract: To enable accurate prediction of the thermo-mechanically coupled dynamic behavior of rolling bearings operating under complex service conditions, this study develops a thermo-mechanical bidirectionally coupled dynamic model based on a stepwise associative iteration strategy. The proposed framework integrates the discretized thermal network with the dynamics model that accounts for cage flexibility, thereby allowing simultaneous evaluation of the dynamic response, temperature evolution, and thermally induced deformation. The iterative strategy establishes a bidirectionally coupling loop by capturing both the heat generated by friction (mechanical-to-thermal coupling) and the contact condition modifications caused by thermal deformation (thermal-to-mechanical coupling). Based on this framework, the thermal response, dynamic characteristics, slip behavior, and component interactions under various operating conditions are systematically analyzed. The results indicate that thermally induced clearance reduction substantially alters the internal load distribution and inner orbit, and suppresses roller slip at high speeds. Compared with a purely mechanical model, the coupled model more accurately predicts the shifts in natural frequencies and resonance peaks caused by thermal deformation. The proposed modeling and solution framework provides a theoretical basis for understanding the bearing dynamic performance and slip instability mechanisms under thermo-mechanical coupling.

title: Motion acceleration reconstruction of projectiles under launch conditions using generative adversarial networks
abstract: Accurate measurement of in-bore projectile acceleration is critical for optimizing artillery launch systems and evaluating interior ballistic performance. However, signals from projectile-borne storage tests are severely corrupted by high-frequency bore collision noise, masking low-frequency motion features and hindering accurate identification of projectile dynamics. Conventional denoising methods, which rely on cumbersome manual parameter tuning, prove ineffective against such stochastic high-amplitude coupled noise. This study proposes a physics-constrained generative adversarial network (GAN) that integrates physical priors with adversarial training. The method leverages the intrinsic physical mapping between projectile base pressure and in-bore acceleration, including synchronized time-domain peaks, consistent temporal trends, and shared underlying combustion and motion physics, to guide the denoising process. Specifically, the normalized base pressure signal serves as a conditional input to the discriminator, which evaluates the denoised acceleration produced by the generator. Physics-based constraints regulate the acceleration generation scale, enabling synergistic noise suppression and signal preservation while reducing reliance on extensive pristine training data. Simulations across ten noise levels demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional techniques such as discrete wavelet transform and empirical mode decomposition, particularly in high-amplitude noise suppression. Three independent live-fire tests confirm its robustness and generalization capability, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio of up to 40 dB for the denoised in-bore acceleration. This work establishes a new paradigm for denoising dynamic signals in extreme launch environments, greatly enhancing the efficiency of ballistic testing and the accuracy of artillery performance assessment.

title: A method for multi-frequency guided wave response characterization and tightness assessment of bolted joint structures
abstract: Bolted joints, as vital connecting components, significantly influence structural safety and performance through their fastening conditions. To address limitations of existing methods—including strong frequency dependence, the Greenwood–Williamson microcontact theory is employed to establish a physical mapping between preload and guided wave leakage energy. Finite element simulations verify the non-monotonic response characteristics of single-frequency guided wave energy indicators under different excitation frequencies, highlighting the influence of frequency selection on identification results. Based on this, a Chirp-excited frequency-domain reconstruction method is used to extract multiple narrowband responses in the range of 50–180 kHz, and a weight optimization strategy is applied to achieve multi-frequency energy fusion, yielding the bolt tightness index (TI). Results from three repeated loading tests demonstrate good linear correlation between the fused indicator and preload, with fitting performance superior to any single-frequency damage index, mutually validating the simulation findings. To enhance environmental robustness, a bivariate energy-temperature regression model compensates for temperature drift. Validation in 25–60 °C confirms compensated model R2 >0.98 under typical preloads, with RMSE as low as 1.2×10−5, highlighting precision and generalizability. Finite element simulations further verify that increased preload enhances contact area and wave transmission efficiency, corroborating the model’s physical validity. In summary, this method delivers exceptional accuracy, stability, and engineering applicability, providing theoretical and technical foundations for high-reliability health monitoring of bolted structures.

title: Modeling and vibrations of temperature-dependent three-phase double-functionally graded carbon fiber and GPL reinforced composite truncated conical shells with varying thickness, theoretical analysis and experimental validation
abstract: This paper develops a new double-functionally graded (DFG) model and performs the vibration analysis of temperature-dependent three-phase graphene platelet (GPL) reinforced carbon fiber (CF) composite truncated conical shells with exponentially varying thickness under different boundary conditions. Compared with the conventional two-phase composites, three-phase DFG carbon fiber and GPL reinforced epoxy-based composites achieve further enhancement of the mechanical and functional properties by the functionally graded (FG) GPLs and FG carbon fibers as reinforcements. The equivalent thermo-mechanical properties of temperature-dependent three-phase DFG carbon fiber and GPL reinforced conical shells are determined by the improved Halpin-Tsai approach, mixing rule, Mori-Tanaka approach, and modified Schapery model. The effects of the carbon fiber and GPL parameters, varying thickness parameters, boundary conditions, temperature increment, wave numbers, and structural parameters on the frequencies and modes are examined by utilizing the higher-order shear deformation theory (HSDT) and Galerkin approach. The results indicate that the three-phase DFG-A1X2 carbon fiber and GPL reinforced varying thickness conical shell with 1% GPL mass fraction, 30% CF average volume fraction, 90° fiber orientation angle, Nx=1 and h1/h2=2 varying thickness parameters has the maximum fundamental frequency, and improves the fundamental frequency by 282.7% compared to the epoxy conical shell. Moreover, three-phase DFG varying thickness conical shells with 10 layers can obtain a better DFG effect. The experimental study and comparisons are presented to verify the theoretical results. This study guides the modeling and vibration analysis of temperature-dependent three-phase DFG carbon fiber and GPL reinforced composite structures with varying thickness, and provides a novel high-performance material for the aerospace and vehicle industries.
keywords: Three-phase GPL reinforced carbon fiber composite
Truncated conical shells with varying thickness

title: A low-speed camera DIC approach for measuring synchronous vibrations in rotating disks
abstract: During operation, turbomachinery blades are subjected to dynamic excitations, which are the primary drivers of high-cycle fatigue, the leading cause of failure in bladed disks. Therefore, accurate measurement of their dynamic response under resonance is critical for reliable design. Traditional contact-based measurement techniques suffer from drawbacks such as added mass, limited lifespan, and complex data transmission, prompting interest in non-contact alternatives.
