This paper explores the application of digital image correlation (DIC) for analyzing synchronous vibrations in bladed disks. The proposed approach employs low-speed, high-resolution cameras combined with downsampling strategies to enable cost-effective, full-field, high-resolution measurements. A signal processing technique, the circumferential harmonic fit (CHF), is proposed and applied to extract system parameters from downsampled displacement data. The methodology is applied on a simplified bladed disk mounted on a spinning rig, demonstrating successful identification of operational deflection shapes at resonance. • Dynamics of rotating disks recorded at a sampling rate below the Nyquist limit. • Circumferential harmonic adaptation fit was used to avoid aliasing errors. • Excitation of the dummy disk using permanent magnets.

title: Bay-Fi: Approximate Bayesian main Frequency Identification for extremely undersampled signals
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) is increasingly shaped by the adoption of low-power and distributed sensing technologies, which make long-standing challenges — such as limited data transmission, energy efficiency, and computational scalability — more critical than ever. In vibration-based monitoring, these constraints motivate the use of highly compressed measurements, where traditional frequency identification methods often rely on computationally expensive signal reconstruction and problem-specific tuning, limiting their applicability at high compression ratios. This study introduces a novel general method, named approximate Bayesian Frequency Identification ( Bay-Fi ), which enables direct identification of the main modal frequency without requiring signal reconstruction and any prior tuning. The proposed approach adopts Bayesian principles to update prior information on the main frequency using an approximate likelihood derived from compressed measurements, enabling robust estimation under severe data sparsity. The effectiveness of Bay-Fi is first validated through experimental tests on a laboratory-scale, simply-supported beam, demonstrating superior frequency identification performance compared to conventional techniques. Subsequently, the methodology is applied to real-world data collected from an operational composite steel–concrete bridge. Results confirm the robustness of the approach, showcasing its ability to accurately identify structural vibration frequencies even under extreme data sparsity, without requiring prior training. These findings highlight the potential of Bay-Fi for real-time, low-power SHM applications in large-scale infrastructure monitoring.

title: A high-precision control method for nonlinear characteristics of piezoelectric actuators
abstract: This paper presents a high-precision control method for piezoelectric actuators (PEA) to improve displacement tracking accuracy in ultra-precision positioning applications. A discrete Duhem hysteresis model is established to describe the nonlinear input–output behavior of the actuator, and a modelling framework combining wavelet threshold denoising (WTD) with a recursive least-squares algorithm using a time-varying forgetting factor (RLS-TFF) is developed to improve parameter identification accuracy under measurement noise. Based on the identified model, a feedforward-feedback control scheme is constructed for hysteresis compensation and tracking enhancement. Experimental results show that the proposed modelling method achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.0446 μm in hysteresis identification. In addition, the proposed control scheme reduces the hysteresis error from 16.4% FSR to 0.02% FSR and improves tracking performance under both static and dynamic reference trajectories. These results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective for high-precision motion control of PEAs in applications requiring nanoscale positioning accuracy.

title: Tunable noise and vibration reduction on an A3-sized piezoelectric metamaterial panel: Modeling and experimental validation
abstract: Piezoelectric locally resonant metamaterials (PLRMs) show promise as a tunable and lightweight approach for low-frequency noise and vibration control, overcoming the narrow bandwidth limitations of mechanical resonator-based LRMs. This study presents a combined numerical and experimental investigation of an A3-sized PLRM panel designed for tunable vibro-acoustic attenuation. The metastructure comprises an aluminum plate with a 9 × 9 array of piezoelectric elements, individually connected to a tunable inductive–resistive shunt circuit. A unit-cell-based finite element framework, integrating Bloch Mode Synthesis model-order reduction, enables the efficient prediction of vibration attenuation. The model is validated experimentally through transverse plate velocity measurements for multiple excitation locations and tuning configurations up to 1 kHz, showing excellent agreement with simulated frequency response functions. Acoustic radiation measurements further demonstrate that this vibration reduction translates directly into strong, targeted and tunable structure-borne noise attenuation around the tuned target frequencies. These results validate the proposed modeling strategy and demonstrate the practical potential of representative-scale PLRM panels for tunable noise and vibration control.

title: Open-set tool condition monitoring of end mills
abstract: In machining operations, cutting tools not only undergo conventional progressive wear but may also encounter abrupt anomalies such as tool breakage and even tool-body fracture. Compared with wear, these anomalies exert a more severe impact on workpiece quality and operational safety; however, they are rare, difficult to capture, and may be entirely absent from training datasets, causing methods founded on closed-set assumptions to fail at recognizing non-wear anomalies. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an open-set, source-free method for multi-anomaly tool condition monitoring. Relying solely on wear data, the method learns stable representations and uncertainty measures to perform gated detection of unknown anomalies. The network adopts a multi-modal input architecture that jointly models the evolutionary trajectories of time-series signals, the abrupt edges highlighted by differenced signals, and handcrafted prior consensus features, while being aided by a feature-modulation mechanism to enhance class separability under open-set settings. A two-stage training strategy is further devised: in the source domain, joint constraints of directional separation and intra-class aggregation build a stable decision structure; in the target domain, a multi-level class-conditional alignment mechanism is designed to strengthen the discriminability of heterogeneous samples across operating conditions. In addition, an open-set sample evaluation metric based on joint energy-mahalanobis uncertainty is proposed to construct domain-stable open-set gating. Cross-domain transfer experiments across six operating conditions validate the proposed method’s significant performance and strong generalization in open-set monitoring tasks.

title: Load identification methods for screen panels in flip-flow screens under material loading
abstract: A vibrating flip-flow screen (VFFS) is a crucial piece of equipment for the deep dry screening of viscous and fine-grained coal. Under different screening conditions, variations in feed parameters can alter the tensile load of the screen panel, which affects the vibration characteristics of the screen frame. However, due to the limitations of the structure and working environment of the VFFS, the tensile load is difficult to obtain directly. This study proposes signal processing methods including multi-scale time-domain feature extraction and peak–valley oversampling, and develops a particle swarm optimized long short-term memory (PSO-LSTM) method to identify the tensile load of the screen panel-material coupled system. The coupled model of the screen panel and material is validated through a stepwise experimental method. The results show that under different working conditions, the PSO-LSTM method achieves higher identification accuracy of the tensile load than the LSTM and GA-BP methods, with a relative error of 11.42%, demonstrating its applicability and stability under complex conditions. This study achieves accurate identification of the tensile load in the screen panel-material coupled system, providing a basis for developing a more realistic VFFS dynamic model.

title: Uncertainty-involved evaluation of real-time lubrication states in tilting pad thrust bearings
abstract: Lubrication failures in tilting pad thrust bearings arise from the lubrication state degradation. Therefore, real-time evaluation of the lubrication state is critical for monitoring and prediction of lubrication failures. Traditional methods, such as those based on the Stribeck curve, have slow response times and industrial implementation challenges. In contrast, the lubricant film thickness relative to the composite roughness of two contacting surfaces, commonly referred to as the lambda ratio, provides a faster assessment of lubrication states, but it struggles to accurately identify the transition zones between different lubrication states. To address this issue, this paper presents an uncertainty-involved evaluation method of real-time lubrication states in tilting pad thrust bearings. Extensive lubrication state degradation tests are performed on a thrust pad bearing test rig. By leveraging the synchronous variation between the coefficient of friction and the lambda ratio, the maximum likelihood estimation technique is employed to establish threshold sets for the lambda ratio. Additionally, kernel density estimation is used to derive the probability distribution functions for these threshold sets. Through the integration of cumulative probability and probability assignment, a probability characterization method of lubrication states is developed and validated with experimental data, achieving 88% identification accuracy for three-stage classification and 83% overall accuracy for four-stage classification across diverse operating conditions.

title: A domain-correction framework for structural response reconstruction with imperfect FEM and sparse measurements
abstract: Deep learning for structural response reconstruction faces two fundamental barriers: scarce real-world data and the practical inevitability of imperfect finite element models (FEM). While FEM-generated data offer a solution, the systematic bias between simulation and reality is often overlooked, limiting generalization. This work proposes a domain-correction framework that strategically leverages this bias. We employ a minimally calibrated FEM as a biased simulator to pre-train a Bidirectional GRU network with Top-k sparse attention (BiGRU-SA), instilling physics-regularized priors. A Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) regularized transfer learning stage then actively corrects the simulation bias by aligning feature distributions, requiring only a tiny fraction of real data. Validated on a cantilever beam and a wind turbine blade, the framework demonstrates robust bias-correction capability. Crucially, despite significant time-domain discrepancies in the initial FEM, it achieves high-fidelity reconstruction (average R2 > 0.9966) using less than 20% of the available real data. This approach provides a practical and robust pathway for integrating deep learning into structural health monitoring under realistic constraints of model imperfection and data scarcity.

title: 3D fusion meter: enabling accurate full-field 3D localization and displacement measurement with a fused radar-camera sensor
abstract: Achieving accurate, full-field, and contactless three-dimensional (3D) localization and displacement measurement remains a persistent challenge in vibration monitoring and engineering systems. Conventional vision-based systems suffer from limited depth accuracy, whereas radar-based approaches, although highly accurate along the line-of-sight, exhibit poor lateral measurement accuracy and typically require complex sensor networks to enable full-field 3D sensing. To thisend, we propose a unified heterogeneous sensing framework that fuses a millimeter-wave radar with a monocular camera, thereby creating a unique 3D Fusion Meter, which is capable of accurate full-field 3D localization and displacement measurement. To achieve accurate alignment between the heterogeneous sensors, a robust calibration framework based on joint pose optimization is first proposed. Subsequently, a composite target with pronounced microwave reflectivity and distinctive visual features is designed to support consistent cross-modal target perception and measurement. Building upon this target, a 3D localization method and a corresponding 3D displacement reconstruction algorithm are established to exploit the complementary measurement characteristics of microwave and vision sensing. Experimental validations conducted at both near and far ranges confirm that the proposed fusion-based measurement approach achieves accurate full-field 3D localization and high-fidelity 3D displacement reconstruction, providing a low-complexity, in-situ, and real-time solution for vibration analysis and structural health monitoring.

title: Interpretable multiple-sensor spectra fusion methodology for constructing dual-weight composite health indicator
abstract: Machine inevitably exhibits degradation characteristics during operation. Once machine degradation reaches a critical level, it may lead to a severe machine failure. To avoid any unexpected machine failure, Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) technology has been widely adopted, leveraging online sensor data for real-time performance monitoring and preventive maintenance. Performance degradation assessment serves as a foundation of the PHM; however, most existing studies primarily focus on single-sensor applications. The effectiveness of single-sensor modeling is highly dependent on the sensitivity of sensor data, and it is further influenced by factors such as sensor type, installation position, and environmental conditions. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a multiple-sensor spectra fusion methodology for constructing a dual-weight composite health indicator. The proposed model simultaneously incorporates frequency weights and sensor weights, optimizing both through a dual-weight optimization framework. A stepwise optimization strategy is introduced, breaking the optimization process into two manageable stages. Our proposed methodology was verified through two illustrative experiments using gearbox run-to-failure vibration data. Results demonstrate that optimized frequency and sensor weights align well with fault characteristics and sensor importance, confirming the physical interpretability of the optimization process.

title: A comprehensive benchmark analysis of the HUMS2025 data challenge dataset
abstract: The Defence Science and Technology Group (DSTG) conducted a Data Challenge at HUMS2025 focused on fault detection in helicopter gearboxes. The dataset was obtained from an endurance test of a retired Bell Kiowa 206B-1 main rotor gearbox at the DSTG Helicopter Transmission Test Facility. The test, intended to study gear tooth spalling from artificially inserted notches, produced a casing crack, allowing observation of its progression. The dataset spans 86 load cycles recorded between Day 3 and Day 22. Each cycle followed a repeated load profile of 100, 125, 150, and 125 percent rated load, with 20 min at each level. It includes 1830 pinion/bevel gear hunting-tooth synchronous signal averages (H-SSA) and 414 raw vibration files, each containing 30 s of high-sampled data across four vibration channels. This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark analysis of the this dataset, evaluating multiple signal processing methods for early fault detection, including cepstral editing (CE), power spectral density (PSD), singular spectrum analysis technique (SSAT), squared envelope analysis, and cyclostationary analysis. Two data representations were analysed: H-SSA and raw vibration signals. H-SSA averages vibration over repeated gear rotations to highlight periodic behavior. It showed limited sensitivity to the casing crack but captured the initiation phase of gear tooth spalling from the artificial notches at the later stage of casing crack propagation. CE, used to isolate transfer path effects, detected structural changes at the ring front sensor from Day 10, with clear deviation by Day 16. Raw vibration analysis provided earlier and clearer indicators. PSD revealed increasing energy trends under fault conditions. Under 125 percent loading, PSD-based features generated alerts between load cycles 65–69, while CE identified changes earlier between load cycles 62–65. Under 100 percent loading, CE triggered the earliest alert at File 54 (Day 8, Load Cycle 26) and an alarm at File 138 (Day 16, Load Cycle 62). SSAT captured long-term energy trends, while squared envelope analysis revealed modulation linked to crack breathing. Cyclostationary analysis at the planet pass frequency showed the most consistent performance, with alerts near load cycle 30 and alarms near load cycle 65. These results show that using multiple signal domains and advanced signal processing techniques improves early and reliable fault detection in helicopter casing structure.

title: Enabling impedance-mobility method into a matrix framework for vibration analysis of mechanical beam systems
abstract: Differing from the traditional mechanical impedance/mobility method for lumped-parameter model of discrete systems nor the four-pole substructure method that relies on a transfer matrix operation, an idea of mechanical impedance-mobility matrix is proposed for the vibration analysis of hybrid beam systems including mass-spring-damper elements. The free and forced steady-state vibration analyses of hybrid beam systems with serial-parallel branches can be significantly streamlined by developing a scheme of mobility matrix summation for serial beam chains and impedance matrix summation for parallel branches. Such an impedance-mobility matrix summation operation enabled by distributed mass separation and grounding simplifies the modeling of serial-parallel beam systems with rigid bodies and discrete elements, hence offers a straightforward way to decompose a complicated modeling task into quite easier steps. The local-to-global coordinate transformation formulation of impedance and mobility matrices for hybrid beams is derived, providing a new perspective in contrast to previous studies. Case studies of beam structures with eccentric rigid bodies and discrete elements, as well as a practical design of piezoelectric nanopositioner confirm the advantages of the proposed method, including a straightforward modeling process, easy of programming and reduced matrix order.

title: Physics-informed kernel mixtures for structural dynamics
abstract: The effective integration of physical prior knowledge and measured data is critical for developing robust physics-informed machine learning frameworks. Calibrating the balance between structured physical approximations and data-driven flexibility is a key challenge of model development, particularly when physical models are only valid within specific operational regimes. In such cases, a global reliance upon a physical approximation can lead to model misspecification. This paper introduces a physics-informed kernel mixture framework for Gaussian process regression, capable of dynamically varying the reliance upon available physical knowledge based on identifiable switching variables. This ensures that physical understanding is prioritised in valid regimes and relaxed in favour of flexible data-driven components elsewhere. Rather than relying on soft constraints or loss-based penalties, known physics is explicitly embedded within the construction of kernels, enforcing desirable properties within predictions (e.g. quadratic lift force, localised behaviours). This allows model structure to mimic available physical intuition in an interpretable manner. Furthermore, the framework incorporates regime-dependent heteroscedastic noise to accurately capture varying uncertainty across different operational states. The versatility of the physics-informed kernel mixture framework is demonstrated through two distinct engineering case studies: the aerodynamic directional loading of a long-span suspension bridge and the prediction of aircraft wing strain during in-flight manoeuvres. The proposed kernel structures improve predictive accuracy and extrapolation whilst recovering an interpretable representation of regime-dependent system behaviour.

title: Editorial Board
How localized nonlinear losses condition the acoustical design of a self-sustained oscillator: The clarinet and its register hole
abstract: The register tube marks the invention of the clarinet in the early eighteenth century, tripling the range of its ancestor, the chalumeau , and giving it the widest range among wind instruments. Opening this narrow tube causes the fundamental frequency of the played note to increase by a factor of three, from the first to the second register of the resonator. The geometry and location of the register hole condition not only this mode selection mechanism, but also the global tuning of the second register. However, existing self-sustained nonlinear models of reed instruments fail to predict whether a register transition can occur, limiting optimization of the register hole geometry. Here, we introduce a sparse self-oscillating clarinet model that includes localized nonlinear acoustic losses in the register hole. This nonlinear mechanism is shown to be necessary to reproduce register transitions observed experimentally. Using systematic exploration of the control and design parameter spaces, we identify combinations of register hole diameter, position, and chimney length that ensure reliable register transitions. We show that the competing demands of playability and tuning are only satisfied by a long and narrow tube. Our findings provide a predictive tool for instrument making, assisting manufacturers in refining clarinets as well as other reed instruments, including oboes, bassoons, and saxophones. • A sparse physical waveguide model predicts register transitions in the clarinet. • Nonlinear losses enable reliable register transitions. • Register hole geometry controls both playability and tuning. • Competing constraints explain the long and narrow clarinet register tube. • Alternative designs improve tuning when chromatic constraints are relaxed.

title: Data-driven predictive model and uncertainty analysis of vehicle-induced vibrations based on experimental measurements
abstract: Rapid urbanization has increased building construction near railway tracks, where ground vibrations induced by trains can damage structures and cause occupant discomfort, including headaches, nausea, and sleep disturbances. A number of different vibration comfort indicators were proposed for the assessment purposes, including the root mean square (RMS), vibration dose value (VDV), and maximum transient vibration value (MTVV). In order to better evaluate them, a multi-output chained gradient boosting model (MOC-GBM) is proposed in this paper, which adopts a strategy of integrating target variables into the input dataset and continuously updating the inputs during the predictions. Five locations across northern Poland were selected, and buildings with timber, steel, and reinforced concrete (RC) structural systems were investigated to compile a comprehensive dataset. They were used to evaluate the capability of MOC-GBM model. Then, two different locations were used to measure a new unseen dataset for general assessment of those predictive models. In the individual dataset, the proposed MOC-GBM model obtained accuracies of 98.2%, 99.2%, and 92.7% for predicting RMS, VDV, and MTVV, respectively. In addition, in mean value dataset, the proposed MOC-GBM model demonstrated very good predictive performance across all vibration comfort indicators with the accuracies of 99.4%, 99.7%, and 99.5% for predicting RMS, VDV, and MTVV, respectively, as well as the best fitted curve and promising results for curve fitting.

title: Impact excitation correction to improving frequency response function in structural flexibility identification
abstract: Flexibility reflects changes in structural stiffness and serves as a key parameter for evaluating structural safety. The integration of impact testing and experimental modal analysis has become a promising approach for acquiring structural flexibility in practice. In this process, the excitation signal serves as the sole reference for determining the scaling of the mode shapes, making it indispensable in flexibility identification. However, pulse excitation signals are characterized by short duration and broad frequency bandwidth, making them susceptible to distortion during measurement. This study proposed an improvement method for impact excitation signals to enhance flexibility identification accuracy. First, the mechanism by which pulse signal distortion affects flexibility identification was investigated. Second, three typical types of excitation signal distortions, including force spectral inconsistency, Gibbs phenomenon and baseline drift, were summarized. For the first two types, the relationship between data acquisition parameters and measurement error was quantitatively evaluated. Based on these findings, practical constraints for testing were proposed. For baseline drift, a pulse extraction method based on monotonicity change was proposed. An adaptive force window was developed to automatically remove trend noise and enable signal validity verification. The proposed method was validated through impact tests on a lumped-mass structure and a continuous girder bridge. The results indicated that processing hammer excitation signals is essential for reliable flexibility identification. The proposed adaptive force window effectively corrected the amplitude of the measured frequency response functions, thereby enhancing the accuracy of modal parameter and flexibility identification.

title: Microcrack damage characterization of aerospace ceramic bearings based on global feature stitching and illumination-balanced enhancement
abstract: There are problems of curvature variation and illumination imbalance in the damage characterization of aerospace ceramic bearings. An image processing method integrating global feature stitching and illumination-balanced enhancement is proposed. The method achieves parametric, accurate reconstruction of damage characteristics in aerospace ceramic bearings. A consistency verification mechanism removes mismatches. The method constructs the optimal homography matrix and cumulative cost function. Dynamic programming searches for the optimal stitching path and improves stitching quality. Customized structural elements perform illumination balancing. The nonlinear reflection characteristics of spherical bearings are considered. A nonlinear illumination variation compensation model is constructed. Adjacent reconstructed pixels are utilized. A compensation function is fitted. Accurate light correction is achieved. After enhancement, the average peak signal-to-noise ratio is 40.4245, and the average normalized coefficient is 0.9960. The method effectively eliminates the effects of curvature variation and illumination imbalance on accurate parametric reconstruction for damage characterization of aerospace ceramic bearings.

title: Multi-sensor anomaly detection using Scalograms and Kurtograms fusion on the Paderborn University dataset
abstract: Accurate and timely fault detection in rotating machinery is essential for industrial safety and operational efficiency. The predominant reliance on single-sensor systems, typically vibrationbased, limits insights into machinery health and is vulnerable to sensor-specific noise, malfunctions, and the challenge of subtle fault signatures in dynamic environments. Furthermore, traditional supervised classification methods struggle with unseen faults and data scarcity. This study overcomes these limitations by conducting a comprehensive evaluation of oneclass anomaly detection (AD) methods combined with multi-sensor feature fusion, using the Paderborn University bearing dataset, which includes synchronous vibration, current, and torque measurements. We systematically fuse sensor signals at the feature level, applying four AD algorithms: Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, Autoencoders (AE), and Variational AE, across 15 sensor combinations and three feature sets (scalogram, kurtogram, and merged). Results from 30,450 experiments per feature set and per AD algorithm demonstrate that merging scalograms and kurtograms features consistently enhances AD, with several multi-sensor combinations achieving F1 and AUC scores above 0.95. Sensor fusion amplifies these effects, and notably, merging features leads to substantial performance gains. By systematically evaluating every possible combination of sensor types across four AD algorithms and three feature sets, this study eliminates arbitrary fusion strategies and rigorously identifies the most effective sensor and feature integrations for machinery fault detection. These findings confirm that integrating complementary feature domains through multi-sensor fusion produces significantly improved, generalizable, and practical solutions for machinery health monitoring.

title: Adaptive wavelet-enhanced data-driven framework for surface quality prediction in ultra-precision manufacturing
abstract: Real-time surface roughness prediction is pivotal for enabling autonomous quality control in ultra-precision manufacturing, bridging the gap between process dynamics and product quality. However, the inherent non-stationarity of multi-source signals and harsh industrial noise pose significant challenges for existing predictive models. To address these limitations, this study presents a novel end-to-end data-driven framework that integrates differentiable parameterized Morlet wavelet encoding with deep spatiotemporal learning. Unlike traditional methods with fixed parameters, the proposed framework enables the adaptive learning of wavelet center frequency and scale via backpropagation, thereby providing a task-adaptive time–frequency representation for noisy sensor data. Validated on an ultra-precision lathe, the method achieves superior predictive performance with a coefficient of determination of 0.9715. Crucially, the framework demonstrates an ultra-low inference latency of 3.34 ms per sample, meeting the stringent real-time requirements of in-process monitoring on the investigated platform. This work provides an effective and computationally efficient framework for intelligent quality characterization under the investigated ultra-precision machining conditions, and offers a methodological basis for future validation in more complex manufacturing environments.

title: Theoretical and experimental investigations of a compact bistable triboelectric vibration energy harvester
abstract: Traditional energy harvesters struggle with inefficiency in low-frequency vibration energy harvesting and often feature bulky designs. To address these limitations, this study innovatively combines flexible beams and magnets to achieve negative stiffness, constructs a bistable structure, and proposes a compact bistable triboelectric energy harvester (CBTEH). This design minimizes mechanical connections while achieving bistability within a compact size. Leveraging the bistable mechanism, the CBTEH can transform small-amplitude and low-frequency vibrations into large-amplitude and high-velocity motion, thereby effectively converting low-frequency vibrations into electrical energy. The research begins with an introduction to the design concept and modeling of the CBTEH. Theoretical analyses of its mechanical behavior and electrical performance uncover the interaction between motion responses and electrical outputs. The impacts of key parameters on the CBTEH’s performance are also explored, revealing mechanism to boost energy-harvesting performance. A series of experiments are carried out to confirm the theoretical model’s precision, prove the prototype’s durability, and show its capability to drive low-power electronic devices. Notably, the CBTEH generates 0.50 mW of power at 12 Hz and 60 MΩ, and the corresponding power density is 0.926 W/m2. Through optimal parameter selection, the CBTEH can effectively improve energy-harvesting performance. Its ability to power micro-sensors highlights its potential in intelligent sensing.

title: Time-domain constrained mode decomposition via autoregressive model
abstract: Mode decomposition is a widely adopted data-driven strategy in modal analysis. It is an essential tool for identifying modal parameters and understanding the dynamic behavior of systems. However, existing mode decomposition methods often suffer from modal aliasing and lack clear physical interpretability. This study introduces a time-domain constrained mode decomposition method that employs a linear combination of free response signals to extract clean intrinsic mode functions and accurate modal parameters. A constraint matrix, derived from the autoregressive model of single-mode signals, is used to form a characteristic constraint equation and determine the decomposition coefficients. The influence of the autoregressive calculation time interval on the stability of Prony polynomial solutions is analyzed to determine the order and form of the constraint filter. Furthermore, combining the constraint filter with a low-pass FIR filter improves the noise robustness of the proposed method. For modal identification, the preliminary eigenvalues are determined using the Yule-Walker equation, followed by iterative elimination of spurious eigenvalues and refinement through the application of multi-objective constraint filters. Ultimately, the proposed method enables accurate, adaptive, and physically interpretable signal decomposition and modal parameter identification. Statistical results from numerical simulations validate its robustness to noise and stability, while comparisons with other mode decomposition techniques confirm that it achieves complete signal decomposition. Experimental verification using a frame test model further demonstrates the accuracy of the proposed method in modal identification.

title: Synthetic Complex-Frequency wave for SNR boost in rail EMAT testing
abstract: Railway safety and efficiency rely on real-time monitoring of rail conditions, yet magnetic losses and long propagation distances severely attenuate signals in electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT) guided-wave testing, leading to compromised detection accuracy. To address these issues, this study adapts complex-frequency wave technique (a multi-frequency excitation and synthesis method) to improve the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and amplitude of received ultrasonic guided waves. Based on actual frequency measurements, a complex-frequency synthetic wave is constructed, and a virtual gain is introduced to compensate for the magnetic loss in the rail. Both numerical and experimental studies were conducted on different segments of P60 rail. Compared with signals generated by traditional single-frequency excitation, the proposed method achieved an approximate 15 ∼ 25% increase in signal amplitude and 2 ∼ 3 dB improvement in SNR. These findings demonstrate the method’s potential for practical application in enhancing the performance of electromagnetic ultrasonic rail inspection.

title: An active feedforward headrest system using virtual sensing method based on auxiliary microphone and relative path
abstract: The virtual sensing (VS) method is designed to address the challenge of placing error microphones in the target zone of active noise control (ANC) systems, where direct placement is often impractical. The most commonly used virtual sensing methods can be broadly categorized into two types: the remote microphone technique (RMT-VS) and the auxiliary filter (AF-VS) method. The remote microphone technique estimates the error signal using remote microphones placed at a distance, while the auxiliary filter method retains the optimal filter for achieving maximum noise reduction and allows flexible filter adjustments according to different scenarios. However, when the acoustic paths change, the pre-established filters become invalid, and traditional virtual sensing methods are unable to effectively attenuate noise due to its inability to adapt to such variations. This paper proposes a novel auxiliary microphone and relative path based virtual sensing (AMRP-VS) method, which utilizes an auxiliary microphone positioned near the target zone to achieve noise attenuation. Meanwhile, it eliminates the impact of the secondary path on the modeling of the auxiliary filter in the AF-VS method. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that, under invariant acoustic paths, the proposed method can achieve the same noise reduction performance as traditional virtual sensing methods. Moreover, when acoustic paths vary, the proposed AMRP-VS method exhibits a certain degree of robustness. An active headrest system is built up to verify the effectiveness of the AMRP-VS method. Simulations and experiments show that the AMRP-VS method has superior performance in dealing with changing paths and noise situations.

title: A compact 3-DoF nonlinearity-tuning motif for multi-direction vibration isolation
abstract: This paper introduces a compact 3-DoF structural motif equipped with multiple nonlinear stiffness-tuning mechanisms, developed to address the need for broadband, high-performance vibration isolation in multi-degree-of-freedom (multi-DoF) mechanical systems for multi-direction vibration isolation or suppression. Two quantitative indicators for capturing the quality of nonlinear stiffness and quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) behavior are proposed to rigorously evaluate both static and dynamic characteristics. The proposed motif achieves precise global and local stiffness shaping in Z-translation, X-translation, and Y-rotation, and can therefore enable the construction of highly tailorable nonlinear restoring-force profiles. Dynamic analyses show that the integrated tuning mechanisms can effectively suppress complex nonlinear responses, including stiffness softening and internal resonances, and result in stable, broadband low-frequency isolation across all three DoFs. The high degree of tunability substantially enhances the feasibility of configuring multi-direction vibration-isolation platforms while maintaining predictable and identifiable dynamic behavior. Three prototyped platforms incorporating two, three, and four motifs are developed, experimentally validated, and benchmarked against established designs. The results consistently demonstrate exceptional adaptability, strong robustness to payload variation, and effective low-frequency isolation across all six DoFs. With these results, this work establishes a new tunable, nonlinear building block for multi-DoF vibration-isolation systems. The proposed 3-DoF motif is demonstrated to be a versatile and experimentally validated foundation with strong relevance to applications in vibration and noise control, structural dynamics, energy harvesting, and advanced robotic and mechatronic design, where multi-directional stiffness tuning is essentially demanded.

title: A quasi-zero stiffness dual-functional device based on magnet-piezoelectric cantilever beams for vibration isolation and energy harvesting
abstract: To address the challenges of low-frequency vibration isolation and energy harvesting in engineering environments, this study proposes a magnet-piezoelectric cantilever beam-based dual-functional quasi-zero stiffness vibration isolation and energy harvesting device (MQZSI-EH). The magnetic repulsive force between the cantilever-tip magnet and the platform-mounted magnet induces quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) characteristics, thereby reducing the isolation onset frequency while simultaneously enhancing the cantilever bending response under low-frequency excitation to improve energy harvesting performance. An electromechanical coupling model is established to investigate the effects of magnet spacing and cantilever length on the stiffness characteristics. The harmonic balance method is employed to analyze the influence of key parameters on vibration isolation and energy harvesting performance. Experimental results validate the theoretical predictions. Compared with a conventional linear isolator, the proposed device achieves an isolation onset frequency of approximately 7.45 Hz, representing a reduction of about 50%, along with a significant decrease in peak force transmissibility. Moreover, a maximum output power of approximately 0.6 mW is achieved under low-frequency excitation, which is about 350% higher than that of a cantilever-beam harvester. This study provides a new approach for low-frequency vibration isolation and energy harvesting.

title: A triple-magnet magnetic-suspension parallel nonlinear vibration absorber for low-frequency broadband vibration control
abstract: In the field of low-frequency vibration control, bistable nonlinear dynamic vibration absorbers (BNDVA) have demonstrated substantial application potential due to their inherent advantages arising from nonlinear dynamics. However, existing studies primarily focus on single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) configurations, whereas vibration-reduction studies on multi-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) nonlinear dynamic vibration absorbers, particularly for structures such as cantilever beams, remain comparatively limited and merit further in-depth investigation. This study proposes and designs a triple-magnet magnetic-suspension parallel nonlinear dynamic vibration absorber (TMSP-NDVA). By leveraging a bistable mechanism for low-frequency mitigation and a parallel MDOF architecture, the design enhances nonlinear energy absorption efficiency. An equivalent dynamic model of the TMSP-NDVA is first established, with the nonlinear magnetic forces of the triple-magnet configuration accurately characterized using the equivalent magnetic charge method. Subsequently, damping parameters are identified through transient vibration tests, followed by a dual-parameter synergistic optimization of magnet spacing and mass distribution using a genetic algorithm (GA). Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that under both transient and sinusoidal excitations, the proposed TMSP-NDVA achieves superior broadband, high-efficiency performance compared to conventional SDOF absorbers of equivalent total mass.

title: An evolutionary fusion framework with physics-informed and uncertainty-aware learning for tool wear prediction driven by milling force
abstract: In the context of intelligent manufacturing, achieving high-precision prediction of tool wear is crucial for enhancing manufacturing efficiency. However, this field currently faces three major challenges: the difficulty of directly measuring key physical quantities such as milling forces, the complexity of accurately interpreting process mechanisms, and the physical inconsistency and predictive uncertainty of purely data-driven models. To systematically address these issues, the objective of this research is to propose a novel paradigm that deeply integrates physical mechanisms with data-driven approaches. First, a multi-scale temporal convolutional network-frequency domain hybrid model (MSTCN-FD) is developed to achieve high-precision indirect perception of milling forces using easily measurable vibration signals. Secondly, a “physical wear value” is derived based on the physical relationship between force and wear, and embedded as a strong constraint into an ensemble learning physics-informed multi-source uncertainty-aware model (ELPI-MSUA). Thirdly, through a physics-guided loss function, data fitting and physical consistency are co-optimized, while uncertainties in the prediction process are quantified, thereby producing wear predictions with high accuracy and reliability. Finally, interpretability analysis methods are employed to reveal the physical basis of model decisions at the feature level. Experimental validation on two milling datasets under different working conditions shows that the wear prediction results achieve R2 values above 0.96, along with low RMSE and MAE values. The proposed framework not only accurately predicts milling forces and tool wear but also achieves deep closed-loop integration of physical mechanisms and data-driven approaches throughout the entire prediction process.

title: In-situ optical emission spectroscopy monitoring of laser powder bed fusion based on spectral data prior knowledge and feature-decision level fusion network
abstract: Porosity defects are common quality issues in Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) manufacturing. Optical emission spectroscopy (OES), a key technique that reflects the interaction between the laser and the material, has been widely used in laser processing monitoring. However, the spectral signals in the LPBF process are extremely weak and complex, and there is a lack of reliable OES monitoring approaches. To address these challenges, this study proposed an OES monitoring framework driven by spectral data prior knowledge. First, the spectral signals and plasma features of different porosity defects in the LPBF process were systematically analyzed, and the correlation between the process and spectral signals was explored, revealing the defect-related spectral features of both emission lines and the background continuous spectrum, along with their underlying physical mechanisms. Building on this, a physics-informed spectral signal-to-image mapping method was proposed, which converted high-dimensional spectral data into dual-channel spectral grayscale mapping images, thereby enhancing spectral features strongly correlated with defects. Finally, the MSI-FDFNet model was developed for in situ porosity monitoring during the LPBF process. Results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively extracts distinctive features from different spectral bands, achieving an accuracy of 95.51% in identifying multiple porosity defects, significantly outperforming models using only feature-level or decision-level fusion. Additionally, visualization analysis confirms that the model can adaptively focus on defect-sensitive key spectral band information, enabling reliable monitoring through multi-level fusion. This study highlights the potential of physics knowledge-driven OES monitoring for in-situ monitoring of the LPBF process.

title: Early multi-crack parameters identification of rotor systems based on an energy trajectory unbalance phase vector method
abstract: Rotating shafts are prone to multiple fatigue cracks under long-term cyclic loads and corrosive environments, threatening the operational safety of mechanical equipment. The coupling effects among cracks alter the time-varying stiffness of the rotor system, intensifying nonlinear dynamic responses and making the weak features of early cracks difficult to extract. Traditional methods based on superharmonic amplitudes fail to capture complex multi-crack interactions and exhibit limited sensitivity to early cracks. This study proposes an Energy Trajectory Unbalance Phase Vector (ETUPV) method for early multi-crack identification in rotor systems. First, a coupled multi-crack rotor Finite Element Model (FEM) is developed by incorporating additional flexibility from crack interactions. Then, energy trajectories are constructed by combining bending strain energy from the coupled stiffness matrix with vertical and horizontal vibration displacements. Subsequently, novel ETUPV features, comprising vector lengths and unbalance phase angles, are derived through three-dimensional vector parameterization of the energy trajectories. Finally, to overcome the limitations of surrogate models with fixed correlation structures, an Adaptive-Weight Kriging Model (AWKM) is developed using Random Forest-based correlation weighting and integrated with NSGA-III to identify the depths and positions of multiple cracks. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate identification accuracies of 96–98% and 89–93%, respectively, for cracks shallower than 0.2D. The proposed method exhibits superior robustness and significant potential for early multi-crack fault diagnosis in rotating machinery.

title: Evolutionary hypergraph: A Kalman-guided spatiotemporal dynamic hypergraph neural network for multi-sensor rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Modern multi-sensor systems generate high-dimensional, noise-contaminated, and dynamically evolving multivariate time-series data, in which complex spatiotemporal dependencies play a key role in accurate fault diagnosis. However, effectively modeling these high-order correlations remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Kalman-guided spatiotemporal dynamic hypergraph neural network(KSD-HGNN), which is designed to comprehensively characterize high-order relationships and dynamic evolution among multiple sensors. The framework first employs a learnable band-pass filter bank for adaptive frequency-domain feature extraction, and then constructs and optimizes a dynamic spatiotemporal hypergraph to jointly encode spatial adjacency and cross-step temporal dependencies. Furthermore, by integrating Kalman filtering into hypergraph convolution, the model performs temporal smoothing and state estimation over hyperedge sequences, yielding more stable spatiotemporal representations. Finally, the state dynamics learned by the Kalman-guided branch and the structural dynamics captured by the adaptive topology branch are fused via a gating mechanism, yielding a more stable and comprehensive system representation. Experimental results demonstrate that KSD-HGNN consistently outperforms existing methods under varying operating and noise conditions, significantly improving multi-sensor bearing fault diagnosis performance.

title: Prediction of dynamic behavior of a system undergoing an exchange of components using a transmission simulator method
abstract: In systems with modular design, it is of interest to perform component exchanges to upgrade components and explore new system configurations. If the dynamics of the components are known, then dynamic substructuring can be used to obtain a prediction of system performance for the new configuration. The transmission simulator method is a substructuring technique that utilizes an additional fixture to apply an elastic boundary condition to a test article such that an appropriate dynamic response can be obtained for a given substructuring application, and the technique has been used widely for performing coupling and decoupling operations. In this work, a modified transmission simulator method is proposed that allows a direct exchange of components to be performed. In a numerical demonstration, the proposed method is shown to accurately predict the dynamics of an assembly that has undergone a component exchange in which the exchanged components have different material properties and different geometric properties. This approach can be applied to dynamic qualification frameworks in which structures undergo modifications or upgrades rather than complete redesigns.

title: A graph lifting driven dynamic graph mode decomposition and fusion framework for bearing fault feature extraction
abstract: Complex operating conditions and harsh environments pose a serious threat to the health of critical components such as rolling bearings. In such settings, weak fault signatures are often buried in strong interferences. This makes fault feature extraction highly challenging. This paper proposes a graph lifting driven framework, termed Graph Lifting Driven Dynamic Graph Mode Decomposition and Graph Domain Fusion (GLDF), for bearing fault feature extraction. First, multichannel vibration signals are embedded into a rotation related graph structure. Graph lifting is then used to enhance the similarity and coherence of homologous impulses across channels. Dual graph domain representations are constructed, respectively from the perspectives of structural priors and data driven correlations. They are further fused to form a robust weighted graph. This fusion suppresses the propagation of random noise and non-fault impacts. Second, a dynamic graph mode decomposition scheme is developed to achieve adaptive component decoupling under time varying graph constraints. The extracted modes comply with both energy concentration and a graph prior that enforces structural consistency. Graph domain evaluation metrics are introduced to discriminate candidate modes. Finally, guided by node degree, graph modal fusion is performed, followed by envelope spectrum analysis. Comparative experiments show that the proposed method yields clearer characteristic spectral lines and more stable mode selection under various operating condition disturbances, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Graded diagnosis of gearbox scuffing faults based on multi-sensor heterogeneous data
abstract: To elucidate the thermomechanical response of spiral bevel gears under the coupled effects of temperature rise and scuffing failure, this study integrates heat transfer modeling, vibration signal analysis, and dynamic modeling. A gearbox thermal network model is first established, and steady-state temperature fields under various operating conditions are obtained using infrared thermography. Meanwhile, the gear body temperature is monitored in real time through a self-developed measurement system. The results demonstrate that frictional heat generated by tooth scuffing markedly increases both the gearbox surface temperature and the gear steady-state temperature. After the initial detection of abnormal temperatures in infrared images and gear body measurements, a second-stage diagnosis is performed. In this stage, a TimesNet model is applied to six-channel vibration acceleration signals to identify scuffing conditions, achieving a maximum classification accuracy of 95.3%. For the dynamic analysis, a temperature-dependent spiral bevel gear model is developed. As the gear temperature increases to 40 °C, 60 °C, and 80 °C, the mean dynamic transmission error (DTE) rises by 3.83%, 6.70%, and 13.4%, respectively, while the maximum DTE increases from 52.0 μm to 59.3 μm. The vibration acceleration amplitude also increases by 8.56%–29.7% with the temperature. Furthermore, the multimodal fusion results reveal strong complementarity between the temperature fields and vibration signals, and their combined use significantly enhances the accuracy of scuffing identification. These findings provide theoretical insights and technical support for understanding the thermomechanical mechanisms of scuffing and enabling early fault diagnosis in spiral bevel gears.

title: A bionic multimode piezoelectric actuator with switchable driving characteristics for high-performance micromanipulation
abstract: Developing a multimode piezoelectric actuator compatible with both direct-drive and stepping-drive mechanisms to meet the multidimensional requirements of complex micromanipulation tasks poses a significant challenge. In this study, a bionic design concept was adopted to propose a dual-output cooperative module (DOCM) with a single-input dual-output characteristic. Inspired by the synergistic mechanism of lizard locomotion, the module enables compact integration of direct-drive, crawling, and inertial-striding modes using only two PZT units. The structural design and motion characteristics of the DOCM were systematically analyzed, and the working principles and control strategies of the three driving modes were explained in detail. Finite element analysis was employed to optimize and validate the feasibility of the proposed module. A prototype was then constructed, and an experimental platform was established to comprehensively evaluate the output performance under different driving modes. The results demonstrated that the actuator achieved a maximum speed of 45.26 mm/s in the inertial-striding mode, a maximum output force of 9.17 N in the crawling mode, and a positioning accuracy of 3 nm in the direct-drive mode, respectively. Moreover, proof-of-concept demonstrations of chip decontamination and cell puncture are presented to illustrate the actuator’s potential for micromanipulation tasks.

title: Dual-functional parallel magnetic-piezoelectric nonlinear energy sinks via strong-modulation-informed optimization
abstract: • Parallel magnetic–piezoelectric NESs with two repulsive magnets are proposed. • A novel quantitative criterion is proposed to identify NES-induced SMRs. • A response-regime-based framework enables systematic NES parameter optimization. • Proposed parallel NESs outperform a benchmark single NES across regimes. • The proposed model, methodology and prototype are validated experimentally. The nonlinear energy sink (NES) has attracted increasing attention in vibration suppression and energy harvesting (VSAEH) due to its targeted energy transfer (TET) capability. The performances of NES-equipped structures, however, are highly sensitive to NES-induced response regimes—periodic, quasi-periodic, and strong modulated responses (SMRs). Despite this, quantitative SMR identification and regime-guided NES design methodologies remain underdeveloped. Moreover, multi-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) NESs, which are expected to provide richer energy dissipation pathways and enhanced harvesting potential compared with single-DOF designs, have received limited investigation for integrated VSAEH. To address these challenges, this study develops tunable parallel magnetic-piezoelectric NESs incorporating dual repulsive magnets (P-2RMPNESs) and establishes their coupled dynamic model with the primary structure. A novel SMR identification criterion is proposed and embedded into an optimization framework, enabling response-regime-based parametric optimization of both P-2RMPNESs and a benchmark single 2RMPNES. Simulation results show that the single 2RMPNES achieves effective VSAEH only under SMRs, whereas the P-2RMPNESs demonstrate excellent performance under quasi-periodic and periodic responses, and exhibit superior suppression under localized SMRs at high-amplitude excitations. The generalizability of the proposed SMR-based optimization framework is demonstrated via its extension to a tri-magnet configuration (3RMPNES), without modifying the optimization scheme. Experimental validation confirms the accuracy of the proposed model, criterion, and optimization method, demonstrating that the P-2RMPNESs outperform the 2RMPNES. Overall, this work establishes a response-classification-based framework for NES design and optimization, clarifies the link between NES-induced response regimes and system performances, and provides valuable guidance for developing multifunctional MDOF NESs that integrate VSAEH.

title: Investigation on skidding characteristics and dynamic responses of rolling element bearing under thermal elastohyrdodynamic lubrication
abstract: The unstable movement of the cage will lead to frequent collisions between rolling elements and cage, which inevitably results in wear and failure of the cage or the rolling element bearing. However, most studies assume that the rolling elements move under pure rolling conditions. Hence, this study abandons the assumption of pure rolling, and the thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication, cage flexibility and pocket clearance are considered to establish a multi-DOF skidding dynamic model of rolling element bearings based on time-varying comprehensive stiffness and damping. The intrinsic relationship between thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication and oil film thickness, contact damping, and stiffness is studied. Considering the viscous resistance and centrifugal force acting on the rolling elements, a flexible cage model is established, and the effects of pocket clearance, radial clearance, and the rolling element deformation on interaction force between the cage and rolling elements are analyzed. The influence of operational conditions and bearing parameters on skidding characteristics is explored, and the model is validated using an existing model and experiment. The results indicate that thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication has a significant impact on oil thickness, pressure, and temperature. The skidding speed and rate increase with the increase of the rotational speed, and decrease with the increase of the radial load. As the cage pocket clearance and equivalent stiffness increase, the skidding speed and rate are decreased. This study can provide support for the optimization design, friction reduction, and early failure prevention of rolling element bearings.

title: Accurate multi-scale displacement measurement with FMCW radar based on all-phase compensation method
abstract: Frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar has shown great advantages in non-contact displacement measurement and has been widely used to monitor small-scale motion displacement. However, the large-scale motion displacement beyond range resolution units can lead to significant errors and distortions, and the existing solutions have serious limitations. In this paper, an all-phase compensation (APC) method is proposed for the accurate multi-scale displacement measurement with FMCW radar. The approach leverages multiple sub-signals of the beat signal to construct the all-phase beat signal. Furtherly, the range unit where the target is located during the movement is tracked and the motion displacement is simultaneously extracted by interferometric phase evolution tracking. Through rigorous mathematical derivation, it is proved that the proposed method can effectively eliminate the phase jump caused by the target crossing range units and the phase shift caused by dynamic index tracking. Finally, simulations and experiments demonstrate its effectiveness and accuracy in extracting small-scale motion displacement within a fixed range resolution unit and large-scale motion displacement beyond multiple range resolution units, offering a promising approach for accurate multi-scale displacement measurement.

title: Size estimation approach for naturally extended bearing spall based on proximity probes
abstract: Bearing fault severity assessment is a key obstacle which lies between bearing diagnostics and prognostics. Most developed methods up to date are based on vibration, acoustic emission (AE), and instantaneous angular speed (IAS) signals, however, a recent study suggested that the relative displacement between bearing inner and outer race could better reveal the naturally extended spall size than the traditionally used signals. To validate this finding, a proximity probe-based approach is proposed in this paper, and it is tested on two different facilities: a small bearing rig, and a large multi-stage gearbox rig. This approach has the advantages of low signal processing requirement and intuitiveness, and it has been proven effective on both cases.

title: Spectrum- and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (SaPINNs) for input–state–parameter estimation in dynamic systems subjected to natural hazards-induced excitation
abstract: System identification under unknown external excitation is an inherently ill-posed problem, typically requiring additional knowledge or simplifying assumptions to enable reliable state and parameter estimation. The difficulty of the problem is further amplified in structural systems subjected to natural hazards such as earthquakes or windstorms, where responses are often highly transient, nonlinear, and spatially distributed. To address this challenge, we introduce Spectrum and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (SaPINNs) for efficient input--state--parameter estimation in systems under complex excitations characteristic of natural hazards. The proposed model enhances the neural network with governing physics of the system dynamics and incorporates spectral information of natural hazards by using empirically derived spectra as priors on the unknown excitations. This integration improves inference of unmeasured inputs, system states, and parameters without imposing restrictive assumptions on their dynamics. The performance of the proposed framework is demonstrated through comparative studies on both linear and nonlinear systems under various types of excitation, including the El Centro earthquake, where the seismic spectrum is assumed to be not precisely known. To account for predictive uncertainty, the proposed architecture is embedded within a Deep Ensemble (DEns) networks architecture, providing distributions over possible solutions. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms conventional PINNs, as the incorporation of spectral information introduces an inductive bias that guides the network more effectively through the solution space and enhances its ability to recover physically consistent state and parameter estimates with realistic uncertainty levels.

title: Remaining useful life prediction of complex equipment based on adaptive dual-branch multi-scale feature fusion model
abstract: Precise Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is critical for ensuring the reliability and operational efficiency of complex equipment. However, existing data-driven methods are often limited by their inability to capture multi-scale degradation dynamics or sustain performance under fluctuating operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an Adaptive Dual-Branch Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (ADB-MSF) framework. The architecture integrates a self-attention mechanism to elucidate inter-sensor correlations, followed by a multi-scale Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) that simultaneously captures transient anomalies and long-term degradation trends. A gated enhancement module is further incorporated to refine feature representations by highlighting informative features while suppressing irrelevant noise. Uniquely, the model features an adaptive dual-branch prediction module that dynamically activates the most appropriate prediction pathway based on the input degradation state, ensuring robustness in complex environments. Additionally, a weighted Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function is introduced to prioritize prediction accuracy near the critical end-of-life phase. Extensive experiments on stratospheric airship and C-MAPSS datasets confirm that ADB-MSF yields superior predictive performance compared to existing state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Experimental investigation of the vibration suppression performance of a polynomial stiffness nonlinear vibration absorber
abstract: This study mainly aims to experimentally validate the vibration suppression performance of a polynomial stiffness nonlinear vibration absorber (PNVA) with a sole stable equilibrium, which was recently proposed and investigated both theoretically and numerically by some of the authors. A PNVA prototype is physically implemented using linear coil springs arranged perpendicular to the motion of the PNVA and driven along tracks with a specified nonlinear profile. Tests on the stand-alone PNVA indicate that the implementation scheme enables accurate reproduction of the specified nonlinear stiffness. The results confirm that the PNVA’s response exhibits softening behavior at small amplitudes, which transitions to hardening behavior at higher amplitudes. An experimental investigation was conducted to evaluate the vibration suppression performance of the PNVA prototype, sequentially attached to a single-degree-of-freedom shear frame and a two-degree-of-freedom shear frame, under impulsive excitation and/or harmonic base excitation. The experimental results show good agreement with numerical simulations and theoretical predictions based on identified system parameters. The PNVA prototype demonstrates effective vibration suppression performance in both cases. Overall, this research provides a systematic experimental investigation of the PNVA and supports its potential for practical vibration suppression applications.

title: IAA-CRL: A universal information-adaptive augmentation based contrastive representation learning framework for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
abstract: Accurate degradation-state identification and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of rolling-element bearings are pivotal for predictive maintenance, yet these tasks are severely challenged by ambient noise, complex operating conditions, and the intrinsic non-linearity of the degradation process. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Introspective Adaptive Augmentation Contrastive Representation Learning (IAA-CRL) framework tailored for bearing RUL prognosis. IAA-CRL innovatively integrates contrastive learning with a dynamically optimized data-augmentation strategy. An augmentation selector is introduced to adaptively determine the optimal fusion of transformations from a physics-constrained candidate pool, ensuring that the generated samples preserve critical degradation semantics while maximizing diversity in a purely data-driven manner, without requiring prior domain knowledge for the fusion strategy. Furthermore, a multi-scale contrastive loss is devised to effectively fuse instance-level and timestamp-level features, thereby capturing discriminative degradation representations. The superiority of IAA-CRL has been empirically validated through comprehensive benchmarking on both the FEMTO-ST and XJTU-SY datasets. Compared with state-of-the-art methods (including CBHRL, USL, SimCLR, and SupCon) IAA-CRL yields significant improvements in prediction accuracy on the majority of bearing samples, demonstrating enhanced robustness and generalizability.

title: Unified dynamic compensation method for heterogeneous sensors under few-shot conditions
abstract: Minimizing dynamic errors in transient measurement systems via sensor dynamic compensation is critical for achieving high-precision testing. However, owing to significant disparities in the dynamic characteristics of different sensors, existing compensation models typically exhibit “one-to-one” specificity; consequently, current methods struggle to meet the requirements for the parallel compensation of heterogeneous sensors. Furthermore, the high cost associated with dynamic data acquisition results in limited availability of datasets within the field of dynamic testing. In this paper, a deep learning training architecture is redesigned based on meta-learning principles to achieve unified compensation for heterogeneous sensors under few-shot conditions. First, the Reptile algorithm is introduced to decompose the model training process for sensors of varying ranges into distinct tasks. Second, a single-type dynamic compensation task is constructed based on the Speech Enhancement Generative Adversarial Network. By treating multiple tasks as “training samples” at the secondary level, the meta-learner is updated through parallel learning to obtain a foundational model for the unified compensation of heterogeneous sensors. Finally, few-shot incremental learning is performed on unknown sensors to achieve specific adaptation of the dynamic compensation model for heterogeneous sensors. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can obtain a universal dynamic compensation model for heterogeneous sensors via pre-training on 8510C series pressure sensors. Furthermore, the time-domain and frequency-domain dynamic characteristics of three types of sensors — 8510B series pressure sensors, armored thermocouples, and strain force sensors — are significantly improved through few-shot incremental learning using only 5, 12, and 6 groups of samples, respectively. The proposed method enables high-precision, batch dynamic compensation for heterogeneous sensors within the field of distributed testing.

title: Stochastic dynamic substructuring: A frequency domain perspective
abstract: This paper presents a stochastic dynamic substructuring framework for coupling substructures subjected to stationary stochastic excitation in the frequency domain. A closed-form input–output relation is derived to directly compute the power spectral density (PSD) of the system response from the PSD of the excitation. The method leverages the isolated frequency response functions (FRFs) of individual subdomains and a viscoelastic coupling matrix to predict the stochastic response of the assembled system. Deterministic linear FRFs, which can be either numerically computed or experimentally measured at a limited number of degrees of freedom, are combined through the proposed substructuring formulation. This enables hybrid modeling, integrating experimental and numerical data from different components as well as allowing for parallel computation of subdomain responses. It also eliminates the need to reanalyze the full-order system in tasks such as model calibration or component redesign. The approach is validated through two case studies. The first involves a lumped parameter system subjected to white noise excitation. The second applies the method to a finite element model of an offshore wind turbine structure, where a transition piece connects the turbine to a monopile foundation under stochastic wave loading. Results confirm that the stochastic dynamic substructuring yields significant computational savings without compromising accuracy, compared to solving the full-order system, offering an efficient and scalable alternative for spectral analysis of coupled systems.

title: Study on multi-directional response control of floating offshore wind turbine using three-dimensional pounding tuned rotary mass damper
abstract: Offshore floating wind turbines (FOWT) are located in complex marine environments and will experience rigid body motion under the action of wind and wave loads. To reduce the impact of overall rotation of FOWT on upper structure, such as tower and blades, a three-dimensional pounding tuned rotary mass damper (3D-PTRMD) is proposed. Taking the Barge-type FOWT as an example, a numerical model of controlled FOWT was established using the Euler-Lagrange method to evaluate the performance of control device. According to previous research, a low-frequency 3D-PTRMD with large mass ratio is installed in platform to control the overall rotation of FOWT, while a high-frequency 3D-PTRMD is installed in nacelle to reduce tower vibration. The Bayesian optimization algorithm is employed to select relevant parameters for 3D-PTRMD. The calculation results showed that the optimal 3D-PTRMD could reduce pitch and tower fore-aft vibration responses by 40.18% and 30.8%, at the maximum. Considering the variation of wave loads, a multiple 3D-PTRMD device with different tuning frequency is established, and the control performance of it and 3D-PTRMD with single tuning frequency are compared. Moreover, the 3D-PTRMD still has a good control effect under different wind-wave angles, which shows that 3D-PTRMD has an extensive applicability.
keywords: Three-dimensional pounding tuned rotary mass damper

title: A biomechanics-informed nonlinear dynamic model for seated occupant exposed to vertical vibration and impact
abstract: Helicopter occupants are exposed to both acute injuries caused by crash impacts and long-term health problems associated with sustained vibration exposure. As the main structural interface between the occupant and the aircraft, helicopter seats play a key role in reducing impact loads to improve safety and in isolating vibrations to enhance comfort. Due to the high cost of physical testing, dynamic modeling has been widely used to lower experimental expenses and speed up the design optimization process. However, most existing dynamic models rely on equivalent damping approaches that fit experimental data to mathematical expressions, while overlooking the incorporation of fundamental biomechanical principles and mechanisms. Therefore, these empirical models are typically limited to single loading scenarios and do not provide the level of generalizability and robustness needed for application across different loading conditions. To address this limitation, a new biomechanics-informed nonlinear dynamic model is proposed, together with a systematic validation framework. First, the mechanical behaviors of intervertebral discs, ligaments, and muscles are incorporated into a single dynamic framework. In contrast to conventional approaches that depend on mathematical curve fitting, the nonlinear behavior of key soft tissues is derived from their physiological mechanisms and experimental tissue data, while the remaining phenomenological parameters are limited to physiologically reasonable ranges. This provides a well-defined physical foundation for the model parameters, improving both biological fidelity and interpretability. Second, unlike conventional validation approaches for dynamic models, a multi-level validation framework is introduced that spans a range of loading conditions to provide a more comprehensive assessment of the model’s validity. Finally, the proposed framework is compared with existing models, and a global sensitivity analysis is performed to capture interactions among parameters. The findings show that relative to current models, the proposed model achieves a 2.4% reduction in error in impact simulation cases. In vibration simulations, the proposed model more accurately predicts resonance frequencies and spectral peaks, with reduced errors compared to other models. In addition, the method preserves its generalizability across different loading conditions without the need for repeated parameter re-optimization, thereby addressing the limited adaptability commonly observed in traditional models. Consequently, this framework serves as an effective analytical tool for optimizing helicopter seat design and may also be extended to a wider range of engineering applications.

title: Enhancing performance of a spherical FIV piezoelectric energy harvester by tandem cube effects
abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoTs) has intensified the demand for sustainable energy solutions to power decentralized sensing nodes. Flow-induced vibration (FIV) of spherical structures offers a promising approach for energy harvesting. However, enhancing their response bandwidth and power output remains a significant challenge. This study proposes a novel Spherical Flow-induced Vibration Piezoelectric Energy Harvester (SFVPEH), featuring a fixed upstream interference cube and a vibrating downstream sphere mounted coaxially. The performance of the SFVPEH was systematically evaluated through experimental characterization and Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) simulations. Experimental results demonstrate that the upstream cube achieves effective flow field modulation, leading to a robust lock-in effect and significantly enhanced output. Specifically, at L = 0.5D and s = 0.1D, the lock-in range expanded from 1.91–2.52 m/s to 1.75–3.67 m/s, representing a 315% increase in bandwidth. Under the optimal matching (s = 0.2D, L = 0.5D), the RMS voltage reached 23.38 V, a 284% improvement over the standalone sphere.
