LBM simulations further confirm that the enhanced performance stems from highly coherent 3D vortex structures induced by the interferer. Finally, the SFVPEH successfully powered a wireless sensing node, demonstrating its practical viability for battery-free IoTs applications. This research provides a high-efficiency strategy for FIV energy harvesting in complex fluid environments.

title: A rotor-aligned multi-harmonic d-q-n model for efficient simulation of guide bearing faults in large-scale submersible pumps
abstract: The numerical simulation of guide bearing faults using the Modified Winding Function Approach (MWFA) becomes computationally prohibitive when modeling systems with numerous rotor loops, hindering its use in real-time applications. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a novel rotor-aligned multi-harmonic d-q-n model that significantly enhances computational efficiency while preserving accuracy for asymmetric air-gap faults. The method begins with the fault model in the abcs coordinate system, where the air-gap permeance and winding functions are expanded into trigonometric series. Key harmonic groups are then selected as basis functions according to the stator–rotor coupling criterion under air-gap asymmetry. A specifically designed rotor-aligned d-q-n transformation is applied to these harmonic bases, effectively reducing the dimensionality of the rotor loop matrix and alleviating the ill-conditioning issues inherent in traditional flux- or current-method solutions. The simplified electrical dynamic equations in the d-q-n reference frame are solved, and the resulting currents are inversely transformed to reconstruct the stator current signals. A key innovation is the tunable trade-off between simulation speed and fidelity, achieved by adjusting the harmonic basis set. Simulation results demonstrate a >7x speedup compared to the full-order MWFA model while accurately capturing fault signatures like half-frequency whirl. Experimental case studies further validate the model’s effectiveness under realistic industrial noise, confirming its potential for efficient fault simulation and real-time monitoring.

title: A dual-stage framework for industrial fault diagnosis under domain shift via enhanced voiceprint representation and hierarchical ensemble learning
abstract: While existing acoustic-based fault detection and diagnosis (AFDD) methods have achieved notable success, their performance in real industrial environments remains constrained by domain shifts, scarce fault samples, and limited computational resources. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight dual-stage framework that integrates enhanced voiceprint representation with hierarchical ensemble learning to achieve robust AFDD. First, an adaptive time–frequency feature modeling module is developed to construct enhanced local voiceprint representations from Mel spectrograms, effectively extracting fault-related acoustic patterns with improved discrimination and robustness under noisy and dynamic operating conditions. Second, a hierarchical ensemble learning strategy that integrates CatBoost, XGBoost, and logistic regression is designed to progressively refine the decision boundaries in the extracted feature space, thereby enhancing multi-level feature utilization, diagnostic stability, and decision process interpretability across different domains. Finally, extensive experiments on the DCASE 2022 Task 2 benchmark and a real-world power transformer dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability compared to state-of-the-art AFDD approaches. Especially in various noise scenarios, the average diagnostic accuracy of the power transformer is improved by nearly 10%.

title: Adaptive neural network control for ship-to-ship crane systems with dead-zone nonlinearity and actuator saturation
abstract: Ship-to-ship crane system plays a crucial role in offshore material transfer in modern maritime engineering. As a typical underactuated nonlinear system, the ship-to-ship crane system is subject to multiple challenges, including hull-coupling disturbances induced by ocean waves, parameter uncertainties, actuator dead-zone nonlinearity, and saturation constraints, all of which severely degrade positioning accuracy and swing suppression performance. To address these issues, an adaptive neural network control strategy is proposed in this paper. A smooth approximation function is employed to model actuator saturation, thereby avoiding potential instability and simplifying the controller design. A radial basis function neural network is applied to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics arising from system uncertainties and external disturbances, while an adaptive law is developed to compensate for the approximation errors and unknown parameters. By integrating the proposed adaptive mechanism, rapid swing elimination and accurate payload positioning are achieved simultaneously. Rigorous stability analysis based on Lyapunov theory and Barbalat’s lemma proves the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Finally, experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control scheme.

title: Visual sound recovery from flexural vibrations: A cost-effective approach using a line-scan camera
abstract: Vision-based approaches for sound acquisition have become a rapidly advancing area in recent years. This research presents a cost-effective method for capturing audio by using line-scan camera to detect flexural vibrations of object surfaces induced by nearby sound sources, and to reconstruct the original audio signal from the recorded videos using image-processing techniques. The proposed approach leverages a Laplacian image decomposition technique and a phase-based motion extraction algorithm using Hilbert transform. Compared to conventional methods that rely on high-speed area-scan cameras and complex steerable pyramid algorithms, the proposed approach uses a more affordable camera and a less complex algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, showing strong performance across multiple evaluation metrics, while exhibiting a lower SI-SNR compared to conventional approaches. These findings highlight the proposed visual approach as a cost-effective and less complex alternative to other non-contact vibrometry systems, with the ability to detect surface vibrations in the nanometer to micrometer range. While audio capture is demonstrated here as one application, the capability also shows significant potential in broader areas such as structural vibration analysis, nondestructive material testing, and other mechanical measurements.

title: Generative adversarial networks for high frequency ultrasonic field modelling near fluid-solid interfaces
abstract: The propagation of high frequency ultrasonic waves enables the detection of fine inclusions and cracks in solid media, often induced by fatigue or impact loads. Accurate modelling of high frequency wavefields significantly enhances the ability of structural health monitoring systems to detect fatigue cracks and localize stress concentrations near defects within solid plates. Numerical solvers, such as the Finite Element Method (FEM), require fine meshing of the problem geometry, whereas semi-analytical modelling, such as the Distributed Point Source Method (DPSM), demand large number of distributed point sources to accurately model high frequency ultrasonic fields, resulting in significant computational overhead. However, such computational constraints limit their applicability in real-time or large-scale monitoring systems. To address these challenges, we propose a surrogate model for expensive numerical solvers (FEM/DPSM) to efficiently predict high frequency ultrasonic wavefields in isotropic solids coupled with a fluid medium. A conditional generative adversarial network (cGANs), based on the Pix2Pix architecture, which features a U-Net as a generator and a PatchGAN as a discriminator is employed for training. Multiple tailored loss functions, including frequency, edge, perceptual, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) based losses are included within total generator loss to ensure physical accuracy and structural fidelity. The Pix2Pix model is trained on paired low- and high-frequency wavefield data encompassing both healthy and damaged configurations with a circular hole in the solid half-space. For both cases, the trained model demonstrates excellent predictive performance for generating high frequency wavefield, with SSIM values for displacement and normal stresses consistently exceeding 0.85.

title: Online identification of unbalance load in rotor-bearing systems by integrating Vold-Kalman and augmented Kalman filters
abstract: To address the decline in unbalance identification accuracy of rotor-bearing systems under strong noise interference, speed fluctuations, multi-order signal coupling, and sudden unbalance changes, this paper proposes an online identification method that integrates Vold-Kalman filter (VKF) with augmented Kalman filter (AKF). First, a finite element model of the rotor system is established and transformed into a state space, where the unbalance is introduced as an augmented state variable, and recursive online estimation of the unbalance is achieved using the AKF. Second, to improve the identification accuracy, VKF is used to extract synchronous order components from the vibration response, effectively suppressing noise and non-target orders and thereby providing observation inputs that are highly correlated with unbalance excitation for the AKF. The proposed VKF-AKF integrated method enables accurate online identification of rotor unbalance. Both simulations and experimental results demonstrate that the method can reliably estimate unbalance parameters and remains effective under non-stationary operating conditions such as low signal-to-noise, variable speeds, speed fluctuations, and sudden unbalance changes, providing an effective online solution for condition monitoring and dynamic balancing of rotating machinery.

title: Interlaminar shear stress continuity and transient stress constrained topology optimization of piezoelectric structures under active vibration control
abstract: Piezoelectric materials are widely used in active vibration control due to their high sensitivity and self-sensing capability. However, despite these advantages, piezoelectric materials remain at risk of failure in practical engineering applications because of their brittle nature, whether under combined mechanical–electrical loads or either type of load alone. To address this issue, this paper proposes a topology optimization method for active vibration control of piezoelectric structures with stress constraints. Self-sensing piezoelectric materials are employed to avoid numerical problems caused by the asymmetry of the equivalent damping matrix in active control. Meanwhile, considering that the conventional equivalent single-layer approach leads to interlayer shear stress discontinuity, a finite element model that inherently satisfies stress continuity is adopted in this work. Moreover, a stress relaxation parameter is introduced and adjusted to ensure stress continuity throughout the optimization process. In the optimization problem, the nested p-norm method is employed to approximate the maximum stress, while the sum of squared displacements at discrete target points over each time interval serves as the objective function. An adjoint-variable sensitivity analysis scheme is developed to compute sensitivity analysis of both the objective function and the constraints. Finally, numerical examples are presented to investigate the influence of various parameters on the optimization results. The results demonstrate that stress constraints are crucial for the design of piezoelectric composite structures, and this approach effectively reduces the risk of excessive stress and fracture.

title: Federated RUL prediction for bearings under multiple failure modes using connectivity evolution of spectral connected graphs
abstract: Reliable degradation trajectories and failure thresholds are essential for accurate bearing remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. However, variations in installation and fault types induce multiple failure modes that severely limit prediction accuracy. This study focuses on developing mode-specific bearing degradation trajectories and failure thresholds using a spectral-feature degradation connected graph. The method aims to automatically determine the degradation starting point, degradation trajectory, and failure threshold without predefined thresholds, enabling reliable RUL prediction under varying failure modes. The degradation features of different failure modes are characterized using envelope-spectrum connected graphs, and a nonlinear hyperplane is adaptively learned from spectral-distribution differences to identify the degradation starting point. On this basis, a degradation connectivity graph is established to describe real-time degradation evolution across multiple failure modes, with the connectivity induced by graph-topology evolution serving as the degradation-trajectory indicator. The failure threshold is then automatically determined when the connected graph splits into disconnected components and its connectivity approaches zero. During federated training, monotonic connectivity decrease and spectral-feature energy increase are imposed as physical-consistency constraints, and a federated degradation scale library is established to provide online bearings with more reliable and flexible RUL estimate values under multiple failure modes. Benchmark dataset validation shows that the proposed method improves RUL prediction accuracy by 26.04% across multiple failure modes, compared with state-of-the-art methods. The NIO real-world dataset further demonstrates an advanced RUL prediction interval ranging from 4.4 to 7.3 days.

title: In-plane perpendicular oscillation-driven friction modulation for backward motion suppression in stick–slip piezoelectric actuators
abstract: Stick–slip piezoelectric actuators are promising for cross-scale precision positioning but inherently suffer from backward motion especially at low-frequency, as friction acts as a driving force in the stick phase and a resistance in the slip phase, thereby degrading positioning accuracy. Effective modulation of friction is therefore critical for suppressing backward motion. In-plane perpendicular oscillation (IPO)–assisted friction modulation is an attractive active control approach due to its broad frequency applicability and structural simplicity. However, its integration with stick–slip driving strategies remains insufficiently established, and the mechanism by which IPO suppresses backward motion during the slip phase is not fully understood. To address this issue, this study proposes a slip-phase-oriented IPO strategy that actively modulates friction by reorienting the relative velocity vector, thereby reducing its component along the driving direction and suppressing backward motion. A nonlinear dynamic model is developed to elucidate the underlying mechanism and to analyze the effects of waveform, amplitude, frequency, and phase. Simulations and experimental validation on a mechanically decoupled two-axis stator prototype demonstrate improved motion linearity over a broad frequency range. Its robustness is further demonstrated through load capacity tests, wear characterization, and simulations under different contact materials, confirming its effectiveness and practical potential.

title: A Grating-Angle-Positioning method for dynamic clearance measurement of rotating blades
abstract: To address the common problem of repeatable pose recognition and dynamic clearance measurement in multi-body relative motion of complex rotating machinery, this study proposes a grating-angle-positioning method for dynamic clearance measurement. This method collaboratively attaches gratings on the relative motion components and innovatively uses the grating direction angle as a spatiotemporal positioning signal to lock the repeatable meshing position from a continuous image sequence and calculate the dynamic clearance variation. Its core contribution lies in achieving precise identification of repetitive measurement positions and stable extraction of relative gap changes in complex periodic motions. To validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, it was applied to the dynamic gap measurement of a challenging dual-rotor vertical kneader, where repeatable meshing positions were accurately located with an angular error of less than 0.05°, and clearance variation sequences at the blade meshing point over 11 operating cycles were obtained. An independent verification experiment further confirmed that this method still has high measurement accuracy under non-ideal oblique imaging conditions, with an error of less than 0.02 mm. The results show that the proposed method can achieve sub-angle repetitive pose recognition and sub-millimeter dynamic gap monitoring, providing a non-contact, full-field measurement method for the state monitoring of complex rotating machinery such as vertical kneaders.

title: Model-data integration and visual transfer for small sample intelligent fault diagnosis of spindle thrust bearing
abstract: The demand for condition monitoring and stable operation of high-precision equipment such as machine tools has promoted the optimization of maintenance strategies. However, the traditional equipment signal acquisition and intelligent diagnosis framework faces double limitations, that is, the scarcity of historical bearing fault data seriously affects the accuracy of the diagnosis model based on deep learning, and the contact vibration measurement method is difficult to cope with the layout requirements of complex industrial environments. For this reason, an intelligent diagnosis workflow of model-data integration and visual transfer is proposed for the raceway fault of thrust bearing of machine tool spindle. Firstly, the dynamic model of four-degree-of-freedom contact bearing is established to generate displacement simulation data with rich characteristics. Secondly, a sub-pixel visual vibration measurement method is proposed to collect the displacement signal of real equipment operation. Finally, the dynamic simulation data is migrated to the visual displacement data diagnosis. To address the inherent limitations of simulated signals and the instability in model accuracy caused by domain shifts, we propose a Mutual Information − Domain Adversarial Network. By incorporating the key principles of minimal-redundancy-maximal-relevance from information theory, this approach significantly enhances the robustness and accuracy of domain adaptation tasks. The effectiveness of the proposed method and diagnostic workflow is validated and analyzed through six simulation-to-reality transfer tasks. Results demonstrate that the intelligent diagnostic framework based on model-data integration and visual transfer effectively addresses the under-sampling problem and improves fault diagnosis accuracy.

title: UNFIT monitoring of roller bearing degradation: A new event-based concept for early defect detection
abstract: Rolling element bearings (REBs) perform a fundamental role in rotating machinery, with accurate and robust knowledge of their health state, as well as prognostics for remaining useful life (RUL) being critical to optimising maintenance strategies. A key challenge to such health indication lies in reducing defect detection latency (DDL): the time between the onset of an incipient defect and its identification. Existing trend-based signal processing approaches employ various forms of temporal and spectral analysis to identify characteristic defect frequencies of the REBs but are often limited by their reliance on monotonic trend evolution, retrospectively recognising defect onset once the trend has developed sufficiently. This study introduces a novel event-based approach; the UNFIT (contracted from Unstable Negentropy Fluctuations with Indication Trace) methodology for early defect monitoring and detection, which extends prior research on informational entropic change as a means of detecting impulsive signals and proposes an alternative to traditional trend-based techniques. The proposed method applies a spectral-temporal assessment that both emphasises and characterises impulsive events shown to ultimately lead to failure, and does so at the point of defect emergence rather than retrospectively, thereby theoretically minimising the DDL. The methodology is validated using the industry-recognised IMS dataset published by NASA, providing fault detection results across all three (3) accelerated run-to-failure tests and benchmarking them against fault detections reported in existing signal-processing literature for trend-based methodologies. Supplementary datasets from XJTU-SY and Ferrara are presented for further comparison, with further investigation required to confirm robustness under noisy operating conditions. Results from a subset of test cases demonstrate that the UNFIT methodology can reduce DDL and enhance defect identification, particularly in cases where conventional trend-based indicators are less effective, thereby improving maintenance optimisation and supporting Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) workflows by providing earlier, actionable diagnostic information, amenable to integration within Digital twin and Industry 4.0 predictive maintenance frameworks.

title: An interpretable adaptive denoising convolutional network for intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: Deep learning has achieved significant success in intelligent fault diagnosis owing to its powerful nonlinear mapping capabilities. However, the lack of interpretability of deep learning-based fault diagnosis methods with black-box characteristics has seriously hindered their widespread industrial application. To address this issue, an interpretable adaptive denoising convolutional network (IADC-Net) is proposed for intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery in this paper, which constructs a comprehensive interpretability framework. In this method, the interpretable signal processing layer is driven by adaptive fusion denoising wavelet convolution (AFDWC) module, enhancing the model’s generalization capabilities in various scenarios. The AFDWC integrated with multiple wavelet basis kernel can capture abundant multi-scale mechanical fault information. The adaptive soft threshold denoising (ASTD) dynamically removes noise interference on channel features, and the energy-entropy ratio channel weighting adaptively highlights frequency bands more relevant to faults. Then, the interpretable feature extraction layer leverages the sparse interaction characteristics of traditional convolutions to elucidate its intrinsic mathematical implications through sparse representation, which is of great significance to the engineering applications of various convolutional networks. And, the interpretable result analysis layer visualizes the model results with attention weight and output features to help users understand the decision process and trust diagnosis results. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified and analyzed by the public fault datasets and the industrial robot experimental platform, demonstrating the interpretability of model, the rationality of network structure and the superiority of diagnostic performance. The code library is available at: https://github.com/GTH25/IADC-Net.

title: Development and experimental verification of the aviation High-Speed gear traveling wave resonance measurement monitoring system and calibration system
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the conventional vibration and stress measurement methods are difficult to monitor the traveling wave resonance (TWR) characteristics of the aviation high-speed gears under extremely complex working conditions. In this paper, the gear TWR measurement and monitoring system based on the derived noise measurement method based on the principle of pipeline sound transmission is developed, and the microphone dynamic characteristic calibration system based on the principle of substitution method is developed. The standing wave effect is eliminated by designing a non-reflective terminal attenuator tube, and the acoustic attenuation of acoustic waveguides with different lengths in the whole frequency band is obtained by using the method of dynamic calibration of the whole frequency band of the system to realize the accurate correction of the measurement data. The results show that in the laboratory environment, the error between the measurement results of the monitoring system and the reference microphone is not more than ± 1 dB in the frequency range of 30 Hz ∼ 13 kHz, which verifies that the developed system has high measurement accuracy. Meanwhile, the experiment of TWR characteristics of aero-engine central drive driven bevel gear further verifies that the system can accurately identify and effectively monitor the TWR frequency and resonance speed of gear under actual working conditions.

title: Measuring full-field vibration and dynamic deformation using single time-gated camera stereo-digital image correlation
abstract: Quantitative measurement of full-field vibration and dynamic deformation is essential for characterizing the mechanical properties of materials and the dynamic behavior of structures, as well as validating numerical models under dynamic loading. However, capturing high-speed transient events typically faces challenges regarding motion blur and high hardware costs. This study proposes a novel transient deformation measurement method by combining a time-gated imaging technique with single-camera split-screen stereo-digital image correlation (stereo-DIC). The proposed system employs a time-gated CMOS camera featuring nanosecond-scale ultra-short exposures, synchronized with a pulsed laser source, to effectively freeze the motion of high-speed objects and eliminate motion blur. To achieve cost-effective stereo imaging, a four-mirror adapter is adopted to capture binocular views on a single sensor. The established single time-gated camera stereo-DIC (STG stereo-DIC) system was validated through vibration response measurements of a cantilever aluminum plate and full-field deformation analysis of a rotating fan. Experimental results demonstrate that the first three natural frequencies and mode shapes of the plate agree closely with those obtained from conventional high-speed DIC and finite element analysis. Furthermore, the system accurately captured the surface 3D deformation fields of fan blades at various rotational speeds. This work not only introduces a novel technical route for vibration and high-speed deformation measurement but also highlights its strong potential for applications involving objects subjected to both high temperatures and high rotational speeds, such as aero-engine turbine blades.

title: A hybrid active–passive control strategy of zero-stiffness vibration isolation integrated with energy harvesting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new hybrid active–passive absolute-zero-stiffness vibration isolator (HAZSVI) that achieves long-stroke, full-band vibration isolation under large-displacement excitations with minimal power demand. The key innovation is a feedforward–feedback hybrid control (FFHC) framework that flattens the static restoring force of a quad-stable magnetic negative-stiffness mechanism (MNSM) to establish a practical AZS condition, while reserving feedback control solely for disturbance rejection and uncertainty compensation. The MNSM is modeled using the filament method and validated by finite-element simulations, enabling systematic tuning of air–gap parameters to realize a quad-stable force–displacement relation with seven equilibrium points and an extended quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) region in a compact configuration. A high-order nonlinear dynamic model and incremental harmonic balance analysis further reveal the regime transition of the quad-stable response and explain the loss of isolation robustness in purely passive operation under large displacements. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed HAZSVI system eliminates resonance amplification and maintains robust full-band isolation, with transmissibility consistently suppressed below − 10 dB even at a base-excitation amplitude of 4.5 mm. Owing to the static compensation mechanism, the control effort remains low, and the maximum average power consumption of the fuzzy PID-based FFHC is only 0.77 W and 1.67 W under 3 mm and 4.5 mm excitations, respectively. A metric-based benchmarking against representative isolators further confirms the superior scalability of the proposed architecture toward compact, high-load, and large-stroke isolation scenarios. The proposed framework redefines multi-stability as a static resource that can be actively reshaped, offering both theoretical insight and engineering feasibility for energy- and weight-constrained precision platforms.

title: Towards trustworthy milling chatter detection via physics-assisted feature extraction and stacking-based decision-level fusion
abstract: Chatter is an instability phenomenon in the milling process that may adversely affect surface quality and machining efficiency. To achieve high-performance machining, online chatter detection is of critical importance in mechanical manufacturing. However, existing methods primarily rely on signal processing techniques and single classifiers, which limits their interpretability and generalization capability, thereby resulting in untrustworthy detection results under variable cutting conditions. To deal with this limitation, this paper proposes a milling chatter detection method via physics-assisted feature extraction and stacking-based decision-level fusion. First, a physics-assisted feature extraction method is proposed to extract interpretable and discriminative features by modeling dynamic milling forces and characterizing the chatter evolution mechanism. Then, multiple deep learning-based classifiers are constructed as base models, including a convolutional neural network, a residual network, an Inception network, a capsule network, and a dilated convolutional network. Subsequently, a stacking ensemble learning based on XGBoost is designed to perform decision-level fusion of the outputs from these base models. Milling experiments are conducted to construct a dataset under different cutting conditions, and cross-validation is employed to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

title: A novel frictional contact correction transfer matrix method for bolted vibration systems: modeling, simulation, and experimental validation
abstract: Bolted connections are widely employed in clamps and flanges for vibration control in aerospace and marine systems. However, the imperfect interfaces of bolted connections hinder accurate dynamic evaluation and degrade computational efficiency. To overcome these limitations, a novel frictional contact correction transfer matrix method is proposed. Unlike the traditional transfer matrix method (TMM), which assumes a perfectly rigid connection, this model incorporates a frictional contact correction that iteratively accounts for the relationship between the shear forces of the bolted connection components. In addition, the generalized transfer matrix of elastic beam elements with arbitrary input/output locations is derived, enabling modular assembly of complex connection structures. To validate the proposed method, three bolted connection vibration systems are constructed and finite element simulations with improved friction contact correction are conducted. In addition, three bolted vibration systems were experimentally investigated, and the results of other TMM variants were compared with those of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves computational efficiency over 100 times greater than finite element simulations, with accuracy comparable to finite element simulations for the first mode. For the second mode, prediction error increases significantly. Specifically, the method significantly improves computational accuracy compared to other TMM variants, albeit with modestly increased computational cost relative to the other TMM variants. The method provides a concise modeling framework with high computational efficiency, serving as an effective theoretical tool for vibration control and identification within its validated scope.

title: PI-DSTHP: A Physics-Informed dynamic symplectic tracking and Hamiltonian projection framework for roller bearing RUL prediction under multi-source noise interference
abstract: Accurate Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction for roller bearing is severely hindered by static decomposition and multi-source noise interference, which often lead to mode mixing and feature fractures during long-term service. To address these bottlenecks, this paper proposes a novel Physics-Informed Dynamic Symplectic Tracking and Hamiltonian Projection (PI-DSTHP) framework. First, a dynamic symplectic tracking model is developed to continuously track physical mode identities via Hamiltonian minimum action path optimization, fundamentally eliminating mode mixing and ensuring continuous feature evolution across the full lifecycle. Second, an asynchronous Hamiltonian defense mechanism driven by Hamiltonian intrinsic momentum gliding is constructed, which isolates noise into independent phase-space orbits to adaptively bypass and restore distorted signal regions via physical inertia. Finally, the Hamiltonian energy trajectory projection model transforms RUL evaluation into a deterministic geometric intersection problem within the phase space, which can utilize the relative energy expansion effect to quantify system degradation and enable robust cross-domain prediction without target-domain priors. Experimental validation on two full-lifecycle roller bearing datasets demonstrates the significant superiority of the PI-DSTHP model in continuous degradation tracking and prognostic accuracy, offering full-chain physical interpretability from symplectic geometry to final life extrapolation.

title: Study on real-time prediction for porosity in laser melting based on a digital twin-driven deep learning framework
abstract: The keyhole-induced pore defect is recognized as a major nuisance in laser melting (such as welding and 3D printing). As a crucial indicator for assessing the specific severity of pores, porosity has long been obtained only through complex and offline internal inspection after manufacturing. In this paper, guided by the formation mechanism of pores revealed via numerical simulation, a digital twin-driven deep learning framework (DTDLF) is proposed that enables direct and real-time porosity prediction during laser beam welding. In the perception field, keyhole depth and keyhole opening circumference are acquired through multi-sensing measurement and signal processing. In the physical field, simulation can acquire maximum temperature on the bottom wall of the keyhole. Subsequently, a sparse auto-encoder is constructed to fuse the original fluctuation characteristics mined from their respective digital twin data sources, and all of the obtained overall features are demonstrated to be highly correlated with porosity. In the DTDLF, a tandem structure of two deep neural networks (DNNs) connected in series is adopted, where the former DNN conducts online prediction of the fused overall feature in the physical field utilizing process parameters to circumvent the long simulation runtime, and the latter DNN couples all the fused overall features in the perception-physics fields for predicting porosity online. The final results indicate that the DTDLF has a significant accuracy advantage over monitoring frameworks that use solely single-field information, and meanwhile its real-time performance is not compromised.

title: Compact spatial phase-shifting quadrature detection for nanometer displacement measurement
abstract: Conventional phase-shifting detection system enables compact quadrature signal acquisition; however, it suffers from severe sensitivity to angular perturbations induced by spatial positional shifts of non-collinear beams. Here, we present a robust spatial phase-shifting interference detection method using spatial interference fringes and a dual-detector configuration arranged along the fringe normal direction. A physical model for quadrature signal acquisition is established, in which the robustness is quantitatively characterized by the ratio of the projected fringe periods along the detector axis before and after angular perturbation. The analysis demonstrates that under a specific homologous angular perturbation of 0.005°, the relative deviation of the longitudinal fringe interference geometric configuration is 3 × 107 times that of the optimized transverse fringe interference geometric configuration. The optimized transverse fringe interference geometric configuration can maintain the ratio at a level extremely close to 1, thereby ensuring stable phase matching and signal orthogonality. The proposed method is applied to a grating interferometer and validated through simulations and experiments. The optimized system achieves a maximum residual error of 21.29 nm and a maximum standard deviation of 12.71 nm over a 300 µm measurement range, demonstrating enhanced robustness and suitability for compact grating interferometric displacement measurement system.

title: A novel experimental methodology for the calculation of mesh stiffness in straight bevel gear systems using precision angle measurement
abstract: Mesh stiffness strongly influences the vibration and dynamic response of straight bevel gear (SBG) systems; however, existing analytical methods show limited accuracy and high computational complexity under cracked conditions. Previous experimental methods have provided improved reliability, yet this field still requires more practical and high-resolution approaches to evaluate mesh stiffness accurately. This study proposes a new experimental methodology based on high-resolution precision angle measurement (PAM). The method quantifies the elastic angular deformation of the gear pair during meshing using PAM, calculates the applied torque based on the measured weights and lever length, and then determines the torsional and linear mesh stiffness. Validation is performed by comparing PAM-derived mesh stiffness with a potential-energy analytical model and laser extensometer measurements, showing close agreement under healthy conditions. The method is further applied to an SBG with a tooth root crack at different depths, demonstrating its capability to indicate mesh-stiffness reduction as the crack depth increases. The results confirm that the proposed PAM-based approach offers a reliable and accurate tool for evaluating mesh stiffness in both healthy and cracked SBG systems.

title: Staged active-learning-based multi-fidelity Kriging method for reliability analysis with small failure probabilities
abstract: Estimating the small failure probability is crucial in reliability analysis of complex engineering systems. Although surrogate-based methods have been recognized as one of the most effective representatives, they are still less satisfactory in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy when applied to rare event problems involving nonlinear/dynamic finite element analyses. In this work, a staged active-learning-based multi-fidelity Kriging method is developed for assessing small failure probabilities. We firstly develop a new multi-fidelity Kriging model, in which a joint architecture is proposed to characterize the cross-fidelity correlations. Then, a multi-fidelity sampling scheme is established to assign different fidelity levels to a series of intermediate failure domains. With this sampling scheme, a staged active learning strategy is further developed to sequentially refine the constructed multi-fidelity model for reliability analysis. In our method, since the intermediate failure domains are assigned with varying low-fidelity levels, they can be approximated just with inexpensive low-fidelity evaluations to sequentially identify the critical regions. Within these identified regions, the accuracy of multi-fidelity surrogate can be effectively improved with just a few high-fidelity observations due to the joint architecture of the developed multi-fidelity model. Thus, the rare event probability can be estimated with high precision and significantly reduced computational burden. Four illustrative examples, including a nonlinear Duffing oscillator system and a transient contact spur gear dynamic system, are investigated to validate the developed method.

title: An innovative quasi-zero stiffness isolator for excitation adaptability via dual nonlinear stiffness regulation
abstract: Conventional quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) vibration isolators suffer from low-frequency resonance, severely compromising their isolation performance and limiting their usable frequency range. This work proposes a novel adaptive-excitation QZS isolator (AQZSI) based on dual nonlinear stiffness regulation, which achieves excellent resonance suppression, broadband vibration isolation, and varying-load capacity. The experimental prototype consists of a negative stiffness mechanism made of spring steel buckling beams and a positive stiffness mechanism made of neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets, which have the advantages of low energy consumption and low damping characteristics. The vibration isolation system is designed based on a smart and rapid switch between dual nonlinear systems of QZS and high stiffness (HS) isolators by tuning the positive stiffness. By timely identifying the excitation frequency, a semi-active control system is employed to adaptively switch the working state to the HS mode at the low frequency and to the QZS mode at the high frequency. Thus, the resonance at low frequencies is alleviated while maintaining excellent isolation performance at high frequencies. In addition, the varying-load adaptability is achieved by simultaneously tuning both positive and negative stiffness to realize the rated load adjustment. Static analyses are conducted, and the dynamic characteristics are analyzed by using the harmonic balance method. Experimental results show that the resonance peak of AQZSI in the low-frequency region is reduced by up to 82.3% compared to a standalone QZS system and that the rated load can be readily changed according to the payload, verifying its superior broadband vibration isolation performance as well as varying-load capacity.

title: Editorial Board
Optimisation of the Azadegan oilfield wellbore lost circulation diagnosis model: A hybrid model combining the SIKPW denoising framework and SSA optimisation
abstract: Lost circulation represents a common yet high-risk complex condition in drilling operations, significantly impacting drilling safety and operational efficiency. Addressing the existing research gap where most studies focus on predicting the onset of wellbore leaks while neglecting the identification of leak severity, this paper proposes an intelligent lost circulation diagnosis method integrating adaptive signal denoising with model optimisation. The approach constructs a hybrid framework comprising signal processing and intelligent diagnostic models. At the signal processing level, the Subtractive Averaging and Batch Optimisation (SABO) algorithm is employed to perform adaptive parameter optimisation on the Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Additive Noise (ICEEMDAN) for adaptive parameter optimisation. This is combined with a kurtosis-correlation criterion and an improved wavelet threshold function to effectively suppress high-noise intrinsic mode function (IMF) components, thereby significantly enhancing the data quality of wellbore leakage characterisation parameters. At the model level, a CNN-SVM model is constructed by integrating a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a support vector machine (SVM). The Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) dynamically optimises the model’s hyperparameters to enhance its discriminative capability and stability. Experimental results based on Azadegan oilfield data demonstrate that the proposed SIKPW denoising framework and SSA-CNN-SVM intelligent lost circulation diagnosis model achieved an average diagnostic accuracy of 98.989% in the lost circulation severity classification task, with a standard deviation of merely 0.423. Compared to traditional machine learning and deep learning models, this approach improves overall diagnostic accuracy by approximately 7%, while reducing false positive and false negative rates by about 3% and 4% respectively under complete lost circulation conditions. It demonstrates robust stability and resilience even under imbalanced sample conditions.

title: Nonlinear dynamic modeling and vibration analysis of high-contact-ratio electric drive gear system with multi-source excitation coupling
abstract: To address the issue of local bearing damage in the gear-bearing-housing coupled system of electric drive assemblies for new energy vehicles, this study establishes a coupled dynamic model to investigate the evolution law of nonlinear vibration responses under fault excitation. Firstly, the definition of high contact ratio (HCR) gears is clarified, and gear pairs with total contact ratios of 4.297 and 4.077 are selected to calculate the time-varying friction coefficient (TVFC) and time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS) of the gears. Secondly, a mathematical model for local bearing failure is constructed and integrated with the gear, leading to the derivation of coupled dynamic equations for the system incorporating a flexible housing. Subsequently, numerical methods are employed to solve the dynamic equations and extract the multi-dimensional dynamic characteristics of the system. Meanwhile, the dependability of the developed model is confirmed by contrasting simulation findings with experimental results, and the underlying mechanism whereby local faults in bearing raceways affect the system vibration response is disclosed. The results reveal that the local defects can cause periodic impact, leading to a significant accumulation of vibration energy at the fault-induced frequency and its harmonics, and induces dense harmonics. Subject to the modulation imposed by the shaft rotary frequency, the fault characteristic frequency associated with the bearing inner ring couples with the gear meshing frequency to constitute combined side frequency bands, and fault excitation gives rise to a distinct enhancement of the sideband amplitudes.

title: Robust physics-informed thermal error modeling for ball screw feed drives via in-process data assimilation
abstract: Thermally induced positioning error (TIPE) in ball screw feed drives critically affects the machining accuracy of high-precision machine tools. Existing thermal error models are challenged by their reliance on extensive labeled datasets, which increases data acquisition costs and prolongs production cycles. In addition, these models utilize sparse temperature measurements as inputs, which are insufficient for reconstructing the full temperature field and therefore limit the characterization of non-uniform TIPE distributions under complex feed motions. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed digital twin (PIDT) framework for TIPE prediction that does not require labeled TIPE data for supervised training or parameter fitting, while explicitly incorporating the time-varying nut trajectory. First, an independent reduced thermal domain of the screw shaft is established by assimilating measured boundary temperatures, while a convolution-based physics-informed solver reconstructs the transient temperature field induced by the moving nut and stationary bearings. Subsequently, the TIPE profile along the feed axis is derived by integrating the axial temperature distribution and is dynamically constrained by a novel in-process end-displacement (IPED) measurement, thereby enabling online correction without interrupting machining. Across four operating conditions with different feed rates and reciprocating ranges, the proposed model achieves accurate and robust prediction under parameter uncertainty, reducing the maximum TIPE from 42.3, 56.7, 58.3, and 53.7 μm to 2.9, 4.6, 4.1, and 3.6 μm, respectively. This framework provides an efficient, physically interpretable, and cost-effective solution for TIPE compensation under complex and variable machining conditions.

title: Non-contact 3D displacement measurement of structure based on the fusion of millimeter wave radar and digital image correlation
abstract: Three-dimensional digital image correlation (3D-DIC) displacement measurements based on binocular vision are typically used for indoor, close-range structural testing. However, the accuracy of field and remote 3D-DIC displacement measurements is often strongly affected by environmental conditions, equipment setup, and on-site target calibration. This study proposes a novel three-dimensional (3D) displacement measurement method that determines the 3D displacement of the target through combining its in-plane two-dimensional (2D) displacement using a monocular vision two-dimensional digital image correlation (2D-DIC) with the out-of-plane displacement using a millimeter wave radar. By exploiting the spatial relationships between the observation and target points, their horizontal and vertical angles are computed. The displacement data derived from the millimeter wave radar and 2D-DIC were then calibrated and fused through spatial component mapping to achieve high-precision 3D displacement measurements. Numerical simulations revealed that the measurement accuracy of this method is angle-dependent, with errors converging as both the detection distance and lateral offset of the target increases. Laboratory experiments demonstrated that this method exhibits certain sensitivity to spatial positioning, with optimal 3D measurement accuracy achieved when the target point is located at the center of the field of view. Measurement errors progressively increased with greater deviation from the central point. Field experiments revealed that the integrated method is susceptible to thermal flow disturbances. However, the influence of such noise and other interference could be effectively mitigated through median filtering processing, maintaining a measurement accuracy of ± 0.2 mm at a distance up to 40 m. This study successfully implemented the technology for 3D dynamic displacement monitoring at the mid-span of a cable-stayed bridge model, achieving precise measurement and trajectory tracking of 3D displacements. Overall, the paper provides an innovative solution for non-contact 3D displacement measurements through the fusion of a millimeter wave radar and DIC.

title: A novel thermal hysteresis-RC pressure perturbation dynamic characteristic model of air spring considering the bending effects and energy dissipation shifts of hysteresis loops
abstract: Abstract The dynamic characteristics of air springs are mightily hysteresis nonlinear, stemming from the complex structure of the rubber bellows, material nonlinearity, and pressure dependence. This paper aims to precisely capture the dynamic characteristics of air springs, particularly characterizing the pronounced bending effects at the extremes of the hysteresis loop under high amplitudes(>10mm). The friction between the cord and the rubber, the bellows viscoelasticity, and the pressure fluctuations are considered comprehensively. A novel piecewise methodology for characterizing the hysteresis loops is proposed by introducing the resistor-capacitor (RC) operator and pressure parameter. The frequency-dependent Quadratic Parabola Fractional Derivative Kelvin-Voigt Pressure Perturbation Model (QKPPM) is integrated to formulate the RC Pressure Perturbation Hysteresis Nonlinear Model of Rubber Bellows (RCPPM-RB), depicting the evolution laws of model parameters in response to the changes in amplitude, frequency and pressure of rubber bellows. Subsequently, the Thermal Hysteresis-RC Pressure Perturbation dynamic characteristic Model of air spring (TH-RCPPM) under variable working pressure is established. The test results demonstrate that the static hysteresis loops show a maximum relative error of less than 1.6%, with a hysteresis area error of 8.1%. Furthermore, the dynamic hysteresis loop and dynamic stiffness values only have maximum relative errors of 7.1% and 5.4%, respectively. The accuracy and broad applicability of the novel model proposed are verified by experiments. The research results present an innovative approach for accurately modeling the dynamic characteristics of air springs and a fresh idea for the precise characterization of the dynamic characteristics of air springs.

title: Layout optimization of multi-type resonators using frequency-dependent fictitious grounded spring
abstract: In this study, the layouts of multiple types of resonators are optimized within a multi-material topology optimization framework to maximize damping performance in multiple vibration modes of thin plates. The optimized configurations are validated experimentally. Each resonator consists of a metallic mass embedded at the tip of a rubber cylinder. To maximize resonator damping, two conditions must be satisfied. The resonators must be placed at vibration antinodes, and their natural frequencies must be tuned to those of the entire system, namely the combined system of the thin plate and the attached resonators. Because thin plates are lightweight, modifications in resonator layout readily alter both the mode shapes and the natural frequencies of the entire system. Consequently, identifying a layout that simultaneously satisfies displacement and frequency tuning requirements is nontrivial. To overcome this difficulty, a novel fictitious grounded spring element is introduced to represent the damping of the resonators. Displacement dependence is modeled by grounded springs. Frequency dependence is incorporated into the spring modulus to capture the resonators’ resonance. In the optimized layouts, resonators associated with each target mode are distributed at the corresponding antinodes, and the natural frequencies of the entire system are tuned accordingly. Experimental results confirm substantial improvements in damping performance for all targeted modes. By maximizing the system damping represented through the grounded springs, both displacement and frequency tuning requirements are satisfied without explicitly incorporating them into the objective function. The satisfaction of these conditions through an implicit procedure indicates the high generality of the proposed method.

title: Modelling method for bending stiffness of bolted flange joint with spigot and analysis of rotor vibration characteristics
abstract: To meet the rapid iteration demands of the bolted rotor system for the next-generation aero-engine in the conceptual design phase, the bending stiffness model of the bolted joint is required to have the characteristics of high accuracy and easy solvability. A new analytical model of bending stiffness for bolted flange joint with spigot considering all parameters is established based on the theory of plates and shells, and the effects of preload and preload unevenness on the bending stiffness are analyzed. By performing a comparison study with the finite element contact model, the maximal calculation error of the bending stiffness is approximately 6.83%, and the time required to calculate the bending stiffness once is reduced from 7 min to 5e-5 s, the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed model are validated. After that, an equivalent method for characterizing bolted joint using virtual shaft segment is proposed, and a dynamic model of the bolted rotor system is developed, in which the proposed bending stiffness model is introduced. The influence of preload and preload unevenness on the vibration characteristics of the bolted rotor system is analyzed by combining numerical calculation and experimental investigation. The results show that increasing preload can narrow the non-synchronous response interval of the bolted rotor system and reduce the proportion of strain energy for the bolted joint, the amplitude of subcritical self-excited vibration decreases with the reduction of preload unevenness.

title: Reliability evaluation of the micro-milling process based on time-varying parameters prediction and multi-index correlation analysis
abstract: This study proposes a reliability evaluation method integrating time-varying parameter prediction with dynamic multi-indicator correlation to address the challenge of accurately assessing machining reliability in micro-milling processes undergoing tool degradation. A mechanical model for micro-milling is established, incorporating the effects of tool runout, minimum cutting thickness and tool wear. Then combined the model with an integrated optimization strategy utilizing a kernel smoothing-enhanced particle filtering algorithm, enabling the online identification of time-varying cutting force coefficients. Furthermore, a time-varying mixed copula function is constructed to characterize the dynamic correlation between the maximum cutting force and the root mean square value, while a dynamic threshold model that accounts for tool degradation effects is developed. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. It achieves a cutting force prediction error below 1.65% and accurately tracks the decay process of both the correlation coefficient and system reliability. Compared to traditional models based on the independence assumption, the method provides a significant improvement in reliability assessment accuracy during the final stage of machining. The research provides a solid theoretical model and an effective technical approach for precision monitoring and predictive maintenance of micro-milling processes.

title: In-process measurements of lightweight gear deformations with laser speckles imaging
abstract: Gears are standard machine elements and are produced in high numbers. A bionic lightweight construction contributes to reducing CO2 emissions on the one hand but requires a paradigm shift in the design procedure on the other hand, as the standard methods to proof the strength do not apply. Here, a non-contact method to experimentally analyze deformation fields on lightweight gears under load is presented. The digital speckle photography is capable to resolve deformations with uncertainties of 1.3 μm and can be applied for static loads and even for dynamically meshing gears. The measuring uncertainty was estimated according to the guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM) (ISO/IEC Guide 98-3, 2008). In comparison with simulations, it was shown that systematic influences, which mainly occurred due to the mechanical stiffness of the test rigs, can be compensated by means of measuring data. Thus, the digital speckle photography has proven to be a non-invasive method to acquire laterally resolved deformation fields on gears under load to validate lightweight designs for gears.

title: Acoustic pressure distribution propagated by power ultrasound in cement paste
abstract: Although power ultrasound technology has emerged as a promising technique for accelerating cement hydration, its application remains constrained by insufficient understanding of ultrasonic wave propagation mechanisms within cement paste. This study represents the first systematic investigation into the acoustic pressure properties of power ultrasound in cement paste. An emission-reception system utilizing both single transducer and 3 × 3 array configurations (28 kHz, 100–900 W) was developed to characterize acoustic pressure distributions at various water-to-cement (w/c) ratios (0.30–1.0) and propagation distances (30–240 mm). Results revealed that viscous attenuation dominated the acoustic pressure decay, with attenuation coefficients increasing from 10.25 dB/m to 357.50 dB/m as the w/c ratio decreased from 1.0 to 0.30. To further elucidate these observations, a simulation model based on the Helmholtz equation was developed to describe the overall acoustic distribution patterns. Notably, a strong correlation was observed between experimental data and simulation results under low ultrasonic power conditions (approximately 100 W). These findings provide a theoretical foundation for the propagation of power ultrasound in cement paste.

title: A method for satellite component health monitoring and remaining life prediction based on data spatiotemporal distribution characteristics
abstract: Health monitoring of key satellite components is essential for understanding their operational status and optimizing mission planning. This paper presents a method for health monitoring and remaining life prediction based on data spatiotemporal characteristics to address the challenge of existing methods failing to fully capture the evolution of component health status. First, a parameterized health status model is developed based on three dimensions: data distribution, frequency, and local dynamics, to comprehensively depict changes in operational status. A dynamic time-weighted feature calculation method based on degradation rate is then introduced, which adaptively adjusts the time-weight function parameters to improve the model’s ability to integrate historical state information and detect abnormal changes. Finally, an efficient degradation trajectory fitting and late-stage remaining life prediction method based on Incremental Sparse Gaussian Processes is proposed. This method uses incremental learning to periodically update the model parameters, improving the accuracy and efficiency of remaining life prediction. Experimental results show that the method effectively captures the evolution of component health status and predicts remaining life, offering reliable support for mission planning and resource optimization.

title: Engineering perspectives on spin-induced wave steering in elastic media
authors: Luiz Henrique Marra da Silva Ribeiro
abstract: Spin phenomena are well known in quantum mechanics, but recent works have shown that spin can also be found in continuum mechanics. Spin angular momentum (SAM) can be a mechanism for steering elastic waves through phase-shifted external excitations. While spin-related phenomena have been mainly addressed in physics-oriented studies, an engineering perspective supported by analytical tools remains lacking. Previous studies have demonstrated that combined shear and bending excitation with suitable magnitudes and phases can induce one-sided propagation. In this work, we interpret the wave steering phenomenon in beams from an engineering perspective using a frequency-domain wave propagation solution. Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the magnitude and phase relation of the shear force and bending moment that cause SAM in Euler–Bernoulli beams. These analytical expressions are dependent on the excitation frequency and wavenumber. It is shown that the required phase angle for optimal unidirectional propagation is 90 degrees. Spectral and time-domain numerical simulations and experiments confirm that switching the sign of the SAM reverses the propagation direction, and that the ratio of shear to bending moment for optimal wave steering varies with frequency. These results establish a consistent engineering perspective on spin-driven wave control and pave the way for practical applications.

title: O(n) Local Eigenvalue Modification Procedure for real-time updating of structural digital twins with sub-millisecond-latency performance
abstract: Real-time structural digital twins require rapid and reliable model updating to maintain accuracy as the physical system evolves, particularly in high-rate dynamic environments where microsecond to millisecond scale decisions are critical. Traditional finite element (FE)–based updating methods rely on repeatedly solving the Generalized Eigenvalue Problem (GEP), whose 𝑂(𝑛^3) computational cost prevents deployment in real-time digital-twin frameworks for even moderately sized structural models. This work develops and validates a two-dimensional extension of the Local Eigenvalue Modification Procedure (LEMP) as a reduced-order, physics-based updating strategy that enables fast, continuous synchronization of structural digital twins without resolving the full eigenvalue problem.Using a steel plate modeled with bilinear quadrilateral finite elements, a systematic mesh-convergence and modal-error study identifies a 25-node reduced-order model capable of maintaining <10% modal-frequency error relative to a high-fidelity reference mesh. Localized stiffness perturbations are introduced across the plate to emulate evolving structural states, and comparisons between GEP and LEMP show that mode seven (7) offers a more reliable sensitivity for real-time updating. Across all introduced local changes, LEMP maintains frequency-prediction errors below 10% while avoiding global eigenvalue recomputation.Timing analyses demonstrate that LEMP achieves update latencies as low as 0.43 ms for the 25-node model and remains below 1–2~ms up to 169 nodes, offering speedups exceeding 2500× relative to GEP. Empirical scaling analysis confirms near-linear 𝑂(𝑛) algorithmic complexity for LEMP compared to the cubic 𝑂(𝑛^3) scaling of GEP. These results establish LEMP as a computationally efficient and experimentally validated mechanism for real-time digital-twin updating of 2D structural systems. The approach provides a practical pathway for integrating physics-based model updating into high-rate structural model updating, active control, and edge-deployed digital-twin applications.

title: Theoretical modeling and experimental validation of a dual-disk rotor system with coupled spatial crack and bearing outer race defects
abstract: The coexistence of fatigue cracks and localized bearing defects in rotating machinery poses challenges for accurate dynamic modeling and composite fault diagnosis. In this paper, a composite fault model for a dual-disk rotor system featuring a spatial crack and an outer race bearing defect was proposed. In this model, a dual-impulse mechanism is employed to describe the impact force induced by the outer race defect. Furthermore, the maximum relative error of the dual-impulse time intervals between the numerical simulations and experimental results is controlled to less than 5.5%. The effects of different axial crack locations and unbalance phases on the dynamic characteristics of the rotor system are further investigated. The results demonstrate that the nonlinear breathing behavior is governed by the rotor’s first bending mode, with the 2fr super-harmonic response reaching its maximum at the mid-span. Finally, for the coupled fault system, acceleration envelope analysis is successfully utilized to simultaneously identify the crack-induced super-harmonic 2fr and the bearing fault frequency fBPFO within a unified spectral domain.

title: Integrating VMD denoising with optimized MMAS via multi-domain feature fusion for intelligent bearing diagnosis under variable operating conditions
abstract: When gearboxes operate under variable speed and variable load conditions with strong background noise, the vibration signals of bearings exhibit significant non-stationary characteristics, posing severe challenges for accurate fault diagnosis. To address this issue, this study constructs an integrated intelligent diagnostic framework that sequentially covers three core stages: vibration signal denoising preprocessing, multi-domain feature extraction, and diagnosis-oriented feature selection. Firstly, the denoising performance of an approximate implementation of Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Wavelet Threshold Denoising (WT), and Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) under variable operating conditions is systematically compared. Visualization and quantitative evaluation are performed using waveform observation, radar charts of five reference-free indicators (kurtosis, envelope entropy, Gini index, impulse factor, and spectral kurtosis), and a newly constructed Comprehensive Performance Index (PI). Rigorous statistical validation is completed through Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), Tukey’s HSD post-hoc test, and Cohen’s d effect size. Subsequently, the denoised signals are mapped into multiple analytical perspectives, including the time domain, wavelet domain, angular domain, order domain, and cepstral domain, to construct a high-dimensional candidate feature pool. The Max-Min Ant System (MMAS) is introduced for feature selection, and an innovative three-stage parameter optimization framework comprising sensitivity analysis, interaction-effect study, and orthogonal experimental design is proposed. Response surface methodology is employed to reveal parameter coupling laws and determine the globally optimal parameter configuration. Furthermore, nested cross-validation is adopted to obtain an unbiased estimate of generalization performance, and the cross-operating-condition generalization capability of the method is validated under unseen load conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the VMD method significantly outperforms WT and EMD in terms of time-domain waveform clarity, multi-indicator radar chart coverage, and Comprehensive Performance Index (PI) values ranging from 0.800 (for other conditions) to 0.942 (for ball fault). Statistical tests further confirm its highly significant advantages (ANOVA p < 0.001) with effect sizes all exceeding the “large effect” threshold (|d| ≥ 0.8), and 3D heatmaps verify its cross-sample stability. The globally optimized MMAS, in feature scale analysis, achieves 100% classification accuracy under the same operating condition using only two wavelet-domain features. Under the more rigorous nested cross-validation framework, the stably selected feature subset maintains an average accuracy of 95.33%, confirming the robustness and generalization capability of the feature selection. In cross-operating-condition experiments, using 1200rmp04a as the training set, the average accuracy on three unseen load conditions reaches 76.11%, with the highest load condition achieving 83.7%. In summary, the proposed framework provides a novel approach for in-service intelligent diagnosis of gearbox bearings in industrial settings, characterized by high reliability, efficiency, and systematicity.

title: Feasibility study on residual strength prediction and failure mechanism analysis of laser-textured clinched joints based on frequency-domain signals
abstract: Clinching, as a core joining method for lightweight structures, offers the technical advantages of high efficiency, low cost, and environmental friendliness. Given the practical limitations of clinched joints in static load-bearing capacity, laser micro-texturing can effectively improve load-bearing performance by regulating the interfacial morphology between the two sheets. However, the tighter interfacial interlocking of the sheets leads to more complex fatigue wear accumulation and failure crack propagation. Further research is needed to characterize the evolution law of frequency-domain signals of micro-textured clinched joints under fatigue conditions using non-destructive testing techniques. In this paper, aluminum alloy clinched joints (AC) and laser-textured aluminum alloy clinched joints (LAC) were used as research objects to compare the influence of laser texturing on mechanical and fatigue properties. By designing and conducting an alternating test of dynamic response and strength degradation under constant-amplitude fatigue conditions, the intrinsic correlation between the frequency-domain signals variation law and the strength degradation mechanism was revealed. A residual strength prediction model for clinched joints was established by fitting based on the evolution law of frequency-domain parameters. The results show that laser micro-texturing can increase the interfacial friction of joints and disperse stress concentrations, thereby improving the static strength, average peak load displacement, and energy absorption of clinched joints, with increases of 123.21%, 111.88%, and 170.37%, respectively. Both the static and fatigue failure modes of AC and LAC joints are neck fractures. Due to uneven laser energy distribution, tearing along the texture boundaries occurs in the lap zone of LAC joints, and their fracture surfaces exhibit fatigue fracture characteristics. Under a fatigue load level of 1.400 kN, the natural frequency and residual strength of the LAC joint decrease synchronously. Based on the coupling mechanism of “crack propagation − stiffness degradation − natural frequency attenuation − residual strength decrease”, a nonlinear residual strength prediction model based on the change of natural frequency under constant-amplitude loading is established. Laboratory validation demonstrates that the model exhibits high predictive accuracy.

title: A magnetically coupled footstep energy harvester for embedded pavement systems
abstract: The development of smart roads and urban infrastructure has created an urgent need for long-term, stable, and maintenance-free energy supply for embedded pavement systems. Herein, we propose a magnetically coupled footstep energy harvester for embedded pavement systems (MCFEH-EPS). By introducing a magnetic coupling mechanism, irregular pedestrian-induced mechanical excitations are converted into relatively controllable magnetic excitations, enabling stable mechanical energy input to the power generation unit. The non-contact magnetic energy transmission reduces mechanical wear and structural failure risks, while enabling full sealing of the power generation unit and thereby enhancing long-term operational reliability under complex excitations and harsh environments. The harvester can function individually or in arrays in high pedestrian-density areas to boost energy output. An electromechanical coupled model of the MCFEH-EPS is established and validated by good agreement in overall trends between experimental and simulation results. Experimental results show that, at an excitation frequency of 3 Hz and a stroke of 50 mm, the MCFEH-EPS can generate up to 59 J of electrical energy within 5 s. The self-powered environmental monitoring and intelligent traffic control in embedded pavements are demonstrated. This work provides a sustainable and low-maintenance energy solution for emergency power supply of public facilities, pedestrian safety monitoring, and environmental sensing.

title: Online monitoring and prediction of abrasive belt wear in robotic grinding of Ti–6Al–4V workpieces using multimodal data
abstract: Continuous abrasive belt wear during robotic grinding of TC4 workpieces adversely affects surface quality. Existing image-based monitoring methods lack real-time capability, while multisensor data under varying conditions remain underutilized, limiting real-time wear height monitoring. To address these challenges, a multimodal framework is proposed to predict abrasive belt height and enable real-time wear monitoring under diverse grinding conditions. Acoustic emission, acceleration, and force signals acquired during the grinding process are segmented using a sliding window and subjected to multiscale decomposition for feature extraction. A VMRF-based feature selection method is employed to evaluate and optimize feature importance. The selected features are then fed into a DCDA-SBiLSTM model to achieve multifeature fusion for belt height prediction and real-time monitoring. Experimental validation on a robotic abrasive belt grinding system under varying operational conditions demonstrates average improvements of 34.82% in height prediction accuracy and 51.61% in real-time monitoring accuracy compared to conventional models. Additionally, ablation studies confirm an average improvement of 24.84% in prediction accuracy over ablated configurations.

title: A generalized zero-shot learning framework for bearing compound fault diagnosis using a class-aware VAE-based semantic vector extractor
abstract: This paper presents a Generalized Zero-Shot Learning framework for compound fault diagnosis in rolling element bearings, which incorporates characteristic fault frequencies to construct class-aware semantic representations and latent space. The proposed method addresses the limitation of conventional supervised models that fail to generalize to fault combinations not seen during training. By integrating fault frequency characteristics and semantic vectors learned via a class-aware variational autoencoder, the framework constructs a structured latent space for single fault classes and linearly interpolates their semantic vectors to model compound faults. A contrastive learning-based embedding module aligns feature and semantic spaces, and a similarity-based thresholding mechanism is introduced to improve classification of previously unseen conditions. The model is trained solely on normal and single fault data, requiring no labeled samples of compound faults. Comprehensive experiments conducted under diverse load conditions and various compound fault combinations demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms existing supervised and zero-shot learning baselines. It achieves accurate diagnosis of both seen and unseen fault types while reducing classification bias, thereby validating its effectiveness and applicability in practical industrial scenarios.

title: Energy-based dual-phased dynamics identification for forced nonlinear vibrations
abstract: System identification is critical to many engineering applications, especially in vibrating structures. The recently introduced Energy-based Dual-phase Dynamics Identification (EDDI) method is a data-driven technique to discover equations of motion using measured responses in compliance with physical balance laws. This work expands the original EDDI method for system identification for nonlinear single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) oscillators under the influence of external forcing. The major innovation presented in this work is the reformulation of EDDI to incorporate external forces into the identification process. The method is deployed in two phases to systematically extract mathematical models for the damping and stiffness of the structure. At its core, EDDI leverages conservation of energy and Newton’s second law to express the measured data into a form that allows identification of the underlying dynamics. Phase I estimates the energy dissipated by the damping in the system using conservation of energy, then uses that to identify a mathematical model for the damping. Phase II applies Newton’s second law to isolate the conservative force directly, which is then used to identify a mathematical model for the stiffness of the structure. EDDI requires only the measured response, the external force, and the mass of the oscillator for the identification with no prior information of system dynamics necessary.
