Using the Nonlinear Frequency Index as an optimization criterion, the magnitude order was adaptively tuned to amplify faint characteristic sidebands. Multiple experimental validations were performed on CFRP laminates subjected to impact energies ranging from 4 J to 10 J. The results demonstrated that the AMSBSE framework identified characteristic nonlinear features even at the low impact energy of 4 J. Quantitative analysis indicated that the extracted bicoherence coefficients exhibited a strong monotonic correlation with the impact energy levels (linearity coefficient > 0.97) and superior measurement consistency (standard deviation reduced to 0.042). This approach provides a non-contact solution for the quantitative characterization of early-stage impact damage severity in composite structures.

title: Bifurcation and stability analysis by tracking energy trajectory of a bolted rotor-bearing system under multi-nonlinearity coupled effect
abstract: The rotor system is a core component of various critical machinery. When nonlinear factors such as nonlinear contact stiffness, oil-film forces, and rub-impact forces are taken into account, the rotor system exhibits considerably complex bifurcation phenomena, complicating its dynamic characteristics and stability conditions. Traditional research methods for rotor systems also have limitations in real-time monitoring of bifurcation phenomena. This paper investigates the bifurcation phenomena and stability issues of the rotor system from an energy perspective. A dynamic equation for the rotor system that considers nonlinear contact stiffness, oil-film forces, and rub-impact forces is established. The steady-state response of the rotor system is obtained using numerical analysis methods, and the relationship between bifurcation and energy transfer is analyzed. Based on theoretical analysis and experimental results, the relationships between three-dimensional energy trajectories, two-dimensional energy trajectories, and the bifurcation forms and stability of the rotor are studied. Experimental tests are conducted on a rotor test bench. The collected data is analyzed to validate the practical effectiveness and applicability of the proposed energy trajectory method in identifying actual bifurcation types in a physical system. The results demonstrate that the energy curve exhibits more detailed fluctuations compared to the smooth displacement curve during the speed-up process, confirming its capability in capturing transient dynamic behaviors. The research indicates that, compared to traditional methods, monitoring the energy transfer in the rotor system can accurately determine its bifurcation phenomena and unstable motions. These findings can be applied to condition monitoring and stability prediction of rotor systems, marking significant progress in the translation of rotor system theory into engineering applications.

title: Understanding effects of central moment and raw moment in kurtosis for characterizing envelope signal sparsity
abstract: Sparsity is one of natural signal properties and it can be characterized by sparsity measures. One of the most popular sparsity measures is well-known kurtosis that has been widely studied in many fields, such as machine condition monitoring, oceanic engineering, blind source separation, noise filtration, compression, sampling and signal analysis, etc. Kurtosis can either be defined by central moment or raw moment. A previous study has shown that raw moment based kurtosis is equivalent to the square of the ratio of norm 2 to norm 1, which is recognized as a modified sparsity measure. Since envelope signals play an important role for machine condition monitoring, a detailed connection between central moment based kurtosis and raw moment based kurtosis for characterizing envelope signal sparsity is still not exploring. Especially, a numerical study by using Bernoulli samples (simplified simulated envelope for exhibiting signal sparsity changes) shows that kurtosis based on raw moment is a monotonically decreasing function about an increase of a Bernoulli distribution parameter p, while central moment based kurtosis is a symmetrical function about an increase or decrease of the Bernoulli distribution parameter p, which is prone to be confused by the “bilateral reduction” effect of complexity measures, such as Shannon entropy, sample entropy, correlation dimension, approximate entropy, etc. This paper aims to clarify the distinctions between the two kurtosis measures and provides a theoretical proof that kurtosis based on central moment follows three intuitive properties (Scaling, Cloning and Bill Gates) of sparsity measures. Subsequently, based on the intrinsic differences between central moment and raw moment, qualitative analysis of the representation performance of squared envelope spectrum and centralized envelope spectrum under different impulse intensities are conducted. Furthermore, on this basis, it further compares the differences in performance of the two sparsity measures in terms of fault impulse distinguishability. Bearing and motor run-to-failure experiments show that central moment based kurtosis and raw moment based kurtosis fully follow their theoretical properties and proved trends.

title: CS-SHAP: Extending SHAP to cyclic-spectral domain for better interpretability of intelligent fault diagnosis
abstract: Neural networks (NNs), with their powerful nonlinear mapping and end-to-end capabilities, are widely applied in mechanical intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD). However, as typical black-box models, they pose challenges in understanding their decision basis and logic, limiting their deployment in high-reliability scenarios. Hence, various methods have been proposed to enhance the interpretability of IFD. Among these, post-hoc approaches can provide explanations without changing model architecture, preserving its flexibility and scalability. However, existing post-hoc methods often suffer from limitations in explanation forms. They either require preprocessing that disrupts the end-to-end nature or overlook fault mechanisms, leading to suboptimal explanations. To address these issues, we derived the cyclic-spectral (CS) transform and proposed the CS-SHAP by extending Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to the CS domain. CS-SHAP can evaluate contributions from both carrier and modulation frequencies, aligning more closely with fault mechanisms and delivering clearer and more accurate explanations. Three datasets are utilized to validate the superior interpretability of CS-SHAP, ensuring its correctness, reproducibility, and practical performance. With open-source code and outstanding interpretability, CS-SHAP has the potential to be widely adopted and become the post-hoc interpretability benchmark in IFD, even in other classification tasks. The code is available on https://github.com/ChenQian0618/CS-SHAP.

title: An efficient optimal sensor placement method considering structural parameter uncertainty
abstract: Traditional optimal sensor placement methods are primarily constrained by two limitations: the high computational burden associated with securing a globally optimal configuration, and the inherent uncertainties in structural model parameters. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes an efficient optimal sensor placement method for modal identification, which incorporates parameter uncertainty. The proposed method consists of two main processes: Gaussian process regression (GPR) and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)-based Bayesian sampling. In GPR, a functional relationship is established between the structural global mode shape and the coordinates of all observed degrees of freedom (DOFs) for each mode, while systematically accounting for the uncertainty in structural model parameters. In MCMC-based Bayesian sampling, the optimal sensor configuration is efficiently identified via kernel density estimation across all possible locations, ensuring that the optimal sensor placement achieves global optimality without excessive computational expense. The objective function for optimal sensor placement is formulated based on the information entropy of the predicted global mode shape at each structural mode, which allows the entire analysis to proceed independently of any measured data. The number of sensors defines the model class in MCMC-based Bayesian sampling, and Bayesian sampling is conducted once for each model class until the optimal number of sensors is determined. The optimal number is decided with modal assurance criteria (MAC), which evaluate the similarity between the global mode shapes predicted by GPR based on the optimal sensor configuration and those from original finite element models. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through numerical simulations of a 20-story shear building and an experimental study on a two-story frame, both of which demonstrate its superior calculation efficiency and accuracy. By leveraging the measured data at optimal sensor configuration obtained by the proposed method, GPR enables the prediction of the system’s mode shapes at unmeasured DOFs.

title: Vibration energy harvesting by hybrid electromagnetic-piezoelectric structure with dynamic buckling bistability
abstract: A hybrid vibration energy harvesting structure integrating electromagnetic and piezoelectric mechanisms is proposed. A buckling beam with magnets and two side magnets with springs are introduced. The harvester is small in size and simple in structure. It can efficiently harness vibration energy by exciting inter-well jumping over a broad frequency range. The harvester is composed of a buckling beam with a middle magnet, a set of coils, two symmetrical magnets with springs and a piezoelectric sheet. Under external excitations, the repulsive forces between the middle and side magnets drive the beam to undergo an inter-well motion, thereby generating electrical outputs through electromagnetic and piezoelectric effects. The dynamic coupling equations are derived, and the potential energy is obtained. Corresponding simulations are carried out for harmonic and random excitations. Finally, the validation experiments are conducted. The experimental results prove that the presented harvester can harness vibration energy efficiently, even under weak excitations and broadband excitations. At a random excitation of power spectral density of 0.06 g2/Hz, or the root mean square acceleration of 1.225 g, the generated electrical RMS power could exceed 27.09 mW.

title: Self-supervised ViT-driven whole-line alignment of multi-date rail ultrasonic B-scan data for longitudinal infrastructure inspection
abstract: Multi-channel rail ultrasonic B-scan data provide critical evidence for defect identification, cross-period reinspection, and longitudinal condition assessment. However, reliable comparison of inspection records acquired on different dates requires mileage alignment, so that B-scan indications from the same physical rail locations can be compared over time. Existing alignment methods generally follow two routes. Methods relying on external mileage or positioning references may suffer from accumulated drift, initialization offsets, and local data loss during long-distance inspection, whereas methods based on local signal similarity are easily disrupted by sparse indications, noise, missing features, and false alarms. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a whole-line cross-date alignment framework for multi-channel rail ultrasonic B-scan data. The method first converts pseudo-color B-scan indications into structured event-level cues and extracts repeatable local patterns from unlabeled inspection data. These cues are then used to estimate a global coarse offset, construct reliable candidate correspondences, enforce global order consistency, and fit a piecewise mileage mapping between inspection runs. Experiments on real multi-date heavy-haul railway inspection data show that the proposed method achieves stable whole-line alignment under noise, data discontinuities, and missing indications, suppresses drift accumulation, and reduces the mean alignment error to within 3 m. The results indicate that the proposed framework can provide a reliable mileage reference for cross-date ultrasonic reinspection and long-term rail condition assessment.

title: A generalized semi-analytical modeling method for in-plane dynamics of arbitrarily curved beams with variable thickness
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic modeling method for arbitrarily curved beams with variable thickness (ACBVT) under multi-region arbitrary constraints. Firstly, due to the complex geometric properties of ACBVT, achieving a unified mathematical representation of coordinate and geometric relationships is challenging. Additionally, analytical determination of the neutral surface of ACBVT is infeasible. To address these challenges, based on the mechanical relationship between the neutral line and the upper/lower surface functions of ACBVT, an optimization algorithm is employed to obtain high-precision discrete neutral line data, thereby deriving an approximate fitting function. Subsequently, a unified mathematical integration method for ACBVT is established by mapping the sub-coordinate system to the global coordinate system. Meanwhile, a displacement function family tailored to ACBVT is constructed, with integral mapping functions and thickness feature functions as weighting terms, while virtual artificial springs are employed to simulate multi-region arbitrary stiffness constraints. The vibration behavior of ACBVT is solved using the Rayleigh–Ritz method. Meanwhile, the dynamic response and dynamic stress distribution of ACBVT under forced vibration are determined by incorporating the Lagrange function. The effectiveness of the proposed method under complex curvature, non-uniform thickness, and arbitrary constrained boundaries is validated through finite element analysis. Moreover, the acceleration amplitude and dynamic stress distribution patterns of ACBVT with multi-point supports are systematically analyzed, and several key conclusions are drawn accordingly.

title: Passive elastic mode-resolver with dispersion-engineered metasurfaces
abstract: Intrinsic modal dispersion confines most elastic metasurfaces to a single encoded functionality, and mode-resolved analysis of plate-guided waves therefore still relies on bulky transducers or extensive signal postprocessing. Here, we introduce a passive elastic mode-resolver for Lamb-wave identification based on a frequency-specific dispersion-engineered metasurface. A birefringent meta-atom is designed to exhibit pronounced mode-dependent dispersion, and its dynamic behavior is systematically characterized through eigenanalysis. By leveraging the fabrication flexibility of elastic metasurfaces, the required meta-atoms can be arranged without relying on extensive meta-atom libraries or computationally intensive optimization. Designed to operate at a specific frequency of 100 kHz, the proposed metasurface selectively focuses incident S0 and A0 modes to spatially encoded positions, thereby enabling identification of the propagating mode from the resulting intensity distribution. By integrating a piezoelectric element at each encoded focal position, the mechanically concentrated wave energy is converted into a mode-dependent electrical signal, enabling passive electrical readout of the encoded modal response. As a result, the mode-resolver provides a compact and passive alternative to bulkier systems conventionally used in structural health monitoring, ultrasonic sensing, and related industrial applications. By independently processing mode-dependent information within a single passive platform, it offers a practical route toward expanded mechanical functionality in transportation infrastructure, large civil structures, and smart facilities.

title: Interaction and propagation of breathing crack and rub-impact of a flexible blade-rotor-casing system
abstract: Vibration localization induced by blade cracks can significantly amplify rub-impact severity and trigger chaotic dynamics in high-speed rotor systems, posing a critical threat to operational safety. While existing studies often treat blade cracks or rub-impact in isolation, the coupled interaction and how they propagate under interactions are still unclear, particularly regarding their roles in nonlinear response evolution and instability onset of the rotor system. This study proposes a coupled dynamic model of a flexible blade–rotor–casing system that incorporates breathing crack and multi-blade rub-impact coupling failures. The governing equations of motion are derived using Hamilton’s principle and a novel breathing crack model as well as a blade contact force model considers cracks are proposed. Through comprehensive nonlinear dynamic analysis, this work reveals that blade cracks not only act as a trigger but also serve as a potent amplifier of rub-impact nonlinearity. Specifically, the reduction in stiffness caused by cracks can trigger combined resonance between the various components, thereby reducing the system’s stability margin. Moreover, the crack propagation caused by rubbing further intensifies the rubbing severity. These findings demonstrate that ignoring the coupling between blade cracks and rub-impact may severely underestimate instability risks.

title: Method to improve blade life prediction accuracy based on dynamic stress non-contact monitoring aided Basquin equation and Paris law
abstract: Blades are critical components in turbomachinery and often operate under severe conditions. High-cycle fatigue (HCF) is one of the primary life-limiting damage mechanisms for these components. This study introduces a life prediction method based on non-contact dynamic stress measurement to address crack initiation and propagation under HCF loading. The approach uses non-contact measurement technology to obtain real-time data on blade tip displacement amplitude and blade resonance frequency. These data are applied to modify the Basquin equation for fatigue life prediction. The Paris law is also adapted to estimate crack propagation life using both tip displacement amplitude and resonance frequency. Validation began with a strain-to-displacement calibration test, showing errors below 10%, which supports the feasibility of the dynamic stress calculation. Twenty sets of blade fatigue initiation tests demonstrated that all predicted fatigue lives fell within a 1.5 × scatter band, compared with the 3 × band obtained using traditional contact methods. In addition, ten sets of short-crack propagation tests showed that the predicted propagation lives were within a 1.5 × scatter band, compared with the 2.5 × band obtained using conventional contact measurements. Crack propagation prediction was thus successfully achieved via non-contact measurement. This research offers valuable insights for predicting high-cycle fatigue life and supporting maintenance strategies for turbomachinery blades.

title: Dynamic study of a rolling linear guideway workbench under combined thermal effects and guideway assembly deviations
abstract: This paper presents a systematic methodology, from thermal-field prediction to coupled dynamic response, targeting two long-standing factors that degrade the accuracy and stability of high-precision rolling linear guideway workbench (RLGW): thermal effects and guideway assembly deviations. A thermal network model that captures the dominant heat-transfer paths is developed to predict transient and steady-state temperature distributions under operating conditions. Local thermally induced deformations are extracted and mapped to deformations at the ball contact zones, serving as key inputs for the dynamic coupling. A five-degree-of-freedom dynamic equivalent model, consisting of the platform and four carriages, is developed. By applying coordinate transformations, the platform’s overall motion is projected onto each carriage’s local degrees of freedom, which mediates the transfer of contact-induced forces into the system’s vibratory response. To represent manufacturing and assembly uncertainty, five-component guideway deviation samples are generated by random sampling within the specified tolerance ranges, allowing systematic assessment of how assembly deviations affect dynamic characteristics and vibration sensitivity. Multiple validation tests confirm the model’s accuracy and reveal the primary differences and governing trends in system response under external loading, assembly deviations, thermal effects, and their couplings. The results deepen understanding of the thermal-assembly-dynamics coupling in RLGWs and provide actionable guidance for guideway tolerance design and thermal compensation strategies.

title: Dual-decoder network regularization for ultrasonic guided-wave full waveform inversion
abstract: Full waveform inversion (FWI) based on ultrasonic guided waves has been widely employed as a tomographic approach for nondestructive evaluation (NDE) of structural defects. In practical monitoring scenarios, however, noise and weak prior information can degrade reconstruction fidelity and drive the inversion toward local minima. To address these challenges, we propose an FWI framework that incorporates a dual-decoder network (DD-Net) as a deep image prior (DIP). Through its encoder-dual-decoder architecture, DD-Net provides implicit regularization via network structure and feature fusion, which helps alleviate cycle-skipping effects in time-domain inversion. By feeding the DD-Net output back as the initial model for subsequent FWI iterations, the proposed method yields more stable model updates and more reliable defect imaging. Numerical simulations and experiments show that, under weak priors, the proposed method improves the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) from 7.16 dB to 28.91 dB and the structural similarity index measure (SSIM) from 0.62 to 0.85. In addition, it tolerates initial-velocity deviations of up to ±16%, compared with approximately ±6% for conventional approaches. These results indicate that the proposed framework improves the robustness and practical applicability of ultrasonic guided-wave FWI for structural health monitoring (SHM) of safety-critical structures.

title: Predictive maintenance decision-making framework under stochastic imperfect maintenance effects
abstract: Imperfect maintenance, characterized by its flexibility, represents an essential approach for improving equipment operational efficiency and cost-effectiveness. However, the effectiveness of imperfect maintenance decision-making remains constrained by weaknesses in state assessment and policy optimization: (1) Current models typically fail to decouple imperfect maintenance effects from baseline degradation trends. The limitation hinders model updates and compromises state assessment accuracy. (2) Conventional theoretical decision models generally oversimplify the stochasticity of imperfect maintenance. The oversimplification deviates from engineering practice and leads to suboptimal policies. To address these deficiencies, we propose a predictive maintenance decision-making framework under stochastic imperfect maintenance effects. Regarding state assessment, the framework constructs a decoupled remaining useful life prediction network. By decoupling the effects of imperfect maintenance from the baseline degradation trends and correcting the baseline predictions, the network reduces prediction errors and enables accurate assessment. For policy optimization, the framework constructs a modeling paradigm based on deep reinforcement learning. By incorporating imperfect maintenance characteristics into data generation and decision modeling processes, the paradigm ensures learning a more robust dynamic policy. The proposed framework is validated through a case study on aircraft turbofan engine maintenance, where it demonstrates high cost-effectiveness compared to benchmark methods.

title: Misalignment safety threshold and stability driven controller tuning for AMBs–rotor systems
abstract: Active magnetic bearings (AMBs)–rotor systems are widely used in high precision machinery and energy equipment due to their contactless support capability. In these systems, coupling misalignment caused by manufacturing, assembly, or wear can induce asymmetric forces, leading to excessive rotor vibrations and decreased stability. Although controller parameter tuning methods are commonly based on empirical rules, classical control design, or numerical optimization, most existing approaches focus on conventional performance indices. They rarely consider coupling misalignment tolerance as an explicit design objective, making it difficult to guarantee system robustness and safety under varying misalignment conditions. Herein, a controller parameter tuning method based on both the misalignment safety threshold and system stability constraints is proposed. Specifically, the misalignment safety threshold is defined by the allowable misalignment area from the nonlinear electromechanical model of the AMBs–rotor system with coupling misalignment, while system stability is evaluated through root locus analysis. Simulation and experimental verifications under coupling misalignments are conducted. This method maximizes the system’s tolerance to coupling misalignment while maintaining stability margins and introduces a novel criterion for tuning controller parameters in AMBs–rotor systems.

title: Prediction framework establishment and experimental verification for operating zones of paroxysmal impulse vibrations in defective inter-shaft bearings
abstract: Inter-shaft bearings with localized faults exhibit two distinct vibration modes: paroxysmal and continuous impulse vibrations. Paroxysmal impulse vibrations have historically been regarded as rare phenomena, which has limited related research attention and practical significance. This study demonstrates that paroxysmal impulse vibrations are triggered by multiple broad rotation speed ratio zones that occupy a substantial proportion of the operational range. This finding establishes paroxysmal impulse vibrations as a highly probable and critical vibration mode in aero-engine inter-shaft bearings. A dynamic model of a dual-rotor system featuring a defective inter-shaft bearing is developed. The effect of localized defects in the inter-shaft bearing is modeled using a time-varying displacement excitation. A novel time-interval modulation behavior of paroxysmal impulse vibrations governed by rotation speed ratio zones is investigated. The underlying mechanical mechanism of paroxysmal impulse vibrations is elucidated. Building on this mechanism, a predictive framework and analytical formulas are proposed, enabling not only the quantification of paroxysmal impulse vibration time intervals but also the identification of all rotation speed ratio zones capable of inducing such vibrations. Furthermore, by determining all rotation speed ratio zones capable of inducing paroxysmal impulse vibrations, the proposed prediction framework provides a criterion for defining the transition boundaries between paroxysmal and continuous impulse vibrations. The paroxysmal impulse vibration phenomena and the proposed prediction framework are experimentally validated, providing a generalized theoretical foundation for inter-shaft bearing dynamics. For engineering guidance in dual-rotor design, these specific rotation speed ratio zones should be avoided to prevent destructive vibrations triggered by inter-shaft bearing faults.

title: Shape sensing of complex plate based on the inverse Rayleigh-Ritz method
abstract: For plate structures with complex geometries such as circular and truncated circular plates, conventional inverse finite element methods (iFEM) usually rely on mesh refinement to ensure reconstruction accuracy, which results in excessive degrees of freedom and increased ill-conditioning. To address this issue, an inverse Rayleigh-Ritz method (iRRM) is developed within the Kirchhoff-Love plate theory and a weighted least-squares framework. In this approach, boundary satisfying Ritz trial functions are introduced to directly represent the full-field displacement using a small number of high order p-type basis functions. The displacement field is reconstructed from a limited set of measured strains without mesh refinement or intermediate interpolation. A fixed–fixed circular plate is analyzed using high-fidelity finite element results as reference, and the outcomes show that comparable reconstruction accuracy can be achieved with far fewer degrees of freedom, effectively reducing geometric approximation errors associated with curved boundaries. Further experimental studies are performed on a cantilevered irregular plate under both concentrated and uniformly distributed loads. The reconstructed displacement contours obtained by iRRM are found to be highly consistent with the optical measurements in overall morphology and extreme-value distribution. The root-mean-square error (RMSE) reaches 6.2460 mm under Load-1 and 7.6773 mm under Load-2; when normalized by the maximum deformation, the corresponding values are 1.97 % and 1.93 %, respectively. The corresponding standard deviations remain narrow, indicating good robustness and repeatability. The results demonstrate that, with only known boundaries and sparse strain data, iRRM enables smooth, full-field, and efficient deformation reconstruction for complex geometries, providing a feasible and reusable approach for engineering structural health monitoring (SHM) of plate and shell components.

title: Enhanced force reconstruction for finishing broaching process with weak excitation using a quasi-static shift factor
abstract: Indirect reconstruction of broaching force using a single accelerometer offers significant economic and practical benefits for monitoring tool wear and cutting quality during production. However, under signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)-constrained conditions, the acquired acceleration signal has a low and fluctuating SNR due to non-uniform system noise and weak excitation. Consequently, the reconstructed cutting force becomes distorted in both dynamic and static components. This paper proposes an enhanced broaching force reconstruction method that incorporates a quasi-static shift factor (QSF) for achieving higher accuracy than conventional methods. The accurate reconstruction of a full broaching force signal necessitates the precise recovery of both the direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC) components. The AC component of the broaching force is extracted by applying an acceleration-to-force transfer function and a high-pass filter to the acceleration. This AC component, along with workpiece thickness, tooth spacing, cutting speed, and a low-pass filter, determines the quasi-static multi-tooth cutting force (termed the multi-tooth DC component). This multi-tooth DC component is then integrated with the AC component, obtaining an enriched cutting force. Due to the SNR-constrained condition, the waveforms of both the dynamic and static components in the enriched cutting force are inevitably distorted and thus require compensation. The QSF is then proposed to shift the enriched cutting force, resulting in a final, high precision enhanced broaching force. Even under SNR-constrained conditions, experiments demonstrate the feasibility and high precision of the proposed broaching force reconstruction method.

title: Application of machine-vision-driven physics-informed neural networks in pantograph–catenary system state detection
abstract: The pantograph–catenary system is a core component for energy transmission in electrified railways for high-speed trains, and its stability directly affects train operation safety and power supply quality. With the continuous increase in train operating speed and line power demand, accurate state detection of the pantograph–catenary system has become increasingly important. However, traditional monitoring schemes rely on sensor installation and structural modification of the pantograph, which not only increases cost and may alter the original dynamic characteristics, but is also susceptible to external environmental interference, thereby limiting their practical application. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) embed system physical equations into network training, providing a potential approach for high-precision modeling and state prediction of the multiscale spatiotemporal nonlinear frequency-response characteristics of the pantograph–catenary coupling process without additional hardware cost. However, existing PINN methods still face three major challenges in pantograph–catenary system applications. At the feature extraction level, existing methods struggle to fully exploit the spatiotemporal multidimensional physical features of event-stream images. At the physical-variable processing level, they have difficulty deeply characterizing the complex nonlinear coupling between time-domain and frequency-domain physical quantities in the pantograph–catenary system. At the model training level, adaptive loss-weight learning based on gradients requires repeated solution of high-dimensional quadratic optimization subproblems, resulting in excessive training complexity and computational cost. Therefore, this paper proposes a machine-vision-driven physics-informed neural network (VIPINN) for state detection and prediction of the pantograph–catenary system. First, event-stream images are regarded as heat sources, and spatiotemporal physical features are effectively extracted through frequency-domain Fourier transform and diffusion-process simulation, thereby enhancing the physical interpretability of visual embeddings. Then, Fourier neural operator and liquid time-constant network modules are combined to deeply explore system dynamics from the frequency domain and time domain, respectively, enabling comprehensive perception of multiscale nonlinear features. Finally, a random loss-weighted optimization strategy is proposed, which dynamically balances data loss, physical loss, and partial-derivative loss by randomly sampling mini-batch data and weights for each loss function. Without quadratic optimization, this strategy can avoid gradient conflicts and local minima, improving training efficiency and stability. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly improves detection accuracy in pantograph–catenary system state detection and exhibits strong robustness, effectively addressing noise interference in complex environments and verifying the great potential of VIPINN methods in practical applications.

title: High-precision identification of robot dynamics model and collision detection considering multi-source uncertainties
abstract: To enhance the accuracy of the robot dynamics model and ensure safety in human–robot interaction under complex assembly conditions, this paper proposes a high-precision identification method for the robot dynamics model and collision detection considering multi-source uncertainties. First, a dynamic model incorporating nonlinear friction is established, followed by an offline pre-identification process with physical feasibility constraints. To address uncertainties introduced by tools and loads, a stepwise identification strategy is proposed, in which static and dynamic parameters are separately identified. This approach ensures accurate load dynamic modeling even when the robot’s workspace is limited or the excitation trajectory is short. Second, to compensate for multi-source uncertainties such as load variations, assembly clearances, and measurement noise, a semi-linear online identification method that can be embedded into external force observers is proposed, in which the linear and nonlinear components of the friction model are decoupled and combined with recursive estimation to achieve online compensation of the robot dynamic model. Furthermore, to simultaneously detect unexpected collision forces and desired contact forces, an online extended state observer (OESO) with a dual-filter structure is designed, effectively overcoming the inherent limitation of single-filter approaches in balancing collision force and contact force detection. Finally, experiments conducted on a 7-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robot verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method. The research results of this paper can effectively guarantee the safety and robustness of robots in assembly tasks.

title: Biologically inspired novel design strategy for integrated regenerative shock absorbers: a review
abstract: In response to the increasing demand for sustainable and intelligent vehicle technologies, automotive suspension systems are experiencing a paradigm shift from energy-consuming to energy-saving designs. Traditional active and semi-active suspensions encounter two primary challenges: excessive energy consumption and structural complexity, largely due to their dependence on external power sources. Drawing inspiration from the highly coordinated and compact functionality of biological limbs, this paper introduces a novel integrated damper design paradigm. This approach is based on the use of regenerative shock absorbers (RSAs), which harvest vibrational energy to facilitate self-powered operation while also functioning as sensors for road perception and actuators for damping adjustment. This paper systematically reviews the key technologies that enable integrated systems. It begins with energy-harvesting mechanisms and multifunctional structural designs, examines coupling modeling methods within vehicle dynamics, explores strategies to optimize the trade-off between energy efficiency and dynamic performance, and summarizes self-powered control technologies derived from principles of internal energy flow. The statistical results indicate that RSAs have achieved energy harvesting across a significant range, from milliwatts to kilowatts (typical values of 10 W to 1.5 kW), while simultaneously reducing vehicle body acceleration to a minimal level of 0.04 to 0.6 m/s2 root mean square (RMS). Finally, the study addresses current challenges and outlines future research directions, including the integration of artificial intelligence and advanced materials, to provide theoretical insights and practical guidance for developing the next generation of self-adaptive suspension systems for autonomous vehicles.

title: Neural network assisted-augmented Kalman filter for joint input-state estimation
abstract: The augmented Kalman filter (AKF) is widely used for joint input-state estimation by augmenting the state vector with unknown inputs. However, its performance critically depends on the Gaussian white noise assumption and the proper selection of noise covariance matrices, making it sensitive to modeling errors in the state-space representation and hyperparameter tuning in practice. To address these challenges, this study proposes an AKF-inspired hybrid learned observer, termed AKFNet, for joint input-state estimation from sparse output-only measurements. Unlike the classical AKF, AKFNet no longer computes the Kalman gain analytically based on the minimum mean square error principle; instead, it is a hybrid data-driven and model-based algorithm that embeds a recurrent neural network (RNN) module into the AKF recursion and empirically learns the gain directly from measurements. The RNN module learns to map the information of real data within the state-space model to an effective Kalman gain, thereby improving the accuracy and robustness of joint input-state estimation in practical scenarios where model mismatches and complex noises are present. The proposed AKFNet is first validated on a numerical 9 DOF building for seismic input-state estimation, and compared with the classical AKF, dual Kalman filter (DKF) and an adaptive AKF with online covariance adjustment. Subsequently, an experimental shaker table test is conducted on a three-story frame to further validate its effectiveness. Finally, the AKFNet is used to estimate wind loads on a real-world large-span cable-stayed bridge using field data. In all tested scenarios, AKFNet provides competitive or improved accuracy, demonstrating its robustness and adaptive capability in the presence of modeling errors and non-white Gaussian noise.

title: Physics-guided neural network architectures for modeling nonlinear behaviors: Application to shape memory alloy wires
abstract: A novel physics-guided machine learning framework is proposed for the numerical simulation of complex nonlinear behaviors and to improve the generalization capability of data-driven models under limited information conditions. It combines an a priori physics-based model with a new neural network (NN) architecture designed to compensate for its inaccuracies. A differential evolution algorithm is adopted for the parametric identification of the physics-based model. On the other hand, an original transformer-based NN, enhanced with a long short-term memory (LSTM) feature fusion layer, is employed to capture the inherent aspects of the nonlinear behavior that are overlooked by the physics-based model so as to reduce overall errors.This approach is applied to simulate the hysteretic tensile behavior of NiTiNOL shape memory alloy wires subject to different loading rates. A comprehensive experimental comparative assessment is carried out between a physics-based (phenomenological) model and four NN architectures, including the uni- and bi-directional LSTM models, a transformer model, as well as the proposed model merging LSTM and transformer components. These NN architectures are employed both in a fully data-driven setting and within the physics-guided framework herein conceived with the purpose of mitigating the inaccuracies arising from the selected phenomenological model.The results indicate that the proposed NN architecture connecting LSTM and transformer components achieves the best overall performance. Furthermore, the physics-guided approach consistently improves both accuracy and reliability of the predictions.

title: A vibro-acoustic analysis method of a flexible propulsion shaft–shell coupled system under multi-source excitations
abstract: Vibro-acoustic characteristics of the propulsion system should greatly affect the working performance of underwater vehicles. Most existing studies only considered single propulsion shaft or shell, which used single excitation source or ideal fixed boundary conditions. The coupled dynamics and acoustic responses induced by the combined flexible shaft-shell excitations cannot be fully captured. The present work conducts a vibro-acoustic analysis method for a coupled flexible propulsion shaft-shell (FPSS) system. The multiple excitation sources in the propulsion shaft are considered, which include the motor excitations, bearing excitations and shaft excitations. The governing equations of the structural components are derived by using the energy method. The exterior acoustic field is modeled according to the spectral boundary element method. The developed dynamic model can completely describe the coupled vibro-acoustic behaviors of the FPSS system. A test is also introduced to validate the accuracy of the proposed method. The results may provide some theoretical support for predicting the vibro-acoustic responses of the propulsion systems in the underwater vehicles.

title: High dimensional stochastic dynamic response analysis with randomness in both system parameters and external excitations based on cell renormalized method
abstract: Evaluating the response’s probability distributions of dynamical systems with randomness in both system parameters and external excitation is a problem of sustained interest. It is demonstrated that the marginal distributions of the quantities of interest satisfy the reduced dimension probability evolution equation. This paper develops the cell renormalized method for stochastic dynamic response with both random parameters and excitation. The probability space of the elementary random variables and the state space formed by the displacement and velocity of the target degree of freedom are partitioned to obtain representative samples of derivate moments. Subsequently Gaussian process regression yields continuous derivate-moment surfaces in the state space. Finally, the path integral approach is applied to recover the probability distributions of displacement and velocity. To demonstrate the advantages of proposed method, several numerical examples including linear, fractional-order systems and nonlinear cases are all considered to illustrate the accuracy and efficiency.

title: Experimentally validated reconfigurable piezoelectric metamaterial plate for sound directivity control
abstract: This work presents an experimentally validated investigation of a reconfigurable piezoelectric metamaterial plate designed for sound directivity control. The metastructure consists of an aluminum plate with an array of piezoelectric patches, each connected to a tunable resonant shunt circuit. By selectively adjusting the spatial distribution of tuned and open-circuit elements, it becomes possible to modify vibration modes and steer the radiated acoustic energy without physically modifying the structure. The study presents transverse velocity and near-field acoustic measurements of the metastructure, which also validate the finite element simulations of the vibroacoustic system. Results demonstrate that different tuning patterns can confine vibrations to specific regions of the plate, producing far-field radiation patterns that range from omnidirectional to highly directional lobes. These findings emphasize the potential of reconfigurable piezoelectric metamaterials as a versatile solution for adaptive noise and vibration control in engineering applications.

title: Rapid and ambient-noise-robust synchronous secondary-path modeling via Kronecker product decomposition for multichannel active noise control
abstract: Secondary-path modeling is pivotal to the convergence and stability of multichannel active noise control (ANC) systems. Conventional random-noise modeling necessitates quiet environments and sequential excitation of control sources, leading to prohibitive path-by-path modeling time. Synchronous Wiener-based modeling accelerates this process by simultaneous excitation, but it is hindered by large matrix inversions and degraded estimation reliability under noisy and finite-sample measurements. This paper proposes a rapid and ambient-noise-robust synchronous secondary-path modeling framework leveraging the low-rank structure of the secondary-path matrix, together with a computationally efficient Kronecker-factorized adaptive algorithm. First, the secondary-path matrix is decomposed as the truncated sum of Kronecker products during synchronous modeling, reducing computational complexity and modeling time. Second, the reduced effective dimension suppresses the noise-induced cross-correlation bias in noisy environments, enhancing robustness compared with high-dimensional Wiener-based modeling. Third, the Kronecker factors are directly exploited to compute the filtered-reference signals, further lowering computational cost via channel sharing without sacrificing control performance. Representation capability and estimation accuracy are quantified using normalized truncation error, normalized modeling error, and phase-response discrepancies. Ordinary room experiments achieve stable modeling of 81 secondary paths within 2 s, with approximately − 15 dB error under both quiet and noisy conditions. Vehicle experiments further validate practical effectiveness by modeling 64 secondary paths within 1 s, with approximately − 19 dB error. Overall, the proposed method reduces modeling time and computational cost, while alleviating ambient-noise-induced degradation in control performance, thereby enhancing practical applicability in real-world scenarios.

title: Dynamic modeling and analysis of bidirectional sliding guide systems considering wear and creep effects
abstract: The dynamic behavior of bidirectional sliding guide systems directly impacts the machining accuracy and long-term operational reliability of CNC machine tools. However, existing research primarily focuses on dynamic modeling under ideal conditions, lacking a systematic analysis of the combined effects of wear and creep. To address this issue, this paper proposes a dynamic modeling method for bidirectional sliding guide systems that couples bearing wear, nut wear, sliding guide interface wear, and bearing end cap bolt creep. By quantifying the time-accumulated effects of wear and creep on the elastic restoring forces of each functional component, the proposed model predicts the evolution of dynamic responses during long-term operation. Experimental and simulation results demonstrate that the wear model effectively predicts wear depths on bearings, nuts, and guideway mating surfaces, while the creep model accurately forecasts changes in bearing end cover bolt preload. Findings reveal that wear behavior on bearings, nuts, and guideway mating surfaces significantly degrades system dynamic response characteristics, whereas preload decay induced by bolt creep further exacerbates system vibration amplitude. Moreover, the rate of bolt preload reduction varies with material properties, and the structural parameters of each component, along with the initial preload configuration, significantly influence the wear depth. This study provides valuable insights into mitigating system wear and bolt creep, thereby establishing a theoretical foundation and methodological support for life prediction, maintenance strategy formulation, and structural optimization of bidirectional sliding guide systems.

title: Causal disentangled task adaptive prototypical network for few-shot cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Few-shot cross-condition fault diagnosis is critical for ensuring the reliability and safety of bearings under variable operating conditions. Prototypical network (PN), as a typical meta-learning model, has shown great potential in addressing this problem owing to its “learning to learn” paradigm. However, existing PN-based methods are still susceptible to domain-related nuisance information under large domain distribution shifts, and the inherent prototype rigidity restricts their adaptability to new tasks. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Causal Disentangled Task Adaptive Prototypical Network (CDTAPN) for few-shot cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis. Specifically, a causal disentanglement module is designed to separate fault-intrinsic features from domain-nuisance features. Meanwhile, it constructs a cooperative auxiliary loss function to enhance fault-intrinsic features, while suppressing domain-nuisance information. Furthermore, a task-conditioned adaptation mechanism is introduced to overcome prototype rigidity, which adopts inner-outer loop optimization to dynamically adjust class prototypes for each specific task, thereby enhancing task-level adaptability. Extensive experiments on three bearing fault datasets demonstrate that the fault diagnosis accuracy of CDTAPN improves by over 3% compared to various advanced meta-learning methods in few-shot cross-condition fault diagnosis. These results confirm that the proposed CDTAPN provides an effective solution for bearing fault diagnosis under data-scarce and variable operating conditions.

title: Physics-guided safe collaboration: an uncertainty-gated heterogeneous semi-supervised regression framework for tool wear prediction
abstract: To address the dual challenges of labeled sample scarcity and poor physical interpretability in tool wear prediction, this paper proposes a Physics-Guided and Uncertainty-Gated Safe Collaboration Regression (PGS-CoReg) framework. This heterogeneous dual-branch design achieves closed-loop calibration between mechanism-driven and data-driven paradigms. Specifically, a Physics-Guided Gaussian Process Regression (PGGPR) embeds Zhu’s wear mechanism as a Bayesian prior to anchor global trends, employing combinational kernels to decouple non-stationary fluctuations. Concurrently, a Physics-Constrained Long Short-Term Memory (PG-LSTM) network introduces a multi-task loss with monotonicity and mechanism consistency constraints, ensuring predicted trajectories strictly adhere to thermodynamic laws. Crucially, the framework utilizes PGGPR’s posterior variance as a dynamic gate to filter pseudo-labels, effectively blocking error accumulation and logical drift. Experiments on the PHM 2010 dataset demonstrate that PGGPR and PG-LSTM reduce prediction errors by 10.0% and 18.2% against baselines. With only 20% labels, PGS-CoReg achieves an RMSE of 17.50 μm, surpassing the fully supervised LSTM baseline. Incorporating Non-IID heterogeneous data further reduces error by 19.6%, increasing the Confidence Interval Coverage Rate to 94.0%. Remarkably, cross-scenario validations on the NASA dataset confirm its robust sensor-agnostic transferability, effectively overcoming mathematically ill-posed early-stage extrapolation and massive blind-zone interpolation under severe domain shifts and extreme label scarcity (merely 3 labels). This study establishes a verifiable methodology for highly reliable predictive maintenance and tool health management in small-sample industrial scenarios.

title: Creating a smooth and wide attenuation band in the transmissibility of beam vibration using a neutraliser
abstract: This paper investigates how a single vibration neutraliser can be attached to a beam to create a wide frequency range in which vibration transmission is reduced. This range, termed the smooth wide attenuation band (WAB), is defined as the region where the displacement transmissibility across the beam is below unity and exhibits no peaks or troughs. The concept is motivated by similar behaviour observed in mono-coupled periodic rods. The primary aim of the study is to identify the physical mechanisms responsible for the formation of the WAB and to establish an effective approach for tuning the neutraliser. Using the receptance method, with the beam modelled using its vibration modes, it is shown that the formation of a WAB requires specific conditions. The neutraliser must be placed at a nodal point of the beam and be tuned such that the real part of its dynamic stiffness is equal and opposite to the mass-like receptance of the beam at the corresponding natural frequency. The analysis shows that the WAB results from a degenerate mode condition in which two vibration modes of the combined beam–neutraliser system coincide in frequency. Numerical simulations indicate that attaching the neutraliser at the nodal point nearest to the end of the beam which is excited, produces a wider WAB and greater reduction in transmissibility than using the nodal point near the opposite end. These findings, which are supported by experimental validation, provide new physical insight into the WAB phenomenon on a beam.

title: Simultaneous identification of system and interactive fault parameters in an active magnetic bearing integrated rotor train system with offset disc configuration: numerical and experimental validation
abstract: Reliable identification of systems and fault parameters in rotating machinery remains challenging due to the simultaneous presence of multiple interacting faults. This work presents a comprehensive modeling, identification, and validation framework for the reliable estimation of both individual and coupled interactive fault parameters, with the key novelty in the integrated modeling with AMB and simultaneous numerical and experimental fault identification under gyroscopic effects generated by an offset disc configuration. The developed rotor model incorporates major faults, including unbalance, residual shaft bow, angular coupling misalignment, and internal damping associated with coupling looseness. The misalignment is modeled through equivalent excitation, introducing multi-harmonic components into the system dynamics, enabling a realistic representation of misalignment-induced vibration behavior. Furthermore, multiplicative interaction loads arising from the combined influence of misalignment and residual bow are included in the dynamic formulation. The identification framework is formulated in the frequency domain using a least-squares-based algorithm to simultaneously identify system and fault parameters, and tested under various noise and modelling errors. The algorithm is validated through experimental investigations using a developed test rig replicating the numerical model, where responses recorded under different operating conditions are used for parameter estimation. The reliability of the identification approach is assessed by multi-dataset statistical repeatability analysis employing mean, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation. Further validation is performed by comparing numerical and experimental results for fundamental frequency, orbit patterns, and full-spectrum signatures. The remarkable agreement between numerical and experimental results demonstrates the effectiveness and resilience of the proposed identification framework.

title: Adversarial representation learning for generalizable remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) through domain generalization has recently been introduced to address the challenge of domain bias in unseen conditions. Current approaches primarily focus on extracting domain-invariant features from multiple source domains. However, obtaining valuable failure data from different machines or operational settings is difficult, as most available datasets are derived from a single condition. This paper presents a novel Adversarial Representation Learning (ARLearn) framework, which includes three modules designed for cross-domain RUL prediction under unseen conditions using only one source domain. The first module, responsible for generating diversity, augments data to mimic the unseen target domain. To further enhance the generated data’s utility, a diversity enhancement module is employed to refine its distributional properties. Additionally, a discrimination preservation module is incorporated to retain the semantic information of the generated data, thereby improving the model’s resilience to noise. Extensive experiments conducted on two public datasets confirm the proposed method’s effectiveness and superiority.

title: Adaptive fuzzy practical prescribed-time fault-tolerant constraint control for active suspension systems against time-varying actuator faults
abstract: Active suspension systems improve vehicle ride comfort by actively regulating suspension parameters to adapt to varying driving conditions. However, the control of active suspension systems is confronted with challenges arising from parameter uncertainties, nonlinear dynamics and actuator faults. To address these issues, this paper proposes an adaptive fuzzy practical prescribed-time constrained control method for active suspension systems in the presence of time-varying actuator faults. A fuzzy logic system with adaptive parameter estimation is adopted to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics and lumped uncertainties of the system. The controller design takes actuator faults into account to achieve targeted control for fault scenarios. In addition, a novel adaptive modulation function is developed to adjust the controller output amplitude and suppress overshoot. Through rigorous Lyapunov-based analysis, the uniform ultimate boundedness of all closed-loop signals is guaranteed. Simulation and experimental results under multiple operating conditions demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control method in complex road environments, thus providing a reliable technical solution for the engineering application of active suspension systems.

title: Physics informed terahertz multi-label dual adversarial network for intelligent identification of composite overlapping defects under variable testing conditions
abstract: Composite overlapping defects, occurring between the interfaces in multilayer composite, bring great challenges for accurate structural integrity evaluation due to the complexity and unpredictability. Terahertz (THz) technique, as a novel nondestructive testing (NDT) method, has emerged great potentials for complex multilayer composites. However, current THz feature extraction methods, including physics-driven and pure data-driven methods, mainly focus on the identification of simple defect form, such as single non-overlapping defect, while ignoring the applicability of multiple overlapping defects. In addition, the variations of THz testing conditions can cause the variations of THz signals from the same sample, which will inevitably degrade the generalization performance of methods. Therefore, in this work, a physics informed THz multi-label dual adversarial network (PI-THzMDANet) is proposed for intelligent identification of composite overlapping defects under variable testing conditions. It includes a data alignment layer, a multi-label classification layer, and the dual adversarial network. Initially, the data alignment layer is constructed to align the different temporal THz signals in data space based on the transmission and variation characteristics of THz wave. Then, the multi-label classification layer with multi-attention class encoding module (MACE) is innovatively proposed to accommodate the output form of composite overlapping defects. Finally, the dual adversarial network, including the global and local adversarial learning processes, is proposed to improve the generalization performance of PI-THzMDANet under different THz testing conditions by aligning the source and target THz data in latent feature space. The experimental results indicate that the effectiveness of proposed PI-THzMDANet for intelligent identification of composite overlapping defects under variable testing conditions, which provides a novel paradigm for the structural integrity evaluation of complex defect forms in multilayer composites in THz NDT.

title: Interpretable multiscale algorithm unrolling network using learnable Gabor filters for fault diagnosis
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis has emerged as a pivotal research area in intelligent maintenance systems, stressing interpretable intelligence and trustworthy decision-making for reliable and safe engineering applications. To this end, this study proposes the Interpretable Multiscale AlGorithm unrolling Network using learnable Gabor filters (IMAG-Net). Specifically, IMAG-Net establishes a physically optimization-unrolling framework that integrates learnable Gabor filtering with multiscale convolutional sparse coding, embedding the sparsity prior of fault-induced into a trainable neural architecture for adaptive and interpretable fault diagnosis. Distinct from traditional deep learning approaches, the proposed framework enhances interpretability and decision transparency through structured convolutional sparse coding and adaptive multiscale decomposition, where Gabor filters with learnable center frequencies automatically capture dominant signal components that correspond to fault characteristic frequencies and their harmonics. To further ensure physical fidelity, the learned multiscale representations are analyzed alongside sparsity-guided signal reconstructions derived from salient sparse activations, thereby validating the reliability and internal consistency of the network’s decision logic. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a diagnostic accuracy exceeding 94% under high-noise conditions (σn=1.0), consistently outperforming conventional deep learning baselines while preserving physically meaningful and interpretable diagnostic representations.

title: System-level degradation modeling and remaining useful life prognosis for stochastically deteriorating feedback control systems
abstract: Predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of stochastically deteriorating feedback control systems at the system level is challenging due to their inherent fault tolerance. This property masks true degradation behind seemingly normal behavior, complicating degradation-based RUL prognosis. To mitigate these negative effects, we propose an inspection strategy using a low-efficiency controller, activated only during inspections, to reveal degradation through step response analysis. This allows us defining the L∞-norm of the step response as system-level degradation index and modeling its evolution as a nonlinear stochastic diffusion process with age- and state-dependent drift and diffusion. Failure occurs when this index exceeds a critical threshold. For RUL prognosis, we apply transformations, including translation, the Lamperti transform, drift approximation, and the Ricciardi transform, to convert the model into an equivalent Brownian motion with a nonlinear failure function. In particular, the “drift approximation” step ensures that the age- and state-dependent drift and diffusion are not constrained to specific forms typically assumed in conventional transformation procedure. A tangent-like method is then used to compute the RUL distribution. Numerical experiments on an inertial platform’s stabilization loop device validate our prognosis method. Numerous comparisons with alternative degradation indices, conventional inspections, and learning-based prognosis confirm its superior performance.

title: Nonlinear dynamic modeling and characteristics analysis of slewing bearings considering tooth meshing-bearing coupling for rotary cranes under eccentric loads
abstract: Eccentric load is a typical operating condition for rotary cranes, which significantly affects the dynamic performance of key slewing bearings. To accurately reveal the dynamic behavior of single-row four-point contact ball slewing bearings under dynamic eccentric loads, a systematic study is conducted. Based on Hertz contact theory and deformation compatibility, the nonlinear restoring force of dual contact pairs under combined axial force, overturning moment and radial load is derived. The time-varying meshing stiffness of the driving gear is calculated via the potential energy method, and a time-varying nonlinear friction torque model considering viscous, sliding and elastic hysteresis friction is established. A 9-degree-of-freedom(DOF)tooth meshing-bearing coupled dynamic model is developed and solved by the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method, with its validity verified by vibration tests. The influences of eccentric loads on contact behavior, friction characteristics and vibration responses are analyzed. Results show that the overturning moment causes misalignment of the outer gear ring, thus intensifying system dynamic responses. This work provides theoretical support for slewing system optimization and fault diagnosis, laying a foundation for improving the reliability of heavy-duty rotary machinery.

title: Tunable flexural wave beamforming based on the coupled acoustic vortex with structural Luneburg lens
abstract: The Luneburg lens is a symmetrical gradient index lens with a refractive index that increases radially from the outer surface toward the center. Owing to its distinguished wave-control properties, this lens is widely employed in energy conversion systems, waveguiding applications, and transducer integration. This research innovatively combines a structural Luneburg lens with acoustic vortices on a thin-plate platform, enabling tunable flexural wave steering through frequency-modulated excitation. Through integrated theoretical analysis, computational modeling, and empirical investigations of vortex wave transmission characteristics across the lens structure, our findings demonstrate that acoustic vortex wave beamforming can be obtained after passing through the structural Luneburg lens. The direction of the beamforming can be tuned via changing the excitation frequencies or topological charges, providing a direct and straightforward method for acoustic vortex beamforming, which enhances acoustic vortex sensing and beam scanning capabilities.

title: Conditional diffusion-based time–frequency data augmentation with multi-scale coordinate attention for diesel engine fault diagnosis
abstract: Diesel engine vibration signals are characterized by multi-source impulsive excitations and strong non-stationarity. The scarcity of fault samples and severe class imbalance make it difficult for existing generative models to simultaneously achieve high generation quality and effective diagnostic improvement after augmentation, and often lead to attenuation of mid- and high-frequency textures as well as over-smoothed edges in generated time–frequency images. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-scale time–frequency coordinate-attention conditional diffusion model (MSTFCA-CDM) for fault time–frequency sample augmentation in diesel engines. Continuous wavelet transform (CWT) time–frequency images are used as the generation target, and a multi-scale time–frequency coordinate-attention module is embedded into the conditional diffusion framework to enhance the representation of impulsive structures at different scales and critical time–frequency regions. In addition, a frequency-domain consistency loss is introduced to constrain the two-dimensional spectral magnitude distributions of the predicted and true noise, thereby improving the recovery of mid- and high-frequency textures and local edge details. Experiments on the TBD234 diesel engine dataset show that the proposed method achieves better performance than the compared methods in terms of generation quality, distribution consistency, and augmentation-assisted diagnostic performance within the investigated experimental setting. When the sample ratio between the normal class and each fault class is gradually balanced from 20:1 to 1:1, the classification accuracy improves from 58.34% to 98.90%. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of multi-scale modeling, coordinate attention, and frequency-domain consistency constraints. The results suggest that MSTFCA-CDM is effective for fault time–frequency sample augmentation and diagnosis under severe class imbalance in a controlled experimental setting.

title: High-order multiscale symbolic transfer diversity entropy: A novel complexity measure with application to aero-engine bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Multiscale diversity entropy (MDivE) quantifies nonlinear signal complexity by constructing pattern probability distributions across multiple scales using cosine similarity. However, its coarse-graining mainly relies on a mean operator, which may over smooth bearing fault signals and consequently attenuate critical impulsive and transient components. Moreover, MDivE estimates entropy from pattern occurrence statistics at each scale and does not explicitly account for temporal transitions among pattern states, which limits its ability to capture fault induced dynamic evolution. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a high- order multiscale symbolic transfer diversity entropy (HMSTDE). HMSTDE incorporates time-shifted segmentation and a high-order amplitude difference operator to strengthen the dynamic response of fault impulses while preserving multiscale compression. In addition, symbolic transition analysis is implemented by constructing a state transition matrix and computing entropy over the transition distribution, thereby embedding temporal ordering and directional information into the feature representation. Simulation studies and experiments on multiple aero-engine bearing datasets demonstrate that HMSTDE provides improved noise robustness and fault class separability compared with MDivE and other widely used entropy measures. These results indicate that merging enhanced multiscale coarse-graining with transition modeling yields an effective complexity indicator for aero-engine bearing fault feature extraction.

title: Simultaneous inversion of elastic modulus and thickness in thermal barrier coatings using harmonic surface acoustic waves
abstract: Accurate measurement of thermal barrier coating (TBC) thickness has long been challenging due to variations in coating elastic modulus caused by processing inconsistencies and lamellar heterogeneity, which necessitate specimen-specific pre-calibration in conventional methods. To address this issue, this study proposes a calibration-free approach based on grating laser-induced multi-harmonic surface acoustic waves (SAW) for the synchronous inversion of thickness and elastic modulus. By utilizing the multi-frequency dispersion characteristics of SAW harmonics, the method dynamically compensates for modulus fluctuations in real time. A theoretical model was established to relate multilayer dispersion information to characteristic harmonic frequencies, systematically analyzing the influence of thickness and effective modulus on SAW frequency distribution. A finite element model was further developed to validate the feasibility of multi-harmonic excitation. By combining the forward model with the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, reliable parameter inversion was achieved. Experimental results on actual TBC samples demonstrated a relative thickness error within 10 % across the typical 100–600 μm range compared to scanning electron microscopy (SEM) benchmarks. The results confirm that this multi-harmonic framework realistically captures the inherent heterogeneity of plasma-sprayed coatings, offering a robust theoretical and algorithmic foundation for future high-temperature and in-situ health monitoring in extreme environments.

title: Understanding biases in machine learning-based strain predictions for fighter aircraft
abstract: The use of machine learning models for strain prediction in aircraft structural health monitoring has shown a considerable interest in recent years. The confidence we can place in these models however depends on our ability to understand when and why they can make biased predictions, which is particularly important in critical applications. In fatigue monitoring, such biases may shift the mean stress level of the reconstructed signal and therefore affect fatigue damage estimation. In this context, our work investigates the origin of systematic prediction biases observed when estimating strains from standard flight parameters on a fighter aircraft. Similar biases were already mentioned in the literature, but no in-depth study was dedicated to their analysis. About a hundred flights of a Rafale fighter aircraft was used for this study. An amount of 20 input variables was also used for strain predictions, some of them representing environmental measures and other ones the flight controls. Our study identifies the source of bias in three steps. It first shows that the biases are not due to model-specific limitations, but rather to the data and/or physics-driven mechanism. We then combine explainability tools with aeronautical expertise, which shows that the trained models over-emphasize inertial variables, which govern high-frequency strains, while variables describing the flight environment have substantially weaker influence. Building on this insight, we finally decompose the measured strains into inertial components and environmental baselines. Each part is predicted separately using exclusively physically relevant variables. Interestingly, only the environmental baseline carries the systematic bias, while the inertial part is reconstructed accurately. These findings demonstrate that bias originate from the environmental contribution of the strain signal, with temperature effects emerging as a plausible root cause. The study thus provides a principled diagnostic framework for identifying and interpreting bias mechanisms in data-driven structural monitoring.

title: Torsional vibration suppression for an electro-mechanical transmission system under driving conditions using a dual-channel adaptive control strategy
abstract: As a core component of heavy-duty hybrid electric vehicles, the Electro-Mechanical Transmission (EMT) system is susceptible to output shaft torsional vibrations induced by engine torque fluctuations, which significantly compromise ride comfort and component reliability. To address this issue, this paper proposes an active torsional vibration control method. First, a dual-loop decoupling control framework (DDCF) based on torsional vibration feedback is established, in which the main loop is responsible for power output control and the secondary loop is responsible for torsional vibration suppression. Within the secondary loop, a dual-channel control strategy (DCCS) is designed to allocate torsional vibration suppression tasks with different frequency characteristics to different motors. A dual-channel adaptive control method incorporating multi-harmonic narrowband and wideband disturbance compensation is developed. Specifically, a narrowband multi-harmonic adaptive disturbance control algorithm implemented via Motor A and a filtered minimum variance adaptive control algorithm implemented via Motor B are designed. Finally, the results of simulations, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests, and bench tests demonstrate that the proposed strategy can effectively attenuate output torque fluctuations under steady-state operating conditions while maintaining vehicle dynamic performance during dynamic driving scenarios involving mode transitions.

title: A new method for monitoring the wear state of grinding wheel based on similar pattern
abstract: Grinding is a finishing operation in which process efficiency and quality largely depend on the condition of the grinding wheel. Acoustic emission (AE) monitoring method has been widely used for wear detection due to its high sensitivity and non-destructive installation. However, effective interpretation of AE signals remains challenging due to irregular grain distribution, process complexity, noise, and large data volumes. To overcome these limitations, a similarity-based pattern recognition method is proposed to monitor the wear of grinding wheels. An improved method based on arrival and end times has been developed to automatically extract AE signals during grinding. Multi-source data were collected. The surface roughness of the workpiece is used to define wear stages. The power, force, and wheel surface morphology data are employed to verify classification accuracy. AE signals are analysed to extract features of different wear states. For signal alignment, a wavelet packet denoising method driven by similarity is applied to identify key frequency bands, followed by cosine similarity (CS) analysis. The correlations between CS and conventional features with workpiece surface roughness are analysed. The selected features are used to train an artificial neural network (ANN) model. Its prediction performance is compared with the random forest (RF) model. The classification results confirm that the extracted feature set provides effective discriminative information for different wear stages. In the diamond grinding wheel experiment, the proposed method could accurately distinguish between the medium and rapid wear stages, while in the chromium corundum grinding wheel experiment, it could accurately identify the severe wear stage.
