Feature comparisons before and after filtering and alignment demonstrates that the relationship between AE signals and grinding wheel wear is effectively captured by the proposed method. Grinding experiments under different scenarios further verifies the applicability of the proposed method. Therefore, it provides a reliable and efficient solution for accurate wear identification and shows strong potential for industrial applications.

title: A robust approach for vehicle load identification based on physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold network
abstract: Overloaded vehicles may induce fatigue damage and accelerate pavement deterioration, potentially leading to cracking and even catastrophic bridge failures. Vehicle load information is essential for bridge safety assessment and maintenance. The vehicle load can be inferred by the bridge influence lines (ILs), and the accuracy of vehicle load identification depends critically on the reliable extraction of ILs from measured bridge responses induced by a calibrated truck. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have been widely investigated to incorporate physical relationships between measured responses and ILs into the learning process, enabling vehicle load identification with limited data. Existing PINN-based methods typically rely on multilayer perceptron architectures with limited interpretability and insufficient capability for precisely representing ILs. Measurement noise, vehicle-bridge dynamic interaction effects, and incomplete calibration information can interfere with PINN-based IL identification, thereby undermining the accuracy of vehicle load estimation. This paper proposes a physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (PIKAN) for robust vehicle load identification. First, by embedding the physical relationships into the learning process, the proposed method enables the joint optimization of ILs and vehicle axle weights, even when partial axle weights of the calibration vehicle are unknown. Second, the PIKAN architecture enhances functional representation capability under noise and dynamic effects. Third, multi-location bridge response data are utilized to enhance the robustness and accuracy of vehicle load identification. A computational vehicle-bridge interactive model and a nine-span bridge are employed to assess the performance of the proposed method PIKAN for vehicle load identification. The results demonstrate that PIKAN achieves high accuracy and strong robustness in vehicle load identification.

title: Circular Halbach flexible electromagnetic energy harvesting from rotating machinery: design, modeling and experiments
abstract: Condition monitoring of critical rotating components, such as shafts, bearings, and gears, is essential for the reliable operation of industrial machinery and the prevention of catastrophic failures. However, existing energy harvesters often fail to meet the requirements for self-powered condition monitoring because of insufficient output power and bulky form factors, which limit their practical deployment in space-constrained industrial environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a circular Halbach flexible electromagnetic energy harvester (CHFEEH) with enhanced power density. The proposed device integrates a Halbach magnet array with flexible printed circuit (FPC) coils, enabling magnetic flux concentration and improved spatial adaptability. A theoretical model based on the surface magnetic charge method is developed to predict the voltage output response of the CHFEEH, and finite element simulations are performed to compare the magnetic flux distribution of three magnet array configurations and identify the optimal design. Experimental results validate the accuracy of the proposed model with a maximum error of 3.44%, and demonstrate an output power of 1783.0 mW at 296 rpm, corresponding to a volume- and linear-velocity-normalized power density of 10.58 mW/(cm3∙(m/s)2). Practical demonstrations further confirm its ability to charge a 0.22F supercapacitor and power a wireless sensor node for vibration monitoring. These results indicate that the proposed CHFEEH provides a compact and high-performance solution for self-powered sensing in low-speed rotational applications.

title: A Bayesian modal identification method considering latent excitation effect based on physics-data fusion model
abstract: Modal identification under operational conditions is extensively used in long-term structural health monitoring to identify the dynamic characteristics of structures. However, external excitations like wind and traffic loads have a significant effect on the structural dynamic properties. Conventional modal identification methods without considering such impact will lead to biased estimation of dynamic properties. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Bayesian modal identification method integrating a structure dynamic model with a Gaussian Process (GP) to identify the dynamic properties of structures while simultaneously capturing the effects of excitation variations. Recognizing the impracticality of directly measuring external excitations such as vehicular loads and wind forces, this study employs modal force power spectral densities as indirect indicators of excitation intensity. The identified power spectral densities are utilized as inputs for the GP, and a latent function is proposed that quantifies the influence of excitation variations on dynamic properties. A variational-Laplace generalized Expectation-Maximization algorithm is developed to jointly identify the dynamic properties as well as the hyperparameters of the GP model. Validation using four synthetic examples demonstrates that the proposed method can accurately and reliably identify modal parameters with reduced bias under varying excitation conditions. Applications to in-situ data from a full-scale bridge and typhoon-response data from a super-tall building further validate its practicality and robustness under real operational conditions.

title: An updating prediction interval field method for embankment settlement based on Unscented Kalman Filter considering spatial variability propagation with sparse measurements
abstract: The spatial variability of mechanical properties can significantly impact the accuracy of structural settlement prediction. The non-probabilistic prediction interval field method is developed as a complementary tool when a complete probabilistic analysis is not supportive. However, identifying spatial variability in practical scenarios remains challenging, particularly when measurement data are sparse and limited. In this study, an updating interval field method is proposed by integrating a novel correction algorithm, the Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF), into a deterministic interval finite element method (IFEM). The UKF-IFEM framework is established to account for uncertainties in the characterization of spatial variability, propagation through predictors, and calibration toward measurements. The method combines truncated Karhunen-Loève decomposition, Galerkin approximation, and the secondary development of a finite element platform. The prior eigenvalues are iteratively calibrated using sparse measurement data based on a reference set of 6 measurement points through the coupling UKF-IFEM framework, enabling iterative updating of the entire displacement interval response field. The proposed method is validated through application to a rockfill dam. Results demonstrate that the initial interval field closely matches that obtained from the vertex method while requiring fewer computations. The updated interval responses exhibit a narrower range and progressively converge toward the measurements. The method presented in this paper has the potential to facilitate real-time structural uncertainty analysis under conditions of spatial variability and limited observations.

title: Design of an auxetic defect-mode superlattice structure for enhanced piezoelectric energy harvesting
abstract: The low energy density and conversion efficiency of environmental vibrations hinder piezoelectric energy harvesting and its application in self-powered wireless sensor networks. To address this issue, this work innovatively integrates defect-mode phononic crystals and auxetic structures to create three types of auxetic defect-mode phononic crystal meta-plates, including elliptical perforated (EPCM), missing-rib chiral (MPCM), and double-arrowed re-entrant (DPCM). These are compared with a solid defect-mode phononic crystal meta-plate (SPCM) and a plain plate. The results indicate that the DPCM exhibits superior energy harvesting performance, with an output power 26.2 times and 68 times greater than that of the SPCM and the plain plate, respectively. Mechanism analysis reveals that the defect-mode phononic crystal localizes vibration energy to increase input mechanical energy density. The auxetic substrate provides the same-sign average stress that avoids charge cancellation and induces stress concentration, and the double-arrowed re-entrant angle further enhances this concentration, thereby improving electromechanical conversion efficiency. Based on these findings, a parametric study has been conducted using an experimentally validated model to investigate the effects of various parameters on the DPCM’s energy-harvesting efficiency. The results reveal that the beam thickness in the double-arrowed structure significantly affects the DPCM’s resonant frequency. Furthermore, modifying the short beam side length can substantially enhance the energy harvesting performance of the DPCM. These findings provide theoretical support for the application of defect-mode superlattice structures in self-powered systems.

title: Approximation of structural intensity from experimental structural response data using a hybrid method − methodology, verification, and validation
abstract: Structural intensity is a response quantity that allows visualization and quantification of the vibrational power flow in structures. Numerical simulations allow for easy calculation, i.e., by combining standard result datasets of finite element analysis. However, this is not the case for experimental data, where usually an incomplete set of response quantities (i.e., just translational responses) of a subset of the degrees of freedom of the corresponding finite element model serves as the fundamental dataset to compute the structural intensity. This paper provides a comprehensive guide for a hybrid method that allows the calculation of structural intensity on arbitrary surfaces in three-dimensional space. The hybrid method utilizes experimentally acquired structural response data as an input. The corresponding measurement point locations build a mesh with associated trial functions. Furthermore, we verify the methodology utilizing numerical data to quantify the method's accuracy. Moreover, comparing structural intensity fields acquired from a numerical model and measurement data helps to validate the proposed approach further. Finally, the methodology supports engineers in utilizing the concept of structural intensity to optimize mechanical systems in terms of structural dynamics, e.g., the smart application of damping elements to control system dynamics efficiently.

title: Stability analysis of a coupled nonlinear shaker-structure system in fixed frequency voltage control tests
abstract: Recent research has exploited the coupled electromechanical shaker-structure dynamics to experimentally stabilize structures with various types of nonlinear physics, including strongly nonlinear vibro-impacts. Experimental continuation was achieved through fixed frequency voltage control tests leveraging the force drop-out phenomena caused by the coupled shaker-structure interaction. Through simulated and experimental studies, previous work has demonstrated that moving the shaker to active drive points near the target resonance stabilized the coupled shaker-structure system such that the intermediate, unstable branch was measured through the reconstructed S-curves. This research seeks to validate this stabilization behavior of the coupled system using a coupled nonlinear shaker-structure finite element model to predict the response of the fixed frequency voltage control tests at different drive points. First a linear model of the electromechanical shaker-structure system was created and validated through a shaker system identification and linear modal test comparison where the linear mechanical and electrical parameters of the shaker were identified. The fixed frequency voltage control tests at varying levels of voltage input were then used to compare the S-curves between the model and experiments to validate the fully nonlinear shaker-structure model with contact nonlinearity. The stability of resultant S-curves at different shaker drive points was analyzed using the harmonic balance method and Floquet theory. The Floquet multipliers were calculated to quantify the stability of the periodic solutions and evaluate the types of bifurcations present in fixed frequency voltage control tests.

title: An early-fusion framework integrating vision and vehicle dynamics for adaptive tire–road friction coefficient estimation
abstract: Accurate estimation of the tire–road friction coefficient (TRFC) remains challenging under complex driving conditions, particularly when vehicle excitation is insufficient and friction observability is degraded. To address this issue, this paper proposes an early-fusion framework for TRFC estimation, which integrates visual road-surface perception with vehicle dynamics-based estimation within a probabilistic filtering framework. A visual perception module based on an improved EfficientNet-DeepNet network is developed to extract discriminative features from road-surface images under varying environmental conditions. To establish a physically interpretable connection between visual perception and friction estimation, a class-wise Gaussian prior modeling strategy is introduced, mapping visual classification probabilities to continuous friction estimates with associated uncertainty. The visual priors are directly incorporated into a Sage–Husa adaptive unscented Kalman filter as pseudo-measurements, enabling early-fusion of visual and dynamic information at the estimation level. This tightly coupled fusion strategy allows visual perception and vehicle dynamics to jointly influence the filtering process, rather than using visual information only as an external correction after the filter update. Simulation and real-vehicle experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves improved estimation stability and responsiveness under low-excitation driving and abrupt friction transition conditions, compared with the dynamics-only approach and conventional fusion methods.

title: In-band noise-suppressed bidirectional reweighted cyclostationary analysis for acoustic emission-monitored fault diagnosis
abstract: Weak fault-induced transients generated in the early stages of gear drive degradation are frequently buried beneath strong in-band noise caused by complex resonance and modulation phenomena, which poses a major challenge for accurate feature extraction from acoustic emission (AE) signals. To address this issue, this study proposes an In-band Noise-suppressed Bidirectional Reweighted Cyclostationary Analysis (IN-BRCA) method for AE-based fault diagnosis of gear reducers. The proposed framework constructs a spectral coherence matrix as the analytical foundation and introduces two complementary mechanisms. Along the spectral frequency direction, a multi-kernel maximum mean discrepancy measure is employed to adaptively reweight frequency subbands according to their divergence from healthy references, thereby enhancing fault-related spectral contributions. In the cyclic frequency direction, differential residual operations emphasize fault-induced cyclic components that are absent in healthy signals, while a rotational interference suppression weighting mechanism and a harmonic product spectrum strategy jointly amplify weak modulation features and attenuate in-band noise. Extensive experimental verification on planetary gearboxes and harmonic reducers confirms the superior diagnosis performance and robustness of the proposed method compared with several state-of-the-art benchmarks.

title: Pixel-wise adaptive structural color patterning on non-planar metals using a compact self-sensing vibration cutting system
abstract: Vibration-assisted diamond cutting has emerged as a promising route to high-quality structural color fabrication; however, achieving pixel-wise patterned structural colors on non-planar metallic surfaces remains challenging. Traditional constant force-based adaptive depth control is limited in this setting because patterned cutting requires frequent modulation of cutting velocity, which directly influences the cutting force along with the actual cutting depth. In this study, a pixel-wise adaptive vibration cutting strategy combined with automatic tool setting is proposed to address these challenges. First, a compact (58 mm × 39 mm) self-sensing elliptical vibration cutting device with an embedded piezoelectric element is developed, enabling real-time cutting depth sensing without external dynamometers or complex mechanical structures. Then, an estimation model of actual cutting depth is established and parameterized by the cutting velocity and the measured amplitude of the piezoelectric sinusoidal voltage. Based on this model, a PID feedback control strategy is implemented to adaptively regulate the cutting depth to a constant setpoint during structural color fabrication. Moreover, automatic tool setting based on the intelligent vibration cutting device is employed to mitigate the influence of initial fluctuations in the actual cutting depth along the cross-feed direction. Finally, by adopting the proposed control approach, high-quality structural color patterns with a pixel size of 0.27 mm × 0.27 mm have been successfully fabricated on non-planar aluminum workpieces, exhibiting significantly improved pattern integrity. In sum, the proposed method provides a simple, reliable, and scalable solution for adaptive patterned structural color fabrication without a pre-flatten process.

title: Waveform command shaper design based on the designed fixed-output response method for residual vibration mitigation in an underactuated double-pendulum crane system with hoisting and lowering
abstract: Overhead crane systems in industrial settings often face residual vibration problems during point-to-point payload motion with hoisting and lowering actions. This paper presents the design and validation of a smooth waveform command shaper for residual vibration elimination in double-pendulum crane systems with time-varying cable length, using the Designed Fixed-Output Response (DFOR) method. The dynamic model of the double-pendulum crane is derived and linearized yielding a coupled, time-varying system of equations. The two-mode system is decoupled to establish an analytical relationship between the hook and payload swing angles, enabling a single-mode command shaper to simultaneously suppress both pendulum modes. The time-varying system is transformed into an equivalent time-independent formulation by substituting the initial cable length as a fixed design parameter. A three-harmonic waveform command acceleration profile is designed, and its closed-form parameters are analytically derived. The main contribution of this paper is that the resulting smooth waveform command shaper is derived entirely in closed-form and can generate continuously differentiable acceleration trajectories that follow actuator constraints without requiring iterative numerical optimization or frequency modulation during operation computation. The method is validated both numerically and experimentally utilizing different hoisting trajectories on a laboratory-scale crane testbed. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the new shaper in eliminating residual vibrations, with residual swing angles below 0.5° across all cases. Comparative evaluation against unshaped and zero-vibration input shaper commands confirms the superiority of the proposed approach. Robustness analysis due to uncertainties in both initial cable length and payload mass shows that residual vibrations remain below 2.5°, confirming the reliability and novelty of the method used to design the smooth waveform shaper for industrial crane applications.

title: A modal high-order moments-based spectral framework for fast full-field non-Gaussian random vibration fatigue analysis
abstract: Large-scale finite element (FE) fatigue assessment under non-Gaussian random vibration remains a computational bottleneck, as conventional spectral methods lack accuracy while time-domain transient simulations are prohibitively expensive. This paper proposes a unified and high-efficiency computational framework that resolves this dilemma by combining a physics-based spectral correction model with an efficient moment-computation algorithm. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that kurtosis is insufficient to characterize fatigue damage, and establishes the b-th order moment of stress amplitude as the governing descriptor linking signal statistics to material fatigue properties. Based on this insight, a new spectral correction model is derived and systematically validated using 5,800 synthesized signals covering diverse spectral shapes and non-Gaussian intensities. To enable practical frequency-domain FE implementation, a modal-based tensor formulation combined with an Even-Anchor Logarithmic Interpolation strategy is developed, allowing high-order response moments to be computed analytically from modal properties without time-domain reconstruction. The framework is validated on a fine-meshed cantilever beam model with over 27,000 nodes, achieving fatigue prediction accuracy comparable to rainflow counting (relative errors below 9% in critical regions) while providing a computational speedup of nearly 350 times. The proposed framework offers a fully spectral, scalable, and efficient solution for non-Gaussian vibration fatigue assessment in large-scale structural systems.

title: Measurement of high-frequency vibration modes using event cameras and low-rank tensor completion
abstract: Various optical methods have been developed to visualize and measure dynamic structural behaviors, such as vibration modes and frequency spectra, for detecting fastener loosening and crack propagation. However, capturing high-frequency vibration modes typically requires high-speed cameras, which involve substantial power consumption, data volume, and cost. This study addresses these challenges by introducing a vibration measurement method based on an event camera, which records only logarithmic changes in luminance, combined with rectangular tracking and low-rank tensor completion for displacement reconstruction. The proposed method was experimentally validated through vibration measurements of a 630-mm-long polyvinyl chloride pipe and a coil spring. The results demonstrated that the method can quantitatively measure displacement waveforms under single-frequency, multi-frequency, and band-limited noise excitation conditions. For the pipe vibration tests, the normalized mean squared error (MSE) of the measured displacement waveform was less than 3% at relatively large displacement amplitudes of approximately 0.5 pixels, corresponding to 0.25 mm. Even at smaller amplitudes of approximately 0.1 pixels, corresponding to 0.05 mm, the MSE remained below 25%, demonstrating that the proposed method can quantitatively measure subpixel vibrations. The vibration modes exhibited a modal assurance criterion ≥ 0.9 under all test conditions, demonstrating excellent agreement with finite-element method results. Additionally, the proposed approach successfully detected changes in vibration modes caused by loosened bolted joints. The upper frequency measurement limit was assessed using an ultrasonic transducer experiment, achieving quantitative displacement spectrum measurements at a vibration frequency of 19.75 kHz and amplitudes of 30.1–37.6 μm. The mean MSE was below 10% for frequencies above 1 kHz. However, since ultrasonic vibrations are extremely subtle, it is necessary to zoom in significantly to capture them, and we have not yet been able to measure the vibration modes; this will be a topic for future research.

title: An improved dynamic model for defective Inter-Shaft bearing incorporating rolling element dimensions and Multi-Impact vibration behavior analysis
abstract: Aero-engine inter-shaft bearings in dual-rotor systems are subjected to dual rotational speeds, leading to highly complex defect-induced vibration behavior. Existing dynamic models for defective inter-shaft bearings are predominantly based on lumped-mass formulations and simplified displacement-based defect models. As a result, they neglect the finite geometry and centrifugal effects of rolling elements (REs) and fail to capture multi-stage contact transitions and the resulting multi-impact vibration mechanisms. To address these limitations, this study develops an improved dynamic model for defective inter-shaft bearings, in which the finite geometry of REs, the geometric interaction between REs and defects, and the centrifugal effects of REs are explicitly incorporated. Based on the geometric relationship between REs and defect size, a classification criterion is proposed to distinguish two defect types: line-spall defects and extended-spall defects. The results reveal that extended-spall defects induce pronounced multi-impact vibration behavior. The underlying physical mechanism is clarified by analyzing the distinct contact states between REs and the defect leading edge, defect bottom, and trailing edge. Specifically, interactions with the defect leading edge produce a low-frequency step response associated with a de-stressing state, whereas interactions with the defect bottom and trailing edge generate multiple high-frequency impulsive responses corresponding to successive re-stressing states. Compared with conventional displacement-based models, the proposed model captures the full sequence of contact transitions and provides a physically consistent description of multi-impact excitation mechanisms. The transmission of impact vibrations from the inter-shaft bearing to the rotor structure is further investigated, showing that the impulsive characteristics are preserved despite significant amplitude attenuation. Quantitative validation through simulations and experiments demonstrates strong agreement in impact timing, characteristic frequencies, and energy distribution across time, frequency, time–frequency, and envelope domains. These results confirm the capability of the proposed model in accurately characterizing defect-induced multi-impact vibration behavior and provide a reliable basis for defect severity assessment in inter-shaft bearings.

title: Improving monocular pose variation estimation with displacement amplification effect of CCD Moiré patterns
abstract: Monocular pose variation estimation measures the six-degree-of-freedom variations of a camera coordinate system in 3D space using images captured pre-motion and post-motion. As a pivotal technique in photogrammetry, it supports diverse measurement applications, including measurement correction on unstable platforms and non-line-of-sight deformation monitoring using distributed cameras. However, the accuracy of existing methods remains insufficient for high-precision applications. Through systematic simulation, this study identifies the displacement measurement accuracy of markers in images as the decisive factor governing overall monocular pose variation estimation performance. Motivated by this finding, a high-precision monocular pose variation estimation method leveraging the displacement amplification effect of CCD moiré patterns is proposed. The method employs a periodic grating as the cooperative marker, utilizes the periodically amplified CCD moiré patterns formed by the superposition of the grating real image and the imaging sensor, and achieves high-precision measurement of the grating marker displacement in images through phase analysis. By combining the displacement amplification effect of CCD moiré patterns with monocular pose estimation methods, the proposed method significantly improves pose variation measurement accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate angular variation accuracy of 0.0005° (1.8 arcseconds) and displacement accuracy of 0.002 mm (equivalent to 0.006 pixel in the image plane) within a 210 mm × 168 mm field of view. Requiring only a cooperative target replacement, this method is fully compatible with existing monocular pose estimation systems and has been successfully applied to error correction in photogrammetry under vibration conditions, offering significant theoretical and practical value for high-precision pose variation measurement.

title: A long-stroke fast tool servo system equipped with floating stator and its application in ultra-precision machining
abstract: Long-stroke fast tool servo (FTS) systems have been widely applied to the machining of freeform surfaces. However, the inertial force generated by long-stroke motion still constitutes a key bottleneck restricting the improvement of machining accuracy for such systems. In this paper, a balanced long-stroke fast tool servo (BFTS) system integrated with a voice coil motor (VCM), an aerostatic guideway and an inertial balancing device is designed. Aiming at the conventional mounting scheme in which the VCM of traditional FTS systems is fixed on the machine tool, this study proposes a structural improvement scheme featuring a floating stator, drawing on the flexible tool-tip guiding design concept of FTS. Two rectangular thin plates are employed to suspend the stator of the VCM, thereby realizing the balancing of inertial forces.This study adopted a combined method of theoretical calculation, finite element analysis, and experimental verification to systematically investigate the influence laws of the stiffness of rectangular thin plates, the mass of the counterweight system, and the operating frequency of the BFTS on the inertial force attenuation effect. Theoretical analysis and experimental test results show that when the operating frequency of the BFTS is 30 Hz, the inertial force output by the VCM decreases from 10 N to less than 1 N.Experiments confirm that the inertial balancing system does not affect the system bandwidth. Moreover, the thrust ripple of the VCM introduced by the inertial balancing system is negligible. Finally, inclined surface turning experiments confirm that the proposed inertial balancing system can significantly improve the surface quality of machined workpieces. The system can meet the precision requirements for the ultra-precision machining of optical components with high aspect ratios.keywords:Fast tool servo; Counterbalance ; Rectangular thin plate ; Inertial balance ; Finite element analysis

title: Adaptive and robust motor intent decoding for cross-day dexterous finger force predictions
abstract: Motor intent decoding based on neural signals provides a promising pathway for intuitive human-robot interactions. Among various neural signal sources, binary spiking activities of motor units (MUs) serve as a reliable basis for intent decoding. However, the non-stationary nature of MU action potential poses a major challenge for robust intent decoding. To address this issue, we developed an adaptive motor intent decoding framework that dynamically refined the MU pool to maintain cross-day reliability. The framework integrated three modules: (1) a cross-validation component for selecting MUs with consistent decoding performance across days, (2) a flag policy to exclude inactive and inaccurate MUs based on temporal activation consistency, and (3) a refinement component to retain only finger-specific MUs that can lead to accurate individual finger force predictions. We validated our new approach by quantifying finger force performance. We obtained high-density surface electromyographic (sEMG) recordings over three days. We then performed adaptive source separation to extract neuronal firing spikes for subsequent motor intent decoding. We also demonstrated the feasibility of our approach during real-time control of a robotic finger. The results demonstrate that our developed adaptive motor intent decoder consistently achieved higher prediction accuracy across multiple days than the non-adaptive decomposition method. Compared with deep learning approaches, our approach outperformed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), while achieving comparable performance to CNN-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) across days. These findings highlight the robustness of MU-level adaptive motor intent decoding in overcoming cross-day neural signal variations, thereby contributing to the development of accurate and robust signal processing strategies for reliable and practical applications in human-robot interactions.

title: Robust dynamic contrastive learning framework for wear fault diagnosis of hydrodynamic mechanical seals with imbalanced samples
abstract: To enable reliable diagnosis of rare wear faults in Hydrodynamic Mechanical Seals (HDMS) of reactor coolant pumps under extreme long-tailed distributions, this paper proposes a Robust Dynamic Contrastive Learning (RDCL) framework. Traditional methods struggle to address the safety-constrained data imbalance and the stringent need for false-alarm suppression in nuclear monitoring. To bridge this gap, RDCL builds upon the SURE architecture with four safety-driven innovations: 1) safety-aware feature balancing through class-frequency-weighted manifold alignment, 2) noise-robust feature compactness with dynamic scaling factors, 3) safety-margin boundary regularization expanding margins for high-risk categories, and 4) a dynamic secondary auxiliary network that adjusts loss function weights based on feature states. Experimental results on an HDMS dataset demonstrate the superiority of our method. Specifically, RDCL achieves a peak classification accuracy of 99.78 % and a harmonic mean accuracy of 99.80 %, significantly outperforming the SURE baseline and other state-of-the-art models. Crucially, it achieves an observed FPR95 of 0.00 % on the evaluated benchmark split under the optimal configuration, indicating strong empirical false-alarm suppression capability in safety–critical nuclear monitoring. Furthermore, robustness evaluations reveal that RDCL maintains strong performance under compound stress involving 20 % training data availability and severe noise interference at 3 dB, achieving a mean ACC of 92.91 ± 1.33 % and a harmonic mean accuracy of 94.88 ± 1.08 %, thereby providing solid support for high-reliability operation.

title: A novel semi-active control method for flexible manipulator’s residual vibration based on a parallel magnetorheological damping structure
abstract: In order to solve the problem of energy-efficient control of residual vibration for space flexible manipulator caused by arm-flexibility, a new semi-active vibration control method based on a parallel magneto-rheological damping structure (PMRDS) is proposed. Firstly, the dynamic transmission characteristic of PMRDS is analyzed and a novel solid–liquid two-phase constitutive model of MR damper is proposed to describe the phase transition effect of MR fluid on the boundary condition of flexible manipulator. Secondly, by segmenting the manipulator at the installation position of PMRDS, the rigid-flexible coupling dynamic model of the flexible manipulator with PMRDS is established based on Euler-Bernoulli beam theory and Lagrange equation. Thirdly, the influence of input current, installation parameters of PMRDS and operation parameters of manipulator on system performance is analyzed by numerical simulation. Then, based on the obtained vibration control mechanism, an anti-solidification control strategy is proposed. Finally, the experimental study is carried out by a self-built test bench, the feasibility of PMRDS, the accuracy of the theoretical model and the effectiveness of the anti-solidification control strategy are verified. The results show that the proposed method can effectively suppress the residual vibration of flexible manipulator; compared with the fixed input current control, the anti-solidification control improves the vibration suppression efficiency by 43.23% on average under different operating conditions. The research can provide reference for the application of magnetorheological damping in vibration control of flexible structures.

title: Noise-firewall: mitigating pseudo-label poisoning in semi-supervised fault diagnosis via parameter decoupling
abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis in industrial settings faces the dual challenges of scarce supervision and label noise. Although semi-supervised learning (SSL) can leverage unlabeled data, it becomes fragile under label noise because corrupted supervision distorts representation learning and subsequently contaminates pseudo-labels, causing confirmation bias and error propagation. To mitigate this issue, this paper proposes a Noise-Firewall framework that couples robust representation learning with SSL via additive parameter decomposition (ω=σ + γ) and dynamic regularization. The σ-branch is encouraged to learn stable fault representations, while the auxiliary γ-branch absorbs noise-induced optimization pressure, thereby structurally shielding σ from corrupted labels. Built upon the protected σ-branch, Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Labeling (CAPL) is further developed: pseudo-labels are generated strictly from σ predictions, and the γ-branch is frozen during pseudo-label backpropagation to prevent pseudo-label poisoning. Extensive experiments under multiple noise types (20%/40%) and up to 40% unlabeled data on two public benchmarks—Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and Paderborn University (PU)—validate the mechanism and stability of the proposed components, and further perform systematic comparisons with representative SSL methods on a real robotic belt-grinding dataset. For example, on CWRU with 40% symmetric noise, accuracy improves from 61.8 ± 6.9 to 78.6 ± 1.1; under the joint setting of 40% symmetric noise with 40% unlabeled data, PU and the robotic dataset reach 93.15% and 90.2% accuracy, respectively. Finally, γ is discarded at inference, enabling a “train-complex, infer-simple” deployment with no additional inference overhead.

title: Sensor informativeness, identifiability, and uncertainty in Bayesian inverse problems for structural health monitoring
abstract: In Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), the recovery of distributed mechanical parameters from sparse data is often ill-posed, raising critical questions about identifiability and the reliability of inferred states. While deterministic regularization methods such as Tikhonov stabilise the inversion, they provide little insight into the spatial limits of resolution or the inherent uncertainty of the solution. This paper presents a Bayesian inverse framework that rigorously quantifies these limits, using the identification of distributed flexural rigidity from rotation (tilt) influence lines as a primary case study. Fisher information is employed as a diagnostic metric to quantify sensor informativeness, revealing how specific sensor layouts and load paths constrain the recoverable spatial features of the parameter field. The methodology is applied to the full-scale openLAB research bridge (TU Dresden) using data from controlled vehicle passages. Beyond estimating the flexural rigidity profile, the Bayesian formulation produces credible intervals that expose regions of practical non-identifiability, which deterministic methods may obscure. The results demonstrate that while the measurement data carry high information content for the target parameters, their utility is spatially heterogeneous and strictly bounded by the experiment design. The proposed framework unifies identification with uncertainty quantification, providing a rigorous basis for optimising sensor placement and interpreting the credibility of SHM diagnostics.

title: Carrier tuning and ESNet for harmonic distortion suppression in nanoscale vibration measurement using LDV
abstract: Laser Doppler vibrometry enables noncontact, high precision full wavefield measurement and imaging of ultrasonic guided waves, greatly improving inspection resolution and broadening the range of applications. However, in ultrasonic guided wave scenarios excited by a piezoelectric transducer, the combined effects of nanoscale vibration responses and strong noise cause the Lissajous curve of the nonorthogonal I/Q baseband signals to degenerate into an arc segment broadened along the normal direction, which renders traditional ellipse fitting algorithms ineffective. To address the above problem, a carrier tuning and ESNet based method for harmonic distortion suppression in nanoscale vibration measurement using laser Doppler vibrometer is proposed. First, an adaptive carrier tuning scheme is designed, where the tuning offset between the tuned carrier and the original carrier is dynamically adjusted to compensate the phase of the I/Q baseband signals, transforming the degraded arc into a more geometrically salient valid arc and thereby ensuring accurate extraction of ellipse parameters. Second, an ESNet based ellipse fitting network is constructed, in which a two-stage ellipse parameter regression scheme and a center annealing strategy are incorporated during training to mitigate error propagation while accelerating model convergence, enabling accurate and robust regression of ellipse parameters under strong noise. This substantially improves the orthogonality of the I/Q baseband signals and thus effectively suppresses harmonic distortion. Finally, experimental results under nanoscale vibration conditions demonstrate that the proposed method achieves remarkable harmonic distortion suppression, reducing total harmonic distortion by 92.2% compared with traditional methods, providing an innovative approach for vibration measurement in non-destructive testing.

title: Physics-informed stereo vision for structural displacement measurement with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Accurate displacement measurement with uncertainty quantification is essential for structural vibration testing and health monitoring. However, existing vision-based methods process frames independently without leveraging structural dynamics knowledge, limiting computational efficiency and robustness under challenging conditions. This paper proposes a Physics-Informed DIC framework integrated with Stereo Vision and Temporal filtering (PI-DIC-SVT) that reformulates vision-based displacement measurement as a physics-constrained Bayesian state estimation problem. Three key contributions are presented: (1) a physics-guided search constraint that leverages Extended Kalman Filter predictions to adaptively reduce the search range from ± 30 pixels to approximately ± 10 pixels, achieving 2.5–3.0 × computational speedup; (2) a quality-adaptive Bayesian fusion mechanism that ensures robust tracking under adverse imaging conditions; and (3) a multi-source uncertainty quantification framework that decomposes measurement uncertainty into physically interpretable components. The method was validated through shaking table experiments under sinusoidal and seismic excitations. Results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves sub-millimeter accuracy (RMSE of 0.31 mm) that remains below 0.5 mm even under ± 50% natural frequency mismatch, while providing reliable uncertainty estimates with 94.3% coverage rate for 95% confidence intervals.

title: A physics-informed dual-stream convolutional neural network method for in-situ continuous bolt preload monitoring and detection
abstract: Accurate perception of bolt preload is crucial for ensuring the reliability and safety of critical equipment such as aero-engines, high-speed trains, and wind turbines. To address the limitations of existing data-driven methods, including poor interpretability, heavy reliance on labeled data, and weak out-of-distribution generalization, this paper proposes a Physics-informed Dual-stream Convolutional Neural Network (PI-CNN) method for bolt preload detection. The core of the method lies in embedding the experimentally verified linear physical relationship between the square of natural frequency of bolt vibration and the preload into the neural network training process in the form of a gradient consistency loss. The model adopts a dual-channel 1D-CNN architecture to extract features from the raw vibration acceleration signals and their frequency spectra separately. It then incorporates handcrafted feature, specifically the squared natural frequency, to construct a data-physics dual-driven loss function. This design constrains the model predictions not only to fit the data but also to strictly adhere to known physical law, thereby significantly enhancing the physical interpretability of the model. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method, guided by physical principles, markedly improves model interpretability, reduces dependency on labeled data, and enhances generalization performance under unseen working conditions, offering an efficient data-physics dual-driven solution for bolt preload detection.

title: Discrete variable topology optimization for large-scale high-order eigenvalue problems by high-frequency harmonic excitation response surrogate method
abstract: Large-scale high-order eigenvalues topology optimization of dynamics holds significant engineering and theoretical value. However, many challenges remain, including the high computational cost of large-scale high-order eigenvalue analyses, repeated eigenvalues caused by densely packed eigenvalue spectra, and real modal order shifting caused by gray densities and weak structural connections. To address them, an efficient high-frequency harmonic excitation response surrogate method is proposed. Firstly, a theoretical demonstration is provided that by carefully selecting high-frequency harmonic response loads, the manipulation any order eigenvalues (either increasing or decreasing) can be achieved under the unified minimum dynamic compliance. Based on this theorem, computationally expensive high-order eigenvalue problems can be replaced by a computationally efficient high-frequency harmonic excitation response optimization problem. Secondly, the Real Modal Identification Method (RMIM) is proposed to address real modal order shifting, thereby enabling the efficient acquisition of the required harmonic load parameters. Finally, since high-frequency harmonic response optimization can trigger prominent gray densities issues under continuous variable topology optimization, the discrete variable topology optimization framework, i.e., Sequential Approximate Integer Programming (SAIP) is used. Numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively solve the large-scale high-order eigenvalue and eigenvalue gap optimization for both 2D and 3D structures. As the discretization of the design domain increases, the proposed method can directly produce multi-scale superstructures that simultaneously achieve high-frequency vibration isolation and load-bearing properties.

title: Remote vibration-based debonding identification in hidden-frame glass curtain walls using a UAV-mounted LDV system
abstract: Structural adhesive debonding in hidden-frame glass curtain walls is a concealed damage mode that can compromise facade safety, while conventional manual and contact-based inspections are inefficient and difficult to apply to high-altitude building envelopes. This study proposes a remote, non-contact, and nondestructive vibration-based debonding identification framework using an unmanned aerial vehicle-mounted laser Doppler vibrometry system. A custom-developed remote excitation device, used in coordination with the measurement system, is experimentally validated to provide stable modal excitation comparable to that of hammer testing. To reduce measurement errors caused by unmanned aerial vehicle flight instability, a data- and physics-driven compensation method is developed by integrating finite-element analysis with real-time flight logs, enabling vibration responses to be more accurately reconstructed from noisy aerial measurements. The proposed framework is validated through full-scale experiments with progressive structural adhesive debonding. The results show that the reconstructed vibration responses effectively capture debonding-induced dynamic degradation and support quantitative damage identification. Based on the equivalent damage degradation parameter (d), three panel-specific risk states are defined: Safe (d ≤ 11.25 %), Warning (11.25 % < d ≤ 26.75 %), and Danger (d > 26.75 %). This study provides a remote vibration-sensing and assessment framework for high-altitude curtain wall inspection, offering a basis for quantitative structural maintenance and safety decision-making.

title: Time-domain nearfield acoustic holography with wavelet preprocessing for identifying transient pulse sources under harmonic interference
abstract: Time-domain nearfield acoustic holography (TNAH) effectively identifies transient sound sources but has difficulty in identifying pulse sources obscured by harmonic interference, a common scenario in mechanical faults. This limitation occurs because the conventional TNAH processes full-bandwidth time-domain signals, preventing clear differentiation between harmonic and pulse sources. To overcome this challenge, a modified TNAH method with wavelet preprocessing is proposed. The approach employs the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and the inverse CWT (ICWT) to extract pulse components within target frequency bands from the measured sound signals, effectively suppressing harmonic interference. Subsequent sound field reconstruction employs the time-domain equivalent source method (TESM) — a TNAH technique suitable for arbitrarily shaped sources — applied to the wavelet-filtered time-domain signals, enabling independent identification of pulse sources. Theoretical analysis confirms that the wavelet-filtered time-domain signals remain consistent with the acoustic transfer relationship governing the TESM, thereby establishing the physical validity of the methodology. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the method can effectively separate and accurately identify weak pulse sources under strong harmonic interference, substantially outperforming the conventional TESM and the TESM with wavelet post-processing. Experiments on a compressor further validate the practical effectiveness of the method in identifying faults that generate pulses. This work provides an effective technical solution for identifying transient pulse sources in complex acoustic environments.

title: Improved vehicle-bridge interaction element including speed effects for time-varying modal analysis
abstract: An improved vehicle–bridge interaction (VBI) element for modal analysis is proposed in that vehicle’s forward motion is explicitly included. Effects such as Coriolis and centrifugal forces, related to bridge inclination and curvature, were omitted in existing VBI elements. They are included by expressing the vehicle response relative to the vehicle-bridge contact point in addressing the time-varying properties of the VBI systems. The improved element is verified against analytical solutions and validated through inverse identification using simulated signals of a periodic multi-vehicle scenario, demonstrating that it is more suitable for modal analysis than existing VBI elements. Theoretical and numerical studies lead to the conclusions: (1) vehicle speed effects slightly intensify the extreme variations of system frequencies; (2) vehicle speed effects may cause abnormal instantaneous bridge damping ratios, but only lead to a slight increase in the mean bridge damping ratio; (3) for heavy high-speed VBI systems, vehicle speed effects should be carefully considered, as they may no longer be negligible in modal analysis. A link to the improved VBI element in MATLAB is given at the end of the paper.

title: Digital twin-enhanced framework for rolling bearings fault diagnosis under imbalanced and open-set conditions
abstract: Deep learning-based fault diagnosis is constrained by inherent data imbalance and the presence of unseen fault types. While digital twins can augment data through simulation, the idealized signals they produce exhibit distribution discrepancies with measured data and cannot model atypical faults, leading to limited generalization in practical open-set environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a digital twin-enhanced diagnosis framework for rolling bearings under imbalanced and open-set conditions. First, a Physics-Consistent Data Fusion Strategy (PCDFS) is proposed to align simulated data with measured signals in a physics-statistical feature space, thereby generating high-quality digital-twin-enhanced data for training. Second, an Adaptive Prototype Open Network (APONet) is proposed to perform fine-grained domain adaptation and learn a structured feature space with prototype-based representations. On this basis, a class-adaptive threshold is introduced to reliably detect atypical faults that are unseen during training. Finally, experiments on a drivetrain diagnostics simulator and wind turbine gearboxes demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Hybrid Kalman filter and physics-informed long short-term memory network for enhanced fault diagnosis of aircraft angle-of-attack sensors
abstract: Angle-of-attack (AoA) sensor faults have historically contributed to several aviation accidents. To address this issue, a sensor fusion-based fault diagnosis framework is introduced that integrates first principles of physics with sensor data. A reduced-order aircraft model that incorporates sensor biases and gains is first developed using first principles of physics. This model is used to propose a two-stage fault detection scheme: an extended Kalman filter (EKF) innovation monitoring with covariance regularization (IMCR) for initial fault detection and Euclidean bias/gain deviations (EBGD) for fault confirmation. A physics-informed long short-term memory (PILSTM) network is then trained as a virtual sensor for use in the case of dual AoA faults. Finally, a fault mitigation method is developed to determine the appropriate actions in the event of a fault. It uses the IMCR-EBGD fault detection, aircraft sensor redundancy, and the PILSTM virtual sensor. The full framework is validated using flight data from the Advanced Technologies Testing Aircraft System (ATTAS) under both fault-free and fault-injected conditions. The proposed method detects ramp-type AoA faults within 0.18 s and yields a lower 95% Clopper–Pearson false alarm upper bound under fault-free scenarios. A sensitivity analysis incorporating Gaussian noise shows the proposed method achieves a lower false alarm rate. Furthermore, under the dual AoA fault test, the best estimation performance was obtained when the PILSTM loss function included a 15% contribution from the physics-informed loss function. These results demonstrate that hybridizing data-driven learning with first principles of physics improves fault diagnosis in complex sensor environments.

title: A data-mechanism fusion modeling approach for tracking error prediction and compensation in dual-drive feed system
abstract: The dual-drive feed system (DDFS) is widely used in high-precision manufacturing equipment, but electromechanical coupling, asymmetric dual-axis dynamics, and nonlinear friction can cause significant positioning and tracking errors. To improve motion accuracy, this paper proposes a proactive error compensation strategy based on a data–mechanism fusion model (DMFM). A rigid-flexible electromechanical coupling model is established to capture the dominant tracking-error characteristics, and a CNN-BiLSTM residual predictor is introduced to learn nonlinear and time-varying residual errors that cannot be fully described by the mechanism model. The predicted compensation sequence is generated in advance and superimposed on the original position command without changing the original three-loop servo-control structure. Experimental results show that the proposed DMFM reduces the positioning error standard deviation by up to 83.9% compared with the CCC-P strategy. Machining validation and comparisons with mechanism-only, data-only, and disturbance-observer-based compensation strategies further confirm the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the proposed DMFM provides an accurate and industrially applicable solution for improving the positioning, tracking, and contouring accuracy of DDFS under actual machining conditions.

title: Ensemble learning for safety-critical fault detection in industrial distillation: A comprehensive benchmark with noise robustness analysis
abstract: Deep Learning architectures dominate fault detection research in industrial environments. However, their high noise sensitivity and black box nature pose risks to processes with strict safety requirements. We benchmark 26 classification configurations (eleven base algorithms, four sequential deep-learning baselines (1D-CNN, LSTM, CNN–LSTM, TabNet) and four ensemble strategies) ranging from traditional statistical methods to Machine Learning and DL on a 9-class fault detection problem on an operational distillation column. Three results merit emphasis. First, Voting (Calibrated) attains the highest mean balanced accuracy (87.79%), narrowly ahead of Random Forest (87.44%); the two are not statistically distinguishable. Three of the four ensembles tested are significantly worse than Random Forest alone and probability calibration, not ensemble diversity, is what allows soft-voting to recover information that majority voting and stacking discard. Second, as a result of Friedman–Nemenyi analysis over 150 cross-validation evaluation, the top tier (Voting Calibrated, Random Forest) is separated from a mid-field clique of fifteen statistically indistinguishable methods, including XGBoost, SVM-RBF, four DL baselines, and the remaining ensembles. On this dataset, deployment choice should be driven by robustness and interpretability rather than marginal accuracy differences. Third, Synthetic Minority Over-sampling TEchnique (SMOTE) response is determined by model architecture: every classical model tested degrades or is unaffected, while every deep-learning architecture benefits. SMOTE should not be applied as a default for tree-based, kernel, or distance-based learners. A noise-robustness benchmark covering Gaussian, α-stable, and autoregressive corruption reveals a near-complete inversion between clean and noisy rankings: Random Forest, the top clean-data base model, ranks seventh under noise, while K-Neighbors rises from mid-field to first. We introduce the feature necessity metric to distinguish statistical contribution from operational necessity, identifying sensors that require hardware redundancy despite low statistical visibility.

title: A dimensionality reduction method for probability density evolution method based on manifold learning
abstract: The probability density evolution method and the physical synthesis method provide a scientific approach for calculating the probability density of stochastic system responses and time-varying global reliability. To accelerate the computation, surrogate modeling techniques have been widely adopted. However, the high dimensionality of both input and output variables poses a critical challenge to constructing high-precision surrogate models. A common approach to addressing this issue is low-dimensional feature mapping, which involves simultaneously reducing the dimensionality of input and output variables, establishing a mapping relationship in the reduced low-dimensional space, and then projecting back to the original space. Current low-dimensional feature mapping methods, such as proper orthogonal decomposition, principal component analysis, active subspace method, are primarily limited to capturing linear low-dimensional relationships, often neglecting the intrinsic manifold structure of data points. This paper introduces a nonlinear subspace-based method for input dimensionality reduction, combined with an output dimensionality reduction technique based on manifold learning, to construct a novel class of high-precision low-dimensional feature mapping surrogate models. The proposed framework is successfully applied to probability density evolution method and the physical synthesis method.

title: Configuration identification methodology for nonlinear spring–damper–inerter absorber design: Theoretical analysis and experimental study
abstract: While the integration of nonlinear stiffness and inerter elements has been shown to broaden suppression bandwidths and reduce physical mass, existing research has primarily focused on a few fixed layouts, leaving the vast space of potential structural topologies largely unexplored. This paper proposes a systematic configuration-optimization methodology for nonlinear spring–damper–inerter absorbers, inspired by the structure-immittance approach. The generic networks covering all the candidate absorber layouts are identified, with which the dynamic model of a primary structure is established. The steady-state responses are derived via the harmonic balance method, while the stability of the solutions is evaluated through Lyapunov’s first method. Building upon these results, optimal absorber parameters are identified by balancing control effectiveness with system stability. Furthermore, the physical realization of the proposed absorber is developed and modeled, with its performance validated through numerical simulations and experimental tests that account for parasitic effects. The impact of identified parasitic nonlinearities on the system response is analyzed, leading to a refined absorber design with enhanced vibration suppression, while further robustness assessment considering parameter uncertainties, manufacturing tolerances, parasitic-effect variations, and long-term parameter drift is identified as an important direction for future work.

title: Filtered output approximation perspective on blind deconvolution
abstract: Blind deconvolution (BD) methods, such as minimum entropy deconvolution (MED) and maximum second-order cyclostationarity blind deconvolution (CYCBD), are widely adopted in rotating machinery condition monitoring to extract defect-induced repetitive transients under noise and interference. However, the implicit filtered output preference induced by BD remains insufficiently understood, and resulting optimal outputs may deviate from intended fault-related components. This article establishes a filtered output approximation (FOA) framework by introducing a relaxed optimization problem to explicitly interpret the preferred structure of optimal filtered outputs. Under this perspective, MED is proven to drive optimal filtered outputs to a single impulse, and optimal solutions of CYCBD may not correspond to genuine cyclostationary filtered outputs. To mitigate such ambiguity, an improved method, termed uniformity-regularized CYCBD (UR-CYCBD), is proposed by incorporating a uniformity regularizer, which suppresses non-cyclostationary patterns and enables more reliable identification of fault-related components. Moreover, a numerical example and a bearing run-to-failure case study demonstrate the effectiveness of UR-CYCBD.

title: Broad-range continuous load adaptability with electromagnetic constant-force compensated stair-step quasi-zero-stiffness vibration isolators
abstract: Traditional quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) vibration isolators suffer from high sensitivity to load variations and limited adaptation ranges. To overcome these drawbacks, this paper proposes a broad-range continuous load adaptability regulation method with a novel electromagnetic constant-force compensated stair-step quasi-zero-stiffness vibration isolator (EMCF-SQZS-VI). The stair-step quasi-zero-stiffness (SQZS) characteristic is constructed with a rectangular magnet array to realize discrete load adaptability, while a semi-active electromagnetic constant-force (EMCF) is designed to continuously adjust the load deviation within any QZS range. The static and dynamic models of EMCF-SQZS-VI are established. The effects of structural parameters on EMCF, and of EMCF on static load adaptability, are evaluated. The load adaptability of EMCF-SQZS-VI is verified numerically and experimentally. The SQZS vibration isolator can adapt discrete loads, and the EMCF mechanism further compensates for load deviation continuously within any QZS range. This ensures that EMCF-SQZS-VI with a 3 × 2 magnet array achieves continuous load adaptability from 0 to 6 kg while maintaining excellent low-frequency vibration isolation performance. This work provides a guideline for designing SQZS vibration isolators with continuous load adaptability via EMCF compensation.

title: Reconciling the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in stochastic wind field simulation: A dual-level parallel algorithmic perspective
abstract: This study presents a high-performance, fully parallelized computational framework for stationary and non-stationary stochastic wind field simulation that reconciles the conflict between computational efficiency and spectral fidelity. The framework reformulates the classical Shinozuka spectral representation method into a dual-level parallel algorithm that (i) eliminates nested spatial loops for computing pairwise spectral densities with array broadcasting and (ii) parallelizes frequency-wise synthesis via vectorized mapping, transforming the original sequential complexity into fully parallelizable operations. Unlike existing computational acceleration techniques that rely on dimension reduction or frequency interpolation, this reformulation maintains complete spectral fidelity without introducing approximation errors. To bound peak memory use while preserving full spatial coherence, the framework integrates an adaptive frequency batching strategy for large-scale problems. A multi-backend implementation (JAX, PyTorch, NumPy) enables efficient deployment on CPUs and GPUs. Extensive benchmarks show significant performance improvements, achieving speedups of up to several thousand-fold compared with conventional methods and demonstrating superiority over other mainstream algorithms. Practical applications to several engineering case studies, with comparisons to field measurements and theoretical models, validate the accuracy and reliability of the simulated wind fields. This software is released open-source on GitHub to support reproducible research and inspire further innovations in wind engineering.

title: Lightweight off-grid Bayesian inference: A low-complexity and high-precision sparse reconstruction method
abstract: Blade tip timing (BTT) is an effective non-contact vibration measurement method for monitoring the condition of rotating blades owing to its high efficiency and long service life. However, due to its limitations in the number of sensors and measurement principles, the BTT signal is often severely undersampled. Although some sparse Bayesian learning-based methods have offered a promising solution to this problem, they either suffer from basis mismatch due to predefined frequency grids or involve computationally intensive matrix inversions, hindering high-precision and real-time BTT signal analysis. To overcome these limitations simultaneously, we develop a lightweight off-grid Bayesian inference (LOGBI) approach for BTT signal post-processing. First, by integrating variational inference with the majorization-minimization principle, we adopt a quadratic surrogate of the original likelihood term in the Bayesian formulation. Under the variational expectation–maximization framework, the posterior covariance is approximated in a diagonal form, thereby avoiding explicit matrix inversion process. Meanwhile, the corresponding M-step is equivalent to a standard convex quadratic optimization problem, resulting in a tighter surrogate and improved inference stability. Then, to compensate for the weakened suppression of highly correlated atoms caused by the diagonal transformation, a Bayesian information criterion-guided peak selection strategy is further introduced to filter out spurious peaks and provide reliable coarse frequency initialization results. Subsequently, a Levenberg–Marquardt-based local refinement strategy is applied to calibrate the identified frequency candidates and achieve high-precision parameter estimation. Finally, extensive numerical simulations and experiments demonstrate that LOGBI effectively mitigates basis mismatch while significantly reducing the computational cost of classic Bayesian methods.

title: A noise-corrected data-driven approach for nonlinear dynamical system modeling in frequency domain
abstract: The development of parsimonious and accurate models is highly dependent on the quality of training data. To extract the underlying physical laws from noisy data, we introduce a noise-corrected data-driven approach. It begins by formulating a nonlinear sparse least-squares problem in the frequency domain, where noise correction terms and physical parameters are treated as unknowns. To solve this problem, we present a novel nested Levenberg-Marquardt (LM)-Sequential Thresholded Least-Squares (STLS) approach, which inherits the strengths of LM algorithm for solving nonlinear optimization problems and the sparsity-promoting capabilities of the STLS. This approach also offers a simple and intuitive way to incorporate prior physical knowledge into the sparsification process, preventing small coefficient terms from being pruned due to excessively large thresholds. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated by both numerical simulations and experimental tests. The results indicate its effectiveness in extracting underlying dynamic structures from measured data, which might be corrupted not only by white noise but also by distorted streaming.

title: Fast multiscale order-frequency spectral correlation estimator with sparse prior for rotating machinery signals
abstract: Recent research indicates that rotating machinery signals often exhibit cyclostationarity under constant speed and angle-time cyclostationarity under variable speed. Correspondingly, two core statistical descriptors—the spectral correlation (SC) and order-frequency spectral correlation (OF-SC)—are estimated via the averaged cyclic periodogram (ACP)-based or cyclic modulation spectrum (CMS)-based estimators. CMS-based estimators are widely favored due to their reduced computational cost compared to ACP-based estimators; however, their performance remains subject to the time–frequency resolution trade-offs inherent to short-time Fourier transform (STFT)-based implementations. In particular, the detectable range of periodic modulation components is limited by the resolution characteristics of the STFT. To address this limitation from a scale-adaptive perspective, the continuous wavelet transform is incorporated into the CMS-based estimators within the cyclostationary framework, resulting in the wavelet CMS (WCMS) estimator for SC estimation. This estimator is further extended to the angle-time cyclostationary framework, yielding the order-frequency WCMS (OF-WCMS) for estimating OF-SC. Moreover, inspired by the prior knowledge that modulation components in many practical rotating machinery signals exhibit sparsity, a modified sparse fast Fourier transform algorithm is integrated to improve computational efficiency along the cyclic frequency or cyclic order axis. This leads to the sparse WCMS (SWCMS) and order-frequency SWCMS (OF-SWCMS) estimators. The proposed estimators are comprehensively evaluated in terms of resolution characteristics, computational complexity, and observable cyclic frequency/order range. Simulation results using typical cyclostationary and angle-time cyclostationary signal models indicate that the proposed estimators can detect a broader range of periodic modulation components while maintaining low computational cost. Two application cases further demonstrate their practical applicability in prognostics and health management for complex rotating machinery within the existing cyclostationary and angle-time cyclostationary frameworks.

title: Nonlinear impact characteristics of non-circular gears under backlash excitation based on harmonic balance method and optimization strategy
abstract: To solve the problem of tooth impact during the service of non-circular gear pairs, this paper proposes a new scheme for optimizing the basic tooth profile strategy. By establishing a nonlinear vibration model of non-circular gear with backlash excitation and solving the analytical solution of the model based on harmonic balance method, the nonlinear response characteristics under multiple meshing states were analyzed. The impact state, instantaneous transition frequency, and vibration characteristic distribution law of the non-circular gear system were obtained, and the key factor affecting the smoothness of non-circular gear transmission was determined to be tooth backlash. To reduce the influence of backlash on the transmission stability of non-circular gear transmission systems, non-circular beveloid gears were designed. The mathematical model of was derived, and a transmission test platform was built to verify the superiority of non-circular beveloid gear transmission performance. The research results indicate that the transmission ratio error of the non-circular beveloid gear transmission system is smaller than that of non-circular gears, and the torque error, vibration, and noise are all reduced under the same operating conditions. Therefore, the optimization strategy of variable tooth thickness can alleviate the impact characteristics of non-circular gears within a certain range.

title: Real-time surface defect detection for edge-based inspection via efficient feature learning
abstract: This work presents HARTNet, a high-accuracy, real-time defect detection framework for intelligent mechanical systems. HARTNet introduces a lightweight feature processor with a Deep Global Module (DGM) to effectively capture defect features while maintaining a low parameter footprint. A structured aggregation network is integrated to perform efficient multi-scale feature fusion, thereby alleviating semantic degradation and improving feature representation efficiency. In addition, a weighted loss function is introduced to dynamically adjust sample contributions according to localization quality and sample difficulty, thereby alleviating the negative influence of imbalanced defect distributions and enhancing the learning of rare classes. To overcome the limited nonlinear capacity of existing activation functions, a new function with two tunable parameters is proposed and evaluated under both learnable and fixed settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HARTNet, with only 2.7M parameters, achieves state-of-the-art performance across two challenging industrial scenarios, while the effectiveness of the DGM module is further validated through comparisons with three state-of-the-art baselines. The proposed activation function also outperforms 25 widely used alternatives in terms of both accuracy and feature separability. Finally, HARTNet achieves real-time detection at 22.5 FPS on an edge computing platform. These findings highlight the portability and efficiency of HARTNet in practical engineering applications, such as intelligent manufacturing and quality assurance in mechanical systems.

title: Digital twin assisted surface roughness prediction in milling processes
abstract: In milling processes, surface roughness prediction is essential for enhancing machining efficiency and reducing production costs, as it can effectively save the measurement time. In recent years, data-driven methods have made significant progress in surface roughness prediction research. However, existing methods are highly dependent on sufficient historical data. To overcome this limitation, a digital twin assisted surface roughness prediction method is proposed in this paper, in which abundant simulated data are utilized for model training. First, the dynamic and mechanistic models of milling force and surface roughness are established based on the physical entity of the machine tool to generate simulated data as the corresponding virtual entity. Then, a network architecture integrating mechanistic information and signal features is designed to deep learn surface roughness knowledge from both simulated data and measured data. Furthermore, the maximum mean discrepancy is introduced into the loss function to enable domain adaptation from the virtual entity to the physical entity. Experimental results on a milling dataset under different machining conditions demonstrate the proposed method’s effectiveness. When measured data is limited, the proposed method can improve surface roughness prediction performance, overcoming the typical challenges of data-driven methods.

title: Cohesive mode decomposition
abstract: Impulse signals are common across various engineering and scientific fields. However, extracting impulse components from mixture signals remains challenging due to their complex time–frequency structure. Most existing methods rely on strong prior assumptions (e.g., narrowband or periodicity) and empirical setups, limiting their generality and adaptability. While the data-driven approaches like EMD extract oscillatory modes adaptively, they often fail to capture transient impulse features. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel, fully adaptive impulse decomposition method termed “Cohesive Mode Decomposition (CMD)”, specifically designed to extract impulsive modes based on the fuzzily defined concept of “cohesiveness”. Operating entirely in the time domain, CMD constructs asymmetric filters through a “Dominant-Extrema Exclusion Interpolation” scheme, requiring no pre-defined basis or mode number. It sequentially separates cohesive impulses from the mixture, ending with a residual trend line or carrier. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world signals demonstrate that CMD accurately extracts impulse components with high efficiency and robustness, offering a powerful tool for analyzing transient signals in practical applications.

title: Physics-inspired multiwavelet KAN for interpretable bearing fault diagnosis under harsh operating conditions
abstract: Deep learning models for rotating machinery diagnosis often lack interpretability and suffer severe performance degradation under strong noise. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Physics-Inspired Multiwavelet Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) for robust and transparent bearing fault diagnosis. Building upon the Wav-KAN architecture, we develop a parallel multiwavelet expert framework utilizing Morlet, Laplace, and Mexhat activations to structurally capture complementary fault signatures.
