An adaptive evidence-weighting fusion mechanism is further introduced to dynamically balance expert contributions based on input signal characteristics. Extensive experiments across three bearing datasets, including a complex turbopump test rig, demonstrate the framework’s superior noise robustness. Notably, it achieves 92.05% accuracy on the PU dataset under severe −10 dB noise, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art deep learning, wavelet-based, and single-wavelet KAN baselines. Further analyses show that the learned wavelet scales remain close to theory-derived characteristic scales, that fusion weights vary across fault categories, and that decision attribution focuses on localized fault-related signal regions, providing supportive evidence for the interpretability of the proposed framework.

title: Sparse Gramian Angular Field-Based Bayesian-Weighted Multi-Source domain adaptation for remaining useful life prediction of belt conveyors
abstract: Accurate prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) for belt conveyor idler bearings is essential to ensure continuous transportation and reduce maintenance costs. However, industrial settings often face a shortage of fault samples. Existing domain adaptation methods fail to effectively leverage prior knowledge between inter-source domains to mitigate negative transfer and are further hindered by high computational redundancy when integrated with image coding techniques. To address these issues, a Sparse-Gramian Angular Field-based Bayesian-Weighted Multi-Source Domain Adaptation (SGB-MSDA) method is proposed for the RUL prediction of the belt conveyor idler bearings. The method introduces a Sparse-Gramian Angular Field (Sparse-GAF) adaptive encoding that identifies high-information segments based on information entropy and generates high-resolution images, while low-information segments are represented at lower resolution to retain fault features while significantly reducing computational overhead. An inter-source graph structure alignment strategy is constructed to capture differences in feature distributions across source domains, with feature consistency enhanced via graph regularization. Source-target domain similarity is integrated with inter-source alignment results to design a Bayesian source-domain re-weighting mechanism that dynamically adjusts transfer weights, emphasizing high-correlation sources and suppressing low-correlation sources to mitigate negative transfer. Additionally, domain adversarial learning and discrepancy-based alignment are jointly optimized to obtain domain-invariant representations. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in prediction accuracy, generalization, and computational efficiency. On the coal-mine belt conveyor idler bearing dataset, it achieves MAE and RMSE values of 0.0462 and 0.0618, respectively, improving upon state-of-the-art methods by 20.9% and 26.6%, showing strong promise for industrial applicability.

title: A variable-gain active disturbance rejection vibration control for all-clamped plate with inertial actuator based on time delay estimation: mechanism interpretation and experimental validation
abstract: Active vibration control systems for the all-clamped plate structure are generally subjected to unknown disturbances, including model parameter perturbations, electromechanical coupling nonlinearities, unknown external excitations and sensor measurement noise. To address these issues, this paper proposes a variable-gain active disturbance rejection control method for vibration suppression, which is based on the filtering of the variable-gain extended state observer (VGESO) and the variable-gain tracking differentiator (VGTD). First, to capture the complex dynamic interactions, a comprehensive electromechanical coupling model is formulated for the all-clamped plate driven by an inertial actuator, explicitly accounting for the actuator’s inherent feedback effects. Second, based on the equivalence relationship between time delay estimation (TDE) and the extended state observer, the design criterion of the nonlinear variable-gain function is systematically analyzed and derived, realizing the adaptive dynamic adjustment of the bandwidth along with the real-time error of the system. Meanwhile, to reduce the influence of noise, VGTD is designed on the basis of the conventional tracking differentiator, which provides smooth and accurate state feedback for the closed-loop system. In addition, rigorous theoretical analysis guarantees the uniform ultimate boundedness (UUB) of the estimation errors for both the VGESO and VGTD. Finally, to experimentally validate the proposed control scheme, a hardware-in-the-loop platform utilizing an NI PCIe-6343 data acquisition system is developed. The results of multiple groups of comparative experiments show that the validity of the TDE-based interpretation and the proposed control scheme combining the VGTD and VGESO achieves superior vibration suppression performance compared with other control methods.

title: Phase-delay inversion imaging of low-velocity impact damage in CFRP laminates based on ultrasonic guided wave
abstract: To address the detection of impact damage in composite materials, this study proposes a phase-delay inversion imaging method based on ultrasonic guided wave. The phase compensations corresponding to the spatial positions within the inspection region are applied to the effective frequency components of response signals extracted from different sensors where we account for the elastic anisotropy as well as guided wave dispersion behavior and skewing effect. These delayed signals are then superimposed at the target location to achieve virtual wavefield focusing, with phase coherence ensuring maximum amplitude, thereby indicating the presence of the scattering source, i.e., the damage. To validate the effectiveness, a PZT excitation–SLDV acquisition-based ultrasonic testing method is adopted. Experimental investigations are conducted on two representative CFRP laminates configurations, [0,90]2S and [0, 45, 90, –45]S, in which 3 J and 4 J impacts were first applied to induce damage, followed by measurements of dispersion relation and skewing angle, and finally, response signals were extracted for imaging analysis. To further assess the general applicability, numerical simulations were performed. A mapping modeling strategy, incorporating impact-induced geometric damage features and property degradation effects was developed. Using this model, the imaging performance under broader testing conditions—for example, in a strongly anisotropic [0]8 laminate, as well as in damage scenarios with several orientations and numbers—was investigated. Results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively detect the impact damage in CFRP laminates while maintaining robustness across multiple testing conditions.

title: Stiffness-constrained bandgap tailoring in sinusoidal compression-torsion metamaterials: inverse design and MIGA-PINN optimization
abstract: Effectively attenuating low-to-mid-frequency vibrations while maintaining load-bearing stiffness remains a critical engineering challenge. This study introduces a novel sinusoidal compression-torsion coupling metamaterial, whose vibration bandgap characteristics and mechanical stiffness can be synergistically tailored. Analytical models for stiffness and bandgap boundary frequencies are derived theoretically to provide physical constraints for a physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based forward model. Conversely, a neural network (NN)-based inverse model maps target mechanical properties back to unit cell geometric parameters. Subsequently, a Multi-Island Genetic Algorithm (MIGA)-PINN optimization strategy is implemented to tailor vibration bandgaps to target ranges while satisfying stiffness constraints. The optimization targets include: (1) minimizing the onset frequency of the first bandgap; (2) minimizing the interval between the first two bandgaps; (3) maximizing the bandgap width; and (4) customizing bandgap ranges. Experimental and numerical validations demonstrate the efficacy of both the forward-inverse design and the MIGA-PINN optimization strategy, with predictions showing strong agreement with experimental and simulation data. Notably, an optimized metamaterial subject to a stiffness constraint of 5000 N/m achieves stable vibration attenuation across the 100–1000 Hz range. These findings demonstrate the targeted vibration control capabilities of the metamaterials under stiffness constraints and provide a computationally efficient approach for their rational designs.

title: Editorial Board
An improved unsupervised domain adversarial transfer network for motor eccentricity monitoring assisted by simulation data
abstract: Rotor eccentricity in motors frequently leads to severe vibration. Although deep learning algorithms provide an effective approach for monitoring eccentricity conditions, labeled data for such faults is typically scarce in real-world industrial settings. To address this, we propose a novel unsupervised domain adversarial transfer network, assisted by simulation data, for monitoring motor eccentricity. First, a multiphysics-coupled model integrating electromagnetics and stator structure is established to simulate the vibration response of the stator casing under different rotor eccentricity conditions, thereby generating a simulated dataset with varying eccentricity levels. Then, an electromagnetic–mechanical excitation separation test device is designed to validate the multiphysics model through modal testing. Next, an adaptive wavelet image style transfer network is employed to migrate the “style” of the time–frequency images from the experimental data to those of the simulated data, enhancing their similarity in the time–frequency domain. Finally, the stylized simulated images serve as the source domain, while the unlabeled experimental images constitute the target domain. Within the framework of a domain adversarial neural network (DANN), joint distribution adaptation (JDA) and conditional contrastive domain (CCD) adaptation loss functions are incorporated to jointly optimize the model. Experimental results on the electromagnetic–mechanical excitation separation device demonstrate that the proposed method effectively detects the degree of rotor eccentricity.

title: Adaptive Bayesian grid-free 3D acoustic source imaging for nose landing gear using No-U-Turn sampler
abstract: Conventional on-grid and off-grid methods for 3D acoustic source localization suffer from the curse of dimensionality, while existing grid-free approaches often lack adaptive sampling control and exhibit low efficiency. To address these limitations, an adaptive Bayesian grid-free 3D localization method based on the No-U-Turn Sampler (GF-NUTS) is proposed. Built upon the Bayesian inference framework grounded in equivalent source theory, the proposed method introduces the No-U-Turn Sampler to sample posterior distributions of source positions. This enables efficient exploration of high-dimensional parameter spaces via adaptive step size and step count control through binary tree recursion and dual averaging. Source strengths and noise variance are estimated through fixed-point iteration and projection-based inference, respectively. Finally, a potential-energy-based Bayesian Information Criterion is formulated for adaptive source enumeration. Simulation and experiments involving spatially distributed sources confirm that GF-NUTS outperforms existing on-grid, off-grid, and other grid-free methods in terms of localization accuracy, convergence reliability, and computational efficiency. Finally, the method is integrated with Proper Orthogonal Decomposition to identify and analyze aerodynamic noise sources in a nose landing gear model, enabling both localization and physical interpretation of narrowband and broadband noise mechanisms.

title: A hybrid deep learning framework for reliable and interpretable remaining life estimation in turbofan Engines: Focusing on Robustness, Generalization, and Sensor-Level interpretability
abstract: Reliable prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is crucial for improving maintenance planning and operational safety in turbofan engines. This study proposes a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network–Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN–GRU) framework for prognostic analysis using the NASA C-MAPSS benchmark dataset. The CNN layers are employed to extract local degradation-related features from multivariate sensor measurements, while the GRU structure captures temporal degradation trends over long operational sequences. Beyond conventional accuracy-focused evaluations, the proposed framework emphasizes robustness, reproducibility, and interpretability through a reliability-oriented experimental strategy. Comparative analyses were conducted against standalone CNN and GRU models together with component-level ablation experiments and repeated training runs to assess statistical stability. In addition, SHAP and LIME methods were utilized to provide global and local explanations of model behavior and sensor importance. Experimental validation across FD001–FD004 subsets demonstrates that the hybrid CNN–GRU model achieves competitive prediction accuracy with improved consistency under varying operating conditions and fault scenarios. The explainability analysis further reveals strong dependence on degradation-sensitive thermodynamic sensor signals. Overall, the proposed framework offers an interpretable and reproducible deep learning approach for benchmark aero-engine RUL prediction while also acknowledging limitations related to real-world industrial deployment.

title: Influence of a three-dimensional defect on cage dynamics and vibration behavior in a double-row angular contact ball bearing
abstract: Double-row angular contact ball bearings (DACBBs) are widely applied as critical support elements because of their high rotational accuracy and strong load-carrying capability. However, the local defect inevitably develops during long-term operations, inducing vibration and reducing cage stability. To investigate this problem, a comprehensive dynamic model of a DACBB considering three-dimensional defect geometry is proposed to capture random contacts between the balls and defect edges, as well as defect-induced cage whirl instability. Based on this framework, defect offset is characterized through the axial azimuth angle, while irregular three-dimensional defect morphologies are modeled using a morphology function and a gradient depth function. The influences of defect position, defect range, defect offset, and defect edge-extension effect on the vibration response and cage stability are systematically analyzed. In addition, the collision pattern of the ball within the defect region and the load transfer mechanism induced by the integrated structure of the double-row system are revealed, which are identified as the dominant factors governing the evolution of vibration time–frequency characteristics and cage motions. The results indicate that inner and outer raceway defects exhibit different sensitivities to axial and circumferential defect ranges. Increasing axial defect offset reduces vibration amplitude, whereas the edge extension effect weakens ball-defect impact intensity. Moreover, a combined defect generates a superimposed impact, while the integrated ring structure induces a row-coupled effect and enables load fluctuations to transfer between both rows. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the dynamic analysis of defects in DACBBs.

title: Multi-modal vibration control of composite airfoil structures under varying temperatures: A self-configuring decoupled optimal control strategy
abstract: Composite airfoil structures are widely used in aerospace vehicles. During service, they are frequently subjected to the coupled disturbances of thermal loads and broadband external excitations. Revealing their dynamic behaviors and effectively suppressing multi-modal vibrations remain crucial ongoing challenges. This study develops a coupled thermo-structural-piezoelectric dynamic model for composite airfoils composed of skins, spars, and ribs, and investigates multi-modal vibration suppression using active control techniques. In the modeling process, a layerwise theory is employed to independently describe the displacement fields of the skin and spar-rib layers, accurately characterizing the influence of the spar-rib configuration on the overall dynamic characteristics. Additionally, thermal effects are effectively incorporated by considering both the thermal strain energy induced by thermal expansion and the temperature-dependent material properties. Experimental tests demonstrate that the proposed model can accurately predict the natural frequencies and vibration responses of the structure under varying temperatures. Regarding the control strategy, a self-configuring decoupled optimal control (SCD-LQR) method is proposed. By decoupling multi-modal signals and dynamically updating the state-space model, this strategy achieves online adjustment of optimal control inputs while preventing modal interference. Finally, the effectiveness and robustness of the SCD-LQR strategy for multi-modal vibration control of composite airfoils under varying temperatures are comprehensively evaluated through both simulations and experiments. Comparative tests against a conventional proportional-derivative (PD) controller further validate the superior multi-modal control performance of the proposed method. At room temperature, the vibration suppression rates of the first two structural modes reach 79.1% and 66.9%, respectively. The findings of this study provide a valuable technical reference for the multi-modal vibration reduction of composite structures in thermal service environments.

title: Beyond static models: Hypernetworks for adaptive and generalizable forecasting in complex parametric dynamical systems
abstract: Dynamical systems play a key role in modeling, forecasting, and decision-making across a wide range of scientific domains. However, variations in system parameters, also referred to as parametric variability, can lead to drastically different model behavior and output, posing challenges for constructing models that generalize across parameter regimes. In this work, we introduce the Parametric Hypernetwork for Learning Interpolated Networks (PHLieNet), a framework that simultaneously learns: (a) a global mapping from the parameter space to a nonlinear embedding and (b) a mapping from the inferred embedding to the weights of a dynamics propagation network. The learned embedding serves as a latent representation that modulates a base network, termed the hypernetwork , enabling it to generate the weights of a target network responsible for forecasting the system’s state evolution conditioned on the previous time history. By interpolating in the space of models rather than observations, PHLieNet facilitates smooth transitions across parameterized system behaviors, enabling a unified model that captures the dynamic behavior across a broad range of system parameterizations. The performance of the proposed technique is validated in a series of dynamical systems with respect to its ability to extrapolate in time and interpolate and extrapolate in the parameter space, i.e., generalize to dynamics that were unseen during training. Our approach outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both short-term forecast accuracy and in capturing long-term dynamical features such as attractor statistics.

title: Towards a more realistic evaluation of machine learning models for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Reliable detection of bearing faults is essential for maintaining the safety and operational efficiency of rotating machinery. While recent advances in machine learning (ML), particularly deep learning, have shown strong performance in controlled settings, many studies fail to generalize to real-world applications due to methodological flaws, most notably data leakage. This paper investigates the issue of data leakage in vibration-based bearing fault diagnosis and its impact on model evaluation. We demonstrate that common dataset partitioning strategies, such as segment-wise and condition-wise splits, introduce spurious correlations that inflate performance metrics. To address this, we propose a rigorous, leakage-free evaluation methodology centered on bearing-wise data partitioning, ensuring no overlap between the physical components used for training and testing. Additionally, we reformulate the classification task as a multi-label problem, enabling the detection of co-occurring fault types and the use of prevalence-independent metrics based on the ROC curve. Beyond preventing leakage, we also examine the effect of dataset diversity on generalization, showing that the number of unique training bearings is a decisive factor for achieving robust performance. We evaluate our methodology on four widely adopted datasets: Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), University of Ottawa (UORED-VAFCLS) and Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST bearing). This study highlights the importance of leakage-aware evaluation protocols and provides practical guidelines for dataset partitioning, model selection, and validation, fostering the development of more trustworthy ML systems for industrial fault diagnosis applications.

title: BiMSFNet: A binarized multi-scale feature fusion network for privacy-preserving enhanced diagnosis on edge devices
abstract: Rotating machinery is critical equipment in modern industry, and the health status of its bearings directly affects system safety and efficiency. Due to the complexity of the deep learning diagnostic model and the large number of parameters, it is difficult to deploy it in resource-constrained edge embedded devices in real time, and there is also a risk of data privacy leakage. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Binarized Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network (BiMSFNet) for edge embedded devices. First, in data preprocessing, quantization and bit-plane decomposition convert 2D time–frequency maps into multi-dimensional binary matrices, achieving information transformation and initial privacy protection. Moreover, by leveraging the inherent discretization and non-continuity of the binary neural network itself further resist gradient inversion attacks at the model level. Then, by combining binary neural networks with adaptive weighting, a lightweight model is constructed. Finally, integrating multi-dilation-rate convolutions with adaptive weighting enables multi-scale feature extraction while drastically reducing model size and training cost. Experiments show that BiMSFNet achieves 99.54% average accuracy on a self-built testbed and 99.18% on the SEU bearing dataset with only 0.169M parameters and 17.6MFLOPs, 1–2 orders of magnitude lower than mainstream lightweight models, and effectively resists gradient inversion attacks on the CWRU dataset. Deployed on a Raspberry Pi 5B, inference time is 2.8ms per sample, meeting the real-time, low-power, and privacy requirements of edge scenarios.

title: Extreme reciprocal asymmetric elastic wave energy transport enabled by an ultra-thin, non-deflecting Willis structure
abstract: Signal rectification protects sensor systems that are vulnerable to external disturbances and enables diode-based signal control. Achieving such direction-dependent energy transport, however, typically requires breaking reciprocity through cumbersome devices, which limits practical feasibility. In addition, metamaterial- or diffraction-based approaches often rely on bulky structures or deflect the wave propagation direction, with wave deflection compromising signal fidelity. Therefore, realizing strong asymmetric energy transport in a compact, non-deflecting, and reciprocal device remains elusive. Here, we present a subwavelength mode-coupled Willis-type structure that enables highly asymmetric elastic wave transmission by fundamentally engineering the elastic constitutive relations. By identifying and enhancing the mode coupled Willis coefficients, which are otherwise weak, we establish a systematic route for controlling direction dependent intermodal energy exchange between longitudinal and shear wave modes. Leveraging this mechanism, we demonstrate unidirectional perfect transmission and reflection, in which complete mode converting transmission occurs for one sided incidence while total reflection arises for the opposite direction, all while preserving reciprocity. Ultrasonic experiments in a plate confirm unidirectional perfect mode-converting transmission and reflection for shear-horizontal wave incidence, in good agreement with numerical simulations. Unlike previous approaches, the proposed ultra-thin structure achieves strong asymmetric energy transport while preserving the signal direction and reciprocity, thereby enabling reliable signal communication. As potential applications, we further demonstrate elastic wave diodes and signal isolation, highlighting the practical utility of mode coupled Willis structures for directional wave control.

title: An experimental study on vibration absorber and adaptive-tuning strategy in multi-mode vortex-induced vibration control
abstract: Integrating tuned mass damper inerters (TMDIs) with adaptive-tuning strategies offers a promising solution for multi-mode vortex-induced vibration (VIV) mitigation in long-span suspension bridges. This approach overcomes the inherent limitations of conventional tuned mass dampers (TMDs), namely excessive static elongation and narrow functional bandwidth. Despite its potential, the interaction between the nonlinear fluid–structure coupling of VIV and adaptive control logic, especially in the overlapped lock-in region, remains insufficiently explored. In this paper, a prototype adaptive-tuning TMDI featuring a variable inerter was developed. The single-mode and multi-mode control performances of TMD, passive TMDI, and adaptive-tuning TMDI have been experimentally validated and compared. The results demonstrate that while the introduction of an inerter involves a slight compromise in peak reduction from 91.7 % to 87.9 %, it successfully reduces static elongation to 57.2 % of the standard TMD. Crucially, the adaptive system automatically synchronizes with the shifting dominant VIV mode even in the overlapped lock-in region, enabling robust suppression across multiple modal responses. Furthermore, the applicability of the wake oscillator model for theoretical analysis of VIV control is experimentally confirmed, and a simplified performance evaluation framework based on an equivalent damping ratio is proposed. These findings provide robust experimental evidence for the efficacy of advanced vibration absorbers and adaptive-tuning strategies in mitigating multi-mode VIV.

title: Trajectory generation for NURBS toolpath via reparameterization function with low residual vibration
abstract: High-efficiency and high-quality trajectory generation is crucial for machine tools or industrial robots to execute NURBS toolpath tracking tasks, such as milling. However, the residual vibration induced by motion, which exists in the flexible structures, is a critical factor affecting machining quality. Moreover, traditional two-stage trajectory generation methods do not directly express the trajectory, resulting in difficulties in suppressing residual vibration. To obtain a direct expression of the motion trajectory, a B-spline reparameterization function is designed to project the NURBS toolpath into the time domain. Consequently, the analysis of residual vibration is conducted based on the expression and the classical spring-mass model, and the mathematical formulation of residual vibration is deduced in the form of an integration based on the fundamental solution matrix. Then, the time-optimal reparameterization function is determined using a hybrid algorithm of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) and gradient descent, taking into account the chord error, kinematic, and residual vibration constraints. Finally, the numerical simulations and an actual experiment are carried out to validate the feasibility and efficiency of our method. The results show that our method can improve efficiency and significantly suppress the residual vibration.

title: Remaining useful life estimation of ball-screw feed drives using a nonlinear digital twin and PINN–AIDB framework
abstract: Ball-screw feed drives (BSFDs) govern positioning accuracy and operational availability in computer numerical control (CNC) machine tools, yet reliable remaining useful life (RUL) estimation remains challenging owing to constrained controller sensing and complex electromechanical interactions. This study presents a real-time RUL estimation framework operating exclusively on controller-resident OPC–UA telemetry, without auxiliary vibration instrumentation. A validated nonlinear digital twin, confirmed at 0.020%–0.026% stroke error under pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS) excitation, provides surrogates for frictional dissipation and torsional microslip, defining a physics-derived degradation driver Φ(t). This driver regularises a compact physics-informed neural network fused with an anchor-informed degradation baseline (PINN–AIDB). The framework incorporates residual ODE constraints, monotonicity enforcement, and anchor consistency, whereas the Weibull model serves as a transparent statistical baseline. Pre- and post-accelerated life test (ALT) states calibrate an acceleration factor AF∗≈82.6 that maps laboratory exposure to an equivalent field horizon of approximately 8260h, consistent with catalogue-referenced BSFD fatigue lives. Validation under no-load and loaded conditions (0kg to 150kg, 5000 to 20 000 mm/min) confirms severity-consistent RUL compression across a 249h range (≈3% of nominal lifetime). The proposed PINN–AIDB projects the field horizon with a deviation of 11h from the catalogue-anchored reference, a 90% confidence-interval width of 211h, and 100% threshold-crossing feasibility, while reducing feedrate-order monotonicity violations from five (baseline estimators) to one across all 16 operating conditions. Ablation confirms that Φ(t), monotonicity enforcement, and anchor constraints address complementary identifiability limitations under controller-resident sensing without auxiliary condition-monitoring hardware.

title: Research on generative diffusion-based over-threshold restoration for oil and gas pipeline signals
abstract: Oil and gas pipeline detection signals are critical for pipeline defect diagnosis and assessment. However, during field signal acquisition, complex operating conditions, harsh detection environments, and inherent limitations of detector response and signal conversion may lead to over-threshold distortion in pipeline signals. Since the true complete defect distribution of field distorted signals is inaccessible, traditional supervised deep learning methods face limitations in constructing paired distorted-clean training samples. To address this problem, this study proposes an Over-Threshold Distortion Restoration (OTDR) method based on the diffusion probabilistic principle. OTDR adopts unsupervised forward diffusion training to learn the feature distribution of normal pipeline defect signals and incorporates a progressively guided restoration mode with a dynamic resampling mechanism to reconstruct over-threshold distorted regions during reverse diffusion. Case validations indicate that OTDR can reconstruct the main morphological structures, local details, and statistical feature distributions of field distorted signals. In the quantitative tests based on simulated distortion conditions, the restoration results achieve an average MAE of 0.045. The effects of different resampling strategies, prediction models, and diffusion strategies on restoration performance are further analyzed, and failure-case analysis is conducted under constructed extreme distortion conditions. Overall, the experimental results suggest that OTDR provides a feasible generative diffusion restoration mode for over-threshold distorted signals in oil and gas pipeline detection.

title: Recursive Gaussian process state space model
abstract: Learning dynamical models from data is not only fundamental but also holds great promise for advancing principle discovery, time-series prediction, and controller design. Among various approaches, Gaussian Process State-Space Models (GPSSMs) have recently gained significant attention due to their combination of flexibility and interpretability. However, for online learning, the field lacks an efficient method suitable for scenarios where prior information regarding data distribution and model function is limited. To address this issue, this paper proposes a recursive GPSSM method with adaptive capabilities for both operating domains and Gaussian process (GP) hyperparameters. Specifically, we first utilize first-order linearization to derive a Bayesian update equation for the joint distribution between the system state and the GP model, enabling closed-form and domain-independent learning. Second, an online selection algorithm for inducing points is developed based on informative criteria to achieve lightweight learning. Third, to support online hyperparameter optimization, we recover historical measurement information from the current filtering distribution. Comprehensive evaluations on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superior accuracy, computational efficiency, and adaptability of our method compared to state-of-the-art online GPSSM techniques.

title: A data-driven digital twin update technology based on an invertible attention-enhanced conditional invertible neural network
abstract: The fidelity of a digital twin is maintained by continuously updating the models embedded in its virtual entity with real-time sensor data. Conditional invertible neural networks (cINNs) offer a promising data-driven approach for likelihood-free model updating. However, they struggle to capture strong couplings among model parameters and often fail to effectively use suboptimal or limited sensor measurements. Additionally, epistemic uncertainty cannot be rigorously quantified in standard cINNs. To address these issues, an invertible attention-enhanced cINN (IA-cINN) is proposed. A novel invertible attention layer is integrated into the architecture. This layer explicitly models intrinsic correlations among model parameters and cross-dependencies between parameters and measurements through self- and cross-attention mechanisms while rigorously preserving invertibility. Monte Carlo dropout is incorporated into the IA-cINN to quantify epistemic uncertainty. The method was validated on two engineering cases. In a simulated case of a material handling device, three material parameters of structural components were updated using only strain and deformation measurements. In an experimental bearing case, contact stiffness, defect length, and radial clearance were updated using vibration features. In both cases, the IA-cINN outperformed the conventional cINN, as well as a Bayesian updating method based on Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. The IA-cINN achieved significantly higher updating accuracy, especially for parameters that exhibited complex coupling relationships with others. It produced more reliable uncertainty intervals in both cases, as indicated by lower interval scores. These intervals were shown to be sensitive to key sources of epistemic uncertainty, including data scarcity and insufficient model learning.

title: System-oriented demand modeling and mutually exclusive co-optimization for hybrid electromagnetic active suspension
abstract: To address the inherent trade-off between energy efficiency and dynamic performance for spatially constrained electromagnetic active suspension, a magnetorheological-electromagnetic parallel actuator (MPA) suitable for hybrid electromagnetic active suspension (HEAS) is proposed by integrating a dual-channel magnetorheological damper with a permanent magnet linear synchronous motor. A system-oriented design method is developed by introducing an LQR demand generator, which maps multi-condition suspension demands into a probabilistic F-V domain. A system-level objective is then formulated by combining time-domain statistical coverage and boundary capability constraints, enabling demand-driven matching between the suspension requirements and the actuator’s reachable domain. To resolve the mutually exclusive coupling between sub-actuators under limited radial space, a sequential co-optimization framework integrating heterogeneous actuator models with the RIME algorithm is proposed. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is validated through component-level experiments. Finally, a dual-layer switching control strategy tailored for the MPA is developed and implemented on a full-vehicle experimental platform. Comparative results show that the MPA achieves superior overall performance compared with the PMLSM: under severe random road excitation, it improves ride comfort and attitude control while reducing mean energy consumption by 80.164 %; under mild random road excitation, it maintains comparable dynamic performance with lower energy consumption; and under the single lane change condition, it reduces the peak roll angle and load transfer ratio by 42.217 % and 20.289 %. These results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving coordinated enhancement of system performance and energy efficiency, while long-term thermal durability under sustained severe excitation remains to be further investigated.

title: Preload-adjustable compliant torsional quasi-zero-stiffness isolator for flexible beam structures
abstract: With higher aspect ratios and the trend toward compliant designs in morphing aircraft, such structures are prone to undesired structural responses under fuselage vibration and aerodynamic loading. To address this issue, this paper proposes a preload-adjustable compliant torsional quasi-zero-stiffness (CT-QZS) isolator for low-frequency vibration isolation of flexible beam structures through boundary modification. The CT-QZS isolator integrates a negative-stiffness (NS) component composed of rotated bistable buckled beams and a positive-stiffness (PS) component composed of compliant curved beams. A tunable sliding groove on the rigid outer ring of the PS component allows continuous preload adjustment by changing the relative angle between the PS and NS components without altering the quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) range. The torque–angle characteristic of the PS component is derived using Euler beam theory and the unit-load method and validated through quasi-static experiments. The threshold condition and parametric tuning rule of the negative stiffness are investigated through bifurcation analysis and parametric finite element simulations. Two CT-QZS isolators obtained from two different design strategies are integrated as non-invasive rotational boundaries at the root of a PLA cantilever beam. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed preload-adjustable QZS isolators significantly reduce the first natural frequency and the vibration isolation onset frequency, achieving high static stiffness and low dynamic stiffness simultaneously compared to both the baseline fixed support and various linear isolators. The design offers an effective solution for low-frequency vibration isolation of flexible aerospace structures, such as high-aspect-ratio wings, morphing wings, and deployable space mechanisms.

title: Design and dynamic behaviors of a novel cage-free zero-clearance auxiliary bearing for drop protection of rotor
abstract: Active magnetic bearings (AMBs) are essential for high-performance rotating machinery, and auxiliary bearings play a critical protective role during AMBs malfunctions. Traditional auxiliary bearings have a fixed clearance with the rotor, which causes sustained vibration and high whirl risk after rotor drop. To address these problems, this study proposes a novel cage-free zero-clearance auxiliary bearing (CF-ZCAB) with a compact structure for drop protection of rotor. A comprehensive nonlinear multi-degree-of-freedom dynamic model was established to characterize the coupled dynamic interactions among the rotor, wedge-shaped sliding blocks, and cage-free ball bearing, and the dynamic behavior of the CF-ZCAB during rotor drop is systematically analyzed. The simulation results show the CF-ZCAB can rapidly eliminate initial radial clearance and realize rotor self-centering after rotor drop. During the inner ring acceleration phase, the balls experience severe slip and collision, which primarily occurs in the non-loaded region. A dedicated test rig is built for experimental verification, and the extracted rotor center trajectory, ball rotational speed and bearing inner ring rotational speed are compared with the simulation results. The experimental results are highly consistent with numerical results, and the errors are within an acceptable range, which verifies the correctness of the dynamic model and the rationality of design. This work provides a compact, high-load and zero-clearance auxiliary bearing design solution for AMB systems.

title: Enhancement method of bearing fault feature based on spatial double coil acoustic metamaterials
abstract: An enhancement method of bearing fault feature based on spatial double coil acoustic metamaterials (SDCM) is proposed to enhance bearing fault feature for improving the accuracy of bearing fault diagnosis in strong noise. This method can directly enhance the sound pressure signal at the fault resonant frequency band, which significantly improves the accuracy and reliability of bearing fault detection in strong noise environment and reduces the dependence on complex signal processing algorithm for providing a low-cost and high-sensitivity acoustic detection solution for the industrial machinery fault diagnosis. The frequency selective enhancement characteristics of SDCM are used to enhance sound pressure amplitude of frequency band neared the center frequency in bearing fault signal, and then the bearing fault feature are identified. SDCM consists of double layer Mie resonators, and its size is less than that of acoustic metamaterials based on gradient. When the sound wave propagates in the air channel, the refractive index increases due to the increase of the propagation path, and its propagation speed gradually slows down, which realizes the sound energy accumulation. Besides, the internal and external Mie air channels are set to different widths, resulting in the gradient impedance to eliminate the impedance mismatch. When the scale factor of SDCM is changed, the resonance frequency changes but the enhancement ratio remains the constant. The simulation results verify that SDCM has the significant acoustic enhancement characteristics, and the sound pressure amplitude at resonance frequency is increased by about 24 times. SDCM can effectively enhance the acoustic pressure amplitude of weak Gaussian pulse signal in strong noise environment, which proves that SDCM has the ability to detect the weak acoustic signal. The proposed SDCM can effectively extract the weak bearing fault features by amplifying the sound pressure at characteristic frequency. Furthermore, an experiment is employed to validate the capability of the proposed SDCM.

title: New insight into the modelling, identification, and analysis of a hybrid active vibration control of structures
abstract: In the present paper, a new perspective on comprehensive experimental–numerical modelling and identification of active structures is presented. The control object is a flat beam with one piezoelectric actuator and a contact sensor, forming a collocated system, or with three non-contact sensors, such as eddy-current or laser sensors, forming a hybrid non-collocated system. First, an analytical model of an actuator is derived from equilibrium equations. Next, the active beam is modelled analytically and numerically using 1D, 2D, and 3D Finite Element Method to comprehensively analyse the effect of actuator placement on the beam’s modal parameters. In addition to this aim, calibration of the actual industrial actuator and sensor responses was performed to obtain an accurate 3D FEM model of the piezoelectric patches based on the electromechanical coupling. The obtained active beam models are calibrated using experimental results for active beam vibration excited by a modal hammer impact and by a continuous chirp function generated by the actuator. An analytical model of the actuator, combined with finite-element and experimental results, enabled us to define optimal and quasi-optimal control forces and actuator placement that satisfy two proposed force- and energy-quality indicators. In addition, the effect of actuator length on modal frequencies, forces, energies, masses, and stiffness is examined in depth. Finally, the ARX identification procedure is applied to time-dependent experimental and 3D FEM numerical vibrational responses of the beam to obtain discrete and continuous single-input triple-output (SITO) state-space models with the maximum reduced order for the first three/four resonances. At the end, the impulse responses and stability of the ARX discrete and continuous models were shown in the time and frequency domains to demonstrate their correctness and accuracy. The proposed design methodology of the active control structure may be applied to both classical and composite structures. Next, different control laws can be tested in simulation and experiment to confirm the proposed design methodology of the active system.

title: Performance assessment of a novel vertically interconnected tuned mass damper system with inertial coupling for vibration control in high-rise buildings
abstract: This study introduces the vertically interconnected tuned mass damper with inertial coupling (VITMD-IC), an innovative passive seismic control system for high-rise buildings, and benchmarks its performance against conventional roof-mounted TMDs, a strategically configured multi-TMD (MTMD) system, and the uncontrolled structure. In the MTMD, one TMD is positioned at the foundation-superstructure interface and another at the roof, functioning as a seismic isolation-like mechanism that effectively suppresses inter-storey drift while improving overall vibration mitigation. The VITMD-IC extends this concept by integrating vertical inertial coupling between the TMDs, enabling superior redistribution of seismic energy, including input, kinetic, strain, and damping components, while controlling peak displacement, acceleration, velocity, and inter-storey drift ratio. All systems were optimized via a multi-objective ant lion optimizer (MOALO) under a representative artificial earthquake and validated against twelve recorded seismic events, comprising six near-field and six far-field scenarios. Comparative analyses confirm that the MTMD outperforms conventional TMDs, and the VITMD-IC consistently achieves the highest suppression across all response and energy metrics relative to both controlled and uncontrolled structures. By combining passive reliability with adaptive-like energy redistribution through inertial coupling, the VITMD-IC provides a robust, scalable, and practically feasible framework for seismic protection, establishing a transformative paradigm in high-rise vibration control that bridges conventional tuned mass damping and base isolation strategies.
keywords: Vertically interconnected tuned mass dampers with inertial coupling

title: Continuously updatable temperature-displacement hybrid neural network model for tracking performance degradation of expansion joints in long-span bridges
abstract: The neural network models driven by long-term monitoring data of structural temperature and thermal displacement in expansion joints are commonly employed to understand the operational condition of expansion joints in long-span bridges. But the continuous performance deterioration of expansion joints during the long-term operational period would change the temperature-displacement relationship and reduce the reliability of the corresponding neural network model. This paper presents a continuously updatable temperature-displacement hybrid neural network model for tracking the time-dependent performance degradation of expansion joints. First, a multi-domain feature fusion model fusing time-domain, difference-domain and spatial-domain features of long-term monitoring data is proposed by integrating a bidirectional long-short term memory network, an encoder-decoder, and a graph convolutional network to describe the complicated temperature-displacement relationship of expansion joints. Then, a model update method based on residual guidance and knowledge distillation was developed to continuously update the multi-domain feature fusion model so that the model could adapt to the degraded condition of expansion joints. Finally, long-term monitoring data from a long-span cable-stayed bridge is adopted as a case study to examine the accuracy of the proposed multi-domain feature fusion model and the effectiveness of the developed model updating method. The results indicate that the multi-domain feature fusion model has the capability of accurately capturing the historical temperature-displacement relationship embedded in expansion joints. The model updating method enables efficient and continuous updating of the temperature-displacement neural network, and the updated model can accurately track the performance degradation of expansion joints.

title: A new method to identify closely spaced weakly nonlinear modes from ring-down data
abstract: Transient ring-down measurements are widely used for the identification of nonlinear systems. Existing techniques typically require mono-harmonic responses and fail when modes are closely spaced. This paper introduces a new method known as time–frequency modal decomposition, or TFMD, for identifying closely spaced modes from ring-down data. The novelty of the method lies in the integration of singular value decomposition with the continuous wavelet transform to enable direct separation of closely spaced modes and estimation of amplitude-dependent modal parameters from multi-harmonic signals. The proposed approach was validated using two numerical test cases and one experimental case study. For the numerical cases, a two degree-of-freedom system with softening behavior and nonlinear damping due to an Iwan element, and a three degree-of-freedom oscillator with stiffening nonlinearity due to a cubic spring were considered. In both cases, TFMD successfully isolated the closely spaced nonlinear modes and estimated the instantaneous modal parameters. The results were compared against an established alternative method based on the Hilbert transform to demonstrate the improvements in accuracy and robustness offered by TFMD in case of closely spaced nonlinear modes. Further, experimental results from a benchmark frame–wing structure demonstrate the method’s ability to resolve closely spaced nonlinear modes in the presence of measurement noise where conventional Hilbert transform based approaches may fail.

title: Study on acoustic–solid–electrical multiphysics coupling model of vibrating liquid column system for primary calibration of piezoelectric hydrophones
abstract: The axisymmetric standing wave acoustic field of a vibrating liquid column (VLC), widely employed for the primary calibration of piezoelectric hydrophones, is generally governed by the Helmholtz equation. However, the multiphysics coupling interactions between the VLC and the hydrophone significantly perturb the original acoustic field, rendering traditional analytical models—which assume ideal conditions—insufficient for accurately characterizing the actual test acoustic field. In this scenario, an acoustic-solid-electrical multiphysics coupling model (ASEMCM) comprising a fluid medium, an isotropic elastic layer, and a radially polarized piezoelectric spherical shell is developed to accurately characterize the complex acoustic field of the VLC under calibration conditions in this paper. Specifically, the acoustic field in the fluid domain is expressed as a Rayleigh series expansion via spherical Bessel (or spherical Hankel) functions and Legendre polynomials, and the elastic layer displacement field is derived via Helmholtz decomposition using two scalar potential functions that satisfy the standard wave equation. Traditional potential function methods fail for the radially polarized piezoelectric spherical shell due to its transverse isotropy and spatially varying principal material axes. Consequently, a coupled system of ordinary differential equations governing radial displacement and electric potential is formulated, and a semi-analytic solution is derived using the Frobenius series method. Subsequently, a global modal matrix equation is constructed by applying interface coupling boundary conditions regarding stress, displacement, and the electric field. Cramer’s rule is then employed to determine the unknown coefficients for the proper modes of each order across these physical fields. Furthermore, an attenuation factor for hydrophone test sound pressure levels (AFHSPL) is proposed, based on the hydrophone integrating properties and the incident/scattered acoustic fields, to quantitatively assess the impact of multiphysics-coupled acoustic fields on the calibration accuracy of the vibrating liquid column system. Finally, the ASEMCM is validated via finite element simulations and experimental, and the results reveal that the piezoelectric effect exerts a negligible influence on the multiphysics-coupled acoustic field. Conversely, geometric parameters affecting calibration accuracy—which exhibits frequency-dependent behavior—include the hydrophone’s outer diameter, wall thickness, and truncation angle, as well as the heights of the liquid column and the measurement point.

title: MBGN: multimodal BiFPN gate network for in-process GMAW defect detection
abstract: In-process defect monitoring is critical for guaranteeing the integrity of Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) joints. Conventional non-destructive testing (NDT) delivers high-quality diagnostics only after the weld has finished, precluding immediate corrective action. We present the Multi-modal BiFPN Gate Network (MBGN), a deep-learning framework that fuses two complementary data streams: (i) time-synchronized welding current and voltage waveforms processed by a one-dimensional CNN, and (ii) high-speed molten-pool imagery processed by a ResNet backbone. The two modalities are merged through a Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN), and a lightweight Gate module adaptively recalibrates cross-modal interactions before a final classifier. Experiments on an industrially collected multimodal dataset demonstrate that MBGN achieved 0.748 accuracy and 0.719 macro-F1 on the held-out evaluation set. Compared with the strongest task-matched multimodal baseline, MWFN, MBGN improved macro-F1 by 0.120 while maintaining comparable accuracy. These results indicate the potential of multimodal fusion for in-process GMAW defect monitoring under the investigated industrial conditions, while broader deployment still requires validation across additional materials, joint types, and online system configurations.

title: Eigenmode-decoupled multilayer differential magnetoelectric sensor for robust magnetic signal extraction under vibration and common-mode disturbances
abstract: Weak magnetic sensing on mobile or mechanically disturbed platforms is often limited by vibration-induced common-mode interference that masks the target magnetic response. To address this problem, we propose an eigenmode-decoupled multilayer differential magnetoelectric architecture in which magnetic-field-induced and disturbance-dominant responses are separated into differential and common-mode channels, respectively, through anti-parallel poling and differential processing. A mode-matching factor k is further introduced as a directly measurable indicator to quantify the relative dominance of common-mode and differential-mode components. The proposed approach is validated under magnetic excitation, base-vibration loading, line-frequency interference, mixed magnetic-vibration conditions, and UAV-borne operation. Experiments show that low-frequency vibration components are suppressed by more than −15 dB and 50 Hz common-mode interference is attenuated by up to −47.13 dB, while differential processing reduces the equivalent magnetic noise density to 21.45 pT/Hz1/2 at 1 Hz. At 20.19 kHz, the differential-mode magnetoelectric coefficient reaches 8689 V·cm−1·Oe−1, with an equivalent magnetic noise density of 15.77 fT/Hz1/2. These results suggest that the proposed structural design, combined with physics-informed differential processing, provides a compact and robust solution for weak magnetic signal extraction in vibration-contaminated environments.

title: Model-free model predictive control for active mass damper structures based on fuzzy parallel coupled virtual object
abstract: In structural vibration control utilizing active mass dampers (AMD), conventional model-based control algorithms rely heavily on the precise mathematical representation of the controlled plant. However, in practical engineering applications, uncertainties in structural parameters and environmental disturbances often hinder accurate modeling, leading to performance degradation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel model free control strategy integrating a parallel coupled virtual object (PCVO), model predictive control (MPC), and fuzzy controller. A PCVO is introduced between the true structure and the AMD to establish a designable model, eliminating the need for an explicit structural model. A fuzzy controller adaptively updates the PCVO parameters in real time based on the displacement error between the PCVO and the true structure and its derivative, ensuring the PCVO accurately tracks the true structural response. The MPC algorithm then utilizes the PCVO to solve for the optimal control force under actuator saturation. Numerical simulations on a three degree of freedom structure show that the PCVO-MPC achieves performance comparable to LQR and MPC. Specifically, the inter-story drift and absolute acceleration peak reduction rates reach 33.07% and 43.98%, while the maximum RMS reduction rates for displacement and absolute acceleration reach 38.62% and 44.91%, respectively. Furthermore, the strategy maintains stable effectiveness under measurement noise, where the maximum reduction rates for inter-story drift and absolute acceleration peak are 33.47% and 45.33%, and the maximum reduction rates for displacement RMS and absolute acceleration RMS are 34.61% and 43.62% respectively, ensuring control reliability.

title: PIDUQ: an interpretable physics-informed distribution uncertainty quantification network for unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis of rolling bearings
abstract: In practical industrial scenarios, distribution shifts induced by varying operating conditions severely hinder the accuracy and reliability of cross-domain fault diagnosis for rolling bearings. Moreover, existing domain adaptation methods generally lack interpretability and still face challenges in handling unreliable pseudo-labels in the target domain. To address these issues, a novel Physics-Informed Distribution Uncertainty Quantification network (PIDUQ) is proposed. First, a Physics-Constrained Differentiable Convolution (PCDConv) module is constructed to replace the conventional first-layer convolution. Through parameterized modeling and physics-based regularization, PCDConv reconfigures convolutional kernels into learnable band-pass filter banks, enabling the network to adaptively focus on fault-induced resonance frequency bands and thereby enhancing the physical consistency and noise robustness of feature extraction. Subsequently, the Uncertainty-guided Local Maximum Mean Discrepancy (ULMMD) metric is introduced. By jointly quantifying prediction reliability using normalized entropy and confidence margins, ULMMD employs a dynamic reweighting strategy to suppress the interference of highly uncertain samples during subdomain alignment, thereby alleviating negative transfer and refining decision boundaries. Extensive experiments are conducted on the Paderborn University and Mechanical Fault Simulation datasets. The results show that PIDUQ achieves accuracies of 95.15%-98.27% on the PU dataset and an average accuracy of 89.87% on co-located transfer tasks of the MFS dataset, while maintaining superior performance under multi-speed, cross-location, and compound fault scenarios. Furthermore, visualized filter responses validate the capability of the proposed method to capture physical information. Code is available at GitHub.

title: A non-Gaussian frequency-domain fatigue damage estimation method under multi-source vibration excitations
abstract: Critical components of high-speed train bogies are subjected to complex multi-source vibration excitations and are prone to vibration-induced fatigue failure. However, in-service stress responses are difficult to obtain in a stable and long-term manner, which introduces considerable uncertainty into vibration-fatigue damage assessment. To address this issue, a power spectral density (PSD) matrix is introduced to retain the auto- and cross-spectral information of multiple excitation sources, and a multi-input–multi-output transfer function model is established for accurate stress PSD prediction under correlated multi-source excitation. To further account for the non-Gaussian characteristics of structural responses, an improved non-Gaussian frequency-domain fatigue assessment method is proposed to construct the stress-amplitude probability density function (PDF) of non-Gaussian signals from the stress PSD and derive its explicit expression, based on which fatigue damage can be further estimated. The engineering applicability of the proposed method is validated using on-track measurement data from a high-speed train sanding device, and its reliability is demonstrated through comparison with time-domain rainflow counting (RFC). The results indicate that the proposed method can provide accurate stress-amplitude PDFs and fatigue damage estimates at critical locations while reducing reliance on long-term continuous stress monitoring, thus providing practical engineering value for vibration fatigue analysis and structural health monitoring (SHM).

title: Noise-aware reliability mapping and structure-aware reconstruction for full-field vibration measurement and imaging
abstract: Phase-based vibration measurement from ordinary videos provides a low-cost, marker-free route to obtain full-field displacement, but is often degraded by imaging noise, weak texture, and background interference. These factors can produce noise-dominated pseudo motion, fragmented displacement fields, and vibration images with poor spatial coherence and noticeable background leakage. This paper presents a two-stage reliability-guided framework to improve the robustness and interpretability of phase-based full-field vibration measurement. First, a noise-aware reliability map is derived to quantify pixel-wise measurement reliability under imaging noise. Coverage-controlled thresholding is then used to extract a spatially coherent candidate region for subsequent analysis and reconstruction. Second, a structure-consistent displacement field is reconstructed within the candidate region using reliability-weighted data anchoring, boundary-aware neighbor coupling, and region-wise affine regularization. This reconstruction suppresses noise-induced pseudo motion while preserving component-level motion coherence. The proposed approach is evaluated on a synthetic cantilever-beam benchmark, a laboratory steel-frame experiment, and a real engine case. The results show that the proposed reliability map provides stable pixel-wise reliability assessment under different noise and scene conditions. The reconstructed displacement fields yield cleaner vibration images with reduced noise-induced artifacts and background leakage. Quantitatively, the proposed method reduces background leakage, improves structural coherence, and enhances amplitude fidelity on synthetic data, as measured by BBER, nSSI, and RelRMSE, respectively. Overall, the proposed framework improves the robustness and interpretability of phase-based full-field vibration imaging and provides a practical route for vibration inspection using ordinary cameras.

title: Theoretical and experimental analysis of active–passive hybrid control for electromechanical coupling rotor systems
abstract: To address the broadband torsional vibration in electromechanical coupling rotor systems, a hybrid active–passive vibration control strategy is proposed. Distributed multi-stable nonlinear energy sinks (MNESs) are incorporated as the passive component to overcome the limited vibration suppression performance of conventional single active control. The models of the motor, vector control system, and gear mesh torque are developed, and a dynamic model of the electromechanical coupling rotor system is subsequently constructed. Considering the multimodal characteristics of the motor-driven rotor system, the structure and principle of the MNESs are introduced. The hybrid control strategy that combines the active harmonic voltage injection (AHVI) with distributed MNESs is proposed for the steady-state excitation, and the corresponding dynamic model is developed in a simulation environment. For the impact excitation, the hybrid control strategy incorporating the active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) with distributed MNESs is established. Through numerical simulations, the suppression effects of the system without control, with active control, and with hybrid control are compared. The combined effect and suppression effectiveness of the hybrid control on the primary system are emphasized. Finally, the hybrid control strategy is implemented on the rotor system experimental platform, and its suppression performance is evaluated experimentally. The results indicate that implementing vibration suppression at both the electrical and mechanical levels effectively compensates for the limitations of active control in practical applications.

title: An Integrated novel random decrement technique and system identification framework for modal features extraction in structural health monitoring
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) techniques are used for monitoring the condition of structures, including bridges, buildings, dams, among others, through data acquired from embedded sensors. An integral aspect of SHM involves feature extraction, wherein algorithms analyze raw sensor data to generate explainable features regarding the health state of structures. The random decrement technique (RDT) is a notable signal processing method used to estimate the free response of mechanical structures, crucial for extracting frequency features related to structural dynamics. However, studies have shown that RDT encounters performance issues in cases of nonlinear damping, significant signal noise, and overlapping vibration modes. In a previous study, a data-driven classifier for transient and stationary regimes in multivariate dynamic systems was introduced, employing differential geometry tools to analyze stochastic properties. In this paper, the authors applied this classifier to develop a novel frequency-feature extraction method for SHM. This method incorporates a modified triggering condition for RDT and a recent system identification technique, aiming to improve frequency-feature estimation, especially in segment selection and modal parameter estimation of free responses in non-linear structures. Validation of the proposed approach employed mechanical vibration data from four accelerometer sensors on the “Andoian DF 12” bridge in Guipuzkoa, Spain, covering a one-year period and providing comprehensive insights into structural dynamics across different seasons. Comparative analysis against traditional RDT and various system identification techniques demonstrated that the proposed methodology improve the estimation of structural free responses by reducing noise and requiring fewer data compared to traditional RDTs. Moreover, the estimated modes aligned with the spectral content of mechanical sensors, indicating suitability for online applications with minimal computational costs and accurate modal parameter estimation for SHM in structures.

title: A semi-supervised tool wear monitoring approach integrating physics-guided weak labels and uncertainty quantification
abstract: Driven by the Industry 5.0 paradigm, tool wear monitoring has become essential for ensuring machining quality and production efficiency. However, the supervision asymmetry between readily available sensor signals and scarce labeled data hampers the industrial deployment of monitoring models. To address this issue, a physics-guided semi-supervised learning method with uncertainty quantification is proposed. First, multi-source heterogeneous features that characterize local cutting dynamics and historical degradation information are constructed via adaptive feature filtering. Second, the improved parallel symbolic regression learns trend-constrained symbolic degradation mappings and generates physics-guided weak labels that are consistent with the irreversible evolution of tool wear, thereby alleviating the supervision bottleneck caused by insufficient true labels. Subsequently, a staged conformal prediction strategy quantifies stage-related uncertainty of weak labels and constructs adaptive loss weights to reduce the interference of low-reliability weak labels during model training. Finally, a physics-guided cross-attention fusion module is designed to leverage degradation trend information as guidance for adaptive interactions among heterogeneous features, while a raw-feature bypass is introduced to preserve data-driven information and reduce the risk of negative transfer caused by local weak-label bias. Ablation studies confirm the advantages of the proposed method in preserving trend smoothness, suppressing heteroscedastic noise, and improving late-stage identification accuracy. Compared with the best-performing baseline, the proposed method reduces RMSE and MAE by 14.2 % and 10.9 %, respectively, while R2 increases by 1.2 %. Further validation shows that the proposed method can robustly adapt to different cutting conditions. Meanwhile, its lightweight online inference architecture enables deployment on resource-constrained industrial edge devices.

title: A Time-Frequency Fusion Spiking Neural Network for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Learnable Neuronal Dynamics
abstract: Bearing fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions often suffers from insufficient feature representation and unstable performance. Many existing spiking neural network (SNN)-based methods use fixed neuronal dynamic parameters, which may limit their ability to accommodate operating-condition variations. Moreover, some diagnostic frameworks construct two-dimensional time-frequency representations before model training, introducing an additional offline transformation stage. In addition, some SNN-based diagnostic frameworks place less emphasis on explicit frequency-domain information. To address these issues, this paper proposes a time-frequency fusion SNN for bearing fault diagnosis based on learnable neuronal dynamics. First, one-dimensional vibration segments are replicated across four simulation time steps, and spectral information is modeled by an embedded Sinc-based branch. Then, temporal features and frequency-domain information are fused within a unified SNN framework, where learnable neuronal dynamics adjust temporal integration and spike-generation behavior during training to better match vibration patterns at different temporal scales. Experiments on the MFPT and JNU datasets show that the proposed model achieves accuracies of 98.33% and 99.33%, respectively, demonstrating competitive diagnostic performance.

title: Design and validation of a multi-modal resonant metamaterial for broadband sound insulation improvement in orthotropic panels
abstract: Resonant metamaterials offer a promising lightweight solution to achieving strong vibroacoustic attenuation in panels. While conventional resonator designs exploit a single transversal mode, limiting the achievable attenuation bandwidth, recent studies indicate that multi-modal resonators, leveraging multiple transversal and rotational modes, enable broader-band attenuation. These can suppress the broadband sound transmission loss (STL) dip due to coincidence effects in thin orthotropic panels. However, experimental validation is lacking in practically relevant configurations, which often deviate from the ideal thin-plate behaviour. This work presents the modelling, optimization, and experimental validation of a multi-modal resonant metamaterial treatment for broadband STL enhancement in a moderately thick orthotropic panel made of cross-laminated timber (CLT). The proposed treatment integrates medium-density fiberboard resonators featuring two distinct rotational modes, which generate two directional bandgaps exploited to suppress coincidence effects along the principal axes of the CLT panel. Two complementary modelling frameworks are explored. Efficient design optimization is enabled by extending conventional effective-mass thin-plate models by frequency-dependent bending stiffness parameters that capture quasi-static shearing and inter-layer interactions in the CLT host structure. A second framework allows detailed vibroacoustic predictions of the finite-sized panel through the assembly of reduced unit-cell models retaining all relevant geometrical details, and coupling with deterministic–statistical energy analysis. Experimental validation via laser Doppler vibrometry confirms the formation of two directional bandgaps, while airborne and structure-borne sound insulation measurements demonstrate 8-10 dB attenuation within the bandgaps and suppression of the broadband coincidence STL dip.

title: A two-layered control for backlash compensation and oscillation suppression in ball screw drives
abstract: Backlash in ball screw drives causes torque loss and engagement impact during motion reversal, resulting in tracking errors and oscillations. Existing compensation methods, which treat backlash as a lumped disturbance, fail to balance fast estimation and smooth compensation, leading to delayed or abrupt responses. This study introduces a two-layered composite control structure for backlash-affected ball screw drives, featuring a torque-loss compensation layer and an oscillation-damping layer to enhance tracking accuracy and suppress reversal oscillations. The backlash transition process is divided into three phases. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that tracking errors primarily occur in the first and third phases due to torque loss, while oscillations occur in the second phase due to engagement impact. A continuous prediction method for backlash transitions employs motor-side position increments after velocity reversal to achieve accurate phase switching and torque compensation. A combined backlash–friction feedforward strategy is developed to compensate for torque losses, while an extended state observer (ESO)-based controller rejects residual disturbances. An oscillation-damping layer with velocity-difference feedback suppresses engagement-induced vibrations, and a back-propagation artificial neural network characterizes position-dependent backlash using laser interferometer measurements. Comparative motion and milling tests validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Optical-acoustic mode coupling in a hierarchical nonlinear acoustic metamaterial
abstract: Locally resonant nonlinear acoustic metamaterials can provide low-frequency control and bandwidth extension, but many designs are narrow-band, have limited tunability and robustness, and face low-frequency–thickness trade-offs. To address these limitations, this work investigates wave propagation in a one-dimensional inward configuration hierarchical metamaterial with weakly nonlinearity using an approximate analytical method of Lindstedt–Poincaré and numerical simulations; the analytical model captures the acoustic and first-optical branches, while the second-optical branch is characterized numerically. Spectro-spatial analysis reveals coupling between the acoustic and optical branches, which broadens the effective bandwidth. From the dispersion relation, we observe that chain hardening/softening primarily upshifts/downshifts the acoustic and second-optical branches, whereas resonator nonlinearity mainly tunes the optical branches; the first-optical branch is largely insensitive to chain nonlinearity. Consistent with these shifts, under hardening nonlinearity, the chain generates solitary-like and dispersive packets, whereas with softening, propagation is primarily dispersive. Finally, two passive, time-invariant diode architectures are numerically examined to demonstrate that hierarchy-enabled optical-acoustic mode coupling can produce direction-dependent transmission, with an explicit efficiency-isolation trade-off. These results suggest that hierarchy-enabled optical-acoustic coupling may provide a passive mechanism for broadband wave-control concepts and direction-biased device designs, with potential relevance to energy-transfer and sensing applications.

title: Two-stage optimization of multi-channel delayed feedforward-feedback control for an active quasi-zero-stiffness vibration isolation system
abstract: Although time-delay coupling poses a major challenge to high-performance control in active quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) vibration isolation systems, the involved delays can be exploited as tunable parameters for control optimization. To exploit this potential, this study develops a multi-channel delayed feedforward-feedback (MCDFF) control strategy for active QZS isolation, in which four delayed displacement-velocity channels are independently tuned to shape both stability and isolation performance. First, analytical frequency-sweeping and numerical-iteration procedures are introduced to evaluate delay robustness and stability margin, respectively. Second, a two-stage optimization framework is established, in which feedback tuning first secures stability and feedforward tuning then refines the desired isolation performance. Third, two joint optimization schemes are developed to balance anti-resonance attenuation with resonance suppression and transient performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized MCDFF strategy outperforms the representative baselines. Compared with the QZS-only system, it achieves displacement transmissibility reductions of 81.55% under a 3 Hz single-frequency excitation, 65.92% at 2 Hz and 81.23% at 4 Hz under dual-frequency excitation, and 58.72% over the 2–12 Hz broadband range. Furthermore, the proposed strategy experimentally reduces the initial isolation frequency to below 0.5 Hz, demonstrating its potential for ultra-low-frequency isolation.
