title: A novel compound fault feature synthesis framework for industrial motor diagnosis via interactive semantic composition mechanism
abstract: In industrial motor systems, Compound Fault (CF) samples are characterized by both insufficient quantity and random coupling of multiple Single Faults (SFs), posing a significant challenge to operational safety and production efficiency. However, existing diagnosis methods typically treat CFs as independent fault modes and ignore the intrinsic coupling relationships and latent uncertainties among SFs, leading to degraded diagnostic performance. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel intelligent fault diagnosis method for industrial motor systems. First, a Deep Fault-Sensitive Feature Hierarchical Learning Network (DFS-FHLN) is proposed to enhance the comprehensive representation of SF features by adaptively capturing both local spatial information and global hierarchical dependencies. Subsequently, a CF feature synthesis strategy is developed based on a Latent-Space Relation Variational Auto-Encoder Network (LSR-VAEN) and an interactive semantic composition mechanism. This approach generates high-fidelity CF features by learning individual SF semantic prototypes and mining their interactive compositional patterns. Based on the above, an adaptive CF diagnosis model is developed to accurately identify unseen CFs by building a diagnosis-oriented semantic embedding space that preserves the intrinsic feature patterns of various CFs. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated on two industrial motor datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively generate high-fidelity CF features and significantly outperform state-of-the-art methods in diagnostic performance.

title: Dynamic modeling and experimental investigation of a snap-through triboelectric nanogenerator for low-speed wind energy harvesting
abstract: This paper presents a snap-through triboelectric nanogenerator (STENG-BA) integrating a buckling bistable structure with an antipolar magnetic arrangement to enhance low-speed wind energy harvesting. The device converts random wind into periodic magnetic excitation via a coupled antipolar magnetic arrangement and snap-through bistable motion, reliably driving the buckling beam to undergo rapid snap-through, promoting effective contact-separation between triboelectric functional material layers for high electrical output. A coupled wind-mechanical–electrical dynamic model is established and experimentally validated. The effects of different staggered magnetic pole arrangements and key structural parameters on the output performance are systematically investigated. The results show that the STENG-BA, with three effective staggered magnetic pole pairs, achieves a cut-in wind speed of 3 m/s. The device delivers a maximum output voltage of 470.2 V, an average power of 115.6 μW, and a corresponding power density of 8.75 W/m3 at a modest wind speed of 5 m/s. Further comparisons indicate that, in contrast to the same-pole magnetic arrangement, the proposed antipolar magnetic arrangement reduces the starting torque, thereby significantly lowering the cut-in wind speed and enhancing the output performance. Moreover, long-term stability tests and application demonstrations show that the device can light up more than 600 LEDs, quickly charge capacitors, and reliably power a low-power digital thermometer. This work provides an efficient solution for low-speed wind energy harvesting and shows promising potential for application in self-powered Internet of Things systems, such as those used in smart agriculture and field environmental monitoring.

title: Multiphysics modeling and nonlinear dynamic characteristics analysis of aerostatic spindle considering active piezoelectric compensation
abstract: Sliding mode control is applied to stabilize precision machining due to its excellent robustness. This paper establishes a multiphysics coupling dynamics model for the high-speed aerostatic motorized spindle incorporating active sliding mode compensation. The sliding surface is defined based on position and velocity errors, and the control gains in different directions are calculated by coupling the equivalent acceleration components generated by the multiphysics load excitation model into the control algorithm as the inversion feedforward terms. Additionally, the continuous saturation function is constructed to mitigate the effects of oscillation, and real-time active control excitation is derived using the piezoelectric mechanism. The induced currents for each phase are solved based on the electromechanical coupling behavior of the embedded motor, thereby determining the three-phase magnetic potential. The stator-rotor spatial coordinate system is established to derive the instantaneous air gap length considering the influence of nonlinear vibration responses. The transient unbalanced magnetic pull excitation is obtained by integrating the magnetic pull components across different cross-sections. Dynamic mass eccentricity and air film support excitation are also influenced by displacement field variations, reflected in deflection angles and air film thicknesses. By determining multiple excitation loads, a coupling dynamic model for vibration suppression compensation is constructed to achieve closed-loop active sliding control simulation. The piezoelectric vibration suppression test bench is established based on the conversion from displacements to control signals to validate the proposed coupling model. The response amplitude trajectories under simulated multi-parameter conditions are examined to discuss nonlinear characteristics and active control performance, providing theoretical guidance for structural design and control parameter selection.

title: Physics-informed identification of stochastic vibration for the bearing-rotor system
abstract: Uncertainty quantification and prediction of vibration characteristics in bearing-rotor systems constitute critical challenges in energy, marine, and aerospace engineering applications. In this regard, a physics-informed fusion approach is presented for stochastic vibration identification in bearing-rotor systems by integrating a virtual physical model with multi-source heterogeneous information. The proposed virtual bearing-rotor model incorporates multi-physics coupled interactions among transient temperature, lubrication, and vibration. Meanwhile, an adaptive strategy for acquiring high-quality information is developed. Multi-source heterogeneous prior statistical information for the bearing-rotor system is established based on expert knowledge and high-quality data. The initial configuration of the bearing-rotor system is inversely identified by integrating Bayesian inference with transient thermal information. Subsequently, the stochastic vibration of the bearing-rotor system is characterized in terms of inverse identification results. Eventually, the inverse inference and stochastic vibration identification capabilities of the physics-informed fusion framework are experimentally validated. The proposed physics-informed fusion approach provides theoretical guidance for cross-physical field inference from temperature to vibrations in aero-engine, marine propulsion, and wind turbine rotor systems.

title: ToolMamba: a physics-informed framework for interpretable tool condition monitoring under various machining conditions
abstract: Although data-driven tool condition monitoring (TCM) has demonstrated promising results, its generalization across different tools and varying machining conditions remains a critical challenge. To address this issue, this study proposes a physics-informed tool condition monitoring framework for cross-tool and cross-machine applications. First, sensitive features are selected based on the Altintas cutting-force model and tree-based SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to quantify feature importance, yielding a compact set of physically interpretable features. Then, a physics-informed framework, ToolMamba, is developed by integrating convolutional layers with a structured state-space sequence model to capture temporal dependencies from machining signals, augmented with physics-informed loss functions that enforce monotonicity and boundary constraints consistent with irreversible wear progression. Finally, Meta-learning with Stochastic Gradient Descent (Meta-SGD) is employed to adapt the model across different tool and machine domains with minimal retraining. Experimental validation on the PHM 2010 benchmark dataset yields an RMSE of 2.268 μm and MAE of 1.514 μm, representing a reduction of over 53% in RMSE compared to the best-performing baseline. Cross-tool transfer achieves R2 > 0.93 across all tested tools on both PHM 2010 and HMoTP 2024 datasets, and cross-machine transfer to a local milling dataset attains R2 = 0.938 on the best-aligned target tool. The proposed framework offers a robust, interpretable, and transferable solution for tool condition monitoring under various machining conditions.

title: An improved model for the Langevin transducer with numerous piezoelectric ceramics and electrodes
abstract: The Langevin transducer, configured with numerous piezoelectric ceramics (PZTs) and electrodes, exhibits a high-power density and can be designed and optimized through dynamic modeling. However, existing modeling approaches face a significant computational challenge, as the dimension of the system matrix increases rapidly with the number of PZTs and electrodes. To address this issue, an improved transfer matrix method (TMM) model is proposed in this paper. First, the transfer equation of the piezoelectric stack (PS), which acts as the vibration excitation source in the Langevin transducer, is derived based on the electromechanical transfer condition. A ternary operation is introduced to combine PZTs and electrodes, resulting in a 3 × 3 matrix. Subsequently, by eliminating the state vectors of internal elements such as the PS, the transfer equation of the entire Langevin transducer is obtained, and its overall transfer matrix retains a dimension of 3 × 3. A Langevin transducer with 12 PZTs and 13 electrodes is used for validation. The resonant frequencies obtained by the proposed TMM, the finite element method (FEM), and experiment are 32,190 Hz, 31,628 Hz, and 30,824 Hz, respectively. The relative error between the TMM and FEM results is 1.78%, showing good agreement. The error compared with experimental results is 4.43%, demonstrating practical applicability. Besides, compared with the conventional TMM, the proposed TMM reduces both the dimension and the condition number of the system matrix while improving computational accuracy, making it an efficient and practical modeling tool.

title: Theoretical and experimental study on dynamic behavior of a flexible rotor-support-casing system considering complex supporting-frames and connecting casings
abstract: This study mainly focuses on the dynamic characteristics of rotor-support-casing system with squirrel-cage squeeze film dampers (SFDs), as well as complex supporting-frame casings, connecting casings. The casings were modeled with 20-node solid elements, using Craig-Bampton method to reduce model dimensionality. For flexible rotor shaft, variable cross-section beam elements were used. Introducing multiple reference points, the kinematic coupling constraints were established and the boundary nodes of bearing housings. The equations of motion were derived, considering restoring forces of elastic support and nonlinear oil film forces. Dynamic responses of system were simulated using the predictor–corrector Newmark combined with Newton-Raphson method. Experimental studies were conducted to validate the feasibility of theoretical approach, and the transmission rate was obtained from bearing housing to casing through the supporting-frame. The results indicated that considering the complex casing, the rotor critical speeds are slightly reduced compared to neglecting casings, and both the resonance peaks induced by rotor critical speeds and those excited by casing natural frequencies appear in amplitude-frequency responses. Furthermore, resonance peaks also appear when the rotating speed reaches one-third, half, or twice the critical speed of rotor system, or half the natural frequency of casing. The amplitude-frequency responses obtained by simulation and experiment were essentially the same as the speed variation, and the whirling trajectory were also similar. For the 1# supporting-frame casing, the acceleration decreases as the vibration is transmitted from bearing housing to the outer casing. Overall, it provides flexible simulation method and experimental data support for vibration prediction of rotor-support-casing systems.

title: Natural gradient active control for coupled vibro-acoustic systems under spatially structured metrics
abstract: Active noise and vibration control (ANVC) in coupled vibro-acoustic systems often suffers from severe convergence imbalance and poor numerical conditioning caused by heterogeneous acoustic and structural channels. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physically informed adaptive control framework based on a block-diagonal stochastic natural gradient descent (BDSNGD) algorithm. By introducing structured metric preconditioning within a Riemannian metric space, the proposed method effectively aligns the dominant spatial eigenvalues of heterogeneous actuation channels, thereby eliminating convergence disparity without requiring computationally expensive full-rank matrix inversion. Furthermore, to overcome the trade-off between transient convergence speed and steady-state excess mean square error (EMSE), a correlation-driven variable step size (CVSS) strategy is developed. Instead of relying on raw error energy, the step size is regulated using the normalized temporal correlation of residual errors, enabling fast adaptation to structured disturbances while suppressing unnecessary updates under uncorrelated noise and impulsive perturbations. Comprehensive theoretical analyses, numerical simulations, and real-time experimental validations on a multichannel vibro-acoustic platform demonstrate that the proposed CVSS-BDSNGD algorithm achieves rapid, synchronous, and well-balanced convergence across heterogeneous channels, superior steady-state noise reduction, and strong robustness against impulsive disturbances, while maintaining a low computational complexity comparable to the conventional FxLMS algorithm.

title: Real-time monitoring and intelligent decision system with a dual-sensing module for optical lens centering
abstract: High-precision optical glass lenses are critical components in semiconductor lithography. Lens imaging quality and positioning accuracy are primarily influenced by the optical axis accuracy, which depends on adequate centering. Grinding during centering frequently causes edge cracks, surface scratches, and roundness errors. The inherently low material removal rate and the interference of cutting fluid further complicate process monitoring and real-time defect diagnosis. This study presents a dual-sensing module that integrates acoustic emission sensing with a self-developed online module for optical axis measurement to identify both the location and the root causes of defects during centering in real time. Convolutional neural networks are employed to classify optical axis deviation and machining anomalies, with corresponding accuracy rates of 96.18% and 97.59%, respectively. Recommended process decisions are provided for parameter tuning, improving product quality and production efficiency. Experimentally, the proposed intelligent monitoring and decision-making system with dual-sensing architecture shortened the average processing time by 25.8%, increased the yield from 65% to 95%, and reduced the unit cost by 22.2%, with edge cracks <E0.1, roundness <0.1 mm, and optical axis error <30″. This system can assist operators in determining the exact timing and location of machining defects, further increasing production efficiency and product quality. This system provides an effective and practical solution for optical lens manufacturing.

title: Multi-modal cross-domain mixed fusion model with dual disentanglement for fault diagnosis under unseen working conditions
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis has become an indispensable technique for ensuring machinery reliability. However, existing methods suffer significant performance decline in real-world scenarios where models are tested under unseen working conditions, while domain adaptation approaches are limited to their reliance on target domain samples. Moreover, most existing studies rely on single-modal sensing signals, overlooking the complementary nature of multi-modal information for improving model generalization. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a multi-modal cross-domain mixed fusion model with dual disentanglement for fault diagnosis. A dual disentanglement framework is developed to decouple modality-invariant and modality-specific features, as well as domain-invariant and domain-specific representations, enabling both comprehensive multi-modal representation learning and robust domain generalization. A cross-domain mixed fusion strategy is designed to randomly mix modality information across domains for modality and domain diversity augmentation. Furthermore, a triple-modal fusion mechanism is introduced to adaptively integrate multi-modal heterogeneous information. Extensive experiments are conducted on induction motor fault diagnosis under both unseen constant and time-varying working conditions. The results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms advanced methods and comprehensive ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of each proposed component and multi-modal fusion. The code is available at: https://github.com/xiapc1996/MMDG.

title: Mechanics-informed full-field deformation identification of flexure-dominated high-rise buildings using sparse inclinometer data
abstract: Abstract Structural deformation is a critical indicator of the safety and performance of high-rise buildings. Accurate deformation identification not only provides essential insights into structural behavior but also informs effective maintenance strategies. However, due to sensor limitations and cost constraints, full-field and full-band structural deformation identification remains a significant challenge in current monitoring practices. This study introduces a novel spatiotemporal framework for reconstructing deformations in flexural-dominated high-rise buildings by fusing multisensor data with a deep learning–based model. A system-level dynamic rotation field is first reconstructed from sparse inclinometer data using a physical-enhanced adjacency matrix and is subsequently calibrated with limited accelerometer measurements. The complete deformation field is obtained by superimposing the quasi-static and calibrated dynamic components. Numerical investigations demonstrate the feasibility and robustness of the proposed framework, even under severe sensor sparsity and sensor noise, while maintaining high accuracy in full-field and full-band deformation reconstruction. Comparative studies further indicate that the proposed strategy effectively enhances capability of current deep learning (DL) model for inferring unobserved nodes responses. Real-world validation using data from a super-high-rise building under strong wind and earthquake excitations confirmed the applicability of the method, with results showing good agreement with Global Positioning System (GPS) measurements. The findings also highlight the importance of incorporating full-band responses for reliable assessment, particularly for drift-sensitive components, underscoring the practical potential of the proposed framework.

title: A domain knowledge informed approach for anomaly detection of electric vehicle interior sounds
abstract: The detection of anomalies in automotive cabin sounds is critical for ensuring vehicle quality and maintaining passenger comfort. In many real-world settings, this task is more appropriately framed as an unsupervised learning problem rather than the supervised case due to the scarcity or complete absence of labeled faulty data. In such an unsupervised setting, the model is trained exclusively on healthy samples and detects anomalies as deviations from normal behavior. However, in the absence of labeled faulty samples for validation and the limited reliability of commonly used metrics, such as validation reconstruction error, effective model selection remains a significant challenge. To overcome these limitations, a domain-knowledge-informed approach for model selection is proposed, in which proxy-anomalies engineered through structured perturbations of healthy spectrograms are used in the validation set to support model selection. The proposed methodology is evaluated on a high-fidelity electric vehicle dataset comprising healthy and faulty cabin sounds across five representative fault types viz., Imbalance, Modulation, Whine, Wind, and Pulse Width Modulation. This dataset, generated using advanced sound synthesis techniques, and validated via expert jury assessments, has been made publicly available to facilitate further research. Experimental evaluations on the five fault cases demonstrate the selection of optimal models using proxy-anomalies, significantly outperform conventional model selection strategies.

title: A generalization of the Whittaker–Shannon interpolation formula for non-bandlimited signals
abstract: Reconstructing continuous signals from discrete samples is a fundamental task in interpolation theory. Under ideal assumptions, the classical Whittaker–Shannon interpolation formula guarantees perfect reconstruction for bandlimited signals sampled at the Nyquist rate. However, many real-world systems, particularly sampled-data systems, produce non-bandlimited signals whose intersample behavior is governed by the continuous-time dynamics encoded in the system model, making classical bandlimited reconstruction methods inappropriate. This paper presents a generalized interpolation framework that reconstructs continuous-time outputs from their samples using a model-induced kernel, thereby extending Shannon’s formula to a broader class of signals. The proposed method derives the interpolation kernel from the governing equations of the underlying system, enabling accurate reconstruction of intersample content. Numerical simulations and laboratory experiments on a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) validate the approach, demonstrating its effectiveness in reconstructing intersample behavior from output samples by leveraging model information.

title: Physics-regularized Bayesian neural network with time-of-arrival refinement for acoustic emission-based damage source localization in concrete beams
abstract: Accurate acoustic emission (AE) source localisation is essential for structural health monitoring (SHM) of concrete structures; however, heterogeneous material properties and complex wave propagation limit the reliability of conventional approaches. This study proposes PR-BNN-ATR, a physics-regularised Bayesian neural network (BNN) with acoustic time-of-arrival refinement for uncertainty-aware AE localisation. Time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) features extracted using an adaptive Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) picker are used to train a variational BNN, whose hybrid loss combines data fidelity, geometric feasibility, TDOA kinematic consistency, and Kullback–Leibler (KL) regularisation. A deterministic artificial neural network (ANN) and Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout serves as accuracy and uncertainty baselines, respectively. Validated on five notched concrete beams (notch positions 80–40 mm), PR-BNN-ATR achieved mean localisation errors of 3.10–6.19 mm (overall mean 4.04 mm) compared to 1.47–6.58 mm for the ANN. Although the ANN produced lower point errors, PR-BNN-ATR provided calibrated event-wise uncertainty estimates, with Spearman correlation positive for all five beams (ρ = 0.110–0.387), and Mahalanobis joint coverage averaging 91.3% at the 95% nominal level. The variational BNN outperformed MC Dropout on Negative Log-Likelihood in four of five beams. A semi-supervised calibration experiment using a calibration beam b0 with true physical ground-truth coordinates reduced cross-beam error by 82%, confirming genuine localisation learning beyond multilateration replication. Independent digital image correlation (DIC) strain-field measurements confirmed spatial co-localisation of BNN-predicted sources with crack trajectories and linked elevated predictive uncertainty to crack branching, dual crack interaction, and boundary reflection zones, providing non-circular physical validation. These results establish PR-BNN-ATR as an accurate, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware method for risk-informed SHM of concrete structures.

title: Bridging known and unknown: A distribution generation Schrödinger bridge for generalized zero-shot fault diagnosis
abstract: Generalized zero-shot learning offers a promising paradigm for fault diagnosis when samples of certain categories are unavailable. However, the domain shift caused by the absence of unknown-class data leads to a significant performance degradation. Existing methods have shortcomings in their construction of decision boundaries for known and unknown classes. To tackle the problem of domain shift, this paper proposes a distribution generation Schrödinger bridge (DGSB) framework. DGSB effectively compresses the decision boundary by generating multivariate pseudo-unknown fault data. A novel lightweight diffusion Schrödinger bridge network is presented, incorporating a label-embedded fast convolutional Kolmogorov–Arnold network for parameter-efficient generation guided by optimal transport theory. At the data level, a multivariate distribution augmentation strategy produces samples from diverse distributions, enhancing the boundary diversity. Furthermore, the semantic construction is extended to a gear system based on the characteristics of various faults. Comprehensive experiments across part-, component-, and system-level tasks under nine operating conditions indicate that DGSB outperforms seven classical and state-of-the-art benchmarks. Ablation and parameter studies validate the efficacy of the multivariate distribution augmentation strategy and label-embedded fast convolutional Kolmogorov–Arnold network design. Visualizations confirm the model’s ability to generate a variety of distributions and learn separable feature representations.

title: A rapid surface roughness evaluation method for single-point diamond turning based on the frequency sensitivity function
abstract: To address the pronounced within-batch surface roughness dispersion of workpieces in single-point diamond turning (SPDT) and the difficulty of rapidly characterizing such differences using conventional feature indicators, a mechanism-constrained frequency-domain attribution and quantification method is proposed. First, a frequency sensitivity function (FSF) is constructed based on the end-face generation and trimming mechanisms to describe the differential response of surface roughness to vibration components at different frequencies. Subsequently, by combining the power spectral density (PSD) of vibration signals, a Frequency-dependent Roughness Contribution (FDRC) spectrum is established, and a Roughness Sensitive Energy (RSE) index is further proposed to achieve targeted characterization of the contributions from sensitive frequency bands. To balance computational efficiency and peak fidelity, a coarse-to-fine two-stage scanning strategy is employed to construct nonuniform FSF nodes, which are then mapped onto the Welch frequency grid through Frequency Grid Alignment (FGA). The proposed method is validated using within-batch ZnSe workpieces and high-purity aluminum alloy workpieces. The results show that, compared with feature indicators and the simplified lightweight reference models, the proposed RSE can still effectively distinguish relative surface roughness differences among within-batch workpieces even when the vibration signals are highly similar. The proposed method provides a physically interpretable auxiliary indicator for rapid relative evaluation of within-batch surface roughness dispersion in SPDT.

title: Cooperative feature extraction for state monitoring of multiple motors in hub-driven electric vehicles
abstract: In-wheel motors of hub-driven electric vehicles operate in complex environments with highly variable working conditions, where fault features are easily masked. Conventional signal processing methods that isolate a single motor can be limited in removing strong and dynamic interference features. Considering the dynamic similarities in the operating environments and conditions of multiple in-wheel motors, a novel cooperative fault feature extraction approach for multiple similar objects is proposed. By exploiting the similarity of common road interference shared among multiple in-wheel motors, this approach filters out common disturbances and enhances the private fault features of the specific faulty motors. Firstly, a dynamic time delay estimation method for multiple signals is introduced to align the distribution of multi-motor signals and enhance their comparability. Secondly, an adaptive hash representation method is proposed to dynamically encode the time–frequency matrices of each signal, improving feature discrimination. Considering the temporal–frequency continuity of fault features, a regionalized processing strategy is adopted to reduce feature loss. Finally, a search method for common features is developed to eliminate common interference features in relevant time periods and frequency bands, thus enhancing the private fault feature expression. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can adaptively remove strong common interference features in varying scenarios and effectively enhance and extract local fault features.

title: Regularization strategies of an adaptive active road noise control headrest with the remote microphone technique under head translation
abstract: For adaptive active noise control (ANC) headrests, secondary path variations induced by head movement are of great impact on the road noise reduction performance, and different methods can be adopted to reduce the effects of head translation on the system performance. In this paper, two regularization strategies, one in the modeling of the observation filter and the other in the implementation of adaptive control, are analyzed and compared for an adaptive active road noise control headrest with the remote microphone technique. The simulation results based on the measured data indicate that better noise reduction can be achieved by applying the regularization in the observation filter modeling if the modeling accuracy is sufficiently high. The ANC headrest becomes unstable when the head translates beyond 8 cm from the initial position without head tracking, but with proper regularization, the system remains stable with a noise reduction of at least 3.9 dB in an area of 16 cm by 8 cm.

title: A systematic study of the synergy between passive and active components in a hybrid active–passive sound absorption control system
abstract: Passive sound absorbers, like micro-perforated panels (MPPs) and porous materials, are typically limited in bandwidth or low-frequency performance. Active absorption systems can achieve broadband low-frequency performance but require electrical power and may fail, e.g. during power loss. Hybrid active–passive absorbers therefore offer a promising route to combine the strengths of both approaches. However, existing studies treat the active and passive components independently, without analysing potential synergies that could reduce power demand or ensure sufficient fallback passive performance. This study presents a systematic numerical analysis of a hybrid absorber in a duct, consisting of a porous layer and an elastic MPP driven by an electromagnetic actuator. A feedforward active structural acoustic control strategy is used to actively control sound absorption via the actuated MPP. A regularisation method is introduced to limit actuator electrical power and prevent exceeding the operational constraints. The numerical model is validated through impedance tube measurements and subsequently used to investigate how MPP design parameters (porosity, thickness, hole diameter) and different configurations of the MPP/porous layer arrangement influence both passive and hybrid active–passive absorption. Two design strategies are examined: one with the MPP parameters optimised for maximum passive absorption and one optimised for maximum hybrid performance. The results reveal a fundamental trade-off: designs that maximise hybrid performance reduce passive absorption to improve active control efficiency, while designs prioritising passive performance reduce the effectiveness of the active control. This investigation highlights physical insights that allow effective design of hybrid active–passive systems that could be extended to other similar systems.

title: Hybrid approach for metamaterial behavior prediction for non-uniform resonator grids
abstract: A novel methodology to predict the behavior of metamaterial solutions is presented, with application to a simplified academic structure and an automotive electrical component. In scenarios where a non-uniform grid of resonators is employed, it is essential to consider an alternative to the unit cell modeling strategy, which is typically applied, to ensure robust predictions of metamaterial behavior. In this work, a simulation model of the resonators is combined with experimental transfer functions of the host structure through frequency-based substructuring to obtain these predictions. By employing the recently introduced longest vector approach, the necessity for a substantial number of driving points corresponding to the locations of the resonators, is avoided. Additionally, a metric is proposed to compare various configurations, demonstrating the potential of the presented technique for precise optimizations. The predictions obtained from experimental measurements are compared with those from unit cell modeling. The substructuring methodology offers a robust framework for predicting metamaterial performance in cases where a uniform grid of resonators cannot be placed, or when accurate simulation models of the complex host structure are not readily available.

title: A universal domain adaptation fault diagnosis method based on feature invariance and collaborative mutual learning
abstract: In practical rotating machinery systems, variations in operating conditions, noise interference, and evolving fault modes can cause both cross-domain distribution discrepancies and category shifts, where the target domain may contain unknown fault classes absent from the source domain. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a universal domain adaptation method for robust diagnosis of known and unknown faults. First, a feature invariance learning mechanism is developed to extract domain-stable and class-discriminative representations, thereby reducing distribution discrepancies and improving known-class recognition. Second, a cross-domain mixup augmentation strategy synthesizes potential unknown-class features through interpolation between source- and target-domain samples, expanding the unknown decision space and enhancing sensitivity to abnormal target patterns. Furthermore, a dual-classifier co-guided consistency optimization mechanism collaboratively employs a closed-set classifier and an open-set classifier. Through mutual consistency constraints and reciprocal feedback, the two classifiers jointly refine target-domain predictions and dynamically calibrate the decision boundary between known and unknown categories. Experiments are conducted on two aero-engine bearing datasets and a self-built gear dataset under closed-set, partial-set, open-set, and open-partial-set transfer scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in known-class classification, unknown-fault identification, and noise robustness compared with representative domain adaptation fault diagnosis methods.

title: Multimodal spatiotemporal graph attention network with uncertainty quantification for aircraft engine prognostics
abstract: Aircraft engine prognostics is critical for safety, cost reduction, and efficient fleet management. Despite the availability of rich multimodal sensor data, most current prognostic approaches are limited to single-modality analysis, lack uncertainty quantification, and rely on predefined sensor graphs. To address these limitations, this paper introduces the Multimodal Spatiotemporal Graph Attention Network with Uncertainty Quantification (MST-GAT-UQ), a novel deep learning framework for aircraft engine prognostics. The proposed model integrates temporal patterns via CNN-LSTM networks, spatial correlations through graph attention mechanisms, and frequency signatures using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) with 2D CNN processing. Key innovations include a correlation-driven graph construction method that automatically learns sensor relationships from operational data, hierarchical attention fusion to adaptively weight different modalities, and Monte Carlo dropout augmented by temperature scaling for simultaneous Remaining Useful Life (RUL) and health state prediction with calibrated uncertainty intervals. The framework is comprehensively validated on a real-world operational dataset comprising 84 sensors and 43,492 samples from F100-PW-229 turbofan engines, achieving R 2 = 0.911, RMSE = 0.087, MAE = 0.072 on a normalized RUL scale within a synthetic-label verification framework (no ground-truth operational RUL is available for this dataset; reported metrics quantify the model’s fidelity in reproducing a synthetically imposed linear degradation trajectory and should not be interpreted as ground-truth remaining-life predictions), and a synthetic health-state replication accuracy of 99.5% (auxiliary task; health-state labels are a deterministic step-function of the synthetic RUL signal and carry no independent diagnostic information). Comparative analysis against the standard NASA C-MAPSS benchmark is presented as a zero-shot domain-transfer diagnostic, characterising the label-distribution shift between the two datasets, and confirms that native C-MAPSS training yields positive R 2 across all four subsets (FD001–FD004: R 2 = 0.607–0.863). This work represents a significant step toward reliable, uncertainty-aware, and multimodal prognostic systems for safety–critical aviation applications, with uncertainty intervals that are directionally informative but moderately overconfident (empirical coverage 88.7% at the 95% nominal level; ECE = 0.254), indicating that further calibration refinement is required before safety–critical operational deployment.

title: Time-optimal motion trajectory generation incorporating an input shaper for overhead cranes operated by industrial servo systems
abstract: This paper proposes a motion trajectory generation method that achieves time-optimality under input shaping constraints for overhead cranes operated by industrial servo systems. The proposed approach formulates a constrained trajectory optimization problem that minimizes motion time while suppressing residual vibration by embedding a zero-vibration (ZV) or zero-vibration-and-derivative (ZVD) input shaper into the trajectory generation process. By using a simplified model that requires only the natural frequency and damping ratio to characterize vibration, this approach enables practical implementation even when full system identification is difficult. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method are demonstrated through simulations and experiments using an overhead crane apparatus. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves shorter motion times with effective vibration suppression compared to conventional input shaping and maintains robustness against modeling errors in natural frequency and damping ratio.

title: Adaptive cochlea-simulating acoustic diagnosis method of industrial robot RV reducers
abstract: The rotate vector (RV) reducers are consistently subjected to progressive wear and pitting due to the reciprocating rotational motion and variable dynamic loads commonly encountered in industrial robot operations. The internal contact state change of RV reducers caused by these defects would induce abnormal tones when compared with that of health state. It is well known that skilled technicians in industrial sites can identify the machine health state from subtle auditory cues. Therefore, to transfer this ability into an automatic system and provide a clear view of the diagnostic sound patterns, an adaptive cochlea-simulating acoustic diagnosis method is developed to identify the health state of RV reducers in industrial robots through the sound energy distribution obtained by the proposed cochlea-grams. Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) features are extracted from the cochlea-grams to represent the dominant frequency bands in high-energy regions. A cochlea-simulating filter bank design method is then proposed to further strengthen the energy in target frequency bands and to improve the classification performance of different health states. Various experiments of industrial robot are performed to record the operating sound under different health states of RV reducers. The adaptive cochlea-simulating diagnosis method achieves an average fault identification accuracy of 95.98% ± 0.49% and clearly outperforms a Short-Time Fourier Transform-based method and a Gammatone filter bank-based method. The results show that the proposed method will helpful for convenient fault detection for industrial robot RV reducers. The proposed method also shows good performance when analyzing the signals with industrial environmental noise.

title: Cross-specification abrasive belt wear monitoring: a physics-informed deep learning framework with acoustic emission burst indicator
abstract: In abrasive belt grinding, switching between belts of differing grit sizes reduces the predictive accuracy of data-driven wear monitoring models. To address this issue, a physics-informed deep learning framework is proposed for continuous abrasive belt wear monitoring across varying belt specifications, in which grinding mechanics are encoded as mechanism-derived input features and physical constraints are embedded in the loss function to guide network learning. An analysis of grain-workpiece contact mechanics reveals that progressive grain dulling shifts the dominant energy dissipation from efficient cutting to parasitic friction. To capture this transition, Acoustic Emission (AE) signals are leveraged, and a novel indicator, the Cumulative Impulse Density–Duration Ratio (CIDDR), is introduced. This metric captures the statistical evolution of AE burst characteristics providing a physically interpretable proxy for the progressive loss of cutting effectiveness. Subsequently, the framework employs a denoising-aware Stacked Sparse Auto-Encoder (SSAE) to extract compact latent representations from these physics-enhanced inputs, followed by a Physics-informed Causal Temporal Convolutional Network (PI-CTCN) regularized by physics-informed loss to ensure physically consistent wear monitoring. To achieve cross-specification generalization, a parameter-based transfer learning strategy adapts the learned representations to belt-induced domain shifts through selective fine-tuning. Experimental validation on two belt specifications (A45 and A160) grinding TC4 titanium alloy demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves an RMSE of 33.54 mg and R² of 0.9857 under cross-belt transfer conditions, reducing RMSE by approximately 20% compared to training from scratch on the target belt, while maintaining stable and continuous wear monitoring.

title: A multi-dimensional rate-independent hysteretic model for homogeneous, isotropic Duhem-like solids
abstract: The class of Duhem-like solids comprises solid bodies composed of rate-independent hysteretic material modeled via a rate-type constitutive equation including the time-derivatives of the stress and strain tensors. To accurately simulate such a complex behavior, a multi-dimensional model is established in the framework of continuum thermodynamics. Particularly, the proposed model is based on three basic assumptions on the size of the deformation (small deformations), the type of material (rate-independent hysteretic material with linear kinematic and/or isotropic hardening), and the properties of the body (homogeneous and isotropic body). Moreover, it requires four material parameters: two govern the rate-independent hysteretic behavior without hardening, whereas the other two control the linear kinematic and isotropic hardening, respectively. A series of simulations are carried out to show the responses provided by the model for different infinitesimal strain histories, hardening conditions, and values of the material parameters. Finally, both numerical and experimental validations are conducted by adopting, in the order, an existing multi-dimensional model and a set of experimental data available in the literature.

title: Fundamental nonlinear mechanisms for vibration energy harvesting: A unified framework for static and time-varying potentials
abstract: Nonlinear vibration energy harvesters based on bistable mechanisms can achieve broadband response and frequency up-conversion, but their performance strongly depends on the underlying dynamical regime and excitation conditions. In this work, two representative architectures are systematically compared: a static-potential energy (SPE) harvester and a time-varying potential energy (TVPE) harvester based on magnetic interactions. A reduced-order nonlinear model with physically consistent parameter sets is developed for both configurations and used to analyze regime activation, frequency response, and load sensitivity. Experimental investigations are conducted to assess qualitative regime consistency and dynamical trends. Results show that SPE devices rely on threshold-driven inter-well activation and exhibit strong sensitivity to excitation amplitude and electrical load, whereas TVPE systems enable robust slow–fast plucking dynamics and effective energy conversion at low-frequency and low-amplitude inputs typical of human motion. Regime transitions and dominant response patterns are consistently reproduced by the model. The proposed comparative framework highlights key dynamical features that can guide the design of nonlinear energy harvesters and vibration control devices.

title: Convex force reconstruction via non-convex regularization
abstract: Inverse force reconstruction using ℓ1-norm promotes sparsity but suffers from amplitude underestimation. To improve amplitude estimation, this study employs the minimax-concave penalty with a convexity-preserving framework that maintains convexity of the overall cost function despite non-convexity of the regularizer. A numerical solver using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is developed to resolve the saddle-point problem associated with underdetermined force reconstruction in the frequency domain. The proposed scheme operates up to the maximal convexity limit, distinguishing it from existing solvers. Beyond improved amplitude estimation, the non-convex regularization exhibits a unique solution-path characterized by plateau regions where reconstructed amplitudes remain nearly constant across a range of regularization parameter. A parameter selection strategy is introduced using the plateau structure. Numerical and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for sparse force reconstruction.

title: Noise analysis and suppression of whole-angle MEMS gyroscopes based on detection-axes-rotation
abstract: With the development of robotics, aerospace and other fields, the demand for low-cost and low-power MEMS inertial sensors is growing rapidly. MEMS gyroscope operating in whole-angle mode plays an extremely important role due to its high bandwidth, large measurement range and stable scale factor. In the whole-angle mode MEMS gyroscope system, the noise is one of the most challenging issues, as it is closely related to key performance parameters such as bias instability (BI), angle random walk (ARW) and angle resolution. However, the mechanism of noise impact on whole-angle mode MEMS gyroscopes has not yet been elucidated, and there are few corresponding methods to reduce the noise. In this paper, a comprehensive noise model for the whole-angle mode is established to reveal the mechanism by which circuit gain influences gyroscope output noise. Through analysis, we find that increasing the gain before ADC (Kc) can mitigate the impact of such noise. However, in the conventional whole-angle mode, this gain is constrained by the full-scale range (FSR) of the ADC device. To address this issue, the detection-axes-rotation method is employed, which can achieve the effect of detecting axes rotation by adjusting the amplitude configuration of the injected carrier waves. It is only necessary to align the detecting axis x with the pattern angle in real time, and the signal detected by the y-axis will approach zero. In this case, Kc of the y-axis is no longer restricted, and the impact of noise injected during ADC on the angle noise can be reduced by maximizing Kc before ADC. Experimental verification is carried out using the micro-hemispherical gyroscope. The experimental results show that, compared with the conventional whole-angle mode, the whole-angle mode with DAR (Kc of 100) achieves a 75% reduction in ARW (from 0.036∘/h to 0.009∘/h) and a 66% reduction in BI (from 0.132∘/h to 0.045∘/h). Meanwhile, the whole-angle mode with DAR achieves a bandwidth of 100 Hz and a measurement range of ±500°/s.

title: Spatial movement reduction and multidirectional tuning design of an innovative combinational tuned mass damper for floating offshore wind turbines
abstract: Due to stable additional damping to the floating platform, the tuned mass damper (TMD) has become one of the most popular dynamic vibration absorbers for floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs). However, limited by the inherent movement stroke constraints, conventional TMDs cannot fully suppress the dynamic responses of all six degrees of freedom (DOFs) of the floating platform, resulting in insufficient spatial movement reduction of the upper structure of the FOWT. To extend the movement DOFs of the conventional TMDs, an innovative combinational TMD (CTMD) with four DOFs is proposed in this work to mitigate the spatial vibrations of the floating platform for barge-type FOWTs. The structural multi‑body dynamic model of the FOWT attached with a CTMD is established, and multiple loading models of the FOWT are constructed under wind and wave actions. Spatial movement reduction mechanism of the CTMD is revealed, and the multidirectional tuning design of the CTMD is carried out to determine the design parameters of the CTMD control system. The reduction performance of dynamic displacement and spatial movement responses of the CTMD for the FOWT structure are comparatively investigated under wind and wave excitations. The theoretical and numerical results showed that the CTMD improves the reduction effects of the peak and RMS responses at the tower top by over 4.1% and 6.2%, respectively, under five load conditions in different directions compared with conventional TMD, and it is more beneficial for the stability enhancement of the support structure and the fluctuation reduction of the turbine power for FOWT.

title: Calculation and experimental verification of steam turbine journal bearing dynamic coefficients based on experimental trajectory
abstract: The critical speeds of steam turbine rotors depend on the rotor geometry and the accurate calculation of dynamic bearing coefficients. This paper presents a novel numerical approach for calculating the coefficients of hydrodynamic bearings in steam turbines using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Here, two types of journal bearings are considered: plain journal bearings and three-pad journal bearings. The dynamic coefficients are determined using the Linear Regression method, based on the results of CFD simulations performed for a simplified rotor trajectory. The results are compared with those obtained from MESWIR in-house software using 2D Reynolds equations. An innovation in using the Linear Regression method, as well as the Least Squares Regression method, is that the dynamic coefficients can also be calculated for experimentally measured rotor trajectories in two journal bearings of a 1 MW steam turbine in real operating conditions. These results are compared with coefficients derived from theoretical trajectories and MESWIR calculations. This novel approach can be extended to other types of bearings and operating conditions. This study shows that the dynamic coefficients calculated based on the two experimental journal bearing trajectories, a theoretical trajectory, and the MESWIR trajectory all differ from each other, at times even considerably. Nonetheless, more significant are the critical speeds of the rotor, which also are demonstrated in this paper. All the numerically calculated critical speeds are compared with the experimental critical speeds of a 1 MW steam turbine. The three methods for calculating dynamic coefficients are also used to determine the rotor critical speeds. In all these methods, the first synchronous (1X) critical speed of the system is below 2757 rpm, and the superharmonic (2X) critical speed is below 2212 rpm, which is relatively close to the experimentally identified critical speeds (2852 rpm and 2507 rpm) of a 1 MW steam turbine rotor. For the first time, critical speeds calculated using theoretical trajectories have been compared with those obtained from experiments and used to compare various journal-bearing dynamic coefficient methods.

title: Energy-based sum rules for one-dimensional Lorentz resonator systems: Explicit bounds on band-limited absorption and transmission loss
abstract: Conventional acoustic sum rules, typically formulated with wavelength-based integrals and logarithmic expressions, establish performance limits linked to a system’s spatial extent, such as thickness. However, these formulations obscure direct energy relations and leave the equally important role of dynamic mass largely implicit. This work establishes a complementary set of energy-based sum rules for passive one-dimensional Lorentz acoustic resonator systems under plane-wave incidence, providing a framework that explicitly quantifies the distinct contributions of inertia and compliance. By constructing a Herglotz function from the acoustic radiation ratio, we derive two parent integral identities without auxiliary correction terms. The first is an inertial identity governed solely by the system’s effective dynamic mass, which determines the high-frequency behavior. The second is a compliance identity governed by the effective static stiffness, which is related to the system’s spatial extent and controls low-frequency behavior. Using Hölder’s inequality, these two foundational rules yield a continuous family of non-logarithmic bounds on average absorption and transmission loss over arbitrary frequency bands. The theory also yields a generalized band-limited mass law that sets a lower bound on the average transmission loss. Case studies of parallel and cascaded resonators, stretched membranes, and shunted loudspeakers validate the theory, showing how effective mass and stiffness can be extracted from asymptotic limits. Together, the inertial and compliance-based sum rules provide physically transparent design criteria for broadband passive noise control.

title: RGB-D vision for relative motion monitoring of mated components during OWT installation
abstract: Offshore wind turbine (OWT) installation is challenged by the need for precise alignment of large structural components, which makes conventional contact-based measurement methods, such as GNSS or robotic total stations, impractical. This paper presents a vision-based framework for real-time, non-contact monitoring of relative motion between two mated structural components (e.g., a suspended segment and an installed base). The framework formulates position tracking as a state estimation problem, where RGB-D sensors provide position and orientation measurements, further refined through an extended Kalman filter to ensure smooth and accurate tracking. Experimental validation was conducted on two scaled setups: a 1:100 tower segment installation and a 1:160 blade-to-hub mating experiment. The results demonstrate the framework’s capability in tracking individual components. Further evaluation of the 6-DOF relative motion yields EKF-filtered translation root-mean-square errors (RMSE) of 17.3 mm and 29.4 mm for the tower segment and blade-to-hub mating scenarios, respectively. The orientation tracking is quantitatively validated, achieving a high precision of 0.501° RMSE for the installed hub, while also capturing the spatial motion trends of the suspended blade despite the challenges posed by its quasi-cylindrical geometry and low-texture surface. While these scaled laboratory results establish the algorithmic foundation for non-contact relative motion tracking, achieving the strict sub-centimeter tolerances (e.g., 2–5 mm) required for actual 15-MW class OWT flange mating would necessitate the integration of industrial-grade long-range sensors. Overall, the approach enhances installation safety, reduces assembly time, and supports informed decision-making in complex marine environments, providing a foundational vision-based framework that shows potential for offshore wind turbine assembly monitoring.

title: Three-dimensional spherical gradient-index acoustic focusing structure for broadband omnidirectional sound enhancement
abstract: Traditional acoustic sensing has long been constrained in weak signal detection by the rapid attenuation of sound waves propagating through air, severely limiting effective detection ranges. Meanwhile, the approach of ‘sensor-end enhancement’ relying on optimizing the sensor itself is facing significant diminishing marginal returns. Concurrently, existing acoustic metamaterials based on resonance or slow-wave effects commonly suffer from bottlenecks such as narrow operating bandwidths, high angular sensitivity, and difficulties in achieving three-dimensional (3D) integration. To address this, this paper designs a radial gradient refractive-index distribution and proposes a Spherical Acoustic Focusing Structure (SAFS) based on a nested cubic micro-lattice. Within the constraints of additive manufacturing processes, the proposed structure achieves precise control of the equivalent refractive index between 1.0 and 2.5, successfully constructing a 3D SAFS capable of omnidirectionally converging sound waves. Experiments demonstrate that the SAFS achieves stable sound pressure gain for omnidirectional incident sound waves across a broad frequency range of 1.5–4.5 kHz. Application tests further show that the SAFS significantly improves weak-signal detectability, providing a generalized signal-to-noise ratio gain of 14.1 dB for a 2 kHz single-frequency signal and 11.8 dB over the 1.5–4.5 kHz target band. It also exhibits selective enhancement under low- and high-frequency non-target noise interference, confirming its ability to amplify target-band acoustic signals without globally amplifying background noise. As a universal physical front-end enhancer, the SAFS improves system perception performance without requiring modifications to the back-end sensor. It is suitable for applications including micro-drone detection, industrial fault diagnosis, security early warning, and ecological acoustic monitoring. Furthermore, it can serve as a front-end amplification module for acoustic energy harvesting systems in acoustic power generation.

title: Entropy-driven hierarchical framework for robust acoustic emission detection with false-alarm control
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) signals generated by stress corrosion cracking (SCC) are strongly affected by multi-source interference and pronounced nonstationarity, leading to blurred event boundaries and high false-alarm rates. To address these challenges, this study proposes an Entropy-Driven Multi-Stage (EDMS) framework for robust and interpretable AE event detection. EDMS establishes a joint entropy–entropy-rate representation to model crack-induced complexity collapse in non-stationary AE signals, where the synchrosqueezed wavelet transform enhances time–frequency concentration, and the Tsallis entropy–entropy-rate criterion captures transient complexity transitions associated with crack activity. A hierarchical confidence inference and stability-constrained search strategy further ensure reliable detection under complex industrial noise. Experiments conducted on a dedicated SCC monitoring platform with Q235 steel specimens of varying thicknesses demonstrate consistent performance, achieving an Accuracy Gain Rate (AGR) above 0.90, an Error Occurrence Rate (EOR) below 0.10, and Coverage (Cov) exceeding 0.85. The results confirm the high sensitivity and robustness of the proposed entropy-dynamic representation, providing a physics-informed and data-efficient approach for automated AE event detection in noisy environments.

title: Low-complexity recursive constrained adaptive filtering under an M-shaped error-weighted framework with applications in mechanical signal processing
abstract: Constrained adaptive filtering (CAF) has become an essential tool in mechanical signal processing, particularly for applications such as dynamic load identification and active noise control (ANC). A key challenge in this field lies in designing adaptive algorithms that maintain robustness against impulsive disturbances while balancing convergence performance and computational efficiency. This brief proposes a recursive constrained M-shaped error-weighted logarithmic (RCML) algorithm by introducing an M-shaped error-weighted criterion into the constrained adaptive framework. Benefiting from the ability of the M-shaped weighting function to exploit both high-order and low-order moment information of impulsive noise, the RCML algorithm achieves superior convergence and steady-state performance compared to existing recursive methods. In addition, the mean-square convergence analysis and theoretical transient mean-square deviation of the RCML algorithm are presented. To further improve computational efficiency, a low-complexity DCD-RCML algorithm is developed by incorporating the dichotomous coordinate descent scheme, together with its filtered-x form (DCD-FxRCML). Simulation studies and experimental validations with real-world data confirmed the theoretical analysis in non-Gaussian environments and demonstrated that the proposed algorithms provide enhanced robustness and applicability in both dynamic load identification and active noise control applications.

title: Impact acoustic-based damage identification of bridge expansion joints under vehicle-induced excitation using attention-enhanced one-class learning
abstract: Bridge expansion joints are susceptible to deterioration under long-term vehicle loading and environmental effects. The resulting damage may affect structural performance and driving comfort, making rapid and reliable damage identification important for bridge maintenance. This study proposes an impact acoustic-based damage identification method for bridge expansion joints under vehicle-induced excitation using attention-enhanced one-class learning. Acoustic sensors are integrated into a moving load system to acquire acoustic responses from key components, including the center beam, support bar, and concrete in the anchorage zone. The resulting acoustic signals are characterized using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). On this basis, a compact Transformer encoder with an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism, termed ECA-TinyTransformer, is constructed to jointly model global temporal dependencies and critical frequency-band information. At the decision level, Deep Support Vector Data Description (DeepSVDD) models damage identification as anomaly detection using only healthy samples, addressing the scarcity of damage data. Experimental results demonstrate that, under the fully damaged condition (State 4), healthy and damaged samples are clearly separated in the learned feature space. The proposed method achieves accuracies of 0.968, 0.965, and 0.968 for the center beam, support bar, and concrete in the anchorage zone, respectively, with recall values approaching 1.000. Comparative studies further demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over representative temporal modeling architectures and one-class anomaly detection methods. The proposed framework provides an effective and practical solution for intelligent condition assessment of bridge expansion joints under moving-load excitation, highlighting the potential of one-class acoustic monitoring for bridge infrastructure inspection.

title: Dynamic force identification in time domain via dual-level structured sparsity with optimized sensor placement
abstract: Dynamic force identification (DFI) in time domain is a challenging inverse problem due to limited sensing resources, measurement noise, and severe ill-conditioning. Although sparse regularization has proven effective in under-determined settings, existing single-level sparsity models fail to fully exploit the intrinsic spatio-temporal structure of dynamic excitations, often resulting in biased amplitude estimation, unstable force localization, and frequent identification failures. In this study, a novel dual-level structured sparse regularization framework is proposed for time-domain DFI, in which group-wise sparsity is enforced to select active excitation locations while element-wise sparsity captures the compact sparse structure of forces at each location. The resulting non-convex optimization model is efficiently solved using a tailored majorization–minimization algorithm with closed-form updates. In addition, a tensor-based optimal sensor placement strategy is developed to identify informative measurement configurations under sparse sensing constraints. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach are demonstrated through comprehensive numerical simulations and laboratory experiments, highlighting its superior accuracy for time-domain DFI.

title: Nonlinear vibration of a shaft-disk-shaft rotor with initial bending induced by bearing angular misalignment
abstract: The bolted flange spigot connected rotor plays a critical role in rotating machinery due to its high reliability and load-carrying capacity. Nevertheless, bearing angular misalignment, one of the common assembly errors, not only changes the internal contact state of the bearing but also induces initial bending of the rotor, posing a significant challenge to the dynamic performance of the rotor. Existing research lacks investigations into initial bending faults in rotors connected by bolted flanges with spigot joints. In this study, using Euler-Bernoulli beam theory for the shafts and Kirchhoff plate theory for the disk, the nonlinear dynamic model of a bolted flange spigot-connected shaft-disk-shaft rotor (BFSSDSR) is established, accounting for the initial bending resulting from bearing angular misalignment. Based on the model, the effects of rotational speed, misalignment angle, and the phase difference on the rotor’s vibration characteristics are investigated. The results show that the BFSSDSR with initial bending exhibits multiple harmonic responses as well as combination frequency responses associated with the bearing variable compliance frequency. With the variation of rotational speed, the motion state of the rotor system alternates between periodic motion and chaotic/quasi-periodic motion. An increase in the misalignment angle significantly enhances the synchronous vibration response induced by the initial bending, causing the system spectrum to gradually concentrate around the rotational frequency. Moreover, the phase difference between the initial bending and unbalance mainly modulates the spatial distribution of the synchronous response, significantly affecting the rotor orbit shape without altering the frequency components of the system.

title: Prediction of railway-induced ground vibrations incorporating track resilience
abstract: To improve the vibration reduction performance of rail systems, this study incorporates all parameters affecting track resilience into the analysis of railway vibrations. This is performed through a new prediction model developed based on the dynamic reciprocity theorem and transfer mobility concepts. Extensive measurements were conducted over different combinations of tracks with various resilient elements. Based on these measurements, the new model is constructed and validated. The performance of the new model is assessed in vibration analyses of rail transit systems. It is shown that the combined effect of track resilient elements has significant effects on ground vibrations, while neglecting this effect creates an error of approximately 10 dB in predictions. The extent of this error was shown to pose the risk of misleading the decision between variants of new lines or cause frequency interference between the track and receiving structure. The capabilities built into the new approach provide better insight for engineers into the key track factors influencing ground vibrations.

title: Methodology and implementation of a dual-tier dynamic parameter identification for rigid-flexible coupling hoisting robot
abstract: Accuracy of the dynamic model directly affects the control performance of rigid-flexible coupling hoisting robot (RFCHR). Existing methods often fail to identify both robot body and payload parameters under coupling conditions, which greatly limits the control performance of robot in the high-precision applications. To address this issue, a dual-tier dynamic parameter identification method is proposed. An iterative covariance-weighted physical constraint least squares (ICWPC-LS) algorithm is designed to achieve parameter identification in the inner-tier system. This algorithm combines the covariance weighting of torque errors with physical constraints, significantly improving the identification accuracy of RFCHR parameters in practical application. Combining the physical coupling relationship of robot joints and based on deep learning technology, a dynamic compensator suitable for RFCHR is designed with Gated Recurrent Unit-Attention (GRU-AT) in the outer-tier system, which effectively reduces the influence of nonlinear effects that are difficult to model precisely on the parameter identification accuracy, further enhancing the torque prediction accuracy of the dynamic model. The payload parameter identification is also incorporated into the method framework. Effectiveness and superiority of the method are verified on the experimental platform.

title: Time-varying input shaping technique for rigid-flexible coupled linear servo based on online resonant frequency estimation
abstract: Since traditional input shaping techniques have certain limitations in handling vibration frequency mismatch, this paper proposes a time-varying input shaping technique (TVIST) based on online frequency estimation and updating for rigid-flexible coupled linear servo systems. To estimate the system resonant frequency in real time with high accuracy, an online frequency estimation method based on a composite second-order generalized integrator-frequency locked loop (SOGI-FLL) is adopted, where the q-axis current is used as the target signal, eliminating the need for end-effector position sensors. From the perspective of digital implementation, the nonlinear effects of TVIST frequency variations on reference trajectory shaping are analyzed. Based on this, a TVIST-based vibration suppression strategy is developed. It realizes the input shaper through an output-side algorithm and incorporates a frequency updating algorithm that takes into account both the nonlinear effects and the dynamic characteristics of frequency estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that, even in the presence of frequency parameter mismatch, the proposed method can effectively suppress residual vibration within the current motion cycle, thereby improving the end-effector positioning accuracy of precision motion systems.

title: Nonparametric seismic fragility curves for structural systems using ordinal regression
abstract: This study presents a nonparametric ordinal regression framework for constructing seismic fragility curves for structures. This approach preserves the ordered structure of the damage states without relying on predefined distributional assumptions, as in traditional methods. The proposed methodology employs a nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation coupled with kernel density estimation to estimate a flexible link function, thereby avoiding assumptions regarding a specific error distribution. Three numerical case studies were considered: a four-story reinforced concrete (RC) moment-resisting frame building, a three-span concrete box-girder bridge, and a four-story steel special moment-resisting frame building. Each structural system was analyzed using nonlinear time-history analyses with 320 ground motions, and the damage states were defined based on the simulation results. The proposed nonparametric ordinal model (NPOM) achieved test accuracies of 82 %, 83 %, and 81 % for the RC frame, bridge column, and steel frame, respectively, outperforming the ordinal probit model (OPM), which achieved test accuracies of 78 %, 78 %, and 76 %, respectively. Furthermore, seismic fragility curves for the three structures were developed and compared using two ordinal models (NPOM and OPM) and the traditional linear regression method (LRM) under the assumption of a lognormal distribution. For all three structures, the LRM-based fragility curves exhibited higher median fragility values for higher limit states than the fragility curves derived from the ordinal models. For the RC and steel frames, OPM yielded median fragility values that differed from those of NPOM by up to approximately 12 %, whereas for the bridge column the OPM and NPOM fragility curves were comparable.

title: Data-driven modeling of synthetic wind speed signals with adaptive temporal resolution
abstract: As wind energy systems continue to expand in size and complexity, ensuring their structural reliability under stochastic wind loading has become increasingly critical. Accurate wind speed modeling across multiple temporal scales is essential for reliability assessment, extreme load estimation, and risk-based design. However, a central challenge in data-driven wind speed and storm hazard analysis is the limited temporal resolution of available wind measurements. In practice, wind speed data are often provided as 10 min or hourly averages. While such coarse discretizations are sufficient for estimating aggregate power production, they fail to capture the high-frequency variability that governs extreme loading, structural response, and short-term system dynamics.This paper introduces a novel signal-processing based framework for synthesizing high-resolution wind speed time series from coarse measurements while maintaining statistical and spectral consistency. The methodology operates in the frequency domain, where spectral components are extrapolated and modeled to reflect physically plausible high-frequency behavior while also enforcing a strict energy conservation and preserving extreme-value characteristics.The resulting synthetic wind speed exhibits essential statistical characteristics, including mean values, variance, maximum amplitudes, and distributional properties, this enables high-fidelity stochastic simulations at resolutions suitable for advanced engineering and environmental analyses. The results indicate that the proposed methodology is capable of generating high-resolution, data-informed wind speed realizations with consistent statistical and spectral behavior. The framework provides a robust and computationally efficient tool for wind modeling.

title: A physics-guided evidential multimodal uncertainty framework for small-sample welding defect detection using magneto-optical and infrared imaging
abstract: Traditional data-driven welding defect detection methods often suffer from poor interpretability, performance degradation under small-sample conditions, and an inability to quantify decision-making reliability. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel Physics-guided Evidential-based Multimodal Uncertainty Framework (PEMUF) for weld defect classification using magneto-optical imaging (MOI) and infrared thermography (IRT). A coordinated MOI-IRT nondestructive testing system is developed to acquire complementary magnetic and thermal responses of weld defects. Based on the distinct physical sensitivities of the two modalities, leakage magnetic field information from MOI and heat diffusion characteristics from IRT are explicitly encoded into modality-specific prior channels, improving the physical interpretability and discriminability of input representations. PEMUF further combines hierarchical multimodal interaction, spectral manifold augmentation, and evidential fusion. The hierarchical attention mechanism enhances intra-modal representation learning and cross-modal complementary interaction, while spectral manifold augmentation enriches the effective feature distribution under limited training samples. In addition, Dempster-Shafer evidential fusion with Dirichlet uncertainty modeling is introduced to generate both defect-category predictions and uncertainty scores. Experiments are conducted on a four-class resistance spot weld defect dataset, including defect-free, crack, pit, and incomplete fusion samples. Using the full training set, PEMUF achieves an Accuracy of 99.04 %, a Macro F1 of 0.9908, and a Brier Score of 0.0271. More importantly, when only 20 % of the training samples are used, the model still maintains an Accuracy of 96.31 %, a Macro F1 of 0.9617, and a Brier Score of 0.0529, demonstrating strong robustness and probability calibration under small-sample conditions. Comparative experiments, ablation studies, confusion matrices, t-SNE visualization, Grad-CAM++ analysis, and uncertainty evaluation further confirm that physical priors, spectral manifold augmentation, and evidential fusion jointly improve feature discrimination, generalization, and reliability-aware decision-making. These results indicate that PEMUF provides an effective and reliable solution for small-sample multimodal weld defect inspection.

title: Anti-load performance evaluation method for electro-hydrostatic actuators based on physics-embedded attention mechanism
