abstract: High-precision performance degradation evaluation of electro-hydrostatic actuators (EHAs) is critical for aerospace reliability. Among all potential hardware degradation, internal leakage stands out as the most frequent and dominant fault in EHA systems. However, existing methods often fail in dynamic flight environments, where genuine internal leakage signatures are deeply entangled with external variable load disturbances. To address this load-fault coupling challenge, this study proposes an Anti-load Performance Evaluation Method. Firstly, an EHA dynamic model is established to analytically derive a Baseline Contribution Score (BCS), explicitly quantifying the relative sensitivities of multi-source signals to faults versus loads. Then after a dual-screening purification of statistical features, the BCS is deployed as a dual-purpose physical constraint linking the subsequent core modules. It first functions as a physical prior in a Physics-Embedded Channel Attention Mechanism to adaptively highlight fault signatures while suppressing load noise, and then acts as a regularization penalty within a Correlation-Regularized Stacked Autoencoder to constrain the deep fusion process. Driven by this sequential BCS guidance, the network ultimately condenses these refined representations into a highly robust, anti-load 1D Health Indicator. Validated through simulations and physical testbench experiments, the ACFN successfully disentangles complex coupled signals into a linearly separable manifold. It achieves a superior diagnostic accuracy of 95.24% under the 3 kN load. This physics-guided framework effectively bridges the gap between mechanistic interpretability and deep learning, providing a highly robust solution for EHA health management.

title: Physically driven multi-modal feature fusion for interpretable tool wear state identification in CFRP milling
abstract: Tool condition monitoring (TCM) in Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) milling remains highly challenging due to the pervasive lack of physical interpretability. To address the gap, this study proposes a physically driven multi-modal feature fusion framework. The methodology is rigorously validated on 118 experimental samples derived from four distinct cemented carbide substrates—varying in WC grain size and Co content—under fixed industrial cutting parameters (Vc = 200 m/min, fn = 0.5 mm/rev, ae = 4 mm, and ap = 10 mm). Cutting force and acoustic emission (AE) signal features were dimensionality reduced via Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Tool wear states are subsequently classified using a novel gated multi-modal fusion network reinforced by a hybrid GAN-Mixup data augmentation. Cross-substrate generalization is empirically verified through a leave-one-substrate-out testing protocol, achieving accuracy of 93.10%. Comprehensive ablation studies corroborate the necessity: isolating either force or AE signals degrades accuracy to 62.07%, while the physical gating mechanism independently yields a 10.34% accuracy improvement over standard feature concatenation. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis is employed to map critical PCA features back to the raw sensor domains, which reveals that the collapse of force spectral energy and the dynamic shift in AE peak frequencies physically encode the transition from fiber shearing to matrix friction during tool wear. Ultimately, this approach provides a robust, physically interpretable pathway for deploying multi-sensor condition monitoring in intelligent composite manufacturing.

title: Meta-excitation of shear waves in three-dimensional elastic solids
abstract: Shear-wave (S-wave) excitation in elastic solids typically relies on tangential actuation to achieve high modal purity, thereby limiting flexibility and efficiency in practical applications. In this work, a surface-normal encoding paradigm is proposed to enable directional S-wave generation using only normal surface excitation. By spatially encoding the phase (0 and π) of an array of normally oriented point sources, a directional shear wavefield can be synthesized without introducing tangential displacement or traction, thereby transforming the excitation mechanism from conventional tangential driving to phase-controlled wavefield construction based on normal actuation. To efficiently predict three-dimensional elastic wavefields, a machine learning-assisted semi-analytical framework is developed, allowing rapid evaluation under both single- and multi-source excitations. Based on this framework, square and circular meta-exciters are designed and optimized. The square configuration generates highly directional S-waves concentrated at horizontal angles of 0° and 180°, with dominant radiation in the vertical range of 25°–50°, whereas the circular configuration enables S-wave excitation over the entire horizontal plane (0°–360°). These results provide an efficient and flexible strategy for controllable S-wave excitation, with strong potential for high-throughput, couplant-free nondestructive testing (NDT) applications.

title: Stable bandwidth expansion for FTR measurement in modal-frequency-mismatched MEMS gyroscopes over a wide temperature range
abstract: The Force-to-Rebalance (FTR) mode has become the most widely adopted measurement scheme for MEMS gyroscopes. Nevertheless, the rate-measurement bandwidth remains a key bottleneck that restricts its deployment in broader application scenarios. To address this issue, this paper proposes a bandwidth-expansion method based on a proportional–integral–resonant (PIR) controller for a quad-mass MEMS gyroscope operating under modal frequency mismatch. First, a bandwidth-expansion flowchart integrating time-domain and frequency-domain analyses is established, providing the theoretical basis for subsequent controller design and performance evaluation. Next, the mechanism underlying the bandwidth limitation of PI-controlled FTR rate measurement is analyzed, revealing the intrinsic difficulty of simultaneously achieving sufficient stability margins and a widened bandwidth with conventional strategies. Then, guided by the proposed workflow, a PIR-based FTR bandwidth-expansion scheme is developed and validated through simulations. Finally, experiments were conducted at room temperature under four different controller parameter configurations. The results demonstrate that the PIR controller increases the FTR measurement bandwidth to 125 Hz, while the measured bandwidths under different ambient temperatures remain above 120 Hz, thereby significantly enhancing the gyroscope’s dynamic response capability and expanding its potential application range.

title: Intelligent identification of bearing dynamic parameters using a two-stage physics-informed residual KAN with TSA and frequency-domain integration
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage physics-informed residual Kolmogorov–Arnold Network framework integrated with Time Synchronous Averaging and frequency-domain integration for identifying the equivalent mass and damping parameters of bearing–rotor systems from measured acceleration signals. First, a two-degree-of-freedom bearing dynamic model is established to derive the time-varying equivalent stiffness in the selected direction. Time Synchronous Averaging is then applied to the measured acceleration signal, and the corresponding velocity and displacement signals are reconstructed through frequency-domain integration. In Stage 1, a constrained linear physical backbone, mathematically equivalent to a linear regressor, traverses the simulated stiffness phases and provides preliminary estimates of the equivalent mass and damping. In Stage 2, the principal nonlinear role of KAN is realized through an additive B-spline residual representation, which accounts for unmodeled dynamics while keeping the physical mass and damping terms explicitly separated. A near-optimal stiffness-phase ensemble strategy is further employed to reduce parameter sensitivity to small phase deviations. Experimental results at 1800 and 2400 r/min yielded equivalent masses of 4.3201 and 4.3385 kg, respectively, with a cross-speed difference of 0.43%. Under the same residual-capacity limit, the residual KAN and residual MLP achieved similar equation-reconstruction errors, whereas the residual KAN provided more stable equivalent-mass estimates. The proposed framework provides a physically structured residual-learning approach in which the explicit physical coefficients are separated from the nonlinear model-discrepancy representation.

title: Finite-time backstepping control for nonlinear active suspension with time-delay compensation via IT2 fuzzy observer
abstract: Active suspension systems (ASS) are widely employed in intelligent chassis to improve vehicle ride comfort. However, their performance is significantly degraded by nonlinear characteristics, external disturbances, and input time delay encountered during vehicle operation, leading to reduced ride comfort and handling stability. To address these issues, this paper proposes an adaptive control strategy that integrates interval type-2 fuzzy logic with backstepping control. First, an interval type-2 fuzzy system is utilized to approximate system nonlinearities and external disturbances, thereby enhancing model accuracy. Then, a backstepping controller is designed, in which a time delay compensation mechanism is incorporated to mitigate delay-induced effects and ensure system stability under dynamic conditions. Furthermore, a finite-time dynamic surface control approach is introduced to overcome the slow convergence and the “explosion of complexity” inherent in conventional backstepping methods. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is validated through numerical simulations and experimental studies. The results demonstrate that, under both random and bump road conditions, the proposed method significantly improves ride comfort performance compared with existing control approaches, while achieving the smallest tracking error. The proposed strategy provides an effective framework for vibration control of ASS under multi-source uncertainties and time delay effects, and offers valuable insights for engineering applications in intelligent vehicle chassis systems.

title: Predicting chaotic average output power in bi-stable energy harvesters through unstable periodic orbits: Theoretical analysis and experimental validation
abstract: While bi-stable energy harvesters (BEHs) provide a promising approach to broadband vibrational energy harvesting, they frequently exhibit chaotic motion. Although chaotic responses can be efficient, quantitatively evaluating their average output power poses significant challenges for deterministic theoretical frameworks. To address this challenge, this paper investigates the theoretical approach for predicting the chaotic average output power of BEHs utilizing the unstable periodic orbits (UPOs) that form the skeleton of the chaotic attractor. Through numerical iteration on the corresponding Poincaré map, 1,106,388 UPOs up to period 20 are detected. Their geometry, characteristic multipliers and bifurcations are systematically analyzed. We demonstrate that the chaotic average output power can be quantitatively evaluated using UPO-based averaging frameworks, including the cycle expansion formula, which is established with a rigorous mathematical proof. Furthermore, the theoretical predictions are validated through experiments on a magnetically coupled piezoelectric cantilever beam. Experimental validations demonstrate that the UPO-based analytical framework accurately predicts the chaotic average output power across diverse excitation conditions, achieving an absolute error of less than 10%. These findings provide new insights in understanding chaotic motion of BEHs and illustrate the relationship between the regular and chaotic dynamics. The results can be further applied as deterministic foundations for optimization of a BEH in its chaotic regime.

title: Utility-driven adaptive model selection for digital twinning
abstract: Digital twins have become central to modern engineering by providing interconnected virtual representations that mirror the behavior of physical assets. Their effectiveness, however, depends critically on the fidelity and efficiency of the underlying computational models used for decision support. This work introduces an adaptive Bayesian framework for quantifying and optimizing the fidelity, efficiency, and overall utility of such virtual representations when approximating system responses in decision-oriented contexts. By integrating reduced-order models (ROMs) within a Bayesian inference and decision-theoretic setting, the framework identifies, at any point in time, the lowest-cost model capable of delivering the required predictive accuracy across all quantities of interest, while rigorously accounting for the uncertainty associated with each model resolution. The approach maximizes an expected-utility function that balances two competing attributes: (i) precision, reflecting the effect of over- or under-estimating target quantities on decision quality, and (ii) computational efficiency, ensuring feasibility for real-time inference. Leveraging continuously assimilated monitoring data, the framework performs this model selection recursively, enabling the virtual twin to evolve in tandem with the physical system. The resulting methodology supports automated decisions on whether to retain the current model, switch to an alternative resolution, or trigger retraining—thus establishing a pathway toward adaptive, trustworthy digital twins for engineering decision support.

title: Kalman filter-aided vision transformer for seismic deformation measurement of self-centering structures
abstract: Accurate, long-duration, and marker-free measurement of seismic deformation is critical for evaluating the performance of self-centering structures. Conventional contact sensors offer limited spatial coverage and are challenging to deploy, while vision-based tracking is susceptible to baseline instability and jitter, especially under small, cyclic, and non-monotonic joint opening responses. This study proposes KF-STARK, a Kalman filter-aided vision-transformer tracking framework for self-correcting, non-contact deformation measurement. By coupling transformer-based template–search region matching with Kalman filter-based state estimation, KF-STARK enforces motion continuity, stabilizes the measurement baseline, and suppresses transient tracking errors and jitter, with negligible computational overhead. Validated through pseudo-dynamic tests on T-shaped and cruciform self-centering frame joints subjected to eight earthquake-like excitations, KF-STARK achieves a maximum normalized root mean square error of 3.08% for column-top displacement, 7.80% for joint opening displacement, and 4.41% for joint opening rotation, compared to sensor-based reference measurements. It reduces tracking jitter by more than 40%, supports marker-free tracking on natural targets, maintains accurate global displacement tracking under random frame drops, and enables real-time processing of 4096 × 3000-pixel image sequences, demonstrating its effectiveness as a vision-based deformation measurement framework.

title: A unified framework for equation discovery and dynamic prediction of hysteretic systems
abstract: Hysteresis is a nonlinear phenomenon with memory effects, where a system's output depends on both its current state and past states. It is prevalent in various physical and mechanical systems, such as yielding structures under seismic excitation, ferromagnetic materials, and piezoelectric actuators. Analytical models like the Bouc-Wen model are often employed but rely on idealized assumptions and careful parameter calibration, limiting their applicability to diverse or mechanism-unknown behaviors. Existing equation discovery approaches for hysteresis are often system-specific or rely on predefined model libraries, which limit their flexibility and ability to capture the hidden mechanisms. To address these challenges, this research classifies equation discovery problems for hysteretic systems and develops a unified framework in which the state-space form is reformulated, and hysteretic variables are treated as trainable parameters from data. The framework further employs symbolic regression (SR) to automatically recover explicit governing equations without relying on predefined libraries, unlike methods such as sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in recovering governing equations for hysteretic systems, even in a challenging Full Equation Discovery setting, where prior information is extremely limited, and solving the equations naturally enables the dynamic prediction of hysteretic systems.

title: An acoustic velocity-constrained equivalent source method for acoustic imaging with the acoustic vector sensor array
abstract: Acoustic vector sensor arrays can simultaneously acquire acoustic pressure scalar and three-dimensional acoustic velocity vector data. However, in complex experimental environments such as aeroacoustics, effectively fusing multi-dimensional acoustic information to achieve high-precision acoustic source imaging remains challenging. This paper proposes an Acoustic Velocity-Constrained Equivalent Source Method (CESM), which constructs a multi-physics coupled inverse problem solution framework by integrating acoustic pressure and acoustic velocity. The core innovation lies in establishing an explicit physical relationship between acoustic pressure and acoustic velocity. By synergistically applying Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, it imposes robust physical constraints on equivalent source inversion, significantly reducing the solution space while enhancing stability and fidelity. Systematic numerical simulations and experimental validations demonstrate that, under the same amount of boundary condition data, CESM exhibits superior acoustic source identification capability and reconstruction robustness across a broad frequency band. Under adverse conditions, such as small source spacing, considerable array distance, and background noise, its localization accuracy and reconstruction error are significantly better than those of traditional equivalent source methods that rely solely on acoustic pressure or normal acoustic velocity. This study substantially enhances the information utilization efficiency of vector arrays through a multi-physics coupling mechanism, providing a novel solution for high-precision acoustic source imaging in acoustics and aeroacoustics.

title: Hydraulic system compound fault diagnosis based on decoupling-oriented feature optimization and uncertainty-aware evidential fusion
abstract: Compound fault diagnosis in complex hydraulic systems remains challenging because of strong feature coupling among fault combinations. This paper proposes a D-S (Dempster-Shafer) theory-enhanced convolutional neural network (DSNN) integrating decoupling-oriented feature optimization with uncertainty-aware evidential fusion. The proposed method reconstructs the original diagnosis task into several similarity-aware subtasks to improve the separability of compound fault features under coupled fault modes. Fault categories are first grouped according to feature-distribution distances. The divided groups are used as the focal elements for subsequent D-S theory-based diagnostic reasoning, where uncertainty-aware soft grouping allows overlapping focal elements. Then, dedicated CNN-based submodels are trained to estimate basic probability assignments (BPAs) for divided focal elements while performing task-specific feature optimization. Finally, a differentiable D-S evidence fusion layer combines the BPAs from all submodels and indicates conflicts among submodel evidence through the conflict factor. Experiments on an SCM hydraulic test rig and an open-source hydraulic dataset show that DSNN achieves superior diagnostic accuracy and robustness.

title: Nonlinear structural health monitoring of a planar Slider-Crank linkage using VAM and HHG techniques
abstract: Mechanisms and other moving devices typically have joints with clearance due to manufacturing and assembly requirements. However, if the clearance value becomes excessive, it can indicate potential damage to the mechanisms and lead to reduced accuracy, efficiency, and other issues. Therefore, it is essential to identify increased joint clearance promptly to prevent destructive effects and high maintenance costs. Recently, structural health monitoring (SHM) methods have gained significant attention from researchers because of their effectiveness and cost-efficiency. This research analyzes the performance of a slider-crank linkage with radial clearance in its revolute joints by examining the time histories of the links’ accelerations. In this way, the fast Fourier transform of the acceleration time signal is analyzed using nonlinear monitoring methods, including vibro-acoustic modulation (VAM) and higher harmonic generation (HHG). The primary objective of this research is to investigate how variations in clearance affect the frequency characteristics of the mechanism’s acceleration response. By accounting for the nonlinear nature of the mechanism, our approaches differentiate between the outputs of the damaged mechanism and those of a healthy reference mechanism, thus isolating the additional nonlinear contribution induced by joint clearance. In this context, the term “healthy reference mechanism” denotes a physically consistent baseline response obtained from the validated model, rather than an unrealistically perfect or noise-free signal. Finally, the validity of the proposed baseline-referenced method is demonstrated through a detailed numerical example.

title: Revisiting the characteristics of repetitive transients caused by rotating machinery faults and A new fault signature indicator for quantification and extraction
abstract: Repetitive transients, as typical vibration fault components caused by rotating machine faults, are widely regarded as exhibiting both impulsiveness and cyclostationarity. Therefore, many fault signature indicators (FSIs) are designed based on the criteria of impulsiveness and cyclostationarity. These FSIs are then employed within signal processing models to extract the fault components of interest. However, our experimental observations reveal several previously overlooked phenomena: (1) Some repetitive transients exhibit impulsiveness weaker than that of white Gaussian noise (WGN); (2) Some repetitive transients originate from the rotating shaft rather than from bearing or gear faults. These phenomena indicate that characterizing fault components by impulsiveness and cyclostationarity is neither universally applicable nor sufficiently comprehensive for fault component extraction in certain scenarios. To address this challenge, first, a new concept—termed pseudo-non-impulsive repetitive transients (PNIRT)—is introduced to describe fault components exhibiting quantitatively weak impulsiveness. Second, simulation study reveals that that such PNIRT tend to occur when the FCF is relatively high and each transient decays slowly. Third, to quantify and detect repetitive transients specifically induced by bearing and gear faults, this article directly models and characterizes the fault characteristic frequency (FCF) to construct a dedicated FSI. The resulting FSI is subsequently adopted as the objective function of a signal processing model to extract repetitive transients. The proposed FSI not only enables fault component extraction but also yields an estimated FCF, thereby facilitating identification of the fault type associated with the extracted transients. The FSI-based method outperforms kurtogram, Autogram, and IMD in extracting PNIRT in two real-world experimental cases. The significance of this work lies in prompting researchers to critically reexamine the widespread reliance on the impulsiveness criterion for extracting fault-related repetitive transients—thus offering a novel research perspective to enhance signal processing methodologies for rotating machinery diagnostics.

title: Fault transient extraction for rolling bearing fault diagnosis based on coefficient-orthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization
abstract: Extracting fault transients from vibration signals is crucial for rolling bearing fault diagnosis. Existing signal decomposition methods, however, generally isolate such transients only within frequency bands where they are initially dominant, while failing to recover those masked by interference in other bands. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a fault transient extraction method based on coefficient-orthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization (CONMF). First, the raw vibration signal is mapped into the time–frequency domain via a complex-valued continuous wavelet transform (CWT), yielding the corresponding magnitude and phase matrices. The magnitude matrix is then decomposed by CONMF over a range of factorization ranks into a series of rank-one component matrices, enabling the separation of fault transients from interference components along the temporal dimension. These component matrices are subsequently recombined with the original phase matrix to reconstruct the complex-valued coefficients, from which the time-domain sub-signals are recovered through the inverse CWT. Finally, the sub-signal with the maximum frequency-domain signal-to-noise ratio is identified as the one containing the target fault transients. Validation using simulated and experimental bearing signals demonstrates that the proposed CONMF-based fault transient extraction approach achieves a more complete extraction of fault transients than benchmark methods, particularly for those masked by interference, and produces clearer diagnostic features.

title: The adaptive blind filtering: A unified framework for repetitive transient extraction linking blind deconvolution and narrowband envelope analysis
abstract: Blind deconvolution is a popular signal processing method in rotating machinery fault diagnosis to extract repetitive impulses induced by rotating component faults. However, blind deconvolution methods rooted in time domain convolution are limited by the filter length parameter and may behave unstably under varying operating conditions. To this end, a new paradigm for repetitive transient extraction, named adaptive blind filtering (ABF), is proposed in this paper and applied to the fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. ABF essentially deconvolves the measured signal from the frequency domain perspective to recover the original repetitive transients and novelly links blind deconvolution and another popular approach, i.e., narrowband envelope analysis. In this methodology, a cyclostationarity significance index-gram (CSIgram) is developed to estimate the differential distribution of repetitive transient information across the entire frequency band, enabling adaptive identification of one or multiple resonant frequency bands dominated by repetitive transients. The distribution of repetitive transient information within various frequency bands also allows a frequency-dependent weight function to be automatically constructed, which acts as the frequency-domain form of the inverse filter, enabling the measured signal to be adaptively filtered through frequency-domain blind deconvolution. ABF is a unified framework for blind deconvolution and narrowband envelope analysis and is able to automatically extract and fuse repetitive transient information in multiple resonant frequency bands while effectively removing multi-source interference noise. It overcomes the limitations of blind deconvolution that requires filter length configuration and narrowband envelope analysis that struggles to accurately determine the resonant frequency and bandwidth and focuses only on one resonant frequency band. Validations on synthesized simulation signals and actual railway train bearing experimental signals, as well as comparisons with typical envelope analysis and blind deconvolution methods, demonstrate that ABF is an excellent and promising repetitive transient extraction method in rolling element bearing fault diagnosis.

title: Convolution-based reformulation and Kalman-filter identification of short-time kernel operators for seat-human vibration modeling
abstract: Accurate modeling of seat-human vibration dynamics is important for response prediction and vibration-control design. However, practical seat-human systems may exhibit locally varying dynamic behavior because of occupant-seat interactions, contact-condition changes, and operating-condition variability, which limits the effectiveness of models based on globally fixed mass, damping, and stiffness parameters. This study proposes a short-time dynamic-operator identification framework based on a convolution-based reformulation of the classical vibration model and Kalman-filter-based recursive estimation. The local input-output relationship between the relative motion and head acceleration is represented by three low-order equivalent operators derived from the temporal moments of an equivalent convolution relationship. Within each short-time window, the operators are treated as a slowly varying state vector and are recursively identified using measured relative displacement, velocity, and acceleration. The operators obtained from multiple windows are subsequently aligned and averaged to construct a reusable finite-support operator representation for prediction on unseen data segments without further parameter updating. The framework was evaluated using vertical floor and head acceleration measurements obtained from three different truck-seat systems under idle-in-park conditions. Multiple operator lengths and identification-prediction data partitions were examined. The results show that the proposed method consistently reconstructs the dominant waveform, local response variation, and phase evolution of the measured head acceleration using limited identification data. Baseline comparisons further indicate that the time-varying operator model provides more accurate response reconstruction than fixed operator, fixed-parameter mass-damping-stiffness (MCK), and time-varying MCK models. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for short-time identification and extended prediction of seat-human vibration responses under the tested operating conditions. Further validation is required before extending the method to other excitation conditions or dynamic systems.

title: A lightweight multi-scale ensemble learning framework for seismic fragility assessment of damped outrigger structures
abstract: An increasing number of supertall buildings have adopted damped outrigger systems (DOS) as an effective strategy for mitigating seismic hazards. However, structures equipped with DOS exhibit complex nonlinear behavior under earthquake loading, and substantial computational resources and data are required for fragility analysis. Consequently, existing seismic fragility frameworks often fail to provide reliable and rapid estimates of damage probabilities for DOS-equipped structures. To address these challenges, a Multi-Scale Ensemble LightGBM framework (MSE-LightGBM) is developed in this study. The framework is constructed based on the LightGBM architecture and incorporates an entropy-guided multiscale resampling (EGMSR) strategy to extract informative multiresolution subsamples and enhance data diversity. In addition, a redundancy-aware ReliefF feature selection method (RA-RFS) is integrated to construct a discriminative feature subset with low redundancy, thereby enabling efficient damage state classification. The MSE-LightGBM framework that has been proposed is validated through its implementation on a typical damped outrigger system (DOS). A detailed nonlinear finite element model of a viscous-damped outrigger structure (VDOS) is developed to accurately capture its dynamic response. Utilizing this model, an extensive dataset is compiled from 600 nonlinear time-history analyses conducted with 40 unique ground motion records. The maximum inter-story drift ratio is chosen as the key engineering demand parameter to define structural damage and to aid in the classification of damage states and fragility evaluation. Building on this dataset, seismic fragility analysis is conducted using the MSE-LightGBM model. The results indicate that the proposed framework exhibits strong generalization capability, achieving prediction accuracies exceeding 96.43% even under conditions of limited sample size and class imbalance. This marks a significant improvement over conventional seismic fragility analysis methods. Overall, the MSE-LightGBM framework provides an effective and practical solution for rapid seismic vulnerability assessment and intelligent performance evaluation of complex supertall structures.

title: Beyond the fit: assessing bias-variance trade-off in johnson-cook constitutive modeling for AA5182
abstract: Physics-based predictive models often contain known inadequacies due to their simplified representation of underlying physical systems, introducing systematic deviations from reality. Despite this, they tend to generalize better than their purely empirical counterparts and are often the only tools available to evaluate or predict the performance of complex engineering systems. In this paper, we present a principled framework for calibrating simulation models with known deficiencies against experimental data and for evaluating their predictive ability. Discussions explore the modeling of a cylindrical AA5182 aluminum alloy specimen tested in compression at temperatures ranging from 200 - 500°C, and at strain rates of 0.001 and 1s-1. A finite element model of the specimen is constructed in Abaqus/CAE 2025 using the Johnson-Cook constitutive model, a common choice for simulating alloy behavior due to its computational efficiency. The Johnson-Cook model has several alloy-specific parameters that must be calibrated against experimental data, introducing uncertainty into the finite element model predictions. Additionally, its simplified treatment of strain hardening leads to systematic discrepancies between simulated and observed material responses, which can be inferred through an independent, empirically trained error function. Herein, we explicitly account for these uncertainties and discrepancies and evaluate the bias-variance trade-off in the model predictions. We propose a metric, Calibration Flexibility Measure, to quantitatively evaluate the trade-off between goodness-of-fit and model complexity. Key decisions, such as selection of calibration parameters, integration of prior knowledge, and definition of model-form error are explored to assess and characterize their effects on posterior distributions and predictive performance.

title: Stochastic wave simulation of non-Gaussian wind fields based on the maximum entropy-enhanced piecewise Hermite polynomial model
abstract: Addressing the non-Gaussian characteristics prevalent in wind fields for large-span structural engineering projects, as well as the computational cost and numerical instability issues associated with traditional cross-power spectral density (CPSD) matrix decomposition methods when applied to large-scale simulation points. To this end, this paper proposes a new method for simulating stationary non-Gaussian wind fields by integrating the stochastic wave approach, the maximum entropy method (MEM), and the piecewise Hermite polynomial model (PHPM). Based on the frequency-wavenumber spectrum (FWS), the method first efficiently generates the underlying Gaussian wind velocity field in a continuous spatial domain using the stochastic wave approach. It then uses the MEM to reconstruct the target marginal probability density function (MPDF) under finite-moment constraints and embeds it into the moment-based PHPM, thereby enabling accurate translation of the non-Gaussian wind velocity field from the underlying Gaussian one. Therefore, the proposed method possesses high accuracy and efficiency, and is particularly suitable for simulating large-scale non-Gaussian wind fields. Numerical examples with four distinct non-Gaussian target distributions are utilized to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Results show the proposed method is more accurate and efficient than the traditional method, especially for strongly non-Gaussian and large-scale simulation point conditions.

title: A physics-based analytical model of blade tip sensor waveforms for vibration parameter identification
abstract: Monitoring rotating blade vibration is essential for turbomachinery operational reliability. Parameter identification based on sensor waveform analysis offers potential advantages over traditional blade tip timing (BTT) due to its rich information content. However, many waveform-based identification methods still rely on simplified or symmetric empirical waveform models, such as Gauss-type functions, especially when used as forward models in dynamic parameter identification. When applied to blades with complex geometries such as grooves or twists, these models may introduce waveform-model mismatch and reduce identification accuracy. To address this issue, a geometry-adaptive physical model (GAPM) is proposed for capacitive blade-tip sensor waveforms. Derived from electrostatic field theory, GAPM integrates an equivalent geometry method and a nonlinear correction strategy to represent waveform asymmetry and distortion. Furthermore, a two-phase identification framework is established to decouple static sensor parameters from dynamic blade vibration. Numerical simulations evaluate the model’s ability to represent the sensor responses of straight, grooved, and twisted grooved blades. Rotating experiments using a straight blade further show that the proposed framework can identify the main vibration-frequency and amplitude trends under the tested transient run-up and steady-speed conditions. These results provide a physical modeling basis for waveform-based vibration monitoring of turbomachinery blades with geometry-dependent sensor responses.

title: Adaptive short time fractional Fourier transform and its applications in locomotive gear fault diagnosis
abstract: Transient Motor Current Signature Analysis extends the applicability of motor current signature analysis by tracking the time–frequency trajectory of fault components in the motor current signal through time–frequency analysis. However, commonly used time–frequency analysis methods suffer from time-frequency blurring when dealing with strongly time-varying signals. The fractional Fourier transform achieves time–frequency representation by rotating the time–frequency plane coordinate axes around the origin, and it offers high time–frequency resolution when the parameters are chosen accurately. This paper introduces the short-time fractional Fourier transform for tracking the time–frequency trajectories of fault information. It is largely unaffected by the rate of change of the signal frequency and can achieve higher time–frequency resolution. To address the difficulty of selecting the optimal order for short-time fractional Fourier transform, a new hybrid entropy is proposed to uniformly describe the sharpness of the spectral peaks and the energy concentration in the fractional domain. This hybrid entropy is used as a fitness function, and the optimal order is determined through a limited exhaustive search, resulting in an adaptive short-time fractional Fourier transform (ASTFrFT). To address the issue of overlapping motor current signal spectra under variable speed conditions, a fault feature extraction method suitable for variable speed conditions is proposed. The method first uses warped variational mode decomposition to separate overlapping components in the harmonic order domain, extracting instantaneous sideband harmonic components containing fault information. Then, ASTFrFT is used to track the selected harmonic components and extract fault features. Locomotive and railway line operation experiments show that the proposed method can effectively diagnose traction gear faults.

title: Dynamics and vibration suppression of asymmetric nonlinear energy sinks: Theory and experiment
abstract: The lack of adaptability in the excitation intensity has always been a weakness of the nonlinear energy sink (NES). This paper utilizes asymmetric nonlinear stiffness to address this issue, thereby enhancing the adaptability and suppression performance of the NES under low excitations. The steady-state responses of the coupled system are derived using the alternating frequency/time harmonic balance method, and the stability of the solution branches is evaluated. Through the analysis of the zeroth-order slow invariant manifold, the underlying dynamic mechanisms are elucidated. It is revealed that increasing the asymmetric stiffness coefficient and nonlinear stiffness lowers the first peak of the stable manifold branch, thereby lowering the energy threshold for the strongly modulated response. While strong asymmetry and nonlinear significantly improve suppression performance in the low excitation regime, it induces high-energy detached resonance branches (frequency islands) at higher excitation levels, potentially compromising system stability. In addition, the system exhibits lower parametric sensitivity to stiffness asymmetry compared to nonlinear stiffness, offering a more gradual adjustment method. Finally, a vertical track experimental prototype is constructed to validate the theoretical findings. This research provides an effective vibration reduction strategy under low excitation vibration.

title: Prescriptive design of multifunctional metamaterials: A topology optimization method for simultaneous customization of negative Poisson’s ratio and band gap
abstract: Multifunctional metamaterials, which could synergistically regulate multiple physical fields within a single structure, exhibit outstanding potential in vibration control, energy absorption and intelligent structures. However, achieving precise customization of their performance indices, such as negative Poisson’s ratio and band gap, remains a significant challenge. To address this, we propose a novel topology optimization method for designing tailored multifunctional metamaterials with dual-customized indicators. Based on homogenization theory, the mathematical expression for the negative Poisson’s ratio is derived, and a novel objective function is introduced to achieve precise tailoring. For band gap customization, band gap constraints are employed to realize the customized band gap design, where a normalized KS function is used to achieve more accurate aggregation and reduce numerical errors. An automated CAD reconstruction method is further integrated to convert comceptual designs into editable models. The sensitivities of the objective and constraints are derived within the framework of the variable-density method. Numerical examples demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving predefined dual-customized targets. The aboved method is then applied to tailored multifunctional acoustic devices, including the acoustic demultiplexer, acoustic filter, and acoustic switch, as well as tunable band gap design under deformation, showcasing its extensibility and potential applications in the acoustic field. Experimental validations, including the mechanical and excitation experiments, conform the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method, underscoring its practical value for advanced engineering applications.

title: Finite-time fault-tolerant control for underactuated mechanical systems with unmeasurable states and actuator faults
abstract: This paper investigates the adaptive observer-based finite-time fault-tolerant control (FTC) problem for a class of underactuated mechanical systems subject to actuator faults, unmeasurable states, and unknown nonlinear dynamics. Due to strong nonlinear coupling and actuation deficiency, actuator malfunctions in such systems may lead to significant degradation in tracking accuracy and oscillation suppression performance, which makes reliable dynamic regulation challenging in practical applications. To address this issue, a control-oriented model reformulation is first introduced to convert the original underactuated dynamics into a generalized nonstrict-feedback structure. An adaptive observer is then developed to estimate unmeasurable states and lumped uncertainties. Based on the transformed model, a finite-time fault-tolerant controller is constructed by integrating command-filtered backstepping with a two-layer neural-network approximation mechanism, where one layer is used to approximate unknown nonlinear functions and the other is employed to estimate actuator fault-related effects online. It is shown that all closed-loop signals remain bounded and the tracking errors converge to a small neighborhood of the origin within finite time. Experimental studies on an underactuated tower-crane platform demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively preserve positioning performance and suppress load swing under actuator efficiency loss and locking faults. The results indicate that the developed framework provides an effective fault-tolerant control solution for underactuated mechanical systems operating under fault and uncertainty conditions.

title: Koopman Neural Operator-based surrogate modelling for high-frequency dynamics of high-speed rail pantographs
abstract: Stable sliding contact between the pantograph and catenary is essential for reliable current collection in high-speed rail. As operating speeds increase beyond 350 km/h, the pantograph-catenary system exhibits unprecedented high-frequency dynamic behaviors caused by the excitation of flexible structural modes. Traditional lumped mass pantograph models are unable to represent the structural flexibility, while fully flexible finite element models, though accurate, are computationally constrained for large-scale simulations. To fill this gap, a Koopman Neural Operator-based surrogate modeling framework is proposed to integrate dynamic theory into a data-driven learning scheme, enabling efficient and accurate representation of the high-frequency pantograph dynamics. The surrogate model integrates a deep autoencoder for the observable and inverse-observable functions with a modified Transformer as the evolution operator. Training data are generated from an accurate fully flexible pantograph model, which has been validated via experimental tests, under broadband random excitations. The training process is supervised by a combined loss of multi-step prediction and physical consistency. Inference tests demonstrate that the surrogate model maintains finite element-level accuracy while reducing computational time by three orders of magnitude when predicting 1000-step dynamic responses. Comparative analyses confirm its superior balance between physical interpretability and forecasting performance, highlighting its potential as a powerful tool for real-time simulation, efficient optimization, and comprehensive evaluation of the high-frequency behaviors of a high-speed pantograph-catenary system.

title: A dual-arch compliant mechanism based piezoelectric inertial actuator with configurable driving foot trajectory for cross-scale stepping and scanning
abstract: This study proposed a novel multi-mode piezoelectric inertial actuator with a symmetric dual-arch compliant mechanism where the driving foot trajectory can be modulated by adjusting a single configurable voltage coefficient. In particular, the proposed actuator can achieve three different cross-scale motion modes: 1) high speed stepping mode, 2) smooth tracking mode, as well as 3) surge stepping mode with ultra-fine stepping resolution, which significantly extends the motion capabilities of existing inertial actuators with only a stepping mode. The proposed design was theoretically modeled and analyzed, where the key parameters were optimized. To achieve cross-scale stepping and scanning, a dual-mode closed-loop control scheme was proposed, where the driving foot trajectory is regulated via a coordinate transformation method, and a phase integration control strategy is combined with the optimization of $\eta$ to effectively suppress backward motion, thereby significantly enhancing long-range tracking accuracy. Experimental results demonstrated motion linearity with correlation coefficient of $R^{2} = 0.9999$ and bidirectional consistency of \qty{97.04}{\percent}. By optimizing the configurable coefficient, the RMS error in long-range tracking is reduced by \qty{73.7}{\percent}, achieving a theoretical resolution of \qty{0.284}{nm}, thereby ensuring high tracking performance. The actuator developed in this work extended the motion capability of piezoelectric inertial actuators by achieving cross-scale smooth tracking, besides the stepping mode of standard inertial actuators, therefore offering significant potentials in various applications such as semiconductor manufacturing and high precision measurement.

title: Inverse spectral Chebyshev and compressed sensing framework for full-field reconstruction in computational mechanics
abstract: This paper presents an inverse spectral Chebyshev (ISC) operator framework and its compressed-sensing extension (ISC-CS) for full-field reconstruction of structural responses from sparse and noisy measurement data. The ISC formulation is developed as a deterministic variational/least-squares inverse technique in which the equations governing the unknown structural fields are discretized based on spectral Chebyshev (SC) method with boundary conditions, strain–displacement relations, and equilibrium constraints enforced through the associated spectral operators. When the available measurements are far fewer than the unknown degrees-of-freedom (DOFs), the framework is extended to ISC-CS by exploiting the intrinsic sparsity/compressibility of mechanical fields in the Chebyshev coefficient space. The Chebyshev representation is particularly suitable for bounded non-periodic structural domains because it provides endpoint-compatible interpolation, rapid coefficient decay for smooth fields, and direct construction of differentiation, integration, and inner-product operators. The sparse inverse problem is solved using an equilibrium-informed iterative hard-thresholding algorithm with adaptive step-size control and momentum acceleration, tailored to the matrix-operator structure of the SC method. This enables robust reconstruction without requiring prior knowledge of the external loads. A theory-guided sparsity selection strategy based on Bernstein-type analyticity arguments is introduced, linking spectral coefficient decay to measurement noise levels and providing conservative, physics-informed sparsity bounds. Dedicated numerical studies using a forward SC method substantiate these theoretical insights by quantifying effective sparsity levels for displacement, curvature, and shear strain fields, demonstrating their suitability for compressed-sensing-based reconstruction despite the presence of spatial derivatives. Building on these findings, the proposed framework is validated through numerical case studies involving a Timoshenko beam and a Mindlin plate under both two-sided and single-sided strain-based sensing configurations. In the two-sided plate case, a purely kinematic ISC reconstruction is achieved, whereas the single-sided configuration, which is known to be ill-conditioned in classical inverse finite element formulations, is stabilized by enforcing equilibrium constraints. Across all cases, accurate recovery of displacement, rotation, curvature, and shear strain fields is demonstrated using significantly fewer sensors than DOFs, with low reconstruction errors even in the presence of additive Gaussian noise. The results highlight the robustness, noise tolerance, and scalability of the proposed ISC/ISC-CS framework, establishing it as a promising alternative to conventional inverse finite element approaches for shape sensing and structural health monitoring applications.

title: Study on multi-physical field coupling experiment under high-density current condition and a wear model considering dynamic interactions of pantograph-rigid catenary system
abstract: The contact pair wear issues of the pantograph-catenary system (PCS) exhibit complex nonlinear behavior under multi-physics coupling condition, which directly impacts system operational stability and maintenance costs. Traditional wear prediction models suffer from inadequate adaptability to different pantograph types and difficulty in accurately capturing the effects of multi-parameter coupling. Therefore, a systematic study is urgently needed to reveal the wear evolution laws and enhance wear prediction accuracy. Firstly, this study proposes a strain-based testing method for friction coefficients (μ) using a beam model, where the tangential force during PCS sliding wear was measured, and the friction coefficient was calculated based on Coulomb’s law of friction. Simultaneously, the first-ever multi-physics coupling wear tests on an actual pantograph under high current loading was conducted. Additionally, the contact strip wear prediction model has been refined by introducing equivalent damping terms that incorporate dynamic interaction parameters. The results indicate that the μ of the contact pair under high current conditions is approximately 0.3, decreasing with increasing sliding speed. Attributed to the high-temperature adhesion effect, μ, increasing with rising current. The Rc stabilizes between 40 and 50 mΩ. The Fstd and Accave decrease with increased speed and increase with higher current. The joule energy rises from 4.05 × 104 J to 4.50 × 104 J with speed, and jumps to 7.14 × 104 J at 1400 A. The wear rate results from the competitive balance between mechanical and electrical wear. The dynamic performance regulates mechanical wear through contact stability, while electrical contact performance is dominated by the arcing effect and Joule heating, primarily due to the significant contributions of the arc and current. The refined wear prediction model exhibits significantly improved accuracy, effectively capturing the impact of structural parameter changes on wear performance and overcoming the adaptability shortcomings of traditional models, thereby enabling precise wear predictions for different types of pantographs. This research provides a reliable theoretical foundation for the performance evaluation and wear prediction of systems under multi-physics coupling.

title: Collaborative denoising of multi-point vibration signals using a physics-guided graph neural network
abstract: The acquisition of clean vibration signals is a fundamental prerequisite for structural health monitoring. With the development of distributed monitoring technologies, a key challenge for traditional single-point denoising methods is how to denoise signals from densely distributed measurement points while simultaneously preserving data quality and enforcing physical constraints. To address this issue, this study proposes a physics-guided graph neural network framework for collaborative denoising of multi-point vibration signals. The framework constructs a physics-embedded adjacency matrix to define node connections and introduces a physics-guided loss function with partial differential equation constraints, together with a boundary compensation mechanism, so that the denoised results not only conform to the statistical characteristics of the data but also satisfy mechanical laws. Experimental results from multiple test cases show that, compared with existing denoising methods, the proposed model achieves superior performance across all evaluation metrics and preserves the consistency of physical field characteristics more effectively. This study provides a new approach for vibration noise suppression in structural health monitoring.

title: A probability integration filtering method for response PDFs of uncertain structures subjected to random loads
abstract: This paper proposes a probability integration filtering method (PIFM) to determine response probability density functions (PDFs) of structures with uncertain parameters and random loads. Firstly, the discretized probability integration equations (DPIEs), derived from the principle of probability conservation, are transformed into the first-order linear differential equations (FLDEs) of cumulative distribution functions with noises. The transformed FLDEs avoid calculating the Dirac delta function and sub-domain probability. And then, the state space models that fully reflect the probability conservation and data information of system are derived from the FLDEs. The PIFM of response PDFs is established based on the state space models and Kalman filtering technique. After that, a general implementation procedure is presented according to the proposed PIFM. Finally, five representative examples are investigated to test the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed PIFM has both high calculation efficiency and accuracy, because it does not involve the difference solution, the approximate alternative operation of the Dirac delta function, and the large sample statistics for the sub-domain probability estimation. That means the proposed method can efficiently and accurately provide full response probability information for parameter evaluation and reliability analysis of actual structures.

title: A mechanism-driven severity-aware prototype-guided cross-domain quantitative diagnosis method for pitting damage of helical gears
abstract: To address the limitations associated with insufficient damage samples and the high feature similarity among different severities in the quantitative diagnosis of helical gear pitting faults, a mechanism-driven severity-aware cross-domain diagnostic framework is proposed. The framework is centered on the generation of pitting fault data with consistent severities through dynamic simulation, while a linearly modulated Gaussian mixture model is employed to mitigate the statistical distribution discrepancy between simulated and measured signals. On this basis, a severity-aware cross-domain diagnostic network is developed. Specifically, a multi-scale feature fusion and adaptive enhancement mechanism is introduced to improve feature representation capability, and a structured prototype dual-branch classifier is designed to explicitly characterize the geometric ordinal relationships among different pitting severities. Furthermore, structure-preserving and prototype-separation loss functions are jointly utilized to enhance feature discriminability, while conditional domain adversarial learning is adopted to suppress feature confusion during cross-domain alignment. Experimental results obtained from nine transfer tasks demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an average diagnostic accuracy of 86%, outperforming mainstream methods by up to 25%. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective solution for the quantitative diagnosis of rotating machinery faults.

title: Theoretical and experimental investigation of the dynamic deployment of Jessen’s icosahedron tensegrity structure
abstract: This work investigates the dynamic deployment of Jessen’s icosahedron tensegrity structure through nonlinear flexible-beam modeling and high-speed 3D-DIC experiments. A dynamic deployment model based on gradient-deficient ANCF beam elements is developed, in which rods and cables are retained as deformable members to capture member flexibility during large deployment motion. A 3D-printed specimen is tested to validate the model. Compared with a conventional truss model, the proposed model better reproduces the measured deployment path, overshoot, decay trend, and cable motion. The results reveal a two-stage deployment process: an initial deployment stage and an overall deployment stage, comprising rapid upper-rod unfolding with slack-taut cable re-tensioning, followed by global height adjustment and damped residual oscillations. Further numerical analyses show that the initial self-stress acts as the main internal constraint mechanism, governing modal frequency evolution, slack–taut-induced cable vibration, and residual rod-cable coupling. In contrast, the folding ratio has only a limited influence on deployment time within the investigated range.

title: Structured low-rank enhanced inverse-free Bayesian estimation for high-precision blade tip timing measurement
abstract: Rotating blades are critical but fragile moving parts in turbomachinery. Therefore, it is of great significance to monitor rotating blades in service. Blade tip timing (BTT) is an effective non-contact measurement technique for achieving online monitoring of blades owing to its high efficiency and long service life. However, due to limitations in the number of sensors and the passive sampling property, the BTT signals are inherently undersampled. Inverse-free sparse Bayesian learning (IFSBL) is a low-complexity sparse reconstruction algorithm by bounding the original posterior distribution, while it often converges to a suboptimal solution with spurious spectral components owing to the neglect of correlation atoms. Meanwhile, it also suffers from basis mismatch caused by frequency discretization and inevitably results in reconstruction errors. To address these limitations, we develop a structured low-rank enhanced inverse-free Bayesian estimation (SLR-IFBE) method for BTT signal analysis. Instead of fully diagonalizing the original posterior covariance matrix as in IFSBL, the proposed method recovers the dominant coupling structure followed by an adaptive low-rank subspace selection strategy, thereby suppressing spurious components under strong ambient noise interference while retaining a relatively low computational complexity. Then, to mitigate the errors between the coarse estimates and the target frequencies, a local grid calibration technique based on Brent’s one-dimensional search is further developed. Owing to its derivative-free nature, super-linear convergence, and reliable numerical behavior, the proposed grid calibration technique enables efficient correction of the off-grid errors. Both numerical and experimental validations demonstrate the superiority of SLR-IFBE, and the overall algorithm achieves a two-order-of-magnitude speedup compared with the existing methods. This trade-off between estimation accuracy and the computational cost of SLR-IFBE establishes itself as an efficient and practical algorithm in real BTT applications.

title: Noncontact quantification of bolt prestress degradation via full-field laser scanning imaging and second-order perturbation-based stepwise vibro-acoustic modulation
abstract: Under high prestress tightening, bolted interfaces exhibit elastic–plastic contact behaviors, which alter the mechanism of nonlinear harmonic generation compared to low-prestress conditions. Conventional vibro-acoustic modulation (VAM) methods, which rely on the first-order nonlinearity, typically struggle to distinguish these changes, leading to potential misjudgments in accurately evaluating prestress degradation. Additionally, sensor-based measurements introduce extrinsic contact nonlinearities, further compounding uncertainties on vibro-acoustically modulated waves. To address these challenges, we develop a new characterization framework for bolt prestress degradation in a quantitative and noncontact manner, referred to as stepwise vibro-acoustic modulation (SVAM). This method uses stepwise-enhanced pumping excitation in conjunction with full-field laser scanning imaging. Theoretically, the framework is extended to the second-order nonlinearity, which novelly considers the cascade modulation of higher-order nonlinearities on the linear wave counterparts. The spectral features of stepwise-modulated waves demonstrate a strong correlation with the underlying nonlinear acoustic mechanisms, thereby offering enhanced sensitivity and detectability to prestress degradation even at its early stage. Based on these spectral features, two modulation indices, using single-point sampling and full-field scanning, respectively, are proposed for prestress quantification. Experimental results demonstrate that both indices enable monotonic noncontact quantification of prestress across both the elastic and elastic–plastic fastening stages, extending the detectable range to 85% of the bolt yield strength (33% improvement over the conventional VAM method).

title: Nonlinear dynamic instability of railway coupler systems: modeling, parameter identification, and safety assessment
abstract: In railway engineering, the instability behavior of couplers under combined compression and bending influences the collision dynamics response of trains, yet the dynamic interaction mechanism between impact velocity and deflection angle remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigates this coupled instability mechanism comprehensively by integrating full scale impact testing, refined finite element simulation, theoretical modeling, and train system dynamics. The results demonstrate that an increase in impact velocity elevates the axial force demand on the expansion collapse tube through the strain rate hardening effect of the material, whereas an increasing deflection angle degrades the available compressive bending load bearing capacity of the drawbar by introducing an eccentric bending moment. When the platform force elevated by velocity exceeds the critical buckling load reduced by the deflection angle before the expansion collapse tube completes its designated crushing stroke, the coupler response transitions from stable crushing to premature drawbar buckling, thereby triggering the valley effect. On this basis, the present study establishes a theoretical framework that integrates a buffer model dependent on velocity, a platform force model sensitive to strain rate, and a dynamic compressive bending interaction buckling criterion. Following rigorous validation, this theoretical model is embedded into the train system dynamics analysis to achieve a bidirectional coupling between local instability and global collision response. The analytical results further reveal that the coupler instability process comprises three sequential phases consisting of buffer compression, expansion collapse tube crushing, and drawbar buckling. The proposed theoretical model restricts the prediction errors for the platform force, critical buckling force, and equivalent bending stiffness to within 15%, 15.2%, and 13.2% respectively, while faithfully reproducing the valley effect. The train system analysis further discloses that under medium and high speed collision scenarios, the transient load redistribution induced by coupler instability significantly intensifies the transient wheelset lift and amplifies the derailment risk. This study provides a solid theoretical foundation for coupler modeling considering instability characteristics and train crashworthiness safety assessment.

title: A multichannel feature-interaction image-based method for interactive fault diagnosis
abstract: Electrical control systems are widely used in industrial applications, and faults may seriously affect their safe and stable operation. Therefore, fault diagnosis is essential for system condition monitoring and health assessment. Interactive faults involve two or more faults that occur together and influence each other. They are a common and complex fault type in electrical control systems. Existing methods usually rely on raw signals or single-feature modeling. They cannot fully describe the correlation and time-delay features in interactive faults. This limits the effective separation of different fault patterns. To address this issue, a feature-interaction image construction method is proposed for interactive fault diagnosis in electrical control systems. It jointly encodes inter-variable correlations, time-delay relations, and amplitude variation information to transform raw time-series signals into more discriminative images. On this basis, a fault diagnosis model is developed by combining Res2Net and ESCA. This improves the extraction and identification of complex interactive fault features. A subsea blowout preventer (BOP) electrical control system is used to evaluate the performance of the method. The results show that the separability of interactive fault features is improved. Besides, the local confusion between classes is reduced.

title: Frequency veering in spatial fluid-conveying pipe systems: unified ANCF modeling and experimental validation
abstract: Clamps are key local constraint components that affect the modal characteristics of spatial fluid-conveying pipe systems. However, a unified representation of clamp constraints within the absolute nodal coordinate formulation (ANCF) remains insufficiently developed. The mechanisms of clamp-mediated coupled vibration and frequency veering also require further clarification. A dynamic model for multi-clamp spatial fluid-conveying pipe systems is established within a three-dimensional ANCF framework. By expressing local translational and rotational clamp deformations in terms of ANCF generalized-coordinate increments, parameterized equivalent single-clamp and double-clamp models are derived based on the principle of virtual work. The proposed model is validated against modal experiments and a finite element model. Clamp-position and directional-stiffness sensitivities are analyzed to identify critical clamps. The clamp-mediated frequency-veering behavior is further investigated through mode exchange and modal strain-energy redistribution. The results indicate that single clamps mainly induce local frequency modulation, whereas double clamps more readily alter inter-pipe coupling by constraining the relative displacement and rotation between adjacent pipes. Frequency veering is accompanied by mode exchange, reconstruction of dominant vibration regions, and redistribution of strain energy among pipes. Additional clamp-adjustment experiments are conducted to further verify the predicted frequency-variation trends. The proposed framework provides guidance for support-layout optimization and vibration control of complex spatial pipe systems.

title: Integrative approach to predict the vibration reduction characteristics of viscoelastic polymeric patches wrapping around vibrating pipelines
abstract: Vibration mitigation in the pipelines is critical in maintaining their functionality and integrity. Although viscoelastic polymer-based damping is a mainstream method for piping vibration suppression, much still remains unclear due to the complex response of viscoelastic polymers influenced by multiple mechanophysical players. In this study, a prediction model is developed by incorporating a modified fractional derivative standard linear solid (FDSLS) model into the harmonic base excitation of a damped single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) system, which enables an accurate estimation about the vibration reduction characteristics of viscoelastic polymeric patches without extensive experimentation. The modified FDSLS model is derived by combining an intact FDSLS model with a beam-column analysis, a one-phase exponential growth function, and a Williams-Landel-Ferry (WLF) model-based shift equation, thus being able to depict the effective dynamic modulus of viscoelastic polymeric patches. The accuracy of the proposed model is evaluated through a set of vibration tests, focused on the effects of thickness, central angle, shape factor, and compressive prestrain on the cut-off frequency of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), polysulfide rubber (PSR), and silicone rubber (SR) patches. The model’s validity is further substantiated through finite element vibration analysis using either the static (or constant) modulus or the effective dynamic modulus derived from the modified FDSLS model. Furthermore, the applicability of our predictive framework is substantiated by experimental validation employing a commercial compressor. The findings will provide a generalizable basis for designing and optimizing viscoelastic polymeric patches across different materials.

title: Corrigendum to “Broad-range continuous load adaptability with electromagnetic constant-force compensated stair-step quasi-zero-stiffness vibration isolators” [Mech. Syst. Signal Process. 258 (2026) 114647]
Robust feature selection for cross-domain fault diagnosis using deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Recent research on deep learning-based fault diagnosis has made significant progress. However, over-parameterized models often introduce redundant features, leading to degraded cross-domain generalization and limited deployability on resource-constrained devices. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reinforcement-learning-based robust feature selection (RFS) framework for cross-domain fault diagnosis. Unlike existing methods that treat network pruning and domain adaptation as separate processes, the proposed approach integrates them at the decision level via a domain-aware reward formulation. Specifically, channel pruning is formulated as a sequential decision-making problem, where a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent learns an adaptive pruning policy. Meanwhile, domain alignment loss is incorporated into the reward function, enabling the pruning policy to directly optimize cross-domain feature robustness during the decision-making process rather than through post-hoc feature alignment. This mechanism promotes the retention of features that are both discriminative and transferable, while eliminating redundant or domain-specific components. This framework offers a principled approach for jointly optimizing model compactness and cross-domain generalization, rather than treating them as independent objectives. Extensive experiments on two gearbox datasets under various domain shift scenarios demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves cross-domain diagnostic performance while reducing model complexity. In particular, the method achieves up to 19.59 % improvement in target-domain accuracy and reduces computational cost by up to 73.87 % in FLOPs, with reduced inference latency. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in jointly achieving robust cross-domain generalization and efficient model deployment in practical industrial scenarios.

title: Continuously morphing rotor eccentricity compensator for active magnetic bearings
abstract: High-speed rotors supported by Active Magnetic Bearings (AMBs) must traverse system resonance frequencies during run-up and coast-down. Unbalance-induced synchronous vibration can then cause excessive displacement, amplifier current saturation, and even instability. Existing approaches such as Peak-of-Gain Control (PGC) and Automatic Balancing System (ABS) are effective only over limited speed ranges and often rely on mode switching, which may introduce discontinuities and chatter. This paper proposes a Continuously Morphing Rotor Eccentricity Compensator (CMREC) based on a tracking-filter structure whose behavior is continuously morphed by a single parameter k: PGC-like action for low-speed centering (k < 0), ABS-like action for high-speed inertial-axis rotation (k > 0), and a neutral buffer (k = 0) enabling near-bumpless transitions. The compensator can be integrated with existing PID loops without explicit mode switching. The closed-loop stability and frequency-domain (pole and sensitivity) characteristics are analyzed to support the design. Steady-state and 0–6000 rpm transient experiments, quantified using boxplots and P95/MAE/RMSE metrics, demonstrate improved displacement suppression and an enlarged stable operating envelope via an RPM–k scheduling table, while the per-axis control current remains within the ±0.8 A amplifier limit across the full speed range. Additional aggravated-eccentricity experiments further show that fixed PGC-like, ABS-like, and neutral configurations suffer from narrowed stable speed ranges, current saturation, or displacement divergence as rotor unbalance increases. In contrast, the scheduled CMREC maintains stable levitation over the entire 0–6000 rpm range without amplifier-current saturation, confirming its superior robustness against rotor eccentricity variations.

title: A physics-based model for individual bouncing load incorporating dynamic and kinematic characteristics of human body
abstract: In this study, a physics-based model for individual bouncing loads that integrates both the dynamic and kinematic characteristics of the human body is proposed. First, a single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) dynamic model was employed to reconstruct the ground reaction force (GRF), as GRF was found to be strongly correlated with body acceleration. Second, the kinematic relationship between the vertical displacement of the center of mass (CoM) and both geometric parameters (i.e., height) and postural configurations was established using a planetary two-segment lower limb model. Third, a comprehensive experimental campaign was conducted with 24 participants performing bouncing movements from 1.5 Hz to 3.5 Hz at 0.2 Hz intervals, while body-motion tracking and GRF were recorded simultaneously. The collected bouncing data were subsequently used to identify parameters of the physics-based model. Finally, the physics-based model was developed by integrating the dynamic and kinematic models, and was validated from both dynamic and kinematic perspectives. The proposed model shows potential advantages over traditional force models by coupling an SDOF representation of GRF with a planetary two-segment kinematic description of the lower limb. By accounting for body stiffness, damping, a frequency-dependent effective-mass participation ratio and height, it supports low-dimensional, analytical reconstruction of GRF from simple anthropometrics and posture and provides a practical interface for coupled human–structure interaction simulations; it may also facilitate non-contact, large-scale structural vibration assessment using computer vision.

title: Flexural wave trapping and vibration suppression of annular ABH metasurfaces with radial periodicity
abstract: An annular acoustic black hole (ABH) metasurface with radial periodicity is proposed for broadband flexural-wave attenuation in plate structures. By combining the ABH tapering unit cells with the radius-dependent geometric modulation induced by radial expansion, the proposed metasurface introduces the wave-trapping mechanism, thereby enhancing bandgap formation and vibration suppression performance. The spectral element method (SEM) under the approximate radial translational-periodicity assumption is adopted to investigate complex band structures and dynamic transmission characteristics of the proposed ABH metasurface. The numerical predictions are validated through comparisons with the plane wave expansion (PWE) method, extended plane wave expansion (EPWE) method, and 2D/3D finite element simulations.
