However, PINN usually employs multilayer perceptrons with fixed activation functions, resulting in limited model interpretability and flexibility, which constrains its performance in complex acoustic environments. Therefore, this study proposes a sound field estimation method based on a physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold network (PIKAN). PIKAN constructs its edge activation functions as a linear combination of radial basis functions (RBFs) and adaptively learns the RBF coefficients during training, thereby substantially enhancing the interpretability and expressive capability. The proposed method is evaluated on sound field interpolation and extrapolation tasks across small and large meeting rooms at multiple frequencies, and benchmarked against plane wave expansion (PWE) and PINN. Analysis of the learned edge activation functions reveals that they spontaneously exhibit sinusoidal-like oscillatory characteristics. For interpolation, PIKAN demonstrates clear advantages over PINN and PWE under sparse training conditions at mid-to-high frequencies. For extrapolation, PWE retains a competitive advantage. Furthermore, to improve the performance under high reverberation, a transfer learning strategy is introduced, fine-tuning parameters pre-trained under moderate reverberation. Overall, this study demonstrates PIKAN as a promising alternative for sound field estimation, with results highlighting its potential for practical acoustic modeling.

title: Vibration suppression of supercritical transmission shafts via active limiting ring
abstract: This study addresses the dual challenges of transcritical and self-excited vibrations in helicopter supercritical tail drive shafts by proposing and validating a novel piezoelectric-actuated limiting ring. A comprehensive dynamic model of the supercritical shaft system, incorporating a floating spline coupling and a limiting ring, is established. This high-fidelity model characterizes the stiffness and friction torque of the spline, along with the rub-impact and stick–slip dry friction characteristics of the limiting ring components. Numerical calculations based on this model reveal that while passive limiting rings effectively suppress transcritical vibrations, they inherently face a contradiction: reducing clearance to suppress self-excited vibrations significantly intensifies impact during transcritical passage, widening the critical region and compromising safe operation. To overcome this limitation, the core innovation lies in an active adjustment strategy for the limiting ring’s preload force, leveraging piezoelectric actuation. This strategy dynamically applies a smaller preload during critical speed passage to minimize impact and rapidly traverse the critical region, then adjusts to a larger preload in the stable operating regime to efficiently suppress self-excited vibrations. Both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations demonstrate the significant potential of this active limiting ring in simultaneously achieving safe transcritical passage and effective self-excited vibration suppression. Finally, experimental validation using a specially designed supercritical shafting test rig confirms the accuracy of the established dynamic model. Crucially, the experiments validate the engineering feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed piezoelectric-actuated limiting ring, offering a promising, novel solution for advanced vibration control in helicopter tail drive shaft systems.

title: A differentiable physics-embedded framework for thermally informed Neural-UniTire modeling and identification
abstract: To address the need for thermally informed tire modeling for handling-oriented force prediction under limited thermal sensing, this paper presents a differentiable physics-embedded sequential framework for thermally informed Neural-UniTire modeling and identification. First, a differentiable radial thermal model is developed from a continuous radial thermal formulation through finite-volume Crank–Nicolson discretization, with hybrid global, physics-parameterized, and neural thermal coefficients used to reconstruct radial multilayer thermal states from sparse boundary measurements. Then, a Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model is developed by embedding neural networks into the UniTire framework and extending it to unsteady conditions through a second-order hysteresis element. Finally, a thermally informed correction mechanism is introduced for the Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model, in which reconstructed radial multilayer thermal states with operating-condition information are used to generate neural thermo-correction factors for stiffness- and friction-related parameters. Experiments on an MTS flat-track test rig with a passenger-car tire and a semi-slick tire under pure lateral-slip and longitudinal-slip conditions show good agreement with the measured temperature and force responses. The radial thermal model achieves accurate temperature estimation from sparse boundary measurements. The unsteady Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model improves force prediction over the steady-state formulation, especially in the nonlinear slip region and phase lag. The thermally informed model improves force prediction over the baseline and sparse-input ablation models under pulse-excitation conditions, while the learned thermal correction remains physically interpretable.

title: SFDM: Structural full-field dynamic displacement monitoring utilizing computer vision-enhanced targetless monitoring system
abstract: Full-field dynamic displacement monitoring with high spatial resolution provides a more comprehensive representation of the dynamic characteristics of bridge structures, thereby significantly enhancing the effectiveness of bridge structural health monitoring (BSHM). In this study, a structural full-field dynamic displacement monitoring (SFDM) method is proposed to overcome the limitations of traditional discrete-point measurement techniques. To achieve targetless and accurate extraction of the lower edge of bridge structures, an effective computer vision framework is developed by integrating a robust fusion image processing (RFIP) strategy with a row-wise adaptive edge detection (RAED) approach. Additionally, a multi-target displacement transformation model (MDTM) is proposed to convert subpixel-level image displacements into physical displacements. A tied-arch bridge field test was conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The experimental results indicate that the proposed SFDM achieved correlation coefficients higher than 0.964, while the corresponding RMSE and NRMSE remained below 0.282 mm and 9.178% across all test cases, respectively, thereby confirming its accuracy and effectiveness for full-field displacement monitoring in BSHM applications.

title: An adaptive recursive stochastic subspace identification method for time-varying structural systems subject to non-Gaussian impulsive excitation
abstract: The excitation of structural systems in practical engineering may be contaminated by non-Gaussian impulsive noise, which in turn introduces outliers into the measured response signals and consequently leads to distorted results in output-only modal parameter identification. To overcome this issue, a novel adaptive recursive stochastic subspace identification (ARSSI) method for time-varying structural systems subject to non-Gaussian impulsive excitation is proposed in this paper. The proposed ARSSI method introduces an adaptive weighting strategy to automatically adjust the influence of new data observations on the update of the signal subspace based on residual information at each time instant, thereby mitigate the interference of impulsive noise on the output-only modal parameter identification results. The detailed theoretical derivation of the proposed ARSSI method and its identification process are first presented. Thereafter, numerical and experimental verifications are respectively carried out to validate the feasibility and robustness of the method based on different structural systems subject to non-Gaussian impulsive excitation. The validation results demonstrate that the proposed ARSSI method is capable of applying adaptive weighting to the measured response signals to reduce the interference of randomly occurring outliers caused by impulsive noise, and accurately track modal parameters of time-varying structural systems when conventional methods fail in such case, which provides an effective solution for output-only modal parameter identification of time-varying structural systems in complex noise environments.

title: Experimental–numerical validation of a contact-interface-induced squeal model under uncertainty
abstract: Understanding the mechanisms that trigger braking instabilities is essential for more reliable brake-noise simulations, but remains challenging despite previous experimental and numerical studies. This study investigates brake squeal through the development of an experimental–numerical model that reproduces several experimentally observed instabilities and incorporates an enhanced description of the contact interface with uncertain parameters. Using complex eigenvalue analysis and surrogate models, the key parameters triggering each instability mode are identified, enabling efficient exploration of the parameter space. The methodology also makes it possible to assess contact localization as a driver of instability via virtual braking tests. The results show that contact conditions strongly influence the onset of dynamic instabilities. By connecting experimental observations with numerical modeling through surrogate modeling, this approach provides deeper insight into the mechanisms governing brake squeal and emphasizes the importance of an enriched contact-interface description for predictive modeling.

title: End-to-End predictive modeling of excavator hydraulic systems
abstract: Accurate prediction of the dynamic response of excavator hydraulic systems is a key prerequisite for model-based control applications. However, existing studies have not established a direct mapping from cylinder outputs to joystick signals. To address this issue, this study proposes an end-to-end predictive model that integrates a joystick-signal baseline with data-driven modeling. Specifically, the joystick-signal baseline is jointly determined by the mechanism-based relationship between cylinder motion and hydraulic flow and the predefined electro-hydraulic control mappings, providing an initial prediction reference for the model. Subsequently, a two-stage long short-term memory (LSTM) network is introduced for data-driven modeling. In the first stage, sensitivity-based weighting dynamically adjusts the weights of the input variables to capture the dynamic nonlinear characteristics of the system. In the second stage, the weighted input features from the first stage are combined with the joystick-signal baseline to form a new input sequence, which is then modeled using a multilayer LSTM. In addition, a delay-aware structure is designed to account for the non-fixed delays between joystick signals and cylinder states. Experimental results show that the prediction errors remain within 10 % under in-distribution validation, while R2 values above 0.88 are achieved on an independently collected gravel excavation dataset from another excavator of the same model, demonstrating good prediction performance and generalization capability. The proposed architecture requires only 4 MB of storage and achieves an inference time of less than 2 ms per prediction, indicating strong potential for real-time applications.

title: Binary phase-coded 3D chiral metamaterials with re-entrant ligaments: Programmable auxeticity, torsion, and energy absorption
abstract: This study proposes a binary connection-phase coding strategy for tailoring the mechanical response of three-dimensional re-entrant–chiral metamaterials. Two unit cells with identical global dimensions but different circumferential connection orientations are defined as a coaxial-phase state coded as 0 and an orthogonal-phase state coded as 1. Seven representative 3 × 3 × 3 configurations were fabricated from 316 L stainless steel by selective laser melting and investigated through quasi-static compression tests and finite element simulations validated against the experiments under two orthogonal loading directions. The two discrete connection-phase states share a common geometric framework, and their spatial arrangements are used to tailor collapse, apparent Poisson’s ratio, layer-wise torsion, and energy absorption. The 0-coded unit cell exhibits a long stable stress plateau and densifies at a nominal strain of approximately 0.75, whereas the 1-coded unit cell shows a higher initial stress peak, a descending plateau, and earlier densification at approximately 0.65. At the multicell scale, the all-0 configuration undergoes smoother progressive collapse, while the all-1 configuration exhibits larger stress fluctuations and more pronounced layer-wise torsion. The hybrid configurations further show that similar phase fractions do not necessarily produce similar densification and energy-absorption responses. Among the seven investigated configurations, Model E provides the highest usable SEA under Y-direction compression, Model B provides the highest usable SEA under X-direction compression, and Model G maintains effective crushing to a strain of approximately 0.64 under X-direction compression. These results demonstrate the feasibility of tailoring multiple mechanical responses through binary connection-phase coding within the sampled configuration set without changing the basic unit-cell dimensions.

title: Free interface blade mistuning model: Experimental validation with measured blade variability and contact conditions
abstract: Accurate modeling of mistuning in bladed disks requires a consistent representation of blade-to-blade variability and its impact on the assembled system dynamics. This work presents an experimental validation of a reduced-order modeling approach for mistuned bladed disks, where the variability of individual components is directly derived from measurements. Free–free modal hammer tests are performed on individual blades to quantify the dispersion in natural frequencies arising from manufacturing tolerances and geometric variability. These experimentally measured perturbations are introduced into the reduced-order formulation of the blade component, enabling a physically consistent representation of intrinsic mistuning. The finite element model of the disk is updated based on experimental data, and the full assembly is modeled using a component mode synthesis framework, combining Rubin reduction for the blades and Craig–Bampton reduction for the disk. The assembled bladed disk is experimentally characterized through modal testing, and the numerical predictions are compared against the measured natural frequencies and mode shapes. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately captures the effect of blade variability on the global dynamic behavior. The study highlights the effectiveness of incorporating experimentally derived blade properties into reduced-order model, providing a robust and physically interpretable framework for the analysis of mistuned bladed disks.

title: High-Order Fourier-Basis LSTM-PINN for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction in whole-angle vibratory gyroscopes
abstract: The bias of a whole-angle vibratory gyroscope is not a stationary offset but an angle-dependent waveform shaped by structural errors, circuit-induced control and detection errors, and thermally driven operating variations, whose coupled effects are represented in the present observation model by effective Fourier bias components rather than separated into source-specific parameters. Existing bias models usually rely on low-order angular harmonics, especially the 2θ and 4θ components, which limits their ability to represent high-order angle-dependent bias structures. This study proposes a High-Order Fourier-Basis Long Short-Term Memory Physics-Informed Neural Network (LSTM-PINN) framework for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction and harmonic component characterization. High-order potential and Rayleigh dissipation functionals are retained up to the eighth order, from which a 2/4/6/8 even-order Fourier harmonic basis is derived. This Lagrangian-derived harmonic structure defines the Fourier-basis analytical decoder of the LSTM-PINN solver. Instead of treating the angle-dependent bias waveform as an unconstrained regression target, the solver infers the scale-factor term and Fourier bias components from historical sequences of the amplitude-control envelope, quadrature-control envelope, and resonant frequency, and reconstructs the angle-dependent bias waveform through the Lagrangian-derived analytical decoder. Experiments on 16-electrode micro-shell gyroscopes show stable reconstruction, with a mean RMSE of 6.62×10−4 deg/s and a mean R2 of 0.9886. Architecture ablations show that both the PINN and the LSTM are necessary: relative to the black-box LSTM baseline and the MLP-PINN baseline, the full LSTM-PINN reduces the 1 Hz mean RMSE by 90.5% and 59.2%, respectively. Expanding the physically admissible basis from 2θ/4θ to 2θ/4θ/6θ/8θ reduces the across-label mean RMSE by 32.0%, while repeated-segment tests show quasi-stationary inferred high-order components. Over a seven-day evaluation horizon at ±1 and ±8deg/s, the Day-7 across-rate mean RMSE and R2 were 9.765×10−4deg/s and 0.9857, respectively. Within the validated micro-shell device and laboratory operating range, these results support the proposed framework as a device-physics-constrained temporal method for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction.

title: Robust concurrent input shaping and LQR control for underactuated overhead cranes under uncertainty
abstract: Overhead cranes experience significant payload sway during aggressive maneuvers. To mitigate this without requiring a full nonlinear framework, the proposed controller is synthesized on a linearized nominal model and is evaluated under bounded parametric uncertainties to enhance robustness while ensuring safe and efficient operation. Standalone input shaping lacks robustness to modeling errors, whereas conventional linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control does not account for the delay introduced by input shaping. To address these limitations, the proposed concurrent framework integrates Zero-Vibration (ZV) and Zero-Vibration-Derivative (ZVD) input shapers with a robust LQR controller in a unified co-design framework. A minimax optimization strategy is employed to optimize the worst-case performance over the prescribed ±10% uncertainty range of the parameters, while Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) tunes the elements of the LQR weighting matrix to minimize the settling time within a 2% tolerance band. Simulations and experiments testbed evaluate the proposed method against seven benchmark controllers. Among the investigated configurations, the Robust-PSO-LQR-ZVD controller achieves the best overall performance, with a simulated settling time of 4.07 s, a peak in-motion sway angle of 2.59°, representing a 66% reduction compared with the baseline LQR controller, and zero residual sway. Experimental results demonstrate a settling time of 4.13 s, a residual sway angle of 0.5°, an 81% reduction in peak in-motion sway, and actuator voltages remaining within the ±10 V limit. These results demonstrate that the proposed concurrent framework improves robustness and vibration suppression while achieving faster settling and near-zero residual oscillation within the prescribed uncertainty range.

title: Evidence-causality dual adversarial framework for fault diagnosis in dynamic open environments
abstract: The practical implementation of deep learning models for real-time mechanical fault diagnosis in open environments remains challenging, primarily due to data acquisition difficulties, dynamic industrial fluctuations, and the emergence of novel failure modes in real-world applications. Conventional open-set domain generalization (OSDG) methods often fail to generalize to such scenarios, as they typically necessitate extensive offline training data spanning multiple source domains. To address these limitations, an evidence-causality dual adversarial framework for single-source OSDG is proposed, enabling online fault diagnosis in dynamic open conditions under limited data. Specifically, a sample weight-aware evidential loss is introduced to mitigate overconfidence in boundary-ambiguous samples. Furthermore, an evidential neural network is employed for uncertainty quantification, thereby enhancing diagnostic reliability and the robust detection of unknown failure modes. Concurrently, an uncertainty-guided data generation module is developed to augment data diversity while preserving semantic consistency. Finally, an adversarial causal feature disentanglement module is designed to extract highly discriminative causal features, effectively suppressing spurious correlations induced by dynamic distribution shifts. Extensive experimental evaluations conducted on three rotating machinery datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in fault diagnosis under dynamic, open industrial environments. The code will be available on GitHub at https://github.com/Fanyang199711/SOSDG.

title: Vibration suppression and multi-objective optimization of an aeroengine rotor system: Theory and experiment
abstract: Aeroengine rotor vibration seriously threatens unit operating safety, and squeeze film dampers (SFDs) are core passive vibration reduction components. This study investigates the optimization of vibration amplitude in a squeeze film damper-rotor system under constant speed or acceleration conditions. Dynamic models of the squeeze film damper-rotor system, the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), and the Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm were established. The factors influencing the dynamic characteristics of the squeeze film damper and the dynamic response of the rotor system were analyzed. Both optimization algorithms were employed to perform multi-objective optimization calculations for the steady-state and transient responses of the system. The results indicate that reducing the oil film thickness, along with increasing the damper length and oil viscosity, enhances the suppression of the unbalanced response of the rotor system. Both the NSGA-II and MOPSO algorithms demonstrated significant effectiveness in optimizing the steady-state response at typical locations within the squeeze film damper-rotor system, with a certain degree of effectiveness observed for the transient response as well. Quantitative comparison of six steady-state and six transient working conditions reveals that NSGA-II achieves optimal or good comprehensive performance in above working conditions. In contrast, MOPSO only delivers good or poor optimization results across transient cases, exhibiting an overall weaker vibration suppression performance. The findings provide a theoretical foundation for further research of multi-objective optimization in the dynamic response of rotor systems.

title: A nonlinear elastic-Preisach hysteresis model for bowl-shaped metal rubber isolators: modeling, identification and dynamic response prediction
abstract: To enhance vibration isolation performance under complex excitation environments, a bowl-shaped metal rubber (B-S MR) isolator composed of B-S MR and a helical spring is proposed. Considering the coexistence of structural and material nonlinearities, a nonlinear elastic-Preisach hysteresis (NE-PH) dynamic model is developed to consistently characterize the nonlinear stiffness evolution and path-dependent hysteretic behavior of the isolator. The nonlinear elastic restoring force is derived from a metal wire micro-spring equivalent model combined with large-deflection plate theory, while the nonlinear hysteretic force is described using a Preisach hysteresis operator to capture memory effects and energy dissipation mechanisms. Model parameters are identified via nonlinear least-squares optimization. The proposed model is validated through dynamic hysteresis loop tests, quasi-static force–displacement measurements, and swept-frequency response experiments. An equal-volume, equal-density ring-shaped metal rubber (R-S MR) isolator is selected as a benchmark for comparative analysis. Results indicate that the B-S MR configuration promotes more intensive internal contact and sliding interactions, thereby enhancing nonlinear deformation capacity and energy dissipation performance. Compared with the R-S MR isolator, the proposed configuration exhibits a lower resonance frequency and more effective suppression of resonance peaks under various excitation levels. The predicted responses agree well with the experimental measurements, confirming the validity and robustness of the proposed model. This study provides a theoretical basis for nonlinear dynamic modeling and performance optimization of B-S MR isolators in engineering applications.

title: Full-field identification of multi-cable tension using segmented super-sensitivity optical flow with spatially averaged spectral analysis: Wind tunnel tests and field study
abstract: Cables are primary load-bearing components but typically most fragile in cable-supported structures; measuring the tension of in-service cables, which is a critical indicator of their health state, is essential to ensure structural safety. As a potential alternative to conventional contact sensors, vision-based techniques, combining with vibration theory, provide low-cost, non-contact, and intrinsically full-field measurement capability for cable tension measurement. However, existing methods suffer insufficient accuracy under long measurement distances and weak surface textures. In addition, they are constrained by point-wise spectral analysis that leads to strong dependence on the selection of measurement location and limited robustness against local disturbances. To address these challenges, this study develops a new vision-based framework for accurate simultaneous estimation of multi-cable tension at full field by integrating super-sensitivity displacement measurement with spatially-averaged spectral analysis. The key is to effectively exploit full-field vibration measurement information in both the time and spectral domains. Specifically, the segmented super-sensitivity optical flow enables accurate pixel-level displacement estimation of each cable at full field beyond the sensitivity limit of photogrammetry; whereas spatial averaging of response power spectral densities yields modal-rich and local-fluctuation-suppressed spectra with reduced dependence on measurement locations. Wind tunnel experiments on a stay cable show that the developed method is able to identify the multi-modal cable displacements across the full field and provides enhanced identifiability of vibration frequencies for tension estimation, achieving an accuracy comparable to coherent laser displacement sensors. Field tests on a cable-stayed bridge of a 580 m main span are conducted for further validations. It is observed that despite low-resolution conditions at long measurement distance, displacements below 0.071 pixels are resolved and tensions of full-field cables are simultaneously estimated by the developed method, in excellent agreement with the installed accelerometer measurements. Finally, the applicability and challenges of the developed method are discussed.

title: Automatic identification of bridge damping ratios using clustering-aided SSI and multivariate signal decomposition
abstract: Accurate identification of structural damping is critical for predicting bridge dynamic responses and evaluating bridge health conditions. However, traditional identification methods require the manual interference and only focus on the analysis of single-channel monitoring data. Their performance is often degraded by the inevitable measurement noise, particularly in the damping estimation. To this end, this paper proposes an innovative method incorporating multivariate fast iterative filtering (MvFIF), covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification (COV-SSI), and density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) for the identification of bridge damping ratios. This method can simultaneously address the multi-channel data and effectively reduce the interference of measurement noise or irrelevant components in the data. Meanwhile, the corresponding identification is performed in an automatic manner. Specifically, DBSCAN is first incorporated into COV-SSI for extracting the modal frequencies. Then, MvFIF is employed to decompose the multi-channel data into a series of subseries with different frequency information and only those subseries with the frequency bandwidths covering the identified modal frequencies are retained. Finally, COV-SSI is reapplied to the retained signal for identifying the damping ratio. Based on the finite element modeling analysis, the performance of the proposed method is evaluated under various levels of signal-to-noise ratio where the conventional COV-SSI, empirical mode decomposition-aided COV-SSI and multivariate variational mode decomposition-aided COV-SSI are utilized for comparison. Furthermore, the real bridge monitoring data is also carried out to examine the ability of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that this method outperforms other relevant methods in terms of both accuracy and stability.

title: Resilient control of active suspension systems under DoS attacks: A hybrid framework for actuator saturation and multi-rate sampling
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid system framework for resilient controller design in active suspension systems under multi-rate (asynchronous) sampling, actuator saturation, and Denial-of-Service attacks. First, an attack detection mechanism is proposed by comparing the controller command with the actual actuator output. When an attack is detected, the controller output is forced to zero, and the internal states of the controller are reconfigured on the fly to prevent state divergence. Second, to address the state discontinuities induced by multi-rate sampling and attack switching, a hybrid controller is designed, and timer variables are introduced. This enables the closed-loop system to be uniformly modeled as a hybrid system that integrates continuous-time evolution, discrete state resets, and attack-induced switching. Finally, by employing a Lyapunov-based approach for hybrid systems and saturation control theory, a set of sufficient linear matrix inequality conditions is derived to guarantee regional exponential input-to-state stability of a compact set containing the origin. Furthermore, a semidefinite programming optimization problem is formulated to maximize the estimated region of attraction. Simulation results demonstrate that, under the considered challenging conditions, the proposed controller maintains ride comfort and handling stability.

title: Dual-end sparse based real-time 3D ultrasonic imaging system with high-density matrix array for non-destructive testing
abstract: Spatial characterization of internal defects is critical for non-destructive testing (NDT) and residual life assessment of mechanical components. The total focusing method (TFM) is increasingly regarded as a key direction for advancing 3D ultrasonic NDT. Despite its excellent image quality, 3D-TFM remains notoriously demanding in practice, requiring high-end hardware, massive data throughput, and substantial computation due to its stringent spatial sampling condition. To overcome these challenges, a real-time 3D ultrasonic imaging system with a dual-end sparse array for spatial characterization of defects is proposed. A full-rank binary matrix is used to generate a dual-end sparse-array layout, in combination with the beam-pattern evaluation criterion for arbitrary 2D arrays. An adaptive directivity correction algorithm is introduced to suppress artifacts. The entire pipeline is implemented on a GPU to maximize computational efficiency. Experimental validations on industrial specimens (steel rail and bolt) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves image quality comparable to that of fully addressed TFM. Memory usage is reduced by a factor of 5.18 on average, and imaging efficiency is improved by a factor of 12.38 on average. Furthermore, the proposed method enables the operation of a 256-element 2D array using a 64-channel acquisition device, thus validating its effectiveness. This work significantly advances the practical deployment of real-time 3D ultrasonic imaging in industrial NDT applications.

title: Digital twin-driven timely self-healing of machining accuracy for precision machine tools
abstract: Machining accuracy of machine tools is a core indicator for measuring the level of manufacturing equipment, directly determining component quality and overall machine performance. However, various errors such as thermal and wear during the machining process significantly affect machine tool accuracy. In recent years, digital twin-driven data modeling methods have shown significant advantages in error prediction and closed-loop feedback, yet challenges remain in the compensation stage, including difficulty in ensuring sensing data quality, inability to correct compensation delays, and static and rigid compensation strategies, which correspond to the bottlenecks of accuracy, timeliness, and intelligent adaptive compensation, respectively. To address these issues, this study proposes a digital twin-based timely self-healing framework for machining accuracy. First, a cascaded “prediction-identification-correction” strategy is designed to obtain high-fidelity sensing data. Then, a cross-scale time window feature aggregation method is developed to accurately deduce key physical characteristics of machine tools, providing forward time for compensation decision-making. Finally, a geometric error propagation model incorporating reverse clearance is constructed to evaluate the positioning capability through a dual-stage qualitative and quantitative strategy, enabling intelligent compensation command generation to achieve accuracy self-healing. On a self-constructed dataset containing anomalies, the proposed cascaded correction framework improves data quality by at least 36.5%. The proposed forward deduction method achieves at least 5.7% improvement compared with six mainstream methods on the self-constructed feed axis thermal characteristic dataset and the PHM2010 wear characteristic dataset. Furthermore, case studies on multi-axis machine tools validate the effectiveness of the intelligent adaptive compensation method.

title: Dimension-reduced probability density evolution equation for spatial three-dimensional vehicle-rail-bridge partitioned system
abstract: Stochastic dynamic response analysis of three-dimensional (3D) vehicle-rail-bridge (VRB) systems is challenging due to time-varying coupling, high-dimensional uncertainties, and strongly nonstationary and non-Gaussian response characteristics. This study develops an efficient stochastic dynamic analysis framework by introducing the dimension-reduced probability density evolution equation (DR-PDEE) into a non-iterative partitioned VRB model. The vehicle, rail, and bridge subsystems are formulated as time-invariant stochastic subsystems connected through time-dependent wheel-rail and time-independent rail-bridge interfaces, thereby avoiding repeated assembly and factorization of global time-varying system matrices. Based on this deterministic backbone, the DR-PDEE is used to characterize the time-varying probability density evolution of selected displacement responses under random system parameters and stochastic track irregularities. To improve numerical robustness for highly nonstationary and non-Gaussian VRB responses, a dimension-reduced Monte Carlo solution strategy is adopted for solving the DR-PDEE and compared with the classical path-integration scheme. Numerical results are validated against Monte Carlo simulations with 10,000 realizations. The proposed framework accurately captures nonstationary and non-Gaussian response distributions using a limited number of samples, demonstrating its efficiency and potential for stochastic analysis of complex coupled railway systems.

title: Chatter-sensitive feature construction and dual-branch learning for machining state identification in micro-milling of glow discharge polymer
abstract: Glow discharge polymer (GDP) ablators with micro-milled modulated microstructures are increasingly used in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) applications. However, self-excited vibration/chatter, generated from an insufficient-stiffness manufacturing system, could degrade the resultant surface quality and process productivity during micro-milling. In this study, a physically guided data-driven framework was developed for chatter-sensitive feature construction and machining-state identification in micro-milling of GDP polymers. Tri-directional milling-force and acceleration signals were in-situ acquired during micro-milling with a single-edge diamond tool. Wavelet packet decomposition (WPD) was initially employed for noise suppression and signal reconstruction, with optimal parameters determined using an energy-weighted feature evaluation strategy. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) was then applied to isolate state-sensitive intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), and a state-discriminative energy–entropy criterion was developed to determine task-oriented decomposition parameters. Based on the selected chatter-sensitive modes, eight multi-domain features were extracted and organized into two heterogeneous feature tensors. A dual-branch Inception Residual network (DIR-Net) was constructed to independently encode force- and acceleration-related features before high-level feature fusion. Experimental results showed that WPD improved the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the milling-force and acceleration signals by 65.8 % and 43.0 %, respectively. DIR-Net achieved an identification accuracy of 97.08 % and a macro-averaged F1-score of 97.02 % on the independent test set, outperforming conventional CNN and ResNet benchmarks. Feature visualization and online monitoring results further indicated improved separability among air-cut, stable cutting, and chatter states, as well as stable recognition performance under the unseen tool-overhang and tool-size conditions. The proposed research framework provides an interpretable solution for chatter identification and online monitoring in ultra-precision micro-milling of GDP.

title: Towards in-situ monitoring of floating platforms: geometry-anchored recurrent diffusion for long-sequence motion reconstruction based on monocular marker-free video
abstract: Long-sequence motion reconstruction of floating platforms is important for response-informed monitoring because downstream tension estimation and fatigue-related assessment depend on temporally consistent motion histories rather than isolated pose estimates. In practical offshore applications, direct and accurate long-term in-situ measurement is especially difficult, since the monocular marker-free vision is constrained by limited geometric observability, full-sequence label unavailability, and growing drift risk over extended durations. To address these challenges, this study develops a new response-informed vision-based monitoring framework for floating platforms under monocular, marker-free observation. The framework combines geometry-anchored pseudo-supervision, recurrent diffusion-based temporal inference, stabilization-oriented long-sequence tracking, and downstream tension and damage-equivalent-load (DEL) calculation under an adopted simplified mooring model. The method is evaluated through an OpenFAST-based primary case, ablation studies, a supplementary-view analysis, a controlled wave-tank test demonstration, robustness evaluations under changed excitation and controlled visual disturbances, and a runtime assessment. The results show that the dominant platform motion can be reconstructed with stable long-sequence behavior, while recurrent temporal inference and reliability-aware stabilization play complementary roles in preserving sequence continuity and suppressing drift accumulation. By integrating learning-based efficient reconstruction with stabilization-oriented temporal inference, the proposed framework addresses a critical methodological gap in achieving computationally efficient and temporally consistent motion reconstruction over long sequences, even under visual degradation. This capability demonstrates the potential for in-situ offshore infrastructure monitoring. Under the adopted quasi-static mooring model with axial elasticity, the reconstructed motion preserves the main information required for the mooring tension and downstream DEL estimation, facilitating the fatigue-related assessment.

title: A hybrid-magnetic bistable nonlinear energy sink for enhanced energy transfer and non-contact stroke regulation
abstract: A magnetic bistable nonlinear energy sink (MBNES) with a hybrid magnet arrangement and non-contact magnetic restoring action is proposed for vibration attenuation over the investigated low-frequency range. The device integrates horizontal and vertical magnet arrays in a bistable nonlinear attachment. The horizontal magnets tailor the double-well potential, reduce the activation threshold, and facilitate nonlinear energy transfer, whereas the vertical magnets introduce a large-amplitude magnetic restoring force to reduce excessive relative displacement without mechanical impact. An equivalent magnetic-charge model is developed to derive the restoring force and potential energy, and the nonlinear force is fitted by a polynomial for dynamic analysis. A coupled linear oscillator–MBNES model is established to examine equilibrium stability, bistable dynamics, strongly modulated response, and targeted energy transfer. Slow invariant manifold analysis shows that the hybrid magnetic configuration shifts the folded slow-flow region to lower response amplitudes, reducing the predicted SMR threshold from 0.0373 to 0.0328 compared with the horizontal-magnet layout. Numerical simulations demonstrate primary-resonance attenuation over the investigated frequency range, with a maximum LO response reduction of 85.28% and a 13.25% reduction in the maximum MBNES relative displacement compared with the horizontal-magnet layout. Parametric analyses reveal that the excitation amplitude, nonlinear stiffness, and damping ratio jointly determine the activation threshold, energy-transfer efficiency, response stability, and stroke-reduction performance. Experiments further confirm the vibration-suppression capability of the proposed device, with a 63.03% reduction in the peak acceleration of the primary structure under 5 mm base excitation. This magnetic potential-shaping strategy provides a compact passive approach for reducing the SMR activation threshold, attenuating vibration in the investigated frequency range, and introducing impact-free large-amplitude magnetic restoring action in bistable nonlinear energy sinks.

title: Modeling and vibration characteristics of flexible thin-walled aviation bevel gear systems with excitation coupling
abstract: To address the prominent vibration challenges posed by the lightweight design of aviation thin-walled bevel gear systems, this paper presents a systematic investigation into multi source excitation coupling modeling and dynamic characteristics analysis. Fully accounting for the structural characteristics of thin-walled spiral bevel gears, the flexibility of the gear body is incorporated through segmented modeling approach. A hybrid dynamic model is subsequently developed which comprehensively accounts for the multi source excitation effects arising from bearing supports, pitch deviations, and unbalance excitations. It is capable not only of predicting the overall system vibration response but also of capturing vibration characteristics of the gear body, such as traveling wave resonance. This study analyzes the modulation effects of multiple excitations on vibration spectral components, reveals the variation patterns of bearing dynamic contact forces and the amplitudes of various frequency components with respect to unbalance magnitude and rotational speed, and the distinctive characteristics of traveling wave resonance in thin-walled bevel gears are also elucidated. Experimental comparisons demonstrate that the proposed model can accurately simulate the multi-source excitation coupling vibration characteristics of the system, and exhibits good predictive capability, particularly for traveling wave resonance. This study provides a theoretical basis for establishing vibration limits and identifying resonance failure modes in aviation transmission systems.

title: An active suspension integrated with a series-connected rotary magnetorheological damper for inertia decoupling
abstract: Ball-screw active suspensions (BS-AS) are promising for vehicle applications because of their compact structure, high transmission efficiency, and high output force density. However, in conventional rigidly coupled configurations, motor rotational inertia is reflected to the suspension port through the transmission mechanism, thereby deteriorating vibration isolation and impact response performance. To address this issue, this study proposes a series damping actuated active suspension (SDA-AS). Unlike conventional BS-AS configurations, the SDA-AS incorporates a controllable rotary magnetorheological (MR) damper between the permanent magnet synchronous motor and the ball screw, thereby altering the mechanical path through which motor inertia is transmitted to the suspension port. By allowing relative rotation between the motor and screw sides, this configuration weakens the rigid reflection of motor inertia while retaining controllable torque transmission and providing a controllable dissipative path for impact energy. To elucidate the inertia-decoupling mechanism enabled by series damping, analyses are conducted at the actuator and suspension-system levels based on actuator-port mechanical impedance and quarter-car dynamics, respectively; the proposed concept is subsequently implemented in a compact prototype with a hierarchical control strategy and validated through bench tests. Compared with BS-AS, the SDA-AS without hierarchical control reduces the root-mean-square sprung-mass acceleration by 26.1% under random-road excitation and the peak sprung-mass acceleration by 43.4% under bump excitation. Hierarchical control provides further vibration attenuation without compromising the structural decoupling benefit. These findings demonstrate that controllable series damping can mitigate motor-inertia coupling while preserving active force-generation capability, offering a mechanical approach to improving medium- and high-frequency vibration isolation and impact attenuation in ball-screw active suspensions.

title: Speed-informed multi-resonance fault-order extraction with verifiable interpretability
abstract: Variable-speed operation distorts the time periodicity of bearing fault impulses, causing order-locked resonance responses to fluctuate across revolutions under resonance coloring, colored noise, and intermittent non-synchronous impacts. Although envelope formation and tacholess order tracking have progressed, many industrial platforms provide speed/phase measurements; the practical challenge is therefore to extract order-domain variables that remain robust to outliers, stable across revolutions, and coherent across multiple resonance bands, without relying on complex black-box back ends. This paper proposes a Multi-resonance Fault-order Sparse and Stable Extraction (MFoS2E), a speed-informed and angle-resampling-free framework built on multi-resonance analytic envelopes. MFoS2E constructs (i) a revolution–time lattice (Y-space) that preserves within-revolution impulsiveness and (ii) an order/sideband coefficient tensor (C-space) indexed by resonance band, defect order, and revolution number. Its core is a physics-aligned proximal stabilization in C-space that jointly enforces robust fidelity (Huber-type), speed-aware across-revolution trend filtering, cross-resonance coupling, and structured sparsity over fault-order/sideband families. From the stabilized coefficients, we derive interpretable power/coherence/stability descriptors (augmented by lightweight Y-space ridge summaries) and perform diagnosis with shallow linear classifiers. Experiments on multiple variable-speed bearing datasets show that MFoS2E improves accuracy and worst-regime robustness over representative tachometer-based baselines and time–frequency CNNs, while enabling quantitative verification via analysis–synthesis consistency and cross-band agreement metrics for the extracted fault-order components.

title: A unified semi-analytical modeling for the global mode and vibration characteristics of elastic supported and connected structures with application in large-scale flexible spacecraft
abstract: Flexibly connected structures composed of plates, shells, trusses, and other components joined by hinges, bolts, or other connection interfaces are widely used in the aerospace field. In order to analyze the dynamic characteristics and global mode of such multi-substructure connection systems, this paper proposes a unified semi-analytical modeling framework for elastic supported and flexible connected structures. Using the admissible function expansion as the displacement approximation, and the constraints such as elastic support, bolt support and hinge connection are characterized by the equivalent stiffness, and the unified generalized characteristic equation is established. For the flexible connection interface, the displacement continuity condition and Lagrange multiplier are further introduced to establish an extended characteristic equation for the multi- component connection system. Several representative models are presented, where their results are compared with ANSYS, experimental, and literature data to assess the performance of the proposed method. Subsequently, it is extended to the large-scale flexible spacecraft, in which the periodic space truss is equivalent to a Timoshenko beam. Then a rigid-flexible coupling dynamics model is constructed in combination with the central rigid body, which realizes the unified assembly and global modal solution of the multi-component system. Numerical results are conducted to investigate the frequency and nonlinear vibration characteristics of truss structures and rigid-flexible coupling spacecraft systems, which indicates the validity of the framework in the global modal modeling and response analysis.

title: Load reconstruction digital twin based on an ultra-high-density fiber-optic tri-axial strain sensor network
abstract: Accurate and reliable load reconstruction is essential for driving the evolution of digital twins (DTs) of structures, enabling optimizing structural design, operation and hence extending their service life. This paper proposes a load reconstruction digital twin framework for precise load monitoring of low aspect ratio structures (plate-like structures). The framework integrates a novel high-density optical fiber tri-axial sensor network based on saddle-shaped sensing units, which is especially designed and realized with a density up to 3842/m2, ensuring the “pixel level” acquisition of strain field data. To mitigate the external environmental impact during measurements, an external load reconstruction algorithm based on strain data from the internal surface of the structure is developed. The proposed load reconstruction methodology is experimentally validated under two typical partial load types under laboratory environment and distributed air loads in a wind tunnel. A load field evaluation mechanism based on structural similarity index is introduced and a quantitative evaluation of the reconstructed load distribution is conducted, indicating the effectiveness of this DT based methodology with field reconstruction accuracy of higher than 87% in amplitude. The proposed digital twin method provides a reliable and accurate approach based on high-density measured strain data for the reconstruction of complex load fields.

title: Dual-domain collaborative deconvolution and its applications to the rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: The Fourier spectrum plays a critical role in signal processing-based fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. It has been demonstrated that vibration signals from rolling bearing faults exhibit a series of equally spaced discrete spectral lines in the Fourier spectrum. These spectral features offer essential diagnostic clues for fault identification. Maximum second-order cyclostationarity blind deconvolution (CYCBD) is an established technique for enhancing fault-induced impulses in time-domain signals. However, existing deconvolution methods primarily operate on time-domain or envelope-domain criteria and do not fully exploit the rich harmonic information present in the Fourier spectrum. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a dual-domain collaborative deconvolution (DDCD) method, which integrates both the temporal impulsiveness and the spectral harmonic sparsity of the signal within a unified framework. The method is developed by extending the mathematical principles of CYCBD to the frequency domain, with the objective of effectively suppressing strong background noise and enhancing fault-related spectral structures. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm offers marked advantages over conventional deconvolution methods in rolling bearing fault diagnosis.

title: Multi-task mixture-of-experts vision transformer for cross-bridge anomaly detection
abstract: Structural health monitoring systems deployed on large-scale bridges accumulate massive amounts of anomalous data, which undermines the reliability of structural condition assessment and damage identification. As monitoring targets gradually expand from individual bridges to bridge groups, the costs associated with model training and management continue to increase, placing higher demands on unified model deployment and centralized system management. Meanwhile, although anomalous patterns from different bridges contain potentially shareable information, such commonality cannot be fully exploited through simple data aggregation. This study proposes a multi-task mixture-of-experts Vision Transformer (MT-MoE ViT) framework for data anomaly diagnosis, which imposes parallel constraints during the joint optimization of multi-bridge tasks to reduce reliance on structure-specific or local condition features and instead learn anomalous features that remain discriminative across multiple bridge scenarios. To further characterize task-level differences among bridges, task embeddings are incorporated into the gating network to guide adaptive expert selection and balance shared representation learning with task-specific modeling. To mitigate routing collapse and optimization conflicts in multi-task learning, sparse routing strategies achieve feature-level expert selection, while adaptive multi-task optimization mechanisms dynamically adjust gradient weights and expert load balancing. Experimental validation conducted on real structural health monitoring data from nine long-span bridges of different structural types demonstrates that the proposed method enables stable cross-bridge anomaly representation and collaborative diagnosis within a unified model framework.

title: Magnetic-gear-enabled counter-rotating electromagnetic energy harvester for capturing low-speed wind energy
abstract: Wind energy is an abundant ambient power source for self-powered sensing, but conventional electromagnetic wind harvesters remain constrained under weak wind due to low rotor speed and limited magnetic flux variation. To address this issue, this paper presents a magnetic-gear-enabled Savonius-driven counter-rotating electromagnetic energy harvester (MG-SCR-EMEH) that integrates a Savonius turbine, an axial magnetic gear, and upper and lower electromagnetic power-generation modules. A non-contact magnetic speed amplification mechanism and a coaxial counter-rotating configuration triple the effective magnet-coil relative speed over direct-drive, thereby enhancing the magnetic flux variation and induction output while avoiding the wear and dissipation of contact-based frequency up-conversion. A theoretical model that combines aerodynamic drag and induced-voltage analyses, supported by finite element simulations, elucidates the mechanisms of magnetic-field modulation, torque transmission, and voltage generation. Experimental results show that the proposed MG-SCR-EMEH starts up at 3.5 m/s and, at 4.5 m/s, delivers 5.552 mW system-level equivalent charging power (27.76 mJ over 5 s into a 1 mF capacitor, 1.903 W/m 3 power density). At the same input speed of 50 RPM, increasing the magnet-coil relative speed from 50 RPM in the direct-drive configuration to 150 RPM in the magnetic-gear-coupled configuration raises the peak power from 22.78 to 166.78 mW. Furthermore, integrated with an energy-management unit, layered millimeter-wave radar nodes, and a BLE module, the MG-SCR-EMEH serves as the power source for a falling-object warning system, highlighting strong potential for low-speed wind energy harvesting and structural safety monitoring.

title: A half-synchrosqueezing transform method for the decomposition of space-close modes
abstract: This study focuses on the challenge of using the synchrosqueezing transform (SST) to decompose space-close modes. Traditional SST requires a minimum frequency interval of approximately one window length between two modes to avoid severe interference in instantaneous frequency (IF) estimation. We theoretically prove that when this separation is reduced to half the window length, the standard SST fails. To overcome this limitation, we propose the half-synchrosqueezing transform (HSST). The core innovation lies in a new squeezing strategy that processes only the non-interfering (un-cross) regions in the time–frequency (TF) plane. This method effectively reduces the required separation distance, achieves a clear TF representation, and accurately reconstructs modes that were previously considered too close for SST-based decomposition. The performance of HSST in instantaneous frequency estimation and mode reconstruction in space-close scenarios is verified through numerical and experimental signals.

title: Dual-hierarchical multi-scale distance similarity entropy as a novel nonlinear measure for wind turbine gearbox intelligent fault diagnosis
abstract: Accurate feature extraction and reliable multi-type fault diagnosis remain challenging in wind energy conversion systems. Wind turbine gearboxes operate under complex and variable conditions, resulting in diverse and nonlinear fault characteristics. Although entropy-based measures have been widely adopted for fault diagnosis, existing hierarchical entropy methods based on conventional hierarchical decomposition often suffer from insufficient data utilization and unstable entropy estimation at deeper decomposition layers owing to progressive shortening of the subsequences. To address these limitations, this paper proposes dual-hierarchical multi-scale distance similarity entropy (DHMDSEn). A dual-hierarchical decomposition strategy is introduced to improve information utilization and alleviate instability caused by data-length reduction. Unlike conventional single-phase hierarchical decomposition, the proposed approach employs two complementary phase-shifted decompositions to exploit the original signal more fully and enhance decomposition robustness. Distance similarity entropy (DSEn) is then calculated for each subcomponent, and the resulting values are averaged for fusion, while a coarse-grained process is incorporated to capture fault-related characteristics across multiple temporal scales. By integrating dual-hierarchical decomposition with multi-scale analysis, DHMDSEn provides a robust characterization of vibration signal complexity from both structural and temporal perspectives. Experimental results from a laboratory wind turbine gearbox dataset and a real industrial dataset yield mean diagnostic accuracies of 91.22% and 99.98%, respectively, demonstrating that the proposed method outperforms existing hierarchical entropy-based methods.

title: Visual fault diagnosis of rolling bearings based on semantic segmentation and geometric motion modeling
abstract: Existing vision-based bearing monitoring methods rarely establish a direct relationship between the geometric motion of internal bearing components and fault characteristic frequencies. To address this issue, this paper proposes an interpretable visual fault-characteristic-frequency identification method based on semantic segmentation and geometric motion modeling. First, an analytical framework of “semantic segmentation, motion modeling, and fault diagnosis” is constructed. A high-speed industrial camera is used to acquire internal bearing motion images, and pixel-level semantic segmentation is used to accurately extract key structural information such as rolling elements and the inner race. Second, a visual geometric observation signal is constructed based on the minimum Euclidean distance between rolling-element centers and reference points. From a kinematic perspective, the main frequency of this signal is proven to be consistent with the characteristic frequencies of outer race and inner race faults, thereby establishing a physical mapping relationship between the visual measurement signal and the bearing fault mechanism. Given the slender morphology, blurred boundaries, strong texture anisotropy, and complex background interference of internal bearing components, a semantic segmentation network integrating an asymmetric dilated feature enhancement module and a direction-decoupled deformable cross-attention mechanism is designed to enhance the representation of local edges, long-range dependencies, and irregularly deformed structures. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves mIoU values of 96.70% and 95.93% and mAcc values of 98.15% and 97.75% in outer race and inner race fault segmentation tasks, respectively. Under multiple rotational speeds of 1200, 1500, 1800, and 2100 r/min, the method can stably extract fault characteristic frequencies corresponding to BPFO and BPFI. Across rotational speeds of 1200, 1500, 1800, and 2100 r/min, the BPFO and BPFI peak locations extracted by the proposed visual method match well with the theoretical values and synchronously collected acceleration reference signals, and this measurement approach maintains the merits of non-contact detection and clear physical interpretability.

title: Fractional-order skyhook positive real network for semi-active inertial suspension system of a hub motor driven vehicle: optimal design and experimental validation
abstract: Semi-active inertial suspension system (SISS) based on skyhook control strategy has attracted considerable attention for improving vehicle ride comfort and road-holding performance. However, its application to the hub motor driven vehicle (HMDV) remains limited, and the potential benefits of incorporating fractional-order theory into skyhook control strategy remain largely unexplored, particularly under severe vibration conditions encountered in HMDVs. To address these challenges, this study proposes an SISS based on a fractional-order skyhook positive real network synthesis. In this framework, first and second-order positive real networks are constructed and implemented in a quarter-car model of an HMDV. The fractional-order theory is integrated into the skyhook control strategy to further enhance vibration suppression capability and dynamic performance. The optimal design parameters are determined using a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm incorporating crowding distance and an adaptive grid strategy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SISS with a fractional-order skyhook second-order positive real network achieves superior vibration isolation performance compared with traditional suspension system. Furthermore, experimental validation through bench testing confirms notable improvements in ride comfort and vehicle stability, thereby verifying the correctness of the proposed approach. The findings of this research establish a novel design methodology for SISS in the HMDV, offering enhanced ride comfort and road-holding performance under harsh operating conditions.

title: An iterative sparse Bayesian method based on adaptive pruning for damage identification of offshore wind turbine jacket structure
abstract: Under conditions of limited sensors and finite modal information of low order, the influence of local damage in jacket structures on the global modal response is usually weak. Meanwhile, parameter identification in a high dimensional space after regional discretization tends to introduce many degrees of freedom that contribute little to the observations, leading to parameter diffusion, compensation by adjacent members, and unstable identification results. To address these issues, this paper proposes an iterative sparse Bayesian method based on adaptive pruning for damage identification in offshore wind turbine jacket structures. First, a joint residual model integrating natural frequencies and mode shapes is constructed, and an iterative sparse Bayesian solution framework is established on the basis of regional parameterization to update the damage parameters. Then, an adaptive pruning strategy is introduced by combining posterior relevance, parameter magnitude, a memory mechanism, and an ablation-based data consistency test, so that redundant parameters can be progressively compressed while preserving data fitting capability. Finally, the proposed method is validated through numerical case studies and physical experiments. The results show that, under the dual damage scenario, the proposed method can simultaneously identify the two actual damaged locations, while the maximum spurious damage response is only −0.0427. Compared with existing methods, the proposed method achieves higher localization accuracy, stronger suppression of spurious responses, and better identification stability.

title: On the geometry of Population-Based Structural Health Monitoring: Part I — sheaves on graphs
abstract: Population-Based Structural Health Monitoring (PBSHM) has recently emerged as a means of using data from multiple structures to enhance diagnostic capability in any given individual structure. As part of a sequence of papers on the foundations of PBSHM, a geometric picture was proposed for the methodology. Although this picture provided some insight into PBSHM generally, it could not provide a rigorous basis for study as it was based on a fibre-bundle viewpoint that did not exactly match the ‘geometry’ of PBSHM. Assuming that a rigorous framework could provide valuable guidance into designing workable PBSHM systems, the objective of this paper (and a companion paper) is to provide a rigorous geometrical picture. The current paper achieves this by eschewing the fibre bundle as the main geometrical object of interest and replacing it with a cellular sheaf. It is shown how a population of structures, represented in abstract form, can be encapsulated in a cellular sheaf, together with the SHM feature data for the structures. Furthermore, a geometrical operation – a variant of local PCA alignment – is introduced which actually implements (linear) transfer learning between structures and naturally provides a generalisation of some previously-proposed algorithms. The methodology is validated on a population of simulated structures in the context of novelty detection. Further analysis of a multi-class SHM problem exposes some issues for PCA-alignment and statistic-alignment algorithms generally where rotations are included. As this paper possibly represents the first use of sheaves in engineering dynamics, substantial background material is included here and other aspects of sheaf technology are discussed.

title: Online evolutionary method of thermal error compensation for machine tool feed axes: Online autonomous parameters identification enabling efficient generalized application
abstract: Thermal error compensation is an effective means to improve accuracy stability of machine tools. However, existing methods rely on artificial offline identification of thermal error model parameters, which require collecting thermal error and temperature over several hours or even days. It is cumbersome and time-consuming, significantly reducing compensation implementation efficiency and becoming a major obstacle for the generalized application of thermal error compensation. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes an online evolutionary method of thermal error compensation for machine tool feed axes. By online autonomous parameters identification (OAPI), the efficient generalized application can be realized. The thermal error mechanism model (TEMM) was established for calculating frictional heat generation in ball screws and rolling bearing pairs, as well as the resulting thermal error of the feed axes. In a brief process of feed motion and static cooling (less than 1 h) in machine tool, autonomous parameter identification of thermal error model for feed axes is completed. The time-consuming artificial testing is not necessary. Furthermore, the thermal error compensation values can be calculated using only the motion information from the CNC system and the ambient temperature of the feed axis. Thermal error compensation experiments conducted on the X, Y, and Z axes of a vertical machining center. It has significantly improved implementation efficiency while simultaneously reducing thermal errors on the X, Y, and Z axes by 88.2 %, 65.0 % and 71.6 %, respectively. This method effectively strikes a balance between compensation accuracy and implementation efficiency. It can solve the key problem of thermal error compensation, which relies on human collection of a large amount of data and takes a long time, and provide a new pathway for applying thermal error compensation.

title: A deep reinforcement learning method applied to remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
abstract: As an important component of mechanical equipment, the health status of rolling bearings directly affects the reliability and safety of the equipment. Due to the harsh working environment of rolling bearings and the difficulty in identifying the early degradation trends, the accuracy of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is significantly challenged. To address these issues, this paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) prediction model based on the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, which reconfigures the RUL prediction task as a sequential decision-making problem under Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework in a continuous action space. The DDPG algorithm can effectively capture the temporal dependencies among original data. By combining the feature extraction capabilities of residual networks (ResNet) and the time series modeling capabilities of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, high-precision RUL prediction is achieved. Firstly, a reinforcement learning (RL) agent based on ResNet-LSTM is constructed to extract deep degradation features from the original data. Subsequently, by designing appropriate reward functions and action spaces, the agent learns to map the current operating state of the rolling bearing to its RUL under the guidance of the DDPG algorithm through repeated trials and optimization. The proposed model was validated on two open-source datasets and a private dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves lower root mean square error (RMSE) and more stable degradation trend prediction compared with other approaches.

title: Shield-ground interaction during earth pressure balance shield tunneling: insights from field strain monitoring
abstract: Shield-ground interaction delineates the coupled ground responses and shield kinematics during tunneling. Yet, it remains elusive how this interaction evolves under complex ground conditions, e.g., composite ground, or complicated shield operations, e.g., steering in a curve, which underpins safer and more automatic tunneling engineering. In this study, a strain monitoring system was developed and deployed on the shield shell of an earth pressure balance machine in a railway tunnel project at Shenzhen, China, offering an unprecedented opportunity to uncover hidden patterns of shield shell mechanical responses during tunneling. Correlation analysis among strain responses, operating parameters, and ground conditions reveals that: (1) The axial strain along the shield shell demonstrates a negative correlation with thrust at the shield head, yet a positive correlation at the shield midsection and tail, implying that the front part of shield is generally under compression, but the rear part of shield is generally under tension when thrust application; (2) The axial strain demonstrates significant asymmetry between inner and outer arcs during shield steering. This asymmetry is opposite at the shield head and tail, and how this asymmetry is distributed along the shield depends on where the rotation center is located; (3) The axial strain gradient increases as the shield advances from soft ground into relatively stiff ground, reflecting a redistribution of axial loads within the shield shell in response to spatial variations in penetration resistance of the surrounding ground.

title: Q-shift dual-tree complex wavelet phase-based vibration displacement measurement for wind turbine towers
abstract: In the context of the global energy transition, wind turbine towers serve as the primary load-bearing structures of wind energy systems, and accurate measurement of their vibration-induced displacements is essential for structural health monitoring and safety assessment. Conventional contact-based measurement techniques suffer from complex installation procedures and limited spatial coverage. In contrast, existing vision-based vibration measurement methods are often highly dependent on surface texture and exhibit insufficient phase stability under challenging imaging conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a non-contact vibration displacement measurement method for wind turbine towers based on the phase information of the Q-shift dual-tree complex wavelet transform. The proposed approach exploits the multi-scale and multi-directional complex coefficients obtained from the Q-shift dual-tree complex wavelet decomposition to construct a phase representation with approximate shift invariance and improved inter-scale consistency. Displacement estimation is performed within regions exhibiting stable phase responses, such as structural edges, thereby enhancing robustness against complex backgrounds and noise. Furthermore, an adaptive downsampling strategy is introduced to alleviate phase wrapping effects in large-scale structural vibrations, enabling reliable displacement measurement under relatively large vibration amplitudes. Numerical simulations and wind turbine tower model experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves sub-pixel displacement accuracy under complex environmental conditions. Compared with conventional vision-based approaches based on phase or image intensity information, the proposed method exhibits superior overall stability, providing a high-precision and robust visual vibration measurement solution for the non-contact monitoring of tall and flexible structures.

title: Bayesian learning in structural dynamics: a comprehensive review and emerging trends
abstract: Bayesian learning has emerged as a compelling and vital research direction in the field of structural dynamics, offering a probabilistic lens to understand and refine the analysis of complex dynamical systems. This review meticulously traces the three-decade evolution of Bayesian learning in structural dynamics, illuminating core principles, groundbreaking methodologies, and diverse applications that have significantly influenced the field. The narrative commences by delving into the basics of Bayesian theory, clarifying essential concepts, and introducing primary methods for deriving posterior distributions, with an in-depth exploration of three types: Laplace approximation, stochastic sampling, and variational inference. Subsequently, the text explores the implementation of two types of Bayesian learning in structural dynamics: physical model learning and data-centric statistical model learning. Physical model learning emphasizes inferring physical model parameters within a Bayesian framework for system identification and prediction, while statistical model learning integrates Bayesian learning methodologies into data-centric statistical modeling within probabilistic machine learning. Both types resonate across various applications, such as modal analysis, model updating, damage detection, and reliability updating, highlighting their pivotal role in enhancing comprehension of dynamical systems and decision-making. The paper also navigates obstacles by proposing ways to enhance existing Bayesian inference strategies. Distinguished from previous research, this study offers a thorough examination of both traditional and cutting-edge Bayesian methods. It not only underscores the transformative influence of Bayesian approaches but also serves as a beacon, guiding researchers in the judicious selection and refinement of suitable methods for various challenges in structural dynamics.

title: A novel method for bearing fault diagnosis based on deep compressive sensing and contrastive transfer learning
abstract: Bearing health monitoring is crucial in rail transit vehicles, and deep compressive sensing has gained attention for its low redundancy, minimal storage, and fast signal reconstruction. However, conventional networks often adopt single-branch convolutional structures, limiting feature stability and temporal modeling, especially under complex conditions and strong noise. Moreover, typical transfer learning approaches rely on a single loss function during fine-tuning, which, under small sample scenarios, can cause intra-class feature dispersion, blurred inter-class boundaries, and reduced discriminative ability. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis method combining deep compressive sensing and contrastive transfer learning. In the compressive sensing stage, a multi-branch attention-based reconstruction network is designed to capture key signal features under complex conditions, enhancing feature richness and providing a conditional analytical explanation for the possible domain-discrepancy suppression mechanism between source and target data.
