In the transfer learning stage, a staged loss optimization strategy is employed: pre-training uses contrastive loss to obtain discriminative embeddings, while fine-tuning combines Triplet Loss and Cross Entropy to balance embedding structure and classification power. Experiments on Case Western Reserve University bearing open datasets and BJTU-RAO Bogie Datasets demonstrate the method’s effectiveness, achieving a signal MSE of 0.00321 and fault diagnosis accuracy of 98.51 %, highlighting its superior cross-domain diagnostic performance under small sample conditions.

title: Sparsity-measure-informed methods for machinery condition monitoring and fault diagnosis: fundamentals, methodologies, and future directions
abstract: Sparsity measures (SMs) have emerged as powerful tools for machinery condition monitoring and fault diagnosis (CMFD) due to their ability to quantitatively characterize the impulsiveness and cyclostationarity inherent in repetitive fault transients. Despite the widespread applications of SMs—such as kurtosis, Lp/Lq norm, pq-mean, Gini index (GI), relative entropy (RE), etc., —in numerous CMFD methods over the past two decades, a comprehensive review dedicated to this topic has been lacking. This paper fills this gap by providing a systematic and holistic review of SM-informed methodologies for machinery CMFD. The review is structured into three main parts. First, fundamental knowledge of SMs is presented, including definitions of classical and recently proposed SMs, six essential properties that a valid SM should satisfy, two general frameworks (ratio of quasi-arithmetic means and sum of weighted normalized square envelope) for constructing new SMs, and sparsity quantification gradient curves that reveal the sensitivity of different SMs to sparsity changes. Second, SM-based methods for machinery condition monitoring are reviewed, focusing on two research hotspots: (i) adaptive weighted signal preprocessing technique (AWSPT)-based indicators that enable simultaneous incipient fault detection and monotonic degradation assessment, and (ii) data-driven optimized weights spectrum (OWS) methods that yield interpretable fault signatures. Third, SM-based signal processing methods for fault diagnosis are systematically examined, covering fast kurtogram, blind deconvolution, general signal decompositions (e.g., empirical mode decomposition, variational mode decomposition, empirical wavelet transform), and tailored signal decompositions such as impulsive mode decomposition. Experimental comparisons between representative methods are also provided to offer intuitive insights. Finally, future research directions are discussed, including the need for deeper theoretical investigations of SMs, clarification of their effective boundaries, and integration with machine and deep learning models. This review is expected to accelerate the development of advanced SM-driven CMFD technologies.

title: A numerical approach for analyzing load uniformity and vibration behaviors over the entire tooth meshing cycle of herringbone gear
abstract: Asymmetric pitch deviation (APD) is an inevitable manufacturing deviation in herringbone gear pairs, and existing research literature has not yet conducted in-depth exploration into the effects of APD on the load distribution, multi-origin excitation, and vibration behaviors of herringbone gear throughout the entire tooth meshing cycle (ETMC). Moreover, the objective functions of existing optimization models are mostly set to multi-origin excitation and vibration acceleration, lacking an optimization design method that can balance the load uniformity performance and vibration performance of the ETMC. To solve these problems, a tooth contact analysis (TCA) model, an enhanced loaded tooth contact analysis (LTCA) model, and a meshing impact force (MIF) model for herringbone gear were first established. The load distribution coefficient (LDC), load distribution, comprehensive meshing stiffness (CMS), axial displacement (AD), comprehensive meshing error (CME), and MIF of the ETMC were obtained. A dynamic model for herringbone gear system considering the multi-origin excitation of the ETMC was constructed, with the corresponding parameters involved in the model calculated systematically. A general expression for tooth surface modification (TSM) was derived, and a mathematical model for the collaborative optimization design of load uniformity and vibration of herringbone gear was established. The variation laws in multi-origin excitation and vibration behaviors of the ETMC under different asymmetric pitch deviations (APDs) were revealed, and the vibration characteristics of the ETMC before and after TSM were compared. The correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method were experimentally verified. This research provides support for the load uniformity and vibration reduction design of herringbone gear.

title: High-performance FBG temperature sensing with engineering-oriented tunable sensitivity: A mechanical–optical coupling strategy
abstract: The limited sensitivity of fiber Bragg grating (FBG) temperature sensors restricts their potential to fully capitalize on inherent advantages. This research focuses on enhancing the temperature sensitivity of FBG sensors and addressing key issues such as the design and controllability of the sensitivity enhancement. A novel thermostat metal strip (TMS) configuration is introduced to enhance the temperature sensitivity of the FBG sensor, with the temperature enhancement effect being adjustable by modifying the material and physical parameters of the configuration. The analytical expression for the temperature sensitivity coefficient of this proposed sensor was derived, and the accuracy of the analytical model and the viability of the sensor were validated through finite element simulations and experimental testing. Additionally, the variables in the sensitivity coefficient expression were transformed into dimensionless form to improve the model’s engineering applicability. A Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) model was employed to capture the complex nonlinear relationship between the temperature sensitivity coefficient and the dimensionless variables. Results demonstrate that the theoretical temperature sensitivity coefficient closely matches the finite element simulation results, with overall errors remaining within 5 %. The temperature sensing experiments confirmed a significant enhancement in sensitivity, achieving a temperature sensitivity up to 18 times higher than that of the bare fiber under laboratory conditions. The MLP model successfully captured the relationship between the sensitivity coefficient and dimensionless variables. Finally, a graphical user interface (GUI) tool was developed for sensor design and optimization, and a comprehensive technical framework for structural temperature monitoring and early warning was proposed.

title: Time-shift multivariate multiscale link dispersion entropy: a novel health indicator for multivariate signal processing-driven aeroengine fault diagnosis
abstract: Multivariate multiscale dispersion entropy (MMDE) provides a complexity measure of multichannel signals, facilitating the detection of dynamic variations in mechanical systems. Nevertheless, the method overlooks informative structures within the same scale and fails to capture the temporal evolution of dispersion patterns, thereby limiting its applicability to fault diagnosis. To overcome these shortcomings, this study introduces a time-shift multivariate multiscale link dispersion entropy (TSMMLDE) approach. First, on the basis of time-shift coarse-graining, high-order difference processing is conducted on each time-shift subsequence to extract dynamic features of varying orders. Secondly, phase space reconstruction is performed on the difference sequences to embed temporal dependencies within the dispersion patterns and generate a pattern transition matrix that captures the non-stationary dynamics of the time series. Subsequently, the pattern transition matrices from different channels are superimposed and fused to create a global pattern transition matrix that integrates information from multi-channel signals. Finally, the transition probabilities of dispersion patterns within the global pattern transition matrix are statistically analyzed, and the entropy value is calculated based on Shannon entropy theory. This method not only thoroughly explores the internal characteristics of the time series at the same scale but also effectively captures the pattern evolution laws. Experimental results on simulated signals and three real bearing datasets confirm the effectiveness of TSMMLDE. TSMMLDE achieved 100.00 % accuracy on the Harbin Institute of Technology dataset and high mean accuracies of 99.75 % and 99.49 % on the Politecnico di Torino and drivetrain diagnostic simulator datasets, respectively.
keywords: Time-shift multivariate multiscale link dispersion entropy

title: C-halbach circular array-driven decoupled magnetic isolator: modeling, experiment and torsional vibration isolation performance analysis in rotor system
abstract: For rotating systems, complex internal and external excitations arouse nonlinear high-frequency torsional vibrations, accelerating wear of key transmission components like bearings and gears. Torsional vibration isolation is crucial for ensuring operational stability and reliability of rotating machinery. This study proposes a decoupled magnetic vibration isolator (DMVD) using the clearance-Halbach (C-Halbach) circular array for isolation. The specially developed DMVD achieves vibration isolation through a quasi-orthogonal magnet arrangement, with its optimized configuration enabling low dynamic stiffness and excellent high-frequency isolation performance. Unlike traditional positive–negative stiffness combination methods, this work realizes the DMVD’s constant magnetic torque design, generated by magnetic field distortion, using a fully connected neural network and an optimization algorithm. This mechanism is revealed via detailed magnetic field analysis and validated through finite element simulation. Dynamic models were established for a single-degree-of-freedom rotor system and a multi-degree-of-freedom two-stage gear transmission system to evaluate isolation performance, with experimental validation conducted. Results show that the DMVD exhibits superior wide-frequency decoupled vibration isolation capability, offering a novel alternative for torsional vibration isolation in rotating systems.

title: A physics-guided frequency-domain framework for train load identification with learning-based spectral magnitude priors
abstract: Train loads are the primary excitation source of track structures and underlying infrastructure, and their identification is essential for evaluating structural dynamic performance. However, wheel–rail forces are difficult to measure directly under practical operating conditions, and inferring train loads from structural responses is a typical ill-posed inverse problem that is highly sensitive to noise and modelling errors. To address this issue, this study proposes a physics-guided frequency-domain framework by integrating a spectral forward operator with a learning-based magnitude prior. A physics-based spectral forward operator is constructed from a periodically supported Euler–Bernoulli beam model to characterize the frequency-domain mapping between equivalent wheel–rail forces and rail responses. A learning-based prior is used only to constrain the spectral magnitude envelope, while the mechanics-based operator retains the phase-frequency coupling, enabling the complex force spectrum to be recovered through prior-constrained inversion rather than direct neural-network prediction. Numerical results show that the proposed method can stably reconstruct equivalent wheel–rail forces under different operating conditions and noise levels, and provides better noise robustness than unregularized inversion, sparse regularization, and Tikhonov regularization. Field application further shows that the rail accelerations reconstructed from the identified loads agree well with the measured responses, and that the derived fastener reaction forces exhibit physically reasonable wheel-passage characteristics. These results indicate that the proposed method provides a stable and physically consistent approach for train load reconstruction, vibration source characterization, and dynamic analysis of track structures under practical operating conditions.

title: Parameter identification of a footbridge with adaptive TMD
abstract: To enhance the human-induced vibration mitigation of slender and flexible footbridges, an adaptive tuned mass damper (ATMD) with adjustable mass and eddy current damping is proposed. During long-term use, the mass and stiffness of the TMD may change due to corrosion of the steel and springs, and the frequency of the pedestrian bridge may change as well, causing parameter detuning and compromising control effect. To accurately guide the parameter retuning of TMD, this study utilizes the adjustable mass and damping characteristics of the ATMD and proposes a novel Variable Mass-Fast Independent Component Analysis-Fast Fourier Transform (VM-FastICA-FFT) combined parameter identification algorithm based on ICA and FFT for the ATMD-footbridge coupling system. This parameter identification algorithm can identify the mass, stiffness coefficient of the TMD, and calculate the natural frequency of the main structure under random excitation. The accuracy of the proposed coupled system identification algorithm, the self-tuning function of the ATMD, and its enhanced control performance of vertical human-induced vibrations are validated via both finite element simulations and a steel footbridge model test.

title: Condition-aware cross-device diagnosis for wind turbines under multi-modal heterogeneity
abstract: Cross-device fault diagnosis of wind turbines remains challenging in practice because highly dynamic operating envelopes coexist with heterogeneous vibration and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) evidence, jointly inducing severe cross-turbine distribution discrepancy. Systematic deployment-oriented validation remains limited, and implicit alignment dominated by single-modality evidence is often adopted, leaving cross-modal complementarity insufficiently exploited. In this context, representation drift induced by complex operating conditions and channel/layout inconsistency weakens the consistency between vibration cues and SCADA operating context. To address these issues, a condition-aware, calibration-guided multi-modal cross-device adaptation framework, MMCDA-FS, is proposed. A spectro-contextual unified backbone is first constructed to organize heterogeneous multi-source observations into condition-conditioned transferable embeddings. An interpretable condition-guided channel bridge is then introduced to compensate channel/layout inconsistency. Finally, calibration-aware dual-network refinement is designed within the aligned space to suppress error accumulation and stabilize target-side inference. On two cross-device benchmarks, overall accuracies of 96.49% and 99.37% are achieved, respectively, with clear advantages over representative baselines and ablation-verified gains in calibration, stability, and interpretable alignment.

title: A physics-informed framework for online cable force identification and Bayesian corrosion-fatigue life updating of stay cables
abstract: To address the need for cable force identification and fatigue life assessment of in-service stay cables under long-term structural health monitoring, this study proposes a monitoring-informed framework that integrates time-varying frequency extraction, rapid cable force identification, corrosion-fatigue damage evaluation, and Bayesian life updating. First, based on multi-year monitoring data from the Qingzhou Channel Bridge of the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge, the amplitude and phase estimation of a sinusoid method is employed to extract time-varying frequencies from cable acceleration responses. A dynamic-stiffness-guided micro physics-informed neural network (µDS-PINN) is then developed for rapid and accurate identification of time-varying cable forces. Second, based on time-varying stress data and combined with wind speed and temperature, a corrosion-fatigue coupled damage model is established. Finally, a Bayesian life updating model is developed to update the intercept parameter of the S–N curve posteriorly, thereby quantifying the remaining life distribution and failure probability. The results show that µDS-PINN significantly improves cable force identification efficiency while maintaining high accuracy, meeting the demand for rapid identification in long-term online monitoring scenarios. The proposed life prediction method enables probabilistic characterization of remaining life and failure risk. Long-term monitoring results show distinct cable-to-cable differences in daily fatigue damage, and the remaining life obtained through online updating is significantly negatively correlated with daily fatigue damage, demonstrating that the proposed method can continuously revise life prediction results as damage accumulates. This study provides a practical basis for fatigue state tracking, life management, and risk warning of in-service stay cables.

title: Novel non-contact adjustable torsional electromagnetic negative stiffness device: Theoretical analysis and application
abstract: To address the issue that traditional quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) torsional vibration isolation systems struggle to adapt to time-varying loads due to their fixed structural parameters, this paper proposes a novel non-contact adjustable torsional electromagnetic negative stiffness device (ATENSD). Through the axial electromagnetic coupling between the iron-core coils and the permanent magnets, the ATENSD can generate rotational negative stiffness which can be dynamically adjusted by regulating the current of the iron-core coil. Firstly, the fundamental configuration of the ATENSD is introduced, and the principle of its variable negative stiffness is analyzed. Subsequently, electromagnetic finite element analysis are employed to elucidate the influence of the permanent magnet shape, the permanent magnet thickness, the pole-pair number and the magnetic-pole angle on the ATENSD stiffness characteristics, for guiding the prototype design. Moreover, the analytical electromagnetic-force model of the ATENSD is established by the magnetic energy method. And a comparative analysis is then conducted to examine the influence laws of the control current and the air gap on the electromagnetic torque and stiffness characteristics of the ATENSD. Finally, stiffness characterization experiments and vibration transmission test experiments are conducted on the ATENSD prototype. The results demonstrate that the designed ATENSD achieves continuously adjustable negative stiffness with good linearity during current regulation. And the QZS adjustable electromagnetic torsional isolator (QZS-AETI), integrated with the ATENSD, has a good vibration transmission suppression effect across the entire frequency range.

title: Restoring force modeling of preloaded metal rubber pairs (PMRP) considering component asymmetry for nonlinear vibration analysis
abstract: As a high-performance damping material widely used in extreme environments, metal rubber (MR) is typically employed in the form of preloaded metal rubber pairs (PMRP) in practical engineering. However, most existing PMRP restoring force models require experimental testing and parameter fitting after the entire assembly is manufactured, essentially representing an empirical description. This makes it difficult to directly predict the hysteretic behavior of PMRP under various preload parameters based on the basic material properties of MR blocks during the design stage. To address this, this paper proposes a PMRP restoring force model based on a modified Iwan model. By accurately characterizing the non-monotonic nature of the preloading assembly process and the component asymmetry between the upper and lower MR blocks caused by manufacturing variability, this model establishes a calculation method for the asymmetric equilibrium state after preloading, thereby extending the traditional material-level constitutive model to assembly-level hysteretic performance prediction. This method achieves high-precision prediction of the hysteretic behavior of the assembled PMRP based solely on the experimental parameters of individual MR blocks (with a coefficient of determination greater than 0.97). On this basis, the influence mechanism of preload parameters on the dynamic hysteretic characteristics of PMRP is quantitatively analyzed. The results indicate that increasing the design pre-compression displacement leads to a monotonic increase in equivalent stiffness, while the equivalent damping ratio exhibits a non-monotonic variation of increasing first and then decreasing. Meanwhile, increasing the maximum pre-compression displacement can effectively suppress the asymmetry of the hysteretic response caused by component performance differences. Finally, through frequency sweep vibration tests on an integrated vibration isolation device, the applicability of the model in broadband vibration analysis and its high-precision prediction capability for the nonlinear equivalent stiffness of complex structures are verified. The research results demonstrate that this model can not only accurately characterize the nonlinear hysteretic properties of PMRP but also provide an effective theoretical tool for the performance prediction and design optimization of related vibration isolation devices.

title: An enhanced method for instantaneous angular speed accuracy improvement and its application in variable-speed scenarios
abstract: Tacholess speed estimation serves as a powerful preprocessing method for condition monitoring of variable-speed machinery in scenarios where speed reference sensors are unavailable. However, for a mono amplitude modulated (AM)-frequency modulated (FM) signal contaminated by background noise, the instantaneous frequency (IF) retrieved via phase demodulation tends to fluctuate around its theoretical value. In this study, we first derive the influence of three key factors—carrier signal amplitude, amplitude modulation characteristics, and background noise variance—on the fluctuation (i.e., variance) of the estimated IF. Based on this theoretical insight, instantaneous angular speed (IAS) estimates derived from all vibration harmonics, together with their corresponding instantaneous IAS variance, can be estimated from the vibration signal. The optimal IAS estimate is then obtained by leveraging the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) framework. Accordingly, this study proposes an enhanced IAS accuracy improvement (EIASAI) method for iterative refinement of IAS estimation accuracy. The efficacy of the proposed method is evaluated and benchmarked against existing state-of-the-art methods using both numerical simulations and vibration signals collected from operational wind turbines.

title: Resonance response identification and vibration damping analysis of thin-walled spiral bevel gear
abstract: The traveling wave resonance (TWR) of thin-walled bevel gears in the aviation field continues to pose a significant threat to the overall system’s operational health. Despite extensive research on TWR, the method for determining critical dynamic stress for additional vibration reduction measures remains unclear, and a comprehensive method for predicting the damping effects of supplementary dampers is still lacking. This paper proposes a method for determining the allowable dynamic stress and establishes a single modal forced response (SMFR) model to predict the vibration damping effects of the ring damper. First, the allowable dynamic stress is determined by combining the gear material’s fatigue life curve with the Goodman curve. Using the SMFR model and experimental results, the modal damping ratio and resonance dynamic stress (RDS) at different points can be obtained. The frictional energy dissipation of the ring damper is analyzed to refine the SMFR model, considering the influence of structural parameters of the damper. Additionally, the damping effect is evaluated, accounting for wear between the damper and the gear, providing a solid foundation for the damper’s design. A series of tests, including continuous speed-up tests and speed hold-rise tests, are conducted to identify the TWR speed points and RDS within the working speed range. The dynamic stress reduction within the ring damper is then obtained through both the SMFR model and experimental data. The results show a maximum RDS reduction of over 60 %, with a dynamic stress prediction error of less than 13 %, thus confirming the effectiveness of the proposed model.

title: A Physics-Guided adversarial compensation framework for the dynamic viscoelastic errors in flexible pressure sensors
abstract: Limited by the intrinsic viscoelasticity of flexible material systems, the output signals of flexible pressure sensors exhibit strong time dependence. This time dependence gives rise to phase lag and energy dissipation under dynamic loading, which severely degrade dynamic sensing performance. To mitigate these dynamic viscoelastic errors, we propose a knowledge-informed intelligent compensation framework based on a Physics-guided Adversarial Compensation Network (PACN). Built on a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), the PACN framework jointly enforces data fidelity, physical consistency and structural realism by integrating physical constraints with time–frequency structural constraints. Specifically, the total compensation term is decomposed into multiple first-order dynamic branches, embedding interpretable prior knowledge about multi-time-scale viscoelastic behavior. In parallel, a time–frequency dual-branch discriminator is further introduced to constrain local waveform realism and global spectral consistency, thereby suppressing structural distortion during compensation. On a regular micro-structured flexible pressure sensor, the PACN framework achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 0.0179, outperforming physical, machine learning, and baseline deep learning models. The framework also maintains strong generalization under single-frequency and mixed-frequency conditions and remains effective for an irregular micro-structured flexible pressure sensor. These results indicate that PACN framework provides an effective knowledge-informed method for compensating dynamic viscoelastic errors in flexible pressure sensors.

title: Autocorrelation weighted enhanced envelope spectrum for compound bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Early-stage bearing faults typically exhibit cyclostationary characteristic, spectral coherence (SCoh) is an effective method for analyzing such signals. However, conventional SCoh methods are primarily designed for single fault diagnosis and focus mainly on identifying the fault frequency bands, while neglecting the enhancement of periodic fault characteristics in compound fault diagnosis. To address this limitation, a novel autocorrelation weighted enhanced envelope spectrum (AWEES) method is proposed by taking advantage of autocorrelation in estimating periodicity for the diagnosis of bearing compound faults. First, a periodic peak feature extraction strategy is introduced. The squared autocorrelation function (SAF) of the coherence spectrum is computed to estimate the periodic features across all spectral frequencies, the estimated periodicities and their harmonics are used to construct a periodic peak feature matrix (PPFM), which is employed to reinforce the periodic compound fault features within the coherence spectrum, yielding an enhanced coherence spectrum. Furthermore, an estimated frequency domain signal-to-noise ratio (EFDSNR) is calculated to characterize the distribution of compound fault energy based on the estimated periodic features, and an optimal threshold is applied to determine the frequency bands associated with the compound faults. Finally, the AWEES is calculated by weighting and fusing the compound fault frequency bands with the EFDSNR. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using simulated signals, run-to-failure axle-box bearing compound fault data, and wheelset bearing compound fault data, with comparisons against several novel methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can suppress broadband noise, enhance and accurately extract periodic compound fault features, and reliably diagnose weak early-stage compound faults.

title: A novel low-intervention blade tip micro-Doppler vibration measurement method to avoid undersampling
abstract: Blade vibration monitoring of aero-engines is crucial for ensuring the structural safety and healthy operation of aircraft. Existing non-contact measurement methods, constrained by their inherent principles, generally suffer from high invasiveness and undersampling issues. To address this problem, this paper proposes a novel Blade Tip Micro-Doppler Measurement (BTMM) technology. This technique employs a single microwave sensor, which features a wide field of view and dense measurement points, to acquire echo data that complies with the Nyquist sampling theorem. By leveraging the blade tip micro-Doppler characteristics contained in the data, it achieves low-cost and high-precision estimation of blade vibration parameters. Firstly, the analytical expressions of the blade tip micro-Doppler signals under pure rotation and rotation-vibration coupling conditions are derived, theoretically verifying that blade vibration characteristics are coupled in these signals. Secondly, a complete measurement algorithm framework is established based on theoretical derivation. To tackle the problems of limited signal data volume and energy leakage prone to occur in time-frequency analysis, a sliding time-frequency window decoupling algorithm and an energy-weighted ridge extraction algorithm are proposed, which are suitable for the frequency extraction of blade tip micro-Doppler signals. Finally, simulations and experiments validate that the single sensor can accurately extract the rotational frequency and vibration frequency of the blisk under both rotation and rotation-vibration coupling conditions. The results demonstrate that the BTMM technology can accurately and efficiently identify blade vibration parameters, serving as a new non-contact, low-intervention, and undersampling-free method for aero-engine blade vibration monitoring.

title: A cyclostationarity-guided adaptive mode decomposition theory for enhancing compound fault detectability in rotating machinery
abstract: Compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery under strong background noise remains a critical challenge in industrial applications. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cyclostationarity-guided adaptive mode decomposition theory, namely cyclostationary modulation mode decomposition (CSMMD), for enhancing compound fault detectability. CSMMD constructs a mode decomposition framework driven by the intrinsic cyclostationary properties of fault signals, which strengthens spectral correlation/coherence analysis with adaptive feature localization and enhancement. First, the indicator of cyclic frequency intensity (CFI) is designed to aggregate cyclostationary information across spectral frequencies, enabling robust identification of multiple fault-related cyclic frequencies without requiring exact FCFs or a preset mode number as direct inputs. Then, optimal integration bands for each fault are flexibly delineated by analyzing CFI distribution to avoid limitations of fixed spectral segmentation. Finally, cyclostationary amplitude modulation guided by the estimated cyclic frequency is proposed to nonlinearly enhance fault-related components, which further improves the signal-to-noise ratio of fault features. Comprehensive validations of simulated and experimental analyses demonstrate the effectiveness of CSMMD for multi-interference rotating machinery compound fault signal, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods in fault feature extraction and achieves a balance between computational efficiency and diagnostic precision. This work provides a feasible technical solution for robust compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery in complex industrial environments.

title: Analysis of local fault coupling mechanism and dynamic response characteristics in dual-rotor system
abstract: Dual-rotor systems, the core load-bearing components of aero-engines, are susceptible to typical faults such as flange bolt loosening and localized surface defects on rolling element bearings under extreme operating conditions. Investigating their dynamic behaviors and fault coupling mechanisms under multi-fault conditions is of critical engineering and theoretical significance for aero-engine operational reliability. In this work, high-pressure (HP) and low-pressure (LP) rotor dynamic models are established based on the Euler-Bernoulli and Timoshenko beam theories respectively, with fault effects incorporated into the system as equivalent macroscopic excitation forces. The proposed multi-fault coupling model is validated against experimental data, and systematic full-speed-range numerical analyses are carried out via MATLAB simulations. Results show that flange bolt loosening significantly amplifies vibration responses in the downward direction across the entire speed range. Bearing defects mainly induce pronounced vibration at low speeds and widen the chaotic motion speed range in the low-speed regime. The two faults exhibit an overall positive coupling effect with localized negative coupling zones: at low-to-intermediate speeds, negative coupling is dominated by the Hertzian contact stiffness hardening effect; at medium-to-high speeds, intensified differential motion between bearing inner and outer races causes localized reverse impacts from rolling elements passing through the defect region, which act jointly with the progressively enhanced Hertzian stiffness hardening effect to trigger the localized negative coupling phenomenon. This study provides theoretical support for enriching rotating machinery fault dynamics theory.

title: Design and vibration reduction characteristics of a hollow multi-chambered particle-damped milling cutter inspired by the lotus root structure
abstract: Chatter vibration in milling adversely affects machining stability, surface integrity, and tool life, especially in lightweight or slender tool systems. To enhance vibration suppression while retaining structural lightweight potential, this study proposes a lotus-root-inspired multi-chambered particle-damped milling cutter (LRMC), in which a biomimetic hollow multi-cavity architecture is integrated with distributed particle damping. An energy analysis model was developed by considering structural damping, particle-particle and particle-wall collision dissipation, and interparticle friction dissipation. Geometric morphology margin and constrained-scale margin were introduced to describe the effects of cavity shape, particle diameter, filling ratio, and particle mobility on energy dissipation. Static impact tests and dynamic milling experiments were conducted to evaluate LRMCs with different particle filling ratios. The results show that particle filling significantly improves the dynamic behavior of the hollow multi-chambered cutter by suppressing modal compliance and broadband vibration response. Among the tested configurations, the 36.8%-filled LRMC exhibits the best overall vibration reduction performance, reducing the primary modal peak compliance by 80.5% compared with the empty LRMC and reducing high-frequency acceleration RMS by 50.2%-64.5% compared with the solid toolholder during milling. Acoustic emission analysis further confirms improved cutting stability, with RMS reductions of 27.6%-43.6% relative to the solid toolholder. These findings demonstrate that the lotus-root-inspired particle-damped structure provides an effective strategy for developing lightweight milling cutters with enhanced vibration suppression and machining stability.

title: Fusing multi-sensor data in graph convolutional networks for robust structural damage detection against environmental and operational variations
abstract: In structural health monitoring, environmental and operational variations (EOVs), along with extreme class imbalance in damage severity datasets, substantially compromise damage detection accuracy and reliability. To address these challenges, a collaborative node-edge graph convolutional network (CNEGCN) is proposed for structural damage detection, incorporating advanced feature extraction, node-edge co-embedding, and a physics-informed loss formulation. First, a reference signal reconstruction method combined with wavelet coherence is developed to extract features sensitive to structural damage while remaining robust to environmental variations. Second, a network architecture employing collaborative node-edge embedding is constructed to effectively fuse heterogeneous multi-location sensor data, specifically acceleration and strain measurements. Finally, a two-stage training scheme transitioning from conventional cross-entropy loss to a physics-informed multiple damage location assurance criterion loss is implemented to mitigate overfitting on minority damage classes. Validated across three experimental and numerical cases of varying complexity, the proposed CNEGCN demonstrates stable classification performance and strong robustness to noise and EOVs, achieving classification accuracies exceeding 0.98 and competitive Macro F1 scores. The proposed CNEGCN offers an efficient online diagnostic solution for real-time structural damage monitoring under complex environmental conditions.

title: Mechanism of dynamic response amplification of ropeway cables: Numerical and experimental investigation
abstract: Cables are used in many engineering applications, including transport systems in which mobile cables suspended between supports are used to move attached vehicles. Such systems are prone to self-sustained, high-amplitude oscillations owing to their intrinsic nonlinear nature and the evolution of their dynamic characteristics during steady-state operation. A framework is therefore needed to understand the influence of design parameters on dynamic behaviour and to predict oscillation amplitudes. This paper presents a mechanical model of ropeway cable dynamics, enabling extraction of the modal content and incorporation of nonlinearities. An experimental investigation is then carried out on a real chairlift case study through field measurements, combining video analysis and on-site sensor data, to characterise the dynamic amplification phenomena and the hierarchy of mechanical couplings between the vehicles, the drive system, and the cable. Finally, a transient simulation is performed based on modal decomposition and a reduced-order dynamic model, incorporating parametric excitation induced by cable tension variations, geometric nonlinearities, and nonlinear coupling between the pumping mode and the out-of-plane mode. A test/simulation comparison is conducted for model updating and calibration. The main contributions of this study are: (i) an analysis of the coupled mechanisms underlying the onset of cable pumping based on field measurements; (ii) a coupled multi-span dynamic modelling framework for ropeway cable loops capturing vertical-longitudinal modal interactions under operational conditions; (iii) a reduced-order model built from a pumping-mode subspace enabling nonlinear transient simulations; (iv) surrogate parameters accounting for unmodelled coupling effects such as cable torsion, vehicle swaying, and bullwheel drive dynamics; and (v) experimental calibration and model updating based on in-situ measurements of cable pumping.

title: Investigation into the dynamic behaviour of rotors supported on starved bearings
abstract: This paper presents an experimental and numerical investigation of rotor vibration when a cylindrical journal bearing experiences oil starvation. The primary goals are to enhance the current available experimental data and provide a detailed comparison between starvation models based on experimentally measured rotor vibration responses. A dedicated test rig equipped with two active magnetic bearings was used to levitate and accurately position the rotor shaft at controlled eccentricities, allowing stable and repeatable testing across a broad range of operating conditions. A single hydrodynamic bearing was mounted on the rig, and lubricant flow was progressively reduced to induce starvation. Shaft displacements were measured and thoroughly characterized in time and frequency domains. The experimental results revealed an increase in synchronous vibration under starvation, mainly in a backward whirl component. A low-amplitude, broadband subsynchronous vibration (SSV) was also observed, which is reported as a new rotordynamic feature associated with oil film instability in cylindrical bearings. Numerical simulations were performed using a mass-conserving starvation model with two different inlet boundary conditions: prescribed inlet oil fraction and prescribed inlet flow rate. The results demonstrate that the models produce a distinctive pressure distribution, hence, a different rotor response. The inlet oil fraction boundary condition showed the best agreement with the measurements.

title: Optimal instantaneous frequency fusion for estimating instantaneous angular speed in wind turbine gearboxes
abstract: The Instantaneous Angular Speed (IAS) estimation method, which employs time-frequency analysis, is widely used for its cost-effectiveness and adaptability in directly estimating IAS from the vibration signal’s time-frequency spectrum. However, traditional time-frequency analysis demands a harmonic that consistently maintains a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and aligns with the shaft’s rotational frequency throughout the sampling period, which significantly restricts its practical applicability and reliability. This limitation becomes pronounced under the complex operational conditions of wind turbines, where Instantaneous Frequencies (IFs) with high SNR in the collected vibration signals may not correspond to the shaft’s rotational frequency. Additionally, interference from strong colored noise, cross-frequencies, transient harmonics, and significant damping resonances complicates the extraction process. Thus, extracting IFs that correlate with the shaft’s rotational frequency and maintain high SNR is essential for accurate IAS estimation. This paper presents a novel Optimal Instantaneous Frequency Fusion (OIFF) method for IAS estimation. It consolidates all pertinent information related to the shaft’s rotational frequency from the vibration signals to create a time-frequency distribution with enhanced energy concentration. Initially, the method employs a fundamental component detection technique to identify the frequency band. It then applies an optimal IF extraction and fusion strategy to develop the optimal product spectrum, effectively mitigating the impact of various interfering signals. The corresponding IAS is subsequently extracted and smoothed. The proposed OIFF method capitalizes on the comprehensive information within the vibration signals, ensuring high accuracy of IAS estimation in various application scenarios. The method’s effectiveness, superiority, and real-world reliability are demonstrated through analyses of simulation data, three experimental datasets, and an extensive vibration dataset from wind turbine gearboxes under actual operating conditions.

title: Shuffle attention-driven multi-sensor information fusion network for simultaneous identification of multiple coupler forces in heavy-haul locomotives
abstract: Intensified longitudinal impulse significantly shortens the service life of critical locomotive components, threatening heavy-haul train operational safety. While coupler force monitoring is crucial for evaluating train longitudinal impulse levels, traditional strain gauge-based direct measurement methods suffer from poor long-term stability and complex calibration. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MCFI-Net, a novel multi-sensor information fusion network for the indirect identification of multiple coupler forces in heavy-haul locomotives by integrating coupler displacement with car-body vibration acceleration signals. A decomposed large-kernel attention block (DLKAB) is first introduced for primary feature extraction, effectively capturing global and local feature dependencies while reducing parameter overhead. Tailored to the heterogeneous properties of displacement and acceleration signals, multi-scale depthwise dilated convolution (DWDConv) and depthwise convolution (DWConv) are specifically designed for modality-specific feature modeling. These features are further refined by a channel-aware multi-branch reweighting (C-MBR) module for adaptive intra-modality weighting. Subsequently, a hierarchical shuffle attention (HSA) mechanism is developed to facilitate cross-modality information interaction, effectively suppressing noise and enhancing the representation of task-relevant features. Finally, a pointwise convolution (PWConv)-based decoder maps the high-level features to multiple coupler force estimations. Extensive experiments on field-measured data demonstrate that MCFI-Net consistently achieves superior identification accuracy and strong robustness to noise. Our approach thus provides a promising solution for the simultaneous monitoring of multiple coupler forces in heavy-haul locomotives.

title: Physics-inspired graph fusion and reinforcement learning agent for unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis
abstract: The reliable operation and accurate fault diagnosis of machinery under complex, varying operating conditions are crucial to the safety and reliability of industrial systems. However, existing unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis methods still suffer from limitations in modeling sample relationship topology and domain alignment. Physical information is difficult to integrate effectively with data-correlation features, and the dynamic domain alignment process lacks adaptive regulation. To address these issues, an embodied intelligence motivated physics-inspired graph fusion and reinforcement learning-based domain adaptation (PIFRLDA) method is proposed. First, a physics-inspired residual gated graph fusion mechanism is designed to construct an adaptive topology. It builds a physics-inspired graph in a latent dynamic space and adaptively fuses it with the data-driven graph through residual gating, thereby preserving sample relationships while introducing weak dynamics-related guidance into cross-condition feature interaction. A dual-path transformer sample-and-aggregate graph network is developed on the constructed graph to capture within-sample feature interactions and cross-sample topological relationships, thereby enhancing adaptability to structural correlations under complex conditions. In addition, a dual-agent cooperative domain adaptation framework is introduced to jointly optimize sample selection and feature perturbation, improving dynamic perception and adaptive regulation under varying operating conditions. Experimental results show that, compared with existing advanced unsupervised fault diagnosis methods, the proposed method offers significant advantages in both diagnostic accuracy and cross-condition generalization.

title: Investigation on whole-engine coupled dynamic response and load transmission characteristics of high-bypass turbofan engines
abstract: Accurate prediction of the externally transmitted loads induced by sudden unbalance following Fan Blade Off (FBO) remains challenging for high-bypass-ratio turbofan engines. To address this issue, a whole-engine mechanical model incorporating mounting structures and cross-interface dynamic coupling was developed to investigate load transmission and its influence on system dynamic responses. In this study, “whole-engine” refers to the system-level load-transmission path represented by the scaled rotor test rig. The rig includes the low-pressure rotor, supports, casing, and mounting nodes but excludes the high-pressure rotor and inter-rotor coupling. First, elastic supports, load-carrying struts, and related support structures were coupled in series to formulate coupled support elements, based on which a finite-element model of the low-pressure rotor–coupled support–casing–mounting-interface system was established. Second, a scaled test rig with functionally representative mounting-interface boundary conditions was constructed, and the model was validated by comparing the predicted and measured vibration responses and transmitted loads under FBO conditions. The transient responses under different FBO conditions were subsequently investigated, and the effects of support-induced buffering and strong mounting constraints on radial transient-load transmission were clarified. For the six FBO conditions validated in this study, the model-prediction errors for the transient vibration responses and transmitted loads are all below 10%. The sudden-unbalance response exhibited pronounced modal dependence, while the self-centering effect at supercritical speeds attenuated the higher-order harmonic responses following FBO. The transient load varied non-monotonically as it propagated radially outward through the system, initially decreasing and subsequently increasing. These results provide theoretical and experimental support for system-level dynamic analysis, transmitted-load prediction, and structural safety design of aero-engines under FBO conditions.

title: Integrated actuation-sensing system to enhance vibration stability in ultrasonic-assisted processing with in-situ monitoring
abstract: The ultrasonic-assisted machining (UAM) can provide significant advantages for improving surface quality and enhancing the machinability of difficult-to-cut materials. The stability of vibration amplitude in UAM is crucial for influencing machining behavior. However, achieving high-precision and robust vibration amplitude control during machining process still remains challenging. To address this, an integrated actuation-sensing system is proposed. The annular piezoelectric ceramic is embedded into the ultrasonic transducer as a self-sensing unit. Integrated vibration excitation and amplitude sensing are thus enabled. Then, a modular system architecture is developed. It comprises scalable power amplification and independent signal processing modules. The system load capacity is enhanced. Each functional unit remains independent with standardized interfaces. This facilitates optimization and functional expansion. The amplitude stability during machining is validated by an in-situ monitoring method. The in-situ method is implemented using the high-speed imaging and digital image correlation (DIC). The system response is evaluated on a drop-hammer cutting load test platform. The self-sensing system can achieve stable vibration regulation without frequency scanning. A constant frequency above the series resonance is used. The reduced amplitude fluctuation and better disturbance rejection under load disturbances are exhibited compared with indirect electrical-parameter feedback and open-loop control. The cutting experiments were performed on TC4 titanium alloy. The stable vibration was maintained across various cutting speeds while the improved surface morphology was achieved. The enhanced uniformity and cyclicity of surface textures were also obtained. This work provides a reliable approach for high-stability control and vibration signal acquisition in UAM systems. It is beneficial for the further elucidation of UAM mechanisms.

title: Corrigendum to “Directional coupling analysis and vibration control for transport vehicles with air suspensions based on a matrix decomposition framework” [Mech. Syst. Sign. Proc. 259 (2026) 1–26/114826]
Two-scale concurrent structural topology optimization for transient wave energy-flow control
abstract: Structural energy-flow control enables functionalities such as vibration shielding and energy harvesting, and is of great significance in fields such as aerospace engineering, precision instrumentation, and rail transportation. However, structural design methods for achieving prescribed energy-flow control functionalities remain underexplored. This study proposes a two-scale concurrent topology optimization method for transient wave energy-flow control. To achieve different energy-flow control functionalities, three representative optimization objectives are considered: energy-flow blocking, energy-flow focusing, and zigzag energy-flow routing. The expression for transient energy-flow is derived from the differential form of energy conservation. To suppress the influence of boundary reflections, a Laplace-equation-based absorbing boundary condition is formulated. In the proposed two-scale topology optimization framework, the effective elasticity matrix of the microstructure is evaluated based on the homogenization theory. At the microscopic scale, inter-microstructure connectivity constraints, together with virtual-temperature-based connectivity constraints, are introduced for single-material topology optimization, thereby ensuring the manufacturability of the optimized designs. To obtain diverse optimized configurations, the initial designs are generated using random morphology description functions (RMDFs). In the numerical examples, both bi-material and single-material optimization results are presented for the three optimization objectives. The results show that energy-flow tends to propagate along the direction of maximum stiffness, while the impedance mismatch between different microstructures also affects its propagation direction. These findings suggest that the proposed method has potential applications in structural vibration control, energy dissipation, and energy harvesting.

title: From sparse measurements to probabilistic solution manifolds: an FCWV inverse framework for parameter identification and full-field reconstruction
abstract: Strongly nonlinear and underdetermined inverse problems commonly arise in structural health monitoring, model updating, and deformation reconstruction, where sparse measurements may correspond to multiple admissible parameter combinations. This work presents a probabilistic finite cell weight variation (FCWV)-based inverse framework capable of reconstructing full admissible solution manifolds together with their associated probability distributions. The formulation is derived from the conservation law of probability and the transformation law of probability density, and recursively decomposes a multi-dimensional inverse problem into coupled one-dimensional searches. In this way, admissible solution manifolds can be identified efficiently without reliance on large-scale global optimization or extensive Bayesian sampling. The framework is developed for multi-input, multi-output systems and extended to higher-dimensional inverse problems through a recursive sampling strategy. Two benchmark examples are considered. The first involves identification of unknown parameters in a nonlinear analytical leak-rate model for a cracked pipe using prescribed leak-rate measurements, where the inverse formulation is validated against direct uncertainty propagation. The second considers a beam-element piping system under seismic excitation, in which six unknown support stiffnesses are identified from prescribed target displacement responses at a node, using a surrogate response model constructed from finite element simulations. In both examples, the proposed method successfully reconstructs admissible solution manifolds and quantifies the relative likelihood of competing solutions. The results demonstrate that the FCWV-based inverse framework provides an efficient and physically transparent alternative for solving strongly nonlinear and underdetermined inverse problems with sparse measurements.

title: Parameter identification and unknown excitation inversion of piezoelectric cantilever beams using multi-network PINNs with Fourier feature mapping
abstract: Constructing a highly accurate multiphysics coupling model is a fundamental prerequisite for advancing piezoelectric energy harvesting systems from theoretical design to practical engineering applications. However, in real engineering scenarios, external excitations are often uncertain, and key system parameters, such as mass, stiffness, and damping ratio, are easily affected by operating conditions, leading to significant deviations from their theoretical design values. Conventional system identification methods strongly rely on known external excitations and stationary operating assumptions, and therefore are difficult to apply to piezoelectric systems with time-varying parameter uncertainty and complex oscillatory dynamic responses. As a result, identification failure and insufficient accuracy are commonly encountered in practice. To address these challenges, a multi-network-structure physics-informed neural network (PINNs) method embedded with temporal Fourier feature mapping is proposed in this study. The proposed method improves the representation capability of the multiphysics model for oscillatory responses and local temporal details, thereby enabling accurate identification of key parameters and inversion of unknown excitation forces in piezoelectric systems. Numerical results show that, under free vibration, sinusoidal excitation, and random excitation conditions, the relative errors of the identified equivalent mass, equivalent stiffness, and equivalent damping ratio are all less than 5%. In addition, the unknown excitation force can also be accurately inverted. The proposed method demonstrates satisfactory identification accuracy and robustness, and can provide effective methodological support for high-precision modeling and practical design of piezoelectric energy harvesting systems.

title: Physics-guided Siamese tracker for robust vision-based structural displacement monitoring under visibility degradation
abstract: The vision-based structural displacement monitoring technique has significant potential for structural health monitoring (SHM). However, its field applications are severely limited due to reduced target visibility caused by factors such as occlusion, fog, and light changes. To address these challenges, this paper presents a robust vision-based displacement monitoring framework named CP-SiamRPN. It makes use of an enhanced deep Siamese network architecture, along with a physical consistency mechanism to eliminate non-physical drift and a confidence-guided mechanism to quantify tracking uncertainty and adjust parameters accordingly. In contrast to existing deep learning-based methods, the proposed framework has zero-shot generalization capabilities, which enable deployment on new target instances without target-specific retraining or fine-tuning. This is particularly valuable for reliable structural displacement monitoring of diverse target types under traffic or environmental interference. Systematic validation has been conducted by impact testing on simply supported beams, shake table testing on five-story frame structures, and field monitoring of bridges. The results demonstrate that, under the visibility-degradation scenarios examined (occlusion, illumination variation, and progressive blur), the proposed method maintains accurate displacement measurement and provides an explicit indicator of tracking reliability.

title: Integrated physics-informed and unsupervised learning assessment of hemp-reinforced masonry barrel vaults under shaking table testing
abstract: The seismic assessment of strengthened masonry vaults through full-scale shaking-table testing remains limited, particularly for sustainable, heritage-compatible systems. This study investigates the dynamic response and damage evolution of full-scale masonry barrel vaults strengthened with a hemp-mesh biocomposite embedded in a cocciopesto matrix. A two-phase experimental campaign was carried out on two geometrically identical vaults subjected to progressively scaled three-component earthquake records, enabling the analysis of three representative structural configurations: unreinforced, newly reinforced, and damaged-then-reinforced. Reinforcement effectiveness and damage progression were assessed through a multi-indicator framework combining modal parameters with two proposed indicators: an energy-based indicator derived from Arias intensity and an autoencoder-based indicator. Each is formulated in a baseline-relative (excitation-dependent) form and in an input-normalized form where the energy-based indicator is normalized by the Arias intensity of the input and the autoencoder-based indicator by the squared RMS of the input. It follows that the input-normalized indicators isolate structural regime transitions from the excitation amplitude growth. Results show that the reinforcement, in both newly reinforced and damaged-then-reinforced configurations, enhances seismic capacity and damage tolerance, with delayed damage onset and reduced stiffness degradation. The proposed indicators consistently captured structural regime transitions and damage evolution across all configurations, showing strong agreement with modal trends. In particular, energy-based indicators provide a straightforward signal-level description of regime changes, while the feature-based autoencoder approach proves effective in detecting subtle statistical deviations that may precede visible damage, confirming its effectiveness in tracking stiffness degradation and nonlinear structural response.

title: Latent dynamics-based reconstruction of large gaps in vehicle responses of stationary vehicle-bridge systems
abstract: Accurately reconstructing signals with large gaps has long been a challenge in bridge health monitoring. Therefore, a signal reconstruction method integrating bidirectional deep Koopman and Singular Spectrum Analysis (BiDK-SSA) is proposed. In stationary vehicle-bridge interaction (SVBI) systems, BiDK-SSA reconstructs large gaps in a single-channel vehicle response using only its limited observations. First, observations on both sides of the gap are mapped into a latent space to learn forward and backward linear operators. Subsequently, forward and backward predictions are generated from both gap boundaries and fused by distance-based linear weighting to mitigate cumulative propagation error. Finally, the preliminary reconstructed response is further refined via singular value decomposition and truncation to obtain the final reconstructed response. Numerical results indicate that at an SNR of 30 dB, the vehicle response with a 52% continuous missing rate is effectively reconstructed by the proposed method. Field test results further demonstrate the method’s effectiveness for reconstructing one or multiple large gaps. The reconstructed response can be directly utilized for bridge modal parameter identification without any prior vehicle or bridge information. Furthermore, the proposed method provides a reliable approach for cleaning extreme outliers.

title: Adaptive-orientation phase-based motion estimation for rotational displacement measurement
abstract: In recent years, computer vision-based measurement techniques have experienced rapid development in the field of structural health monitoring (SHM). Among them, phase-based motion estimation (PME), which requires no surface treatment or artificial targets, has attracted increasing attention from the research community. However, conventional PME methods face inherent limitations in handling rotational motions, as the continuously varying motion direction leads to phase wrapping and Gabor filter orientation mismatch. To address this limitations, this paper proposes an Adaptive-Orientation Phase-based Motion Estimation (AOPME) method for accurate and robust rotational displacement measurement. The proposed method exploits the fact that, under high-frame-rate imaging, rotational motion can be decomposed into a sequence of small inter-frame rotations. By adaptively updating the orientation of the Gabor wavelet according to the instantaneous rotation direction, AOPME maintains consistent phase sensitivity and effectively avoids orientation mismatch. An iterative measurement-point update strategy incorporating geometric constraints is further introduced to suppress tracking drift and preserve alignment with structural edges during rotations. The performance of the proposed method is validated through numerical simulations and laboratory experiments. Results demonstrate that AOPME remains robust under varying noise levels and perturbations of the rotation center, confirming its effectiveness and practical applicability for rotational motion measurement.

title: Nonlinear dynamic modeling and experimental validation of rotor drop onto auxiliary bearings in a horizontal AMB system
abstract: Active Magnetic Bearings (AMB) are widely utilized in high-speed rotating machinery due to their frictionless operation, low energy consumption, and controllable stiffness and damping. However, the rotor drops onto auxiliary bearings (AB) caused by AMB overload or failure triggers intense nonlinear impacts and frictional heat accumulation, posing a severe threat to system safety. Current simulations of this process face significant challenges, particularly regarding the numerical stability and accuracy of the dynamic response under nonlinear transient impact conditions. To address these issues, this paper establishes a nonlinear dynamic model of a horizontal AMB-supported rigid rotor-AB system. The elastic hysteresis torque between the rotor and the AB inner race is introduced innovatively, which effectively suppresses the non-physical divergent backward whirl commonly encountered in high-speed simulations, thereby enhancing computational stability. Furthermore, a nonlinear equivalent viscous damping theory is employed to characterize the normal contact force, which is consistent with the physical reality that normal energy is not conserved during the drop impact. A high-stiffness and high-damping linear spring model is proposed for efficient tangential contact force calculation, simplifying the originally complex state-switching logic while balancing computational efficiency and precision. This study provides an effective analytical tool for understanding the dynamic impact behavior of rotor drop, offering significant theoretical value and engineering implications for the design and reliability assessment of AMB protection systems.

title: LCA-PINN: A lightweight condition-aware physics-informed neural network for interpretable tool wear monitoring
abstract: Tool wear monitoring (TWM) is essential to ensuring product quality and sustaining the efficiency of intelligent manufacturing. However, the variability of cutting parameters across different configurations results in significant condition differences, making it difficult to generalize hybrid models built on physical formulas or empirical knowledge for specific conditions to unseen parameter combinations. To address this limitation, a lightweight condition-aware physics-informed neural network (LCA-PINN) is proposed for interpretable TWM under unseen cutting conditions. Specifically, key physical coefficients are dynamically learned by minimizing the residual between the tool wear physics equation and the observed wear. On this basis, a conditional mapping between cutting parameters and physical coefficients is established, enabling adaptive and physically consistent learning across parameter combinations. In addition, a joint data-driven and physics-driven output strategy is employed to estimate tool wear, ensuring accurate monitoring while maintaining physical consistency. Experiments on a full-lifecycle dataset covering a wide range of cutting parameter settings show that, compared with the best-performing baseline, LCA-PINN achieves relative reductions in RMSE, MAE, and MAPE of 36.30%, 34.38%, and 34.57%, respectively, along with an improvement of 2.07% in R2. Moreover, LCA-PINN exhibits favorable complexity, requiring only 5.86 kFLOPs and 23.69 KB memory, meeting the requirements for lightweight deployment in industrial applications. This study offers a feasible pathway to deploying reliable and physically consistent intelligent monitoring in advanced manufacturing environments.

title: Stable vibration: A text-driven conditional diffusion framework for high-fidelity rolling-bearing vibration signal generation
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in generative artificial intelligence (AI) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in synthesizing high-fidelity data across domains. However, their application to vibration signal modeling under realistic operating and acquisition variability remains underexplored. In rolling-bearing monitoring, acquiring vibration signals under varying speeds/loads and measurement conditions is often constrained by strong nonlinearity, low signal-to-noise ratios, and multimodal characteristics, resulting in imbalanced datasets and scarce fault samples. These challenges limit both physics-based simulators (due to heavy parameterization) and existing data-driven generators (due to limited controllability and weak physical plausibility). To address this gap, we propose Stable Vibration, a text-driven conditional diffusion framework for rolling-bearing vibration signal generation. The method uses a pretrained text encoder to encode fixed-order structured engineering prompts describing bearing fault semantics, operating conditions, and measurement settings; the resulting representations condition the diffusion generator for controllable waveform synthesis. We further develop a signal–residual disentangled hierarchical diffusion mechanism to improve interpretability, where the residual branch models unstructured components not explicitly explained by the structured signal branch (e.g., measurement contamination and background interference), without claiming a unique physical noise source. Experiments on two public bearing datasets (CWRU and XJTU–SY) and a custom bearing testbed demonstrate improved distributional fidelity, waveform similarity, and spectral consistency compared with matched baselines. We also provide characteristic-frequency overlays as physics-grounded qualitative sanity checks of spectral placement under prompt-specified conditions. The current validation focuses on rolling bearings; extensions to other components (e.g., gearboxes) require dedicated datasets and prompt-schema design and are left for future work.

title: Adaptive generalized dispersive mode decomposition method for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: To effectively address the issues of energy dispersion and inaccurate localization of fault impulses in rolling bearing vibration signal analysis, a novel adaptive generalized dispersive mode decomposition method that integrates time–frequency feature enhancement and adaptive ridge extraction is proposed. First, the time–frequency representation is sharpened through a multi-strategy feature enhancement mechanism, thereby facilitating more reliable identification of fault-related features. Building on the enhanced representation, adaptive ridge extraction is performed to accurately estimate the number and distribution of initial ridges. Subsequently, modal components are successively extracted from the original signal via a recursive decomposition framework guided by the initial ridge information. A refined time–frequency representation is constructed by integrating modal amplitudes with ridge characteristics. Finally, fault characteristic frequencies are precisely identified through envelope spectrum analysis. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with existing approaches, the proposed method achieves improved diagnostic accuracy and robustness, indicating its potential for practical applications.

title: A novel hybrid data-driven approach for rapid estimation of building vibration responses in urban rail transit systems
abstract: Environmental vibration assessment conducted during the preliminary stage plays a critical role in identifying vibration-sensitive objectives along the railway that may experience excessive vibrations, thereby guiding the subsequent screening process and the design of vibration mitigation measures. This assessment typically relies on empirical formulas; however, the predictive accuracy of these formulas presents certain challenges, such as the risk of overly conservative evaluations, which may lead to unnecessary design expenditures. According to the core idea of multi-stage correction of empirical formulas, this study introduces a hybrid methodology that combines Bayesian Neural Networks with soil-structure coupling loss and building impedance models to enable efficient prediction of train-induced building vibration responses. Ground vibration data were first collected from seven different locations and synthesized into a comprehensive dataset. The spatial distribution of ground vibrations and the characteristics of vibration amplification zones were then systematically examined. Thereafter, a Bayesian Neural Network model was implemented to predict ground vibrations across 1/3 octave frequency bands, while effectively addressing the inherent uncertainties in the data. In the subsequent phase, the predicted ground vibration data were used as inputs in soil-structure coupling loss and building impedance models to calculate the soil-structure coupling loss and the corresponding building vibration responses. Finally, a case study was carried out to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed hybrid prediction framework.

title: Vibration-based evaluation of dynamic efficiency for planetary gear trains
abstract: Transmission efficiency is a key indicator governing the energy consumption of mechanical systems. Planetary gear trains (PGTs), extensively adopted in high power and heavy duty equipment, generally work under dynamic operating conditions. Most existing investigations adopt static analysis based merely on structural design parameters, while neglecting real‑time operating states, which restricts the improvement of dynamic efficiency. To address this issue, this work proposes a novel approach for calculating the dynamic transmission efficiency of PGTs using vibrational feature analysis. A dynamic model considering multiple excitations is constructed to describe the vibrational responses of rotating components. Combined with vibrational analysis and static computation, theoretical models for dynamic angular velocity and driving/driven torques are derived, forming an integrated framework for dynamic efficiency calculation and power flow analysis. A dedicated test rig is developed for signal acquisition and post‑processing, so as to test vibrational features and verify the proposed method. Experimental and theoretical results demonstrate that the relative RMS vibration amplitude is between 2.89% and 7.28%. The relative errors of mean, maximum, minimum and peak dynamic efficiency between predictions and measurements are 0.26%, 0.34%, 0.22% and 7.05%, respectively. This research provides a solid theoretical support for the optimal design of high‑efficiency PGTs.

title: Physics-informed unit-normalized selective embedding with harmonic loss for fault identification using vibration and acoustic signals
abstract: Induction motors generate vibration and acoustic signals from mechanical imbalance, electromagnetic forces, and structural transmission through the machine housing. Interpreting harmonic fault signatures from these responses becomes difficult when different types of sensors are used due to bandwidth and signal scaling limitations. This work investigates how physics-informed signal representation can improve fault diagnosis using both industrial sensors and cell phone sensors. A unit-consistent normalization approach is introduced to allow comparison between vibration acceleration and acoustic pressure signals by converting both signals into equivalent vibration velocity representations. Based on this formulation, a structured signal processing framework named Unit-Normalized Selective Embedding with Harmonic Loss (UNSE-HL) is proposed, combining unit normalization, selective embedding, and a physics-informed harmonic loss function to improve the representation of modulation patterns during diagnosis. Experiments are conducted using the induction motor datasets collected under multiple operating conditions with both structurally mounted sensors and cell phones. Envelope spectral analysis shows that rotor harmonics are observable across cell phone sensors after normalization; this observability does not by itself establish classification reliability, which is evaluated separately. Time-frequency representations combined with the proposed embedding strategy improve diagnosis accuracy and classification stability relative to conventional signal representation approaches on the datasets and devices evaluated in this study. These findings highlight the importance of signal transmission physics in condition monitoring and indicate that, for the specific smartphone sensors and operating conditions tested here, appropriate preprocessing improves the usability of low-bandwidth sensors for fault diagnosis.

title: Image-to-image translation-based visual vibration displacement measurement of a rotating body with tilted viewing angle in horizontal plane
abstract: In the modern industrial field, the dynamic stability of rotating bodies is crucial to the operational efficiency and safety of equipment, and accurate measurement of their vibration displacement is of great significance. Although image recognition algorithms have already realized the visual measurement of vibration displacement of rotating bodies, the existing algorithms still have problems such as targeted data processing and relying on manual labeling. For this reason, this paper proposes a method for measuring the vibration displacement of rotating bodies with tilted viewing angles in the horizontal plane, integrating image-to-image translation with traditional vision techniques. Image-to-image translation is leveraged to convert images of rotors with tilted viewing angles captured at different oblique angles into a unified perspective. This method effectively reduces data dependency in vibration displacement extraction. Additionally, considering the characteristic features of rotor vibration images, a spatial integration and cross-dimensional optimization strategy is designed. A stepwise downsampling scheme, a DepthCascade Block (DCB) module, and a Cross-Axis Grouped Residual Block (CAGRB) module are introduced to optimize the generator network of pix2pixHD, thereby improving the quality of view transformation. The proposed method combines deep learning and traditional vision techniques to realize the vibration displacement measurement of the rotor, while eliminating human-induced errors caused by manual labeling.
