Based on ablation experiments, comparisons with multiple neural networks model, and comparisons with eddy current sensor data, the results show that at an acquisition rate of 2000 frames per second, the root mean square error (RMSE) for vibration displacement measurements at the three oblique angles was as low as 0.0236 mm, 0.0288 mm, and 0.0348 mm, respectively, with peak signal-to-noise ratios (PSNR) reaching 41.18 dB, 39.98 dB, and 39.65 dB, respectively. Furthermore, in comparison with image-recognition-based vibration displacement extraction methods, the proposed method can effectively extract rotor vibration displacement under stable illumination and at the three fixed tilted viewpoints tested in this study. However, a clear failure boundary is observed at viewpoint 3 under the combined effects of low illumination and a complex background.

title: A fully multivariate multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis method for fault diagnosis
abstract: We propose a fully multivariate generalization of multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MFDFA) and leverage it to develop a fault diagnosis framework for multichannel machine vibration data. We introduce a novel covariance-weighted $L_{pq}$ matrix norm based on Mahalanobis distance to define a fully multivariate fluctuation function that uniquely captures cross-channel dependencies and variance biases in multichannel vibration data. This formulation, termed FM-MFDFA, allows for a more accurate characterization of the multiscale structure of multivariate signals. To enhance feature relevance, the proposed framework integrates multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD) to isolate fault-relevant components before applying FM-MFDFA. Results on wind turbine gearbox data demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional MFDFA approaches by effectively distinguishing between healthy and faulty machine states, even under noisy conditions.

title: Structure-enabled vibration encoding for single-sensor UAV actuator fault diagnosis under resource constraints
abstract: Actuator health is critical to multirotor UAV flight safety. However, high-precision actuator fault diagnosis in the UAV remains challenging under constrained sensing and computational resources. This paper proposes a structure-enabled single-sensor actuator fault diagnosis paradigm based on a vibration encoder integrated into the UAV fuselage. The vibration encoder performs physical encoding at the sensing end, converting highly similar actuator-related vibration responses into more discriminative frequency-domain representations before model-based diagnosis. Theoretical analysis suggests that the encoding mechanism is attributed to the combined effect of unit-scale frequency-selective modulation and network-scale non-equivalent propagation paths. The feature separability is quantified using the average correlation coefficient and the Euclidean distance in the normalized feature space. Experimental results show that the vibration encoder reduces the average correlation coefficient among actuator encoding transmissions from 0.88 to 0.16 and increases the average normalized feature-space distance from 0.44 to 1.17, corresponding to an average distance gain of 2.66 times. Under five-fold cross-validation, lightweight SVM and LR models achieve approximately 98% average diagnostic accuracy and favorable classification stability for both propeller and motor fault tasks, while more complex MLP and 1DCNN models provide only marginal performance gains. Further evaluations show that the lightweight models retain 92%–95% accuracy with only 10% training data and maintain over 90% accuracy at SNRs of at least 3 dB. Real hovering-flight validation further yields 94%–96% accuracy and Macro-F1 for propeller fault diagnosis, with an inference time of about 0.03 ms and a model size of about 0.04MB. These results indicate that the proposed paradigm effectively balances diagnostic precision and resource consumption, providing a resource-efficient and deployable solution for single-sensor UAV actuator fault diagnosis.

title: Sonic black hole inspired wave-confining conical acoustic metastructure for physical enhancement and filtering
abstract: It is known challenges to solve noise interference and propagation attenuation for acoustic sensing schemes. In response to the disadvantages of current sensing schemes, sonic black hole (SBH) based acoustic device with features of strong anti-interference, high signal gain and conspicuous sensitivity is studied by utilizing the trapped energy. Sound pressure distribution and energy trapping theory of SBH with greater accuracy is derived, which matches well with actual acoustic performance. To improve performance in compacter structure dimension and wider bandwidth, conical metastructure is designed by introducing the strategy of exchanging internal space for sensing bandwidth, frequency response testing results indicate that wider sensing range and greater pressure gain are realized by utilizing only 1/3 redundant space. Sound waves can be manipulated more efficiently by the proposed metastructure compared with mainstream scheme, and acoustic sensing abilities are further verified by implementing experiments on signal amplification, noise filtering, feature extraction and typical mechanical fault diagnosis. This work blazes a promising and brand-new trail for high quality acoustic sensing under long distance strong noise environments.

title: Semi-TFCDG: Semi-supervised time–frequency contrastive learning for domain generalization in machine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Domain generalization (DG) is a promising paradigm for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction in unseen domains. However, most DG methods assume that multiple fully annotated source domains are available, an assumption that is often difficult to satisfy in industrial scenarios because labeled samples are costly to obtain and unlabeled data are easier to collect. This motivates semi-supervised domain generalization (SSDG), in which unlabeled source data are exploited without access to target information. Although unsupervised contrastive learning can effectively exploit degradation information from unlabeled data, the commonly adopted pretraining-and-fine-tuning paradigm often decouples representation learning from the downstream RUL prediction objective. It also provides limited modeling capability for frequency-domain degradation information and time–frequency relationships. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Semi-TFCDG, a semi-supervised time–frequency contrastive domain generalization method for RUL prediction. Semi-TFCDG uses a limited amount of labeled source data and a large volume of unlabeled source data within a unified one-stage end-to-end training framework to learn robust degradation representations for unseen domains. Specifically, Semi-TFCDG exploits time-domain patterns, frequency-domain structures, and time–frequency consistency information from unlabeled data through time–frequency collaborative unsupervised contrastive learning. It further enables ground-truth labels to continuously guide the learning of degradation-semantic representations through label-aware supervised contrastive learning and RUL regression supervision. Moreover, it establishes fine-grained degradation-related semantic relationships across labeled and unlabeled source domains through semantic-aware cross-domain contrastive alignment. Experiments on one real-world industrial dataset and two public datasets validate the effectiveness of Semi-TFCDG in the SSDG setting.

title: Correlation analysis between dynamic cutting characteristics and workpiece surface integrity in whirling milling
abstract: Among the physical parameters that govern surface integrity, cutting vibration and cutting force play an especially crucial role. Most studies have focused on the influence of single time-series cutting force signals or cutting vibration signals on surface integrity, with limited research addressing the coupling of triaxial cutting forces or triaxial vibrations. Consequently, the critical modal information arising from the synergistic motion of the three axes has been overlooked, making it difficult to elucidate the comprehensive influence of dynamic cutting characteristics on surface integrity. This study investigates the intrinsic relationship between dynamic cutting characteristics and workpiece surface integrity by employing JRP and JRQA based on triaxial cutting force and vibration signals acquired during the whirling milling process. The raw dynamic cutting characteristic signals were denoised using a Butterworth filter and subsequently standardized to eliminate dimensional effects. Based on this, joint recurrence plots were constructed and key joint recurrence parameters (JDET, JLAM, JRPDE) were extracted. The dynamic cutting characteristics were then systematically quantified using the JRQA method. Finally, the correlation between the JRQA parameters and surface integrity data was revealed by integrating both sets of results. The research indicates that the influence of JRQA parameters on surface integrity exhibits significant conditional dependence and selectivity, with correlations varying markedly with changes in cutting parameters. In most cases, JDET and JLAM exhibit a significant negative correlation with surface roughness, particularly showing strong associations when cutting speed increases (correlation coefficient reaching -0.80). Whereas when depth of cut increases, both parameters demonstrate a strong positive correlation with residual stress (correlation coefficient reaching 0.80). JRPDE shows a perfect negative correlation with surface roughness as the number of tools increases (correlation coefficient -1.00), demonstrating strong potential for prediction and control. Furthermore, the study reveals that the contribution of JRQA factors to surface roughness and residual stress is often inconsistent, indicating that multi-objective trade-offs need to be considered when applying recurrence parameters in process optimization.

title: Edge-deployable pseudo-supervised fault diagnosis for RV reducers: a lightweight method based on physical prior guidance and diffusion reconstruction
abstract: As a core component of industrial robots, reliable and edge-deployable cross-domain fault diagnosis for RV reducers remains challenging due to strong background noise, severe domain shifts, and the high computational overhead of some existing methods. To address this issue, a lightweight method based on physical prior guidance and diffusion reconstruction for domain adaptation fault diagnosis is proposed. Specifically, a sample standardization strategy is applied to the raw signal to anchor transient impulses, thereby enhancing cross-domain consistency among samples. To achieve feature decoupling between operational background and transient fault impulses, an innovative orthogonal decoupling operator (ODO) is proposed. By imposing strict orthogonal penalties in the latent space, the ODO effectively ensures high purity and strong discriminative power in fault representation. Furthermore, to enable edge deployment, a conditional multi-layer perceptron mixer diffusion denoising module is designed. This module uses physical prior frequency bands as specific anchors to guide the denoising process, constraining the search space and enabling global information interaction with minimal computational cost. By integrating Sinkhorn subdomain optimal transport and a pseudo label refinement mechanism driven by diffusion reconstruction energy, this method achieves fine-grained cross-domain data matching, effectively mitigating the negative transfer effects caused by severe domain shifts. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of cross-domain fault diagnosis while substantially reducing the number of model parameters.

title: Hierarchical calibration-balanced learning framework for privacy-preserving domain-incremental fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: In health monitoring scenarios for rotating machinery with continuously varying operating conditions, domain-incremental fault diagnosis has become a research focus. However, most existing domain-incremental learning approaches rely on the storage of historical exemplar data, which poses significant challenges in practical industrial applications due to data privacy concerns and limited storage resources. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a hierarchical calibration-balanced learning (HCBL) framework that establishes an exemplar-free domain-incremental diagnosis mechanism from the perspectives of representation-space calibration and decision-boundary reconstruction. First, a hierarchical domain drift calibration module is developed to align feature spaces across different operating conditions through global feature mapping and class-conditional constraints. Meanwhile, historical class statistics are calibrated into the current feature space to preserve cross-domain representation consistency and alleviate distribution drifts caused by domain drift. Second, an analytical balanced classifier is constructed to reconstruct the decision boundary in a closed-form solution manner by integrating calibrated historical statistical information with data from the current operating condition. This design effectively alleviates the classification bias caused by the dominance of newly acquired operating-condition data. Experimental results obtained from continuous operating-condition expansion tasks on the gearbox bearing dataset of the CRH380A high-speed train and the wheelset bearing dataset demonstrate that, without the involvement of historical samples, the proposed method achieves superior diagnostic accuracy and stability.

title: Local-truncated symbol-informed cumulative probability distribution: An interpretable health indicator for degradation tracking of rotating machinery
abstract: Conventional approaches based on information entropy and conditional entropy primarily rely on the global distribution of pattern probabilities, while neglecting the intrinsic temporal dependencies and tail variations within probability sequences. Consequently, these methods often exhibit limited sensitivity and non-monotonic behavior in bearing degradation tracking. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel degradation indicator, termed the local-truncated symbol-informed cumulative probability distribution (LTSCPD). LTSCPD integrates symbolic transformation with local interval truncation, thereby jointly capturing the magnitude, occurrence frequency, and ordering of probability units in time series. Firstly, raw vibration signals are encoded into cumulative symbolic sequences to suppress amplitude noise while preserving the essential structural features of degradation patterns. Secondly, local truncation intervals are defined from the healthy stage to account for extreme-value shifts during degradation. Finally, truncated integration of the tail region of the cumulative probability distribution is performed to emphasize the dynamic accumulation of extreme probability mass throughout the degradation process. Extensive experiments on both simulated signals and two full-life bearing datasets demonstrate that the LTSCPD method consistently yields stable and monotonic degradation curves across diverse fault categories.

title: Causal Bayesian optimization for sensor placement and deconfounding in structural health monitoring
abstract: Structural health monitoring systems must distinguish genuine damage from environmental effects. Current methods rely on correlational reasoning that cannot separate causal influences from spurious associations. Temperature variations, for instance, often produce larger shifts in natural frequencies than actual structural damage does. Here, we introduce a causal inference framework that addresses this limitation at its root. A structural causal model encodes the physical relationships among environmental conditions, structural properties, damage states, and sensor measurements. Formal causal reasoning then separates the genuine effect of damage on sensor responses from the confounding influence of environmental conditions. Counterfactual analysis further allows engineers to evaluate hypothetical scenarios, such as alternative sensor layouts or different environmental conditions, without physical experimentation. Built on this causal foundation, a multi-objective Bayesian optimization algorithm identifies Pareto-optimal sensor placements that balance detection probability, localization accuracy, false alarm robustness, and instrumentation cost. Validation spans numerical and experimental benchmarks together with an end-to-end evaluation on a full-scale bridge. Causal deconfounding lowers false alarm rates compared to conventional normalization, the optimizer reaches better Pareto fronts with far fewer evaluations than evolutionary alternatives, and the advantages persist under model misspecification and hidden confounding.

title: Corrigendum to “Towards in-situ monitoring of floating platforms: geometry-anchored recurrent diffusion for long-sequence motion reconstruction based on monocular marker-free video” [Mech. Syst. Sign. Proc. 259 (2026) 114864]
A smoothed semi-analytical JKR models with hysteresis damping factors for adhesive particle collisions
abstract: The classical Johnson–Kendall–Roberts (JKR) model is unable to account for energy dissipation during adhesive particle collisions. To address this limitation, a semi-analytical dynamic JKR model is developed by incorporating hysteresis and adhesive damping within an energy-consistent framework. Two adhesive damping terms are introduced to represent energy dissipation in both contact and non-contact regimes, with their evolution constrained to remain consistent with the force–displacement behavior of the JKR model. Energy dissipation caused by physical contact event in the contact region is further characterized by a hysteresis damping term. The adhesive damping formulations are derived based on energy conservation by analyzing energy conversion throughout the entire interaction process, including attraction, compression, restitution, and separation. By integrating these damping mechanisms with the classical JKR model, a dynamic JKR formulation is established that accurately reproduces both rebound and adhesive capture behaviors within a unified theoretical framework. This unified description reveals that rebound and capture are not fundamentally distinct processes, but rather two limiting outcomes governed by the competition between residual kinetic energy and dissipative effects. The proposed dynamic JKR model is validated against experimental data for both coarse particles and microparticles over a wide range of impact velocities. The results show strong agreement with experiments, demonstrating its capability to capture multiscale energy dissipation mechanisms. This work extends classical JKR theory by incorporating dissipative effects and establishes a physically consistent and predictive framework for adhesive particle collision dynamics across scales.

title: CNSAO: A complex number space anomaly observer with multi-task masked LLM autoencoder for bearing health monitoring under time-varying speeds
abstract: Health monitoring of bearings under time-varying speed conditions remains a critical challenge in industrial applications. The speed fluctuations may disrupt the phase consistency of fault-related characteristics and lead to the dispersion of fault energy. This makes it difficult to capture stable fault modes for health monitoring in the dynamic scenario. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a complex number space-based anomaly observer (CNSAO) for bearing health monitoring under time-varying speed conditions. Firstly, a multi-task autoencoder (AE) is constructed to perform signal reconstruction and rotational speed prediction. Secondly, a pre-trained large language model-based AE (LLMAE) is used as the backbone for feature extraction and noise reduction. Moreover, a residual connection is applied to LLMAE to enhance information propagation. Thirdly, a complex number space health index (CHI) is constructed to quantify bearing health degradation from both amplitude and phase similarity perspectives, which can sensitively capture phase asynchrony caused by continuous speed variations. In order to verify the effectiveness of CNSAO, three bearing health monitoring tests are performed. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CNSAO can achieve robust early fault detection. It outperforms traditional methods in terms of detection accuracy. Moreover, the visualization results illustrate that CNSAO can accurately extract the amplitude and phase differences in the dynamic industrial scenarios.

title: Prediction method for dynamic stiffness of fixture-workpiece system considering clamping constraints and material removal
abstract: The dynamic stiffness of the fixture-workpiece system governs the vibration response of thin-walled shells under cutting loads. Continuous material removal induces the rebalancing of clamping prestress and results in the redistribution of geometric stiffness. However, traditional structural dynamic modification methods only remove the mass and stiffness contributions of the removed elements from the initial model, rendering such effects difficult to capture. Therefore, a time varying dynamic stiffness prediction method is proposed that combines structural dynamic modification with the element birth & death method. First, a dynamic model that includes clamping‑induced geometric stiffness is built using the energy method and Lagrange equations, and the normal dynamic stiffness is obtained via vector projection. Second, a characterization coefficient based on deformation response differences is introduced to describe the evolution of geometric stiffness during material removal. Then, initial dynamic parameters are derived from prestressed modal analysis. Finally, modal hammer tests and milling experiments validate the proposed method, and the effects of clamping load, layout, and material removal on dynamic stiffness are analyzed. Results show that the geometric stiffness redistribution caused by clamping prestress is spatially localized and becomes more pronounced as material removal increases. Compared with the structural dynamic modification method, the proposed method describes the dynamic stiffness characteristics more accurately, with an average prediction error of 10.58%. This study offers a theoretical basis for clamping design and vibration suppression in thin‑walled components.

title: Study on dynamic behavior of high-speed lubricated bearings in control moment gyroscope electromechanical system under different controller parameters
abstract: The control moment gyroscope (CMG), composed of a gimbal and a rotor, is a key actuator for high-precision spacecraft attitude regulation, and the high-speed bearings supporting the rotor are critical components that constrain the dynamic performance and operational stability of the system. Although existing gimbal speed control algorithms can improve the dynamic and steady-state performance of gimbal motion, speed fluctuations during electromechanical control induce gyroscopic torque variations, leading to significant radial load fluctuations on the high-speed bearings and further causing the dynamic evolution of contact, lubrication, friction, and thermal behaviors. Existing studies have mainly focused on macroscopic control performance, while the evolution of internal bearing states under electromechanical control remains insufficiently understood. To address this issue, an electromechanical coupled dynamic model of the CMG is established by considering lubricated bearing tribological characteristics, time-varying stiffness, and motor drive effects, and a model compensated active disturbance rejection controller (MCADRC) is adopted for gimbal speed regulation. The predictive capability of the proposed dynamic model and the effectiveness of the control algorithm are validated through comparisons between simulation and experimental results obtained from a CMG principle prototype. On this basis, contact, mixed lubrication, friction, and thermal analysis models of the ball–raceway interface are further established to reveal the dynamic evolution of the internal states of the bearings under different controller parameters. Results show that increasing the controller bandwidth ωc speeds up the gimbal response but increases the peaks of contact- and friction-related indicators, whereas increasing the observer bandwidth ωo reduces speed overshoot, lowers these peaks, and improves lubrication. These findings provide guidance for future controller tuning to better balance gimbal motion performance and transient tribological severity.

title: A novel inequivalent discretization modeling for vibration analysis of foam-filled honeycomb sandwich plates with spatially three-dimensional designable composite constituents under elastic boundary constraints
abstract: Foam-filled honeycomb sandwich composite plates are commonly analyzed using equivalent methods, in which the cellular skeleton and foam filler are replaced by an effective homogeneous continuum. This treatment eliminates their explicit spatial distinction, limits the representation of local stiffness, inertia, and deformation mechanisms, and prevents variable-stiffness and functionally graded designs from being introduced directly within the core. This study develops an inequivalent dynamic modeling framework to predict the forced and free vibration behaviors of bidirectional variable-stiffness functionally graded composite sandwich plates with a foam-filled honeycomb core. The principal novelty lies in three aspects. First, geometry-dependent material-allocation functions are introduced to preserve the spatial distinction between the honeycomb skeleton and foam-filled regions, and are embedded directly into the stiffness, inertia, and energy operators rather than replacing the heterogeneous core with averaged properties. Second, a bidirectional variable-stiffness formulation combined with functional grading enables stiffness tailoring. Third, these geometric and material descriptions are integrated into a unified framework for predicting free and forced vibration behaviors under elastic boundary constraints. The formulation is established based on the first-order shear deformation theory, spring constraint technique, Rayleigh-Ritz method, and Gauss-Legendre numerical integration for natural frequency, mode shape, and vibration response analyses. The framework is validated against high-fidelity ABAQUS finite element simulations and published benchmark solutions and compared with the equivalent homogenization methods to quantify the error sources, and the maximum natural frequency deviation is reduced from 79.69% to 4.11%. Parametric studies reveal the coupled effects of honeycomb topology, foam-filling distribution, bidirectional steering angle variation, cell size, load type, and damping magnitude on the vibration characteristics. The results demonstrate that the inequivalent model preserves the mechanical distinction between honeycomb walls and foam-filled regions while capturing the additional design flexibility introduced by bidirectional variable-stiffness functionally graded materials, which could provide improved accuracy and physical insight for the vibration-oriented design of advanced composite sandwich structures.

title: Real three-dimensional volumetric ultrasonic imaging of steel weld defects: exceeding conventional inspection capabilities with a row–column addressed array
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) characterization of weld defects is crucial for reliable integrity assessment and safe operation of critical engineering structures because two-dimensional (2D) ultrasonic imaging often provides incomplete defect information and is prone to missed detection. However, the application of 3D ultrasonic imaging to weld inspection is limited by high structural noise and the reliance of existing approaches on stacked 2D line scans, which fundamentally result in pseudo-3D representations rather than true volumetric imaging. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a 3D volumetric ultrasonic imaging method for steel weld inspection based on a Row–Column Addressing (RCA) array. A volumetric imaging framework is established by modeling ultrasonic propagation paths in a 3D coordinate system. To improve defect visibility in coarse-grained welds, nonconvex overlapping group sparse variational (NOGSV) denoising is applied to Full Matrix Capture (FMC) data, and vector coherence factor (VCF) weighting is further employed to enhance defect contrast in Total Focusing Method (TFM) imaging. Experimental validation on two steel butt-weld specimens containing representative defects demonstrates that the proposed method enables reliable 3D visualization of different defect types and reveals defect characteristics that are difficult or impossible to identify using conventional 2D ultrasonic imaging. High signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) volumetric images are achieved in weld structures, enabling accurate reconstruction of defect 3D geometry and spatial distribution. This study presents the first high-quality real 3D ultrasonic visualization of weld defects, offering an effective new approach for nondestructive testing and 3D characterization of welded structures.

title: Continuum and lumped-parameter modeling of a dielectric elastomer array actuator system
abstract: This paper presents the modeling of a soft array of interconnected dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs). The array exploits selective actuation of dielectric patches through the application of a high voltage to achieve localized deformations. The soft nature of the system induces electro-mechanical coupling between neighboring DEAs, whose interplay with the elastomer’s large deformations and viscoelasticity results in a highly complex and nonlinear dynamic response. Motivated by the need to model those effects in an accurate and computationally-efficient way, so as to enable both design optimization and real-time control, we present a set of models with different levels of complexity and accuracy. First, we introduce a continuum model formulation able to predict the dynamic electro-mechanical response of the overall array, including coupling effects and local deformation patterns, in a completely physics-based fashion. Second, we develop a control-oriented dynamic model that predicts the average response with a significantly reduced number of variables (and, in turn, lower computation burden), while still accounting for several key physical mechanisms of the underlying system. While the former accurately infers the coupled system response solely from material and geometry data, the latter requires a dedicated parameter identification procedure that is here cast as a numerically-efficient optimization problem. Both approaches are extensively validated on an experimental DEA array prototype, demonstrating high accuracy under both static and dynamic actuation.

title: Time–frequency representation of nonlinear structural response through rationally sampled Stockwell analysis
abstract: The reliable analysis of the non-stationary response of mechanical and structural systems under transient excitations, and in particular the tracking of the time-varying evolution of the dominant modal frequencies during damaging events, remains a long-standing challenge for vibration-based monitoring. A persistent practical limitation is that the time-frequency map on which any subsequent automatic or learning-based identification stage relies is built on a frequency grid that depends on implementation choices. This means that records acquired on different sensors or under different events cannot be compared on a common substrate.The present article addresses the limitation at the representational level by introducing the Stockwell-Ditommaso-Ponzo representation (SDP), obtained by sampling the Stockwell transform on an ordered Farey grid of primitive rational frequencies. Each coefficient is assigned a rational label, an ordered Voronoi frequency cell and an exact logarithmic quadrature weight induced by the Stockwell measure. Subsequent to the declaration of the sampling frequency, the analysed band and the maximum conductor, the support, the cells and the weights are uniquely determined prior to the processing of any record. A time-varying modal frequency, such as that observed when the apparent lateral stiffness of an instrumented building degrades under strong-motion excitation and partially recovers afterwards, is therefore encoded as a deterministic path on a geometry shared across sensors, repeated events and simulations of the same structure.The representation is exercised on the simulated top-floor acceleration of a five-storey reinforced-concrete infilled frame, whose apparent first-mode frequency is observed to drop to approximately 0.8 Hz and partially recovers through the simulated closure of column cracks under gravity. The SDP cell-path captures the four phases of the loss-and-recovery sequence, and engineering-oriented descriptors take values consistent with the physical setup. The proposed representation is intended to function as a reproducible, transform-level front end on which calibrated automatic identification and damage-assessment procedures, including artificial-intelligence-based pipelines, can be built in a controlled manner.

title: Bandgap theoretical prediction and broadband vibration reduction of plate-type elastic metastructure with nonlinear particle damping
abstract: This paper presents theoretical and numerical studies on the flexural wave bandgap and broadband vibration reduction characteristics of a plate-type elastic metastructure with nonlinear particle damping. A bandgap prediction model that considers both the frequency–dependent damping and dynamic mass effects of particles is proposed. The bandgap shift mechanism is explored using a coupled simulation approach, and the influence of coupling stiffness between the substrate and resonators on the vibration reduction and dissipation characteristics of particle damping is analyzed. Vibration experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical predictions, simulation models, and bandgap shift characteristic. The results show that the proposed model accurately predicts the bandgap and broadband attenuation characteristics, agreeing well with both simulation and experimental results. Excitation intensity affects the mass of particles participating in dissipation, transitioning their behavior from inertial effect to damping effect, consequently shifting the system bandgap. Increasing coupling stiffness transitions the resonator-substrate coupling mode from global to local, progressively weakening—and eventually nearly eliminating—the suppressive effect of particle damping on elastic waves attenuation rate within the bandgap. Moreover, due to the resonator isolation mechanism, the coupling vibration reduction characteristics of particle damping and plate-type elastic metastructure have three states: strong positive, negative or no impact, and weak positive coupling.
keywords: Plate-type elastic metastructure with nonlinear particle damping

title: Interpretable U-Net RCNN for blind peak detection in vibration spectra
abstract: Accurate peak detection in vibration spectra is key to early fault diagnosis but remains challenging due to noise and unknown spectral content. This paper presents a hybrid approach combining the benefits of U-Nets and Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks for blind peak detection, trained on complex simulated 1D data with extension to real-world signals. The model combines classification and regression to identify and localise peaks without prior knowledge of the signal or machine. Its performance is benchmarked against the Exact Order Model Estimation of Signal Parameters via Rotational Invariance Technique and a Topological Peak Identification approach using labelled simulated data, demonstrating robustness and practical effectiveness. The method is further tested on real offshore wind turbine data, where it successfully detects visually identifiable peaks, confirming its applicability in real-world scenarios.

title: Intelligent non-destructive evaluation of complex defects using magnetization-excited infrared thermography
abstract: Aircraft hydraulic pipelines are critical components of aircraft hydraulic systems, and reliable inspection of their surface defects is essential for ensuring operational safety and maintenance efficiency. Existing inspection methods for ferromagnetic surface defects are often limited by specimen contamination, insufficient adaptability to complex curved structures, or low inspection efficiency. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an intelligent inspection framework that integrates Dual-mode Electromagnetic Magnetization-excited Infrared Thermography (DEMIT) with deep learning-based defect detection. By employing controllable circumferential and longitudinal magnetization, DEMIT enables rapid and non-contact inspection without contaminating the specimen surface, while promoting more uniform thermal excitation and more consistent defect-sensitive thermal responses in complex curved components. The proposed framework is further implemented in a self-developed automated inspection system to support efficient defect imaging and intelligent recognition. For accurate localization and classification of weak and small defects under complex backgrounds, a Calibration Guided Super Resolution Enhanced Transformer Detector is developed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves mAP by 2.5 percentage points over the best-performing baseline and achieves the best overall performance on Scratch, Pit, and Mesh defects, especially for weak and small Pit defects. This study provides an efficient and practically deployable solution for intelligent inspection of surface defects in aircraft hydraulic pipelines and other complex ferromagnetic components commonly found in industrial systems.

title: MILT: A latent temporal framework for domain generalization in bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Domain generalization-based fault diagnosis provides a practical solution for vibration signal-based health monitoring of rolling bearings. It enables diagnosis under unseen operating conditions without requiring target-domain data during training. However, most existing methods focus mainly on feature-level invariance and are insufficient to model the temporal organization and latent dependencies of fault-related vibration information. To address this issue, this paper proposes a latent temporal framework (MILT) for rolling bearing fault diagnosis. MILT consists of a latent temporal mechanism learning module and a cross-domain contrastive optimization module. The former organizes local responses into an ordered latent sequence and guides state transitions with a sequence-level descriptor, capturing fault-related temporal patterns that are less sensitive to operating variations. The latter performs temporal pooling and cross-domain supervised contrastive learning to improve class discrimination and domain consistency, enabling robust diagnosis in unseen domains. Experiments on a public benchmark and an experimental bearing dataset show that MILT outperforms representative state-of-the-art methods in diagnostic accuracy and unseen-domain generalization.

title: Numerical and experimental analysis of a bolted-joint rotor-bearing system with squirrel cage elastic supports during speed-up process
abstract: Aero-engine rotor systems are rotating machines that typically operate at supercritical speeds. To regulate critical speeds and suppress vibration amplitudes, elastic supports are widely employed. Meanwhile, bolted joints are extensively used to ensure structural integrity and assembly flexibility. Although these designs improve system performance and facilitate assembly, they also introduce frequency-dependent stiffness of the elastic supports and time-varying stiffness of the bolted joints. The coupled nonlinear effects associated with these substructures may further deteriorate the dynamic stability of the rotor system, particularly during the speed-up process. This study develops a coupled dynamic model for a squirrel cage supported bolted-joint rotor system under speed-up. The proposed model comprehensively integrates the dynamic stiffness of the squirrel-cage support, the piecewise-linear bending stiffness of the bolted joints, and the transient loads induced by speed-up process. Furthermore, the influences of the support dynamic stiffness and the acceleration on the dynamic behavior of the rotor are systematically investigated. The results indicate that elevating the squirrel-cage support stiffness simultaneously increases the critical speeds and the vibration amplitudes of the rotor. Additionally, the structural resonance of the squirrel cage triggers negative response peaks within the system. Moreover, a higher acceleration rate attenuates the resonance peak amplitude and shortens the resonance duration during critical speed transitions. Finally, experimental validation is conducted on the bolted-joint rotor system with squirrel cage supports to verify the numerical predictions regarding the effects of support stiffness and the acceleration on the dynamic characteristics of the rotor system. The findings of this study provide useful guidance for the motion control and fault diagnosis of bolted-joint rotor systems with squirrel-cage supports.

title: Quickest change detection via statistical electrical signature analysis for motor diagnosis
abstract: Electrical Signature Analysis (ESA) is a widely adopted non-intrusive technique for monitoring induction motors, offering the advantage of using both current and voltage information. However, detecting early-stage faults remains a challenge due to low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and spectral pollution from the power grid that masks weak fault signatures. This paper introduces a robust statistical detection framework designed to identify incipient mechanical and electrical faults despite these constraints. First, a signal enhancement strategy combining Instantaneous Symmetrical Components (ISC) and voltage-referenced multi-variable Wiener filtering is proposed. This approach effectively suppresses grid-induced harmonics to isolate the residual fault signature within the stator current. Based on a unified physical model of torque oscillations, a local spectral health indicator is derived. Statistical analysis demonstrates that this indicator follows a Gamma distribution, the parameters of which are conditioned by the motor's operating point. To address this dependency, an operating point clustering stage, based on the active power estimated from ESA, is proposed to segment the data. Finally, a Generalized Cumulative Sum (CuSum) algorithm, explicitly derived for the Gamma distribution, is developed. Unlike memoryless static detectors such as the Neyman-Pearson test, this sequential approach exploits the temporal history of the indicator to minimize detection delay. Experimental validation on $4$kW induction motors under misalignment and broken rotor bar conditions confirms that the proposed method significantly outperforms standard detection strategies, offering high sensitivity to incipient faults even under light load conditions.

title: Deep learning based reconstruction of fiber orientation in short fiber reinforced composites from ultrasonic wave responses
abstract: Fiber orientation plays an important role in the mechanical behavior of short fiber-reinforced composites, yet its internal distribution is difficult to characterize nondestructively. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework to reconstruct fiber orientation fields from boundary ultrasonic wave responses. A two-dimensional anisotropic wave propagation model with free-boundary conditions was developed to simulate wave signals in composite plates, where the local anisotropy was governed by sectional fiber orientation. Based on this model, a synthetic dataset was generated using a sectional representation of the plate. The simulated sensor signals were used as inputs to a multilayer perceptron, while the section-wise principal-direction angles were encoded using an angle aware representation to account for periodicity. The trained model directly predicted the orientation field from the simulated boundary wave responses. Reconstruction accuracy was evaluated using wrap-aware angular error metrics. Parametric studies were conducted to examine the effects of dataset size, excitation frequency, anisotropy strength, sensor ablation, and wave transmission factor on prediction performance. The results show that the proposed framework can effectively reconstruct the main features of the section-wise principal-direction field and remains reasonably robust under varying sensing and material conditions. The proposed approach provides a promising data-driven strategy for nondestructive characterization of internal fiber orientation in short fiber-reinforced composites.

title: A semi-supervised compound fault diagnosis method based on hierarchical attention and self-supervised graph learning for the rotary components of robots’ joints
abstract: Rotating machinery, which is a key component of industrial robots and precision equipment, is frequently susceptible to compound faults. However, diagnosing such faults remains challenging because of the coupling interference among fault features and the scarcity of labeled fault samples. To address this issue, this study proposes a semi‑supervised intelligent fault diagnosis method that integrates hierarchical attention and self‑supervised graph learning. The proposed method employs a three-layered progressive framework. At the node level, a multi-head self-attention mechanism screens and enhances the local features of each sample. At the edge level, a self-supervised graph autoencoder based on graph attention is constructed to model the correlations between samples from different sensors at the same time steps, thereby extracting and enhancing the features of various fault types. At the feature level, global similarity matching is applied to all extracted features to uncover the intrinsic relationships between compound and single faults. Finally, only a small set of labeled samples is used to train a multi‑label classifier to achieve an accurate diagnosis and effective decoupling of fault categories. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an average accuracy of over 99.0% in diagnosing compound faults, maintaining excellent generalization and stability, even with limited training samples. This study not only presents an effective technical solution for the compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery but also provides substantial theoretical support for the development of predictive maintenance systems in precision machinery applications.

title: Editorial Board
Full-field experimental modal analysis with low-speed cameras: Bandwidth merging and signal reconstruction for high-frequency dynamics
abstract: Vibration measurements and Experimental Modal Analysis (EMA) are fundamental tools for validating complex mechanical systems. While full-field optical techniques, such as 3D Digital Image Correlation (DIC), overcome the spatial limitations of pointwise sensors, they are inherently constrained by the resolution-frame rate trade-off, restricting low-cost cameras to low-frequency dynamics. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for blind, broadband full-field EMA using low-speed cameras, effectively bypassing the Nyquist-Shannon limit. The core novelty is a coherence-based bandwidth merging strategy, supported by an optimized Design of Experiments (DoE), which seamlessly assembles a global Frequency Response Function (FRF) from multiple band-limited measurements without prior knowledge of the structure’s resonances. To efficiently process the massive spatial datasets typical of DIC, a novel frequency-domain Repetition Method is introduced for signal reconstruction. Numerical and experimental validations on a multi-DoF model and a cantilever beam demonstrate high reconstruction accuracy with Frequency Response Assurance Criterion (FRAC) values reaching 0.99. Furthermore, the proposed frequency-domain algorithm reduces computational time by 59% compared to existing time-domain approaches. Ultimately, the framework successfully identified five structural modes up to 689 Hz using camera frame rates as low as 78 fps, offering a scalable, automated, and cost-effective alternative for high-frequency optical modal testing.

title: Vibro-acoustic coupling modeling and active control analysis of distributed piezoelectric laminated rectangular plates
abstract: Surface-mounted arrayed piezoelectric laminated structures have potential applications in active vibration and acoustic control of fluid-loaded structures. However, the distributed actuator layout and the feedback effect of heavy-fluid loading increase the modelling complexity. This study focuses on a representative rectangular plate structure, conducting research on vibro-acoustic coupling modeling and active control. The distributed piezoelectric laminated plate is discretized into multiple control units, with coupling conditions between units and structural boundaries modeled using virtual springs. Unknown field variables are expanded using Chebyshev polynomials. The element mass matrix, stiffness matrix, and vibro-acoustic coupling matrix are derived based on Hamilton’s principle. The underdetermined global vibro-acoustic coupling equation is assembled from these element matrices. Furthermore, a discrete Chebyshev spectral boundary element method is developed, ultimately establishing a complete set of vibro-acoustic coupling equations. Building upon this foundation, an active control model incorporating both minimum mean square velocity control and minimum radiation sound power control is established, and the control mechanisms and effectiveness of different strategies are systematically analyzed. The underwater heavy-fluid vibro-acoustic formulation is verified numerically through comparison with a fully coupled finite element model and through light-/heavy-fluid response analysis. An active vibration control experiment is further conducted to validate the structural-electromechanical control submodel, including piezoelectric actuation, structural response prediction, and vibration suppression. This research provides a theoretical and numerical basis for the preliminary design and mechanism analysis of distributed piezoelectric smart structures under fluid loading.
keywords: Discrete Chebyshev spectral boundary element method

title: Multi-regenerative dynamic modeling and chatter analysis in through-feed centerless grinding for high aspect ratio ceramic tubes
abstract: Grinding chatter is the critical factor limiting high-efficiency and high-quality machining in the centerless grinding of ceramic tubes with high aspect ratio. To suppress chatter in through-feed centerless grinding, a multi-modal dynamic model of the centerless grinding system is established, incorporating multiple regenerative mechanisms, such as workpiece regeneration, grinding wheel regeneration, and geometric layout effect. The stability boundaries of the grinding system are predicted. Multi-sensor experiments integrating vibration, acoustic emission, and grinding power were conducted to investigate the dynamic stability characteristics of the complex grinding system. The results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively predicts grinding stability. Stability lobe diagrams indicate that 60–80 μm represents the critical stability threshold. A dynamic parameter identification method for the workpiece-support system based on follow-up support was proposed in this study. Increasing the feed distances of the regulating wheel reduces the amplitude of the frequency response function, achieving an average suppression rate exceeding 60 %. Considering the stiffness improvement, the optimal range for feed distances of the regulating wheel is 0.4 mm∼0.8 mm. Batch machining of silicon carbide ceramic tubes with a high aspect ratio (L/D≈50) and a wall thickness of 0.395 mm was achieved by the grinding strategy based on stability analysis. Compared with the conventional process, grinding efficiency increased by 62.5 %, while outer diameter fluctuation decreased by approximately 97 %. This study provides theoretical and technical support for the precision centerless grinding of ceramic tubes with high aspect ratio.

title: Research on the bearing dynamic modeling considering the combined friction-damping effect at the cage-guide ring interface and the motion-force coupling mechanism of the cage
abstract: To investigate the motion-force coupling mechanism of cylindrical roller bearing cages under different whirl modes, a dynamic model-based on the dynamic Reynolds equation and the short bearing assumption-for simulating the cage motion trajectory was established on the basis of existing modeling work. The combined friction-damping effect at the cage-guide ring interface is further considered. The capability of the proposed model to predict the motion states and principal motion characteristics of the cage was validated by comparing the simulation results with existing literature and experimental data. The average and the maximum relative error between simulated and experimental dominant frequency components were 8.91% and 19.26%, respectively, and the predicted cage whirl direction and guide clearance phase relationships were generally consistent with the experimental results. On this basis, the motion-force coupling mechanism of cages under three typical whirl modes was further investigated, and the results indicate that: In the stable whirl mode, the oil film force Fco serves as the primary force sustaining the cage whirl, the frictional force Fct determines the whirl direction and the resultant collision force Fcc induces interference. In the random whirl mode, the irregular whirl of the cage is predominantly induced by the resultant collision force Fcc. In the local periodic whirl mode, the oil film force Fco primarily contributes to the eccentric motion of the cage, whereas the resultant collision force Fcc induces the tangential reciprocating motion of the cage.

title: A single-loop reweighted numerical integration method for failure probability function estimation under parametric probability boxes
abstract: Estimating the failure probability function under parametric probability boxes (p-boxes), which capture mixed aleatory and epistemic uncertainties, remains computationally challenging, especially when expensive computer models are involved. To address this challenge, the present paper develops a single-loop reweighted numerical integration method for efficient estimation of the complete failure probability function and its bounds. The generalized failure probability function is reformulated through a reweighting scheme that employs an auxiliary density function. Since the theoretically optimal auxiliary function is intractable, we provide two practical and reliable alternatives. The suggested reweighted probability operation is then combined with Generalized F discrepancy-based point selection strategy to compute the reformulated failure probability in a single-loop manner. This point selection strategy partitions the uncertainty space into Voronoi cells and assigns a representative point with the associated probability to each cell, avoiding brute-force sampling. The framework is fully non-intrusive, as it relies solely on the input p-boxes without relying on the form of the performance function. Finally, four case studies: a mathematical example, a vehicle front axle, a 120-bar truss, and a nonlinear Duffing oscillator, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and efficiency, is applicable to nonlinear and dynamic problems, and integrates seamlessly with black-box simulation codes for complex engineering applications.

title: End-to-end virtual sensing with head tracking using a temporal convolutional network for active road noise control
abstract: Head-tracking active road noise control requires accurate virtual sensing of sound pressure at the occupants’ ears. Conventional approaches based on the remote microphone method (RMM) remain limited because the use of one observation filter per head position does not account for dynamic driving conditions and provides insufficient information for robust model training. This study proposed an end-to-end virtual sensing framework with head tracking that uses a temporal convolutional network (TCN) conditioned on the head-position information via feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM). The proposed model predicts time-domain virtual microphone signals from eight-channel physical microphone measurements and real-time head positions. This formulation enables the segmentation of long recordings into numerous overlapping input–output pairs, thereby providing richer supervision and allowing the model to learn temporal variations in road noise within the tested speed range. Experimental results indicated that the proposed method significantly outperformed the existing learning-based approach that directly updates the observation filters, reducing the virtual sensing error from − 14.79 to − 19.05 dB in terms of NMSE and from − 7.35 to − 12.34 dBA in terms of A-weighted spectral error. Moreover, the training-data duration per head-pose configuration could be reduced without a considerable loss in accuracy when sufficient temporal variability was preserved. Furthermore, the encoder–decoder structure effectively reduced the computational cost while maintaining comparable frequency-domain performance. Active noise control (ANC) simulations demonstrated that the improved virtual sensing accuracy resulted in enhanced control performance, and the proposed method achieved ANC results close to those obtained using actual measured signals without virtual sensing.

title: A multi-scale frequency domain information-driven method for ultrasonic welding quality prediction
abstract: Ultrasonic welding is extensively used in industries such as automotive and electronics, where the tensile strength of the welding joints serves as a critical indicator of manufacturing quality, yet is subject to fluctuations caused by multiple uncertain factors during production. Moreover, the complex physical interactions of the process produce time series features rich in high-frequency ultrasonic information, which is critical for achieving accurate predictions of quality performance. This work develops a deep learning framework that accurately predicts joint tensile strength by fusing multi-source signals. Specifically, a high-fidelity acquisition system was established to synchronously capture high-frequency vibration, pressure, and displacement signals during welding. The proposed Gated Multi-scale Fast Fourier Transform Network (GMS-FFTNet) operates directly in the frequency domain, integrating a global Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to capture long-range dependencies and a local Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to resolve transient details. It is enhanced by an adaptive spectral filtering mechanism that dynamically emphasizes critical frequency bands, overcoming the limitations of conventional time-domain models that often struggle with spectral information loss. To synergize the insights from different sensors, a dedicated gating network effectively fuses the multi-source signal features. The model accurately predicts tensile strength, achieving a coefficient of determination of 82.17%. Furthermore, the visualization of attention weights serves to correlate the model’s inference with the manufacturing process of the ultrasonic welding. This method not only presents a robust solution for reliable quality monitoring of ultrasonic welding but also offers a generalizable framework for other dynamic manufacturing processes with high-frequency information.

title: Modelling and characterization of the unzipping dynamics of dielectric fluid actuators
abstract: Dielectric Fluid Actuators (DFAs) are variable capacitors that contract as a result of electrostatic forces acting on a compliant multilayer structure composed of a polymer film and an insulating liquid. Differences in the dielectric time constants of the liquid and polymeric layers lead to charge retention at their interface, causing a decay in Maxwell stress that ultimately leads to a relaxation of the actuator stroke in the presence of a constant applied voltage. In this work, we introduce a new physics-based continuum framework that extends electrostatic force modelling from fixed parallel-plate capacitors to actuator-level modelling, by coupling continuum electrical dynamics with a lumped mechanical model of the DFA. The DFA is represented as a continuum of infinitesimal variable capacitors, each modelled using simple RC elements. The framework is experimentally validated on a simple multi-layer open-pouch DFA, and on an established layout of hydraulically amplified self-healing electrostatic actuator. Even with a simplified description of the material electrical response (e.g., constant resistivities) and lumped deformation mechanics, the framework captures the relevant trends in unzipping dynamics with respect to geometry and operating conditions (applied voltage and external forces). The proposed framework lays the foundations for electro-mechanical dynamic continuum modelling of DFAs.

title: Prior superpixel-driven multi-modal query hypergraph convolutional network for weld quality assessment
abstract: The quality of weld is critical to the reliability of structural connections and operational safety in applications such as automotive manufacturing, rail transportation, and aerospace. However, conventional single-modal welding quality assessment methods often suffer from limited information representation, weak robustness to interference, and poor adaptability to complex operating conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a prior superpixel-driven multi-modal query hypergraph convolutional network (PS-MQHGN) for high-precision weld quality evaluation. PS-MQHGN employs a cross-modal query hypergraph convolution module to explicitly model the information transfer pathways between different modalities, such as images and process signals, thereby achieving effective multimodal feature integration. In addition, a prior superpixel-driven dual-image interaction module is designed to actively focus on regions relevant to welding quality and to align up and down surface features based on label consistency. To further enhance performance, a dual-dimensional hypergraph feature aggregation mechanism is introduced to suppress the adverse influence of noise and weakly correlated hyperedges on model stability. In a representative resistance spot welding scenario, experimental results demonstrate that PS-MQHGN achieves high-precision weld quality prediction under complex welding conditions, with a mean absolute error of 0.1576 mm, corresponding to a 15.7% reduction compared with state-of-the-art models. PS-MQHGN provides reliable support for weld quality assessment and process control.

title: Hysteresis decomposition and nonlinear coupled modeling of RC hollow piers: Experimental characterization of flexural-shear-bond interaction for seismic response prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of lateral displacement of bridge piers is essential for performance-based seismic design, whereas the deformation behavior of reinforced concrete circular hollow piers under flexural-shear interaction has not been insufficiently studied, particularly for configurations with double-layer reinforcement. Quasi-static tests were performed on five circular hollow piers with a shear span ratio of 2.81 to investigate their deformation characteristics and the effects of flexural-shear coupling. The test results show that pronounced flexural-shear coupled failure is observed, with flexural and diagonal cracks densely intersecting within the base plastic hinge region. Through refined decomposition of the three deformation components, it is revealed that at the ultimate state, flexural, shear, and bond-slip deformations contribute 40%-60%, 20%-30%, and 20%-50%, respectively. With increasing axial ratio, the flexural-shear interaction mode transitions from flexure-slip dominance to flexure-shear dominance, whereas higher stirrup ratios effectively mitigate the strength of flexural-shear coupling. Based on the test observations, modified models for three-component deformations are developed. In the flexural model, an ultimate curvature reduction factor χϕ and a flexural-shear coupled plastic hinge length Lp,fsi are introduced; in the bond-slip model, an axial ratio factor αη, a shear level factor βV, and a failure mode differentiation factor γmode are incorporated; and in the shear model, a moment level factor δm, an axial ratio-dependent crack angle θs(η), and a failure mode coefficient ζmode are introduced. Finally, the three component models are integrated into a unified framework to propose a comprehensive prediction approach for pier-top displacement. The validation results indicate that the prediction error ranges from −0.01% to +1.16%, with a mean absolute error of 0.55% and a standard deviation of 1.60%; compared to conventional methods, the prediction accuracy is improved by approximately 97%, the dispersion is reduced by 82%, and a slightly conservative trend is observed, making the proposed approach suitable for seismic deformation evaluation of circular hollow piers considering flexural-shear interaction.

title: Block-diagonal normalization for robust multichannel underwater narrowband active noise control using parametric-array secondary sources
abstract: Localized underwater narrowband active noise control (ANC) requires secondary sources that balance compact size, directivity, and multichannel control stability. Underwater parametric arrays, which generate highly directional difference-frequency sound, provide a promising secondary-source solution for underwater noise control. However, in such multichannel control systems, secondary-path coupling and filtered-reference energy imbalance may degrade the multichannel normalized filtered-x least-mean-square (MNFxLMS) algorithm. Its global normalization factor can be dominated by high-energy filtered-reference components, reducing the effective step size of weak-energy branches and causing slow convergence or insufficient attenuation at certain target tones. Motivated by the near-block-diagonal secondary-path structure enabled by directional parametric-array secondary sources, this paper develops a branch-wise block-diagonal normalized MNFxLMS formulation. The proposed method replaces global normalization with branch-wise normalization for individual subfilters, thereby reducing the suppression of weak-energy updates. Compared with multichannel filtered-x affine projection algorithms (MFxAPA), it avoids projection matrix inversion while achieving comparable performance at lower computational complexity. A mean-square performance model is further developed to predict the transient behavior of the proposed and reference algorithms. Simulations show good agreement between theoretical predictions and Monte Carlo learning curves, and BD-MNFxLMS is less sensitive to filtered-reference imbalance. Experiments show that, under imbalanced conditions, BD-MNFxLMS outperforms MNFxLMS in 11 out of 12 electrical-domain target-tone comparisons, with particularly pronounced advantages for the weak-energy target branch. For BD-MNFxLMS, acoustic-domain measurements yield positive attenuation at all tested target spectral lines, ranging from approximately 8.16 to 20.63 dB, confirming the practical effectiveness of the proposed system.

title: A novel star-shaped honeycomb with broken diagonal symmetry for enhanced tunability of equivalent elastic properties and bandgap characteristics
abstract: The design of multifunctional honeycomb structures faces critical challenges due to the inherent trade-off between load-bearing capacity and vibration isolation performance. In this paper, a novel geometrically asymmetric design approach for star-shaped honeycombs is proposed through the differential configuration of bidirectional re-entrant angles. The in-plane equivalent elastic properties of the developed diagonal symmetry-broken star-shaped honeycomb (DSB-SSH) under uniaxial loading are calculated using the theoretical model derived from Castigliano’s second theorem. Moreover, a dynamic dispersion model is developed by combining the finite element (FE) method with Timoshenko beam theory to characterize the wave propagation behaviors. The modulation mechanism of geometrically asymmetric design on the equivalent elastic properties and wave propagation behaviors of the DSB-SSH is investigated via parametric analysis and experimental measurements. The results indicate that the tunability of the equivalent elastic modulus and Poisson’s ratio is significantly enhanced due to the transition of the compressive deformation mode driven by differential configuration angles. Additional bandgaps of the DSB-SSH are opened by splitting the crossing dispersion branches induced by modal degeneracy, leading to a broadened vibration isolation bandwidth. Both the enhanced static load-bearing stiffness and the low-frequency broadband vibration isolation performance of the DSB-SSH are experimentally validated through uniaxial quasi-static compression and vibration transmission tests. Therefore, the proposed geometrically asymmetric design strategy based on differentiated re-entrant angle configurations provides a straightforward approach to tailoring the multifunctional mechanical properties of honeycomb structures without introducing additional functional components, thereby significantly broadening their practical application scenarios.

title: Internal combination resonance in a Micro Electro-Mechanical three-axis gyroscope: Experimental results and reduced-order modelling via invariant manifolds
abstract: This work investigates internal combination resonance in a Micro-Electro-Mechanical System (MEMS) three-axis gyroscope, where energy couples among three vibrational modes via the relationship ω1 + ω2 ≈ ω3 . The phenomenon is first characterised experimentally through frequency response measurements and spectrograms, revealing paired resonance peaks that emerge only under dual-frequency excitation. A theoretical framework grounded in complex normal form theory is then developed, deriving analytical expressions for the frequency-response curves which are shown to replicate the experimental findings. A reduced-order model of the fully coupled electromechanical problem is constructed via Direct Parametrisation of Invariant Manifolds applied to the full finite element mesh (1.3 million degrees of freedom), demonstrating quantitative agreement with experiments and validating the predicted mechanisms. By combining invariant manifold parametrisation with complex normal form theory, the methodology bridges the gap between analytical understanding and practical finite element reduction, yielding explicit solutions for nonlinear phenomena whilst maintaining computational efficiency for large-scale systems. The results validate invariant manifold methods as a robust tool for MEMS design and control applications.

title: A joint optimization network for force identification on nonlinear structures
abstract: Accurate force identification is fundamental to the structural health monitoring and integrity assessment of complex engineering systems. However, nonlinear structural dynamics invalidate the superposition principle and render the inverse problem ill-posed, making dynamic force identification highly challenging. Existing model-driven and algorithm unrolling (AU) methods rely on explicit analytical forward models to compute Jacobian matrices, which are often unavailable for practical nonlinear structures. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a joint optimization network (JO-Net) for nonlinear structural force identification. JO-Net replaces the analytical Jacobian with an automatically differentiable surrogate model embedded in a deep unrolling framework. The surrogate network learns nonlinear forward dynamics and provides sensitivity information via automatic differentiation, while the proximal gradient descent algorithm is unrolled into a layer-wise network with a convolutional encoder–decoder serving as a learnable proximal operator. A key feature of JO-Net is the simultaneous optimization of the surrogate model and the inverse AU network, enabling adaptive refinement of structural mappings and mitigation of modeling errors. Numerical and experimental validations on nonlinear structures demonstrate that JO-Net significantly outperforms purely data-driven and model-based Kalman filter methods. By combining the surrogate model gradient with a data-driven gradient mapping matrix, the proposed method achieves a better balance between robustness and accuracy. Furthermore, JO-Net demonstrates superior robustness against measurement uncertainties and maintains reliable identification performance for unseen force–amplitude ranges within the tested nonlinear structures.

title: Nonlinear stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor for UAV blade damage monitoring through hybrid deep learning
abstract: Real-time damage type monitoring of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) blades is essential for flight safety and operational efficiency. Vibration analysis serves as an effective approach to characterize blade damage types. However, existing vibration monitoring technologies exhibit limited responsiveness to low-acceleration vibrations and struggle to capture damage-induced signatures during flight. To address these limitations, this study proposes a nonlinear stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor (NS-TVS). Leveraging its nonlinear stiffness mechanism, the sensor achieves a broad monitoring frequency range of 5 to 1500 Hz and sensitivity to anomalous vibration responses induced by blade damage. Experimental results demonstrate the output characteristics of the NS-TVS and its adaptability to UAV. Outperforming conventional vibration sensors, the NS-TVS achieves a peak sensitivity of 8.33 V/g, an acceleration detection limit of 0.1 g, and an SNR of 45.27 dB under weak excitation. Accounting for merely 5% of a single UAV arm’s payload, it imposes negligible disturbance on blade aerodynamics. For signal processing and condition assessment, a gated-attention-based convolutional recurrent neural network (GA-CRNN) was developed for feature extraction and classification across seven predefined blade types. Experimental findings revealed that the proposed model achieved an average classification accuracy of 95.96% in identifying the predefined blade damage types. The GA-CRNN was subsequently deployed on a UAV onboard computer, and actual flight tests verified the sensor’s engineering practicality and reliability.

title: An efficient fractional Sobol-Quasi-Monte Carlo simulation based reliability estimation with enhanced explainability of machine tool’s thermal error prediction model under sensor degradation
abstract: In machine tools, thermal error compensation is preferred over avoidance due to its lower cost and ease of implementation. However, compensation effectiveness depends on the thermal-error prediction model’s (TEPM’s) robustness. Existing approaches for TEPM selection fail to capture model reliability under degraded sensor states, as they employ accuracy-only selection metrics that consider only healthy states (or only a limited subset of sensor-degradation states), overlook the selection rationale, incur high computational cost, and lose accuracy for non-linear, multi-sensor, mixed degradation. Hence, the present work proposes a novel reliability-driven, explainable framework for robust selection of TEPM under resistance temperature detector (RTD) sensor degradation. For TEPM’s reliability estimation, a physics-reliant RTD degradation plant that emulates all potential sensor states (i.e., normal/lag/noisy/failed) is integrated with a computationally efficient fractional-Sobol quasi-Monte Carlo (FS-QMC) scheme, which covers both discrete degraded-sensor combinations and continuous degradation parameters without limit-state linearization. As degraded sensors increase from one to three, results from a turning-center case-study show significant reliability decline in considered TEPMs [MLR (57% to 17%), SVR (78% to 49%), FFNN (78% to 54%), and LSTM (93% to 79%), based on different learning mechanisms], which is not aligned with accuracy on healthy data. FS-QMC exhibits reliability trends similar to those of the Monte Carlo method while improving computational efficiency by approximately 80%, 57%, and 43% for one, two, and three-degraded sensors, respectively. Compared with the reported literature, the proposed degradation-aware explainability approach identified sensors whose degraded states govern model performance and uniquely quantified sensors’ criticality in an enhanced manner.

title: Phase-locked masking-based vibration cyclostationarity analysis for wear characterization of cylinder liner-piston ring in simulated ammonia engine environment
abstract: Online wear monitoring of the cylinder liner–piston ring (CL-PR) in engines is inherently challenging since friction-induced vibration is masked by reversal impacts and background disturbances. This challenge is further exacerbated in ammonia engines. In this study, a series of experiments were conducted under simulated ammonia-contaminated lubrication conditions, and vibration and friction signals were obtained online. Subsequently, a phase-locked masking method was proposed to extract the sliding region vibration signal, and second-order cyclostationary behavior was quantified using the indicator of cyclostationarity (ICS2). Combining the 1/3-binary tree filter bank with ICS2 to select the optimal frequency band, the cyclic modulation intensity associated with the reciprocating motion period in the vibration signal was quantitatively characterized. Results show that the ICS2 of the sliding region signal is sensitive to lubricant degradation and shows a positive linear fitting relationship with wear volume (R2 = 0.7887), with a higher fitting performance than conventional indicators such as RMS and kurtosis. The proposed method suppresses reversal region interference and highlights friction-induced periodic modulation in the sliding region. These results provide a potential characteristic parameter and an analytical basis for future online vibration monitoring of abnormal CL-PR wear in ammonia engines.

title: Toward compressive sensing of track irregularities
abstract: The management of massive track irregularity data from extensive railway networks poses significant challenges in storage, transmission, and processing.
