The methodology exchanges finite-element sparsity for analytical tractability, positioning it as a component of digital twin applications, in which the updated operators are interpreted as reduced models condensed onto the instrumented degrees of freedom and the measured modes are taken to span that reduced space. In that setting operator-level uncertainty quantification supports probabilistic forward prediction, data assimilation, and lifecycle prognostics that sampling-based alternatives render prohibitive. The scope of the paper is the operator statistics themselves, and their embedding in a particular assimilation architecture is left open. The framework requires as many sensors as identified modes, with the analytical operators condensed onto those sensors, and it recovers the true mass exactly on the span of the identified modes.

title: Control strategy design for an AESDFD-Rotor system under uncertainty based on axial dynamic coupling analysis
abstract: The active elastic support-dry friction damper (AESDFD) provides adjustable stiffness and damping for multi-mode vibration control of aero-engine rotor systems over a wide speed range. However, support stiffness and friction coefficient may deviate from their nominal values in practical systems, resulting in changes in the control performance obtained from deterministic designs. To address this issue, this study investigates the AESDFD-rotor system under parametric uncertainty. The support stiffness and friction coefficient are modeled as ± 10% interval uncertain parameters. Stiffness sensitivity and modal participation factor analyses are used to examine the effects of damper configuration, the stick–sliding state, and axial modal redistribution on the control performance. The influence of rotational speed on the stick–sliding transition is then analyzed to determine the control interval for different modes. Based on these analyses, a damper-oriented Kriging-based decoupled double-loop optimization (DK-DDLO) method is developed to optimize the worst-case vibration response within the prescribed parameter intervals. Under ± 10% uncertainties in support stiffness and friction coefficient, the worst-case vibration responses of the first and second modes are reduced by 96.1% and 90.1%.

title: Blade-tip vibration informed latent physics residual prognostics for fatigue crack growth and remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Fatigue crack growth prognosis of blades remains challenging because crack length is difficult to measure continuously, while vibration responses are influenced by both damage evolution and loading conditions. A blade-tip vibration-informed latent physics residual prognostics (LPRP) framework is proposed for crack-growth modeling and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. Blade-tip displacement and resonance-frequency degradation are used to characterize loading response and structural degradation, respectively, enabling crack-growth-rate prediction without direct crack-length input. Resonance fatigue tests on four compressor blades show that LPRP reduces the mean LOBO RMSE of logarithmic crack-growth-rate prediction from 0.482 to 0.274 and the macro-averaged RUL RMSE from 1.93×105 to 7.25×104 cycles. The results demonstrate the potential of LPRP for non-contact blade crack-growth prognosis.

title: Modified factorized wave model for pipe leak localization via a single access point
abstract: Matched-field processing (MFP) is an accurate, robust, and efficient method for leak localization in water supply pipes. However, its existing built-in wave model requires multiple access points to place pressure sensors, which cannot be guaranteed for buried pipes. To address this problem, this paper derives a modified factorized wave model based on the small-leak approximation. It allows MFP to be implemented via a single access point. Compared with existing models, the modified model is less sensitive to modeling errors, which are canceled out in the analytical derivation. Numerical tests demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately localize a single leak and distinguish multiple leaks with a separation distance larger than the diffraction limit. Laboratory experiments validate that the proposed method can successfully localize unknown leaks in a high-density polyethylene pipe even with the practical field noise.

title: Multi-source uncertainty-aware hierarchical RESCINet residual correction model with conformal adaptive threshold interval for wind turbine condition monitoring
abstract: Condition monitoring based on Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) data can track operating states and support wind turbine maintenance decisions. Nevertheless, due to the complex temporal dynamics, variable coupling, local fluctuations, and uncertainty variations, accurate target parameter prediction and reliable threshold interval construction remain challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hierarchical residual-enhanced sample convolution and interaction network (RESCINet) residual correction prediction model and a multi-source uncertainty-driven conformal adaptive threshold interval for wind turbine condition monitoring. In data preprocessing, after Kalman filtering and Pearson-correlation variable screening, random resampling is performed to obtain multiple datasets, thereby mitigating the impact of data uncertainty and enhancing prediction reliability. In the prediction model, a sample convolution and interaction (SCI) mechanism enhanced by a gated residual path is proposed to better retain local sequence information, and candidate features from different network depths are used for hierarchical residual correction of the base prediction. In threshold interval construction, the proposed method constructs a multi-source prediction uncertainty scale from data and model uncertainty, standardizes conformal residuals using this scale, and updates the conformal quantile online to construct the adaptive threshold interval. The proposed method is evaluated on two real-world wind turbine fault cases involving the pitch and converter systems. The results show that the proposed prediction model improves prediction accuracy and that the proposed interval provides earlier alarms than the compared threshold interval methods.

title: A 2-DOF thin-plate piezoelectric actuator using traveling-wave and radial-bending hybrid vibration modes for multispectral imaging
abstract: To address the integration requirements of multispectral imaging for a miniaturized multi-degree-of-freedom (DOF) actuator, this study proposes a 2-DOF thin-plate piezoelectric actuator (TPPA). A proposed multiplexed excitation strategy for spatially arranged piezoelectric ceramics independently excites circumferential traveling waves and radial-bending hybrid modes in a thin-plate stator, enabling decoupled rotary and linear motions. The finite element method is utilized to analyze the driving trajectories by adjusting geometric parameters. Subsequently, a prototype measuring 34 × 34 × 6 mm3 with a mass of 7.2 g was fabricated. Vibration characterization tests confirmed the successful modal excitation and design feasibility. Experimental results indicate that the maximum linear and rotary speeds, output force, and torque reach 148.3 mm/s, 223.8 RPM, 196 mN, and 0.644 mN·m, respectively, alongside displacement resolutions of 0.24 μm and 19.64 μrad in burst mode. Furthermore, integrating the TPPA into a filtering-focusing mechanism successfully demonstrated spectral channel switching and chromatic focal shift compensation. Focused imaging tests across four spectral bands confirmed the practical capability of the mechanism, proving that decoupled 2-DOF control significantly improves multispectral imaging quality. This study provides a compact actuation solution for the integration of multispectral imaging mechanisms.

title: A novel Order-domain rotating machinery anomaly detection towards non-stationary operating conditions
abstract: Rotating machinery in real industrial systems operates under non-stationary conditions with continuous speed fluctuations, while fault data are extremely scarce due to the high cost and risk of data acquisition. This study proposes a novel Order-domain Graph Residual Autoencoder for anomaly detection under variable-speed conditions with zero fault samples. The method first performs feature extraction based on local time–frequency domain order mapping through the short-time Fourier transform, decoupling fault features from rotational speed. An order-domain graph structure is then constructed by balancing global temporal information aggregation with local speed-invariant characteristics, enabling the model to autonomously learn optimal inter-window feature aggregation patterns. Finally, the graph residual autoencoder with an adaptive gating mechanism learns low-dimensional manifold representations of normal states through dynamic residual connection adjustment and adaptive noise injection, achieving fault detection under both known and unknown speed conditions. Experimental validation is performed on a public dataset and an evolving simulator dataset characterized by fluctuating operating conditions. Superior performance compared to other commonly used anomaly detection methods is achieved without any fault information, along with satisfactory interpretability. The proposed framework provides a promising solution for intelligent health monitoring of rotating machinery in complex variable-speed industrial scenarios.

title: Enhanced broadband 2-DOF rotational energy harvester incorporating centrifugally stiffened and softened beams
abstract: This study proposes a two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) rotational bistable piezoelectric energy harvester that integrates a centrifugally stiffened beam with a centrifugally softened beam. An electromechanically coupled nonlinear dynamic model is established based on the extended Hamilton’s principle, and the dynamic responses and electrical output characteristics are investigated through numerical and experimental studies. The results show that the complementary centrifugal tuning characteristics of the two beams produce two dominant response regions and a corresponding dual-peak broadband electrical response over the investigated rotational-frequency range up to 125 rad/s. Compared with a typical one-degree-of-freedom (1-DOF) rotational bistable harvester, the proposed 2-DOF design expands the frequency-swept displacement-response bandwidth by 112.5%. Experimental results further verify the predicted evolution of motion states and the dual-peak voltage output. Using an average-power threshold of 1 μW, the experimentally validated effective power band extends continuously from approximately 40 to 125 rad/s. In addition, a self-powered TPMS demonstration confirms that the harvested rotational energy can be rectified and regulated to drive a commercial wireless sensor. The proposed design offers a practical strategy for broadening the operational bandwidth of rotational piezoelectric energy harvesters for tire-mounted self-powered sensing applications.

title: A novel inverse super element method for structural shape and stress sensing
abstract: The inverse finite element method (iFEM) has been widely adopted in shape sensing, as it enables full-field reconstruction of structural displacements and stresses by minimizing a weighted least–squares functional of the discrepancy between theoretical and measured strains. However, when the measured strain data are sparse, the equivalent equilibrium equations derived from iFEM become severely ill–conditioned, which tends to underestimate the reconstruction results. To overcome this limitation, this paper presents a novel inverse super–element method (iSEM). Unlike iFEM, where the error functional is formulated at the element level, iSEM constructs the strain error functional directly over the entire structural domain. Through static condensation of degrees of freedom, the equivalent equilibrium equations are reduced to a set of user–selected Primary degrees of freedoms. Together with an energy–based regularization (EBR) strategy grounded in the principle of minimum energy, the proposed method markedly alleviates the ill–posedness of the equilibrium equations. Notably, iSEM does not rely on any concept of master and slave elements; so strain measurements can be taken with greater flexibility in sensor placement. The performance of iSEM is validated through both finite–element simulations and physical model experiments. The results indicate that under sparse uniaxial strain measurements, iSEM reconstructs the structural displacement and strain fields with high fidelity, achieving significantly lower relative errors than iFEM while exhibiting reduced sensitivity to the EBR coefficient. Overall, iSEM provides a novel theoretical framework for high–accuracy shape and stress sensing in scenarios involving sparse strain measurements.

title: Steering feedback torque prediction using a driving-condition clustering-enhanced sequence-to-sequence network
abstract: Accurate prediction of Steering Feedback Torque (SFT) is a key challenge in steer-by-wire (SbW) development, as it directly determines the realism and controllability of the steering experience. Traditional physics-based models rely on complex calibration and struggle to capture the nonlinear, time-varying dynamics inherent in real-world vehicle signals. To address this, a clustering-enhanced SFT prediction framework that integrates driving state clustering with a sequence-to-sequence (S2S) network is proposed. A multi-channel signal dataset, comprising steering, inertial, and wheel-speed measurements, is acquired from on-road experiments on an instrumented test vehicle across diverse driving scenarios. Driving features extracted from these signals are first clustered via unsupervised learning, and the resulting cluster membership probabilities are embedded as supplementary features into the multivariate time series input. This enhances the model’s generalization across driving conditions and improves interpretability by linking model behavior to identifiable driving patterns. An S2S network is then trained to capture the temporal dependencies specific to the steering system. Hardware-in-the-loop experiments with driver-in-the-loop operation confirm that the proposed method outperforms conventional static regression models and non-clustered baselines in both common and extreme driving scenarios.

title: Electromagnetic vibration energy harvester with displacement amplification mechanism
abstract: Electromagnetic vibration energy harvesters (EVEHs) offer a promising alternative to chemical batteries for powering low-power sensing devices, yet their energy harvesting performance is often constrained by the limited relative motion of conventional spring–mass systems. To address this limitation, a displacement-amplified EVEH is proposed, in which the vertical motion of a main mass is converted into transverse relative motion between two horizontal sliders via a triangular lever mechanism, enabling enhanced magnetic flux variation. The geometric amplification characteristics are analyzed, showing that effective displacement amplification is achieved when the assembly angle exceeds 44.91°. A coupled nonlinear electromechanical model is established based on the Lagrange–Maxwell formulation, and the nonlinear dynamic responses are investigated using the semi-analytical harmonic balance–alternating frequency/time (HB-AFT) method combined with arc-length continuation and Floquet stability analysis. The results indicate that the system exhibits effective two-degree-of-freedom behavior with two resonance peaks under equal slider masses, whereas unequal mass configurations lead to effective three-degree-of-freedom characteristics with an additional resonance and broadened energy harvesting bandwidth. Parametric studies further reveal the influences of mass distribution, damping, and stiffness on the amplitude–frequency responses and nonlinear characteristics. Compared with a conventional harvester without displacement amplification, the proposed system achieves a significant enhancement in output voltage, with improvements on the order of two times. An experimental prototype is developed, and the measured results show good agreement with the theoretical predictions, validating the proposed model and analysis.

title: Autoencoder-based dimensionality reduction with multi-layer perceptron surrogates for global sensitivity analysis of high-dimensional nonlinear responses
abstract: Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) of models producing high-dimensional distributed responses remains challenging, as classical Sobol’-based methods become computationally inefficient to apply directly to complex response fields. This paper proposes an autoencoder (AE)-based dimensionality reduction framework combined with multi-layer perceptron (MLP) surrogates for efficient Sobol’-based GSA of high-dimensional nonlinear responses. To accommodate different response characteristics, multiple AE architectures are incorporated to enable effective compression of sequential, spatially correlated, and uncertainty-driven model outputs, while preserving the dominant variance structure of the original responses in a reduced latent space. An MLP surrogate is constructed to learn the nonlinear mapping from model parameters to latent variables. To ensure consistency of variance-related characteristics between latent-space and original-space sensitivity measures, a decoder-based pull-back strategy is introduced to propagate variance contributions back to the physical response domain, facilitating Sobol’-based GSA in the original response space. The proposed autoencoder-assisted multi-layer perceptron (AE-MLP) framework is capable of addressing sensitivity analysis problems associated with highly complex systems and extremely high-dimensional distributed responses, that are difficult to handle without using dimensionality reduction techniques. Numerical benchmark studies and engineering applications demonstrate that the AE-MLP framework achieves accurate sensitivity ranking with significantly reduced computational cost.

title: A boundary-coupled unified frictional hysteresis model for metal rubber under quasi-static and dynamic loading
abstract: Metal rubber (MR) contains numerous internal contact, sliding, and frictional interfaces among metallic wires, which leads to pronounced nonlinear and hysteretic characteristics under quasi-static and dynamic loading conditions. Existing hysteresis models are mostly developed for specific loading conditions and are therefore unable to uniformly describe the transition from quasi-static compressive behavior to dynamic hysteretic response in MR materials. Moreover, their capability to characterize asymmetric hysteretic behavior and equilibrium-position shifts remains limited under variations in biased mass, pre-compression, and support configuration. To address these issues, a boundary-coupled unified frictional hysteresis model (BC-UFH) is proposed in this study. Within this framework, the quasi-static frictional hysteresis (QFH) form is adopted as the baseline to identify the nonlinear elastic and frictional hysteresis parameters of MR under quasi-static compression, thereby providing the parameter basis for the subsequent dynamic extension and boundary-coupled mapping. On this basis, a dynamic frictional hysteresis (DFH) extension form is further developed by introducing a dynamic slip-softening term and a pore-gas pumping viscous damping term. By incorporating the boundary conditions of unilateral and symmetric support configurations, the BC-UFH model provides a unified description of quasi-static and dynamic responses. The proposed model enables the quasi-static compressive properties of MR materials to be consistently transformed into dynamic hysteretic responses under different support configurations. The model is validated through quasi-static compression tests and dynamic loading experiments under different support configurations. The results show that the unified model can not only accurately describe the quasi-static hysteretic response of MR materials, but also effectively characterize the dynamic hysteretic behavior under different support configurations. In addition, it can explain the asymmetric hysteresis loops and equilibrium-position shifts induced by biased loading conditions. The proposed method provides an effective reference for parameter identification, structural design, and engineering application of MR isolators.

title: Triggering high-energy orbits in rotational nonlinear energy harvesters via time-varying external excitation and internal parameter modulation
abstract: The nonlinear dynamics of rotational piezoelectric energy harvesters can enhance power output and broaden the operational bandwidth. However, their practical application is severely constrained by uncontrollable switching between the high-energy orbit (HEO) and low-energy orbit (LEO) induced by nonlinearity and time-varying effects. In addition, centrifugal effects significantly raise the energy threshold required for the harvester to reach the HEO state. To address these challenges, this study proposes an HEO-excitation strategy that combines time-varying external excitation with internal system parameter modulation, enabling synergistic improvements in both power output and operational bandwidth. First, an analytical model of a centrifugal-force-affected rotational harvester is established. A representative nonlinear rotational piezoelectric energy harvester is then designed, and its theoretical model is derived using the method of multiple scales. Next, HEO excitation is investigated through two mechanisms: external rotational frequency modulation and internal electrically induced damping modulation. The corresponding orbit-jump behaviors and performance enhancement effects are validated experimentally. For implementation, rotational frequency modulation is realized through a motor controller, while electrically induced damping modulation is achieved using a bidirectional energy conversion circuit. By inducing and stabilizing the HEO state, the proposed method achieves a maximum 911% increase in output power and a 62.5% expansion of the operational bandwidth. In addition, the harvester operating in the HEO state enables self-powered LoRa-based wireless temperature sensing. Through coordinated parameter modulation, this work presents a new strategy for rotational energy harvesting, providing an effective route for HEO excitation and self-powered sensing.

title: Bayesian model updating via streamlined Bayesian active learning cubature
abstract: Bayesian model updating has been widely used for model calibration in engineering and scientific applications, as it not only updates model parameters but also quantifies their uncertainty. However, for computationally expensive models, efficiently estimating the model evidence (marginal likelihood) and the posterior distribution remains challenging. To address this issue, we propose a novel Bayesian active learning method for Bayesian model updating, which is termed as ‘Streamlined Bayesian Active Learning Cubature’ (SBALC). The core idea is to approximate the log-likelihood function using Gaussian process (GP) regression in a streamlined Bayesian active learning way. Rather than generating many samples from the posterior GP, we only use its mean and standard deviation function to form the model evidence estimator, stopping criterion, and learning function. Specifically, the estimation of model evidence is first treated as a Bayesian cubature problem, with a GP prior assigned over the log-likelihood function. Second, a plug-in estimator for model evidence is proposed based on the posterior mean function of the GP. Third, an upper bound on the expected absolute error between the posterior model evidence and its plug-in estimator is derived. Building on this result, a novel stopping criterion and learning function are proposed using only the posterior mean and standard deviation functions of the GP. Finally, we can obtain the model evidence based on the posterior mean function of the log-likelihood function in conjunction with Monte Carlo simulation, as well as the samples for the posterior distribution of model parameters as a by-product. Four numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method compared to several existing approaches. The results show that the method can significantly reduce the number of model evaluations and the computational time without compromising accuracy.

title: Experimentally validated reduced-order modeling of gear-rotor-bearing systems with three-dimensional shaft compliance and gyroscopic mapping
abstract: Traditional one-dimensional beam models cannot adequately represent the three-dimensional local compliance of stepped transmission shafts, whereas full solid models are inefficient for system-level nonlinear simulations. This study proposes a high-fidelity reduced-order model for gear-rotor-bearing systems by combining Craig-Bampton condensation of solid shaft models with equivalent gyroscopic mapping. Continuously distributed coupling reference points are assigned at shaft shoulders, bearing locations, and gear mounting positions to retain local softening and non-planar warping. Speed-dependent gyroscopic terms are formulated using rotating Timoshenko beam elements and lumped-disk contributions, and embedded into the condensed coordinate space through coordinate transformation, degree-of-freedom alignment, and subspace mapping. The model is validated by input-shaft modal testing and gearbox vibration experiments. Compared with the one-dimensional Timoshenko beam model, the proposed model improves modal-frequency prediction and captures the dominant periodic and mesh-order vibration features. Neglecting local shaft compliance shifts modal frequencies, critical speeds, dynamic transmission error, and nonlinear transition boundaries. The method provides a physically consistent basis for modal prediction, critical-speed evaluation, vibration analysis, and nonlinear stability assessment of high-speed gear-rotor-bearing systems.

title: Flexural-wave shielding in plates through scattering by a curved resonator arrangement
abstract: This study considers a thin elastic plate excited by a harmonic point force and coupled to locally resonant mass–spring attachments distributed along two opposing parabolic trajectories. The resulting resonator arrangement redirects part of the incident flexural-wave energy through repeated scattering along the curved interface, thereby reducing transmission beyond the curved array and producing a downstream shielded region. An analytical model is formulated within the Kirchhoff–Love plate framework, where the Green’s function of an unbounded plate is used to describe the dynamic interaction between the host structure and the resonators. Three-dimensional finite-element simulations are used to verify the analytical predictions and characterize the redistribution of the wave field around the resonator arrangement. Experimental measurements are performed on an aluminum plate equipped with a water-jet-cut resonator arrangement using scanning laser Doppler vibrometry. The combined analytical, numerical, and experimental results show that the curved resonator arrangement produces a pronounced vibration-shielding zone beyond the resonator interface, with a substantial reduction in transmitted flexural-wave amplitude. Parametric analyses quantify the effects of curvature, normalized resonator spacing, and excitation frequency. The resulting design maps identify spacing regimes that minimize the shielded response and provide practical guidelines for curvature-based wave-shielding designs in continuous plate structures.

title: Adaptive event-triggered soft actor-critic control for MR suspension subject to actuator smoothness constraints
abstract: Magnetorheological (MR) suspension control faces high computational and communication burdens, large actuator force fluctuations, and reduced damper service life. This study proposes an adaptive event-triggered soft actor-critic (AET-SAC) control strategy subject to actuator smoothness constraints. First, a quarter-vehicle MR suspension dynamic model incorporating first-order actuator dynamics and hard constraints on the control-force change rate is established. Next, a dual smoothness constraint mechanism is incorporated into the SAC framework. A multi-objective reward function is designed to balance vibration suppression performance, actuator energy consumption, and damper service life. Then, an adaptive event-triggered mechanism based on the relative error of body acceleration is incorporated into the policy inference process, with the triggering threshold adjusted according to the vibration intensity to reduce unnecessary control updates. Lyapunov theory is used to establish uniform ultimate boundedness of the closed-loop system and the absence of the Zeno phenomenon. Finally, comprehensive simulations are conducted under bump and random road conditions, together with hardware-in-the-loop experiments on an STM32H753 embedded platform. The results show that, compared with the passive suspension, the proposed AET-SAC strategy reduces the RMS value of body acceleration by more than 60% and unnecessary control updates by approximately 58%. In addition, the proposed strategy provides smoother control-force output and lower actuator energy consumption than the AET-TD3, AET-DDPG, and conventional LQR controllers.

title: An integrated autoencoder-based framework for unsupervised domain adaptation in structural health monitoring of bridges
abstract: The limited availability of long-term bridge-monitoring data presents a significant obstacle to the application of machine learning in structural health monitoring (SHM). Domain adaptation offers a means of addressing this data scarcity, but existing methods often have limited generalization and are sensitive to hyperparameter choices. This study proposes a reconstruction-based domain adaptation framework in which target-domain observations are geometrically aligned with the latent space learned by an autoencoder trained on data from a source bridge and, subsequently, reconstructed using its decoder. Unlike conventional feature-alignment approaches, the proposed formulation transfers the reconstruction model itself, enabling target-domain evaluation without labels, classifier retraining, or threshold recalibration. The autoencoder is trained on baseline data collected during commissioning of the source bridge, using observations composed of natural frequencies as damage-sensitive features. Adaptation is performed through orthogonal Procrustes alignment in the latent space, followed by reconstruction with the source-trained decoder. Validation using the Z24 Bridge dataset demonstrates that the framework mitigates seasonal domain shift while preserving sensitivity to controlled damage. The approach is then transferred to a twin bridge over the Itacaiúnas River using only latent-space alignment and no model retraining. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables damage assessment across bridges while substantially reducing the data and training requirements for practical deployment.

title: Novel power-sine arch nonlinear energy sink: design, dynamic modeling and torsional vibration suppression performance
abstract: Torsional vibration suppression has always been a tough bottleneck restricting the stable operation of rotating machinery. Conventional torsional nonlinear energy sinks (NESs) adopt discrete multi-component structures, which inevitably introduce multi-body friction and parasitic linear stiffness, and their stiffness characteristics cannot be flexibly tuned within limited installation space. This work proposes a novel quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) torsional NES based on geometric nonlinear deformation of power-sine arches. Symmetric pre-compressed arch units are utilized to generate purely geometric nonlinear stiffness within the absorber. This structural design eliminates frictional energy loss inherent in traditional configurations and achieves a broad and stable QZS operating range. Two dynamic models, including a two-degree-of-freedom rotor system and a multi-degree-of-freedom gear transmission system integrated with the proposed NES, are constructed to analyze its vibration reduction capacity. Quasi-static compression experiments validate the accuracy of the finite element model. Torsional vibration bench tests further demonstrate that the proposed NES can effectively suppress the primary resonance peak during speed acceleration, deliver favorable broadband vibration attenuation and significantly delay the onset of resonance. Under steady-state resonant operating conditions, the absorber achieves remarkable vibration attenuation. It can act as a lightweight and high-stability passive vibration mitigation solution for various rotating machinery.

title: Semi-analytical study on low-frequency bandgap of lightweight corrugated-core sandwich meta-plate using spectral element method
abstract: In this paper, the elastic wave propagation and low-frequency bandgap characteristics of a lightweight high-strength corrugated-core sandwich meta-plate (CSMP) with local resonators under simply supported boundary conditions is studied. Based on the spectral element method, a non-equivalent high-precision theoretical wave dynamic model of CSMP is established to calculate the band structure and transmission characteristics of the structure. The low-frequency bandgap generation mechanism is revealed and the comprehensive performance of the proposed CSMP is compared with that of the typical sandwich metastructures. Numerical calculation and experimental tests are conducted to verify the proposed theoretical model. Results show that the proposed CSMP with only 1.77% mass ratio local resonators can exhibit a low-frequency bandgap, demonstrating significant flexural waves attenuation and excellent vibration isolation performance. The starting and cutoff frequencies of the low-frequency band gap are mainly attributed to the vibration coupling of the local resonator with the connecting plate and corrugated-core sandwich plate respectively. The prediction results of the theoretical model are consistent with those of numerical simulation and experimental test, which verifies the correctness of the proposed theoretical model. The flexural wave bandgap can be effectively adjusted by reasonably changing the design parameters of the CSMP.

title: Editorial Board
Physics-consistent Bayesian early warning of wind turbine blade stall using an auxiliary regularized particle filter
abstract: Early warning of wind turbine blade stall is difficult because early aerodynamic degradation is weak and easily masked by operating-condition variability and non-Gaussian disturbances in SCADA data. This study proposes a physics-consistent Bayesian sequential early-warning framework based on an auxiliary regularized particle filter. A physically constrained nonlinear state-space model with a latent health factor represents aerodynamic degradation while preserving the coupling among wind speed, rotor speed, and power. For stable inference under turbulence and model mismatch, the likelihood-enhanced filter adds a bounded operating-condition likelihood correction, stall-risk-gated noise adaptation, and kernel-density-regularized resampling. A decision layer with dynamic thresholds, persistence constraints, and a recovery-time criterion converts pointwise anomalies into event-level warnings. The framework is validated on historical SCADA data from two wind farms, covering 8 fault cases and 60 healthy runs. Across the eight fault runs, ARPF achieves a mean two-hour pre-shutdown coverage (Coverage@2h) of 96.7%, exceeding RPF by 8.5% and EKF/UKF by 81.3%. On the two stall cases at wind farm A, ARPF detects and warns on both, whereas four standard data-driven baselines (random forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and CNN) detect at most one. These results show that the proposed framework provides earlier and more sustained blade-stall early warning from SCADA data than the Gaussian-filter and power-curve-residual baselines, while maintaining reliability under varying operating conditions.

title: Nonlinear dynamic modeling and parameter identification of air springs in the ultra-low frequency range considering thermal hysteresis
abstract: The nonlinear dynamic performance of a constrained rolling-lobe air spring (CRLAS) is measured using a servo-controlled hydraulic test rig. Experimental results indicate that in the ultra-low frequency range (0.002–1 Hz), the dynamic stiffness increases sharply, while the loss angle increases firstly and then decreases. However, current literature exhibits two primary limitations regarding the nonlinear dynamics of air springs at ultra-low frequencies: 1) parameter identification methods for the heat transfer coefficient are absent, 2) efficient frequency-domain models analyzing the thermodynamic processes of air inside the air spring at ultra-low frequencies are not well developed. To address these gaps, a nonlinear time-domain model considering friction and thermal hysteresis generated by air pressure inside the air spring is established to analyze the hysteresis characteristics in ultra-low frequency range. The heat transfer coefficient is inversely identified using the perturbation amplitude of the measured pressure inside the air spring, and the proposed identification method is easy to apply in engineering applications. Secondly, the time-domain model is linearized by Taylor expansion, and the force versus displacement estimated by nonlinear and linearized models are compared with the measurement. Subsequently, a frequency-domain model is established by Laplace transformation of the linearized time-domain model to calculate the dynamic stiffness and loss angle of the air spring, demonstrating good agreement with experimental results at ultra-low frequencies. Finally, in the ultra-low frequency range, it is revealed by the proposed models that the hysteresis of the air spring is determined by friction and thermal hysteresis, and the thermodynamic process transitions from isothermal to adiabatic.

title: Remaining useful life prediction for multivariate stochastic degradation systems under functionally dependent failure modes
abstract: Multivariate stochastic degradation systems are widely encountered in complex industrial equipment, where performance deterioration exhibits coupling characteristics among multiple indicators. However, functionally dependent failure may still occur even when no single indicator exceeds its individual threshold, leading to unexpected system breakdowns. Compared with the extensive research on competing failure modes, the problem of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under functionally dependent failure scenarios has not received sufficient attention. In this paper, a nonlinear Wiener process framework is established to model the degradation process of multivariate systems. A Copula-based model is employed to describe nonlinear dependencies among degradation variables, and a vector envelope plane method is developed to approximate complex functionally dependent failure boundaries. Bayesian MCMC (Markov chain Monte Carlo) is used for offline parameter estimation, while sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) is adopted for online updating. Furthermore, analytical and semi-analytical RUL distributions are derived for linear and nonlinear associations, respectively, based on first passage time theory. The linear case is handled through equivalent transformation of multivariate degradation processes, while the nonlinear case is addressed using a Copula-based dependence representation combined with the vector envelope plane approximation. Finally, numerical simulations and two engineering case studies involving gearboxes and gyroscopes are conducted to evaluate the prediction performance of the proposed method.

title: Analytical study on the vibration of spatial plate-plate coupled structures with combined simply supported and clamped edges
abstract: Spatial plate-plate coupled structures (cross, L, and T-shaped) are fundamental elements in engineering, yet a unified solution covering multiple coupling configurations, arbitrary coupling angles, and combined simply supported-clamped boundaries remains unavailable. This study develops a unified and rigorous analytical framework using the finite integral transform (FIT) method to obtain the closed-form solutions for free and forced vibrations of coupled plates, without shape function assumptions or numerical discretization. Validations against finite element analysis (FEA) show errors below 1%, demonstrating high accuracy. The main contributions of this study are the derivation of a unified analytical solution for coupled plates and the revelation of mechanistic insights based on the closed-form solution. These new insights include: rigid coupling makes free vibration independent of coupling angle; alternately distributed boundaries (CSCS) outperform adjacently distributed ones (CCSS) by uniformly suppressing rotation and deflection; low-order natural frequencies are sensitive only to the constraints of stiffness-dominant plates, enabling constraint simplification on non-dominant components; and rigid coupling at modal antinode lines maximizes the fundamental frequency by effectively suppressing the maximum modal deflection. These findings demonstrate that constraint spatial topology outweighs constraint number in dynamic regulation, providing an effective analytical tool for lightweight design and vibration control of coupled plate structures.

title: Fault diagnosis of high-speed train bogie bearings under domain shifts via an encoding-matching-interactive framework
abstract: Fault diagnosis of bogie bearings in high-speed trains is challenged by limited labelled data and complex domain shifts caused by varying operating conditions, which severely degrade cross-domain generalization. An encoding–matching–interaction (EMI) transfer framework is proposed to address cross-condition and cross-platform domain shifts in high-speed train bogie-bearing diagnosis. In the encoding stage, a shared convolutional encoder learns hierarchical fault representations, while class-discriminative regularization and scale-aware feature fusion enhance feature separability and transferability. In the matching stage, multilayer higher-order moment matching (mUoMM) and multiclassifier-guided adversarial domain alignment (mGADA) perform complementary marginal and conditional alignment, respectively. These adaptation objectives are further coordinated through an interaction mechanism that dynamically balances transfer objectives according to transfer states. EMI is validated on multiple public machinery benchmarks and an engineering-scale high-speed train bogie-bearing dataset, covering cross-condition, cross-device, and cross-scenario transfers. Compared with eight representative baselines, EMI achieves consistently superior performance, outperforming the best baseline by 3.97–5.43 percentage points across cross-device and engineering-scale HST transfer tasks. Robustness under additive noise during testing (SNR = 12, 8, and 4 dB) is demonstrated, with the average accuracy degradation limited to 0.9 pp. Extensive evaluations, including ablation studies, sensitivity analyses, and statistical significance analysis, further validate the effectiveness and reliability of EMI.

title: Torque evolution for wear failure assessment of a micro-transmission system
abstract: The evolution of system torque in a gear transmission system directly reflects its energy loss and degradation process. In this study, we proposed using system torque as an assessment indicator for the wear failure process of a micro-transmission system, enabling service life prediction. A dynamic simulation model of the micro-transmission system was established to obtain the kinematic characteristics, which then served as input conditions for a self-developed accelerated vibration test platform. Subsequently, torque measurements were conducted under random vibration conditions with varying multiples to obtain torque evolution curves, and the system torque was used to quantify the failure indicator. Additionally, the inverse power law (IPL) model was adopted for service life assessment, and its predictive capability was experimentally validated. The results demonstrate that using system torque as a wear failure assessment indicator effectively characterizes the wear evolution process and shows strong potential for service life prediction.

title: Multi-setup Bayesian FFT modal identification with multiple modes leveraging on second order information
abstract: Conventional multi-setup Bayesian operational modal analysis (OMA) algorithms may suffer from low efficiency and false convergence when dealing with closely-spaced modes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Newton-type Bayesian FFT algorithm to minimize the negative log-likelihood function (NLLF). The gradient vector and Hessian matrix, i.e., the first- and second-order derivatives of NLLF with respect to modal parameters, are obtained semi-analytically by exploring a latent variable structure of NLLF through the expectation–maximization (EM) formulation. The sparsity of the Hessian matrix is explored to enable a fast and robust implementation. In the optimization, an existing EM algorithm is employed in the first round of iterations to improve the positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian matrix, and Newton iterations are then performed to refine the estimate. Since the inverse of Hessian matrix is available at each iteration, the posterior covariance matrix is obtained as a by-product under the Laplace approximation, providing uncertainty quantification without additional computation. A synthetic example of a 30-story shear-type building and a field test of the 292 m SEG Plaza are applied to illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm. Results show that the proposed algorithm achieves high accuracy and fast convergence, while the existing method may fail in challenging scenarios, e.g., multiple closely-spaced modes.

title: A SASM-PDD method for random vibration fatigue damage analysis of structures with uncertain parameters
abstract: This paper develops a semi-analytical spectral moment-polynomial dimensional decomposition (SASM-PDD) method for fatigue damage assessment of structures with uncertain parameters under random loading. First, within the framework of frequency-domain random vibration fatigue analysis, a closed-form solution for the modal spectral moments of linear stochastic structures is derived. By integrating this solution with the Dirlik model, a semi-analytical framework is established to characterize fatigue damage under an induction spectrum. Building on these derivations, component function decomposition is applied to the expected damage to achieve dimension reduction of the uncertain parameters, leading to an efficient SASM-PDD method. Numerical examples involving an L-shaped plate and a notched thin plate are presented to perform sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification of fatigue damage. The accuracy and efficiency of the SASM-PDD method are validated through comparisons with Monte Carlo simulations and experimental fatigue data from the literature. Furthermore, the engineering applicability of the proposed method is demonstrated through uncertainty analysis of fatigue damage at the hotspot locations of a complex industrial fan support frame.

title: Why filter length matters in blind deconvolution for rotating machinery condition monitoring
abstract: Blind deconvolution (BD) methods are widely used in rotating machinery condition monitoring to enhance fault-related components through optimized finite-impulse-response (FIR) filters. This short communication studies a basic but insufficiently explored issue, i.e., filter length can strongly affect the reliability of diagnosis based on optimized filters. Two complementary failure mechanisms are identified. Short filters have insufficient frequency selectivity, causing interference to remain in the filtered output. This limitation is characterized by a frequency selectivity bound on the FIR frequency response, which implies a minimum filter length requirement for achieving a prescribed cutoff level over a specified frequency interval. Conversely, an excessively long filter makes the filtered output overly flexible, allowing it to approximate a prescribed fault-like pattern even when no corresponding component is present in the input. These two risks are further supported by theoretical analysis and experimental validation. Furthermore, a filter length selection method using the Fisher discriminant ratio is introduced, and experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness in identifying an appropriate filter length and mitigating the risks of filter length.

title: Rub-impact fault diagnosis for rotating blade using covariance-reconstructed MVDR and BTT data
abstract: Blade Tip Timing (BTT) is a crucial technique for monitoring the health status of rotating blades in aero-engines. However, the inherently severe non-uniform under-sampling characteristics of BTT signals make the extraction of early fault features highly challenging. To address the aforementioned issues, this paper introduces the principle of Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) method into the problem of blade fault feature identification, and proposes a MVDR algorithm based on Covariance Reconstructed to achieve rub-impact fault diagnosis of rotating blades. By utilizing subspace orthogonality to reconstruct the covariance matrix, this method effectively suppresses the spurious peak interference generated by the traditional MVDR under limited snapshot conditions, while reducing the practical computational burden under limited snapshot conditions. The results of numerical simulations and rotating blade rub-impact tests indicate that the proposed method can accurately recover the fractional harmonic features corresponding to rub-impact faults from severely under-sampling BTT data, including the nX/2 and nX/3 harmonic series, and effectively identify the nonlinear vibration responses under different rub-impact states. The relevant identification results maintain excellent consistency with the analysis results of the synchronously acquired strain signals. The research findings demonstrate that this method can effectively achieve feature extraction and early warning of rotating blade rub-impact faults, providing a feasible technical approach for the online health monitoring of aero-engine blades.

title: Development of a pneumatic-lifting magnetorheological semi-active suspension towards height adjustment capability
abstract: Single-chamber air springs (SCAS) suffer from large dynamic stiffness increments and rubber bladder failures. This paper proposes a Pneumatic-Lifting magnetorheological semi-active suspension (PLMRD) integrating a mechanical spring, a magnetorheological damper (MRD), and a rigid Pneumatic Lifting Device (PLD). The mechanical spring bears the main static load and provides fail-safe support in the event of pneumatic leakage. By replacing the rubber bladder with a rigid cylinder and mechanical spring, the large dynamic stiffness increment of SCAS is avoided. A Bingham Plastic (BP) model and a static stiffness model are established for the MRD and PLD, respectively. A combined LuGre friction and fractional-order Kelvin–Voigt model is developed to capture the PLD’s amplitude- and frequency-dependent dynamic stiffness, and the model is validated experimentally. A Displacement-Sensitive Skyhook (DS-Skyhook) control strategy is designed based on a quarter-car model to adapt damping according to suspension deflection. A quarter-car test shows that compared to the passive SCAS, the passive PLMRD reduces the root mean square (RMS) of the sprung mass acceleration by 16.41%; with the conventional Skyhook control, the reduction is 33.98%, and with the DS-Skyhook control it reaches 36.69%, while maintaining stability over a wide amplitude range. The PLMRD also achieves a 103% increase in static lifting speed. The proposed structure and control effectively address key drawbacks of conventional air suspensions.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for semi-active structural control using a variable inerter device
abstract: Structural control devices employing inerters have attracted considerable attention owing to their superior vibration mitigation performance. Variable inerter devices, which enable real-time adjustment of inertance and damping, offer further performance enhancement but also introduce a challenging nonlinear control problem. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based control strategy for a tuned variable inertial mass electromagnetic transducer (TVIMET) installed in a five-story base-isolated building. The proposed controller is developed using recurrent proximal policy optimization (RPPO) with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to account for both the partially observable nature of practical structural control and the history-dependent nonlinear behavior of the lead–rubber bearing (LRB) isolation system. Numerical simulations are conducted under a wide range of earthquake excitations, and the proposed method is compared with passive base isolation, a passive tuned viscous mass damper (TVMD), and a semi-active tuned inertial mass electromagnetic transducer (TIMET). The proposed TVIMET successfully adapts both the inertance and damping coefficient according to the changing dynamic characteristics of the structure. Unlike the passive TVMD, which is designed assuming post-yield structural behavior, the proposed controller remains effective even under earthquake excitations that do not induce significant yielding of the isolation layer. It also achieves the best overall vibration reduction, particularly in terms of the RMS structural responses. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of simultaneously adapting the inertance and damping through DRL for nonlinear structural vibration control.

title: Acoustic emission-based novel identification method for vertical tool center error in single-point diamond turning
abstract: During single-point diamond turning (SPDT), tool center errors can cause deviations of the tool position relative to the workpiece center, resulting in tool-above-center error (TACE) or tool-below-center error (TBCE) along the vertical direction. These errors generate residual cylindrical or conical deviations on the machined surface, thereby significantly degrading the surface quality and optical performance. To achieve online and high-precision identification of vertical tool center error (VTCE), this study proposes an online identification method that integrates time–frequency feature analysis with deep learning algorithms, thereby significantly improving the accuracy and efficiency of error identification. First, the acoustic emission (AE) signals acquired during the cutting process were analyzed using wavelet transform. The results indicate that the dominant response frequency band of the AE signal is concentrated within 187.5–218.8 KHz, while a higher proportion of high-frequency energy is observed under TBCE condition. Subsequently, time–frequency image features of the AE signals were constructed based on wavelet transform, and an improved GoogLeNet-AE model was developed to perform classification identification of VTCE, achieving a classification accuracy of 100 %. Furthermore, according to the root mean square (RMS) feature responses of AE signals at the final stage of cutting under different VTCE, convolutional neural network (CNN)-TACE and CNN-TBCE models were established to perform regression prediction for TACE and TBCE, respectively. The prediction errors of both models were maintained within 6 μm. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed AE signal-based VTCE identification method enables online and accurate identification of VTCE in SPDT, providing an effective approach for intelligent monitoring and error control in ultra-precision machining.

title: FNO-PD: A Fourier neural operator-based physics-based data-driven framework for efficient dynamic response computation in vehicle-track coupled systems
abstract: Accurate and efficient computation of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems is essential for safe, smooth, and reliable high-speed railway operation and maintenance optimization. However, traditional numerical simulation methods exhibit a significant efficiency bottleneck in solving large-scale dynamic problems, while existing deep learning approaches struggle to accurately characterize the global dynamic coupling characteristics of the system. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Fourier neural operator-based physics-based data-driven (FNO-PD) framework for the efficient prediction of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems. The framework comprises a physics-driven module and a data-driven module: the physics-driven module integrates physical information into FNO to predict train dynamic responses, while the data-driven module combines proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) with FNO for rail displacement field prediction. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed framework are evaluated using the probability density evolution method (PDEM) as a benchmark. Within the same vehicle-track numerical framework, the model is assessed for numerical generalization under measured track irregularity inputs, near-range speed extrapolation, and robustness to noise interference. Results demonstrate that the FNO-PD framework achieves high prediction accuracy and online computational efficiency, with good agreement between its predictions and the PDEM results. During online prediction, the proposed method achieves an approximately 1200-fold speedup over PDEM. Tests conducted with measured track irregularity inputs at speeds within and just outside the training range, together with noise interference tests, indicate satisfactory numerical generalization and noise robustness under the tested conditions. This study provides a novel and efficient technical pathway for the numerical prediction of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems, with potential for large-scale numerical analyses in high-speed railway engineering.

title: Generalized envelope harmonic product spectrum and GESHSgram with application to fault diagnosis of rolling element bearings
abstract: Accurate condition monitoring is crucial for implementing predictive maintenance of industrial machines, where the assessment of health status and the diagnosis of incipient faults rely heavily on the effective detection of machine fault-related information. In vibration analysis, the repetitive impulses induced by the fault of Rolling Element Bearings (REBs) operating at constant speed exhibit approximate periodicity, precisely pseudo-cyclostationarity. The Harmonic Product Spectrum (HPS) generated by the envelope spectrum or squared envelope spectrum has been applied to REB diagnostics by virtue of this property. However, there is a lack of adequate investigation and clear elucidation of their capabilities against multi-source interferences in industrial scenarios. To this end, a family of HPS, called Generalized Envelope Harmonic Product Spectrum (GEHPS), is proposed through the generalized envelope spectrum as the detector and estimator of cyclic frequencies. The performance and characteristics of GEHPS with different parameters are comprehensively verified and revealed by simulating interference noises from multiple sources in industrial scenarios and by comparing with the generalized envelope spectrum under the same parameter configurations. Additionally, taking advantage of the capability of GEHPS to detect cyclic transients, a normalized harmonic significance index with enhanced immunity to interference noise is newly proposed, which promotes a novel envelope analysis methodology, referred to as Generalized Envelope Spectrum Harmonics Significance-gram (GESHSgram), to be developed for fault diagnosis of REBs. The presented method is verified on one simulation case and three experimental cases from different test rigs, along with comparisons with four typical envelope analysis methods. The results demonstrate that the GESHSgram method can effectively and accurately detect various faults of REBs and outperforms four typical envelope analysis approaches.

title: Frequency-domain data-enabled predictive vibration control for longitudinal vibration suppression in variable-speed propulsion shafting
abstract: A vibration-oriented frequency-domain data-enabled predictive control (FreePC) framework is proposed for longitudinal vibration suppression in variable-speed propulsion shafting. The method constructs the prediction model directly from complex frequency–response data at multiple frequency points within the target band, thereby improving the representation of inter-peak and off-resonant dynamics relative to conventional low-order parametric models. To ensure numerical robustness and real-time feasibility, coherence-guided dictionary construction and explicit realization are introduced. In addition, a cost-function shaping strategy centered on the first longitudinal mode is developed to improve in-band response shaping, and a spectral-forgetting-based online update is incorporated to refresh the control-channel representation after operating-condition changes. Numerical and experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively suppress both tonal and broadband longitudinal vibration and recover effective control performance after stepwise changes among locally steady operating conditions.

title: A unified double-bridging TMCMC method for posterior reliability analysis of structures with monitoring data
abstract: To overcome the separation between model updating and reliability evaluation in conventional two-stage posterior reliability analysis, this study proposes an integrated double-bridging transitional Markov chain Monte Carlo (DB-TMCMC) method. Rather than treating Bayesian model updating and reliability estimation as two independent procedures, the proposed method starts from the integral-ratio form of posterior failure probability and constructs a unified sequence of intermediate distributions in the joint prior space of structural parameters and basic random variables. The innovation of the method lies primarily in the unified bridging framework and the associated sequential sampling path, through which likelihood information from monitoring data and failure-event information are introduced in a coupled and adaptive manner within a single TMCMC procedure. Within this framework, a monitoring-data likelihood bridge and a failure-event bridge are incorporated simultaneously, and an effective-sample-size-based adaptive alternating strategy is employed to advance the two bridging processes. A smooth failure-bridging function is further introduced to improve numerical stability and alleviate weight degeneracy during the progressive enforcement of the failure constraint. The method is validated using a five-story shear-type structure, a two-dimensional simply supported truss bridge, and a field case study of the Wangjiabai steel truss bridge. The results show that Bayesian updating based on natural frequencies and mode shapes effectively reduces parameter uncertainty and improves modal prediction accuracy. Monitoring data have a significant influence on structural reliability assessment, and the proposed DB-TMCMC method provides posterior failure probability estimates consistent with benchmark posterior Monte Carlo and sequential TMCMC-Subset Simulation results. In addition, repeated-run statistics and computational-cost comparisons demonstrate that the method enables structural model updating, posterior failure-sample generation, and failure-probability estimation within a single sequential sampling procedure, showing strong applicability to monitoring-data-informed reliability assessment of complex bridge structures.

title: A modal-disturbance-observer-based generalized-force model predictive control for attitude stabilization of a wave-adaptive vessel
abstract: Unknown wave excitation forces pose a substantial challenge to the attitude stabilization of wave-adaptive vessels, as they cannot be measured directly in real time. Conventional feedback control—reacting only after heave, pitch, and roll motions have developed—introduces an inherent response delay. This delay restricts the disturbance‑rejection capability of active suspension systems under phase‑varying wave inputs. This paper proposes a modal‑disturbance‑observer‑based generalized‑force model predictive control (MDO‑GMPC) method for a seven‑degree‑of‑freedom wave‑adaptive vessel. First, a seven‑DOF dynamic model is established to characterize the coupled motion of the upper platform and its four pontoons. A spatial modal transformation is then introduced to decompose the equivalent wave excitation at four pontoon locations into heave‑, pitch‑, roll‑, and torsion‑related modal disturbances. Based on the transformed model, a modal disturbance observer is designed by augmenting the modal disturbance states, thereby reconstructing the unknown wave‑force information from measurable vessel, suspension, and actuator responses. The estimated modal disturbances are further incorporated into the prediction horizon of the MPC scheme as feedforward information, while the control input is formulated in generalized‑force coordinates to coordinate the four active suspensions and reduce actuator redundancy. The main contribution of this work lies in the integration of online modal disturbance observation with feedforward predictive compensation, enabling the controller to respond proactively to wave excitation before significant attitude deviations occur. Experiments under both regular‑ and random‑wave conditions with four‑channel wave excitation are conducted, comparing the proposed method with passive suspension and conventional MPC. The results show that MDO‑GMPC achieves more accurate reconstruction of wave‑force trends and superior suppression of vertical motion, pitch, and roll responses, confirming its efficacy for attitude stabilization of wave‑adaptive vessels subject to unknown wave disturbances.

title: Coupled bearing-rotor modeling of four-point contact ball bearing misalignment and its effects on high-speed flexible rotor vibration
abstract: Four-point contact ball bearings (FPCBBs) can show multi-point ball-raceway contact at high speed. Their contact states may also switch during operation. These features make misalignment effects more complex than in conventional rolling bearings. However, the way in which FPCBB misalignment modifies internal contact states and transfers nonlinear excitation to a flexible rotor remains unclear. This study develops an FPCBB misalignment model based on the assembly adjustment process. The model is then coupled with a high-speed flexible rotor model. The nonlinear bearing reaction force is obtained from the instantaneous ball-raceway contact state and fed back into the rotor equations. The model is verified using critical-speed tests and constant-speed vibration measurements. The results show that static tilt misalignment and shaft-rotating misalignment both reduce the first critical speed, but produce different trends in the second critical speed. More importantly, the two misalignment types induce different nonlinear vibration routes. Static tilt misalignment generates period-doubling motion and high-speed complex nonlinear responses, whereas shaft-rotating misalignment mainly produces lower-speed period-doubling vibration. Analysis of the bearing contact states identifies two related mechanisms. Changes in the number of loaded balls, contact angle distribution, and inner-raceway contact state modify the equivalent radial stiffness. The transition of the contact load distribution from single-period to multi-period behavior is associated with subharmonic excitation. The study clarifies the contact-state mechanism by which FPCBB misalignment affects high-speed flexible rotor vibration.

title: A zero linear stiffness tristable nonlinear energy sink
abstract: The effectiveness of NES-based vibration control is characterized by its inherent frequency adaptability and energy-range robustness. However, conventional NESs are effective only within a limited energy range, whereas existing tristable NESs (TNESs), despite extending the energy range through their tristable characteristics, reintroduce local linear stiffness at stable equilibria, thereby compromising their essential nonlinearity and broadband adaptability. To address this limitation, this study proposes a zero linear stiffness TNES (ZLS-TNES) model, which maintains tristable characteristics while ensuring zero linear stiffness at all equilibrium points. The ZLS-TNES is realized through a cam-roller-spring mechanism, with the desired cam profile generated via an inverse design methodology. The slow invariant manifold and the nonlinear normal modes of the coupled system are derived to reveal the dynamic mechanisms. Systematic parametric investigations unveil a hierarchical activation mechanism involving two distinct energy thresholds: the first triggers intra-well strongly modulated response equivalent to a conventional NES, while the second activates high energy inter-well “snap-through” motions. Consequently, compared with the conventional NES, the proposed ZLS-TNES exhibits a significantly wider effective vibration mitigation amplitude range due to this dual-threshold hierarchical feature. Furthermore, the frequency self-adaptability of the TNES and ZLS-TNES is compared by varying the linear stiffness of the primary system. The results indicate that the ZLS-TNES achieves improved broadband adaptive capability by eliminating the positive linear stiffness at the stable equilibria of the conventional TNESs. Therefore, this study elucidates the hierarchical activation mechanism of the ZLS-TNES and presents a robust methodology to address the inherent limitations of conventional NESs and TNESs in terms of energy-level coverage and frequency adaptability.

title: Performance-based probabilistic RUL prediction via particle filtering with neural-guided inference
abstract: Accurate prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is essential for efficient operations and predictive maintenance of industrial systems. Prognostics is traditionally structured as a two-step procedure comprising estimation of the current system condition and prediction of future behavior and condition. Many data-driven approaches map sensor measurements directly to RUL without explicitly modeling degradation dynamics. We propose a data-driven prognostic framework that preserves this estimation–prediction structure without requiring physics-based state models. In the estimation stage, health indices are inferred from sensor measurements. Degradation parameters are treated probabilistically and inferred within a Bayesian framework, with online sequential updates via particle filtering. In the prediction stage, the stochastic degradation model is evaluated conditioned on the inferred parameter posterior, yielding an RUL distribution as a random variable with a hitting time. An offline-trained neural network serves as a particle-filter (PF) controller to improve adaptability while maintaining principled uncertainty propagation. Evaluation on the N-CMAPSS benchmark demonstrates competitive RUL accuracy and statistically grounded uncertainty across operating conditions, and comparisons indicate the advantages of explicitly separating estimation from prediction in data-driven prognostics.

title: Calculation method and topology optimization design of phononic crystal considering discrepancies from ideal 2D models
abstract: There are obvious differences in band structures between thin-plate phononic crystals (PnCs) and ideal two-dimensional PnCs, which significantly affects the accuracy of band gap (BG) prediction and further restricts the topological optimization performance of plate-type PnC structures. To solve this problem, this study systematically derives the band structure calculation methods of PnCs under plane stress and plane strain assumptions, and mainly establishes the calculation model for flexural wave BGs of PnC plates based on Mindlin moderately thick plate theory. Band structure calculations and comparisons of typical structures verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, and the applicability of Mindlin plate theory to BG calculation of PnC plates is clarified. A BG optimization framework based on the floating projection topology optimization is constructed to drive optimized configurations toward clear 0/1 binary distribution. This framework is employed to perform multi-mode and multi-order band gap optimization of two-phase PnCs under various theoretical models. The influences of BG order and plate thickness on the optimized width of flexural wave BGs are discussed. Typical optimized results are selected for experimental tests to validate the accuracy of the proposed calculation and optimization methods.
keywords: plane stress and plane strain assumptions

title: Tool-grounded large language models for decision-level fusion in fault diagnosis
abstract: Modern condition-monitoring systems generate heterogeneous information, such as high-rate sensor streams, derived health indicators, and discrete event histories, that must be combined into actionable diagnostic statements. Large language models (LLMs) are attractive as a decision-level fusion mechanism because they natively handle the textual modality, but their use in safety-critical fault diagnosis is impeded by hallucinated numerical content and stochastic outputs. This paper proposes a two-level information-fusion framework that uses an LLM as a constrained fusion operator rather than as a generator of facts. At the feature level, a recursive joint state-and-fault estimator built on a linear state-space model produces a vector of derived indicators, including an estimate of the actuator-fault parameter and its uncertainty. At the decision level, the LLM is restricted to interact with the estimator state and the event history exclusively through a finite library of typed deterministic tools, and must copy every numerical token in its response from a tool output. Grounding of the response is then satisfied by construction, and consistency follows once the sequence of tool calls is fixed. The framework is illustrated on a realistic actuator-fault scenario in which an autopilot-driven autonomous surface vessel encounters three fault events of different characters and the LLM produces reproducible operator-facing reports. A structured comparison against the two alternative reporting architectures available for this task, a rule-based template reporter driven by the same estimator and a flat-prompt LLM given the same numerical context, identifies open-ended query coverage at fixed numerical reliability as the property that neither alternative provides, and states the metrics under which that claim is to be tested.

title: Data-driven control for orbit transition of piezoelectric energy harvesters under stochastic excitation
abstract: To address the tendency of bistable piezoelectric energy harvesting systems to remain trapped in low-energy intrawell oscillations and the difficulty of sustaining high-energy interwell motion under stochastic disturbances, this study proposes a data-driven event-triggered jump–drift hybrid control method. The proposed method takes the neighborhood of a high-energy reference orbit as the control target and constructs a complete electromechanical state representation using displacement, velocity, and piezoelectric voltage. A signed orbit error is further defined through local radial projection to characterize both the magnitude and direction of the state deviation, thereby enabling direction-selective event triggering and control release. During the active control phase, a locally corrective control input is generated using an offline-identified one-step prediction model. Once the high-energy state is established, the controller switches to the drift mode and intervenes again only when a pronounced degradation of the system state is detected. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method can drive the system from a low-energy state toward the high-energy orbit while achieving a favorable trade-off among orbit-transition speed, maintenance of high-energy motion, and control effort. The method also retains a certain degree of adaptability under stochastic disturbances and mismatches in load resistance and mechanical damping. Further analyses of the sampling period and control delay indicate that the proposed method exhibits reasonable tolerance to nonidealities associated with digital implementation.

title: SIMBIE: efficient multipoint spectral stacking algorithm for impact-echo defect imaging in concrete structures
abstract: This study proposes Stack Imaging of Multipoint Spectral Amplitudes Based on Impact Echo (SIMBIE) for quantitative imaging of geometrically complex defects in concrete structures. By performing multiple impacts at varied positions and superposing the spectral data, SIMBIE mitigates the inherent ’circular effect’ of conventional single-point imaging while enabling simultaneous depth and width estimation—capabilities critical for characterizing non-regular defect geometries. A fully vectorized matrix formulation is developed to overcome the computational bottleneck of dense-grid imaging, achieving 50–300× speedup and reducing processing time from minutes to seconds. Validation through finite element analysis and laboratory experiments on specimens with diverse defect geometries, including wedge-shaped (oblique), circular (curved), and closely-spaced rectangular voids, demonstrates that SIMBIE achieves depth errors ranging from 0.27% to 8.91% (median: 2.81%) and width errors ranging from 2.8% to 31.5% (median: 13.7%), representing significant improvements over conventional SIBIE. The computational efficiency and enhanced accuracy render SIMBIE suitable for near-real-time defect mapping in structural health monitoring applications.

title: Energy-based dynamic damping identification in vibrating cables governed by hysteretic material behavior
abstract: The vibration of cables in both longitudinal and transverse directions, with or without an attached point mass, plays a key role in numerous industrial applications across a wide range of sectors. Although this problem appears simple and has been extensively investigated, several aspects of its dynamic behavior still require clarification. In particular, few studies explicitly relate local dissipative mechanisms at the material scale to the damping measured at the scale of the entire structure. In this article, two energy-based definitions of the damping ratio are derived analytically from material-scale dissipation, depending on the dominant deformation mode.
